body: THE INTERNET STOCK FUNDS ARE EXPANDING RAPIDLY IN THE unitedstates AS ITS TOTAL ASSETS HAVE GROWN 12.5 TIMES IN THE FIRST NINE MONTHS THIS YEAR, A REPORT SAID TUESDAY. ACCORDING TO A REPORT RELEASED BY THE INDEPENDENT MUTUAL FUND TRACKING SERVICE WIESENBURGER, WHILE OVERALL MUTUAL FUND ASSETS IN THE unitedstates GREW LESS THAN 10 PERCENT DURING THE FIRST THREE QUARTERS OF 1999, MONEY INVESTED IN ALL INTERNET STOCK MUTUAL FUNDS INCREASED BY OVER 1,250 PERCENT IN THE SAME PERIOD. "THE GROWTH OF THESE FUNDS HAS BEEN NOTHING SHORT OF PHENOMENAL IN JUST A FEW SHORT YEARS," WIESENBURGER SAID. "THIS SECTOR IS THE ENVY OF A MUTUAL FUND INDUSTRY THAT HAS POSTED ONLY SLUGGISH EXPANSION ON AN OVERALL BASIS IN 1999. INTERNET STOCK MUTUAL FUNDS CAN PLAY A ROLE IN A WELL-ROUNDED PORTFOLIO FOR INVESTORS WHO ARE WILLING TO FACE MORE RISK." SINCE THE INTERNET STOCK MUTUAL FUNDS WERE INCEPTED THREE YEAR AGO, ASSETS IN SUCH FUNDS HAVE SKYROCKETED, FROM 2.8 MILLION unitedstates  DOLLARS AT THE END OF 1996 TO MORE THAN 4.3 BILLION DOLLARS AS OF SEPTEMBER 30, 1999. THERE ARE 16 ADDITIONAL INTERNET STOCK MUTUAL FUNDS NOW IN REGISTRATION WITH THE unitedstates SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION (SEC) , PLUS THE FIRST TWO INTERNET MUTUAL FUNDS WHICH WERE LAUNCHED IN AUGUST 1996, SAID WIESENBURGER, WHICH HAS BEEN TRACKING 12 INTERNET FUNDS.

title: COPYRIGHT 1999 XINHUA NEWS AGENCY
body: DEMAND FOR HIGH-SPEED INTERNET ACCESS VIA CABLE MODEMS WILL GENERATE BILLIONS OF DOLLARS IN ADDITIONAL REVENUES FOR THE unitedstates CABLE INDUSTRY, ACCORDING TO A REPORT RELEASED BY A TECHNOLOGY AND MANAGEMENT CONSULTING FIRM TUESDAY. A CABLE MODEM IS A TERMINAL DEVICE THAT CONNECT A SUBSCRIBER'S PC TO THE INTERNET VIA THE CABLE TV NETWORK. CABLE TV OPERATORS REPORT THAT MORE THAN A MILLION CABLE MODEMS HAVE NOW BEEN INSTALLED IN unitedstates USERS' HOMES. THIS IS STILL A SMALL FRACTION OF THE OVER 38 MILLION unitedstates HOUSEHOLDS NOW ACCESSING ON-LINE SERVICES, SAID THE REPORT FROM ARTHUR D. LITTLE, INC. THE POTENTIAL DEMAND FOR HIGH-SPEED INTERNET ACCESS VIA CABLE FAR EXCEEDS CABLE'S CURRENT MARKET PENETRATION, THE FIRM SAID. THE FIRM'S RECENT STUDY FOUND THAT UP TO 28 PERCENT OF AMERICAN HOUSEHOLDS ARE LIKELY TO SUBSCRIBE TO A CABLE INTERNET ACCESS SERVICE PRICED AT THE TYPICAL LEVEL OF 40 unitedstates DOLLARS PER MONTH.  THESE HOUSEHOLDS, APPROXIMATELY 28 MILLION, COULD GENERATE 13.4 BILLION DOLLARS IN ANNUAL REVENUES. A HIGH PROPORTION OF THESE HOUSEHOLDS, 43 PERCENT, WOULD DROP THEIR CURRENT DIAL-UP INTERNET SERVICE PROVIDER (ISP) RATHER THAN PAY 10 DOLLARS EXTRA TO BE ABLE TO CONTINUE TO USE THEIR ISP'S E- MAIL SERVICE. ANOTHER 21 PERCENT OF THESE HOUSEHOLDS WOULD PAY THE EXTRA FEE, WHILE 25 PERCENT WOULD POSTPONE ADOPTION OF THE CABLE MODEM SERVICE AND INSTEAD WAIT FOR THEIR ISP TO OFF A COMPARABLE HIGH-SPEED INTERNET ACCESS SOLUTION; 11 PERCENT SAID THEY DID NOT YET KNOW WHAT THEY WOULD DO. GROWTH IN ON-LINE MUSIC, SOFTWARE AND VIDEO DISTRIBUTION WILL GENERATE EVEN GREATER DEMAND FOR HIGH-SPEED ALWAYS-ON INTERNET ACCESS SERVICES, THE FIRM SAID. TODAY, MOST PEOPLE USE THE INTERNET TO RETRIEVE TEXT AND GRAPHICS INFORMATION BUT THE DEMAND FOR HIGH-SPEED CONNECTIONS WILL GROW TREMENDOUSLY AS MULTIMEDIA INTERNET SERVICES BECOME MORE PREVALENT. MORE THAN HALF OF THE 1,000 ADULTS SURVEYED SELECTED CABLE MODEMS, WHEN ASKED WHICH SERVICE THEY WOULD PREFER FOR HIGH-SPEED INTERNET SERVICE, CABLE OR HIGH-SPEED ACCESS VIA TELEPHONE. TWENTY- SIX PERCENT FAVORED A TELEPHONE COMPANY OFFERING. TELEPHONE-BASED INTERNET ACCESS IS TYPICALLY PROVIDED BY A SERVICE CALLED ASYMMETRICAL DIGITAL SUBSCRIBER LINE (ADSL) WHICH, LIKE A CABLE MODEM, ALSO INVOLVES A SPECIAL TERMINAL DEVICE IN THE SUBSCRIBER'S HOME BUT USES THE TELEPHONE LINE INSTEAD OF THE CABLE TV NETWORK. BUT THE VERSION OF ADSL OFFERED AT THE SAME PRICE LEVEL AS CABLE MODEMS DELIVERS A LOWER DATA RATE -- LESS THAN ONE MILLION BITS PER SECOND VERSUS SEVERAL MILLION BITS PER SECOND VIA CABLE MODEMS. ACCORDING TO THE CONSULTING FIRM, IN PRINCIPLE, ADSL SERVICE SHOULD BE COMPETITIVE, AS TELEPHONE COMPANIES COULD PROVIDE A HIGHER ADSL DATA RATE FOR A MORE COMPETITIVE PRICE. HOWEVER, MANY TELEPHONE LINES IN THE unitedstates ARE IN POOR CONDITION AND CANNOT SUPPORT THIS SERVICE, AND TELEPHONE COMPANIES ARE STILL MOVING SLOWLY TO MAKE ADSL AVAILABLE TO CONSUMERS. ALSO, THERE IS A LACK OF A WELL-ACCEPTED SINGLE TECHNICAL STANDARD FOR ADSL.  AGAIN, ADSL IS BEING LEFT OUT OF MOVES BY CABLE OPERATORS AND BY THE DIRECT BROADCAST SATELLITE SERVICES TO INTEGRATE INTERNET ACCESS WITH THEIR TV SET-TOP BOXES TO ENHANCE THEIR SUBSCRIBERS' TV-VIEWING EXPERIENCE.

title: COPYRIGHT 1999 XINHUA NEWS AGENCY
body: GERMAN CHANCELLOR GERHARD SCHROEDER CALLED HERE MONDAY ON THE GOVERNMENT, BUSINESSES AND SOCIETY TO WORK CONCERTEDLY TO PUSH THE COUNTRY INTO THE INFORMATION ERA. SPEAKING TO ABOUT 100 LEADING INDUSTRIALISTS AT THE "GERMANY 21" CONGRESS, SCHROEDER SAID, "WE MUST KNOW THAT IN TERMS OF THE APPLICATION OF NEW TECHNOLOGIES, WE RANK AMONG THE LATE-COMERS INTERNATIONALLY." HE SAID THAT IN THE unitedstates, THE INFORMATION INDUSTRY ACCOUNTED FOR 7.6 PERCENT OF THE GROSS DOMESTIC PRODUCT (GDP) IN 1998, WHILE THE FIGURE IN GERMANY WAS ONLY 4.5 PERCENT. AND THE OVERALL CONNECTIONS TO THE INTERNET IN THE unitedstates ARE THREE TIMES THAT IN GERMANY. GERMANY IS EVEN BEHIND THE SCANDINAVIAN COUNTRIES AND THE NETHERLANDS, HE ADDED, NOTING THAT IN THOSE COUNTRIES 9 PERCENT OF THE LABOR FORCE WORK IN THE INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) FIELD, WHILE IN GERMANY IT IS MERELY 5 PERCENT. "THE COMMON GOAL OF EVERYONE RESPONSIBLE MUST BE REDUCING THE DISTANCE TO OTHER COUNTRIES AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE," HE SAID. SCHROEDER DESCRIBED COMPUTER AND IT, WHICH IS AMONG THE FIVE LEADING SECTORS IN THE GERMAN ECONOMY, AS MORE AND MORE SIGNIFICANT TO THE GERMAN ECONOMY. THE TURNOVER OF THE IT BRANCH WILL OVERTAKE THAT OF AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY THIS YEAR, SAID SCHROEDER. SCHROEDER PROJECTED THAT THE IT BRANCH WILL DEVELOP EVEN FASTER IN THE YEARS TO COME AND BRING GERMANY 250,000 MORE JOBS BY THE YEAR 2005. "ONE IMPORTANT DUTY FOR US IS TO QUALIFY THE PEOPLE FOR WHAT THE INFORMATION SOCIETY HAS OFFERED," SAID SCHROEDER, REFERRING TO THE SHORTAGE OF PROFESSIONAL RESOURCES IN IT COMPANIES. IN GERMANY, THERE ARE SOME 75,000 JOBS WAITING FOR QUALIFIED WORKERS IN THE IT SECTOR. THE OLD-STYLED EDUCATIONAL PROGRAM IN SCHOOLS IS SHORT OF CONTENT ON INFORMATION KNOWLEDGE. "TO TODAY'S YOUNGSTERS, KNOWLEDGE ON INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY IS AS IMPORTANT FOR A JOB AS A DRIVING LICENSE ON THE ROAD," SAID THE CHANCELLOR. "OUR GOAL IS TO PROVIDE EVERY SCHOOL WITH AT LEAST ONE INTERNET CONNECTION BEFORE YEAR 2001, THUS LET EVERY STUDENT LEARN HOW TO DEAL WITH THE NEW TECHNOLOGY." BY NOW ABOUT ONE-THIRD GERMAN SCHOOLS ARE EQUIPPED WITH COMPUTERS WITH ACCESS TO THE INTERNET. HE CALLED ON THE GOVERNMENT TO REFORM THE EDUCATION PROGRAM WITH MORE COURSES ON COMPUTER SCIENCE AND THE INTERNET. "GERMANY 21," AN INITIATIVE RAISED BY SOME 70 GERMAN IT COMPANIES, AIMS TO STRENGTHEN THE TEACHING OF MODERN INFORMATION KNOWLEDGE IN SCHOOLS AND FURTHER EDUCATION IN WORK. UNDER THE PROJECT, THE COMPANIES WILL PROVIDE 20,000 GERMAN SCHOOLS WITH COMPUTERS AND HELP BUILD A "VIRTUAL CLASSROOM" IN EVERY SCHOOL.

title: WORLD'S LARGEST WEB SURVEY FINDS DIFFERENCES BETWEEN COUNTRIES
body: A WORLDWIDE SURVEY HAS NOT ONLY CONFIRMED THE UBIQUITY OF INTERNET USAGE AND PENETRATION, BUT ALSO OFFERED A COMPELLING LOOK AT THE MANY DIFFERENCES THERE ARE ON AN INDIVIDUAL, COUNTRY AND REGIONAL BASIS. unitedstates MARKET RESEARCH FIRM INTERNATIONAL DATA CORPORATION (IDC) REPORTED TUESDAY THAT THE WORLD'S LARGEST WEB SURVEY IT CONDUCTED SHOWS DIVERSE ADOPTION PATTERNS DESPITE THE FACT THAT WEB USAGE AND INTERNET COMMERCE HAVE EXPLODED ACROSS ALL GEOGRAPHIES, CULTURES AND WALKS OF LIFE. THE SURVEY, PROJECT ATLAS, WAS CONDUCTED IN 13 MAJOR LANGUAGES IN COOPERATION WITH SOME OF THE WEB'S TOP PORTALS. MORE THAN 28, 000 RESPONSES WERE RECEIVED FROM MORE THAN 80 COUNTRIES. "WHAT WAS UNEXPECTED WERE THE DIFFERENCES BETWEEN INDIVIDUAL COUNTRIES," SAID IDC, DESCRIBING THE KEY FINDINGS FROM THE PROJECT.  FOR EXAMPLE, A HIGHER PERCENTAGE OF RESPONDENTS ACCESS THE INTERNET FROM SCHOOLS IN MEXICO THAN IN JAPAN, A COUNTRY RENOWNED FOR ITS ADVANCED EDUCATION. THE AVERAGE NUMBER OF HOME DEVICES THAT ACCESS THE WEB IS ABOUT 1.5, BUT THE DISTRIBUTION OF MULTIPLE-DEVICE HOUSEHOLDS IS NOT EVEN, ACCORDING TO THE SURVEY. FOR EXAMPLE, 26 PERCENT OF JAPANESE ADVANCED USERS HAVE OVER THREE INTERNET DEVICES IN THEIR HOUSEHOLDS VERSUS 13 PERCENT IN THE unitedstates AND 7 PERCENT IN THE unitedkingdom. AVERAGE MONTHLY INTERNET ACCESS FEES VARY DRAMATICALLY BY COUNTRY, FROM 78 unitedstates DOLLARS PER MONTH IN ARGENTINA TO 18 unitedstates  DOLLARS A MONTH IN SWEDEN. PURCHASING OF GOODS AND SERVICES OVER THE WEB FROM HOME IS SURPRISINGLY WIDESPREAD AMONG THE USERS POLLED, IDC SAID. EVEN IN LESS-DEVELOPED COUNTRIES, LIKE INDIA AND CHINA, MORE THAN 25 PERCENT HAD MADE PURCHASES FROM HOME. THE AVERAGE AMOUNT SPENT OVER THE WEB RANGED FROM UNDER 35 unitedstates DOLLARS IN DENMARK, SPAIN AND CHINA TO OVER 70 DOLLARS IN THE unitedstates, ARGENTINA AND PUERTO RICO. MOST SURVEY RESPONDENTS SAID THEY PREFERRED TO VISIT WEB SITES IN THEIR LOCAL LANGUAGE ALTHOUGH THE DEGREE TO WHICH WAS SO VARIED CONSIDERABLY. FOR EXAMPLE, 80 PERCENT OF THE RESPONDENTS IN INDIA FAVORED ENGLISH-LANGUAGE SITES, AS DID ALMOST HALF THE RESPONDENTS IN hongkong AND THE NETHERLANDS.

title: EAED112235HKE -- INTERNET BUYING INCREASING AMONG U.S. HOUSEHOLDS
body: ALMOST A QUARTER OF unitedstates  HOUSEHOLDS BOUGHT SOMETHING OVER THE INTERNET DURING THE PAST YEAR, ACCORDING TO A SURVEY RELEASED MONDAY BY THE CONFERENCE BOARD, A BUSINESS-FINANCED RESEARCH GROUP. WHILE PRIVACY AND SECURITY CONCERNS ARE CLEARLY KEEPING MANY CONSUMERS OFF THE NET, THE SURVEY REPORT SAID, THESE ISSUES WILL BE RESOLVED OVER TIME AND MARKETERS WILL EFFECTIVELY PENETRATE THIS VAST BUT STILL UNTAPPED MARKET. THE SURVEY, WHICH WAS BASED ON A REPRESENTATIVE SAMPLE OF 5,000 HOUSEHOLDS, SHOWS THAT YOUNGER HOUSEHOLDS WERE MORE LIKELY THAN OLDER HOUSEHOLDS TO HAVE MADE AN ONLINE TRANSACTION, AND SO WERE CONSUMERS IN THE MORE AFFLUENT BRACKETS, COMPARED WITH POORER HOUSEHOLDS. CONSUMERS MOSTLY FAVORED ENTERTAINMENT ITEMS, MAKING BOOKS, CDS AND COMPUTER ACCESSORIES THE TOP SELLERS OVER THE INTERNET, ACCORDING TO THE SURVEY. THESE ITEMS ARE RELATIVELY INEXPENSIVE; A SUBSTANTIAL PROPORTION OF SURVEY PARTICIPANTS SAID THEIR BIGGEST SINGLE PURCHASE WAS UNDER 100 unitedstates DOLLARS. HOUSEHOLDERS AGE 25-34 ARE THE MOST LIKELY ONLINE SHOPPERS, WITH MORE THAN 40 PERCENT HAVING MADE SUCH A PURCHASE. THOSE IN THE 65-AND-OVER GROUP ARE THE LEAST LIKELY TO SHOP ONLINE, WITH LESS THAN 10 PERCENT HAVING MADE SUCH A TRANSACTION. AFFLUENT HOUSEHOLDERS, WHOSE EARNING IN EXCESS OF 50,000 DOLLARS, TEND TO SPEND WELL-ABOVE AVERAGE, WITH MORE THAN 40 PERCENT HAVING PURCHASED VIA THE INTERNET. WHEN ASKED ABOUT PURCHASING FURTHER ONLINE, MORE THAN 60 PERCENT CLAIM THAT THE PRICE OF GOODS PLAYS HEAVILY IN THEIR DECISION. IMPROVED SECURITY RANKED AS THE SECOND ISSUE. NAVIGATION WAS LISTED THE THIRD BLOCK, AS NEARLY 40 PERCENT OF RESPONDENTS WOULD LIKE GREATER EASE IN FINDING THEIR PRODUCTS.

title: WIRELESS TO DOMINATE ASIA AS INTERNET ACCESS MEDIUM: REPORT
body: ASIA IS RAPIDLY BECOMING THE PROVING GROUND FOR THE NEXT GREAT TREND IN TELECOMMUNICATIONS -- THE MERGING OF MOBILE TELEPHONE AND THE INTERNET, ACCORDING TO A BENCHMARKS REPORT PUBLISHED BY PYRAMID RECENTLY. THE AUTHORS OF THE NEW PYRAMID BENCHMARKS REPORT, ENTITLED INTERNET CONNECTIVITY IN ASIA, ESTIMATE THAT ASIA'S CELLULAR POPULATION WILL BE APPROXIMATELY 125 MILLION BY THE END OF THIS YEAR AND SHOULD REACH OVER 310 MILLION BY 2004. AS CELLULAR SERVICE BECOMES MORE UBIQUITOUS IN THE REGION AND NEW DATA-CENTRIC APPLICATIONS RUSH IN WITH THE ADVENT OF THIRD GENERATION TECHNOLOGY, THE MOBILE PHONE WILL LIKELY BECOME THE INTERNET ACCESS CHOICE, SAID ROSS O'BRIEN, ASIA RESEARCH DIRECTOR OF PYRAMID. O'BRIEN SAID THEY BELIEVE THAT NEARLY HALF OF ALL CELLULAR SUBSCRIBERS IN THE ASIAN REGION SHOULD HAVE MOBILE DATA SERVICE CAPABILITIES IN THE NEXT 10 YEAR. THE PYRAMID REPORTED NOTED THAT THERE ARE MORE CELLULAR PHONES IN SOUTH KOREA THAN FIXED LINES, AND THE SAME WILL BE TRUE IN hongkong AND THE PHILIPPINES IN THE NEXT YEAR. CHINA, WHICH HAS BECOME THE WORLD'S LARGEST MOBILE PHONE PROCURER, CONTINUES TO ADD NEARLY ONE AND A HALF MILLION NEW CELLULAR SUBSCRIBERS EVERY MONTH, THE REPORT SAID. PYRAMID RESEARCH, A DIVISION OF THE ECONOMIST INTELLIGENCE UNIT (EIU), IS THE LEADING AUTHORITY IN COMMUNICATIONS MARKET AROUND THE WORLD.

title: INTERNET DOMINATES IN '99 COMDEX COMPUTER TRADE SHOW
body: AT THIS YEAR'S COMDEX COMPUTER TRADE SHOW, WHICH STARTED ON NOVEMBER 15 IN LAS VEGAS, ONE CAN SEE THAT THE INTERNET WILL SOON BE INVADING PRACTICALLY EVERY ASPECT OF OUR LIFE. IN RECENT YEARS, THE DESKTOP DOMINATED THE COMDEX COMPUTER TRADE SHOWS, WITH EXHIBITING COMPANIES INTRODUCING THE LATEST ADVANCES IN PC TECHNOLOGY. THIS YEAR, HOWEVER, IT IS ALL ABOUT DEVICES, JUST AS HEWLETT-PACKARD CO. CHIEF EXECUTIVE CARLY FIORINA SAID. BUT THE DEVICES ARE NOT JUST INTERNET TERMINALS AND HAND-HELD COMPUTERS. COMPANIES ARE PITCHING SUCH PROSAIC OBJECTS AS ALARM CLOCKS, WRISTWATCHES AND GAS PUMPS AS INTERNET DEVICES. DURING HER KEYNOTE ADDRESS MONDAY, FIORINA PRESENTED AN HP PROJECT UNDER DEVELOPMENT CALLED COOL TOWN - A PLACE IN WHICH EVERYTHING IS CONNECTED TO THE INTERNET. AN ALARM CLOCK, FOR EXAMPLE, WOULD AFFORD YOU A FEW EXTRA MINUTES OF SLEEP IF TRAFFIC IS LIGHT. JOHN CHAMBERS, CISCO SYSTEMS INC. CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER, DEMONSTRATED AN INTERNET-ENABLED GAS PUMP FEATURING A TOUCHSCREEN THAT PROVIDES ACCESS TO TRAFFIC REPORTS, MAPS AND A PERSONALIZED PAGE FOR NEWS, STOCKS AND SPORTS SCORES. EVEN MICROSOFT CORP., THE KING OF DESKTOP SOFTWARE, IS GETTING INTO THE ACT. BILL GATES, MICROSOFT CHAIRMAN AND CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER, SHOWED OFF INTERNET TECHNOLOGY FOR A DEVICE CALLED THE AUTO PC. THE DEVICE WOULD ALLOW DRIVERS TO SCHEDULE TUNE-UPS AT THE NEAREST FACILITY, ACCESS TRAFFIC REPORTS AND DOWNLOAD THEIR FAVORITE SONGS IN DIGITAL FORMAT FROM THE WEB.

title: CHINA LAUNCHES FIRST MOBILE MULTIMEDIA RESEARCH LAB
body: CHINA'S FIRST LABORATORY FOR MOBILE MULTIMEDIA RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT WAS FOUNDED TODAY. THE LAB WAS CO-CREATED BY ERICSSON, CHINA MOBILE TELECOM CORP., BEIJING INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY AND BEIJING UNIVERSITY OF POSTS AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS. THE LAB WILL HELP CHINESE INTERNET SERVICE PROVIDERS (ISPS), IT HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE VENDORS AND ACADEMIC INSTITUTES TO UPGRADE LOCAL MOBILE COMMUNICATION APPLICATIONS AND SERVICES TO THE THIRD GENERATION (3G) TECHNOLOGIES, SAID MICHAEL RICKS, PRESIDENT AND CEO OF ERICSSON (CHINA) CO. THE 3G TECHNOLOGIES INCLUDE THREE KEY TECHNOLOGIES SUCH AS GENERAL PACKET RADIO SERVICE (GPRS), WIDE-BAND CODE DIVISION MULTIPLE ACCESS (WCDMA) AND WIRELESS APPLICATION PROTOCOL (WAP), HE ADDED. THE LAB WILL FOCUS ON THE RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS OF ANALYSIS, SIMULATION, DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING ON WIDE-BAND MOBILE MULTIMEDIA SERVICES FOR THE CHINESE MARKET, HE SAID. IT WILL ALSO HELP DEVELOP NEW MOBILE INTERNET BUSINESS APPLICATIONS, AND MOBILE SERVICES FOR INDUSTRIES LIKE BANKING, FINANCE, TRANSPORT AND RETAIL. AS A WORLD-LEADING SUPPLIER OF MOBILE INFRASTRUCTURES, ERICSSON HAS SET UP 3G EXPERIMENTAL SYSTEMS IN CANADA, JAPAN, GERMANY, ITALY, BRITAIN, SWEDEN AND THE unitedstates.

title: HK HOSTS SYMPOSIUM ON IT FOR YOUTH
body: A SYMPOSIUM ON INFORMATION AND TECHNOLOGY (IT) FOR YOUTH OPENED HERE ON MONDAY TO PROMOTE THE USE OF IT AND E-COMMERCE AMONG THE YOUTH OF hongkong TO HELP THEM GAIN A LEADING EDGE IN THE NEW MILLENNIUM. THE SYMPOSIUM OF DIGITAL 21 POWER FOR YOUTH - THE WAY FORWARD WAS HELD IN RESPONSE TO THE INITIATIVE OF THE hongkong SPECIAL ADMINISTRATIVE REGION TO PROMOTE THE ADOPTION OF IT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF THE GOVERNMENT'S DIGITAL 21 STRATEGY TO ENHANCE THE COMPETITIVENESS OF hongkong. "THE INVOLVEMENT OF YOUNG ENTREPRENEURS IN E-COMMERCE WILL PLAY A PIVOTAL ROLE IN SHAPING hongkong'S FUTURE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, " THOMAS TANG, EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR OF THE hongkong PRODUCTIVITY COUNCIL, SAID AT THE OPENING CEREMONY OF THE SYMPOSIUM. TANG CONTINUED THAT WITH THE WIDESPREAD ADOPTION OF THE INTERNET, THE SUCCESS OF A COMPANY DEPENDS A LOT ON HOW WELL A COMPANY PREPARE ITSELF FOR E-COMMERCE APPLICATION. MORE THAN HALF OF hongkong INTERNET USERS ARE UNDER THE AGE OF 30, OF THEM 55 PERCENT HAVE A MONTHLY INCOME EXCEEDING 30,000 HK DOLLARS (3,846 unitedstates DOLLARS), REFLECTING THE PROFILE OF THIS USE GROUP AS YOUNG BUSINESS PROFESSIONALS, TANG SAID. ACCORDING TO TANG, AMONG THE 112 MILLION INTERNET USERS IN THE WORLD, MORE THAN 12 MILLION OF THEM ARE FOUND IN ASIA. IT IS EXPECTED THAT BY THE YEAR 2003, THE NUMBER OF USERS IN ASIA WILL INCREASE TO 90 MILLION AND hongkong WILL HAVE SOME ONE MILLION USERS, TANG SAID. A SERIES OF IT-RELATED ACTIVITIES WILL BE LAUNCHED ALONG WITH THE SYMPOSIUM, INCLUDING THE SELECTION OF TEN OUTSTANDING YOUNG DIGITAL PERSONS, E-COMMERCE AWARD, TRAINING COURSES AND SEMINARS. THE SYMPOSIUM WAS JOINTLY ORGANIZED BY THE hongkong PRODUCTIVITY COUNCIL, THE hongkong JUNIOR CHAMBER AND MING PAO DAILY NEWS AND BACKED BY THE INFORMATION AND TECHNOLOGY SERVICES DEPARTMENT OF THE HKSAR GOVERNMENT AND FEDERAL EXPRESS CORPORATION.

title: LEGAL FRAMEWORK URGED FOR INTERNET ECONOMY: EXPERTS
body: THE INTERNET, UNDERGOING SKYROCKETING DEVELOPMENT, HAS PRODUCED A SPATE OF CHALLENGING ISSUES WHILE WORKING ITS WAY INTO CHINA'S ECONOMY, CULTURE, MEDIA AND SOCIETY. IN RESPONSE, CHINA MUST ESTABLISH A LEGAL FRAMEWORK TO DEAL WITH THE WEB-RELATED PROBLEMS OF THE FUTURE, EXPERTS SAID TODAY. ZHOU QIREN, A PROFESSOR WITH THE CHINA CENTER FOR ECONOMIC RESEARCH (CCER) OF BEIJING UNIVERSITY, MADE THE REMARK AT THE MEETING ON CHINA'S FUTURE IN THE INTERNET HELD AT THE PRESTIGIOUS SCHOOL. THE INTERNET HAS CHANGED CHINA'S TRADITIONAL COMMUNICATION MODE INTO SOMETHING SHAPELESS AND AS YET UNDEFINED, ZHOU SAID. "THE INTERNET HAS BROUGHT US NEW WAYS OF COMMUNICATION, TRADING, AND EVEN A NEW LIFESTYLE," ZHOU SAID. "PEOPLE WILL FEEL IT IS DIFFICULT TO MANAGE THE INTERNET WITH TRADITIONAL THINKING." CHINA LINKED ITSELF TO THE INTERNET ONLY FIVE YEARS AGO. THE NUMBER OF NETIZENS IN CHINA, HOWEVER, HAS NEARLY DOUBLED EVERY YEAR. ACCORDING TO ESTIMATES FROM THE MINISTRY OF INFORMATION INDUSTRY, THE NUMBER OF PEOPLE HAVING ACCESS TO THE INTERNET WILL HIT 4.5 MILLION BY THE END OF THIS YEAR. THE WORLD INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ORGANIZATION NOTED IN AN EARLIER PRESS RELEASE THAT BY THE YEAR 2005, CHINA WILL HAVE THE MOST NETIZENS IN THE WORLD, TAKING THE PLACE OF THE unitedstates. ACCORDING TO STATISTICS QUOTED BY ZHOU, THE ASIAN-PACIFIC REGION WILL WITNESS THE MOST RAPID GROWTH OF E-COMMERCE IN THE 21ST CENTURY. CHINA, FOLLOWING INDIA, WILL BECOME THE COUNTRY TO MOST QUICKLY DEVELOP E-COMMERCE, WITH A GROWTH RATE OF 243 PERCENT.  AND CHINA WILL RECEIVE 3.8 BILLION unitedstates DOLLARS OF E-COMMERCE INCOME IN 2003. HARRY H. HUANG, NASDAQ-AMEX CHIEF REPRESENTATIVE IN THE CHINA REGION, NOTED AT TODAY'S MEETING THAT THE INTERNET WAS CONVERTING THE CURRENT CURRENCY ECONOMY INTO AN INTERNET ONE. CITING STOCK TRADING AS AN EXAMPLE, HE SAID THAT 80 PERCENT OF THE WORLD'S STOCK TRADING IS DONE VIA INTERNET. HUANG SAID THAT THE INTERNET HAS CREATED A MULTI-DIMENSIONAL SPACE THAT HAS GIVEN BIRTH TO COUNTLESS BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES. " AND ONE CAN NEVER MISS THE BOAT," HE SAID. THE VIGOROUS INTERNET ECONOMY, HOWEVER, HAS ALSO HAD SOME STRONG NEGATIVE IMPACT. THE TRADITIONAL INDUSTRIES SOMETIMES FEEL PRESSED TO ACCEPT THE NEW TRADING METHOD, AND THE SITUATION WILL PROBABLY INTENSIFY IF SOME SOLUTIONS ARE NOT FOUND, HE SAID. PROF. ZHOU SAID IT IS IMPERATIVE TO MAP OUT A SOUND LEGAL BASIS FOR REGULATING INTERNET GROWTH. ZHOU SAID THAT IT IS NOW EVEN MORE NECESSARY FOR CHINA TO ESTABLISH LEGAL GUIDELINES FOR ACTIVITIES OF ALL INVOLVED IN THE INTERNET ECONOMY.

title: TECHNOLOGY'S IMPACT ON U.S. REAL ESTATE INDUSTRY TO CONTINUE: REPORT
body: THE TREND OF TECHNOLOGICAL CHANGE THAT HAS TRANSFORMED COMMUNICATIONS FOR CONSUMERS AND THE U.  S. REAL ESTATE INDUSTRY IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE IN THE NEW MILLENNIUM, ACCORDING TO A NEW REPORT RELEASED SATURDAY. BUSINESS PRACTICES WILL CHANGE WITH TECHNOLOGY, SAID THE REPORT FROM THE unitedstates NATIONAL ASSOCIATION OF REALTORS (NAR), BUT THE HUMAN ELEMENT WILL REMAIN JUST AS IMPORTANT AS IT IS TODAY. "RESEARCH SHOWS CONSUMERS LIKE TO USE NEW TECHNOLOGY TOOLS TO HELP THEM WITH REAL ESTATE TRANSACTIONS, AND REAL ESTATE FIRMS ARE RESPONDING BY IMPLEMENTING THESE TOOLS IN THEIR BUSINESS PRACTICES, " THE REPORT SAID. unitedstates CONSUMERS ARE EMPOWERED WITH TYPES OF INFORMATION PREVIOUSLY UNAVAILABLE TO THEM, ESPECIALLY IN AREAS OF REAL ESTATE, THE REPORT SAID.  WHAT WERE PROPRIETARY DATABASES ONLY A FEW YEARS AGO ARE NOW AVAILABLE TO ANYONE 24 HOURS A DAY. MEANWHILE, REAL ESTATE PROFESSIONALS ARE BECOMING TECHNOLOGICAL SAVVY TO BE ABLE TO WORK EFFICIENTLY AND QUICKLY WITH HOME BUYERS AND SELLERS.  SINCE 1997, THE NUMBER OF THE NAR MEMBERS WITH INTERNET ACCESS HAS RISEN FROM 26 PERCENT TO 71 PERCENT OF MEMBERS.  NINE OUT OF 10 REALTORS OWN OR LEASE A COMPUTER.  THE ASSOCIATION HAS A MEMBERSHIP OF 750,000. NAR SURVEYS SHOW THE NUMBER OF HOME BUYERS USING THE INTERNET AS A SEARCH TOOL HAS INCREASED 20-FOLD, FROM ONLY TWO PERCENT IN 1995 TO 23 PERCENT IN MAY 1999. ACCORDING TO THE REPORT, THREE OUT OF FIVE REALTORS USE email FOR THEIR BUSINESS; 72 PERCENT OF REAL ESTATE FIRMS GENERATE AT LEAST SOME OF THEIR BUSINESS ONLINE WHILE THREE PERCENT GENERATE MORE THAN 20 PERCENT OF THEIR BUSINESS ONLINE; AND NEARLY THREE OUT OF FIVE REAL ESTATE FIRMS HAVE A WEB SITE. BUT THE NAR SAID THAT WHILE THE INTERNET CAN SIGNIFICANTLY SPEED THE TRANSACTIONS PROCESS, IT CANNOT REPLACE MANY OF THE FUNCTIONS THAT REALTORS PROVIDE THEIR CUSTOMERS. THERE ARE STILL CUSTOMERS WHO ARE INTIMIDATED BY TECHNOLOGY AND INFORMATION OVERLOAD. SPECIALIZED SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE OF NEIGHBORHOODS AND GOVERNMENT REGULATION, TOGETHER WITH COMMUNICATION SKILLS AND THE ABILITY TO NEGOTIATE TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR A CLIENT'S BENEFIT, MEAN THE HUMAN ELEMENT CANNOT BE REPLACED, THE REPORT SAID. THE REPORT CONCLUDED THAT TECHNOLOGY WILL COMPLEMENT BUT NOT REPLACE REAL ESTATE PROFESSIONALS, AND AT THE SAME TIME, REAL ESTATE BROKERS AND AGENTS MUST HARNESS THE FORCES OF CHANGE TO MEET THE FUTURE NEEDS OF BUYERS AND SELLERS.

title: craze for on-line literary journals in china
body: some influential literary journals in china are publishing their electronic editions on the web to attract young web surfers. any internet browser can easily find homepages of "xinhua digest", "writer digest", "china writer", "novel monthly", " october", and "harvest", the most prestigious chinese literature periodicals in china. mengya, or burgeonings, was among the earliest owners of a homepage. early this year, the editorial department established its own website (www.mengya.online.sh.cn), providing readers with selected novels and a chat room hosted by chen cun, a famous writer. the chinese writers' association also started a website (www. jrzj.com.cn), through which on-line visitors can read works of chinese literary masters such as lao she, ba jin, xiao qian and ding ling. called "today's writer", the website has links with other sites such as "people's literature" and "october". the chinese writers' association said that the on-line literary journals will attract many more readers. literary journals always show new literary trends in china. but many writers complain that there are few outlets for the works. mengya's editor-in-chief zhao changtian said that being on-line benefits both readers and the editorial department. a toronto on-line book store covers some 50 chinese literary periodicals at its website: www.dragonsource.com.

title: cable wireless hkt, star tv form joint venture
body: cable wireless hkt and star tv announced wednesday the formation of a company that aims to provide leading pay television and internet services to hongkong and the asia region.  the new company will bring together the rich content and extensive asia-wide satellite coverage of star tv, with the worldleading broadband network and interactive multimedia services from cable wireless hkt, said a statement jointly issued by the two firms.  leveraging on these capabilities, the new company will be able to offer a unique and comprehensive package of digital pay television and on-line home entertainment with coverage to virtually every home in hongkong, the statement said.  the new services will include access to an extensive choice of interactive home entertainment, including 50 television channels, the option of conventional or high-speed broadband internet access services, as well as on-line shopping, e-commerce applications and information services delivered to the television or home computer.  the new services are planned to be introduced initially in hongkong during 2000, subject to the granting of a pay television license by the hongkong government.  the new company will initially be 60 percent owned by cable wireless hkt and 40 percent by star tv.  as part of the transaction, which is subject to certain conditions including any necessary governmental, regulatory, shareholder and other approvals and consents, cable wireless hkt will be issued with 300 million unitedstates dollars in redeemable cumulative preference shares together with warrants which will potentially enable it to increase its shareholdings in the company to 70 percent in the future.  cable wireless hkt is a major global telecommunications business of hongkong with customers in 70 countries and regions.  star tv, a subsidiary of the news corporation limited, offers both subscription and free-to-air television services for more than 300 million viewers across asia and the middle east in seven languages.

title: u.s. compaq corp. unveils 499-dollar computer
body: personal computer maker compaq computer corp on wednesday unveiled a 499-dollar computer with internet access that fits at the side of an office desk, according to reports from the company.  the 499-dollar model, which costs about one-third less than compaq's previous least expensive business computer, includes a cdrom or dvd drive and sports a 500 megahertz celeron processor, 64 megabytes of memory and a 4.3 gigabyte hard drive. it doesn't have a floppy disk drive. a monitor is extra.  "we are offering a simpler computer with great design that takes a lot of complexity out of the personal computer," said michael capellas, compaq's recently named chief executive.  the new computer will come in four configurations. variation will depend on whether the user requires a standard 500 megahertz intel celeron chip or a faster pentium iii chip and whether the device is to be hooked up to modern peripheral equipment like printers or older equipment requiring different attachments.  prices start at 499 dollars but officials gave no indication of prices for other configurations.  analysts say pc makers are gearing up to offer a new range of internet-ready machines to coincide with the release of microsoft corp.'s next-generation windows 2000 software in february.  they also say the low-priced machine unveiled by compaq will only inflame the already intense price wars that have hammered pc makers during the past year.

title: china to develop e-commerce in its own way
body: china is planning to multiply the number of people in the country using the internet in the near future by implementing the latest technology.  the integrated e-business service platform, developed by the shenzhen liming networks systems, one of the largest computer network integration firms in china, enables users to access service providers and other users of e-commerce via television, telephones and facsimiles, as well as personal computers. the core of the technology is an information switch, or i-switch, that can bridge the flow of data between such electronic networks as tv, telecommunications, and the internet.  the shenzhen liming network systems signed an agreement today with ibm of the unitedstates on strategic cooperation in developing applications of e-commerce that are suitable for conditions in china today.  director of the national office of information technology song ling said at the signing ceremony that the chinese government is considering listing this new technology as one of the national experimental e-commerce projects.  the shenzhen liming network systems has already installed this technology for the shenzhen stock exchange for the on-line trading of securities.  henry chow, chairman of ibm operations in the greater china region, said today that the company will help china explore various ways to expand e-commerce.

title: u.s. on-line shoppers to triple in
body: this year's holiday shopping season in the unitedstates will see a huge increase in the volume of on-line shoppers and dollars spent on-line, said a report released tuesday by a consulting firm.  according to a report based on a survey of 1,200 on-line shoppers, the number of regular on-line holiday shoppers will almost triple from 1998. last year, 23 percent of the respondents did at least 10 percent of their holiday shopping on-line. in 1999, the number will be 67 percent.  the survey, conducted by ernst young, also found that consumers will do more of their holiday shopping on-line.  in 1998, only four percent of on-line shoppers did at least 50 percent of their holiday shopping on-line. in 1999, the number may jump to 19 percent of shoppers. conversely, the number of on-line consumers who have no plans to shop on-line during the holidays dropped dramatically, from 49 percent to 11 percent.  considering the data as well as the dramatic increase in the number of internet sites and merchandise available, the consulting firm projected on-line sales for the holiday of 12-15 billion unitedstates dollars.  the survey revealed that favorite categories sold on-line during the holidays will be computers and related products, books, cds, toys and videos.  time constraints and frustration with in-store shopping are driving shoppers to the web for holiday shopping this year, the survey said.  price was not a driving factor, nor were value-added services.  when asked why they like to do their holiday shopping on-line, respondents selected: saving time, stores too crowded, more convenient shopping hours, less driving, etc., said the survey.

title: web browser war ends in u.s.
body: a web browser war in the unitedstates has come to an end with microsoft's internet explorer dominating the market, a local market research firm declared here on monday.  in its final browser survey of 236 unitedstates companies, zona research found microsoft's internet explorer was the primary browser choice for 64 percent of the respondents, while 36 percent indicated netscape navigator.  there were nine players on the browser frontier battling for a slice of a market of 200 million unitedstates dollars in 1996, said the firm's first browser study in january of 1996.  browser is the program that serves as the front end to the world wide web on the internet.  in order to view a site, the user types its address (url) into the browser's location field and the home page of that site is downloaded to the user.  the success of internet explorer and navigator are reflected in the growing number of companies with browser policies mandating uniformity in desktop configuration, zona said.  nearly three quarters of companies interviewed have a corporate browser policy that encourages or requires use of a particular browser, the zona study showed.  of the companies with a browser policy, 69 percent dictate the use of internet explorer, while 31 percent require the use of navigator.  no other browser has been named as part of a corporate policy, zona said.  "we are witnessing a shift away from the importance of the browser technology to the content on the internet," zona said.  " it is not surprising that the two dominant browser vendors now play a significant role in the burgeoning content marketplace.  the question is how will the content war play itself out." the latest browser survey also indicated that 36 percent of companies monitor internet content based on a list of approved sites.  twenty-three percent of all monitoring is based on the user's job function, 19 percent of all monitoring is based on the size of the transmission, and 14 percent of monitoring internet content is based on the time of day.

title: explosive growth expected in e-commerce sales, survey shows
body: most unitedstates policy makers, company executives and association heads expected online retail sales to grow by 500 percent in the unitedstates over the next two years, according to a recent survey by the unitedstates chamber of commerce and kpmg llp.  the survey, which was conducted during a conference on e-commerce taxation at the unitedstates chamber of commerce/national chamber foundation and sponsored by kpmg llp, involved 150 policy makers, company executives and association heads.  fifty-three percent of the survey respondents predicted internet sales, estimated to be 8 billion unitedstates dollars last year, would reach 50-100 billion dollars by 2001, with nineteen percent projecting it would top 100 billion dollars. only 7 percent thought that internet sales would remain lower than 25 billion dollars over the two-year period and 21 percent thought sales would reach 25-50 billion dollars.  the conference explored the global implications of e-commerce, state and local impacts of the tax moratorium on internet sales, and examined how internet taxation might affect businesses and customers, according to the unitedstates chamber of commerce.  douglas graham, a partner with kpmg's financial services consulting practice, said that "we are in a transitionary period right now, one in which there is heightened interest in adopting fair policy." fifty-six percent of the survey respondents said a sensible legal, fiscal and regulatory framework that minimized government regulation could be adopted for the internet.

title: hong kong cable and wireless hkt posts interim loss
body: hongkong's telecom giant cable and wireless hkt friday announced an interim loss of 2.76 billion hk dollars (355 million unitedstates dollars) for the six months to september, 1999.  linus w. l. cheung, chief executive of the cable and wireless hkt limited, attributed the net loss to severe competition in international and mobile markets.  "our first-half ifobicmblreflect the increasingly challenging market environment in hongkong, which is now one of the most open and competitive telecommunications markets in the world," cheung said.  "however, our results also highlight the dramatic growth in demand for new internet and e-commerce services," cheung added.  the firm, known until july as hongkong telecommunications ltd., posted a 6.09 billion hk dollar (780 million unitedstates dollars) profit in the previous corresponding period.  the latest result included a one-off loss of 7.08 billion hk dollars, representing write-downs and write-offs on the carrying value of certain fixed and other assets.  the telecom giant said the result came on a 17.3-percent drop in sales to 14.18 billion hk dollars. however, the board of directors declared a final dividend of 38.6 cents, unchanged from a year earlier.  a strong growth was registered in the firm's value-added services, data and internet products, which represent some 23 percent of its total turnover, and its operating costs were reduced, according to cheung.  "we have made great progress in achieving our e-vision to bring the benefits of our broadband network, the internet and e-commerce to our customers in hongkong," the chief executive said.  "cable and wireless hkt is committed to continue to develop hongkong as the leading e-commerce center for the asia region through substantial investment in advanced technology and services, " cheung added.  cheung commented on the company's future development, saying the combined competition from local and global operators is likely to present further significant challenges for the company, but "we are building on our performance culture to transform and reshape our business and we will continue to be one of the most competitive telecommunications carriers in the world." investors in the hongkong stock market were reportedly startled by the news that cable and wireless hkt posted an interim loss and the hang seng index was pulled down by 41.24 points to close at 13,610.27 friday.  but they said other local telecom companies had made similar write-offs and cable and wireless hkt was merely cleaning the air.

title: intel ceo predicts bright future for china's e-commerce beijing, november
body: craig barrett, president of usbased computer chip giant intel, said today that china is in the position to be a major player in the coming world of e-commerce within the next few years. "in the present economic and technological environment, china could grow into one of the largest on-line market segments in the asia pacific region," said barrett at a two day seminar in china.  he noted that it is crucial for china to invest in information technology and e-business to continue its economic growth in the emerging internet economy.  "a vibrant internet economy across china is the foundation for ongoing economic growth into the new millennium," said barrett, adding that information technology and e-business can act as a driver to transform businesses across all segments of the economy.  he predicted that within the next few years, there will be one billion internet-connected pcs in the world which will generate one trillion us dollars of annual e-commerce revenue. china now has over four million internet-connected users.  but he warned that china is now facing a number of challenges as it moves into a internet economy, such as a backward infrastructure.  calling his meeting with chinese high-level government officials today "constructive", barrett said he is confident on china's future in opening its information technology sector. he added that his company will invest more in china.  "looking at what china has achieved in the past five years to build its telecommunications and computing infrastructure and increasing computer literacy, we can be very optimistic about the coming decade." intel is the world's largest chip maker, and also a leading manufacturer of personal computers, networking and communication products. it began investing in china last year and has since put money into 10 chinese companies and set up 12 offices across the country.

title: procurement of financial services via internet predicted to surge in u.s.
body: a survey released thursday shows that the use of the internet to negotiate certain financial products will increase by as much as 12 times in the unitedstates over the next two years.  the projected growth in the use of the internet to negotiate loans, derivatives and foreign exchange contracts was dramatic, said the association for financial professionals, a unitedstates community of 12,000 individuals presenting a broad spectrum of financial disciplines, which conducted the survey.  according to the survey, while only three percent of the companies currently use the internet to negotiate loans, 36 percent said they would do so within the next two years.  similarly, over the same time period, the percentage of companies that will use the internet for derivatives jumps from two percent to 28 percent and for foreign exchanges from seven percent to 45 percent.  the association surveyed 825 american companies ranging in size from those with less than 250 million unitedstates dollars in total revenues to those with revenues greater than 5 billion dollars.  more than 50 percent of the respondents indicated that if sites were available, they would likely use the internet as a one-stop shop for financial services.  commercial banks continue to play the dominant role in providing services to corporate customers, according to the survey. however, 20 percent of the respondents said that traditional banks will play less of a role in providing services in the future.  the association said that the survey validates its strategic direction of delivering more products and services over the internet. the trend is posing both challenges and opportunities for financial professionals, as their role is evolving and their jobs are increasingly tied to information technology, the association said.

title: worldwide internet economy expected to exceed 1 trln dlrs by
body: the worldwide internet economy, by the measurement of an american market research firm, will surpass the mark of 1 trillion unitedstates dollars in 2001.  by 2003, it will be well on its way to 3 trillion dollars, according to a report released wednesday by international data corporation (idc).  the report breaks the internet economy into three key elements --internet commerce, internet information technology infrastructure and internet business infrastructure --and found that the three are shifting in importance in terms of contributions to the internet economy.  in the early internet economy years, idc said, investments focused around technology products and services to strengthen the infrastructure, achieve critical mass and introduce online users to commerce. now, however, non-technology spending is slowly catching on. the marketing and sales functions, along with content creation, will take a lead role in enhancing the internet experience and stimulating internet commerce.  idc's report found that for every dollar of e-commerce revenue generated in 1998, 93 cents were directly invested in the internet commerce infrastructure. the research firm expects corporations to increase their investments significantly to improve this ratio by 2003.  technology investments accounted for 52 percent of worldwide internet spending last year. but in 1999, for the first time, idc expects non-technology investments to surpass technology investments. by 2003, technology investments' share will have decreased to 39 percent.  "building the infrastructure to support internet commerce is not cheap," said the report. "everyone praises the benefits of internet commerce, but few understand the size of the investment required, and fewer still understand that technology infrastructure is just a part of that investment." idc has been revising its predictions on the worldwide internet economy. in september last year, the firm predicted that the internet economy, totaling 200 billion unitedstates dollars then, would approach 1 trillion dollars by 2002. idc also predicted last year that worldwide internet commerce would top 1 trillion dollars by 2003.  according to a recent study by the university of texas, the internet economy in the unitedstates has pumped an estimated 507 billion dollars into the unitedstates economy over the past year. the study divides the internet economy into four layers: companies that provide networked applications, businesses that build hardware for the basic internet infrastructure, companies that act as so-called intermediaries over the net as web gateways or online travel agents, and internet commerce businesses that sell directly over the net.

title: nortel invests 400 million dollars in optical network
body: canada's high-tech giant nortel networks corp. tuesday announced an investment of 400 million unitedstates dollars to meet rising demand for telecom products for the internet.  "we're moving at web speed to meet the growing customer demand for our market-leading optical internet capabilities," said nortel president john roth.  "it is also about enhancing a source of long-term competitive advantage," he added.  nortel's spending priorities include the building of a new research center in ottawa to produce precision lasers and other optical components.  other projects involve the expansion of facilities and operations in montreal, the second largest city of canada, as well as in major cities of britain, northern ireland and the unitedstates.  the distribution of the investment is 143 million dollars in ottawa, 82 million dollars in montreal, 105 million dollars in britain and 70 million dollars in the unitedstates.  the total investment is expected to create 5,000 jobs, of which 2,300 will be in canada, 1800 in britain and 900 in the unitedstates.  nortel is the largest high-tech company in the country, with a work force of 70,000 around the world. it enjoys a leading position in the development of software and telecom hardware for the internet.  the company's revenues were recorded at 17.6 billion dollars last year.

title: u.s. government bonds being sold online
body: the unitedstates treasury department tuesday launched a new internet site through which americans can buy unitedstates savings bonds anytime they want. for the first time, the savings bond connection web site gives internet users the option of buying savings bonds online from the government. the government hopes to boost bond sales by making it easier for people to buy them. it also hopes the venture will attract new investors, such as those who spend a lot of time in cyberspace, and encourage americans to save more. "it has to be of concern to any observer in the american economy that personal savings are today lower than they have been in half a century," said treasury secretary lawrence summers. "americans have relied on savings bonds for decades as an important tool in their efforts to save for their future," summers said. "by bringing savings bonds as close as your home computer, this program makes it more convenient for millions of americans to add to their savings." approximately 55 million americans own savings bonds worth 185 billion unitedstates dollars. the traditional series ee bonds, which sell for half their face value, will be available in denominations ranging from 50 dollars to 1,000 dollars. series i bonds, which carry a lower interest rate but are adjusted to reflect inflation, will be sold in 50 dollars to 500 dollars in denominations. to buy bonds online, a purchaser goes to www.savingsbonds.gov and clicks on the savings bond connection. online buyers provide information, including name, social security number and mailing address, just as when they purchase bonds from banks and other financial institutions. bonds bought on the internet must be purchased by credit card. for now, only mastercard and visa will be accepted.

title: hsbc launches internet credit card payment services
body: the hongkong and shanghai banking corporation limited began offering over the weekend its internet payment gateway, a senior hsbc official announced monday.  the internet payment service, the first of its kind in hongkong, enables merchant customers in hongkong to accept credit card payments for goods and services over the internet, the official said.  "we believe that the launch of this service will provide a significant boost to the growth of e-commerce in hongkong," said eric tai, hsbc's head of personal banking development in asia.  "the response from our merchant customers has been very encouraging so far and we are confident that both merchants and cardholders will benefit from having a secure means to deal with payments over the internet using the hsbc payment gateway service, " tai said.  a number of major organizations in hongkong have already signed letters of intent and are expected to connect their websites to hsbc's payment gateway in the coming months, tai said.  the system, which has developed in conjunction with compaq computer limited, supports both the secure sockets layer (ssl) and secure electronic transaction (set) security standards and allows hsbc's merchant customers to accept visa, mastercard and jcb payments over the internet in a wide range of currencies, tai said.

title: disruptive changes in u.s. health system predicted over next decade
body: consumerism, e-business and genetic mapping will bring about disruptive changes in the way unitedstates healthcare is provided and paid for in the 21st century, according to a report released thursday.  dynamic forces will threaten the status quo of unitedstates healthcare providers, insurers and the government, but also will create opportunities for improved quality of care, greater efficiencies and e-business, said the report from pricewaterhouse coopers, a world's leading professional services organization. to compile the report the organization interviewed and surveyed 400 thought leaders and healthcare executives in the unitedstates, europe, canada and pacific rim to determine the factors shaping the future of healthcare.  the penetrating impact of the internet will recast the distribution, financing, speed and production of traditional medical products and services as well as create increased competition for capital investment, the report said.  the internet gives the advantage of speed over size and bureaucratic healthcare organizations could fail in this race to smaller, adaptive entrepreneurial ventures, said the report, foreseeing new types of business models such as virtual medical records warehousing or insurance products through the internet.  many of those surveyed thought that by 2010 individuals would store their electronic medical records on a source that is not part of the current healthcare system. others thought the source would be an internet portal site and that individuals would use non-healthcare third-party businesses. another way in which e-business will change the healthcare system is interaction between providers and patients. in-office visits may decrease if physicians routinely offer web-based consulting tools.  with the impact of the internet and increasing levels of education, the report said, consumers in the next decade will understand more about healthcare issues and make more decisions about their own treatments. this knowledge thirst will intensify as out-of-pocket spending (the amount consumers spend on health insurance premiums, deductibles and co-pays) increases in the next few years.  according to the report, the biggest change in the next decade will be the type of screening and diagnostic tests that stem from the completely mapped human genome. in the unitedstates, third-party genetic mapping businesses will spring up and become the primary source for an individual's genetic map.  healthcare financing trends are converging in the industrial world as the unitedstates becomes more governmental and privatization efforts increase in europe and canada, the report said. in addition, increasing costs and consumerism are likely to spur insurance changes. for instance, most unitedstates employers will offer employees the option of medical savings accounts by 2010. also, defined contribution programs, which have been popular among corporate retirement plans, would transition to health benefits.

title: survey says european firms not ready for e-commerce
body: large european companies have recognized the long-term potential of electronic commerce but have not invested sufficient funds to reap the benefits, according to a study published recently by pricewaterhouse, an international consulting firm.  in the title of "competing in the internet age -challenges for incumbents", the study said only four percent of european companies surveyed invest more than 10 percent of their turnover in the development of on-line commerce, while a half of the companies are not involved in electronic commerce and have no plans at present to move into the area.  only 11 percent of the firms questioned have implemented complete internet solutions, and more than a third acknowledge that they lack the necessary expertise to develop an internet strategy. about 26 percent of the companies expressed desire to reach more than 90 percent of their clients via the internet, but only one percent are able to do so, the survey said.  meanwhile, one company in four believes that firms operating on the internet will pose a serious threat to their activities within three years. the majority of the companies surveyed therefore regarded electronic commerce primarily as a defense strategy.  companies trading with other businesses invest less than those serving private clients, the european report, one of the european union publications, quoted the survey as saying.  the survey shows that european companies are lagging well behind their american counterparts, the european report said.  moreover, it reveals that most companies are adopting a defensive stance on the issues of electronic commerce, showing an interest in the internet but failing to maximize its potential.

title: study: u.s. internet economy to top 500 billion this year
body: the booming internet economy has grown 68 percent since last year and is on track to generate 507 billion unitedstates dollars in revenue this years, according to a research report released wednesday.  university of texas researchers based their estimates on the worldwide internet-related sales of unitedstates-based companies. while the internet makes up only a small part of the unitedstates 8-trillion-dollar economy, their study suggests it has surpassed such traditional sectors as automobiles, telecommunications and utilities.  the researchers at the university's graduate school of business compiled their results by observing 3,400 unitedstates companies that generate all or part of their revenues from internet products or services. some of their data was gleaned using reports from research companies, financial reports and the web sites of 350 of the largest firms.  according to the study, the rapid rise was led by electronic commerce --sales made directly over the internet, whose revenues rose 127 percent from 16.5 billion dollars in the first quarter of 1998 to 37.5 billion dollars in the same quarter this year.  the study also found that the internet accounted for 2.3 million jobs in the first quarter of 1999, up from 1.5 million a year earlier.  as defined by the researchers, the internet economy is made up of companies directly generating all or part of their revenues from internet-related products and services, such as cisco systems, dell computer corp. and ibm corp.  the researchers divided the internet into four layers, namely, infrastructure, applications, intermediaries and commerce. they view the interplay of these layers as the internet "ecosystem." the internet economy has a major impact on unitedstates economic growth, the research report said. unitedstates gdp is projected to grow 340 billion dollars in 1999. the projected growth of 200 billion dollars in the internet economy in 1999 plays a significant role in the health of the economy, the report said, although differences between gdp and revenues make a precise comparison difficult.

title: china to further readjust telecommunication fees
body: a high-ranking official from the ministry of information said today that china will further readjust telecommunication fees in the next few years to gradually bring the prices to a reasonable level.  "prices of some business items will be raised while some others will be decreased in the next few years, but the frequency of the readjustment will be higher than before," said zhang xiaotie, vice director of the department of financial adjustment and clearance.  the ministry today released a series of price readjustment items, decreasing the prices for internet access and the rent of electric lines, easing the restriction on renting of digital lines over two megahertz and standardizing the price for installment and relocation of telephones.  according to the new fees, the access fee for internet will be set at four yuan per minute, and the telephone charges for internet use will be cut by half.  for those customers using special lines, the access fee will be cut by 45 percent.  zhang noted that the price readjustment aims to spur the use of telecommunication services and promote the rapid development of the sector. it's the second time the country has cut telecommunication fees this year. the first readjustment was in march.  the new readjustment scheme also reduced the rental rates of analogue electric lines, the digital data lines and digital electric lines by 30 percent.  zhang noted that some of these readjustment items went into effect on october 1, while some others will begin on november 1 and december 1.  he added that the development of new technology in the past years has greatly changed the cost of telecommunication business, so the price changes are inevitable.

title: hk launches digital technology campaign for youth
body: a "digital 21 power for youth " campaign to promote the use of information technology (it) and ecommerce among the youth population was initiated in hongkong thursday.  the campaign, which will run through december 19, consists of a series of it-related activities including "ten outstanding young digi persons selection," the "fedex e-business award," training courses, and seminars.  addressing the launching ceremony, thomas tang, executive director of the hongkong productivity council (hkpc), an organizer of the campaign, highlighted the future trend of ecommerce for business.  "among the 112 million internet users worldwide, more than 12 million are found in asia. the total global electronic transactions in 1998 amounted to 43 billion unitedstates dollars and the figure is estimated to reach 1,000 billion unitedstates dollars by 2002," he noted.  tang said more than half of hongkong internet users are under the age of 30 and it is appropriate to launch this campaign to foster leaders of a new generation.  "with the widespread adoption of the internet, the involvement of young entrepreneurs in e-business will play a pivotal role in shaping hongkong's future economic development," he said.

title: electronic transactions progress in malaysia
body: malaysian electronic payment system (meps) has been effective since its nationwide implementation on march 22, 1999, according to a bank negara official.  payments totaled 8.25 million ringgit (2.171 million unitedstates dollars) through the meps secured electronic transactions (set) payment gateway, bank negara (state bank) assistant governor zamani abdul ghani said here tuesday at the launch of premium-link, the online payment and renewal services for motor insurance.  there are already 170 merchants acquired by four participating banks --maybank, public bank, rhb bank and hong leong bank --in the payment gateway and 3,500 e-wallets (digital certificates) have been issued free to cardholders, he added.  meps has been entrusted to develop a payment gateway based on set, given that the credit card is commonly used for internet purchases, he said, adding that set protocol provides a more promising solution in terms of security as the information pertaining to credit cards will not be transmitted over the network and the identity of the cardholder is based on the digital certificate.  he said that as the set technology is new, the central bank has allowed the use of security socket layer (ssl) protocol to coexist with set to support the development of e-commerce.  he urged the insurance industry to prepare itself for the transition to a new business era as it enters the 21st century, saying, "in malaysia, only about half of the licensed insurers had set up information with non-interactive websites on the internet.  as it is, we still have a long way to go." according to the central bank official, studies in the unitedstates estimated that more than 200 billion dollars' worth of business will be transacted over the internet by the end of next year and there are currently more than 8,000 insurance-related websites.  he said the internet enables insurers to expand their marketing potential in ways previously not possible or economically feasible.  the central bank official said that in promoting e-commerce in malaysia, the government established in 1998 the national electronic commerce committee (necc) to provide strategic governance of e-commerce and set the direction for the development of e-commerce.  one of the objectives of the necc is the formulation of an electronic commerce masterplan for malaysia and this is currently being finalized.

title: u.s. home networking set for major growth
body: about 650,000 unitedstates homes have some form of networking installed and that number is expected to reach 10 million by 2003, according to a report released tuesday.  a networked home is the point of digital convergence and today it means that consumers can access the internet from anywhere in their homes, said the report from the yankee group, a unitedstates information technology research firm. but soon familiar products like telephones, stereos and televisions will take on a whole new life, it added.  the rapid growth of high-speed broadband internet access services will also serve as a critical catalyst to the explosive growth of home networking.  according to yankee group analysts, broadband internet brings with it the need to share access among multiple pcs and to deliver internet and multimedia content to many different devices and locations within the home. this generates instant demand for home networking solutions.  meanwhile, the market and consumers in the unitedstates are ready for the digital home. in fact, according to a yankee group's survey, more than 17 million unitedstates households are already interested in home networking.  of the nearly 10 million homes expected to have networking solutions by 2003, the yankee group predicts that the majority of these will be employing pc-based networking.  more than 4 million pc-based homes will install phone linebased networking over existing wiring, according to the report.  nearly 1.5 million homes will use wireless networking technology, and about 300,000 home will use power line networking that works over existing electrical wiring.

title: five u.s. cities reach 50 percent internet penetration
body: five cities in the unitedstates have reached 50 percent internet penetration among the adult population, a unitedstates local market consumer ratings firm reported monday.  washington d.c. ranks number one with almost 60 percent of the adult population online, followed by francisco, austin, seattle and salt lake city, according to a study by scarborough research.  the firm measured internet usage over a one-year period both at home and at work for these findings. more than 170,000 interviews from adults were conducted in 64 leading unitedstates markets.  the ratings firm said that reaching the 50 percent threshold is a significant milestone for the internet as it continues to mature into a mainstream medium.  meanwhile, the firm added, differences in internet usage on a local market level are noteworthy, indicating that technological innovation is impacted by the interplay of local demographic, cultural, retail and media dynamics. to understand both cause and effect, one must telescope down to the local market --the venue in which consumers live, work, recreate, shop and are informed and entertained.  the overall 64-market average internet penetration is currently 43.7 percent. major cities at or above the average include los angeles, boston, chicago, new york and philadelphia. on the low end for internet usage are smaller cities.

title: china unicom to provide long-distance alternative
body: china unicom is expected to begin offering its long-awaited long-distance phone service both domestically and internationally later this year, business weekly reported today.  "by the end of this year, we will provide long-distance phone services in the country's more than 20 cities, both domestically and internationally," tan xinghui, general manager of planning and marketing with china unicom, said.  the business expansion, if implemented as envisioned, will eventually make china unicom a major force in the telecom services sector.  china unicom is expected to benefit from the split up of the china telecom monopoly into three independent operations including mobile phones, fixed phones and satellite services later this year.  china unicom currently operates paging, mobile phone, internet access, ip (internet protocol) phone and limited local fixed-phone services.  chinese customers will have to remember two sets of regional codes with the new service. they have become used to dialing only one phone code during past decades.  china unicom is authorized to conduct local fixed-phone business in tianjin, chongqing and sichuan only.  "we will mainly rely on china telecom's fixed-phone network to provide long-distance services," said tan.  since china telecom, which controls the fundamental fixed-phone network, is reluctant to co-operate with china unicom, the company has faced great difficulties in developing inter-connections across the country.  tan said china unicom plans to lease part of mobile capacity from china mobile communication corp, the most profitable arm separating from china telecom.  "we are in negotiation and it will benefit the two sides since some of china mobile's network capacity is idle," said tan.  the company's internet business will also begin later this year.  tan said a key plan involves co-operating with internet service and content providers.

title: telecom 99 " interactive 99 attracts about 200,000 visitors
body: telecom 99 " interactive 99 has attracted around 200,000 visitors to palexpo in geneva to see the latest technology and services on display from more than 1,100 exhibitors from the telecommunications, information technology and audio-visual entertainment fields, according to a itu press release here sunday.  telecom 99 " interactive 99, the eighth world telecommunications exhibition and forum, hosted by the international telecommunication union (itu) from 10 to 17 october, was the meeting place for the whole communications society, and was the itu's most successful event ever.  the exhibitors met to do business and discuss the issues that will shape the future path of an industry which is now worth well over 1 trillion dollars unitedstates dollars a year.  telecom 99 " interactive 99, more than any event which preceded it, demonstrated the increasing importance of telecommunications in the modern world. it was attended by visitors that were rated by exhibitors as being of both a higher level and quality than ever seen before.  telecom 99 " interactive 99 itself was different from its predecessors in being fully online. the show information was available to all participants by means of more than 300 telecom information kiosks (tiks) which logged more than a million hits during the first five days of the event. the telecom part of the itu's web site registered more than 10 million hits during the first two weeks of october and much of the press coverage achieved for the event came from users of the web rather than journalists at the show.  the event closed with a weekend dedicated to the internet the world telecom internet days. these two days, open to the general public, reinforced the enormous importance of the internet in the world today and provided a bridge into the new millennium, featuring debates, demonstrations and a chance for people to see the shape of the future.  the world telecommunications exhibition will be held in geneva in october 2003.

title: cct telecom to continue invest in china's mainland
body: the investment environment in china's mainland is becoming better and better, according to clement mak, chairman of cct telecom holdings limited, a hongkongbased integrated information technology services provider.  cct telecom will continue to invest on telecom projects in the mainland as the company's business there has enjoyed a smooth development in the past years, flora cheng, executive director of the company, said on thursday.  cct telecom, originally a manufacturer of telecom products and electronic and plastic components, started its telecom networks business in 1997 by cooperating with china unicom in investing on gsm networks in northern china's shanxi province.  later on, the company took part in china unicom's gsm networks project in shanghai, the biggest city in china.  so far, cct telecom has invested more than 500 million hk dollars (64 million unitedstates dollars) in the gsm networks in china's mainland and the company has begun to make profits from the investment.  the company now has several factories on the mainland to manufacture dual and trio band mobile phones and other telecom products.  at the beginning of 1998, cct telecom began entering hongkong' s internet market by buying hk net. eight months later, hk net ranked 2nd in the share of internet market in hongkong with 160, 000 subscribers.  hk net is a provider of diversified internet services including isp, idd, portal/icp, e-commerce, vpn, security, system integration, web hosting and co-location and web design.  hk net has been recently elected the 4th internet company in asia by telecom asia magazine.  earlier this year, japan's ntt communication corporation bought 49 percent of the shares of hk net, becoming a strategic partner of hk net.  cct telecom is planning to list hk net on the nasdaq stock exchange of the unitedstates at the beginning of next year and the company is now applying for the fixed wireless license and the external gateway license from the government.  cct telecom is making efforts to become a global telecom operator in the future, mak said.

title: worldwide business-to-consumer e-commerce forecast
body: business-to-consumer electronic commerce companies have learned their lessons from past years as the unitedstates model of consumer e-commerce is being implemented on a worldwide basis, according to a report released wednesday.  the worldwide business-to-consumer e-commerce market will reach 31.2 billion unitedstates dollars in 1999, up from 11.2 billion dollars in 1998, said the report from unitedstates market research firm dataquest. in 2003, dataquest predicted, revenue will surpass 380 billion dollars.  "the reduced costs of internet access and the growth of locally based online merchants will drive the birth of large-scale e-tailing throughout the world," the report said. "on a regional basis, the so-called 'brick-and-mortar' businesses outside of the unitedstates have had the advantage of watching consumer e-commerce develop over the last two years and are determined not to repeat the mistakes of real-world retailers who were caught off guard by the e-commerce revolution." as for the unitedstates, dataquest found it is on pace to have business-to-consumer e-commerce in 1999 totaling 20.5 billion dollars, and by 2003, reaching 147 billion dollars. the european business-consumer e-commerce market is projected to grow from 5.4 billion dollars in 1999 to more than 115 billion dollars in 2003.  according to the report, the advent of free internet accounts is dramatically increasing the number of internet users in europe.  relatively high penetration of smart cards, digital wallets and other secure payment methods is reducing security concerns.  consumer e-commerce in europe is promoted by the increased development of home-grown solutions, utilizing local currencies, languages and distribution channels. customers in other regions of the world no longer have to order from e-tailers based in the unitedstates, the report said.  meanwhile, the number of business-to-business transactions over the internet has also grown steadily. unitedstates market research firm forrester research recently predicted that the global market will explode to 1.3 trillion dollars by 2003.

title: hk to pick up speed to boost e-frastructure
body: hongkong plans to speed up the development of the internet-based infrastructure in a move to enhance its competitiveness as an international financial center, a report released tuesday showed.  the report, released by the securities and futures commission ( sfc), recommends that to keep the leading position of hongkong as an international financial center in terms of risk mitigation, increased efficiency and cost reduction, hongkong should put together an "e-frastructure." the e-frastructure will facilitate the development of e-trading in securities and derivatives in hongkong and the asia region, sfc chairman andrew sheng told a press briefing.  sheng said that the e-frastructure is a web-friendly technology infrastructure for the securities and derivatives industry that allows local and global market participants to access the full spectrum of financial products and services on an open, robust, secure, scalable, and high performance network.  "with implementation of the e-frastructure, hongkong can aspire to become one of the leading centers for liquidity, clearing, settlement and risk management in asia and the portal for strategic links with global markets in the region," sheng said.  the e-frastructure includes the components of a single clearing arrangement for better risk management, end-to-end straight through processing for improved cost-effectiveness, a scripless securities market for enhanced efficiency and legal certainty, and an open, robust, current and scalable technology structure for local and remote connectivity and high performance.  "hongkong already has the best telecommunications infrastructure to enable the development of e-commerce and etrading," added sheng, who also chairs the steering committee on the enhancement of the financial infrastructure (scefi) in hongkong.  the scefi report has been submitted to financial secretary donald tsang yam-kuen, proposing an array of measures to facilitate and accelerate the implementation of the e-frastructure.

title: most canadian schools reported to have internet access
body: nine out of 10 elementary, intermediate and secondary schools in canada have internet access while students are still in great need of computers, software and well trained teachers, canadian media reported tuesday.  in prince edward island and new brunswick, all schools are connected to the internet while, on average, about one third of elementary and intermediate students and half of all secondary students are using email.  computers are more available to students in higher grades with an average of one computer for seven students at the secondary level, one for eight at the intermediate level and one for nine at the elementary level, the report said.  mathematics is most likely to be a subject being taught by means of instructional software, the report said, adding about 87 percent of elementary pupils are learning their math through such software.  by contrast, about 64 percent of students use software for geography and 56 percent use it for primary language instruction.  despite the major strides in bringing their students online, the report said, schools are going short of computers, software and well trained teachers.  most principals said they need more computers and more time for teachers to prepare computer and internet courses.  teachers are also in need of training to upgrade their computer knowledge and skills, the report said.

title: ibm, nokia to popularize e-commerce over wireless devices
body: unitedstates computer giant ibm and finnish nokia, the world's biggest cell phone maker, monday reached an agreement on popularizing e-commerce over wireless devices connected to the internet.  the two companies would work together to develop enterprise wireless application protocol (wap) solutions that would allow customers to extend their e-businesses beyond the personal computer to a variety of mobile devices.  wap is a new communication standard that allows wireless phones to connect directly to the internet. the technology is designed to try to shrink internet pages to fit on a handset screen. nokia described the technology as "having the internet in your pocket." "no longer must people be tethered to a pc to access the internet," nokia said, "with a wap-enabled mobile device, people will have a simpler, easier and more flexible way to access the internet." mark bregman, general manager of ibm's pervasive computing division, said in a statement that wap is the key ingredient that will enable a mobile phone instead of a pc to access information and services on the internet. "combining nokia's leadership in the wireless space with our expertise in the enterprise, ibm will be able to quickly provide an expanded range of compelling data offerings for the mobile internet," he said.  under the terms of the agreement, ibm will market and distribute the nokia wap server software on its pc servers and license nokia core wap technology for integration with other ibm server platforms.  the alliance between ibm and nokia comes at a time when on-line players are battling to bring their services to wireless devices such as cell phones. last week, amazon said its customers will be able to purchase items from any of its on-line stores using 3com's new palm vii handheld wireless device.

title: u.n. sets internet code for palestinian state
body: the united nations has designated "ps" as the international code on the internet for palestine, signifying "palestinian state". from now on all the palestinian internet code address will end with "ps", the al ayam newspaper here reported monday.  the u.n. has notified the palestinian national authority (pna) of this decision by the weekend, said the report.  the paper quoted palestinian minister of planning and international cooperation nabil sha'ath as saying that he had earlier supported the international telephone and postal codes, which were considered as symbols for national independence.  meanwhile, ghassan al qadah, director of the government computer system, told the newspaper that the internet code "ps" was a symbol of independence. it is the outcome of two years of relentless efforts.  palestinian leader yasser arafat refused an internet code of "wg" in reference to the west bank and gaza last year. after intensive efforts made by its representatives at the u.n., palestine succeeded in obtaining "ps" as its code, said the official.  the u.n. department of economic and statistics which is in charge of the codes prepares a list called the "unified symbols for countries and regions for statistical purposes." the code for palestine is on the list.

title: orange provides wap services for telecom
body: british mobile phone company orange has provided a range of multimedia services using wireless application protocol (wap) for visitors to the weeklong 1999 world telecommunications exhibition, telecom 99.  "whatever questions you may have about exhibitions, events, breaking news or hospitality at telecom 99, there is one simple answer: ask orange," said orange's chief operations officer colin tucker here sunday.  he said that orange will provide visitors to telecom 99 with access to the best information that is currently available on the internet, adding that "this new technology represents the next important step in the evolution of electronic content, and orange believes that it will bring about a sea change in the way people use their orange phones".  orange, one of the world's most advanced and fastest-growing mobile phone companies, intends to be one of the first european networks to launch a comprehensive range of multimedia services, according to tucker.
