"these services are designed to be simple, easy to use and tailored to the individual's needs and are just the tip of the iceberg of the opportunities that wap will enable," tucker explained. "in each of the countries that orange has operations it intends to launch such multimedia services."

title: u.s. computing technology companies to cooperate with shanghai
body: video serving and multimedia access technology from three unitedstates companies have been selected for a shanghai online project, according to a report released sunday.  silicon graphics inc. (sgi), a mountain view, california-based producer of visual computing system, said that shanghai post telecommunications administration has selected its technology and those from oracle corporation and viagate technologies for the shanghai online ii broadband network.  according to sgi, shanghai online ii is expected to offer residential and business customers broadband multimedia services including high-speed internet connections, voice services, video-on-demand and interactive gaming. the project will help address the growing need for enhanced internet services in the shanghai metropolitan area and also will lay out the infrastructure for future communications development.  a broadband network is ideal for these new services, sgi said, and with scalable server technology, shanghai online can expand their service and capacity as their subscribers base grows.  having deployed a fiber network through its metropolitan area, shanghai is expending fiber both to the building and the neighborhood. the initial trial phase of the shanghai online ii project involved 100 users who had access to mpeg-2 video content, according to sgi. mpeg (moving pictures experts group) is a standard for compression video. using 4 to 16 megabits per second, mpeg-2, used in dvd movies, is a broadcast-quality standard that provides better resolution than vhs tapes.

title: learn to survive under pressure, says sohu ceo
body: learning to survive and take life easy under pressure is the key to success, zhang chaoyang, founder of internet technologies china (itc), told the audience attending the forum on founding and investing in high-technology.  the forum is part of the on-going china high-tech fair in shenzhen in south china's guangdong province.  when founding a high-tech company, zhang warned that it is necessary to have one's own ideas and stick with those ideas, and not to be swayed by other people's thoughts. he said that a downto-earth manner and concentration and energy every step of the way also spells success.  "otherwise, you will end up nowhere," he said.  itc, a leading firm offering online information in the chinese language, successfully introduced venture capital from companies including intel, and created sohu.com, a tool for online information searches in chinese opened in 1998.  up to now, well over 100,000 people have accessed this site.  three years ago, zhang felt the happiness of success after traveling for half a year and securing the capital to start his own company.  "looking back, i find that was just a beginning, the road ahead is still a long journey," he said.  zhang also told potential high-tech business founders to be prepared for the pressures of being short of funds, as it is not easy for high-tech businesses to obtain venture capital.  on the other hand, china only recently introduced a market economy, and this has posed a great number of difficulties for the growth of high-tech companies, zhang noted.  "but being accepted by investors does not mean being accepted by the market, so high-tech companies can only struggle to the top through fierce market competitions," said the sohu ceo.  he believes that the competitiveness of an enterprise comes from innovations and the pursuit of changes.  it is necessary for entrepreneurs to learn to put forward countermeasures against market changes, and to initiate them rapidly.  "only by grasping internationalization and localization in a balanced way can a high-tech enterprise survive," said zhang, adding that credibility is the most important factor for an enterprise's success.  the sohu ceo also said it is important for high-tech founders to have a sound mental attitude, because glory and destruction may come together, and right decisions and errors can be committed every day.  china high-tech fair is jointly sponsored by the ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation, the ministry of science and technology, the ministry of information industry, the chinese academy of sciences and the shenzhen municipal government. the fair will close tomorrow.

title: netaid shows internet as engine for development, u.n. says
body: the united nations is teaming up with the private sector in an "historic partnership" to launch an internet project involving the public directly in the fight to eradicate poverty, a senior u.n. official said here friday. the project, known as netaid, "will demonstrate that the internet can act as an engine for development," zephirin diabre, associate director of the u.n. development program (undp), made the statement at a news conference. netaid will be launched saturday at three star-studded concerts to be held simultaneously in new jersey, london and geneva and carried live on television, radio and the internet, the main electronic medium in the wake of the rapid development of today's information technology. the web site was created by cisco systems, the giant internet networking company, and its technology partners, and will be managed by the undp. by logging onto "www.netaid.org," people can go on "their own cyber journey of discovery" and find out ways to help eradicate poverty and contribute to other humanitarian causes, diabre said, adding that the site, currently the world's largest, is designed to take 60 million hits an hour during the three concerts.

title: shopping boom on internet in new zealand predicted
body: online shopping is till in its infancy in new zealand, but pundits predict it will boom in the future, with the float of the first internet shopping company in the wings.  local media thursday quoted idc, a technology research company in new zealand, as believing that internet commerce is developing quickly in the country, with spending expected to leap from 19 million nz dollars (about nine million unitedstates dollars) in 1997 to more than 200 million (104 million unitedstates dollars) by the end of this year.  it is reported that entrepreneurs eric watson and craig heatley, both are based in auckland, the largest city in new zealand, are looking to cash in on the go-ahead sector by setting up a joint internet shopping company to be floated on the new zealand stock exchange.  idc research manager pat pilcher was quoted as saying "it is early days yet in terms of internet shopping, however we are very bullish about it. we do expect some significant growth to happen." internet use in new zealand with a population of about 3.8 million is regarded as high, with idc's latest survey showing that 315,020 new zealanders have internet subscriber accounts at the end of last year.  the number of retailers offering online shopping on telecom's internet shopping service, xshop, keeps on rising, with 90 stores now trading and another 30 in development.

title: hk to hold asia's largest internet conference
body: internet world asia h hongkong'99 will present asia's largest internet conference and exhibition at the hongkong convention and exhibition center from november 3 to 5, organizers announced here wednesday.  as part of the internet world asia h hongkong'99, the conference assembles the premier, cutting-edge leaders of the internet industry from around the world to deliver thoughtprovoking discussions and analysis on all aspects of the on-line world. the luminaries will detail the best strategies from north america, asia and europe to help companies succeed in using the latest internet technologies and business strategies.  internet world asia h hongkong'99 keynotes feature top internet executives, including alan meckler, joann patrick-ezzell, gm o'connell and others.  in addition, the three-day conference program features six indepth industry-specific vertical tracks covering more than 60 sessions. businesses can discover the latest developments at web development forum, preview cool new internet devices and applications during the enterprise internet technology symposium, learn the secrets to measurable advertising results in the asian internet advertising forum, or network with other business leaders in the asian e-business summit and internet financial services forum.  start-up companies and venture capitalists alike will be interested in the special internet investment forum. in addition, new launch-pad east features the hottest asian start-ups, each less than 18 months out of the gate. more than 50 luminaries will meet in the conference, exchanging views and experiences in the interactive presentations and discussion sessions.  in face of the changing market environment, internet applications play a crucial role in business advancement, implying that those who are able to keep in line with the digital economy are winning the battle in advance. this world-class conference delivers discussion and answers on essential issues regarding internet application and its impact and role in enhancing specified industry business.  "this will be the largest conference we have held in asia --a testament to the growing importance of the internet across all industries in the region," noted michael westcott, penton media's managing director in the asia pacific region. "it is the only conference in hongkong which strives to bring it, business, and investment all under one roof," he said.

title: yahoo's profits surge in july-september
body: internet media giant yahoo inc. reported a third-quarter profit wednesday that easily beat wall street estimates. traffic running through its network of web sites increased 24 percent.  for the three months ending september 30, the california-based santa clara reported an operating income of 40.41 million dollars, compared to 6.92 million dollars for the same period a year ago.  revenue climbed 134 percent to 155.1 million dollars against its previous year's results.  analysts were surprised at the success of yahoo's performance in the third-quarter, which is typically a slow period in anticipation of the holiday season.  yahoo, the no.1 web portal and considered by many analysts a bellwether of the rest of the sector, averaged 385 million page views a day in september, up 24 percent from the average of 310 million page views in june.  web portals try to leverage strong traffic growth to lure more advertisers. gary valenzuela, yahoo's chief financial officer, said the number of advertisers on the company's sites grew to 3, 150 from 2,800 in the second quarter.  "our advertisers keep coming back and spending more money with us," said tim koogle, yahoo's chairman and chief executive officer.  during the third quarter, yahoo's advertiser and merchant partner base expanded to 3,150 clients from about 2,700 in the second quarter, according to yahoo officials.

title: pc magazine names 100 most influential companies in u.s. technology industry
body: microsoft was ranked as number one among the "100 most influential companies" for the third consecutive year by pc magazine in its 1999 analysis of the unitedstates technology industry.  america's leading technology magazine said tuesday that for the ratings, its editors considered such factors as revenues, market share, profitability, products performance and subjective assessments.  on the 10 top-ranked list following microsoft are america online, intel, ibm, cisco systems, amazon.com, yahoo, oracle, dell and hewlett-packard.  speaking on the months-long process of developing the list, the magazine quoted its editor-in-chief michael miller as saying that the huge impact that big internet firms are having on the technology industry played a large role.  success in this new era will come to those companies that are the most effective at producing the hardware, software and networking infrastructure products and services that get people online at work and at home and enable them to be productive in both environments, the magazine said.  "survival of the fittest hinges on a company's ability to adapt to the internet, not an ability to withstand it," miller said.  commenting on microsoft as number one, the magazine said that it continues to set the agenda for personal computing. the company, which dominates in operating systems and office applications, has been a strong competitor in providing internet service or internet content.  would microsoft's influence go down some day? the magazine quoted miller as saying: "it seems to me the things that pose the great threats to microsoft's influence are the rise of the internet as an application platform, the development of many 'appliances' that perform specific functions without the need of windows or microsoft applications, and any restrictions or changes in the company's business practices that come out of the department of justice antitrust case."

title: aol launches its first hong kong service
body: internet provider america online, inc. (aol) announced tuesday that it had joined with china.  com corporation, and its affiliate china internet corporation (cic) to launch aol hongkong, the newest member of the aol global community.  the aol hongkong service, the first chinese language aol service, connects hongkong consumers to aol's global community of more than 18 million members for the first time, said judy lau, managing director of the aol hongkong service.  as hongkong's only full-service online provider, aol hongkong will offer the easiest, most convenient and enjoyable online experience available with unique local content, features and services and state-of-the-art communications tools in addition to simplified access to the internet, aol said in a statement announcing the launch of the service.  "our goal in hongkong --as around the world --is to help make the interactive medium a central and valuable part of people' s lives," said steve case, aol chairman.  "at the same time, aol is delighted to join with our partners, china internet corp. and china.com corp., in helping fuel hongkong's development as a key internet hub in asia," he said.  jackie davies, president of aol international, said that hongkong, with its combination of high penetration of home computers, rapid growth in internet usage and tradition of quickly adopting new technology, is a very attractive market for aol.  "we are committed to helping advance the interactive medium here and across the asia-pacific region," davies added.  the number of internet users in hongkong, with a total population of 6.8 million, has surpassed the one million mark, and is continuing to grow, according to government officials.  peter yip, chief executive officer of china.com corporation, the leading pan-asia integrated internet service company, said: " we are particularly pleased to be partnering with aol since we both strive to embrace local culture, language and interest in the content and services that we provide." hongkong has always been about an unparalleled blend of " global" and "local" --it is one of the world's most cosmopolitan cities, yip said.  "our partnership will be instrumental in furthering hongkong's competitiveness as we move into a rapidly maturing internet and ecommerce-based society," he added.

title: china considers readjusting telecommunications fees
body: china is planning to readjust its telecommunications fees to conform with the international price situation, said wu jichuan, minister of information industry here today.  wu told xinhua that compared with nearby countries, china's local telephone calls and mobile phone calls are less expensive, but internet service providers (isp) and the cost of international phone calls are both more expensive.  "the fees adjustment will bring down the income of the telecommunications industry in the short period, but with the increase of users, the sector stands to win in the long-term," he said.  china lowered the its isp charges and telephone installation fees in march, resulting in an income decrease of 12.5 billion yuan to the telecommunications industry, but the number of internet users and telephone users has increased significantly.  the minister said that china's information industry will gradually focus on the development of micro-electronics, software, information infrastructure construction, and market construction, because at present china supplies itself with less than 20 percent of its micro-electronics products.  the chinese electronics industry ranks fifth in the world in terms of production scale. in 1998, china produced 2.9 million computers, 8.6 million mobile phones, and 36 million color tv sets.

title: boeing to provide maintenance documents via web
body: the boeing company began a pilot program monday to provide direct access to airplane maintenance documents over the world wide web.  access to these documents will require only a personal computer, standard internet connection, web browser and boeing password account, the company said. customers no longer will need lengthy user training, special software or costly equipment.  in 1995, boeing was the first airplane maker to provide online access to digitized maintenance information from a central database. that service, known today as boeing on-line delivery (bold), is based on an older software standard called "x-windows." it required customers to be trained on the use of custom search and retrieval software and to purchase specialized computing software and network connections.  by taking advantage of web browser technology and newer software standards, boeing has now repackaged bold for use on the web. the company's ultimate goal is for its customers to obtain all the information they need to operate and maintain their boeing fleets through a single network connection.  initially, web access is limited to the current 95 bold customers in a pilot program that runs until next spring. these customers may use the web to access service bulletins, maintenance tips, configuration change data, in-service fleet reports and other documents, the company said.  as the system evolves, web access will be expanded to include detailed technical drawings, all major maintenance manuals, product standards and other information. the web-based bold system will also accommodate more features, including self-paced training programs and email communication between the customer and boeing.  by next spring, at the conclusion of the pilot program, boeing will designate the web-based bold as the standard offering and making it available to all customers worldwide.  boeing said a key benefit of going online is that customers eliminate the need to distribute, store, file and retrieve huge quantities of paper and microfilmed documents. in addition, the bold database is updated daily, providing customers with the latest, most accurate information for airplane maintenance, repair and operations.

title: citibank introduces new internet services in hk
body: citibank hongkong today announced the launch of the second generation of its internet financial services, which will make on-line investing easier and more convenient.  the internet securities services, introduced by citibank for the first time in the asia-pacific region, will offer users online stock trading access with very low brokerage charges.  the key feature of the services, namely "power trader," allows customers to easily visualize their transactions by viewing the securities and settlement account status on one screen while simultaneously checking stock prices and placing up to five stock trading orders.  another important feature is the "stock watch" service which permits customers to preset stock watching service delivered by email. when a specific stock reaches the preset price, an email notification will be sent to the customer.  in addition, citibank also offers on-line financial services including credit card access, utility bill payment and mutual fund inquiry.  william lo, ceo of citibank global consumer banking for hongkong, said internet financial services have gained increasing popularity and acceptance as a remote banking channel since it was first launched last november.  "currently, eight percent of our banking transactions are conducted on the internet while only 21 percent of them are carried out at branches," lo said. "this clearly shows the growing importance of remote channels compared with conventional banking methods."

title: entertainment giants eye china market
body: sumner redstone, chairman and chief executive officer of the unitedstates entertainment company viacom, said here today that asia, particularly china, has become the area that multinational mass communications companies are highly focused on.  he is here to attend the '99 fortune global forum that the timewarner group's fortune magazine sponsored.  he told a press conference here this afternoon that over the next decade, the number of households receive multichannel programs will boom and triple the advertisement sales of tv stations in the area. he said that since asia has two billion people under the age of 35, the area will yield fantastic payoff for international entertainment companies entering the market.  viacom's mtv channel has already reached 40 million households in china. redstone said that the company will launch a music website dedicated exclusively to chinese speaking music fans.  in the meantime, the world's major mass communications company news corporation set up its first resident representative office in china. it has set up a website jointly with one of china's largest national newspaper people's daily.  laurie smith, chief representative of the news corporation resident in china, said that all major international mass communications companies are actively looking for opportunities to set up partnership with chinese media and entertainment business through various means.  walter disney, 20th century fox under the news corporation and paramount under viacom sold ten hit motion pictures to china every year.

title: information technology boosts china's education
body: the fast-growing information technology has dramatically pushed china's education development forward, which brought about profound transformation in the country's education cause, said chen zhili, china's minister of education at the '99 fortune global forum here today.  addressing the fortune information technology roundtable, chen said that with popularization of information technology, china has established a large group of radio and tv universities, education tv stations and centers, and established three satellite educational channels as well as more than 16,000 ground receivers.  educational and multimedia software are widely used in teaching as well, said the minister, adding that the chinese education and research network (cernet) has so far connected with over 400 universities, and more than 300,000 network users are on line each day.  chen said that information technology has provided technical support for the country's distance-learning program. through radio, satellite tv and the internet, china has trained an army of teachers, and effectively transmitted education courses to islands and plateaux as well as mountainous regions at lower costs.  moreover, multimedia and network technology has already caused major changes in the thinking, philosophy, model, methods and strategies in the country's education development, said the minister.  edward s. tian, president and chief executive officer of the china netcom corporation, also expressed his views at today's fortune information technology roundtable, saying that china will become a wired country and an on-line nation by the year 2003.  he noted that by 2003, there will have had 80 to 100 million people using computerized information terminals or appliances in china. among them there will be 20 million mobile internet subscribers, 10 million broadband interactive users. china will by that time have at least five to eight nationwide high speed ip/wdm backbones in place, and on-line education will become one of the basic applications, tian added.

title: world it giants focus on china market
body: dozens of world information technology (it) giants, experts and chinese ministers gathered here today to discuss the future of it development in china by the 2003 at the first roundtable meeting of the '99 fortune global forum.  zhu lilan, chinese minister of science and technology, said china will promote the use of high technology in industries, agriculture and pollution control and accelerate the industrialization of high technology. china will also apply computerized farming in more rural areas to help farmers garner more income from farm production.  she said china will foster partnerships among production, education and research organizations.  lu yongxiang, president of the chinese academy of sciences, predicted that china is expected to become the most important it market that witnesses fastest development. by 2003, he said, the number of computers possessed in china will be close to 40 million, including 37 million internet users.  lu believed that the development of the it industry will spur china's modernization drive. painting a rosy picture for china's it market, wu jichuan, minister of information industry, said the mobile phone users will increase from the present 36 million to 100 million by 2003. he said china is also expected to have about 20 million internet users, up from four million at present. jorma ollila, chairman of the board of nokia corporation said the world of telecommunications continues to move towards wireless technologies, which will ultimately provide users with mobile access to all types of media and information through a number of portable solutions, including media phones and portable computers.  nicholas negroponte, co-founder and director of mit media lab, massachusetts institute of technology, said because of a combination of technology and culture: within the next 20 years, the most widely-spoken language on the internet will be chinese, and china will have the most advanced and digital educational system..  nearly 40 chairpersons and ceos of the world it giants, economic experts and chinese ministers delivered brief speeches at the roundtable meeting.

title: yahoo launches new website: yahoo china
body: yahoo inc. of the unitedstates announced here today that it has launched yahoo china ( http://www.yahoo.com.cn), an internet guide designed specifically for web users in china. yahoo china is the 20th world property in yahoo's comprehensive global network, offering news, finance and weather information relevant to the region in a total of 20,000 chinese web sites. yahoo china features a directory of web sites in the simplified chinese characters organized by a team of web surfers into 14 easy-to-use categories like government and politics, arts and culture, social science, news and media and business and economy. at the press conference held here today, the co-founder and chief jerry yang said that yahoo china provides relevant online programming and services in the local language to this growing web community and to others around the world with a special interest in china. "with yahoo china, we're able to give internet users in china easy access to a range of yahoo's popular services tailored to meet the needs of this audience," said heather killen, vice president, international at yahoo. yahoo inc. is a global internet media company that offers a branded network of comprehensive information, communication and shopping services to 80 million users worldwide. according to china's ministry of information industry, china will have approximately 4.5 million internet users by the end of 1999. this number is to grow to around 9.4 million by the year 2002. in another development, yahoo inc. and beijing founder electronics co. ltd., a wholly-owned subsidiary of founder (hongkong) limited, today announced that they have signed a letter of agreement to create a joint venture to establish and develop yahoo china. under the agreement, yahoo and founder will work together to promote yahoo china. in addition, the companies will jointly develop internet technology and applications.

title: holiday online sales in u.s. expected to double this year
body: online sales in the unitedstates are expected to double this holiday season, according to a new research report released this week by leading internet research firm jupiter communications.  e-commerce sales in november and december could reach 6 billion unitedstates dollars, up from an estimated 3.1 billion dollars spent during the same period in 1998. jupiter expects online shopping to grow to 78 billion dollars by 2003.  jupiter also expects that 10 million online users in the unitedstates will begin shopping in 1999 and many will make their first purchases during the holiday season.  but jupiter researchers warned that e-tailers will have to deal with issues, such as site failures, inadequate customer service and poor order fulfillment, if they want to stay in the game.  one area that sites should address is performance. jupiter expects traffic volume to grow enormously at leading retail sites this holiday season, jumping from an average 15,000 transactions per day between january and october to 58,000 transactions per day during the winter holidays.  another unitedstates research firm, forrester researcher, predicted this week that online retail sales in north america will be worth 184 billion unitedstates dollars by 2004. further, the internet will influence another 500 billion dollars worth of goods purchased offline.

title: ford, microsoft form venture to create online build-to-order cars
body: ford motor co. and microsoft corp. on monday unveiled a joint venture that will enable the unitedstates automaker to build cars according to online orders and will advance microsoft's efforts to enlist industry partners in its internet endeavors.  at a press conference in san francisco, the two companies also announced a simpler way for consumers to design and order cars.  the alliance between the two companies underscores how ecommerce is challenging traditional ways of doing business and pushing the high-tech and manufacturing industries closer together.  traditionally automakers have competed against each other with new cars and trucks and manufacturing efficiency. now they are seeking technology allies to revamp their distribution systems, cut costs and inventory, and gain the broadest access to internet car consumers and information about them.  under the alliance, ford will be microsoft's lead partner in carpoint, an auto sales web site launched in 1996 offering users complete car-buying and car-care information on all makes and models. now the web site will feature an online build-to-order system that links internet car-ordering services to the back-end systems of an automotive manufacturer.  for ford, the deal represents the next phase of its "e-tailing" strategies that include its dealers and its numerous web site ventures. under the arrangement, ford will have access to reams of data about how shoppers search for cars online.  ford is the world's largest producer of trucks and the second largest producer of cars and trucks combined, marketing and selling about seven million vehicles globally through its seven brands last year.

title: hk poised to ride on e-commerce wave hong kong, september
body: a senior government official monday called for more efforts to encourage government institutions and private sectors to widely adopt e-commerce.  k c kwong, secretary for information technology and broadcasting, said the government should take the lead in the establishment of the public key infrastructure for a wide use of ecommerce.  kwong made the remarks at the opening of the e-services world ' 99 conference and exhibition, which is being held here on monday.  to encourage the wider adoption of electronic commerce by local businesses, the local government will become a leading participant in it through the launching of the electronic service delivery ( esd) scheme, he said, adding that esd will act as a catalyst to pump-prime the development of electronic commerce in the private sector.  "we will also strengthen public confidence in electronic commerce by establishing a local public key infrastructure through the hongkong post," kwong said.  hongkong post's key and certification services will be available by the end of the year, but it will not be given exclusivity in the provision of such services, he said.  "to strengthen the legal certainty of electronic transactions, we have introduced recently an electronic transactions bill into the legislative council," kwong said.  the bill is intended to give electronic records and digital signatures the same legal status as that of their paper-based counterparts, and to seek to establish a clear framework to support the operation of certification authorities in hongkong, according to kwong.  "through these initiatives, we seek to create a favorable environment for electronic commerce to take hold and flourish in hongkong," he said. in hongkong, the number of internet users has surpassed the one million mark and is continuing to grow. in the past 12 months, the volume of internet traffic in and through hongkong has almost doubled and the number of internet users making purchases online has increased by 50 percent, kwong said.  industry estimates suggest that the total value of products and services transacted over the internet in hongkong will increase from 60 million unitedstates dollars in 1998 to 2.4 billion unitedstates dollars by 2003, indicating that hongkong is poised to ride on the electronic commerce wave, kwong said.  he also said that with the increasingly close ties between china's mainland and hongkong, and the affinity on the basis of a common language and culture between the two places, businesses in hongkong should be well positioned to capitalize on the opportunities in the mainland by taking advantage of the development of electronic commerce there.

title: telecom sector to lower prices
body: bowing to consumer's everlouder complaints about high charges, the telecommunications administration is set to initiate another package of price cuts for internet access and phone communications later this year.  today's business weekly says that though zhang cunjiang, director general of the telecommunications administration bureau, did not venture any details, he indicated internet fees will be cut significantly from the present level, four yuan (0.48 unitedstates dollars) per hour.  the price reduction in march in the telecom sector immediately resulted in a consumption spree in the telecom sector, with the number of fixed-line users soared by 14.06 million to over 100 million in the first eight months, and that of internet users from 2.1 million at the end of last year to 4 million by june.  however, the statistics from the ministry of information industry show that the telecom revenue will be reduced by some 8 billion yuan this year due to the readjustments.  while, the ministry has up to now not met the demands of consumers who were hoping that the phone installation fee and the two-way charge system for cellular phones would be abolished.  "telecom service charges must be slashed so consumers can benefit from the application of advanced technologies and products, " said an expert from the china academy of telecommunications technology.  the telecom sector's current charge structure for mobile phones is under pressure from customers and the country's two telecom operators, china telecom and china unicom.  and in order to expand market share and attract new customers, the two have breached the government-set price limits in local markets by lowering network access and phone call charges significantly, said an official with the price control department of the state development planning commission.

title: third telecom operator set
body: china's third governmentbacked telecom operator, the china netcom corp (cnc) is to be set up in the middle of next month to complement established china telecom and china unicom, said today's business weekly.  edward tian, cnc chief executive officer, said the four investors of the company the chinese academy of sciences, the state administration of radio, films, and television, the ministry of railways, and shanghai municipal government will each hold 25 percent of the stake, with the registered capital being 120 million yuan (14.46 million unitedstates dollars).  the company will mainly deal in two businesses, the internet protocol (ip) backbone services, and international integrated data service targeted at multinationals and large businesses in china.  he disclosed that they plan to establish one of the world's fastest optical fiber networks covering 15 chinese cities. and the network, which is to offer an ip backbone network service in the third quarter of next year, will be the world's first ip-based optical fiber commercial network with a bandwidth of 20 gigabitsthe largest to date in the world. cnc's first step after its establishment will be to sell ip phone cards. cnc will provide network access and carrier-tocarrier services for china's internet service providers and large companies, tian said, adding that they are a backbone wholesaler.  the chinese academy of sciences, in a report submitted to the state council, said "the world's internet traffic has been doubling every six months in the past few years and is expected to surpass voice communications next year. many new technologies and applications, including ip technology, are posing a great challenge to the traditional telecommunications industry." while many compare cnc with the two existing telecom companies, and nickname it as "china telecom iii", tian debated that "we are not the third. the two expect to be present in many, if not all, areas. but we are a very focused company; our core competence is based on ip technology and the ip-based backbone." and another big difference is that the cnc operates more like a market-oriented firm.

title: internet engineers crisis looming for europe: report
body: europe will face an internet engineering skills crisis early next century unless more young people undergo training, warned a new report by the international data corporation (idc).  the report predicted that by 2002, europe will see a shortfall of almost 600,000 individuals possessing the fundamental skills to design, build and manage the networks that are the bedrock of almost every business and government worldwide.  it said that the situation will only worsen unless actions are taken by european countries to train young people as engineers to keep pace with the explosive growth of the internet.  among european countries, germany is predicted to suffer the most of the engineers crisis with a 31.7 percent shortfall by 2002, the uk ranked second with a 13.8 percent shortage, which is followed by france, italy and the netherlands.  although business has been discussing the skills shortage for some time, experts said that it is not until now with the explosive use of the internet that europe is facing a new crisis in terms of a networking skills shortage.  however, for people willing to learn, the shortage is offering unprecedented career opportunities, the idc report said.

title: wipo sees two intellectual property treaties to enter force by
body: the head of the world intellectual property organization (wipo) thursday expressed the hope that two wipo treaties signed in december 1996 would enter into force before december 2001.  speaking here at the end of the three-day international conference on e-commerce and intellectual property, wipo director-general kamil idris also asked state parties to the wipo performances and phonograms treaty (wppt) to extend its principles to audiovisual works and performances as a step to the adjustment of the international legislative framework to facilitate e-commerce.  the other treaty signed in 1996 is the wipo copyright treaty (wct).  the two treaties establish the basic standards of protection for copyright and related rights on the internet and other digital networks, according to the wipo. they contain a general update of the legal principles underpinning international protection of copyright and the rights of performers and phonogram producers in cyberspace, more particularly on the internet.  in addition, the wipo internet treaties adopted in december 1996 clarify that national law must prevent unauthorized access to and use of creative works which, given the global reach of the internet, may be downloaded anywhere in the world at the push of a button.  up to now, only nine and seven countries respectively signed the two treaties. at least 30 states must adhere to each of the treaties before they enter into force.

title: china's national day parade to go live on web
body: internet audience across the world can view the grand parade in celebration of the 50th anniversary of the founding of the people's republic of china on the world wide web in real time thanks to the launch of the web site of china 10k.com.  the parade to be held in beijing on china's national day ( october 1) will be broadcast live to a vast audience of academics, well-wishers and overseas chinese via the interactive multimedia web site.  china 10k.com is the only web site outside china's mainland that has been authorized by china international tv corporation to webcast the national day celebration.  to make the webcast possible, china 10k.com is working with technology partners including hongkong-based asia on-line ltd., microsoft hongkong ltd. and tiger information systems.  in advance of the webcast, china 10k.com has set an on-line " museum" displaying a wide range of china's national treasures.  china 10k.com is the world's first multimedia interactive chinese history web site integrating text, voice and video.  leveraging advanced internet technology, the web site provides comprehensive information on chinese history from ancient times to the present day. information is available in english and in traditional and simplified chinese.

title: mfc bancorp to provide swiss private banking on internet
body: mfc bancorp ltd. announced wednesday that it will provide swiss private banking and brokerage services over the internet through its wholly-owned subsidiary, mfc merchant bank s.a.  the swissnetbanking.com web site will offer investors the opportunity to open a private swiss bank account to trade securities over the internet beginning october 15, 1999, mfc said.  "mfc intends to be the first bank to offer small and medium-sized investors the advantages of both swiss private banking and discounted brokerage services on a global basis through the internet," said michael smith, president of mfc bancorp ltd.  smith said, "swiss banks are the largest offshore market in the world, currently managing assets of approximately 1.5 trillion unitedstates dollars, which is 30 percent of the worldwide market for international private banking." "however, switzerland, europe and the rest of the world significantly lag the unitedstates in the development of internet-based discount stock brokerage services." peter jessop, first vice president, mfc merchant bank s.a., said, "our first trading services will be offered for stocks and options traded on the unitedstates exchanges. by the end of next year we will offer trading facilities on the european, south latin american, and asian exchanges, and will provide concurrent multilingual services." mfc bancorp ltd. owns companies that operate in the financial services industry, specializing in private and investment banking internationally.

title: more hk small enterprises urged to use e-business
body: the hongkong productivity council (hkpc) monday urged more small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) in hongkong to use e-business in the drive to turn the city into an innovation and technology center in asia.  a recent survey on the adoption of e-business in hongkong showed that 65 percent of local companies have not used any form of e-business, and 93 percent of them have less than 10 staff, reflecting that local smes as a whole are slow in e-business adoption.  the survey was conducted jointly by the institute of information and media industries of the hkpc and ibm china/hongkong ltd.  a total of 3,702 local companies were interviewed and the result of the survey has been grossed up to the whole population of around 280,000 companies in hongkong.  "in the 21st century, the readiness of a company to adopt ebusiness will become a major determinant of its market competitiveness," said thomas tang, executive director of the hkpc.  since over 98 percent of hongkong companies are small and medium-sized enterprises, how they perform in this area will directly effect the future of hongkong's economic development, he added.  to encourage a wider adoption of e-business, the hkpc will organize over 60 seminars and training workshops on e-business for the smes in the next six months, tang said.  the announcement of the e-business adoption survey result is the first event under hkpc's campaign of "world of innovation --ecommerce week", and other events include the launch of the china ppnet, a hongkong-based information network to facilitate information exchange between companies in the chinese mainland and hongkong.  according to the international data corporation, e-commerce will be the dominant form of business transaction in the future.  the number of internet users worldwide is estimated at 112 million with a total online trade volume worldwide in 1998 topping 43 billion unitedstates dollars, while hongkong has to date over one million internet users.

title: more protection needed for e-shoppers: survey
body: commerce over the internet does not offer enough protection for consumers and the potential of electronic commerce can never be realized until the loopholes in shopping on the internet were wiped away, the european commission said in a newly published report on a survey.  many problems had been found during the e-shopping survey conducted by consumers international on behalf of the european commission, the european union (eu)'s executive body. the investigators ordered over 150 items from easily accessible internet sites, but found finally one article in 10 never arrived.  and a briton and a hongkong citizen waited for five months to get their money back.  the survey also shows that nearly 45 percent of the products ordered reached their destination without acknowledgement of receipt and nearly 25 percent of sites did not give an address or telephone number.  of the total products ordered, 24 percent were not clear about the gross price, according to the six-month survey, which was cooperated with consumer organizations from australia, belgium, britain, germany, greece, hongkong, japan, norway, spain, sweden and the unitedstates.  a federation of 245 consumer protection organizations in 111 countries, consumers international said the finding shows customers in shopping on the internet are kept in the dark about what action to take to lodge a complaint.  the survey writers called for international guidelines to be drafted and a certification or labeling system to be set up to allow consumers to be sure which "electronic stores" meet the basic standards.  they also want to see an appeal mechanism set up to deal with disputes between purchasers and all companies involved in e-business on the internet. it would be an easily accessible, affordable, rapid and user-friendly system for protecting consumers, they added.

title: blair to appoint first e-envoy
body: british prime minister tony blair is set to appoint an "e-envoy" to prepare british business for the electronic age.  blair will announce the appointment during a visit to cambridge university monday, bbc reported sunday.  widely tipped to take the post is alex allan, high commissioner to australia and former private secretary to john major.  the role was announced late last year by peter mandelson during his tenure as trade secretary.  blair is also expected to issue a stern warning to uk businesses during his cambridge visit, urging them to adapt to the world of e-commerce and the internet before their rivals do.  a report by the cabinet office's performance and innovation unit, also due to be released monday, will warn that britain is in danger of lagging behind north american and european competitors in the race to win custom on the internet.  an estimated 9 million britons will be using the internet by the end of the year.  but unless something is done quickly, british industry will be overtaken by international competitors using the internet to sell direct, the report said.  last week, trade and industry secretary stephen byers announced an investigation into competitive barriers in e-commerce.  britain must ensure it remained a source of new and innovative products on the internet, he said.  some regions, such as the southwest and the northeast of england, showed signs of falling behind in their adoption of online technologies in business.

title: boeing: information technology saves time, money in maintenance
body: a boeing official said friday that information technology is the key to boosting productivity in the air transport industry.  addressing a conference in ireland, the vice president for the commercial operation of the company, richard higgins, said that information technology has fundamentally changed the way of airplane's design and build, and now the manufacturer is applying the technology to change the way of maintenance as well.  higgins was quoted by the company as saying that "information technology saves time and money in the maintenance of aircraft and also enhances safety." according to the company, a new family of information tools, under the trade name of boeing digital, has helped airlines make significant improvements in maintenance process.  these tools replace paper and microfilmed maintenance documents with digitized versions that are on compact disks or accessible online. information can be retrieved much faster from these digital sources, speeding up aircraft double shooting.  another key advantage of digitally based information tools is that they can be updated quickly, enabling maintenance staff to work with the most current and accurate information.  one of the most significant information tools in the boeing digital family is boeing on-line delivery (bold). through highspeed network connections, airlines access bold to quickly retrieve service bulletins, component maintenance manuals and airplane technical drawings directly from a boeing database.  to further improve access, boeing said that a trial program will begin later this month to make bold available via the internet. boeing expects to make bold a completely web-based service by the end of next year.  ultimately, bold will evolve into a single point of contact through which airlines will obtain all of the technical information they need to maintain and operate their boeing fleets, boeing said.

title: most u.s. consumers satisfied with online buying
body: in a survey released this week 88 percent of unitedstates consumers rated online buying satisfactory, despite delivery and customer service problems.  the ease of placing orders or reservations is the key to overall consumer satisfaction with online purchasing, according dataquest, the unitedstates market research firm that conducted the survey.  in about a third of the 37 million unitedstates households having access to the internet or online services, there was at lease one person who placed an order or made a reservation online during the period from february to april 1999, according to the survey.  of these households, 2.4 million, or about 20 percent, experienced problems. the research showed that of households experiencing problems, 49 percent reported that they placed orders that did not arrive. nevertheless, in more than half of these households, the customer was billed for the order. for a quarter of the households that experienced problems, the main problem was the inability to contact the merchant's customer service department via email.  in the rush to participate in e-commerce, dataquest said, many merchants have not implemented effective links to back-office system, nor have they given sufficient consideration to online customer support.  "it is vital to win the customer loyalty at this early stage in the development of e-commerce," dataquest said. "internet merchants have the opportunity to gain competitive advantage if they can provide outstanding and imaginative online customer service." dataquest added that consumer satisfaction is crucial to the future of e-commerce, for when an online experience is consistently more satisfactory than in the physical world, and at the same or lower price, consumers' habits are likely to change permanently. but "there is no second chance to win customer loyalty," the research firm said.

title: new magazine aimed at xml development language market
body: a california-based technical publication house friday announced the launch of a new magazine aimed at the growing community of professional xml developers.  xml magazine, to be published by fawcette technical publications, will be the only publication designed to provide information about the architecture and structure of xml.  developed by the world wide web consortium (w3c), a unitedstates technothink tank, xml, or "extensible markup language" has been described as a giant step toward the goal of making a "semantic web," in which all the world's knowledge can become computeraccessible.  xml can describe web pages with far more power than hypertext markup language (html), the internet programming language developed in 1990 by tim berners-lee, creator of the web and founder and director of the w3c. unlike the standard html format, which describes the structure of a page, xml allows developers to make up their own page, or metadata, to describe information content on the page.  while html uses only predefined tags to describe elements within the page, xml allows tags to be defined by the developer of the page. thus, tags for virtually any data items such as product, sales rep and amount due, can be used for specific applications, allowing web pages to function like database records.  emphasizing the magazine's role in helping developers incorporate xml into their e-business solutions, fawcette said that xml is indeed for e-business what html was for the web, enabling businesses to create e-business applications in a way no other development language can match.  xml allows businesses to share one network system, while only allowing each supplier or partner access to authorized information in their particular area of expertise. this translates into the power to make on-line commerce and e-business accessible to every company regardless of size or revenue, the publisher added.

title: wall street stocks end mixed
body: wall street stocks ended mixed friday with the dow jones industrial average falling while most indexes rising.  the dow jones industrial average closed down 50.97 at 11,028.43.  but the technology heavy nasdaq composite index rose 35.04 at 2,887.06, surpassing the record closing high of 2,864.48 set july 16. the standard poor's 500 index also rose 4.00 at 1,351.66.  the labor government reported that the wholesale prices surged 0.5 percent in august but excluding the energy and food categories, the core rate of inflation at the wholesale level actually fell 0.1 percent in the same month.  investors focus on the good performance of core rate in their immediate reaction to the report. but they got concerned with the 0.5 percent overall number lately, dragging the dow lower in fears that the federal reserve would raise interest rates for the third time this year.  but the report did not affected the technology stocks. internet search provider yahoo and online auction house ebay continued to rise, pushing the nasdaq and the sp higher.  on thursday, yahoo rose after lehman brothers raised its rating on the stock and ebay surged after cibc world market launched coverage with a "strong buy" recommendation.  the nyse rose 0.91 at 622.90 and the american stock exchange index rose 1.92 at 805.95. the russell 2000 index of smaller companies rose 3.42 at 441.19.  advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 6-to-5 margin on the new york stock exchange, with 1,605 up, 1,329 down and 589 unchanged.  nyse volume increased to 802.51 million shares from 766.94 million in the previous session.

title: u.s. tech, financial firms collaborating to develop data transfer standard
body: an alliance of unitedstates major computer and internet firms wednesday released a universal format that it hopes to make it easier and more appealing for consumers and businesses to pay for goods and services over the internet.  the format, known as electronic commerce modeling language (ecml), uses a set of uniform field names that streamlines the process by which merchants collect electronic data for shipping, billing and payment.  according to the consortium which includes american online, ibm, microsoft, compaq, american express, visa and other blue-chip companies, merchants today are conducting business on the internet using html-based forms. the data format used in these forms varies from one merchant to another. end-users find the diversity confusing and the process of manually filling in these forms to be tedious.  software tools called digital wallets can help this situation by making the shopping experience easier for consumers. a digital wallet is an application or service that assists consumers in conducting online transactions by allowing them to store billing, shipping and payment information, and to use this information to automatically complete a merchant's check-out page. this greatly simplifies the check-out process and minimizes the need for a consumer to manually complete a merchant's form every time.  digital wallets have been successfully built into browsers, but the proliferation of digital wallets has been hampered by the lack of standard.  most internet merchants use a variety of nonstandard forms. as a result, most consumers have to enter their name, address, credit card number and expiration date at every site each time they want to make a purchase.  according to research firm jupiter communications, 27 percent of consumers have abandoned items at the checkout line at a web storefront because they found filling out forms too tedious a task.  now ecml provides a simple set of guidelines for web merchants that will enbale digital wallets from multiple vendors to automate the exchange of information between users and merchants.  ecml also can be used with existing data privacy and security methods, according to the consortium. online merchants can implement ecml without a license. the alliance said that ecml is the first in what will be a series of e-commerce standard initiatives.

title: clinton, blair, mandela in live internet broadcast
body: unitedstates president bill clinton, british prime minister tony blair and former south african president nelson mandela will take part in a live internet broadcast on wednesday to launch a website aimed at combating global poverty. a british government spokesman said blair would take part in the launch of netaid's website (www.netaid.org) via a videolink from downing street, the reuters reported. the site will broadcast live concerts next month to raise money for the poor. clinton and mandela will also take part in the launch via satellite from the unitedstates and south africa respectively, netaid said in a statement. "they are all going to be launching it. they will be talking to each other via webcast," the downing street spokesman said. the netaid concerts, which are due to be broadcast on october 9 simultaneously at stadiums in london, geneva and new york, will feature stars including robbie williams, george michael and celine dion. organized by the united nations development program and cisco systems, the concerts will also be broadcast on radio and the bbc and mtv television channels. up to 60 million visitors to the website every hour will be able to see and hear the performances, the agency said.

title: malaysia wants internet contents regulated
body: malaysia tuesday called for a global consensus to regulate offensive contents in the internet to protect the public from their adverse effects.  no single country in the world could come up with its own effort to tackle the problem which could damage the culture of many countries especially developing ones like malaysia, energy, communications and multimedia minister leo moggie said here.  "it is difficult unless a common understanding among countries worldwide is reached on the need to restrain unwanted contents in the internet," he told reporters after opening the three-day 30th annual conference of the international institute of communications themed "the knowledge society -commerce, culture and communities in development." moggie said the issue should be raised as often as possible in international fora.  the minister said the malaysian government has a duty to protect the public from adverse contents in the internet especially the exposure of minors to pornography.  however, he said that in the context of the multimedia super corridor (msc) where the government has guaranteed the free flow of information, there would be no censorship on information posted on the internet and it would be accessible to everyone.  according to the minister, internet sales in malaysia were projected to grow from 46 million unitedstates dollars this year to 1 billion dollars by the year 2003.  at the conference, the minister also called on developing countries to work together to establish a common news network to promote fair and accurate news reporting.  he said many of these countries do not have their own news agencies and rely on the services of major news groups, thus exposing them to negative reporting.  moggie said many investment decisions were made on the basis of news and reports published by major news organizations and as such, commercialization together with an open market environment had resulted in news being exploited mainly for economic benefits and financial considerations.  to counter this monopoly on information communication technologies and narrow the disparity between the information-rich and information-poor countries, there is a need for the developing countries to adopt technologies that are able to provide equal access and empowerment for them, he said.

title: dream of doing business at home to come true in hk
body: hongkongers' dream of doing business elsewhere around the world at their homes will soon become a reality, as an e-gateway project is expected to be completed by the year 2000.  "over the last three years, tnt has 'web enabled' most of its major internal applications, and has laid the foundations for a global e-commerce infrastructure," said noud leussink, a regional manager of tnt's customer interface technology (cit) for asia.  leussink was speaking at a media workshop in hongkong thursday, unveiling tnt's latest and complete range of internet services, designed to reshape the marketplace for express distribution services and secure tnt's leadership in internet-based service delivery.  tnt, one of the world's leading companies in global express distribution, logistics and mail, has introduced e-gateway through the cit, offering online integration to complete the internet logistics system.  people are already able to do local e-commerce through the internet, but with the establishment of e-gateway supported by tnt, they will have access to fast, efficient services worldwide, explained bryan chan, general manager of the tnt express worldwide (hongkong) ltd.  "it's extremely encouraging," chan said. tnt' technology is designed to be integrated directly into the customer's supply chain, streamlining operations for organization and allowing an unprecedented control over the shipping and supply process, he added.  the hongkong special administrative region government has made efforts to promote the development of information technology and the internet and this has greatly helped the realization of egateway, chan said.  according to lau kam-hung, director of the hongkong government 's information technology services, who spoke at an e-business symposium in melbourne thursday, establishing an open and common interface, as well as a public key infrastructure to enable individuals, businesses and the government to interact through digital networks easily and securely is one of the initiatives in a move to put hongkong at the threshold to tomorrow's digital world.  "the internet has completely changed people's way of life since its founding 30 years ago," raymond to, senior account executive of the api prism ltd., told the workshop.  to stressed that tnt's increasing focus on internet commerce and application is a direct reflection of their view on the potential of the asia-pacific market, since internet penetration in asia is being driven by businesses while in the unitedstates it was driven by individuals.  there will be a dramatic increase in the use of online business in asia in the next three years and by 2002, 70 percent of all consignments in asia will be handled electronically, to predicted.

title: nokia, reuters team up to develop news services on mobile phones
body: nokia and reuters have signed a global cooperation agreement to develop and deliver financial, sports and general news services based on the wireless application protocol (wap).  the news services are optimized for nokia 7110, the world's first mobile phone for internet access launched early this year.  the services have been developed to work with the nokia messaging platform and are currently available to operators participating in nokia wap pilots.  with the wap system making bitmap imaging possible, the reuters logo, featured as a wireless bitmap, will appear on the phone display when it enters the service.  "the delivery of reuters news and information services via wapbased phones is a strategic objective of ours," said jonathan bailem, managing director of reuters wireless services.  "combined with reuters' position as a global source of content delivery, nokia enables the mobile information society, bringing news to everyone's pocket," said pekka salonoja, vice president of nokia wireless data server systems.  "nokia now has over 20 wap pilots worldwide with innovative operators. reuters news services are an important addition to the services currently offered," he added.  the wap standard includes a wide range of value-added services for mobile phones, such as internet access and data and images transmitting.

title: internet links farmers with wider market
body: chinese farmers used to suffer from a lack of information, and this often led to a terrible waste of farm produce and other agricultural products. however, this situation has been ameliorated by the chinese agriculture information network, an internet website created by the ministry of agriculture. at the address: www.agri.gov.cn, which was registered on the internet in 1996, surfers can discover an ocean of agricultural information. the information includes the development of agricultural products and capital goods in the agricultural sector, analyses of the international agricultural market, import and export analysis, as well as new technologies on crops planting, livestock, and aquatic breeding. an official from the ministry noted that the website has received 214,000 visitors so far and that the information so provided has benefited thousands of people. "internet links my piglets with a wider market," said li minghui, a farmer in north china's hebei province. "it's the network that gave me valuable information on the market prices of the piglets and brought me a large profit of some 100,000 yuan," li added. like li, an increasing number of farmers run their businesses by employing the internet nowadays. in lingxian county in east china's shandong province, though the farmers there have has access to the internet for only three months, they already have gained 40 million yuan in profit by selling garlic, garlic bolts and other vegetables through via the network this year. the jinfeng pear, a specialty of zongzhai town in northwest china's gansu province, in the past had trouble finding a market despite its superior quality. this year, the farmers have contacted prospective buyers on-line even before the fruit matured. at the first on-line grain fair of china this january, the turnover reached 3.3 billion yuan. the agricultural network on the internet has a promising future, and ministry sources said that access to the website has spread to more than 2,000 counties and villages nationwide. approximately one million farmers obtain on-line information nowadays to plant cash crops, and half a million to raise livestock and poultry. and the network has helped spread more than 5,000 new agro-technologies and new varieties so far, sources said. the increasing popularity of the internet among chinese farmers will further facilitate agricultural modernization in china, said xu fengxian, researcher with the chinese academy of social sciences.

title: the post office can work with the internet
body: post offices may become the most effective e-commerce locales in the world, according to some people attending world customer day at the 22nd universal postal congress (upc) here today.  walda roseman, the ceo of compassrose international, inc., said at the meeting today that although people prefer email to writing, they need the postal service as kind of guarantor.  as a government entity, the post office is in an excellent position to act as a "trusted third party" for storage and verification of digital ids. john tait, the chairman of papercom asia pacific, says that because of inadequate on-line id methods, the unitedstates is using more paper confirmation than ever before because each electronic transaction may need many confirming documents, and wang zhanning, the chairman of the 22nd upc, says that post offices have an extensive delivery network that on-line companies lack.  according to roseman, the number one complaint of internet shoppers after the 1998 christmas season was poor delivery. the popular internet retailer, amazon.com, has more limited sales because of its inability to deal in cash.  thomas leavey, director general of the international bureau of the universal postal union (upu), said that post office in the future will be like a one-stop shop. it combines the activities of bank, mail, delivery and information center.

title: uk logs on to e-commerce: surveys
body: britain is experiencing an e-commerce boom, with growing numbers going online to do their shopping or manage their finances, according to local median reports.  a recent survey by management consultants datamonitor said that online shopping and banking are becoming increasingly popular, as more than one in five consumers with access to the internet have ordered products online, while 8 percent of those surveyed used the net to monitor their finances.  internet share trading is showing rapid growth too, up by 21,555 users in the second quarter of 1999, according to a separate survey by the association of private client investment managers and stockbrokers (apcims).  the level of e-commerce penetration was particularly high in london, where almost one in two people have access to a computer at home. in the capital, 27 percent of net users had shopped online, the report said.  "one in four londoners online at home or work order products via the internet," datamonitor analyst alexander rainer said.  "this figure is surprisingly high, considering a minority of uk websites currently have transactional capabilities. " however, for internet banking, rural areas proved the most fertile territory, with the highest rate of use in east anglia, at 14 percent.  "rural regions such as east anglia and scotland appear to have the biggest appetite for online banking as many consumers live far from their branch," a bbc report quoted rainer as saying. "where people live in a more pressured working environment, like in london, online banking is driven by the convenience of 24-hour availabililty." the separate apcims survey showed that internet share trading rose by nearly 60 percent in the last quarter. however, it still only accounts for 1.6 percent of all trades, the association said.  online trades averaged a value of 4,730 pounds, compared to 6,444 pounds for trades through other stockbrokers.  the growth in internet trading is expected to increase in the coming months, as more brokers develop the capacity to trade online, according to analysts.

title: robust asia-pacific internet growth predicted
body: the number of asia-pacific internet users is expected to surpass 374 million by year-end 2005, up from just over 39 million by the end of last year.  according to a forecast report released monday by unitedstates information technology research firm yankee group, the number of paying subscribers, which hovered just under 19 million in the region at year-end 1998, will grow to over 175 million by the end of 2005.  the yankee group notes the difference between a paying internet access subscriber and the number of users (the addressable business-to-consumer audience), as there are often multiple users for one subscription account.  the forecast shows china becoming the leading asia-pacific nation in terms of internet users in 2001, with about 40 million people online. by 2005, the report said, china should surpass the unitedstates to have the most users in the world.  "the implication of this asia-pacific subscriber and user growth will be enormous on global e-commerce opportunities, from business-to-business sourcing, to business-to-consumer marketing," the report said.  factors that have constrained the historical growth of the internet in asia include the regulatory, commercial and access issues that have begun to change and will drive internet growth and penetration going forward, according to the research firm.

title: u.s. online ad spending expected to grow
body: unitedstates online advertising is expected to grow to 11.5 billion unitedstates dollars in 2003, surpassing dollars spent in some traditional media, according to new research released wednesday by an internet commerce research firm.  jupiter communications said that ad spending will increase 40 percent over the next four years, with financial services, automotive, and media ventures leading the spending.  according to an earlier jupiter report, in 1998, online advertising increased 34 percent over 1997 to reach 1.92 billion dollars.  driven by growing online population, the rise in time spent online, and increasing digital commerce adoption, online advertising revenues have already surpassed those for outdoor advertising and will exceed spending for cable advertising and equal roughly three-quarters of today's radio spending by 2003, according to jupiter.  car companies, media firms and financial services companies will account for nearly half of online ad spending in 2003. but packaged goods companies, whose ad spending will account for 18 percent of offline dollars, will only contribute seven percent of online dollars by that time.  "online advertising will serve as a catalyst for change in the traditional ad business," jupiter said. "media integration and the inevitable erosion of traditional markets will be more important than the effects of online ad dollar growth." another unitedstates research firm, forrester research, estimated last week that global spending for online advertising will reach 33 billion dollars by 2004, one-third of which will be spent outside of the unitedstates.  forrester projected that unitedstates online ad spending will hit 22 billion dollars by 2004. this figure represents 8.1 percent of projected expenditures for traditional advertising --exceeding magazine, yellow pages and radio spending.  over the next five years, the internet will siphon 27 billion dollars or 10 percent of all unitedstates ad spending --away from traditional media, according to forrester.  outside the unitedstates, online ad spending will increase from 502 million dollars in 1999 to 10.8 billion dollars in 2004, capturing 33 percent of global spending, forrester estimated. in europe, online ad will total 5.5 billion dollars in 2004, representing 5.1 percent of europe's ad spending. the asia-pacific nations will spend an additional 3.3 billion dollars, or six percent of traditional ad spending in the region. latin america will grow to 1.6 billion dollars in 2004, or 4.8 percent of regional spending.

title: pornography on internet causing concerns
body: child pornography on the internet continues to be a matter of concern both regionally and internationally, a norwegian official from the center for prevention of child sexual abuse said here tuesday. addressing participants to a conference on the prevention of abuse on women and children which ends wednesday, lars gronseth, deputy director of information for the save children's project in norway said experience had shown that a huge amount of documented abuse of children was being distributed through the internet on web sites. he said the lack of legislation in different countries made it difficult to stop and that lack of experience in the police with these kinds of crimes made it difficult to combat.  "until production, distribution and possession of child pornography is illegal in every country in the world, this is a lost battle.  my hope is that people in africa also will join this fight and help to save the children," he said.  gronseth said the most important resource on this battle at the moment are the net users themselves.  as the number of internet users grows, so do the risks of children being exposed to inappropriate materials, in particular criminal activities.  at present not enough was known about the scale or extent of pornographic activities on the net, their consequences and impact on young people.  global estimates showed that 200 million users would be connected to the net by the year 2001 from 20 million in 1998.

title: internet becomes more popular in mideast: study
