body: the internet is gaining a wider popular appeal among communities in the middle east, drawing more users from lower educational backgrounds and entering more homes than offices, a study said saturday.  over the past year and a half, the number of internet users in the region who hold only a high-school diploma or less has dramatically increased from 17 percent to 27 percent, said the study issued by internet arab world magazine.  the increase has come entirely from new adult users, it added.  the users with an undergraduate university degree remained dominant at 58.6 percent among the internet users in the arab world, which are estimated at 1.1 million now.  holders of phds and master's degree account for 14.5 percent of 1,000 surveyed, which was a drop of about 5 percent over 18 months.  the study, made in cooperation with ditnet, is based on a user profile survey conducted on-line for the second time in a year and a half.  one of the significant outcomes of the survey is that an increasing number of users are spending more time on the internet at home than in office.  the majority of respondents, 72 percent, said home was the primary place where they accessed the internet, while only 22 percent said it was the office.  many factors are contributing to the increasing popularity of the internet among arab users, which include falling rates of internet access that are encouraging more people to subscribe at home, and an increasing awareness of the benefits and various services available on-line.  the study also showed that the average age of internet users in the arab world had, meanwhile, increased by one year to reach 30, but remained younger than the global average, which stands at 33.  the internet community in the arab world remained overhelmingly dominated by men, with only a marginal increase in women users in the sample from 4.2 percent to 6 percent, the study said.

title: 22nd postal congress features advanced computer technology
body: the 22nd congress of the universal postal union (upu) in beijing later this month will employ a state-of-the-art computer network system for voting, information dissemination, and other purposes.  the secretariat of the congress's organizing committee told xinhua that the new system has undergone thorough test runs to ensure their smooth operation at the congress.  for the first time, delegates will be offered the alternative of making applications via the internet. the on-line application system was opened earlier in march, according to the secretariat.  the computer network, which used to serve the upu only, has been extended to hotels accommodating the congress delegates, and delegates will have internet access to upu networks in switzerland for all the information provided by upu without leaving their hotels.  at the same time, the electronic voting system, the brainchild of chinese researchers, will use hundreds of monitors to display results and information, in place of the old practice of displaying them on screens.  during the congress, some 500 bills will be discussed and voted on, and the new voting system will greatly facilitate the entire process, officials with the secretariat said.  this is the first time that china will use such technology as host of an international conference, said cheng yongping, in charge of equipment management in the secretariat.  total investment for the new systems is about 10 million yuan ( 1.2 million unitedstates dollars), and several companies including compaq and hewlett-packard have donated their products in support of the congress.  the 22nd upu congress, the first upu meeting ever held in china, is slated for august 23 to september 15 in beijing. more than 2, 000 delegates from the 189 member nations of upu and over 20 international organizations will attend the conference.

title: u.s. launches stamp available online
body: the unitedstates postal service monday launched pc postage, a stamp which users can buy over the internet and print it through personal computers.  the system eventually could change the way many people put postage on their envelopes, analysts said.  consumers would go online to one of the companies offering pc postage. with an ordinary laser or inkjet printer, a barcode would be printed on each envelope to indicatemail processing information and postage payment. for packages, consumers would enter the weight, buy the appropriate amount of postage and print it on labels to be put on the packages.  "with pc postage you can purchase and print postage 24 hours a day, seven days a week from the convenience of your home or office," said pam gibert, postal service vice president of retail.  stamps.com and e-stamp corp., both of whom are based in california, began offering the computerized postage monday. two other companies --neopost inc. of hayward, california, and pitney bowes of stamford, connecticut --are to begin offering the products in coming months.  consumers can use those companies' web sites to purchase and print postage for domestic first-class, priority and express mail and for parcel post envelopes and packages.  with each company, the consumer goes to the company's web site to register and download any required software. some companies offer the software free while others require a fee.  consumers also will pay handling fees to the companies --they will range from 1.99 to 19.99 unitedstates dollars a month depending on usage rates, according to companies' plans --along with payment for the postage. purchases can be made either by debit or credit card.  during the three years of working on pc postage, each company has had to meet requirements to ensure the security of the system, gibert said.  even with high-tech stamps, the traditional stamp isn't headed for extinction, gibert said.

title: on-line ads destined for rosy future
body: fueled by an increasing number of the internet users, on-line advertising is expected to have a glorious future in china, reported today's china daily's weekend edition, business weekly.  "although on-line advertising appeared in china only four years ago, it has great market potential," said li fangwu, director of the information center of the china advertising association (caa).  caa reports indicate china's internet advertising was valued at 20 million yuan (about 2.4 million unitedstates dollars) last year.  li said this can be mainly attributed to the increasing popularity of the internet on the chinese market.  sources from china national network information center (cnnic) indicate that by the end of 1998, there were 2.1 million internet surfers in china, twice the figure in 1997.  by the end of june this year, the figure has increased to four million.  "the advent of on-line advertising has enriched the variety of advertising forms along with television, radio, newspapers, magazines," he said.  at the beginning of the 1980s, most customers preferred to advertise in major central governmental newspapers because of their large circulation and identifiable reader groups.  "however, as the market gradually matured, many businessmen choose to advertise in places where they felt they would have a greater market potential for their products," said li.  he said that compared with other forms of advertising such as tv ads and newspaper ads, internet advertising has many advantages and huge possibilities.  on-line advertising is more effective, he said, with welldesigned three-dimensional pictures and bountiful relevant information.  meanwhile, internet advertising can provide precise feedback for advertising enterprises, because computers may be used to easily record a web surfer's search patterns.  "however, compared with developed countries, on-line advertising in china is still in its infancy," li said.  in 1998, sales of global on-line advertising were two billion u.  s. dollars, 100 percent more than in 1997.  in many developed countries, such as the unitedstates, internet advertising is earning more than three billion unitedstates dollars a year.  it is difficult to clearly define internet advertising in china because many enterprises are using the internet to introduce themselves and their products. controversy remains whether this should be regarded as advertising.  at present, internet ads in china are mainly banners and icons.  problems affecting the industry include a lack of unified standards for billing for internet advertising, he added.  industry analysts believe it would be a good idea to form authoritative advertising companies specializing in offering customers internet advertising services.  "given the rapid development of china's internet and the sustainable economy, market potential is huge and overwhelming," li said.  experts from within the circle predict that by the end of 1999, china will have more than five million internet surfers, and the figure is expected to surpass ten million by 2000.

title: scheme launched to offer on-line government services
body: the scheme will allow filing of simple tax returns or payment of tax through the internet at any time.  the existing 1.23 million drivers and 500,000 vehicle owners can renew their driving and vehicle licenses respectively through the on-line services.  the other seven government departments are: immigration, labor, rating and valuation, industry and social welfare departments, registration and electoral office as well as treasury.  using their electronic services, to cite a few, job-seekers can look for job vacancies while employers can submit job vacancies and search for suitable candidates. those eligible can register as voters, and individuals can book appointments for identity card registration.  members of the public will be able to apply on-line for volunteer scheme registration and senior citizen cards. businesses can seek advice on investment and business licensing requirements.  tourists can access information about hongkong. users can pay tax, rates, government rent and water charges electronically.  the esd scheme will also be operated at a cross-departmental level in a seamless manner. at present, citizens have to notify individual departments of any change in their personal particulars, such as addresses, separately.  esd is a key initiative under the "digital 21" information technology strategy which aims at enhancing and promoting hongkong's information infrastructure and services, making it a leading digital city in the globally connected world of the 21st century.  siu noted that the introduction of esd would pave the way for the development of electronic commerce in hongkong with the government's promotional efforts.  the establishment of a public key infrastructure, supported by certification authorities, and a clear legal framework for electronic transactions will further boost public confidence and provide a secure environment conducive to electronic commerce locally.

title: american retailers feeling e-commerce bite
body: a new report released wednesday shows that traditional brick and mortar retailers in the unitedstates will begin to feel the bite from e-commerce soon.  less than 10 percent of e-commerce revenue in 2002 will be from incremental sales, according to the report from unitedstates research firm jupiter communications. this means that the bulk of the growth in e-commerce will come from sales that would have taken place off-line.  of the 11.9 billion unitedstates dollars in online commerce jupiter is predicting for 1999 in the unitedstates, only 720 million dollars, or six percent, will come from sales that would not have otherwise taken place.  jupiter estimates that the percentage of incremental sales will grow only slightly, to 6.5 percent, or three billion dollars of the expected 41 billion dollars, by 2002, with growth dependent on merchants' ability to target offers and promotions.  the new research urges traditional merchants to build unified ventures that take advantage of their off-line assets --an existing customer base, a trusted brand name, customer data, and sales and distribution infrastructure. otherwise, the research firm said, they will risk losing sales to internet-only merchants.  "with a few notable exceptions," the research firm said, "traditional merchants' internet strategies have been paralyzed by indecision, and the merchants continue to watch web upstarts seize the early momentum." jupiter said that companies need to accept the internet as another channel for their business or risk losing sales to competitors. "building a web site isn't really an option for traditional merchants. it's something that they've absolutely got to do," the research firm said.

title: microsoft's new dictionary released in print
body: microsoft, the world's computer software giant, has released its new dictionary into the world of print.  print versions of the encarta world english dictionary were available wednesday in britain, the unitencbgwctionary released in print los angeles, august 4 (xinhua) --microsoft, the world's computer software giant, has released its new dictionary into the world of print.  print versions of the encarta world english dictionary were available wednesday in britain, the unitedstates and australia.  the dictionary is also available in an electronic version.  microsoft said that its dictionary takes a global perspective, emphasizing how the internet has helped make english a world language, since the majority of web sites are written in english.  more than 300 experts from 20 english-speaking countries used computer and internet technology to compile the lexicon, which was three years in the making. microsoft said that it is the first newly compiled dictionary released in the unitedstates in 30 years, and the first time that print and electronic media have been used together to develop a work of this kind.  meanwhile, the oxford english dictionary (oed), widely regarded as the ultimate authority on the english language, has launched a worldwide appeal for words as it prepares to go online to mark the new millennium with the most comprehensive lexicon ever.  overwhelmed by a flood of new words, phrases and technical terms coined in the last 50 years, the oed is asking anyone who speaks or reads english to submit new words and documentation to lexicographers working on the first complete revision in the work' s 120-year history.  the revision is scheduled to be completed by 2010, but the latest edition published in 1996 will be available online next march and is expected to be updated every six months with incoming contributions.  because the dictionary will be online, it will have no limits.  unitedstates online medium nando commented wednesday that the appeal for new words is no mere marketing gimmick. "published evidence must accompany the words or phrases submitted to the oed, so contributors will have to do research," nando said.

title: uae has largest number of net subscribers in arab world
body: the united arab emriates (uae) has the largest number of internet subscribers in the arab world, according to a gulf news report on thursday.  statistics from etisalat, the country's telecommunications monopolizer, show that the number of net subscribers had reached 81,700 until april this year, which indicates more people in the country are being drawn to the internet.  however, with regard to the number of real users, which includes families of subscribers, the uae is in second place after egypt. statistics show that real internet users have reached 204,300 in the uae.  the growing interest in exploring cyberspace had raised fears of net-related crimes, including illegal access to confidential data which could endanger national security, the paper pointed out.  "although it has facilitated the exchange of information, as well as commercial transactions, the internet has also created a channel for promoting illegal practices and immoral concepts," a sharjah-based police officer was quoted as saying.  the officer stressed the need to install the internet at police departments and to familiarize police staff with its applications. "they would play a major role in curbing internet crimes and international terrorism," he added.

title: internet growth fast in developing countries
body: internet growth is accelerating faster in developing countries than anywhere else, a report presented to the third african communications regional workshop in lusaka said tuesday.  the report presented by zambia telecommunication corporation limited said that internet users in africa have passed the one million mark but south africa accounts for more than 90 percent of internet growth.  meanwhile, sub-saharan africa with a population of 520 million has fewer than 9,000 internet hosts whilst north africa with 130 million inhabitants has only 2,550 hosts, the report said.  the report noted that all african countries have some form of internet access.  however, estimates of internet growth in africa need to be treated with caution.  much of the growth occurred in one country -south africa.  for example, out of the 155,623 hosts, 144,445 are in south africa which ranks about 16th in world terms in number of internet hosts.  the poor state of telecommunications infrastructure adversely affects the internet, which totally depends on some minimum level of telecommunications infrastructure for existence, the report said, adding that measure of tele-density (number of telephone lines per 100 people) in africa is the largest constraint.  average tele-density for the developing world is just 1.5, while in some african countries like guinea, liberia, niger and somalia the figure plummets to just 0.002.  in chad and the democratic republic of congo the figure is 0.0001, it said.  the internet will continue to be one of the buzz-words in the telecommunications industry, appealing to both operating and new entrants in the field, the report said.

title: telecom giants to jointly explore hk internet market
body: two telecom giants cct telecom holdings ltd (cct) and ntt communications corporation announced the partnership here monday to jointly explore the internet and telecommunications service market in hongkong.  according to the agreement, cct will sell its counterpart 49 percent stake in hknet co ltd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of cct and a leading internet service provider in hongkong. cct will remain as the majority shareholder with 51 percent stake in hknet.  clement mak, chairman of cct telecom, said that under this share sale agreement, hknet will benefit from technological expertise of ntt communications corporation which will further strengthen its internet and telecommunications service in hongkong.  he said the extensive experience, massive research and development resources of ntt communications corporation will provide hknet with the necessary support in consolidating its leadership position in the local market.  mak expressed the confidence that with the partnership between cct and ntt communications corporation, hknet would be able to continue expanding its isp and idd businesses, and would be well positioned for a rapid growth in the near future.  founded in 1994, hknet was one of the first licensed internet service providers in hongkong and was acquired by cct telecom in 1998. hknet currently has the second largest internet subscriber base in hongkong.  as the world's largest telecommunication and internet service provider (isp) in terms of revenue, the ntt group provides a full range of services ranging from telecommunications, data communications and multi-media technologies.  the ntt group was reorganized in july 1999 and the ntt communications corporation serves as a key player in the reorganized group.

title: wool trading to go live on internet in new zealand
body: wool growers and buyers in new zealand will soon be able to do business on the internet in what the country's wool industry claims is a world first, the dominion reported monday.  woolnet, to go live in september, will cut selling costs and open new business opportunities, the wellington-based newspaper quoted lance wiggins, managing director of developer woolpro, as saying.  woolpro is a subsidiary of the new zealand wool group.  wiggins said woolnet will present large volumes of wool to international processors keen to work directly with growers.  buyers must have a new zealand bank account, he said, adding transactions will be conducted privately in the database, not on the web site.  on delivery date, the buyers will confirm the wool has arrived and the bank transaction will go ahead, wiggins said.  he said the money will stay in a trust account of asb bank, a bank in new zealand, for 48 hours while levies and any charges are deducted. the grower will then get the balance. woolpro's commission will be half the present commission costs.  registrations will be taken from the first week in august and demonstration in wool growing centers will start this week, according to the newspaper.

title: gates outlines vision for home of the future
body: microsoft chairman bill gates thursday outlined plans to help consumers create the home of the future, according to a report from the software company.  speaking at the company's annual financial analyst meeting, gates described how computers, having revolutionized the workplace, will work with wireless networks and intelligent devices and appliances to help people live the "digital lifestyle" at home and work.  gates repeated his notion of a "pc-plus" era, where computers will continue to act as a basic communications tool and work together with other devices.  he said that the heart of microsoft's vision is the goal of empowering people with software --any time, any place and on any device.  in the office this means software offers screen resolution good enough to make the paperless office a reality, few and more effective meetings thanks to advanced communications tools, digital feedback loops that speed the analysis of complex business problems, and greater competitiveness in the global marketplace.  in the home, he said, the pc-plus era will bring about the most radical changes. pc-based software will combine with a new generation of wireless networks, smart devices and intelligent appliances to bring a wealth of new digital products into the homes.  the developments he described include a high-speed wireless home network that enables users to play music and videos or display family photographs, web-tv network service with on-demand programming and web-enhanced content, and the next-generation of gaming offering online competition with voice interaction, immersive audio, 3-d graphics and the option of parental control.  he said that microsoft plans to invest 3.7 billion unitedstates dollars in research and development this fiscal year, and a big part of that effort will be to make those digital products available.

title: roundup: europeans see internet part of daily life - Correction Appended
body:
europeans are more and more interested in using internet for doing things as part of their daily life despite of their slower pace for embracing information society than that in the unitedstates.  a recent survey shows that many european citizens rely increasingly on the use of new information technology (it) applications. for the interviewed europeans, 47.8 percent usually consult local town or council services from their home in order to get documents they need.  the european union's eurobarometer survey said that 42.3 percent of respondents show their interest in preparing a complete trip from home on a computer screen, while 41.9 get a doctor's advice on a health problem.  meanwhile, many europeans choose an easy way to look for a job by consulting the employment office from a computer. the survey showed 41.5 percent seek their jobs from internet and 33.9 learn a training program from a computer or television at home as if attending the course in person.  some europeans believe that the worthiest spending for using internet is distance learning. some 18.2 percent of the interviewed, an equivalent of 56 million european citizens, expressed their willingness to pay 10 euros (10.4 unitedstates dollars) per month to get such a service.  the data showed internet users in europe have doubled since early 1997. now, about 27 million people use the internet at home and some 22.4 million use it at work.  currently, an average of 8.3 percent of private households in the 15-nation european union have internet access, compared to 4.4 percent in 1997. however, the contrast is obvious in the whole picture of the 15-country bloc. the leading countries using the internet are sweden (39.6 percent), denmark (24.6 percent) and the netherlands (19.6 percent), while the less active countries are greece (2.9 percent), portugal (3.4 percent), france (3.9 percent) and spain (5 percent).  but for internet companies and commercial banks, they are happy to see the growing passion for internet in europe. last week, a two-month old internet firm, funmail, announced its listing plan.  the company providing fun and strange email addresses has lured about 45,000 internet surfers since it established two months ago.  observers said funmail has the right sight over the prospects of internet investment by europeans.  for america online inc. (aol), the unchallenged leader in cyberspace access in the unitedstates, keeping up with growth in europe is important. while aol still has plenty of room to grow in the unitedstates, where about 37 percent of households are on-line, the potential is even higher in europe, analysts said.  according to the jupiter communications, only 13 percent of households are on-line in germany and only 4 percent in italy.  banks are also trying to tap their businesses to cater for the internet fever. some bankers say they would do their businesses on the internet while viewing the european market as a whole.  observers believe the on-line banking will be the best way to tap the market in european.  the on-line businesses of several banks in the nordic countries are in full swing. sweden's seb bank started its internet services at the end of 1996 when they expected some 10,000 clients, but they were surprised to see ten times of the figure six months later. now on-line customers accounted for 20 percent of seb's total retail services.  with the development of information society, europeans would be easy to find that the internet makes their life easier since email, e-commerce, e-shopping, e-course and other e-led activities and services have already entered their daily life, though some countries are still reluctant to push ahead with the trend in the continent. title: ca unveils line of internet-security software
body: computer associates international, the world's leader in mission-critical business software, said tuesday that the company is starting an internet-security line of software as another way to tap into the surge in companies doing business on line.  the e-trust line will include encryption, which creates codes to protect data; fire walls, for keeping out unauthorized users and information; and virtual private networks, which provide privacy while using public networks, charles b. wang, ca's chairman and chief executive officer, said here at the companies 5th annual meeting since 1995.  ca said it is working on a new version of its jasmine program, used in creating software, to sell to companies that want to do business on the internet, the worldwide link-up network.  the new jasmine program is to include neutral-network technology, patterned on the human brain's decision-making ability, that can be used in making forecasts.  "users can build and employ web application in wed speed," he said.  wang, an overseas chinese who was born in 1944 in shanghai, east china, and came to the unitedstates in 1952. he set up ca in 1976 and developed it into the the no. 4 unitedstates software company.  with the revenue of 5.3 billion unitedstates dollars in the fiscal year 1999, ca employs 14,000 professionals in more than 100 countries and regions.

title: feature: new ca division helps clients capitalize on e-commerce
body: internet technology is touching every aspect of our lives, but perhaps the area that has experienced the most noticeable change is in the way business operate. when an organization embraces internet technology as part of their business processes, they can immediately notice the impact on their operation.  today, companies from all industries across the world are capitalizing on internet technology to communicate with their clients and business partners, to link their distributed systems, and to conduct business.  there is no doubt that e-commerce is hot, after all, consumers spent 8 billion unitedstates dollars in 1998, and that figure is expected to grow to roughly 130 billion unitedstates dollars in the next four years.  the economics and statistics administration of the unitedstates department of commerce estimates that by 2002, internet commerce between businesses will likely surpass 300 billion unitedstates dollars.  businesses use the internet to lower purchasing costs, reduce inventories and cycle times, provide more efficient and effective customer service, lower sales and marketing costs, and realize new sales opportunities.  to help clients take complete advantage of this trend, computer associates international (ca), the world's mission-critical business software leader, recently launched "inter-biz solutions", a new division dedicated to assisting worldwide clients, suppliers, and partners to capitalize on e-commerce business opportunities.  according to inter-biz president, reuven battat, "inter-biz can give organizations of all sizes the ability to develop realtime links in the chain community. that means not only collaborating between and across multiple businesses, but optimizing efficiencies by using ca's proven three-dimension technology interfaces to visualize the entire business process --from order to shipping to revenue recognition." "as the leader in enterprise management solutions, ca is taking its knowledge and experience and applying it to make today's businesses as successful as possible," he said.  inter-biz creates realtime business management solutions that reach beyond standard supply chain management and enterprise resource planning strategies.  to achieve this, ca is using the same technology that catapulted the new software, unicenter tng framework, into the infrastructures of millions of clients and partners --to address the challenges of business application integration.  tng stands for the next-generation, meaning the software is designed to meet the demands of the future consumption.  this extensive business management framework, named bizwork, uses core ca technologies --including unicenter tng, 3-dimension-visualization and neugents neutral network pattern recognization --as a new foundation for inter-and intra-business communication.  bizwork provides an array of partner, vertical and homegrown applications with the ability to plug in and achieve enhanced value through an entirely new business management infrastructure.  inter-biz leverages the resources of ca's application business units --inter-biz supply chain group, inter-biz banking group, inter-biz financial group. all these are associated with some famous software companies.  the combination of these organizations creates a powerful delivery vehicle that offers clients access to ca's complete spectrum of enterprise management, financial, manufacturing, and human resources applications, e-commerce supply chain management, logistics, and educational programs.  these business unit applications will be utilized with core ca technologies to create a brand new business paradigm.

title: china promoting digital library services
body: china is introducing digital techniques into its libraries, so as to give more people access to the internet. libraries in beijing, shanghai, shenzhen and nanjing cities and guangdong and liaoning provinces have been pioneers in this respect since 1997, according to the china society of library science. two libraries in guangdong have already copied over three million pages of their documents onto their websites on the www. 163.net and the www.169.net, which are expected to have some two million visitors each month. digital science provides the libraries with more room for further development, experts argue. and it will bring changes not only to the contemporary library service, but also to its stored contents. printed books are only one kind of accumulation of knowledge resources, while digital science greatly boosts information sharing. colleges and universities in china are also trying to make use of digital science in their libraries. up to now, over 100 of them have opened websites. the national library of beijing set up its first electronic reading room in 1996, and the second one in 1997, offering software and cd data services.

title: online retailing revenues surge in north america
body: online retailing in north america is expected to top 36 billion unitedstates dollars by the end of the year and a projected growth of 145 percent in 1999.  according to a report released monday by the boston consulting group, a general management consulting firm, total 1998 online revenues across all categories reached almost 15 billion dollars, presenting 0.5 percent of all retail sales in north america.  online orders in 1998 were up 200 percent and the number of online shoppers was up 300 percent.  the consulting firm based its study on a detailed survey of 158 online retailers. the top 50 retailing sites accounted for almost 75 percent of the market in 1998, and the top 10 sites accounted for 43 percent of the revenues.  the cost of acquiring customers remains high. web sites are spending, in general, between 22 and 42 dollars to get one customer to make a purchase, the study said. but in addition to internet traffic increases, there is also lots of room for growth in the supplemental revenue web sites can earn. such supplemental revenues include the sales of advertising space on sites, permission-based direct marketing and membership. and research fees are an untapped source of revenue for most online retailers, accounting only five percent of overall revenues, according to the study.  "most people think e-commerce is mainly being done by web-only businesses," the report said, but 62 percent of the online revenues in 1998 were from retailers who had businesses that predated the web. these catalog, call centers and brick-and-mortar retailers are a growing force behind the continued rapid growth of online retail.  currently, pure-play retailers are dominant in the collectibles (person-to-person auctions), books, music/video and automotive categories. in categories such as financial brokerage, consumer electronics, apparel and computers, the majority of sales are from multichannel retailers.

title: china telecom expected to further cut internet access fee
body: china's telecom administration is considering to further lower the country's internet access fees under the increasing pressure of internet users, according to today's china daily business weekly.  "it's a trend to cut fees to an affordable level, further price adjustments are being considered," chen yin, a division chief of the planning and development department with china telecom administration bureau, was quoted as saying.  however, chen, who is responsible for internet-related prices, didn't disclose the exact schedule of the price cut.  the telecom administration had already lowered charges over internet access by a large margin in march this year. the price cut contributed to the explosive growth of internet users in the first half of the year.  the number of chinese internet users has hit 4 million by the first six months this year, according to the latest statistics from the china internet network information center.  the figures, showing the number of dial-up users at 2.56 million, have almost doubled last year's 2.1 million users.  "the growth momentum could hit more than 100 percent a year in the coming years," mao wei, director of the center, told china daily. "but another great leap this year has to do with the stimuli of price cuts." according to the center's survey, chinese internet users mainly suffer from the low speed of the connection when accessing websites and the relatively high costs. complaints about speed represent 49.3 percent and complaints about costs account for 36.8 percent.

title: chinese firms doing business via internet
body: firms in china are getting used to doing business via the internet. "china market," the website launched last july by china's ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation (moftec), posted nearly 20,000 commodities produced by more than 5,000 chinese companies, most of which are small and medium-sized. over the past year, over 70 percent of these firms have reached agreements of cooperation with foreign customers, and more than 20 percent have exported their goods. a factory producing art works in east china's zhejiang province attracted new customers from the unitedstates, japan, germany, australia and brazil after connecting to "china market" at: http// www.chinamarket.com.cn in an email message to moftec, the factory thanked the website for providing a convenient and fast way of doing business for such small and medium-sized firms. an international trading company in wuhai, capital of central china's hubei province, logged on to "china market" and struck deals with unitedstates customers for 50,000 unitedstates dollars worth of light industrial products, while also signing agreements with united arabic emirates customers for chemical products valued at 10,000 u. s. dollars. a pharmacy in central china's henan province concluded contracts worth 200,000 unitedstates dollars after going on-line. the "china market" website said it has received 66.3 million hits from 122 nations and regions since it was launched.

title: undp report says internet widening gap among human beings
body: the worldwide computer link-up, the internet, is helping widen the global gap between the haves and have-nots and the knows and the know-nots, according to this year's version of the united nations development program report that appeared this week.  the report has been published annually since 1990. this year's report says that the gap is widening because access to the internet differs widely. the unitedstates, for example, has more computers than the rest of the world combined, and bulgaria has more internet users than the whole of sub-saharan africa, excluding south africa. south asia, with 23 percent of the world's population, has less than one percent of the world's internet users.  elsewhere, the internet divides the literate from the illiterate (60 percent of the users in china have a university degree), men from women (in brazil, 75 percent of the users are men), rich from poor (a computer costs the average bangladeshi more than eight years of salary, compared with a month's wages for the average american), young from old (the average british user is under 30), and urban from rural, the report says.  the typical internet user worldwide is male, below the age of 35, has a university education and high income, is urban based and english speaking, in other words, the member of a very elite minority, it says.  while the rich countries take advantage of the internet's information to help develop their technology and economies, the needs and concerns of poor countries and poor people, who have been denied access almost imperceptibly are being left out of the global conversation, it says.  one way to solve this problem the report suggests is to collect a "bit tax" on data transmitted via the internet. a tax of one unitedstates cent on every 100 lengthy emails would generate well over 70 billion unitedstates dollars a year.

title: news analysis: cyber-shopping taken as next growth wave
body: canada's national economy, one of the g7 generators, is seeing cyber-shopping as its next opportunity for growth.  a record 688 million canadian dollars (about 467.84 million unitedstates dollars) was reported to go to online vendors last year, yet only a trifle of 0.28 percent of the total was netted within the country. the rest? said to move into the southern uncle sam, whose charisma is believed to be ranging from a more of web-sites and commodities to a low of price.  the contrast between quick growth and poor harvest makes the country's economists anxious for improvement. the warning is that anyone who neglects cyber-shopping as the next wave of business is bound to be tramped.  to be more serious, the appeal sounds like a deadline within six month, as if the country's business stall would certainly lose unless something is done to check the trend.  the count is a balance of "three out of every five", meaning at least 60 percent of canadian cyber-spending would flow south in case the cyber-system remains what it was in 1998.  the challenge to a change for the better is obvious: half of the top 200 unitedstates retailers against a quarter of 200 canadian counterparts --in terms of availability of internet shopping sites.  yet the catch-up of the cyber-shopping business may be viewed differently on the other hand. canadian economists believe the country has solid foundation for the on-line business explosion.  with an increasing number of canadians embracing the debit card, the economists even envisage a growth of 1,416 percent in e-commerce revenues by 2003, when a cyber-income is estimated up to 80.4 billion canadian dollars (54.7 billion unitedstates dollars), from the far more insignificant 5.3 billion (about 3.6 billion unitedstates dollars) in 1998.  the pink idea beamed out of the data optimism, where about 10 million canadians were counted as internet users in 1998, while the matter of course momentum could lead to a 23.9 million high out of the then expected population of 32.5 million.  "shopping on the internet is clearly catching on with consumers, and retailers need to keep pace," said the country's retail council president diane brisebois at a recent meeting.  the president, like all others urging for an integrated cyber-strategy for canada, pointed to the significant opportunities to expand business world wide.

title: austrians encouraged to use internet
body: austrian prime minister viktor klima vowed here wednesday that he will enable 50,000 austrians each year to obtain web diploma through his training program. austria is lagging behind most european countries in taking advantage of the information technology (it), with only 30 percent of its population accessing to the internet.  klima told a press conference that he has launched a program " austria advances toward the internet" to encourage more austrians to realize the growing importance of the information technology.  klima, who invited heavyweight business executives in the it sector to his office for an "internet summit", pledged to take steps to help people, especially the old and those with less education, to overcome their fears of the it-associated difficulties.  the first step of his program is to enable these people to have the preliminary know-how to use the internet, and the second step is to help them purchase necessary equipment, said the prime minister. he said his goal is to enable 50,000 people each year to get their "internet diploma" and to place austria among the european countries advanced in this area in the coming century.

title: china to enhance internet development
body: the chinese government will provide a better environment for internet development in the country, an official with the ministry of information industry ( mii) said here today.  a report on internet development released today by the china internet network information center said chinese internet users are concentrated mainly in large and developed cities and provinces such as beijing, shanghai, and guangdong province in south china.  however, the number of users in most remote areas is lower than 1 percent, the report said.  internet surfers are most dissatisfied with slow net-surfing speeds, high fees, and insufficient information, according to the report.  educational and technological information and medical, cultural, and tourism information are in short supply on the 'net, some users complain.  chen yin, director of the development and planning section of mii, said that band width, a key indicator of internet capacity, does not meet users' demand. related departments are making efforts to catch up with international standards in this regard in a bid to increase surfing speed, he said.  china slashed telecommunications fees in march this year, but the payment system still has room for improvement, chen said. he did not rule out the possibility that china may cut down related fees in the near future.  he said china's security department has stepped up efforts to establish network and information security systems, and china will come up with a schedule early next century to provide all primary and secondary schools in china with internet access.

title: asia's e-commerce applications markets to expand rapidly
body: the asia-pacific market for internet commerce applications has been enjoying a robust growth over the past year, and will likely remain that way through 2003, according to a report released tuesday.  internet commerce application software enables companies to conduct business on-line. the asia-pacific market, excluding japan, topped 20.1 million unitedstates dollars in revenue in 1998, up 104 percent from a year ago, said the unitedstates market research firm international data corporation (idc).  the idc estimates a 95 percent growth to 40.45 million dollars this year and 167.76 million dollars in 2000. by 2003, the market is projected to top 1.3 billion dollars.  according to the idc, two types of software should warrant special attention over the next two years. one application allows web sites to better manage on-line content; the other helps sites improve their interaction with customers. both will be increasingly important to companies betting their future on the internet.  the idc expects to see a tremendous growth in the number of ecommerce software vendors indigenous to the region, providing multilingual, business-to-business and business-to-consumer software applications in the next three years.  technology localization will be the key success factor of penetrating the asian markets, the idc said.  right now australia and new zealand are the leading driver of sales for e-commerce software vendors in the region. this is mainly a result of the use of english as the main language medium, a relatively mature information technology infrastructure and high internet user penetration. in addition, the hottest markets for ecommerce software adoption among innovative companies are singapore, malaysia, south korea and taiwan, the idc said.

title: sixty percent of government departments open websites
body: about 60 percent of chinese government departments will go on-line this year, according to the ministry of information industry (mii).  so far, more than 720 government departments have opened web pages on the internet to send out information about their functions, programs, regulations and activities.  this represents a big step forward for the country's information industry as well as for those government developments, said an official with the mii.  the year 1999 is described as the year for government departments to go onto the internet. the idea of creating electronic government was initiated by the china telecom and the state economic and trade commission.  "the move has improved efficiency, and increased political transparency," said wang yuxin, from the china telecom, the backbone of chinese information super-highway.  for a lot of chinese on the street, it is still not an easy thing to get across the guarded gate of a government compound in beijing. to reach the government through the internet help unwrap the mysteries.  the government departments that have opened websites include ministries of the state council such as the ministry of foreign affairs and ministry of foreign trade and economic commission, as well as provincial governments.  the ministry of education has opened on-line schools and the ministry of labor and social security offers information on employment through its portal.  some ministry officials even make public their personal email addresses on the internet to solicit public opinions. according to the mii estimation, 80 percent of chinese government departments will have their own websites next year.

title: singapore airlines introduces internet booking
body: singapore airlines (sia) will launch tuesday an internet-based system called sq-etravel, which will allow sia customers to use the internet to book their seats and pay for sia tickets, the sia announced monday. sia said from july 13, 1999, sia customers flying between singapore and five destinations --hongkong, kuala lumpur, london, manchester and penang --will be able to book their travel via the internet through sq-etravel at www.singaporeair.com. the service, 24 hours a day and seven days a week, will initially be available for economy class travel and will be extended to all classes by september 1999 and more routes will be added by the end of the year, sia said. customers booking their travel through sq-etravel can collect their boarding pass by producing the credit card used to make the booking as verification, sia explained further. recounting the merits of the system, sia said sq-etravel will offer customers greater convenience, choice and control in planning their travel and provide them a just-mouse-clicking means to check flight availability, select the flight of their choice, order a special meal, pay on-line by entering their credit card details and print a receipt. sia also said planning is underway to enhance the system to allow first and business class customers to view real-time seat map and select their preferred seat.

title: south asia has lowest number of internet users: report
body: only 0.04 percent of the population in the south asian region are internet users, the lowest in the world, a united nations report released here monday said.  south asia accounts for 23.5 percent of the world population but only 0.04 of them are internet users, well below the world average of 2.4 percent, said the human development report 1999 commissioned by the u.n. development program.  in the sub-saharan african region, 0.1 percent of the population are internet users while the arabian states have 0.2 percent users, followed by eastern europe, the commonwealth of independent states and east asia with 0.4 percent, the report said.  it noted that the southeast asia and the pacific have 0.5 percent internet users, the latin american and the caribbean region have 0.8 percent users while the percentage for the organization for economic cooperation and development countries (excluding the unitedstates) is 6.9 percent.  the unitedstates, which accounts for a mere 4.7 percent of the world population, has more computers than the rest of the world combined. of its total population, 26.3 percent are internet users, the report said.  it said that the internet, the worldwide computer link-up, is the "fastest growing tool of communication ever," with the number of users expected to grow from 150 million today to more than 700 million in 2001.  the number of internet hosts --computers with a direct connection to the internet --rose from under 100,000 in 1988 to over 36 million in 1998, it said.  "information and communications technology are tremendous tools for development and can open a fast track to knowledge-based growth, a track followed by india's software programming, ireland's computing services and the caribbean's data processing," the report added.

title: "bangladesh marches ahead" goes online
body: bangladesh marches ahead" --"three years' success of the present government" went onto information super highway (world wide web) monday, with foreign minister abdus samad azad inaugurating the internet website at a ceremony in his office. azad inaugurated the website, which has been produced by the external publicity wing of the foreign ministry by browsing it for the first time at http://www.bangladeshonline.com/gob/mofa/. "bangladesh marches ahead", the official home page of the bangladeshi government, contains in brief the following subjects with various pictures: country profile (1998-99 latest data); the presidency; law, justice and parliamentary affairs; peace dawns in the hills (chittagong hill tracts); poverty alleviation; the economy; local government; foreign relations; information and mass media; disaster management and relief operations; education; health; and the vision for the future. people from any corner of the world would be able to visit the site at any time, azad told newsmen present on the occasion. besides, the website is also linked with the email address of the prime minister's office to help the interested persons to send their comments and suggestions on the site with the click of a mouse button, a foreign ministry official said.

title: middle east economic briefs
body: the following are economic briefs from middle east countries. cairo --arab aviation companies are expected to spend around 54 billion unitedstates dollars on the purchase of 700 new aircraft until the year 2017 to meet the rising competition and the increasing demand of regional air transport facilities, the arab daily al hayat reported on monday.  most of the aircraft will go to some of the leading arab aviation companies, such as saudi airways, gulf airways, uae airways and egyptair. sanaa --an official source at the yemeni ministry of oil and mineral resources said that yemen will witness new expansion in petroleum production at the jenna sector, east of shibwa governorate in july. about 40,000 barrels of oil will bring the total output of that sector to 65,000 barrels per day. riyadh --the bahraini telecommunications company has decided to invest 4 million unitedstates dollars in promoting internet services, said bahraini minister of communications sheikh ali bin al-khalifa.  the gulf news agency quoted the minister as saying that a specialized american company has worked out a comprehensive study on all equipment and outfits to upgrade the internet services provided by the company.  and the company has already embarked on expanding its capacity to cover 40,000 users and introducing new technologies.  internet users would get access to much better services by the end of september, said the minister. cairo --an agreement was signed here sunday for the sale of the egyptian beni suef cement company to a french firm of desforges at a total price of 1.2 billion egyptian pounds (350 million unitedstates dollars). desforges is the third largest world cement manufacture with 34 factories all over the world.

title: boc launches internet banking services
body: the bank of china (boc) announced today that it has launched a range of internet banking services providing its customers with online shopping facilities.  the vice-president of the boc, hua qingshan said that this will enable boc customers to conduct online inquiries, account transfers, payments, settlements and other business.  he said that the boc had introduced the state of the art secure electronic transaction model in designing its internet services, in a bid to ensure the security of online payments and shopping.  according to hua, these services include corporate online financing, internet payments and bank-securities express.  the corporate online financing provides corporate customers with online account inquiries, corporate internal transfer of accounts, statements on international income and expenditure and other services.  the internet payment service enables individual customers to do online shopping using the great wall charge card issued by the boc, while bank-securities express is specially designed for securities firms to conduct capital clearing businesses.  "boasting the most advanced internet security measures, these new services can ensure the safety of card holders' trading information," hua said.

title: studies on china's internet market released
body: china's internet user base will exceed 33 million by 2003, growing at an annual rate of nearly 60 percent over the next five years, a unitedstates market research firm reported monday.  in 1999, chinese internet users will climb from 2.1 million last year to more than 6.7 million, according to the strategis group, which has recently conducted a study jointly with bda (china) limited, the leading internet and telecom market strategy firm in china.  the two firms suggest that china is already the fastest growing internet market in asia and will become one of the world's leading markets in the next five years.  with more than 33 million users by 2003, according to the joint study, each new user that comes online creates new opportunities for internet-related business, enabling companies to leverage their technology, service or capital in "one of the world's most exciting internet markets." china's market for internet service providers (isp) is experiencing "survival of the fattest," the strategis group said. those isps, typically owned or funded by china telecom, with access to the fattest pipes such as dial-up lines, leased lines and internet bandwidth, have emerged on top. nevertheless, opportunities are growing for new players, including cable tv operators, to tap revenues in the isp market, which are forecast to exceed 4 billion unitedstates dollars by 2003.  china also presents a burgeoning market opportunity for internet equipment, software and service. this sector is expected to exceed 160 million unitedstates dollars in 1999. foreign vendors currently dominate china's internet infrastructure market, but domestic players are expanding their efforts to serve this growing market, said the strategis group.  according to a report released early this year by china internet network information center (cinic), the number of internet users in china has been growing at an annual rate of over 100 percent. the center's more conservative estimation is that the users will surpass six million by 2000.

title: worldwide e-commerce to top 1 trillion by
body: explosive growth of the internet is expected to push purchases over the world wide web to top one trillion unitedstates dollars by 2003, according to a report released monday.  because of the increase in the number of people who make purchases over the web, said unitedstates market research firm international data corporation (idc), the growth of the average transaction size, and the adoption of the web as a viable vehicle for business procurement, internet commerce will grow substantially.  according to idc, the number of users who make purchases over the web will jump from 31 million in 1998 to more than 183 million in 2003 worldwide. furthermore, there is ample opportunity to expand the 183 million as it will represent only 36 percent of all web users.  internet commerce is currently unitedstates-centric. in 1998, idc said, non-unitedstates internet commerce accounted for only 26 percent of worldwide spending, although 56 percent of web users resided outside the unitedstates. by 2003, idc estimates 65 percent of web users will be international, and the unitedstates will account for less than half worldwide internet commerce.  as for reasons for the unitedstates focus today, idc cited higher home pc penetration and the percentage of business pcs that access the internet in the unitedstates than foreign countries. "but this is changing as europe and other regions quickly accept the web," idc said.

title: web finding its way into rural america
body: internet usage by commercial farmers in the unitedstates has more than doubled over the past two years, according to a report released thursday.  "the computer and the internet have become just as important to farmers as the tractor and good weather," said the report from rockwood, a subsidiary of farm journal corp. and an information service company for the unitedstates agricultural community. the market research firm conducted a survey in april.  the study shows that two-thirds of all commercial farmers own at least one computer. in addition, these farmers spend, on average, at least two hours per week using the internet for agriculture purposes.  according to an earlier study conducted by the unitedstates department of agriculture in 1997, 13 percent of unitedstates farms had internet access, 31 percent of farms owned or leased computers, and 20 percent used a computer for their farm business.  there were approximately 2.06 million crop and stock farms in the unitedstates in 1997. the percentage of crop farms' computer ownership and internet access was somewhat higher than that of stock farms.  the latest study found that farmers use computers mostly for financial reporting and analysis and for business record keeping.  more and more, however, commercial farmers are becoming heavier users of the internet.  "we are seeing evidence that farmers will migrate quickly toward web-based transactions, such as purchasing seed, crop chemicals and farm equipment on the internet," rockwood said. the firm expects internet usage by farmers to be tripled compared with 1997 by the end of this year.  currently, farmers use the internet to gather information, such as commodity prices, and information about weather, farm machinery and chemicals. about a third of current internet farm users said during the survey that they are interested in shopping for agriculture products on-line in the future.

title: malaysian govt supports communications development
body: the malaysian government will continue to support the development of communications and internet infrastructure to facilitate more efficient and cost-effective business transactions.  when closing the microsoft executive summit '99 here tuesday, energy, communications and multimedia minister datuk leo moggie said the prospect to market goods and services to the fast-growing number of internet users in the country remains very bright.  the multimedia super corridor (msc), the kuala lumpur international airport, smart schools, cyber laws, the communications and multimedia act and the setting up of the communications and multimedia commission are to facilitate and advance the growth of this sector, he said.  "these steps taken by the government are in recognition of the importance and impact of technology and multimedia on the economy today. various measures have also been put in place by the government to encourage malaysians to embrace the power of technology," he said.  he said local higher institutions of learning will supply some 25,000 local graduates in computer science, engineering, arts and design, information technology (it) and multimedia fields to meet the need of the present 216 msc-status companies for 35,000 skilled workers by 2001.  moggie said the government welcomes companies such as microsoft with their technology, knowledge and experience to share with business people their vision of how a networked environment can transform malaysian companies into living organisms with a digital nervous system.

title: singapore announces liberalization of internet exchange services
body: the telecommunication authority of singapore will open up the market of international internet exchange service in singapore as another step towards achieving its goal of becoming an internet hub and information society.  minister for communications and information technology yeo cheow tong made the announcement in his address at the opening ceremony tuesday for the telecommunication exhibition communicasia 99.  yeo said the move to allow more providers of internet exchange service in singapore will enhance singapore's attractiveness as a portal for high speed access to the internet backbone.  "in addition, the asian internet access service providers (iasps) will also have more means to interconnect via singapore and this will encourage the development of an intra-asian internet network," yeo said.  internet exchanges are physical interconnection sites for iasps to access the global internet backbone and exchange traffic with one another. such exchanges will enable iasps traffic to be aggregated before being sent via leased circuits to the unitedstates internet backbone and the regional countries.  yeo also billed information and communications technology (ict) as the key driver and transformer in the net economy and information society of the future and said that his ministry is in the midst of formulating the ict21 master plan to facilitate the development of ict in singapore over the next 10 years.  "our vision is to transform singapore into a dynamic and vibrant global ict capital with a thriving and prosperous net economy by the year 2010," he affirmed.  he said the ict21 master plan will map out strategies to attain three key objectives which include developing the ict sector as the key sector of growth in singapore's economy, using ict as a common platform to boost the performance of singapore's knowledge-based economy and leveraging on ict to enhance the quality of life and standard of living of singaporeans in the information society of the future.  some 900 companies from 40 countries and regions participate in the communicasia 99 which will last to june 25.

title: electronic commerce thrives in china
body: the rapidly increasing number of internet users in china has paved the way for the introduction of electronic commerce.  there were two million registered internet users in china at the end of 1998, and the number is estimated to rise to 20 million by the year 2000, laying a good foundation for the development of e-commerce in the country.  electronic business activities, such as on-line ticketing, shopping, banking and securities trading, as well as declaration of dutiable goods, are gaining popularity among chinese commercial circles and ordinary residents.  a growing number of government departments have launched websites on the internet, in answer to the "government-online" plans, which call for 60 percent of related departments to be available on-line by the end of 1999, with the figure rising to 80 percent by 2000.  e-commerce is drawing increasing attention from the chinese government and the country's electronic-commerce framework is to be publicized soon by an office under the ministry of the information industry.  east china's zhejiang province, one of the country's economic giants, had 50,000 registered internet users by the end of april, with the figure growing by 20 percent annually. some 80 percent of internet users in the province show interest in on-line shopping, according to a recent survey.

title: internet users in north america continue to increase
body: the number of internet users in north america has now reached 92 million, and the commercial growth of the web is emerging as a dominant trend in the development of the internet.  according to an april 1999 study released thursday by two unitedstates organizations that have conducted demographic and e-commerce studies of the internet since 1995, the number of internet users aged 16 and older in the unitedstates and canada increased 16 percent in just nine months, and the number of on-line consumers jumped 40 percent to 28 million during the same period.  the increase in the adoption of the internet by consumers is, for the first time, being driven by women, as the number of female consumers on-line jumped 80 percent in nine months, and passed the 10-million mark.  the study, based on interviews with 7,200 people, was conducted by commercenet, a silicon valley-based grouping of e-commerce, and nielsen media research, the leading provider of television audience measurement and related services in the unitedstates and canada.  "more than two of every five people in north america are now internet users, and the web is becoming an integral part of daily life," said a report based on the study. "with more than 30 percent of users being internet consumers, we're seeing a tidal wave of e-commerce in north america." the study found that the proportion of women among on-line buyers increased nine percentage points, from 29 percent to 38 percent since last summer.  now women are active buyers in all the major product categories, such as books, cds/videos, computer hardware and clothing.  of today's 92 million internet users in north america, 46 percent are women, and 41 percent of today's 55 million internet shoppers are women.  of the 28 million people who have made purchases via the web, 9 million people made purchases once a month, and 1 million people made purchases at least once a week.

title: internet users in north america rise to 92 million
body: the number of people over 16 in the unitedstates and canada using the internet has climbed to 92 million, according to a new survey released on thursday.  the study by nielsen media research and commercenet also shows dramatic increases in the number of women who made at least a single purchase using the internet, rising 80 percent over nine months ago.  the most popular items for women to buy on the web were books, cds and videos with 9.6 million purchases of those items taken together. but in a twist, the number of women buying computers over the internet climbed fastest at 160 percent to 1.3 million during the past nine months.  men also bought mostly books, cds and videos but also bought far more computers --4.1 million --than women.  among both men and women, online purchases of software remained flat.  the survey, based on interviews with more than 7,200 people in north america, said 54 percent of people on the internet are men --although men still represent a slightly higher proportion, 62 percent, of all online buyers.  the same study last august showed 79 million people over 16 on the internet in north america with 43 percent of them women. the study in september 1997 counted 58 million, also with 43 percent women.  the latest study also said 72 million people use the internet from home, while 46 million use it from work and 28 million from school. the rest use it from other locations, such as a library or a friend's home.  nielsen and commercenet said the results of its latest study were statistically representative of north america's population of 225 million people over the age 16.

title: quick pace urged for canada's web shopping
body: quick pace is being urged in canada for shopping on-line in order to keep traditional customers while expanding business operations.  only 26 percent of top canadian stores use electronic commerce and web sites to attract consumers, compared with 50 percent of u.  s. major retailers, said a study released monday by the leading canadian industry group for retailers.  ibm canada ltd. and the retail council indicated in the study that even within the 26 percent of canada's shopping on-line businesses, more than 60 percent of the money goes to unitedstates web sites, underlining a view that canadians have been slow to enter the e-retail race.  "unless canadian retailers establish an on-line presence in the next six months, they risk losing traditional store customers and new e-retail shoppers to global competitors," said david marcus, managing principal of retail consumer consulting at ibm of markham, ontario, canada canadian shopping on-line is predicted to increase from about 690 million canadian dollars (about 472.6 million unitedstates dollars) last year to 1.15 billion (about 787.67 million unitedstates dollars) this year. it will soar to 12.75 billion (8.73 billion unitedstates dollars) in 2003, according to forecasts by research house international data corp.
