title: chinese government to open office work on internet
body: the guangzhou municipal government, capital of south china's guangdong province, has signed a deal with china telecom guangdong branch to open an internet website for its daily operations.  after linking to the net, its daily work will be open to public scrutiny. all internet users will be able to refer to the website for details of how things are going on inside government offices.  people from business circles, especially those from overseasfunded businesses often complain about low working efficiency and some underhand operations inside local government departments that hinder the smooth running of some economic projects.  in an effort to insert more operating transparency and efficiency, the central government has urged government departments to open websites by the end of this year.  so far, 57 government websites can be found on the net, where internet users can easily get access to such information as project approvals and taxation indices, something that they must get from civil servants otherwise.  the country has witnessed a vigorous growth in internet use over the past few years with the number of subscribers reaching 1.  5 million. however, people are complaining about the lack of updated domestic news on the internet.  the government websites are expected to expand the sources of official information released on the internet and accelerate the network information growth in the country, according to chinese government officials.  some local governments have learned to use their websites as an electronic bulletin to publish their local strategy and economic advantages.

title: u.s. to allow political fund raising on internet
body: the federal election commission (fec) of the unitedstates voted 6-0 thursday to allow presidential candidates to raise money over the internet.  the ruling will allow presidential candidates who take credit card donations on their web sites to qualify for federal matching dollars during the primary elections, thus giving a major boost to political fund raising in cyberspace.  the ruling will have a sweeping effect for the major presidential candidates, all of whom have web sites, observers here said.  the existing fec regulation had in fact forbidden candidates from collecting federal matching funds on such donations via credit card.  "we recognize the reality that the internet is here and a big part of our life," fec chairman scott thomas said after the vote.  "we need to let it be used freely." the fec voted to allow presidential campaigns to begin collecting credit card donations in anticipation of receiving matching funds for them next january 1.  barring disapproval from the congress or the president, the new regulations would take effect in a few months.  the commission, which oversees campaign laws, is made up of six members split evenly along party lines.

title: hke060939--newspapers not hurt by internet australia: media baron
body: widespread predictions of doom for newspapers in the wake of booming internet and pay television use in australia were groundless, said malcolm noad, general manager of the global media empire news limited group, on wednesday.  in a speech to a meeting of the australian marketing institute in the south australian port city of adelaide, noad said that despite a dramatic rise in internet use and availability of pay-tv in australia during the past decade, newspaper circulation and readership had increased.  "weekday circulation has been steady to rising over the last few years; monday to friday we sell an average of 2.4 million papers per day, 3.2 million on saturday, 3.5 million on sunday," noad said.  he said the average australian over 14 years old spent four hours and 26 minutes per week reading a newspaper, up 11 minutes from three years ago.  about 23 percent of australian adult population accessed the internet in the 12 months to february, 1998, the australian bureau of statistics said earlier this year.  noad said this was despite internet use increasing dramatically from a few "computer boffins" a decade ago to access now being available in about one million australian homes, with the average person spending 25 minutes per week on the net.  "where are people finding the time to sit back on the internet?" he asked.  "they are spending one hour less on watching tv and half-an-hour less on listening to the radio," he said.  noad said the key to newspapers succeeding in an increasingly competitive media market was to create a highly recognizable and trustworthy brand name.  "(news corporation chairman) rupert murdoch summed up our strategy for dealing with the challenge of choice -'faced with the chaos of choice on the one hand and the need to plug quickly into what's happening on the other, people will turn quickly to familiar names'," he said.  noad said news limited used promotions, competitions and loyalty-building products such as lifestyle magazines to boost readership, but sports coverage was the key product.

title: worldwide recovery for semiconductor industry forecasted
body: the global semiconductor market will show recovery this year and double digit growth through 2002, according to new forecasts of a unitedstates industry trade group.  total semiconductor sales worldwide are expected to reach 140.8 billion unitedstates dollars this year, up 12 percent over 1998 --the biggest jump and first year of recovery since 1995, said the semiconductor industry association (sia). in 2000, sales will expand to 162.5 billion dollars, an increase of 15.4 percent.  the sia expects the market to continue its momentum in 2001 with sales of 191 billion dollars increasing 17.6 percent. in 2002, global sales will reach 215.7 billion dollars increasing 12.9 percent.  according to the sia, the internet has been the predominate growth driver for the industry and has demonstrated the shift of pcs --a product which drove the industry in the early 1990s --to the internet and e-commerce. "the electronic highway is paved with silicon chips," said the sia, expecting the continuation of internet traffic growth which will demand infrastructure growth.  the america's market will remain the world's largest in the next four years, representing about one-third of the chip revenues worldwide, the sia said. the asia-pacific region, excluding japan, will make a come-back and emerge as the second largest chip market, shedding the effects of the asian economic crisis that contributed to the 4.4 percent decline of that market last year.  europe will be right behind asia-pacific. japan is still being impacted by the protracted domestic recession.

title: impact of pcs, internet to be explored
body: a unitedstates university announced tuesday the first comprehensive study ever conducted of the sweeping changes produced by the internet.  the study will focus on how computers, information technology and their users are shaping society and how the internet is changing the world, said the university of california, los angeles (ucla) in a statement.  "understanding how people use the internet is even more important than understanding the impact of television," said the statement. "while television is primarily about our leisure time, the internet is already transforming work, school and play.  virtually every business, political and social activity will be affected by the internet, and most activities will be dramatically transformed." funded by america online, microsoft and other companies, the study will survey computer users as well as non-users in the unitedstates, singapore and italy, and will expand to additional 15 countries in europe, asia, latin america and africa over the next three to five years. the ucla center for communication policy which has conceived the study will conduct the unitedstates survey and coordinate the international partner projects.  results of the first study will be released late this year. as part of the release of the second study in 2000, the university will host an international conference for policymakers and industry leaders.

title: u.s. market for electronic funds transfer software expands
body: financial institutions in the unitedstates have made great efforts to deploy transaction processing technology to assist in lowering costs and offering better services to customers, said a research report released tuesday.  according to the research conducted by market analysis firm frost sullivan, the total market for electronic funds transfer software reached 100 million unitedstates dollars in 1998, up 21 percent from a year ago. the market is expected to generate a revenue of 148 million dollars by 2005.  the market for automatic teller machine (atm) processing software accounted for 41 million dollars in 1998. factors driving growth in the market are the continued growth of the internet, integrated architecture and more functionality in atms.  meanwhile, the growth in e-commerce spurred sales of point of sale (pos) transaction processing software, reaching 45 million dollars last year. the market witnessed a rising debit card transactions as well as internet-based payments. although debit cards have yet to be adopted on a mainstream level in the unitedstates, the report said, the growth of e-commerce will be sufficient to generate new sales of pos software during the next five to six years.  internet banking software is another aspect of the growing market, with revenues totaling 14 million dollars in 1998. early adopters so far are large banks, but some community banks are beginning to follow suit. the report said that as more features are added to the core functions of internet banking software, such as mutual fund transactions and loan applications, the market will grow briskly in the next few years.  continued support for standards and interoperability will serve the market well in light of the growing trend toward integration with legacy systems of complete flexibility. future growth may come from the availability of browser-based atms which will greatly reduce costs, simplify software upgrades and become a strong driving force behind this continuously growing market, the report said.

title: key industrial stocks push australian stocks higher
body: the australian sharemarket pushed higher monday as some key industrial stocks provided support for a market initially buoyed by a healthy rise on wall street.  the benchmark all ordinaries index finished 14.8 points stronger at 2,944.1 but off a high of 2,956.5 struck earlier in the day.  the turnover was modest with 281.43 million shares changing hands for 453.38 million unitedstates dollars.  falling stocks outnumbered rises, despite the overall positive tone of the market, 576 to 569. steady trades numbered 437.  the all industrials index lifted 24 points to 5,191.4 while the all resources index picked up 8.5 points to 1,144.7.  providing much of the support was market heavyweight, rupert murdoch's news corp.  ordinary and preferred shares in the company both shot up 20 cents to 13.55 australian dollars and 12.55 australian dollars, respectively.  traders said news corp continued to benefit from reports of better-than-expected advertising revenues for its unitedstates fox television division.  the interest rate sensitive banking sector closed with mixed fortunes as the sub-index gained 31.1 points to 6,697.7.  the biggest four banks in australia were evenly split with the commonwealth bank of australia jumping 40 cents to 25.26 australian dollars and the national australia bank soaring 64.7 cents to 26.60 australian dollars, while anz bank shed 32 cents to 10.86 australian dollars and westpac bank lost 18.6 cents to 10.09 australian dollars.  in the resources sector, market leader bhp rose nine cents to 16.40 australian dollars and global miner rio tinto put on 15 cents to 22.65 australian dollars.  the gold sector was a dull spot in the market with the sub-index slipping 8.5 points to 829.1. gold price in sydney closed at 265.50 unitedstates dollars an ounce compared to friday's close of 266.75 unitedstates dollars.

title: shanghai unveils china's own "venus"
body: in a bid to tackle head on microsoft emperor bill gates in his venus plan project for use with ordinary televisions, which he announced in shenzhen in early march, the shanghai gotop research co. ltd. today unveiled a similar, rival net-surfing gadget, the east-1 machine.  part of the company's much vaunted "east plan", the new east-1 machine can enable users of regular tv sets to have access to the internet for on-line games, software, emails and other facilities, gotop's general manager cui wei said at a news conference here today.  customers can also use the new product for word processing just like the personal computer and may use it as a fax machine as well as a video cd player, according to cui.  the shanghai yihao industrial co. ltd. signed a contract with the gotop to buy 100,000 of its east-1 on the spot.  industry analysts have an optimistic view on the future of the new products as china remains the world's largest potential computer and electrical appliances market.  the availability of personal computers to chinese families is less than three percent and china's "netizens" have just exceeded two million.  "since the east-1 has been researched and developed by domestic manufacturers, its price will be only half of the venus operating system," cui said.

title: u.s. internet penetration continues to grow
body: a total of 67.5 million personal computers in the unitedstates regularly accessed the internet as of january this year, up 50 percent over a year ago, according to a new report released by marketing company ziff-davis this week.  while 31 million home pcs accounted for the largest number of internet-connected pcs, the report said, the workplace segment contributed the highest increase, growing 76 percent last year to almost 28 million pcs.  according to the study based on over 11,000 pc users, 60 percent of unitedstates households with a pc accessed the internet at year-end 1998, bringing the total to 31.2 million. more than 8 million new unitedstates households logged onto the internet in 1998. this household penetration growth continues to be fueled by newly purchased pcs, the report said.  email continues to be the top internet activity among all types of users and has driven much of the growth of the internet to date, the report said. ziff-davis analysts said there is a network effect: the more people on the internet, the larger the attraction and value of the internet for each additional user. the emergence of cheap pcs has also diminished the cost barriers associated with connecting to the internet.

title: more u.s. households expected to be banking online
body: more than 32 million households in the unitedstates are expected to be banking online by 2003, according to a research released tuesday.  online banking is becoming fast a convenient functionality in the country craved by the growing horde of internet users. in 1998, there were already 6.6 million unitedstates households banking online, said the unitedstates market research firm international data corporation (idc).  describing factors driving the explosive growth in online banking, idc said that there has been a proliferation of low-cost pcs and other networking devices in the home market, which is causing a surge in the number of internet users. "because many of the security concerns have been alleviated," the research firm said, "these internet users are becoming comfortable using the internet as a transaction-based medium." the increasing number of banks offering web-based banking services is also triggering the market's growth. idc estimates the number of banks in the unitedstates offering online services will increase from 1,150 in 1998 to more than 15,800 by 2003, primarily via the web. these numbers represent 6 percent and 86 percent respectively of all unitedstates commercial banks and credit unions.  a strong link exists between banking, bill payments and the internet, idc said. "although there is still uncertainty in the bill presentment market," the research firm said, "banks must seize this tremendous opportunity in front of them. online banking may be the critical service that enables banks to maintain their role as the dominant provider of financial services."

title: chinese official says cox report is like hollywood movie script
body: a senior chinese official has suggested that the unitedstates's cox report should have been made into a movie in hollywood with a disclaimer at the beginning, saying " this is pure fiction." at a press conference here this afternoon, zhao qizheng, director of the information office of the state council, commented on the may 25 report, saying that china has never stolen secrets from the unitedstates nuclear weapons lab, as it claims. zhao showed chinese and foreign journalists pictures and technological instructions on w79, w87, w88, and the f-117a nighthawk that were from the internet.  "an ordinary chinese or american without much knowledge about the military might find all this data on warheads surprising," zhao, once a senior engineer, told xinhua, "but, in fact the information is open to the public in the unitedstates and anyone who has access to the internet can get it." zhao said that the cox report is a fabrication for people who are not insiders about someone who just sneaked into some taiwanbased connection of the central intelligence agency's, opened a safe, and took the classified documents about w87 or w88.  "this is like something out of the james bond series," he said.  afterwards, an engineer from the china internet information center showed the journalists how to get at these so-called secrets on the internet.

title: moneyworld asia '99 held in hong kong
body: the latest financial products and services will be displayed at the fourth moneyworld asia hongkong exhibition, which opened friday at the hongkong convention and exhibition center.  with a theme "equip yourself to be a smart investor" the fair this year puts emphasis on investor education.  more than 40 local and international financial institutions take part in the event.  the rapid development of internet services back up by information technology has opened new opportunities for both service providers and investors.  moneyworld asia will therefore keep visitors abreast of the latest trends of on-line financial services such as electronic trading, stock exchanges on the internet, real-time stock quotes and on-line financial news.  organized by the hongkong trade development council (tdc), the exhibition will run until may 30 at the hkcec.  sponsors of the exhibition include the securities and futures commission, the hongkong stock exchange, the hongkong futures exchange and the hongkong investment funds association.  tdc executive director michael sze said at the opening ceremony of the exhibition that hongkong plays an important role in propelling the growth of the regional financial sector as the regional markets start to recover.  sze said that asian economies are trying their best to manage both financial reforms and corporate changes in a bid to regain vitality and competitiveness.  "with china's mainland continuing to liberalize its financial sector, unprecedented opportunities for the region are being created," sze said.  all these factors make moneyworld asia, the most comprehensive money management and investment event in hongkong, most relevant, sze added.  addressing the opening ceremony, liu jinbao, general manager of bank of china hongkong branch and chairman of the hongkong association of banks (hkab), said that the banking system is playing a pivotal role in sustaining hongkong's status as a world financial center.  this year will remain as a tough year for the local banking sector, liu said. however, it has more breathing space, he added.  interest rates have been cut three times since liu's inception as the chairman of the hkab early this year and bank's cost for funding has been lowered.

title: oracle seminar helps hk firms maximize e-business opportunities
body: the hongkong leg of idevelop'99 sponsored by leading software company oracle corporation opened here thursday.  the two-day idevelop'99 comprises of conferences, seminars and hands-on development sessions for local internet developers and software companies.  the largest of its kind in hongkong, the event aims to provide participants with the latest technologies, tools and support initiatives to develop applications for e-business.  "to maximize the opportunities that the internet provides, developers need new tools and a new way of developing and deploying applications," said mark jarvis, oracle's senior vice president of worldwide marketing.  "idevelop'99 aims to introduce developers to oracle's internet computing platform so that they can build e-business applications that take full advantage of the immense business opportunities on the web," said jarvis.  according to jarvis, the internet technology of oracle, the world's leading supplier of information management software with annual revenues of over 8.3 billion unitedstates dollars, has helped the success of e-business sites such as amazon.com, yahoo, and exite.  according to the 1998 collaborative marketing survey, nearly 70 percent of the world's top e-business sites use oracle's database, tools and application products.  "as hongkong strives to become the leading city in asia for ebusiness, it is critical that we develop our expertise in building applications that take full advantage of the internet," said arics poon, oracle's hongkong manager.  "by building new internet applications, local developers and software companies can strengthen hongkong's position as a worldclass, competitive service center," poon said.

title: worldwide internet services revenues projected
body: revenues in the worldwide internet services market will earn a compound annual growth rate of nearly 60 percent in the next five years and pass 78 billion unitedstates dollars by 2003, according to a report released tuesday.  worldwide revenues in the emerging market grew 71 percent in 1998 to reach 7.8 billion unitedstates dollars, said unitedstates research firm international data corporation (idc).  in addition to becoming more prominent, said idc explaining the rapid market expansion, internet projects are becoming more sophisticated and complex, demanding different skills of programmers, designers and business strategists. because companies are having extreme difficulties locating and hiring employees with these skills, they are turning to outside service providers to fulfil their needs.  in addition, corporations are under increasing pressure to execute projects faster and with greater reliability, which is also causing them to turn to outside providers.  according to idc, the unitedstates currently spends more than other regions on internet services. in 1998, it accounted for more than half worldwide spending, with 4.6 billion unitedstates dollars.  western europe is the second-largest market and will maintain a five-year compound annual growth rate of 67 percent between this year and 2003.  unlike traditional, established markets where brand, reputation and years of experience play an important role in the purchasing decision, in today's internet services market issues such as flexibility and creativity are important. therefore, idc said, the emerging market offers a relatively even playing field, allowing for some of the new breed of internet service firms to capture market share, although large, traditional information technology service firms currently dominate the market.

title: internet promotes database software market
body: the worldwide market for database management software (dbms) grew 18 percent to five billion unitedstates dollars in 1998, said a new study released monday.  explaining the rapid market growth, frost sullivan, a unitedstates market research firm that conducted the study, said the internet caused an explosion of data in terms of web content.  in the future, many business practices, including business-tobusiness electronic data interchange (edi), e-commerce and ebusiness, will utilize internet technologies, compounding the need for efficient storage and management software, according to the study.  the edi market is expected to grow from 937 million unitedstates dollars in 1996 to two billion dollars by 2000, according to an earlier forecast by dataquest, also a unitedstates market research firm.  this segment embraces the electronic communication of business transactions, such as orders, confirmations and invoices between organizations.  the dbms controls the organization, storage, retrieval, security and integrity of the data in a database.  the software accepts requests from the application and instructs the operating system to transfer the appropriate data.  according to frost sullivan, the majority of dbms revenues are generated in north america and europe.  the asia-pacific region and the rest of the world are much smaller markets, but they are expected to comprise larger shares of the world market by the end of 2005.  the total database market is split into relational database and object-oriented database.  in a relational database, relationships between files are created by comparing data, while the latter is suited for data with complex relationships that are difficult to model and process in a relational manner and also capable of handling multimedia data types like images, audio and video.  the research firm said that relational database comprised almost 98 percent of the dbms market in 1998.  factors that will drive the relational database software market include the growth of the internet, explosive interest in e-business and demand for improved customer information.

title: internet calls boom boosts bt profits
body: british telecom (bt) has enjoyed record profits on the back of the explosion in internet usage and the growth of calls to mobile phones.  profits rose 22.4 percent in the last quarter to leave 1998-99 profits up 4.5 percent at 3.3 billion pounds even before an exceptional windfall of 1 billion pounds from the group's failed attempt to buy us group mci.  much of this growth came from a 9 percent increase in domestic call volumes and a near doubling of internet access customers compared with the last quarter of the previous year.  an announcement by bt wednesday showed that 18 percent of local residential calls during march were surfing on the internet, up from 15 percent in december and 8 percent in the previous year.  iain vallance, the bt chairman, said the company was traditionally a bellwether for the uk economy and the strong growth in turnover "reinforces the view that things are getting rather better than they were before".  however, bt's robust performance also re-ignited speculation that it might be tempted to join the merger mania that is sweeping the telecoms sector.  commenting on a cross border merger, peter bonfield, bt chief executive, said: "if we can get good value and good growth, we are open minded about these things. we want to be a major global player."

title: revenues from web development, software to grow
body: revenues from worldwide web authoring and design software are expected to rise to over one billion unitedstates dollars by the middle of 2002, according to a report released thursday.  as more and more people create internet and intranet sites, the market for tools to create them is boosting, said report by a unitedstates market research firm, the international data corporation (idc).  the growth in this market can be attributed to the large number of small and medium-sized businesses that have recently come online because of the leaps in ease of use.  last year, the worldwide revenues rose 144 percent from 1977 to reach 243 million dollars, said the idc. the unitedstates accounted for 58 percent of the total worldwide web market with the revenues of 140 million dollars and growth in the unitedstates market will peak in 1999. by 2001, the international market will be larger, it added.  web authoring software is a web site development system that allows web pages to be visually created like a desktop publishing program. the idc said that web authoring design tools have improved in two major areas: sophistication, which pleases the high-end web design firm, and in ease of use.  in another report released wednesday, the idc said that the webto-host browser market worldwide is moving full steam, with revenues increasing 370 percent to 112.4 million dollars in 1998 and expected to reach one billion dollars by 2002.  the idc splits the web-to-host market into internet, extranet and intranet. currently, most sales occur in the intranet market.  in 1998, this segment accounted for almost 70 percent of revenues.  the idc expects the internet segment, which accounted for less than five percent in 1998, to account for more than a third of sales by 2003.

title: survey shows internet goes beyond marketing alone
body: a survey released on thursday indicates that electronic commerce not only allows firms to reach the broadest possible audience, it also provides better customer service and cost efficiency.  according to the new poll of 1,400 chief financial officers ( cfos) in unitedstates firms, the internet has been regarded as a tool for expanding a company's market reach, as well as a medium to improve customer service.  the survey was developed by rhi management resources, north america's largest consulting firm. the cfos were asked to identify the greatest benefits for customers by providing e-commerce in their business over the next five years.  while one-in-three cfos said they looked to e-commerce to expand their client base, one-fifth believe that value-added service to customers will be the primary benefit. seventeen percent of them cited reduced operational costs as the chief advantage.  faster service or product delivery was also cited by 13 percent of the cfos surveyed.  the consulting firm said that electronic commerce enables businesses to meet ever-increasing client expectations for easier access to product information, accelerated ordering and fulfillment, and more competitive pricing.  web-based business-to-business transactions can also result in significant savings, particularly within a company's purchasing department, the firm said. handling orders via e-commerce can promote better inventory control and enhanced cash flow.

title: to excel by cybernating traditional strengths
body: richard li, whose pacific century group will play a leading role in the cyberport development, said the project will alleviate five of the seven most important concerns for it companies in hongkong.  these concerns include high costs of office and residential rents, the high cost of labor relative to productivity, environmental pollution and the need to build a critical mass of it talent.  "it will make hongkong the internet-business gateway between china and overseas markets," he said.  in order not to lag behind in tomorrow's economy, li said, hongkong needs to leverage its traditional strengths in sourcing, transport, distribution and services.  the cyberport will create a strategic cluster of leading-edge it-applications companies and leverage hongkong's world class services infrastructure, he noted.  on the education front, hongkong has spent a great sum of fund and effort in the it area. secretary for education and manpower joseph w.p. wong said the government is committed to promoting it in education so that the young people can "grow up with the knowledge, skills and vision to play an active part in the next century." to turn the vision into reality, the special administrative region government announced a five-year strategy entitled " information technology for learning in a new era" last november.  the four key components of the strategy are to enhance hongkong students' access to it and the internet, to provide training and support for all teachers, to use it to support teaching in the school curriculum and to foster a community-wide culture which helps promote it in education.  the special administrative region government has set aside a capital sum of 3 billion hk dollars (384.6 million unitedstates dollars) and will spend an annual amount of 560 million hk dollars (71.8 million unitedstates dollars) to implement various initiatives in its strategy.  in hongkong's major universities, students have benefited from cyber-learning and experienced the latest internet technology such as java application.  earlier this week the sar government announced the allocation of it coordinator posts to 120 public sector schools to develop and implement their it-based initiatives.  the selected schools consist of primary, secondary and special schools.

title: chinese insurers explore internet opportunities
body: more and more insurance companies in china are now setting up their own internet sites to broaden their business opportunities in cyberspace against the backdrop of rapidly increasing internet users.  investigations show that by the beginning of 1997, most of the 25 insurers operating in china had established internet home pages.  these websites not only provide corporate profiles, and the introduction of insurance products and services, but the abcs of insurance as well.  potential customers may also make on-line inquiries through email.  industrial analysts says the internet is able to provide potential customers with faster and easier access to insurance companies and their products. by a few strokes on the keyboard, customers can access the websites of many insurers and make comparisons before making their insurance decision.  for insurance firms, the internet means they have access to a huge number of potential customers, unlimited by time or space.  it is reported that china now has over two million registered internet users, and this figure is expected to hit nearly five million by the end of the century.  in the words of li gang, deputy general manager of the ping an insurance corporation, the internet has expanded the working hours of insurance companies from eight to 24 hours a day.  the internet also means lower overhead for insurance sales.  according to a survey in the unitedstates, the average cost of consultation is five unitedstates dollars per person per time, while online consultation can cost as little as four cents.  however, analysts says china's insurance industry still has a long way from fully utilizing the internet.

title: northeastern china developing foreign trade via internet
body: the port city of dalian city in northeast china's liaoning province has put a great deal of effort into developing foreign trade on the internet, since last year.  last year it sent over 20,000 emails with information about investment projects and exhibition invitations to more than 10,000 multinationals in 78 countries, and received over 4,000 replies.  the local government has also sent a general introduction to the city and trade cooperation invitations to many companies and officials visited 3 european countries, the unitedstates, and canada last year to discuss the city's investment environment.  more than 200 overseas enterprises have informed the local government via the internet of their intention to attend the city's commodities fair this summer.  the city's website contains an investment guide, policy information, investment and cooperative projects, and data on companies in china and abroad. the local government has decided to focus this year on increasing cooperation with multinationals on the internet and to use the internet for the first export and import fair, for technological export negotiations, and for key investment projects.  officials say the government wants a convenient communication channel with foreign countries.

title: xinhua world economic news summary
body: washington --the unitedstates federal reserve decided tuesday that inflation is not signaling a threat to justify an immediate increase in interest rates.  the federal open market committee (fomc), composed of fed board members and regional bank presidents, ended closed-door discussions with a decision to leave the target for the federal funds rate, the interest that banks charge each other, unchanged.  (us-rates) ----new york --wall street stocks moved lower tuesday after the federal reserve decided to leave interest rates unchanged but warned of possibly higher rates in coming months if necessary.  the dow jones industrial average closed down 16.52 at 10,836.95.  the index plunged as much as 110 points in the hour after the federal reserve announced its decision and warning.  broader stock indicators were mixed. the technology heavy nasdaq composite index was down 3.48 at 2,558.36 while the standard poor's 500 index was down 6.17 at 1,333.32. (wall street-stocks) ----los angeles --the percentage of retail sales generated from catalog and the internet is expected to almost double in the unitedstates by 2004, according to a research released tuesday.  last year, catalogs and the internet generated 3.46 percent of total sales of almost 2.7 trillion unitedstates dollars, said a report from the direct marketing association (dma), the largest unitedstates trade association for businesses interested in interactive and database marketing.  (internet-retail sales) ----washington --the world bank announced on tuesday that it will provide a total of 115 million unitedstates dollars in loans and credits to china to support the government in its economic and structural reform effort and help china improve its higher education.  the bank will provide a loan of 35 million dollars and a credit of 10 million dollars to the fourth technical cooperation project, which will provide continued support to the chinese government in its economic and structural reform effort. (wb-china) ----los angeles --coping with downward price pressure and fast-growing new competition are among the most important marketplace challenges over the next year to chief executives around the world.  in a survey of 656 ceos conducted by the conference board, the world's leading business membership and research organization, more than two-thirds of those heading industrial manufacturing firms and 55 percent of those leading consumer products companies say that pressures on prices will be their major market challenge over the next year. (global concern-price pressure) ----islamabad --pakistan will adopt a market-based unitary exchange rate system and abolish the "official" exchange rate on wednesday when the "floating inter-bank rate" will begin to apply to all foreign exchange receipts and payments.  the state bank of pakistan (sbp) made the announcement through a circular late tuesday night.  in the inter-bank market, the unitedstates dollar currently hovers around 50.50 to 51.00 rupees through the patronage of sbp which intervenes to stabilize the dollar rates in the inter-bank regime.  (pakistan-exchange) ----singapore --singapore's economy grew by 1.2 percent in the first quarter of this year after contracting for two consecutive quarters, the ministry of trade and industry announced wednesday.  the 1.2 percent gain was largely on the back of strong performance in the manufacturing sector and growth momentum measured on a seasonally-adjusted quarter-on-quarter basis showed a strong pick-up of 6.8 percent, the ministry said in its economy survey of first quarter 1999. (singapore-economic growth) ----rio de janeiro --direct foreign investment in brazil totaled 9.  24 billion unitedstates dollars in the first four months this year, more than double the figure of the same period last year.  the number surpassed the most optimistic expectations of the market, which stood at around 17 billion dollars for the whole year. they were made following the devaluation of the brazilian currency, the real, months ago. (brazil-foreign investment) ----bangkok --the thai cabinet has approved an extension of its rubber price intervention program for a further three months in a bid to shore up the domestic price amid a depressed market, a government house press release said wednesday.  the new round of intervention is set to begin on june 16, it said.  of the four billion baht (109.6 million unitedstates dollars) approved by the cabinet in working capital for 100,000 tons of stock, 1.9 billion baht (52.1 million dollars) has been used, but a proportion of the money from the export stockpile has been returned to the fund. title: internet impact on u.s. retail sales to double by
body: the percentage of retail sales generated from catalog and the internet is expected to almost double in the unitedstates by 2004, according to a research released tuesday.  last year, catalogs and the internet generated 3.46 percent of total sales of almost 2.7 trillion unitedstates dollars, said a report from the direct marketing association (dma), the largest unitedstates trade association for businesses interested in interactive and database marketing.  dma projected catalog and internet sales to grow annually 6.1 percent and 50.2 percent respectively from 1999 to 2004, while total unitedstates retail sales are growing 3.6 percent each year. as a result, catalogs and the internet are expected to account for 6.25 percent of total retail sales by 2004.  catalog sales are expected to exceed 93 billion dollars in 1999, an increase from 1998 sales of 85 billion dollars. the internet is expected to generate 11 billion dollars in sales in 1999, up from 5.9 billion dollars in 1998.  consumers and businesses are taking advantage of the increasing choices offered to them by the direct marketing community, from companies that are selling from a combination of catalogs, the internet and brick-and-mortar stores, dma said in the report. this trend toward buying more from catalog and the internet, dma said, reveals an opportunity for marketers, especially the 84 percent of catalog companies that have a presence on the web.

title: china marks world telecommunication day
body: china marked the 31st world telecommunication day, which has the theme of "e-commerce", by launching a "government on-line" project today. at a launch ceremony, minister of information industry wu jichuan confirmed that china now has 12 million personal computers and 1.54 million internet users.  he pointed out that in recent years information services have been growing rapidly in china. now, a public data and multi-media network covers more than 2,000 counties, cities and townships around the country, with 744,000 mainframe computers linked to the internet.  zhang ligui, head of the country's largest internet service provider and operator china telecom, said that the company has followed closely the latest developments of services and technology in the international telecommunication sector.  he noted that china telecom has extended the internet service to almost every place that is linked with a telephone line.  he said that the company will soon put into operation an atm wide-band data network, expanding the band-width of the existing network to 155 mega bites per second. it will also increase the total capacity of the country's outlets to international data networks to 134 mega bites per second.  wu said that in order to accelerate the development of ecommerce in china, the ministry of information industry (mii) is working closely with other relevant government departments on formulating plans, methods, technological standards and regulations and laws. he said that the mii will focus on solving the key technological problems such as on-line security, identification and payment.  he added that the general lack of scientific training and traditional habits are major obstacles to the application and spread of e-commerce in china.  he said that the on-going "government on-line" project will serve as a good model for the application of e-commerce which is the most widely used part of the internet service worldwide.  hundreds of thousands of companies and over 1,500 banks around the world have already adopted this new form of doing business.  annual turnover of business on-line exceeds eight billion us dollars at present. the figure is expected to grow to 450 billion us dollars by 2000.

title: uk supermarket giant leads way for shopping on net
body: the uk's supermarket giant tesco and british telecom are among the world's top 10 rankings in the use of the web for electronic commerce, according to a new survey released here monday.  the london school of economics survey found that european companies take six of the top 10 rankings in an independent worldwide study of the quality and business value of corporate websites.  lufthansa, the german airline, ranked number one in the study.  other top 10 companies include international business machines, the us computer group, british airways, wal-mart stores, deutsche bank, deutsche telekom, comcast, the us media group, and walt disney.  the survey found european companies, which had been considered slow to develop e-commerce, were catching up with their us rivals.  overall, 17 of the top 30 scoring companies were based in the us, 11 in europe and two in asia.  on a sector-by-sector basis, european companies lead their world rivals in four of the eight business categories. in the travel and transport sector, lufthansa and british airway beat rivals delta airlines, american airlines and japan airlines.  bt and deutsche telekom dominated the telecommunications and utilities sector, while tesco lead retailing and deutsche bank came top in banking.

title: former agent says on-line uk spy names damage "exaggerated"
body: a former british intelligence agent, richard tomlinson, said on thursday the british government exaggerated the damage done by his act of posting the names of more than 100 mi6 spies on the internet.  tomlinson said in a statement that the information on his website was already in the public domain and added: "her majesty's government is over-reacting for public effect to stigmatize my efforts." agents of the secret intelligence service (sis), formerly known as mi6, have been named in a list published on the us-based site.  "the names of mi6 officers are the ones i cited in my affidavit on mi6 and princess diana," bbc quoted tomlinson as saying.  the british government has succeeded in closing down at least one website which tomlinson was using to publish the information.  it claimed the lives of british intelligence agents were being put at risk by publishing their names.  meanwhile, the government's defense advisory notice secretary, rear admiral david pulvertaft, issued a notice to the british media urging editors not to publish the address of the website or details of its contents without first contacting him.  the government has been trying to shut down the websites set up by tomlinson since the end of last month. he was sacked by mi6 in 1995 and jailed in december 1997 for breaking the country's official secrets act.  tomlinson was released on probation after six months of his oneyear sentence and has been pursued around the world since by the british government injunctions.

title: un cyberschoolbus selected as finalist for erica award
body: the united nations department of public information announced on wednesday that the u.n. cyberschoolbus, the online component of the department's global teaching and learning project, has been selected as a finalist for the ericsson internet community award (erica) program.  selected from among pool of 1,400 organizations, the finalists were announced this morning as part of the final stage of competition for the 250,000 unitedstates dollars grant.  the erica is the first international awards program designed to help non-profit organizations realize the power of the internet.  the program is seeking new and creative ideas for technology applications from non-profit organizations that take advantage of the community-building power of the internet.  the united nations cyberschoolbus was created in 1996 as the online education component of the global teaching and learning project, whose mission is to promote education about international issues.  the global teaching and learning project produces high quality teaching materials and activities designed for education use, at the primary, intermediate and secondary school levels.  the united nations cyberschoolbus captures the growing potential of the internet as an educational tool and provides an effective medium for the dissemination of information and resources about international affairs, as well as bringing together diverse communities of students and educators from around the world.  over 80,000 schools from over 100 countries regularly use the united nations cyberschoolbus.

title: chinese government going online
body: east china's shandong province has decided to put the provincial government and all its departments on the internet by august, according to a provincial government source.  the source says that this is part of china's ambitious campaign to increase government presence at all levels.  according to a provincial plan, all government offices at the provincial level in shandong will have their own websites by the end of the year.  the move was started by the state economic and trade commission, the ministry of information industry, and other ministries to share their information resources with each other and to improve efficiency.  the state development planning commission opened a website on december 1, 1998, and an increasing number of visitors have expressed their opinions on the site on everything from environmental pollution to a medical insurance system.  the beijing municipal government made its debut earlier this year with a website called window on the capital that provides information about the economic situation, job possibilities, and air-quality reports. the guangzhou and shenzhen governments in guangdong province have also opened trial websites.

title: e-commerce to get boosted in thailand
body: electronic-commerce in thailand, valued at 40 million baht (1.09 million unitedstates dollars) last year, will see a boost to 600 million baht (16.4 million dollars) by 2003, a seminar here was told friday.  e-commerce, which includes every business transaction done electronically in addition to on-line trading and on-line shopping, has been adopted worldwide as a weapon by companies to stay competitive, participants at the seminar on e-commerce law agreed.  many governments are lagging behind the private sector in this regard, according to the seminar, which opened thursday.  it also said that worldwide e-commerce transactions will be worth 300 billion dollars by 2001.  thai finance minister tarrin nimmanhaeminda, who attended thursday's meeting, said thailand needs to step up efforts to meet the world's new economic order by fully adopting e-commerce to improve fiscal and monetary systems and production.  at present, the thai government is working on six new laws on e-commerce, consisting of e-commerce law, edi law, privacy data protection law, computer crime law, electronics digital signature law, electronics fund transfer law and universal access law.  prime minister chuan leekpai has said he believed three of them would be ready for consideration by the cabinet by the end of this year.

title: hongkong telecom to develop beyond hong kong
body: hongkong telecom will diversify its businesses and explore opportunities beyond hongkong to meet tougher competition in the future, the company's chief executive linus cheung said here friday.  "hongkong telecom will have no future if we remain to be a telephone company," cheung said at a press conference to announce the company's final results for the year ended march 31, 1999.  hongkong telecom, hongkong's major full-service communications provider, friday reported a net profit of 11.50 billion hk dollars (1.47 billion unitedstates dollars), representing a 7.7 percent decrease from that of the previous year (before exceptional items).  the company's future will also be dark if it is just a telecommunications company, cheung said. that's why hongkong telecom aggressively adjusts itself to intensify development in internet and e-commerce and explore investment opportunities beyond hongkong.  "we are seizing the growth opportunities of the internet and investing in skills and capabilities to strengthen our position and achieve a clear lead in asia," cheung said.  "we shall drive to capture growth from global internet and data through closer integration with cable wireless on international network sharing, traffic management and new service developments," cheung said. "this will ensure we get the benefit of global reach, scale and early adoption of new technology --all of which is essential to enable hongkong telecom to remain competitive amongst global players," he added.  hongkong telecom will have no future if it restrains itself within hongkong, cheung said. he said that he is ambitious to play the "world cup", not just the "hongkong league".  cheung said that hongkong telecom has a cooperation with china telecom and china's accession to the world trade organization will bring fresh opportunities to the company.  hongkong has its own advantage in investing in china's mainland including good reputation, modern technology and good cooperative relations, cheung said.  the company said friday that its turnover decreased by 7.5 percent to 32.41 billion hk dollars (4.15 billion unitedstates dollars).  also at the press conference, hongkong telecom chairman brian smith said that 1998 has been a very difficult year for companies operating in asia.  "the weak economic environment in hongkong throughout the year has dampened demand for basic telecommunications services," smith said.  "at the same time, hongkong telecom has faced intense price competition, particularly in international telephone and mobile services," he said.  smith said that the board of directors remains confident of the company's underlying strength and its longer term prospects and has recommended a final dividend of 46.6 cents per share, making a total of 85.2 cents for this financial year.  the company's international telecommunication services revenues declined 18 percent to 15.56 billion hk dollars (1.99 billion unitedstates dollars) due to the economic downturn here.  hongkong telecom signed an agreement with the government in march 1998 to surrender its exclusive international license.  however, local telecommunication services revenues grew by 6 percent to 9.40 billion hk dollars (1.20 billion unitedstates dollars).  the firm said its mobile services revenues were 3 percent lower at 5.82 billion hk dollars (74.61 million unitedstates dollars) as the numbers of customers switching networks has increased.  the firm said revenues for its internet and interactive multimedia services increased 146 percent year-on-year to 626 million hk dollars (80.25 million unitedstates dollars).

title: news analysis: asia faces e-commerce challenges
body: as its internet subscriber growth is becoming the fastest in the world, asia is warming to electronic-commerce, which is projected to offer a great promise to the region's economies.  compared with their american and european counterparts, asians are lagging behind in the development of e-commerce at present.  while consumers and business purchasing goods and services over the internet in the west spent 50 billion dollars last year, a mere 723 million dollars in on-line retail sales were booked in the whole asian region, according to the internet market research firm keenan vision.  but with the world's fastest growth in internet subscribers, asia has great potential for e-commerce expansion. with 10.5 million internet accounts, subscriber growth in non-japan asia is rising 39 percent a year.  the market research firm international data corp. estimated that china will surpass australia in 2001 as non-japan asia's top internet user and by the end of 2002 will have about 9.4 million internet users, up from a mere 1.4 million in 1997.  by the end of 2002, australia is expected to have 5.8 million users up from just over 3 million now, while south korea will be the third biggest internet user with about 4 million people logging on, up from less than two million now.  with the fast development of internet, e-commerce is expected to grow significantly in the next few years, experts said.  in a recent survey conducted by pwc for the world economic forum, 60 percent of asia's business executives said that e-commerce will contribute more than 5 percent of their company's total revenues by 2003, with one fifth projecting a revenue contribution of over 20 percent, although e-commerce makes little or non-contribution to their companies at present.  what has prompted asia's business executives to promote e-commerce? some of them said e-commerce could sweep away market inefficiencies, such as excessive transaction costs, asymmetric information, and natural monopolies, breaking up arcane market barriers.  as e-commerce is regarded as the future of business, asians are also getting pushed by western companies demanding for business over the internet to save cost, they said.  moreover, the recent asian recession has made business executives more aware than ever of the pressing need to cut their costs, increase efficiency and stay in touch with their customers.  nevertheless, asia's e-commerce expansion still faces great challenges. many developing economies in the region lack reliable communications, and state-monopoly of telecommunications in some countries leads to high cost for consumers. legal frameworks and taxation issues governing e-commerce are also uncertain.  there are other barriers to consumer e-commerce. not many in asia have credit cards, and many prefer face-to-face buying and most of the region is served by corner shops. for many asian banks, they mistrust on-line transactions, according to the economist weekly.  realizing the importance of e-commerce and its challenges, asian countries are trying to remove these barriers. in vietnam, where just 15,000 people are on-line, the government has slashed 40 percent of access charges to make its use more affordable.  for years, india's telecommunications company vsnl charged its customers 500 unitedstates dollars for 500 hours of slow internet service.  but recently, the government opened the market for competition, 10,000 subscribers signed up for rival satyam infoware's service.  it is estimated that india's internet subscribers could reach 10 million in the next three years.  in singapore, law makers have adopted laws for e-commerce activities and the government is encouraging people to use internet for business. "malaysia's multimedia super corridor, singapore's singapore-one, and hongkong's brand new cyberport are examples of major government-sponsored projects that demonstrated the determination of asian leaders to make the information technology revolution, and e-commerce," said the asian business in its may 1999 issue.

title: more money invested in u.s. net firms
body: internet-related companies in the unitedstates received a total of 2.1 billion unitedstates dollars in venture capital in the first quarter, a market research firm said thursday.  investments in net firms represented 58 percent of all venture capital investment in the past quarter, said san francisco-based ventureone, which tracks the venture capital industry. firms involved in electronic commerce and business services accounted for almost 22 percent of the money invested in internet companies.  ventureone said that total venture capital investment in the unitedstates reached 3.6 billion dollars in the first quarter, up 32 percent from a year ago.  according to ventureone's earlier releases, venture capital investments in the unitedstates reached an all time high of 12.52 billion dollars in 1998. information technology remained the strongest component of investment growth, accounting for 62 percent of the dollars invested, raising 7.77 billion dollars in more than 1,000 deals. its strength was fueled largely by investment in communications and information services companies, the market research firm said.  also in 1998, the unitedstates initial public offerings (ipo) market for venture-backed companies saw a total of 4.23 billion dollars raised by the 77 public companies going public. internet companies led the pack accounting for over 30 percent of all venture-backed companies going public.

title: u.s. company to develop music download system
body: universal, the world's largest music company, wednesday entered into a partnership with a california-based software company to develop a system that would allow customers to download music to their computers in a secure format that prevents mass copying.  "we have to try and find out what the consumers want and what they are willing to pay for," larry kenswil, head of electronic commerce at universal, said wednesday. "one thing for sure is people want to download music," he added.  industry sources say universal's move underscores the music industry's difficult search for a way to take advantage of the internet and, at the same time, curb piracy that cost companies about 5 billion unitedstates dollars a year.  they say universal's announcement is significant because it marks the first attempt by a major music company to go digital.  the legitimate music market is worth about 40 billion dollars a year and a report by forrester research said digital distribution of music will be worth 1.1 billion dollars by 2003.  other technology companies, including sony, microsoft and ibm are competing to develop secure systems for digital transmission of songs.

title: transnational company to speed up net backbone
body: a transnational telecommunications company tuesday disclosed plans to unveil new networking technology that can potentially deliver speeds and capacity 640 times better than current technology for fiber-optic networks.  the technology, an optical amplification system, combines 160 separate channels of light into one beam, with each channel carrying data at a rate of 10 gigabits per second for a total per fiber capacity of 1.6 trillion bits per second, said the ontariobased nortel networks in a news release.  with this fiber capacity and speed, nortel said, the entire four-million book collection of the unitedstates library of congress can be transported to los angeles in just seconds through one single strand of fiber. it can also support --on a single fiber --simultaneously internet connections to 28 million households.  the technology is not due to ship commercially until next year.  essentially, nortel and its unitedstates competitors hope to extend the capabilities of a technology called dense-wavelength division multiplexing (dwdm) to handle more data, video and voice-rich services at high speeds.  the technology uses multiple lasers and transmits multiple light signals simultaneously over a single optical fiber. each signal travels within its unique color band, which is modulated by the data (text, voice, video, etc.). dwdm enables the existing fiber infrastructure of the telephone companies and other carriers to be dramatically increased.  nortel, whose optical networking equipment carries 75 percent of north america's backbone internet traffic, said the new technology would help create a better internet --an "optical internet."

title: u.s. web news users use newspapers online --survey
body: more than half of internet users in the unitedstates looking for news online turn to newspaper sites, said the newspaper association of america (naa) tuesday.  releasing preliminary results of an online usage survey, naa said that unitedstates consumers continue to value what newspapers deliver --both in print and online, noting that 82 percent of the online newspaper audience is reading the printed product with the same or increased frequency.  the study conducted for naa by scarborough research of new york surveyed online users in the top 50 unitedstates markets. it found that 51 percent of those who use an online service, the internet or world wide web to get world or national news said that they read or looked at an online newspaper in the past six months. among those seeking local or community news online, 54 percent turn to online newspapers, and 46 percent turn to online newspapers to get information about events or things to do in their local communities.  preliminary findings from the study also indicate that 56 percent of all adults in the top 50 markets in the unitedstates used an online service in the past year and 54 percent did so during the past six months, representing a projected 72.8 million adults. three-quarters have gone online for world, national or local news and information. more than one-third of all online users have read or looked at newspapers online during the past six months.  explaining the findings, naa said that newspapers were among the first media to see the potential of digital distribution and they are maintaining their competitive position. among current online users, online newspapers are read or looked at as much as all other online sources of news combined, including radio, television, magazine and portal sites.

title: australian stocks continue to fall
body: the australian sharemarket's slide continued monday, shedding almost one percent for its fourth consecutive negative close after many key industrial stocks slumped.  market leader news corp and banking stocks were shouldering much of the blame for a 26.6 point slide in the benchmark all ordinaries index to 3074.5, off an intraday low of 3070.4.  brokers said much of the trading was a reflection of profit taking on wall street on friday night where the dow jones industrial average dropped 89.34 points to 10,789.04.  by the end of trading, the all industrials index had lost 60 points to 5391.7 while the all resources index managed to pick up 4.9 points to 1229.9.  rupert murdoch's news corp took a hammering, falling 28.4 cents to 12.38 australian dollars while its preferred shares were off 26.2 cents to 11.55 australian dollars.  the market continued to mark down the media giant's shares following the company's decision to pick up a 35 per cent stake in telecom italia spa's unprofitable television unit stream.  the commonwealth bank of australia surrendered 47.2 cents to 27.043 australian dollars and national australia bank dropped 42 cents to 29.00 australian dollars.  westpac bank was 23.9 cents weaker to 11.297 australian dollars and anz shedding five cents to 11.92 australian dollars.  in the resources sector, global miner rio tinto was at the head of the upward move, rising 23.9 cents to 25.689 australian dollars while diversified miner bhp lost 20.9 cents to 16.875 australian dollars as profit-takers moved in on last week's gains.  the gold index dipped one point to 1029.9.  gold bullion in sydney at 286.75 unitedstates dollars an ounce after friday's close of 286.10 unitedstates dollars.  national turnover on the australian stock exchange reached 409.79 million shares worth 744.12 million unitedstates dollars. of those stocks traded, 559 rose, 697 fell and 436 were steady.

title: sri lanka launches first internet business facility
body: a cyber trader, the first electronic business facility of the export development board, was launched monday by sri lankan president chandrika kumaratunga at her presidential residence.  president kumaratunga, by the press of a button, lighted the electronic oil lamp over the internet website.  the cyber trader will benefit 3,000 exporters, importers, trading houses and small and medium enterprises, minister of internal and international commerce kingsley t. wickremaratne said in an interview with the official daily news published monday.  it will assist sri lankan businessmen to have access to emerging markets and enable them to be competitive. the cyber trader will also serve as a storehouse of trade information and a base for video-conferencing.  additionally the facility will provide the expertise and electronic infrastructure to gain access to a large client base in the whole world.  buyers could be found and orders could be placed electronically. it combines the state-of-the-art hardware and computer networks and a continuously updated information base, the minister said.  to be available on the cyber trader will be a storehouse of trade information, search and advisory services, advertising on the internet to reach potential customers and pre-planning of business visits for inward and outward marketing missions.

title: web ad revenue in u.s. doubles in
body: online advertising revenues in the unitedstates more than doubled in 1998, reaching 1.92 billion unitedstates dollars, according to a report released monday.  it grew by 112 percent over the 906 million dollars for 1997, said the leading online ad association internet advertising bureau (iab).  in the fourth quarter alone, web ads increased by 34 percent to 655.6 million dollars. two years ago, internet annual revenue was only 267 million dollars.  noting that the internet as a viable advertising medium is barely four years old, iab said that its growth, measured in billions of dollars, is astounding. the association expects a sustained growth period in coming years due to increasing online ad budgets and greater commitment by large traditional advertisers.  the categories which lead the online spending were consumerrelated advertisements at 31 percent, computer-related ads at 26 percent, and financial services at 19 percent. top sectors represented in the consumer category include retail, auto, toys, travel and music.  top 10 web sites drew 71 percent of all ad spending for the fourth quarter of 1998. meanwhile, banner advertising represented 56 percent of all online ads, while sponsorships declined to 30 percent from 36 percent at the end of 1997.

title: wipo aims to curb abuse of trademarks on internet
body: the world intellectual property organization (wipo) has set out recommendations in an effort to curb the abuse of trademarks on the internet in a newly published report.  for the first time, the wipo report sets out a definition for the abusive sue of trademarks on the internet. the report, which addresses questions relating to domain names, intellectual property and related dispute-resolution issues, was initiated by wipo in july 1998 at the request by the unitedstates, one of wipo's 171 members.  wipo will present the report to its members at their annual meeting here in september. the recommendations have been presented to the interim board of the internet corporation for assigned names and numbers (icann) for consideration when it meets on may 25-27 in berlin.  in the report, wipo has recommended that the contact details of applicants using existing generic top level domains (gtlds) be collected, and that those details be freely and instantly available over the internet.  wipo also recommends the establishment of a uniform and mandatory administrative dispute-resolution system, under which panels of three experts would apply the streamlined, quick and cost-effective procedures outlined in the report, to review multiple claims and eliminate cases of clear abuse of trademark holders' rights, leaving the more complex cases to the courts.  the third recommendation that wipo has made is a system by which owners of globally famous marks can obtain exclusions prohibiting others from registering the marks as domain names in gtlds. the status of these marks would be determined by a panel of experts drawn from a list administered by wipo.  at the same time, the wipo report recommends further study and consultation on the feasibility of adding a differentiated non-commercial and use-restricted domain that could address the need for privacy and free speech on the internet.  provided that the recommendations in the report are adopted and implemented, wipo believes that the introduction of new gtlds is possible. however, it does maintain that any new gtlds should, in any event, be added to the domain name system in a slow and controlled manner to ensure that the impact of this experience is monitored and assessed.

title: insurers told to wise up to computers
body: the insurance industry today relies heavily on information technology not only to store its underwriting information but also to acquire, store and analyze all financial, internal, external, macro-and microeconomic data, according to china daily business weekly today.  the computer was just used to automatically produce renewal notices and perhaps to produce account statements to replace primitive punch cards storing key data, when it was first applied in the insurance sector 35 years ago.  governing committee member of the hongkong federation of insurers and general manager of guardian insurance ltd., steven lau, said that the technology not only changes consumers' buying patterns and but requires insurers to anticipate and adapt to these changes as well.  zhang guojun from huatai insurance co. said he believed that the technology would help insurance firms increase their competitiveness by improving management efficiency, upgrading service and enhancing their ability in quick reaction to market changes.  moreover, the development of the internet is changing traditional marketing methods for insurance products.  "the internet makes round-the-clock marketing possible," said frank lee, deputy general manager of the china ping'an insurance co., when he commented on the part of the internet in the insurance industry.  new china life insurance co. delivered its first web life policy last year. and china ping'an has attempted to sell policies through the internet. its home page contains columns on insurance information, proposals and the procedures on purchasing insurance products.  "we must expect that the trend will continue and it will require considerable effort, resources, investment and commitment to keep our industry competitive in the next millennium," lau told a mainland-hongkong insurance conference held last week in beijing.  to create business value from any it investment, lau from guardian insurance added, it must be accompanied by a number of other activities such as analyzing and changing business processes and creating a rule-driven administration and underwriting environment.

title: worldwide outsourcing spending to grow
body: worldwide corporate spending on outsourcing corporate desktops and networks is expected to more than double within four years, according to a report released saturday.  driving by the information technology staff shortage and potential budget savings, network and desktop outsourcing services will reach 30.7 billion unitedstates dollars worldwide by 2003, said international data corporation (idc), a unitedstates market research firm.  the worldwide outsourcing spending grew almost 2 billion dollars between 1997 and 1998 to reach 14.3 billion dollars.  outsourcing usually refers to contracting with outside consultants, software houses or service bureaux to perform systems analysis, programming and datacenter operations. idc said that the challenges of managing servers, network environments and desktops are fueling demands for outsourcing, one of the fatest-growing markets in the information technology industry.  under a desktop outsourcing deal a company typically hires a firm to procure its pcs, provide software licenses and systems upgrades, and supply help desk services from a call center.  according to idc, factors driving desktop and networking outsourcing growth are declining pc prices which have increased computer use, rapid growing employee internet access, increasing portable device use and difficulty hiring and keeping information technology staffers.  in 1998, idc said, the unitedstates accounted for nearly half of worldwide spending on network and desktop outsourcing services, with the banking spending the most. latin america, as well as eastern europe, the middle east, africa and parts of asia are other fast-growing areas.  in an earlier report, idc said that a growing number of companies worldwide are outsourcing their information technology training programs to help keep up with internet commerce and new web-based business applications. the overall training market including tools, content and services grew to 16.5 billion dollars in 1998 worldwide and is expected to reach 22.9 billions dollars in 2001.

title: author wins lawsuit on internet story infringement
body: a beijing court yesterday ruled in favor of a plaintiff whose story, published on his homepage, was printed by a newspaper without permission, china daily reported today. it was likely china's first case in copyright infringement on works published on the internet, the newspaper said. chen weihua, director of beijing rongyida electronic co ltd, posted a story concerning a computer program on a website (www.3d. yeah.net) on may 10 last year, under the pseudonym "wu fang," the name of the homepage owner. chen claimed that the article, which discussed the development of maya, a 3-d animation making software, was accompanied by a copyright statement saying: "all rights reserved; no reprint without permission." however, the chengdu-based computer business information weekly, upon receiving an email from a reader recommending the story, printed it in its october 16 issue, without permission from chen, the newspaper said. the weekly refused to neither apologize to chen nor pay more than its standard fee for contributed articles, as demanded by chen, because it alleged that chen could not prove that he was "wu fang," the author. the beijing haidian district people's court, after investigating, confirmed that "wu fang" is chen weihua, because chen could log onto the homepage, change its password, upload or erase files. "the article should be protected by china's copyright law as a literary creation since it was published on the internet so the public could read it," said li dongtao, chief justice of the court, on wednesday. china just celebrated the fifth anniversary of its access to the internet last week, while the copyright law became effective in 1991, the newspaper said.
