title: china to start ip phone trial service
body: china's ministry of information industry (mii) announced it has approved three chinese telecommunications service providers to conduct internet protocol (ip) phone trial services.  the three companies are the china telecommunications corp. ( china telecom), united telecommunications corp. (unicom), and china jitong telecommunications co.  according to chen yin, an mii official in charge of telecom development planning, china telecom will launch its trial services tomorrow, and the other two companies will start within the first half of the year.  "the trial period is set to be six months and will conclude by the end of the year," chen said, adding that the official operation of the ip phone services is expected to start then.  during the experimental period, international ip calls will be charged at 4.8 yuan per minute, and domestic long-distance ip calls will be charged for 0.3 yuan per minute.  in addition to the above charges, ip phone users will pay the local call that is triggered by each ip call.  regular ddd call in china is between 0.5 and one yuan per minute. regular idd call within asia except for the middle east is 12 yuan per minute; that to other parts of the world is 15 yuan per minute.  li lihua in charge of the telecom financial settlement of the mii said the fee standard is a temporary one applicable only to the trial period. adjustments will be made before the official full time service is introduced.  "the ip phone business is developed among three major telecom outfit," chen said, which is an "important step toward breaking the monopoly and introducing competition in china's telecom industry." china telecom will carry out experimental services in 25 cities, and the other two will handle a further 12 cities.  the mii also pledged to continue to crack down on illegal ip phone services to ensure a "healthy and orderly" development of the telecom market.

title: internet service provider sees good days ahead
body: after years of a painful struggle for survival, sohu.com, one of the country's most successful internet service providers (isp), is now looking for new expansion opportunities.  zhang chaoyang, founder and chief executive officer, has attracted attention from representatives of foreign companies at the china business summit of the world economic forum held in china.  he said that his isp company will balance its income and spending within one or two years. the next step that the company will take is to seek a merger or takeover by a major foreign company so as to expand its operations.  china's isp sector has gone through continuous consolidation in the past five years. the number of isps in the country has decreased from several hundred to scores. most of the isps that survived fierce competition are wholly or partially funded by foreign companies. over 90 percent of sohu.com's capital is from overseas investors.  zhang said that foreign funds did not only ease the shortage of funds of local isps, but also helped enhance their management through strict requirements of economic returns from the overseas investors.  he noted that the failure of most chinese isps can be attributed to a lack of market-oriented management mechanisms.  zhang, a returned student from the unitedstates, expressed optimism about the future of isps in china.  "faced with the same difficulties all internet service providers are competing as equals in the china market and only the fittest can survive and win better returns than in any other markets in the world," he said.  sohu.com had one million us dollars in revenue last year, becoming the best performing isp in the country. now it has about one million pages downloaded from its website every day.  zhang predicts that china's access to the world trade organization will promote the expansion of his company.  "we have already established an advantage in the china market.  increasing international competition will push our operations into wider fields," he said.  by the end of 1998, china had more than two million internet users. the figure is expected to grow to 3.5 million by the end of this year and to 4.5 million by the end of 2000.

title: opening ceremony of horti-expo live on internet
body: if you couldn't be in kunming when the '99 international horticultural exposition opens here friday evening, just start your computer at 8 p.m., access to the internet and there you may enjoy the entire opening ceremony broadcast live. "don't miss the last grand international gathering of this century," says an online advertisement presented by the yunnan provincial infoport, www.yn.cninfo.net, one of the service providers for live broadcast. the horticultural show in kunming, capital of yunnan province, is the first international exposition to be hosted by china, or by a developing country. it is also the first time for china to introduce on-line broadcast of the opening ceremony of a major international activity it hosts. some 7,000 professional and amateur performers will attend a large entertainment show friday evening after the horti-expo is declared open. journalists and kunming citizens who have had the chance to watch the rehearsals described the show, titled "a romantic melody of heaven and earth", as very exciting and inspiring. the opening ceremony and performance will also be broadcast live on www.expo99.net, a website opened on march 1 specially for the upcoming expo. as the chinese government's first attempt to use the internet for publicity of an international activity held in china, the website has to date received more than 70,000 visits. "apart from the opening ceremony, we will plan to broadcast live the inauguration of the expo venue scheduled at 8 a.m. on may 1, as well as some other major events during the six-month run of the exposition," said deng hengyuan, one of the operators of the expo website. as china's several previous attempts of internet broadcast, including one by the china central television to broadcast its 1999 chinese lunar new year entertainment soiree worldwide, have unexpectedly encountered problems like communication jam and even website breakdown, telecommunication departments in yunnan have spent big money on upgrading the facilities of both websites. "our website alone can accept one million visitors at a time," said deng.

title: opening ceremony of horti-expo live on internet
body: if you couldn't be in kunming when the '99 international horticultural exposition opens here friday evening, just start your computer at 8 p.m., access to the internet and there you may enjoy the entire opening ceremony broadcast live. "don't miss the last grand international gathering of this century," says an online advertisement presented by the yunnan provincial infoport, www.yn.cninfo.net, one of the service providers for live broadcast. the horticultural show in kunming, capital of yunnan province, is the first international exposition to be hosted by china, or by a developing country. it is also the first time for china to introduce on-line broadcast of the opening ceremony of a major international activity it hosts. some 7,000 professional and amateur performers will attend a large entertainment show friday evening after the horti-expo is declared open. journalists and kunming citizens who have had the chance to watch the rehearsals described the show, titled "a romantic melody of heaven and earth", as very exciting and inspiring. the opening ceremony and performance will also be broadcast live on www.expo99.net, a website opened on march 1 specially for the upcoming expo. as the chinese government's first attempt to use the internet for publicity of an international activity held in china, the website has to date received more than 70,000 visits. "apart from the opening ceremony, we will plan to broadcast live the inauguration of the expo venue scheduled at 8 a.m. on may 1, as well as some other major events during the six-month run of the exposition," said deng hengyuan, one of the operators of the expo website. as china's several previous attempts of internet broadcast, including one by the china central television to broadcast its 1999 chinese lunar new year entertainment soiree worldwide, have unexpectedly encountered problems like communication jam and even website breakdown, telecommunication departments in yunnan have spent big money on upgrading the facilities of both websites. "our website alone can accept one million visitors at a time," said deng.

title: cisco systems, undp launch "net aid"
body: cisco systems and the united nations development program (undp) on tuesday announced that they would join forces in an effort to eradicate extreme poverty in the world's poorest nations.  about one-third of the people in developing countries struggle for survival on incomes of less than 1 unitedstates dollar a day. their extreme poverty denies them access to such basic needs as safe drinking water, adequate food and health care.  to support its commitment, cisco systems, the worldwide leader in networking for the internet, has pledged its vast resources to develop a global website which will serve as a powerful source of information to mobilize the world's people to action.  as part of its commitment to alleviating world poverty, cisco systems is creating a website which will be maintained by undp.  the site will be solely dedicated to serve as a clearinghouse for organizations and individuals who want to get involved in the effort, and have the infrastructure to support more than one billion hits on the web.  in addition to being stocked with information, live interviews, links and suggestions on how each and every person can help in the race against poverty, the website will also provide a conduit for contributions.  "the internet has the power to change the fortunes of countries,,companies and individuals," said john chambers, president and chief executive officer of cisco systems.  "whether it is managing a micro-loan program to purchase sewing machines for a women's cooperative in jordan, or accessing medical expertise for remote clinics in south east asia, or educating people on how they can make a difference, the internet can play a key role in eliminating extreme poverty," said john.  "poverty eradication must become a central and guiding objective of all development efforts. good health, adequate nutrition, literacy and employment are not favors or acts of charity to be bestowed on the poor by enlightened leaders. they are human rights," said james gustave speth, administrator of undp.

title: intel chief foresees leadership role for hk it industry
body: president of intel corporation craig barrett said here tuesday that hongkong has opportunities to make itself a asia pacific internet hub, thus playing a leadership role in information technology.  addressing an engineering faculty of the hongkong university, barrett said hongkong can build itself into an asia pacific internet traffic hub, an internet content hub and an online financial services hub.  these opportunities of hongkong come from the city's advantage in telecommunications infrastructures, bilingual portal access, productive movie industry and regional financial center status, he said.  meanwhile, he said, hongkong faces challenges that include insufficient bandwidth, economic slowdown and piracy.  he suggested that hongkong re-invent its internet content with digital technology and bring in innovation in electronic commerce solutions.  intel, which plans to produce chips running at giga hertz level by the end of next year, now alone occupies 256-mega hertz bandwidth while hongkong has a total of 243 mega hertz, ranking third in asia next to the republic of korea and singapore.  barrett also predicted that the volume of internet economy will be booming in the next few years and reach 1 trillion unitedstates dollars by the year 2002. he added that the asia pacific region will play an aggressive role in this development.  barrett is now on a five-day tour that will also take him to malaysia, the philippines, singapore and taiwan.

title: china to develop internet's education potential
body: while the internet gets tens of thousands of new users, a group of chinese and foreign experts are working on setting up a national long-distance education system in china to provide educational opportunities via the internet.  tan songhua, of the state educational development research center, told a seminar on education and the internet that opened here today that the system could help speed up the country's development from an agricultural-industrial economy to a knowledgebased economy and from a producing society to an information society in the 21st century.  "the social and economic development in the next century depends more on the creation, spread, and application of knowledge and information," he said.  in recent years, the education-via-the-internet plan has been taking shape, tan said, and a number of universities like hunan university and zhejiang university have got engaged in regional long-distance education, catching the attention of many educators and computer experts worldwide.  he said that the final goal of the plan is to provide educational opportunities to anyone with access to the internet no matter where they are or whatever they need.  wang zhuzhu, a ministry of education official, says that china set up an education and research network (cer net) in 1995, linking all major chinese cities with beijing.

title: china's telecoms sector facing fiercer competition
body: china's telecommunications sector is focusing on service to compete better with foreign companies in the domestic market.  beijing telecom, a branch of china telecom, announced today that on may 1 it will cut the amount of time needed to get a telephone installed or moved and it will try to response more quickly to customer requests.  the deputy-director of beijing telecom, jia yong, says that china's telecommunications sector is set to open to foreign operators and that china telecom's management which developed over a long period of monopoly operations will not survive market competition and needs to improve service and quality to keep its customers.  china telecom still has a monopoly in local telephones, but, according to beijing telecom, the company has had an increasing number of instances of failing to provide quality service and the amount of compensation it has had to give customers has been growing each year.  earlier this month, the unitedstates's att obtained approval for internet-related operations in china and, in response, beijing telecom added new internet services. it promises that customers can get a dedicated line for data transmission within a month of registering and can get dial-in internet service within 48 hours of making their first payment.  the company also promises to compensate customers if it fails to meet the time limit.  jia says that chinese operators lag far behind foreign operators in service. the average time it takes chinese operator to install a new telephone line is 20 days, but it's only 3-7 days for foreign operators.  some chinese operators are trying to streamline management and improve efficiency to reduce this gap and beijing telecom has already laid off a number of employees who have not met efficiency standards.

title: relics on net, websites to be better regulated
body: computer networks should be used to introduce chinese culture to the world, while protecting cultural relics, suggests a state bureau of cultural relics official.  "as a convenient and instant source of information, the internet can satisfy people's curiosity about ancient china and help them understand chinese culture," said hou junkun, director of the bureau's science and education division, quoted by today's china daily.  information about chinese relics can be found at more than 60 websites. these sites were established by local museums and relics bureaus primarily from shannxi, sichuan and henan provinces and shanghai.  hou stressed that establishments of these websites would not have been so smooth without the efforts of devoted domestic computer experts.  foreign involvement, although not forbidden by the bureau, is rare. to better regulate these websites, the bureau ordered them placed under strict scrutiny last month.  local museums and relics bureaus are required to obtain official approval before introducing china's world heritage sites, places being excavated, the latest archaeological findings and cultural relics under state protection on the internet, according to a bureau circular issued last month.  computer and relics experts are preparing for a nationwide information network of cultural relics, expected to be completed this year. it will enhance research regarding relics and improve the exchange of information.

title: "fourth media" to dominate in 21st century
body: the power of the "fourth media", the internet and information super-highway, will probably outweigh the traditional media --newspapers, radio and television within one or two decades, delegates to an international conference on the press were told today.  "press communities all over the world are undergoing a major reform," said zhou guangzhao, vice-chairman of the standing committee of the chinese national people's congress and chairman of the china association for science and technology, at the opening ceremony of the second asia-pacific symposium on the press and scientific and social progress.  he pointed out that the development of the fourth media will be a great gift for the 21st century.  "nowadays, reporters are able to use the internet to cover and write news stories all over the world, and can send out their stories worldwide at any time," said ellis rubinstein, chief editor of american's prestigious science magazine.  he said that the internet has provided rich information sources and opportunities for reporters, and that the wide use of the fourth media is gradually changing the work style of news people.  "the development of internet techniques will have a substantial impact on the development of newspapers in the chinese language," said wang xuan, an academician with the chinese academy of sciences.  the growth of the internet since 1993 has been phenomenal with now an estimated 150 million people worldwide regularly surfing and this is expected to double by the year 2001. this growth rate far surpasses that of radio and television which took several decades to reach comparable figures.  the four-day symposium, with the theme "science and technology and the development strategy of newspapers in the 21st century", is jointly sponsored by the ministry of science and technology, the chinese academy of sciences, the china science and technology association, the xinhua news agency and the chinese foreign language press institute. delegates from more than 100 news organizations, research institutes and enterprises in the asian-pacific region attended the meeting.

title: internet appliance market to grow in u.s.
body: the development and adoption of internet appliances will explode in the unitedstates during the next 12 months, according to a report released wednesday.  by leveraging the capabilities of the internet, the report said, internet appliances stand ready to revolutionize the way that information is used and accessed by enabling universal access --the ability to access any information, over any network and from any device.  and instead of developing proprietary systems to support the underlying platform capability necessary to support internet appliances, service companies will turn to third-party infrastructure software and services companies that have begun to address the unique challenges of the internet appliance market, said the report from san francisco-based internet research group of the investment bank hambrecht quist.  the group defines internet appliance as any non-pc device that leverages the capabilities of the internet to extend content, services and applications to the users of those devices. these may include internet television, network computer, specialized hand-held devices with wireless connection to the internet, and personal digital assistant (pda) --a hand-held computer that serves as an organizer for personal information.  a recent sign of market activity concerning internet appliances was announced last week with the agreement between yahoo and online anywhere. the latter is a provider of products and services that deliver web content to television, pagers, cell phones, pdas and other non-pc devices. companies such as america online, microsoft and excite have also announced initiatives to make personalized content and services universally accessible to users regardless of the appliance or type of network they are using to access the internet.  the research group expects traditional access providers, such as telephone companies, internet service providers, cable operators and wireless carriers, to drive the mainstream acceptance and uptake of internet appliances. "the winners will be the service providers that marry the benefits of the internet with the specific functions the appliance performs," the group said.  highlighting some of the conclusions, the report said that contrary to popular belief, internet appliances will not replace pcs, but in many cases will provide different services than pcs.  certain devices, it added, will capture imagination and enthusiasm, which will add to the viral effect of device adoption.  the power of using the internet as a vehicle for building community around a device and its use should not be underestimated.

title: study: new internet users in u.s. to be older, less affluent
body: as indications of a maturing technology, the characteristics of first-time internet users in the unitedstates will begin to shift during 1999, according to report released tuesday.  based on a survey of 16,500 unitedstates households in december last year, the report said that the number of households with internet access grew exceptionally fast between april and december of 1998, reaching 37 percent of all unitedstates households.  the survey was conducted by inteco corporation, a unitedstates market intelligence firm that forecasts consumer-level actions and attitudes relative to pcs, the internet, online services, interactive tv and other similar technologies.  fifty-five percent of internet households report annual income of 50,000 unitedstates dollars or more. while upscale households continue to dominate the internet, inteco said, this segment is reaching saturation, and first-time users will soon be taking on a new look.  the research shows that middle and lower-income households account for 55 percent of those who intend to become internet users in the next 12 months. other segments showing an upswing include households headed by non-professionals or non-executives and households headed by a retiree.  growth among female users will outpace that of males. single female households comprise 30 percent of all households that expect to adopt internet usage this year.  "internet growth is far from over," the market analysis firm said. "there are still huge advances expected, in terms of numbers of users as well as numbers and types of services being offered to internet users." but as internet penetration among higher-income households is approaching saturation, the "new user" segment will become an increasingly diverse market, the firm said.  the study also found that internet users are increasingly convinced of the value it delivers. ninety-five percent of the internet-using households surveyed at the end of 1998 indicated that they intended to remain internet subscribers for the next year.

title: u.s. to form new internet policy institute
body: the unitedstates will set up a new institute on global internet policy and research later this year, said a working group from the organization in a statement on monday.  the 22 members of the group are from unitedstates businesses, nonprofit groups and academic institutions, which include the washington-based highway 1, nasdaq stock market, the potomac knowledgeway, information technology association of america, university of maryland, university of illinois, the washington post, microsoft and american online.  the internet policy institute will be an independent, nonprofit research and educational organization chartered to provide analysis, research, education, and outreach on a full range of economic, social and policy issues affecting and affected by the global development and use of the internet, the statement noted.  the institute, which will begin operations when funding is finalized and staff has been hired, will have a physical presence in the washington region and an active presence on the internet, where it can draw on the research being conducted on online issues by scholars from around the world.  while its initial staffing is limited, the institute will eventually add staff researchers and senior fellows, the group said.  in the next months the group will establish an organizational structure for the institute and begin reaching out to national and non-unitedstates-based companies and institutions for participation, the statement said.

title: australian stocks inch to another record close
body: the australian sharemarket finished the week at another all time closing high, with solid share price rises in a number of select stocks helping the market inch to a better finish.  the benchmark all ordinaries index ended up 3.8 points to 3060.0, after hitting an intraday high of 3073.5 points.  friday's close eclipsed thursday's record of 3056.2 points.  friday's market managed the stronger finish despite a flat to weak price performance in heavyweight stocks, namely news corp and telstra corp.  "there's good support at 3000 (points) and with the bond market rally i can see further gains," said greg matthews, chief investment officer at macquarie equities.  the all industrials index closed 1.5 points up at 5518.1.  the all resources index closed 7.6 points higher to 1045.2 points.  news corp ended a stunning week of gains on a down note, with its ordinary shares off 11 cents after touching a low of 13.97 australian dollars.  news corp has ridden a wave of enthusiasm on the back of this week's deal with unitedstates cable company liberty media and market players had expected the rally to run out of steam.  telco giant telstra and cable wireless optus ended the week on a down note as investors focused on other plays in the market, with some analysts reporting a switch of funds into kerry packer's publishing and broadcasting ltd.  telstra closed down five cents and cw optus was off one cent while aapt was up 15.1 cents.  elsewhere, resources giant rio tinto helped the resources sector close higher, thanks to renewed enthusiasm for the sector on european bourses.  rio continued its rally of recent days and closed up 45 cents.  bhp was also firmer, up 12 cents, while wmc was off two cents.  banks had a firmer tone, with anz up 20 cents, westpac up 10 cents and national australia bank gaining 10 cents while commonwealth bank slipped 23.6 cents.  national turnover was 493.57 million shares worth 1.195 billion australian dollars (752.8 million unitedstates dollars) with 607 falling stocks, 579 rising and 455 steady.

title: australian media giant drives stocks to record close
body: the australian sharemarket surged to another all-time closing high thursday, powered by a bullish performance in select blue chip stocks, in particular rupert murdoch's news corp.  the benchmark all ordinaries index ended 26.6 points stronger at 3,056.2 after hitting a record intraday high of 3,061.6 points.  it eclipsed the previous record closing high of 3032.9 set on tuesday.  the continuation of the recent strength in the market was driven again by news corp. with the commonwealth bank and rio tinto also leaping ahead, while the broader market was marginally better, shaw stockbroking dealer jamie spiteri said.  the market also showed a trend to stay above the 3,000-point mark.  "probably domestically the catalyst to holding it above 3,000 would be if interest rates do flatten out and could potentially go lower from here," spiteri said.  news corp.'s ordinary shares closed 71 cents, or 5.25 percent, firmer. volume was a massive 8.31 million shares.  the group's preferred shares were 67.5 cents, or 5.28 percent, higher at 13.46 australian dollars.  overall the media sector performed strongly, with publishing and broadcasting climbing 41 cents, or 4.2 percent on speculation that the media company would bring forward plans to float its on-line business.  shares in ten network holdings climbed 7 cents, after it posted solid first-half earnings wednesday, while seven network shares were flat at 5.25 australian dollars.  the commonwealth and anz banks also provided some spark to the banking sector, rising 48.6 cents and 25.5 cents respectively.  the national australia bank closed 5 cents higher while westpac dropped 1.3 cents.  overall, the all industrials index rose 52.9 points to 5,516.6 while the all resources index added 3.4 points to 1,037.6.  the highlight of the resources sector was rio tinto, which jumped 73 cents, or 3.37 percent, after a rise in london wednesday night.  but the rise failed to help fellow miners wmc which lost 3.7 cents at the end of the day and north, which was down 1.2 cents.  sector leader bhp added 2 cents.  the gold index fell 8.4 points to 960.3.  in sydney gold bullion closed at 280.15 unitedstates dollars an ounce, a rise of 1.15 dollars an ounce from wednesday's close.  national turnover stood at 460.71 million shares worth 1.31 billion australian dollars (816.13 million unitedstates dollars). there were 605 falling stocks and 564 rising ones while 450 remained steady.

title: study: broadband pc, interactive tv to battle for market
body: internet operators are shaping up to deliver video-based content via broadband networks, while broadcasters are ready to respond by adding interactive services.  this is the conclusion of a new study by strategy analytics, a unitedstates consulting business in high technology. the study also notes that in the battle for consumer dollar, broadcasters will have the edge in the near future: 14 percent of unitedstates households will have interactive tv by 2002, compared to only seven percent with broadband pc.  a number of new and traditional players in the unitedstates have staked their positions in this new market within the past few months, including internet service providers, network operators, broadcasters and technology providers, according to the study released thursday.  video and interactivity are the catalysts bringing these players into the same marketplace: internet providers offer enhanced content while broadcasters add interactivity.  the emerging broadband pc market is a result of increasing ownership of cable and digital subscriber line (dsl) modems.  analysts at the consulting firm believe that many consumers will not pay the current high costs of broadband internet, and that dsl and cable modems are still unproven as far as full interactive video services are concerned. nevertheless, they forecast that, by 2002, broadband modems will be in seven percent of unitedstates households and two percent in european households.  by this time, however, interactive tv services will be available in 14 percent of unitedstates homes and 23 percent of european homes. the firm predicted that many of these services will arrive "by the back door" as part of enhanced digital television services, allowing consumers to access home shopping, video-on-demand and interactive information services through their tv sets.  according to the study, interactive video will offer the internet four great challenges, namely the cost, usability, technology and tv. internet operators may ultimately find that the challenge from broadcasters is the greatest obstacle to success, the study predicted.

title: australian stocks close lower
body: a strong performance from media baron rupert murdoch's news corp ltd failed to inspire gains in the rest of the sharemarket wednesday as it closed marginally lower.  the all ordinaries index softened 3.3 points to 3,029.6 with most leaders, apart from news corp, surrendering the gains of tuesday that took the market to a record close.  the all industrials index lifted 8.1 points to 5,463.7 while all resources index dropped a hefty 17.7 points, 1.7 percent, to 1,034.2.  overall volume figures showed turnover of 347.13 million shares worth 744.1 million unitedstates dollars with 652 stocks falling, 489 rising and 426 remaining steady.  market leader news corp rose 45 cents by the close to 13.53 australian dollars on turnover of 8.03 million shares as it continued to benefit from tuesday's 2.1-billion-unitedstates-dollar cable television deal with unitedstates-based liberty media.  news corp's preferred scrip jumped 28.5 cents to 12.785 australian dollars.  bank stocks were lower with the industry sub-index sliding 38.5 points to 7,226.9 with anz bank a biggest loser.  anz retreated 26.5 cents to 11.295 australian dollars, commonwealth bank of australia off-loaded three cents to 26.89 australian dollars, westpac bank shed 12.5 cents to 11.613 australian dollars and national australia bank dropped five cents to 28.75 australian dollars.  resource stocks were led lower by diversified miner bhp, which dropped 33.4 cents to 13.61 australian dollars on profit taking.  in the other majors, global miner rio tinto slipped 17 cents to 21.67 australian dollars.  the gold index surrendered 25.8 points to 968.7 despite a 1.60-unitedstates-dollar firming in bullion to 280.00 unitedstates dollars an ounce in sydney in late trade.

title: china to host international seminar on educational use of internet
body: an international seminar on educational opportunities and the internet will be held here april 22-24, the chinese education association for international exchange (ceaie) said today.  more than 200 educators, scientists and entrepreneurs from china, the unitedstates, sweden and the netherlands will attend the three-day event, which is jointly sponsored by the ceaie and the international business university of beijing.  co-sponsors of the event also includes a california-based technological university.  during the seminar, discussions will be held on many hot educational topics including education via the internet, china's education in 21st century, the present and future role of longdistance education in china and the unitedstates, american education and international cooperation, and education modernization and opportunities.  shen xuesong, a ceaie official, said the seminar's theme is the further development of china's internet-education capabilities and exchanges with foreign countries in the fields of information technology and use of educational resources.  at the same time, educators from the unitedstates will demonstrate a series of internet equipment for long-distance education and the technological development of teaching materials.

title: australian stocks cracks record-breaking 3,000 point close
body: a surge on wall street and a sharp spike in news corp ltd shares combined to propel the australian stock market two percent higher for its first close above the 3000-point barrier.  the benchmark all ordinaries index jumped 59.5 points to a record finish of 3032.9, just off its intra-day record high of 3034.9 points.  abn amro chief equities strategist gerard minack said the australian bourse punched through the 3000 point barrier on the back of a strong overnight lead from wall street, where the dow jones industrial average index surged 174.82 points to 10,007.33.  "news corp has been that extra impetus that pushed us through," minack said.  global media company news corp shares stacked on 1.38 australian dollars to 13.08 australian dollars, off a peak of 13.35 australian dollars, and its preferred scrip raced 1.594 australian dollars higher to 12.50 australian dollars after it announced a 2.1 billion unitedstates dollar deal with unitedstates-based liberty media, part of the giant att corp.  on the australian equities market, the all industrials index climbed 108.9 points to 5455.6 and the all resources index stacked on 18.3 points to 1051.9.  banking stocks were robust with the industry sub index gaining 93.2 points to 7265.4.  the commonwealth bank of australia shot up 78 cents to 26.92 australian dollars, anz bank lifted 15 cents to 11.56 australian dollars, westpac bank rallied 14.8 cents to 11.738 australian dollars and national australia bank rose 10 cents to 28.80 australian dollars.  the resource sector was buoyed by australia's biggest industrial firm bhp, recovering 37.9 cents to 13.944 australian dollars, and rio tinto firming eight cents to 21.84 australian dollars.  the gold index lifted 6.9 points to 994.5.  the spot price of gold bullion in sydney closed at 278.60 unitedstates dollars, compared to 280.25 unitedstates dollars last thursday.  national turnover was 295.55 million stocks traded for 572.22 million unitedstates dollars, with rising stocks outnumbering falling stocks 644 to 532 and 399 stocks remaining steady.

title: internet to shape world economies: g77 official
body: the coming century will belong to information technology and the internet will largely shape the economies of the world, an official with g77 chamber of commerce and industry (g77-cci) said here monday.  tariq sayeed, chairman of g77-cci, said in his speech addressed to the eighth general assembly of his organization that one of the most revolutionary uses of the internet is in the world commerce.  he said:"already we can buy books and clothing, obtain business advice, and purchase everything from garden tools to hot sauce to high-tech communications equipment over the internet. we know it is just the beginning." "trade on the internet is doubling and tripling every single year. in just a few years, it will generate hundreds of billions of dollars in goods and services. according to some estimate, commerce volumes will grow to more than one trillion dollars by the year 2010," the chairman noted.  he pointed out that the electronic commerce will give rise to intense competition based on the survival of fittest, standardization of products on the part of companies and integration of economies by the countries themselves.  the use of internet in a big way, especially to bridge the information gap for better trade within g77, is indeed inevitable, he asserted.  the general assembly of g77-cci, which is held every two years, offers an opportunity for the delegates to share information and exchange views. this assembly being held here stresses the importance of advancing information technology in commerce and trade, urging more energy to be put in this direction.
