title: regional workshop on internet begins in dhaka
body: information technology (it) experts from india, pakistan, nepal and host bangladesh began a four-day regional workshop here monday to suggest steps for further development of internet communication in south asia.  the experts will adopt a set of recommendations for removal of legal barriers for development of internet communication, involving the private sector.  some 20 experts are participating in the workshop on "internet: south asian realities and opportunities," organized jointly by the local government engineering department of bangladesh and the kathmandu-based international center for integrated mountain development.  "leave it to the private sector to carve out opportunities for themselves unhindered," ahsan iqbal, state minister and deputy chairman of planning commission of pakistan, told the inaugural session.  presenting the keynote paper, he suggested that private companies of one country having good skill in the field should be allowed to "operate" in another country, as this would help promote transfer of technology as well as boosting intra-regional trade and commerce.  "since internet and it is among the fastest growing sectors, entrepreneurs should be provided with incentives to operate unregulated and untaxed for the next 10 years," said iqbal, who further suggested that governments should also provide private companies with security of capital and policy consistency.  he suggested that legal framework for e-commerce transactions should be developed and implemented so that credit card companies and banks be allowed to conduct financial transactions on the internet which is presently not allowed in the region.  south asian countries should be interconnected through "an optical fiber backbone" to pave the way for a regional information network, which would facilitate fast exchange of information and development of regional e-commerce network at a low cost, he said.  inaugurating the workshop, professor jamilur reza chowdhury of bangladesh regretted that telecommunication infrastructure in the country was very weak.  but the rate of telephone installation was the highest in the region, and "there are prospects for software export from bangladesh" despite certain bottlenecks impeding the growth of the it sector in the country, he said.

title: on-line insurance industry developing beijing, april
body: awareness of the potential of the internet in promoting the insurance business has been growing within the chinese insurance industry, according to today's business weekly.  many chinese insurance firms have dabbled in the internet by establishing homepages to provide visitors with itemized information and details of the insurance industry and their business.  the first chinese insurance policy sold on the internet was bought on november 28, 1997. since then, the on-line sale of insurance products has become a new business development tool for many chinese insurance companies.  however, on-line insurance business is still in its infancy.  "although most chinese insurance firms have applied the internet to their business, the uses remain very basic," said cai ying, an official with the beijing branch of china pacific insurance co. ltd.  the ideal on-line insurance transaction would be complete direct purchases of insurance services and remit the premiums via banks, said lily yang, chief representatives of ing insurance, a dutch firm.  however, current technical standards and legal frameworks have hindered full realization of on-line insurance practices.  it will not be fully realized until the chinese telecommunications industry can offer cheap and convenient internet services, said jean gora, senior researcher with the life office management association from the unitedstates.  on-line insurance has greatly influenced many aspects of daily life in western countries, particularly in the unitedstates.

title: internet set for explosive growth in china
body: the internet is witnessing explosive growth in china, with highly-educated young people accounting for the bulk of the surfers, according to the result of a recent survey released today.  sinclair, a beijing-based consultation company, launched a nationwide survey to find out the readiness of chinese people to take up the latest information technology.  the survey, under guidance of the ministry of information industry, found that 71.2 percent of non-internet-surfers are very interested in getting acquainted with the internet.  it also discovered that 85.6 percent of surfers are seeking information on science, technology, and political and social matters, while 70.8 percent of those questioned log on to the net to send and receive emails.  the major means of learning about the internet is through actual surfing on the net and 52.9 percent of surfers claim the magazine "computer world" is the most helpful and influential media source for their familiarity with the internet.  the survey found that the majority of those questioned, whether they are surfers or not, have acquired basic knowledge and knowhow about the internet.  however, the surfers said that the real age of e-commerce will arrive in about two to three years.  the survey found that 66.3 percent of surfers have computers at home and that an average surfer stays on the net for five hours and 16 minutes a week.  however, the surfers complained about the slow speed of logging on to the net. in addition, 71.6 percent of the non-net-surfers cite the arbitrary cost as the major obstacle that prevents them from logging on.  the survey was carried out in september-december last year but recently china has substantially dropped its internet charges.  the sinclair company received 10,408 effective replies to their questionnaires, which were handed out nationwide through the internet and traditional newspapers and magazines.  more than 85 percent of those surveyed are aged below 35 years of age, and over 77 percent of them have received a college education.

title: myanmar to allow access to internet
body: the myanmar government will allow access to the internet, which will be used more widely in education, health and electronic commerce, said a high-ranking communications official.  addressing a seminar here wednesday on economic benefit through electronic commerce technology on the internet, sponsored by a private company, brigadier-general win tin, minister of communications, posts and telegraph, said, "the world becomes a global village due to information technology (it). we are now in a knowledge era beyond it era." myanmar has been trying to formulate a master plan for the development of the country's it, importing annually tens of thousands of computers with very little tariff and classifying them as education aids and priority items.  the access to the internet for the private sector is also being striven.  meanwhile, myanmar computer associations are also trying to get support from regional and international counterparts, especially those from singapore and malaysia, to enhance the country's systematic it development.  myanmar held the first symposium on it initiative in june last year to promote the development and advancement of computer technology in the country.  for systematic development of it, the myanmar government promulgated the computer technology development law in september 1996 and later founded the computer technology development council.  in 1998, three associations of myanmar computer technicians, entrepreneurs and enthusiasts were also respectively formed.

title: u.s. paper use soars despite internet growth
body: contrary to predictions and forecasts, paper use in the unitedstates continues to swell even as more people go online and use email.  between 1990 and 1998, annual paper consumption in the country rose from 86.8 million tons to 99 million tons, said papercom., a non-profit group that studies the future of paper-based products and services.  "paper is emerging as the currency of the electronic era," said the group in a report this week. "people may read online, but if something is important they save it on paper." morning newspaper sales, the use of paper checks and postal volume have all increased as internet usage has expanded, the group said.  "while the internet and paper products will surely compete in some areas," said the group in the report, "the general pattern is one of mutual growth and interdependence." morning newspaper circulation in the unitedstates went up from 40.4 million copies in 1988 to an estimated 45.4 million in 1997, according to papercom.  mail volume rose from 166.4 billion pieces in 1992 to almost 200 billion last year, while envelope sales were at an all-time high in 1997.  meanwhile, advertising mail volume reached a record high of 82.  87 billion pieces in 1998 against 62.54 billion in 1992.  the volume of paper checks rose from 57.5 billion in 1991 to 66 billion in 1997.

title: beijing, hong kong in high-tech deals
body: representatives from beijing and hongkong at the current techworld'99 signed friday major deals involving capital investment, dealership for technology products and innovation.  the deals included an agreement on international cooperation for internet-based training and software, a joint venture on immunoassay diagnosis re-agent, an agreement on the joint development of pharmaceuticals based on genetic engineering, and a framework agreement on the cooperation in staff training for hightech firms.  the hongkong industrial technology center corporation (tech center), sponsor of the expo-conference, also signed a cooperative agreement with the china council for the promotion of international trade and a memorandum of understanding with beijing hi-tech incubation services center.  dr. lin wenyi, vice-mayor of beijing and head of the beijing delegation, said her delegation was here "to facilitate closer contacts between beijing's technology enterprises and their international counterparts." "we would like to encourage venture capitalists around the world to invest in beijing's high-tech development, and we also want to enhance cooperation between beijing and hongkong in technology development and investment," she said.  the three-day event has attracted more than 300 technology experts, businessmen and government officials from china, the unitedstates, russia, asia-pacific and european countries.

title: trial ip phone service set for authorization
body: preparations for operating an internet protocol (ip) phone service on a trial basis are in full swing in china, as the information industry watchdog promised a permit-issue system would be implemented if the trial goes smoothly.  earlier this month, the ministry of the information industry ( mit) announced that it had selected three telecom operators to provide pilot ip services as the first step towards standardizing this fledgling, but controversial, business.  however, "the ministry has not yet issued a notice to formally implement a plan that allows china telecom, china unicom and china jitong telecommunications co. to operate pilot ip services for six months," xu mutu, director of market administration at the ministry's telecom bureau, said yesterday.  the notice will be soon delivered to the companies, he said.  in january, a court ruled in favor of two business people running private ip services in fuzhou in southeast china's fujian province.  in response to the ruling, xu said the ministry would ban any " illegal establishment of an international telephone service on the internet." it was still setting up and improving facilities for the new business, and studying how to run it, he added.  mii has had to take into consideration the financial settlement between the chinese and foreign companies involved, and the provision of the hardware needed to operate an ip phone system, xu said.  ip calls can be made via conventional telephone when the time is ripe, he said.  a strict permit-issue system will be instituted after any problems emerging in the trial period have been resolved, and relevant standards formulated, he added.  the three pilot companies will be charged a fixed rate during the trial period, according to yi difei, another mii official.

title: china to open internet phone service market
body: chinese telecommunications companies awaiting approval from the ministry of information industry to start internet phone services will possibly obtain licenses in the latter half of this year.  according to officials with mii, three major chinese telecommunications companies, including china telecom, china unicom and china jitong telecommunications company, are piloting ip services in 25 major chinese cities for a period of six months.  zhao baoxin, deputy director of the telecommunications administration department of mii, said that the ministry is considering granting licenses to the three or more telecommunications companies after the aforementioned dealers end their trials later this year.  he said that in order to maintain the healthy development of ip services, a fixed charging rate will be given to the three pioneering telecommunications companies during the trial period.  local observers said that ip services can effectively lower the costs of international long distance dialing, compared with those offered through the current chinese telecommunications networks, since the internet-based services transmit voice and speech sounds through the global web.

title: china to open first on-line export fair
body: the 85th china export commodities fair will open on april 15 in guangzhou, and, simultaneously, on the internet. for the first time, the fair will break out beyond the 160,000square-meter-site near the guangzhou railway station, and connect to businesses all over the world via the 'net. like previous fairs, the first on-line guangzhou fair will present exhibitions and services and trading booths. enterprises taking part in the on-site fair will be able to post commercial information on the internet fair by themselves at any time, as a search engine has been created classifying enterprises and commodities. the on-line fair also provides discuss rooms with various topics where viewers will be able to discuss things freely. there will also be rooms for negotiations, coded for secrecy. moreover, email and fax services will be readily available. the internet was used for the first time three years ago during the 80th fair when a website was opened, and the 83rd fair employed the internet to send invitations to over 2,000 enterprises. the test version of this first on-line guangzhou fair is already on-line at: http://www.cecf-gz.com, or: http://cecf.com. cn.

title: international news corp. opens office in beijing
body: media tycoon rupert murdoch's news corporation (news corp.) opened a representative office in beijing today, the first major international media company to do so.  "the opening of our new representative office in beijing marks another milestone in news corporation's business development in china," said gareth chang, executive director of news corp. and executive chairman of star tv, at the opening ceremony held today.  news corp. investments in china include its star tv network and the star tv joint venture, phoenix satellite tv, which currently broadcasts the phoenix chinese channel reaching over 45 million households, according to chang.  "in addition, news corp. has joint ventures in beijing with the people's daily (pdn xinren information technology co. ltd.) and in tianjin (golden mainland production co. ltd.). its other interests include chinabyte, a major website in china, and golden mainland, a leader in post-production services with a client base including cctv and major provincial stations.  last year, news corp.'s 20th century fox studio enjoyed strong success in china with the release of the films "titanic" and "home alone." "developments in the media industry in china, including rapid technological change, make us optimistic about the potential for our business here," said chang.  news corp. is one of the world's largest media companies with total assets of 36 billion unitedstates dollars and total annual revenues of 14 billion unitedstates dollars.  its commercial empire covers the unitedstates, canada, the uk, australia, latin america and asia, with operations in television, newspapers, magazines and books, the production and distribution of movies, and other areas.

title: microsoft's chinese version of new web browser
body: the world's largest software provider, microsoft, released the chinese version of its internet explorer 5.0 today.  microsoft is scheduled to release versions in 9 languages today but because of time difference, the ie 5.0 is being made available in china earlier than in the us.  the ie 5.0 will make interaction with the internet quicker and more convenient and it is easier for professionals to develop, deploy and manage, according to julia wu, general manager of microsoft (china) co., ltd.  however, the ie 5.0 seems less powerful to some than its predecessor the ie 4.0, which was released in sep. 1998. but, wu says, the new browser may not be a revolution, but it will be a popular product. the ie 5.0 is 20-25 percent faster than the ie 4.  0 and 75 percent faster than its rival the navigator 4.5.  the new browser allows a computer to be used for real-time radio or television reception from the internet. it contains the windows media players and can be applied to vcds, which might make it popular in china, the world's largest vcd market.  the new ie also allows users to choose from the nine search options like yahoo and excite. and, it can be downloaded from the internet or purchased through traditional channels and is smaller than the 4.0 version. the ie 5.0 has 6.5 megabytes, but the 4.0 has 12 megabytes so downloading time is shorter.  in addition to microsoft's chinese language website, internet users can download ie 5.0 from 13 chinese internet service providers and internet content providers.

title: scientists conduct remote experiment via internet
body: scientists in beijing have conducted a high level experiment in a nuclear analysis lab in east china's shanghai, nearly 1,500 kilometers away, via the internet.  according to a report in science times, the first example of such experiments in china underlines the trend for making increasing use of computer and internet technology to help scientists share advanced experimental instruments, even if at a distance.  "if a nationwide network, sharing the resources of advanced and expensive instruments, can be established in china, the duplication of funds and equipment can be avoided and research efficiency greatly increased," a scientist with the chinese academy of sciences, was quoted as saying.  the internet technology will provide a first level research environment for scientists and make it possible to conduct joint experiments participated in by a large number of scientists and labs in different countries and regions.  nuclear scientists are especially interested in the teleexperiment, said one taking part, because most nuclear science experiments in laboratories require the cooperation of many scientists. he noted that "it will save time and money on traveling." however, some experts claims that existing internet technology can not completely meet the demand for such remote experiments and that further development is still needed.

title: hke031264 --australian stocks close at record high for second day
body: the booming australian sharemarket entered uncharted territory again friday, closing at a record high after breaking through thursday the 2,950-point barrier for the first time since 1990.  the benchmark all ordinaries index rose 10.8 points to 2,961.3 friday, marking a record high for the second consecutive day.  "the market finished strongly on a positive note following another strong lead from overseas markets overnight," said morgan stockbroking's simon reed.  in new york, dow jones industrial average picked up 124.60 points to 9,897.44, a new high for the second day in a row.  henderson charlton jones' stuart smith said the local market held on to most of the session's gains, forgoing much of the traditional friday afternoon profit-taking.  the all industrials index rose 6.4 points to 5,328.3 while the all resources index lifted 18.3 points to 1,025.1.  dealers said solid gains made by heavyweights such as news corp., bhp, rio tinto, and the commonwealth bank underpinned the market in the latter half of the session.  national turnover was a reasonably modest 418.64 million shares valued at 1.1 billion australian dollars (698.5 million unitedstates dollars), with 750 rises, 572 falls and 440 stocks steady.  at the top end of the resources sector, bhp continued to power ahead, gaining 21.5 cents.  fellow miner rio tinto was also in the good books, surging 70 cents while wmc picked up five cents.  among the leading industrials, rupert murdoch's news corporation gained 18 cents while the preferred stock lifted 15 cents.  in the banking sector, the standout was the commonwealth bank which rose 24 cents. of the other big four only westpac also made gains, up 6.1 cents, while the national australia bank slumped 29.4 cents and anz dropped 10.5 cents.  telecommunications stocks were mostly lower.  telstra sank four cents as the market remained disappointed that a special dividend was not included in its interim results delivered.  cable wireless optus slipped six cents while aapt bucked the trend to pick up three cents.  the australian gold bullion closed at 293.80 unitedstates dollars an ounce compared to thursday's close of 293.40.

title: vietnam, japan sign internet agreement
body: the vietnam data company (vdc) under the vietnam post and telecommunications (vnpt) and japan's kdd corporation signed an agreement here thursday to connect vnpt-internet with kdd's internet, vietnam news agency reported friday.  under the agreement, the national internet will connect with an internet gate named neweb by a 2 mbps high-speed digital circuit via an optical-fiber submarine cable.  this will provide internet users with easier and quicker access to networks in other countries and territories in the asia-pacific region, including australia, singapore, south korea, new zealand, malaysia, indonesia, the philippines and india.  the vdc, the only internet access provider in vietnam, reported that after more than one year's link to the internet, vietnam has had more than 20,000 internet users.  it also estimated that an additional 1,000 new subscribers join the service every month.  earlier, the vdc opened four international gates to connect the national internet with australia via satellite with a capacity of 256 kbps, with hongkong via a 2 mbps optical-fiber submarine cable and with the unitedstates via satellite and submarine cable with transmission capacity of 64 kbps and 2 mbps respectively.

title: interactive govt service directory launched in hk
body: the hongkong special administrative region (sar) launched here thursday its interactive government services directory (igsd).  employment services, road traffic information, investment services and other information on public services will be at finger tips after the launching of the innovative project.  through igsd, the public will be able to obtain selected government services and information on public services over the internet in an interactive manner.  the new service will offer a web-enabled directory of telephone numbers and web site addresses for public services.  the public can also access selected interactive services provided by the industry department, labor department and transport department.  the implementation of the innovative project is part of the sar government's efforts in promoting the wider use of information technology (it) in the community and the adoption of electronic transactions in hongkong under the "digital 21" it strategy.  the telephone and web site directory on public services provides a user-friendly directory which categorizes public services by their nature, rather than by department.  it also provides hyperlinks to the homepages of government bureaus/departments and public agencies for detailed information on specific types of public services.  through the new service, road users can obtain on-line video images of traffic conditions on major routes and information on major road closure and on public transport services to and from the airport.  the industry department will through the same system provide investors with information about making investment in hongkong; present personalized information to investors; and notify individual investors via email as and when new information of interest to them has been put on the department's homepage.  as for the interactive employment service of the labor department, it will allow job seekers to search for job vacancies registered with the department based on specific search criteria.  similarly, employers will be able to search for potential candidates registered with the department based on specified search criteria.  employers can also submit vacancies to the department through the internet.  apart from personal computers with internet connection, members of the public can access igsd through computers for public use in selected district offices and public libraries. some major telecommunications companies in hongkong also provide access points to the public. k. c. kwong, secretary for information technology and broadcasting of the hksar, said that through this directory, the government can promote public awareness about electronic services, which will pave the way for the launching of the "electronic service delivery" scheme in the latter half of 2000.  in his policy address in october last year, chief executive tung chee hwa set the target of building hongkong into a leading city in the world for the development and application of information technology, especially in electronic commerce and software engineering.  financial secretary donald tsang announced a 13 billion hk dollar (1.7 billion unitedstates dollar) cyberport project in his budget address on march 3.  hongkong telecom and microsoft have announced strategic cooperation to develop high-speed broadband services that will allow hongkong to fully experience the convergence of low-cost personal computer and telecommunications technologies.

title: overpriced internet-service complaints
body: many chinese internet users are complaining that service providers are overcharging them while operating at a snail's pace and failing to provide a full array of information services.  according to a survey conducted by the china computer association, nearly one-third of the people polled, or 31.5 percent, consider high charges the major impediment to their internet access.  almost a quarter, or 24.6 percent, expressed their dissatisfaction with the low speed which some called "slow as a snail." more than one-fifth, or 21.6 percent, complained that there was a lack of useful information on the 'net.  the reason for the first two problems is considered to be the monopoly held by china's domestic telecommunications sector.  currently, china inputs only 0.01 percent and accesses only 0.  05 percent of all information offered on the internet as a whole.  and much of this information is of no benefit to 'net users.  computer experts point out that the development and use of information resources are still very weak in china.  thus, the enthusiasm of internet users is restrained and internet servers are experiencing serious management difficulties, and as a result on-line information services are declining.

title: undp to set up electronic centers in egypt
body: the united nations development program (undp) is prepared to open three electronic community centers in egypt, as part of a series of digital projects in africa, arab states, asia and latin america.  this was announced by the undp here on thursday.  the scheme, to be started on march 14, is aimed at providing community access to the internet and training for civil society groups, the private sector, low-income communities and individuals.  by linking communities to the global economy, the sites are expected to create new opportunities for economic growth, the undp said in a press release.  according to the plan, each center will be equipped with a server and some 10 pentium pcs, backed by additional training computers in each location.  dedicated local internet connectivity will be provided for each center. training and skills development programs will focus on computer literacy, email operations, web page creation and desktop publishing.  the centers are located in sharkeya governorate with a population of 4.2 million. it is one of the 26 of egyptian governorates and some 2 hours by car from cairo.  undp officials believe that such centers can bring information to the unconnected people of the developing world, especially in remote and rural areas.

title: microsoft in deal to give chinese tv users web access
body: bill gates, chairman of the microsoft corp., today unveiled his grand plan, named "venus", to give chinese users of regular tv sets access to on-line games, software and the internet.  speaking in shenzhen, a special economic zone, gates said, "by delivering this technology in a low-cost and easy to use format, we hope to increase access to educational software and ultimately the internet for chinese consumers." in the coming decade, according to gates, most adults will be able to use email and be part of the network. chinese people cannot live without the web as they cannot live without the telephone and the television.  the "venus" project is the best way to increase china's integration into the networking era, an executive of microsoft ( china) co., ltd. said.  the device in the project will be manufactured by microsoft in cooperation with partners in china including the legend group, stone ginbin co., yuxing electronics group, haier group, acer inc., bbk electronics co., ltd., integrated technology express inc., and philips ltd.  china lags behind the world's current level of networking and by the end of 1998 it had 2.1 million internet users, which is an equivalent of the size of a medium internet service provider (isp) in the unitedstates global internet users had reached 153 million by 1998.  on the other hand, china is the largest market for household electric appliances. it has 317 million tv sets, covering 90 percent of households and 40 million video compact disk players.  the national telephone coverage has reached 25 percent and in cities is as high as 50 percent.  "the low costs and easy usage of internet access provided by the "venus" project will create more markets for china's software and web service industries and help expand their business scale," said sean zhang, general manager of microsoft china rd center.

title: hk telecom, microsoft to develop broadband on-line service
body: hongkong's major full-service communications provider hongkong telecom and american software giant microsoft announced here today strategic cooperation to develop high-speed broadband services that will allow hongkong to fully experience the convergence of low-cost personal computer and telecommunications technologies.  the joint effort, announced by hongkong telecom chief executive linus w. l. cheung and visiting microsoft chairman and ceo bill gates at a press conference, is expected to usher in an era of technology convergence for a new lifestyle in hongkong.  cheung said at the press conference that the two companies will be developing "very exciting applications to stimulate the usage of the pcs and their applications." he said hongkong telecom can provide high-speed internet which is 30 to 300 times faster than normal internet and … "it is very important we create applications like turning pcs into interactive tvs." "i hope this partnership of cooperation will not only set an example for hongkong, breaking new markets, but for the world." gates said hongkong is in a "very privileged position" because of the companies that add up the internet to the pcs and the investment that has been made to the existing network.  "there is a chance to really lead the way to show the applications of how businesses will be done in the years ahead," he said.  describing the joint project as a "milestone," gates said, "we see ourselves as really giving the businesses here in hongkong a platform to be created with… and to address the entire market." with the project, home pc users will be able to view exciting movie titles and view these on their pcs or on their tvs --just by browsing through titles of the latest movies, while at the same time having access to the wealth of information available on the internet.  users will be able to communicate with their friends via live video conferencing, participate in voice or on-line chat rooms, send and receive email, check the latest news, go shopping and conduct secure e-commerce transactions.  students will be able to interact and share in the learning experience in new and unique ways.  businesses will benefit from new and advanced solutions and applications hosted and available through hongkong telecom's broadband network, while also gaining access to an entirely new class of video-enabled applications including video conferencing and training-on-demand.  the innovative services will run on a tightly integrated microsoft platform which will accommodate a wide spectrum of existing service components and capital assets.  the new applications scheduled to be implemented include video on demand, music on demand, software on demand, up-to-the-minute news and game zone.  the new application will be added up to the existing and the world's first interactive tv and high-speed internet service, launched by the hongkong telecom a year ago.

title: jetco becomes 1st hk internet certification authority
body: internet banking in hongkong has reached another milestone as the local banking consortium joint electronic teller services ltd. (jetco) became the first internet certification authority in the special administrative region (sar).  following the completion of a major system integration project led by global computing and internet provider hewlett-packard (hp), jetco will be able to provide its member banks with digital certificates for web-based transactions, thus giving customers complete assurance that their home banking transactions are secure, according to hp hongkong today.  at the same time, jetco will offer member banks a "virtual atm" service that duplicates the look-and-feel of the banks' physical atms on their customers' pcs, enabling them to offer a customized home banking service without large-scale investment in new hardware or software.  jetco chairman chung che-shum described this as "another major milestone" in hongkong's history as a world-renowned financial center.  "by becoming a certification authority, we are able to help virtually all of the sar's retail banks to enter the on-line age in one fell swoop," chung said.  established in july 1982, jetco began operations in august 1983.  it now has 49 member banks and operates more than 1,500 atms in hongkong.

title: dell opens online superstore to sell computer-related products
body: dell computer corp. wednesday said it plans to introduce an online superstore for consumers to buy computer-related products.  the store will initially offer more than 30,000 computerrelated products from many leading brand manufacturer's, including printers, digital cameras, scanners, games, software and business products, according to a report from the company.  unlike other online stores, which force buyers to consider only selected goods --making it difficult to comparison-shop --dell promised to allow shoppers to search for products by category, manufacturer, product model, features and price. it also promised to offer extremely competitive pricing on popular products.  dell is the world's top direct seller of personal computers and currently sells more than 14 million unitedstates dollars in computers each day over the web, 25 percent of the company's business.  dell's online superstore will "offer online shoppers a convenient way to buy the software and accessories they need for their computers," said michael dell, chairman and chief executive officer of the company.  the internet superstore is part of dell's commitment to generate 50 percent of revenues through the internet within one and one-half years.  industry analysts see a shift in the personal computer business to sales of consumer electronics and other low-cost commodity goods instead of high-powered, costly pcs. online hardware sales are expected to rise to 15 billion dollars in 2003 from one billion dollars in 1998.

title: china slashes telecommunication fees
body: china announced here today that it will cut the charges on using the internet by about 50 percent and lower international telephone fees as of march 1.  the ministry of information industry (mii) said in a news release today that it will also lower charges on fixed telephone installation and on opening mobile telephone lines.  it also announced to stop levying administrative fees on local telephone call networks and cut administrative fees levied on longdistance telephone calls.  postal fees of letters will be raised by 20-60 percent, mii said in the news release.  "the adjustment of postal and telecommunication fees will greatly lower the general level of charges," the news releases said.  "this move is aimed to resolve the protruding contradictions in the structure of fees," it said.  according to mii, charges on international telephone calls to the unitedstates will drop from 18.4 yuan to 15 yuan per minute, an reduction of 18 percent. fees on international telephones calls to asian countries will be cut to 12 yuan per minute.  individuals using the internet will pay four yuan per hour for the first 60 hours in a month and pay eight yuan for every additional hour in the month. internet service providers (isp) will pay the same fees as individual users do for using dedicated lines linking with internet.  china has adjusted telecommunications fees for several times in the past decade. the latest adjustment took place in december 1996 when international telephone fees were reduced.

title: hke022332-australian personal computers to hit 11 million by
body: there will be an estimated 11 million personal computers in australia -a country with a population of 18.7 million -by the year 2001, new research has revealed tuesday.  according to data compiled by the australian film commission (afc), there were almost 6.8 million computers in 1998, a million more than the previous year.  a study found there was at least one computer in 2.9 million australian homes with 900,000 connected to the internet and another 500,000 expected to access the net within 12 months.  and of the 3.9 million homes without a computer -400,000 expected to buy one within the next 12 months and 3.5 million did not.  overall, there were 1.09 million internet subscribers including 450,000 business customers.  the most common uses for household computers were playing computer games (59 percent), learning or study activities (54 percent) and work-related activities (38 percent).  in february 1998, more than 20 percent of users had spent some time on the internet, compared with only seven percent in february 1996.  the research, released in the afc's fifth edition of get the picture, also found the top five activities nominated as the main reason for internet use were: email (23.5 percent); business (19.7 percent); entertainment (14.4 percent); research (11.4 percent); and news and reference (6.7 percent).

title: greeting friends on net popular in east china province
body: the high-tech world of computers is changing even the face of the traditional chinese lunar new year as increasing numbers of people are sending electronic greetings cards on-line to friends and family and even exchanging messages with relatives across thousands of miles.  a perfect example happened in the eastern coastal province of zhejiang where doctor wu yue clicked his mouse and suddenly on the terminal screen two chinese cartoon children appeared singing a message wishing him happy new year...all the way from singapore, almost as soon as it had been sent.  "it's quick and economical," said doctor wu, "it requires only a few minutes to send an electronic card on the internet. this means i do not have to go to a post office, write an envelope or buy stamps." yao bini, even though in her 60s, is another discovering that the new technology is a boon. she was so excited when she had a dialogue on internet with her son who is studying in the unitedstates that it brought tears to her eyes. yao spent one hour " talking" with her son on-line.  "it costs only 0.35 yuan per minute," explained yao, who had bought a computer and connected it to the internet in order to talk freely with her son.  yao even invited relatives and friends to her home on spring festival eve at her son's request for he wanted to greet them personally during the celebrations via the internet.  hangzhou, the capital city of zhejiang, began to provide people with access to the internet in 1995. today, nearly 40,000 people have taken advantage of the service, according to the city's telecommunications office.  meanwhile, a number of middle school students in beijing have called on people to send less paper cards because of the increasing need to protect wood resources. email and electronic cards are now ideal alternative choices, they insist. latest statistics showed that more than 2.1 million people had access to the internet last year across china.

title: att-tci merger wins approval of regulators, shareholders
body: federal regulators and shareholders of both att corp. and cable giant tci approved on wednesday the merger deal of the two companies that could give consumers one-stop shopping --from local calling to high-speed internet access --over cable tv lines.  federal communications commission officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the agency voted to clear the deal, which was valued at nearly 32 billion when it was announced in june. but the action isn't considered official and final until the commission publicly releases information on the order.  shareholders of att overwhelmingly approved the deal at a meeting this morning in new jersey. and a majority of tci's shareholders, meeting in colorado, approved the deal later in the day. the merger plan must also be approved by local cable franchising authorities.  att is the nation's largest telecommunications company and biggest provider of mobile phone services. tci is the nation's second-largest cable tv company, with lines reaching one-third of all unitedstates homes.  many of those tci lines have been upgraded to permit cable tv customers to connect their computers to the internet and access online data at speeds as much as 100 times faster than conventional telephone lines.  eventually, att intends to make tci's lines capable of providing customers with local phone service, too. att has a separate agreement with cable company time warner to provide local phone service over its high-speed cable tv lines. more cable agreements are expected.  the cable agreements would give att a way to get into homes without having to rely on phone lines controlled by the regional bell companies, which dominate the local phone market.  through the merger, att also will control tci's stake in athome corp., a leading provider of high-speed internet access.  the justice department approved the merger in december on the condition that tci sell its interest in a rival mobile phone company, sprint pcs.

title: white-collar workers keen on helping poor students
body: for the first time since her father's death, min pinghua, a 15-year-old student at the shanghai shuyuan middle school, could not help smiling because the helping hand extended by a complete stranger has just prevented her from dropping out of school.  min's father died in a car accident in 1994, leaving behind his wife and two little girls and more than 60,000 yuan in debts. mrs.  min, a poor farmer living in the outskirts of shanghai, since then has had great difficulty supporting the family and was considering that pinghua might have to leave school.  a senior clerk at the shanghai asian paper co. ltd., who identifies himself only as zhang, read about min's story on the internet and decided to provide her with 1,500 yuan a year until her graduation.  "for us, the figure of 1,500 yuan may only mean a suit, but for pinghua, it can afford her a year's schooling that may bring about great changes in her life, " zhang said. "so, i believe what i've done is worthwhile." zhang is the first, but not the only, white-collar worker offering help to poor students in this largest industrial and commercial city in china. actually, a line of donors has begun to form since the shanghai charity foundation launched an aid-poorstudents web site on the internet last december 25, which carries brief introductions about needy students in the city to find aid for them in a more efficient way.  in less than 40 days, more than 20,000 people, mostly young white-collar workers with good education, have visited the web site one-hundred of these folks have already started funding the first 100 students, and 50 have signed agreements to aid the next 50 students to be listed, and more are waiting for coming announcements of still other needy ones.  "some people worry that young white-collar workers might become indifferent selfish as market forces play a bigger and bigger role in the country," said xu benliang, director of the shanghai charity education center. "now we're relieved to see that they still carry forward the fine chinese traditions of warm heartedness and mutual assistance." statistics from the shanghai professional personnel exchange center indicate that there are more than 300,000 young whitecollar workers in the city's major state-owned enterprises and institutions, and some 10,000 in overseas-funded businesses, with monthly incomes ranging from 1,500 to 25,000 yuan, much higher than the average local salary, and many of them are cyber-surfers.  according to the charity program, a donor is asked to provide at least 1,500 yuan a year to support one poor student. all the donor needs to do is to choose a student, fill out a form, both through the web site and then send the money to the foundation.  and recently, an increasing number of donors are no longer satisfied with their indirect help, and have extended their aid outside the internet by establishing direct ties with the students they fund.  qi jun, an insurance company clerk, and his wife have made additional plans to give study guidance to the two middle-school students they support. the couple intends to help them become university students. "i know how important education is to a person because i myself have benefited a lot from it," qi said. "now i'm glad i can help the needy continue schooling." shanghai, with a population of 13 million, has about 100,000 poor students, and the city has tried many ways to make sure that no student has to drop out because of financial problems.

title: australian stocks close up on higher company profits
body: australian shares closed higher thursday as strong earnings results from market heavyweights overshadowed the weakening effect of the shock resignation of one of the country's top bankers.  the all ordinaries index closed 12.2 points firmer at 2,867.0, the all industrials index firmed 14.9 points to 5,178.6 and the all resources put on 12.0 points to 969.7.  the market was buoyed early by strong earnings results from both news corp and local property and investment company lend lease but drifted a little after the shock departure of westpac chief executive robert joss.  market activity was strong with 391.2 million shares traded worth 1.4 billion australian dollars (903 million unitedstates dollars).  westpac easily topped the value table with 10.97 million shares traded, as it slipped 30 cents. joss's departure overshadowed the news that long-serving coca-cola amatil chairman dean wills would resign at its annual meeting in april.  coca-cola amatil shares dropped 25 cents by the close despite announcing a slightly better than anticipated net profit.  news corp ordinary shares added 40.3 cents while its preferred scrip was 25 cents dearer.  the overall financial services sector was also weaker with a mixed performance from the major banks with national australia bank adding 22.9 cents, commonwealth bank of australia closed 16 cents dearer and anz eased two cents.  telstra closed five cents higher while rival cable wireless optus eased five cents. optus topped volume with 20.8 million shares changing hands. bhp led the resources sector higher with a 31-cent gain, rio tinto was 30 cents stronger, wmc rose two cents, mim was down two cents.  the gold index was marginally firmer at 1,052.0 points with a gain of 3.5 points.  the price of gold bullion in sydney closed at 287.10 unitedstates dollars per fine ounce compared to 288.00 wednesday.

title: general motors opens chinese web site
body: the world's largest automotive manufacturer general motors of the unitedstates opened a chinese web site on the internet about its branch company in china. the www.gmchina.com web site offers more than 40 pages of information about gm china both in chinese and in english. it offers product information on buick, chevrolet, cadillac and opel which are all sold in china, as well as service centers and customer assistance information. it also highlights gm's cooperation with china in technological exchanges, company information on gm's chinese joint ventures and the latest announcements from gm china. "the design of the new gm china website is intended to bring the latest information about the company to the china market," said lawrence zahner, president of gm china group. gm china now has three joint ventures in china, including shanghai gm, an equally shared joint venture with shanghai automotive industries corp., the pan asia technical automotive center, and jinbei-gm, an equally shared joint venture with the no. 1 auto works. shanghai gm produced the first buick car in china in last december. jinbei gm is expected to start producing chevrolet blazers and s-10 crew cab pickup trucks in 2001.
