title: internet links tibet with world
body: china's central government last year spent 600 million yuan to build a long-distance fiber-optic telecoms cable connecting tibet and northwest china provinces, which has provided 20,000 more telephone lines in the region.  and as a result, lhasa's telecoms bureau has been able to register 300 internet users over the past six months.  meanwhile, tibet's tourism department has set up a website about travel routes and programs for people interested in visiting this mysterious land and the internet has shortened the distance between this remote plateau and the outside world.  nyima cering, an official in charge of internet registration with the lhasa telecommunications office, said that anyone who has a valid identification card can register an internet account number which is very cheap, costing about two pennies every three minutes.  he also revealed that the authorities plan to open public cybercafes to meet the demand from internet users.  "before democratic reform in 1959, the whole region of tibet had only ten telephones and they were available only to rich families living in lhasa," nyima cerging added. "but now telephones are very popular throughout tibet even amongst farming and herding families.  although internet use in tibet is much less than in other chinese regions, the users in the region can obtain the same information as in metropolises like beijing and shanghai," he said.  "users in tibet can also read domestic news stories issued by such organizations as the xinhua news agency, people's daily and china daily. they are also able to visit foreign websites," he added.  today, more and more people in tibet are able to have access to domestic and international information through the internet and to open a window on tibetan folk customs and culture for worldwide websurfers.  for example, australian scholar charles ramble is translating the "dba'bzhed", the oldest book tracing the arrival of buddhism in tibet some 1200 years ago. he is also working on a translation of the first tibetan buddhist "samyai" scripture and says that email contact with tibetan academic pasang wangdu is helping his project enormously.  and wangdu, a social sciences researcher, says that he is also enjoying the benefits as he has conducted many joint projects with foreign experts who are keen to translate ancient tibetan books into english.  "for such work i was obliged in the past to attend international seminars or lecture abroad," he said. "but now i can do this easily via the internet every day." last month, pasang received 23 emails from foreign scholars looking for his assistance.  qoipei norbu, a young lecturer in the university of tibet, also maintains regular communication on the internet with his british chum ian ormesher.  "through the net ian is learning chinese and tibetan from me," said qoipei."and merely by using the internet at home i am able to receive information from across the world very conveniently," added norbu, who often visits the websites of american universities.

title: australian stocks close up on media stocks
body: the australian sharemarket wednesday defied negative overseas market leads to close up, but off its highs, with offshore money pouring into the domestic and new zealand markets inspiring a futures-led rally early, dealers said.  the benchmark all ordinaries index closed 11.2 points, or 0.39 percent, higher at 2918.2 -off a high of 2930.5 in the early afternoon -after losing ground on profit taking.  "there were some big offshore orders in the morning session which came into australia and new zealand," said funds manager ausbil partners equities director paul xiradis.  "it looks as if the offshore investors were quite positive on the australian market, but it's hard to know exactly where they have been directing their money." the all industrials index closed up 18.9 points at 5308.1 and the all resources index closed up 5.2 points at 946.4.  media stocks with internet businesses buoyed the market, with heavyweight news corp, which has a business agreement with us-based internet stock yahoo inc, gaining nine cents to 11.84 australian dollars.  kerry packer's publishing and broadcasting, considering a stock market float of its internet business pbl online, gained 20 cents.  newspaper publisher john fairfax holdings surged 16 cents, or 4.21 percent, on a turnover of 2.52 million shares.  telstra corp dipped in late trade as investors took profits, losing 15 cents, on a turnover of 12.08 million shares.  its rival, cable wireless optus, gained three cents, with 27.04 million shares traded.  national australia bank slipped eight cents, commonwealth bank gained 5.1 cents, anz banking group rose 15 and westpac banking corp lost 10 cents.  among the major resources companies, bhp gained six cents, wmc rose one, rio tinto lifted 15.6 and woodside petroleum gained 11.3cents.  the gold index closed 5.8 points, or 0.54 percent, higher at 1085.3 points.  sydney gold bullion lost 0.20 to 288.70 unitedstates dollars an ounce.  national turnover was 508.2 million shares traded valued at 1.25 billion australian dollars (800 million unitedstates dollars), with 643 rises, 543 falls and 482 stocks steady.

title: china's internet fees expected to go down
body: the growing number of complaints from china's 2.1 million internet users may quiet down a bit as the government is considering ways to cut charges.  a source at the beijing telegraph bureau, who refused to give her name, said today that charges will be reduced to some extent and the cut will be more dramatic for institutional users.  the bureau has the biggest number of internet users in the country.  chang xiaobin, deputy director of the telecommunications bureau under the ministry of information industry (mii), confirmed that and said that charges will be cheaper in 1999.  he said that the ministry will begin to study data transmission prices for a more scientific policy for the information industry.  but there isn't any specific timetable for the price cut, added chang, who was cautious about how much it would be.  the high cost of using the information superhighway has become the biggest headache for most chinese, according to a recent survey in beijing, which is home to a fourth of china's internet users.  the people of beijing on average spend 34.8 percent of their monthly salaries just to get onto the internet, a sharp comparison to the one percent in the unitedstates.  the mii, price bureaus and local governments jointly decide how much chinese internet users have to pay, a form of monopolization that has been cited as a major problem.  the high charges have been blamed as one of the factors that hinder the development of the information industry, and many internet providers feel that it's difficult to make money from a small market, according to the survey.  in fact a number of local providers have voluntarily introduced flexible price policies geared to certain time frames and rewarding frequent use.  observers say that if the new government cuts come true, it indicates that china will continue to encourage people to use the internet and allow it to be used for a wider range of things in spite of restrictions on pornography and violence.  most chinese had not even heard of the internet until the mid1990s, but it is predicted that there will be 10 million chinese internet users in the next four years.

title: internet appeal in china gets sperm donors
body: a recent appeal for sperm donations on the internet has drawn responses from more than a hundred men in shanghai.  because of the shortage of sperm, renji hospital opened a web site two months ago and made an emotional appeal for donations. at least 10 volunteers have come to the hospital, giving hope to sterile people, wu yulun, a professor in charge of its male sterility lab, told xinhua tuesday. more than a hundred people promised to donate, most of them young or middle-aged white-collar workers. renji's sperm bank is the only one in shanghai and has had fewer than 100 donors since it opened eight years ago.  artificial fertilization can assist about 30 percent of the sterile couples conceive, professor wu added. selection procedures are very strict about the health of donors to check on the possibility of hereditary or contagious diseases, he said, and the education background is important. donors' names are kept strictly confidential.  many people are hesitant to make a donation because of misgivings about potential legal, moral, and family problems, wu said, and this makes it all the more necessary that all legal documents be standardized. also, the larger the sperm bank, the less the chance will be that there are inbreeding problems.

title: australian stocks hit new record close
body: the australian sharemarket surged to an all-time closing high monday as investors, buoyed by economic fundamentals, poured money into telecommunications, media and bank stocks.  the all ordinaries index closed up 29.9 points to 2,923.7, smashing its previous high of 2,897.3 set on january 7 this year.  strength in key international markets on friday contributed to the rise in the local market.  wall street closed on friday 77.5 points higher at 9,358.83, with surging growth in the unitedstates economy spurring confidence in the corporate profit outlook.  "a firmer lead in the unitedstates set the tone for a very strong day on our market with telecommunications and bank shares continuing to rally, building on last week's strong performances with many stocks reaching record highs during the day," said simon reed, client adviser from morgan stockbroking.  national turnover was a healthy 1.1 billion australian dollars (693 million unitedstates dollars) with 405.84 million shares changing hands with 667 rises, 624 falls and 431 stocks steady.  the all industrials index closed up 69.5 points at 5,319.8, however the all resources index lost 6.8 points to 946.3.  telecommunications giant telstra starred again monday adding 51 cents, or 5.9 percent to close at a record high of 9.15 australian dollars.  rival telecom cable wireless optus was not far behind rising 13 cents, or 3.45 percent. it also topped the day's turnover on a volume of 28.98 million shares.  global media group news corp. also added weight to the domestic market on the back of gains by its american depository receipts in unitedstates trade.  news corp.'s ordinary shares closed up 35 cents, or 3.04 percent, while its preferred shares gained 27 cents, or 2.5 percent.  bank stocks continued to perform strongly after renewed interest rate cut speculation.  westpac led the surge by jumping 27 cents, or 2.45 percent, national australia bank rose 18.5 cents, the commonwealth closed 22.8 cents higher and anz added 3.3 cents.  resource stocks continued to languish with bhp down 6.4 cents, rio tinto falling 39.4 cents and wmc losing 14.1 cents.  the gold index was steady at 1,068.2 points with the price of bullion in sydney closing at 287.45 unitedstates dollars an ounce.

title: bahrain uneasy over internet smut
body: the bahraini government is increasingly concerned over the devastating impact on children of easy access to pornographic materials on the internet, the gulf news reported monday.  the issue has attracted much attention from the education ministry, the paper said.  nowadays children and adolescents get access to pornographic materials, which had remained out of their reach, until the internet came on the scene, a study on the issue said.  now children mature at a very early age and one of the most striking examples of this trend is a 13-year-old boy who said he preferred to stay at home and watch sex materials on the internet when asked why he didn't go out with his friends.  it is not easy to address the issue of pornography among students in a conservative, islamic and eastern society of bahrain, especially when sex-related materials on television programs such as items on aids and other sexually-transmitted diseases are taken into account, the study said.  one headmaster said that when teenagers watch pornographic films they find themselves face to face with a phenomenon which "they cannot turn into reality for themselves." so they become frustrated and isolate themselves from others.

title: ceos worldwide optimistic about economic future in asia
body: seventy percent of the 800 chief executive officers (ceos) questioned in a global survey published here friday said they are optimistic about the future in asia.  more than 80 percent of them are optimistic about the growth of their companies during the next three years, according to the second annual global ceo survey conducted by consultancy price waterhouse coopers.  the survey was commissioned by the world economic forum (wef) annual meeting at the swiss ski resort of davos.  at the same time, half of the respondents foresee threats to their business from non-traditional competitors entering their industries through electronic means, potentially "a 20-year-old in a garage." the survey found that ceos are making more use of the internet.  thirty percent of the respondents rate their internet skills as good or excellent.  two thirds of them sign on for purposes other than email at least one day a month, and a fourth more than 10 days per month, making use of the internet to visit competitors' sites as well.  now that everyone has an abundance of knowledge, the survey said, the major challenge is to convert it to intellectual capital.  "this is a tough area," said price waterhouse coopers' ceo james j. schiro. "successful managers need to find ways to create information filters." "various vision and strategy setting mechanisms help, but this is an individual challenge for every ceo," he added.

title: australian stocks close higher
body: the australian sharemarket returned from the australia day holiday on a high wednesday.  the all ordinaries index climbed 23.5 points to 2851.4.  early strength was fueled by another profit boost by national australia bank, which unveiled a 39 percent higher first quarter net profit of 456.55 million unitedstates dollars, prompting a rally in the stock which later abated.  the all industrials index was up 49.3 points to 5162.9, with global media group news corp mirroring its overnight unitedstates performance to push the market higher.  news corp ordinary shares rose 55 cents to 10.85 australian dollars and its preferred shares improved 59 cents to 10.25 australian dollars.  the rise came after the company announced it had entered a marketing agreement with internet media group yahoo inc and that it was preparing to buy the rights to telecast the series a and b italian soccer leagues.  national australia bank shares surged after the announcement of the swollen profit but moderated to finish just 11.6 cents higher at 26.11 australian dollars.  the other major banks finished higher, with commonwealth bank of australia performing best with a 38 cents gain to 23.04 australian dollars.  anz bank was up 2.8 cents to 10.308 australian dollars and westpac bank improved five cents to 10.75 australian dollars.  the all resources index edged half a point higher to 950.5, with rio tinto shares up after it announced in its annual production report increased production in key commodities rio closed 30.6 cents higher to 19.40 australian dollars.  diversified miner bhp was down 11 cents to 11.77 australian dollars.  the gold index dropped 13 points to 1067.3 as the bullion price closed in sydney at 286.05 unitedstates dollars.  turnover was 383.52 million shares traded at a value of 788.25 million unitedstates dollars, with 674 rises, 566 falls and 543 steady.

title: china's best lawyers offer help on line
body: china's acknowledged ten best lawyers and a number of national model lawyers' offices are now offering legal information on line and seeking clients via the internet. as a result, lawyers at home and abroad, as well as ordinary citizens, are able to look for legal help or get information about china's legal system on line. foreigners may find the answers to legal difficulties they may face in china such as international investment, international commodity trading, maritime affairs, finance, real estate, insurance, travel, rent, and intellectual property rights. the information is released in chinese, english, french, japanese and russian. the web site, www.counsel.com.cn, was opened with guidance from renowned chinese experts on laws, including wang liming, jiang ping, wu changzhen, xiao weiyun, zheng chengsi, and gao mingxuan. these experts will also make comments about major cases and interpret legal issues on line. people can find details on the web site about chinese laws and regulations, both national and local, promulgated since 1949 when new china was founded, and how they can be interpreted. the data resources are updated regularly. information about arbitration committees across the country is also available on the internet.

title: high price, low speed impede people's access to internet
body: many internet users in china are unhappy with the high charges, low speed and narrow information sources. a survey carried out by the china computer association found that nearly one third of people polled, or 31.5 percent, consider the high fees as a major impediment to their internet access.  almost a quarter, or 24.6 percent, expressed dissatisfaction with the low speed which some users said was as "slow as a snail". and over one fifth, or 21.6 percent, complained that there was few useful information about china on the net.  the reasons for the first two problems were attributed to the monopoly held by china' domestic telecommunications sector.  currently, china inputs only 0.01 percent and outputs 0.05 percent of all information offered on the internet as a whole.  and much of that information is of no benefit to net users.  computer experts point out that the development and use of information resources is very weak in china's information infrastructure.  thus, the enthusiasm of internet users is restrained and internet servers are experiencing serious management difficulties, and as a result information services on line are declining.

title: china not to open up internet phone, fax sectors
body: the ministry of information industry (mii) friday reiterated that china would not open up internet telephone and fax services for the time being, according to today's china daily.  a strict permit-issuing system will be introduced when conditions are ripe, the ministry told the english newspaper.  in what appears to be the government's first response to a fuzhou court ruling on wednesday that internet protocol (ip) phone services come under the category of computer information services, open to the public, an mii official told china daily that only the internet information services, excluding ip phone and fax, are currently open.  "we are stilling building and improving facilities for the new business, and studying how to run and manage it," xu mutu, director of the market administration of the telecom bureau under the mii, was quoted as saying.  xu's remarks came only two days after the fuzhou intermediate people's court in east china's fujian province decided in favor of chen yan and chen zhui, who were charged with "illegally setting up an international telephone service on the internet." the court verdict indicated that the ip phone service, which allows people to "call global and pay local", is just one of many computer information services, which, according to a state council circular issued in 1993, are not a monopoly business.  xu argued that the ip phone service in china should be administered by the unified state telecommunications department, and that no one would be allowed to run an ip phone business without prior examination of their qualifications and grant of a business permit from the authorities.  he said that some firms now use the country's internet infrastructure --in the construction and maintenance of which the state invests heavily --to run their ip phone business, only paying the fee for conventional telephones and an internet service provider. this is detrimental to the interests of the state.  however, zhang dongsheng, an official with the state development planning commission, told china daily that the country should encourage the growth of the ip phone service to improve the choice for international callers.

title: company provides free upgraded anti-virus software
body: chinese internet users will receive free upgraded versions of anti-virus software from an on-line service that started yesterday, according to today's china daily. computer associates (china) co ltd yesterday announced that it will email to its customers the latest breaking anti-virus solutions when a destructive computer virus occurs. "by registering at the www.kill.com.cn website, computer users who have already installed kill software will get free upgraded versions able to fight against the latest viruses," the paper quoted wang tiejian, deputy director of computer associates (china) co. kill software is capable of killing more than 20,000 viruses, and upgrades itself every day based on more than 170 virus sample collection centers operated by us-based computer associates international inc. in more than 40 countries, the paper said. the active and free service will provide an easy prescription for those plagued by an increasing number of viruses, noted wang. wang's service may help in the cyberspace, but it will be quite another thing if the virus is intentionally inserted into a computer program at the workplace. in what appears to be beijing's first crime involving computers, a computer technology company's former employee has planted "logical bomb" in more than 160,000 sets of computer educational software programs. the virus has been designed to erase data on computer hard disks if the software is operated on every 27th day after march 27 this year. the company said yesterday that it warranted the educational software distributed in its nationwide distribution networks after january 4 were free from any virus.

title: most urban youth have no internet access
body: as many as 70 percent of the young people in china's urban centers have no access to the internet, according to a survey conducted jointly by the china youth research center and the china youth development foundation.  the survey, which sought to learn about "the situation of modern chinese urban youth," involved nine cities and provinces including beijing, shanghai, chongqing and henan province, and more than 6,500 people aged 14 to 28.  when asked about their attitude toward the internet, 66.4 percent of the respondents including students, workers, teachers and civil servants said the internet is a brand-new method of communication, a miracle of the modern world.  but the survey also revealed that 69.1 percent said they have no way to get on-line, while only 1.9 percent said they are internet fans, and 3.4 percent said they use the internet quite often.  there are still 6.6 percent of the youth who say they have no desire to use the internet, and six percent said they have never even heard of it.  experts believe this demonstrated a great potential for the development of modern communications in china, and also indicated there is still a long way to go before the internet becomes truly popular among chinese youth.

title: canadian cable firms sign up more internet customers
body: canada's cable companies are gaining ground against the telephone firms in the internet service market and signing up more customers, a report said tuesday.  cogeco cable inc. of montreal said that for the three months e nding november 30, it added almost 75,000 customers to its internet service.  shaw communications inc. of calgary announced a gain of 20,000 new internet customers during the same quarter. the firm now boasts more than 81,000 internet customers.  industrial experts estimate that as many as 300,000 households in canada have access to the internet through a cable company, according to the national post newspaper.  canadian customers usually pay about 40 dollars (26 unitedstates dollars) for an unlimited internet service in addition to their monthly cable tv bills.  with cable services, customers can surf on the internet at peak speeds of about 1.5 million bits per second, while those who go on-line through phone lines surf at speeds ranging from 9,600 to 50,000 bits per second.  internet dealers say that the market for high-speed cable services is just at the beginning of a boom. more and more canadians are opting for high-speed internet service and free up their home phone line for voice calls.  however, cable customers still account for a small proportion of the total 3.6 million internet-connected households in the country.

title: chinese government puts politics on net
body: the ministry of information industry of china has recently announced that this year governments at all levels will move toward an increased presence on the internet.  only five days after the state development planning commission launched its website on december 1, 1998, a total of 1,400 visitors had posted their opinions on the site on topics such as environmental pollution, anti-corruption and the establishment of a medical insurance system.  the beijing municipal government made a recent debut on the net with a website called window of the capital, which includes information raging from beijing's economic situation to job seeking and air-quality reports.  most significantly, an email box has been open to beijingers where they can post letters to the mayor on various issues.  the newest statistics show that so far a total of 25,000 citizens have visited this website.  the guangdong provincial government will be connected with the hongkong sar on may 1, 1999, with its 18 departments already establishing their sites. meanwhile the guangzhou and shenzhen city governments have also launched their trial websites.  statistics show that chinese government departments have more than 3,000 databases, making up 80 percent of all social information resources.  "we had taken it for granted that the state development strategy is a policy-makers' affair, but now we can voice our suggestions on the net freely, with a sense of involvement in state affairs," said one recent visitor to the state development planning commission's website.

title: lebanon bans overseas phone calls via internet
body: the ministry of post and telecommunications of lebanon has banned internet service providers from offering voice communications service, the daily star reported monday.  the service, known as the voice over the internet, provides internet subscribers with a cheap means of calling overseas.  internet service providers will be prosecuted if they fail to comply with the terms and regulations of their licenses, warned abdel monem youssef, general director of the ministry's operations and maintainance section. the licenses, which were granted by the ministry, require internet companies to refrain from offering voice services. and video conferencing is also banned.  only the ministry has the exclusive right to provide international and local phone lines, he stressed.  and internet companies which don't abide by the terms of their licenses are undermining the ministry's revenues and depleting public funds, youssef said.  following the ministry's decision saturday, intracom, one of the several companies that offer what is called the "e-phone service", announced to suspend its phone-via-internet service.  the company had launched a nation-wide advertising campaign a week ago to promote the new product.  of lebanon's 10 internet service providers in operation, only four have access lines spread throughout the country.  the service providers are generating approximately 1 million unitedstates dollars a month in revenues, thanks to growing numbers of subscribers.  statistics from the ministry show that lebanon has less than half of the arab world's 85,000 internet subscribers.

title: uae to hold internet exhibition
body: an internet exhibition conference is to be held here next month, said ahmed alhosani, an official from the emirates telecommunications corporation, on monday.  the internet world middle east '99 (iwme), to be held from february 22 to 24, will feature "live" demonstrations of how businesses can use the internet to reduce operating costs and boost bottom lines.  the demonstrations will cover ways of increasing business visibility, enhancing productivity gains, providing service and support to consumers, and selling products and services creatively via the internet, said the official.  "internet usage throughout the middle east has doubled in the past year," said john hassett, general manager of the trade fairs and conferences ltd., which is one of the sponsors of the event.  also the exhibition will be highlighted by an awards ceremony for the best usage of e-commerce, the most creative website, best information website and best arabic website, said a press release issued by the organizers.  high profile industry experts from six nations, including egypt, jordan, saudi arabia, the united arab emirates, britain and the unitedstates will address the conference.  iwme is one of the world's first and leading series of global exhibitions for the internet industry, organized by unitedstates mecklermedia inc in over 23 countries.

title: china needs to improve internet facilities beijing, january
body: china now has more than 1.5 million internet users but information about china and its culture, economy and laws is less than one percent of the database, according to a report in china business daily.  "it's like a tv station opening several channels with no programs or with programs in a foreign language unknown to the vast majority," a software producer said.  now a research project to develop and input information about china on the web has begun which will highlight government policies, in particular the preferential tax system for foreign companies, which will be very useful for those surfing the internet worldwide.  the research panel will also consider establishing brand name enterprises which will provide informa tion services.  china's level of information databases compares to that of developed countries in the 1960s and 1970s but there were plans to invest some 1000 billion yuan (120 billion us dollars) to improve this situation. however, so far only 1.5 billion has been committed to develop software and information resources.  to make things worse, the country's telecommunications monopoly has made the cost of surfing the net quite unreasonable, which has held back an expansion of the network.  in the unitedstates, for example, the cost of surfing the internet accounts for only one percent of monthly income while in china it is about 10 percent. the management expenses for unitedstates internet service providers (isp) is about 5.6 percent of its total administration cost but runs to about 80 percent in china.  experts say that a stable and continuous input is essential and the investment should account for some 30 percent of the total information infrastructure expenditure.

title: chinese crosstalk goes online
body: jiang kun, a famous chinese crosstalk performer, today initiated a new crosstalk website on the internet. china crosstalk net will allow people to listen to, watch, learn, discuss and write about crosstalk on line, said jiang, who has been performing this specialty for more than 20 years. since the late qing dynasty (1644-1911), performers of crosstalk, a chinese version of two-man stand-up comedy, have brought laughter to the chinese people. its humor always comes from discussions of everyday-life topics like love and romance, cultures and customs, and all sorts of trivia. the website includes the history and development of crosstalk, as well as current news about the genre. jiang and his colleagues plan to provide 100 crosstalk routines along with dozens of comments on this unique art form. "the internet has brought a fresh opportunity to inject a new life into crosstalk, and allows chinese all around the world to join in and let the whole world laugh together," jiang said. listening to crosstalk is also an important part of chinese new year celebrations. web surfers can access the site at: http://www.kunpeng.cn.net.

title: australian stocks close down off its lows
body: the australian sharemarket closed down thursday but off its lows after unemployment fell to an eight-year low as the long bond prices weakened, indicating the economy was in "reasonably good shape," analysts said.  stocks opened sharply lower after foreign equities markets plunged overnight on news of the devaluation of the brazilian currency, the real, and the resignation of the country's central bank chief gustavo franco.  "the market started off weak because of the overseas weakness," funds manager ausbil partners equities director paul xiradis said.  "it improved during the day because of some positive australian statistics and improvement in the long bond rate over the last couple of days, and that confirms that the australian economy is in a reasonably good state." the australian bureau of statistics reported thursday that employment in december rose 53,600, seasonally adjusted, with an eight-year low in the unemployment rate of 7.5 percent.  the all ordinaries index closed 17.2 points, or 0.61 percent, lower at 2804.8, off a low of 2793.7.  national turnover was 371.76 million shares valued at 1.074 billion australian dollars (676.6 million unitedstates dollars), with 665 falls easily outnumbering 453 rises and 419 steady stocks.  news corp, national australia bank and lend lease corp limited the industrial sector losses, with the all industrials index losing 12.6 points to 5031.3, off a low of 4999.3.  bhp, which plunged 56.8 or 4.44 percent, and weaker commodity prices led the resources sector down, with all resources index shedding 25.7 points to 986.1.  news corp gained 25.2 cents, national australia bank gained 15.9 and lend lease corp gained 38.7.  commonwealth bank of australia fell 21.6 cents, anz banking group lost 21 cents and westpac banking corp dropped 15 cents.  in the resources sector, wmc dropped 22 cents, or 4.10 percent, rio tinto fell 20 cents and woodside petroleum dipped two.  australian national industries gained five cents, or 4.07 percent, after the smorgon steel group took management control of the heavy engineering group and announced interim changes to the company's board.  a 2.30 unitedstates dollars fall in gold bullion's price in new york led the gold index 16.2 points, or 1.43 percent, lower to 1130.3.  in sydney, gold closed at 286.65 unitedstates dollars an ounce, from 288.05 an ounce wednesday.

title: bangladesh to introduce internet service
body: the bangladesh telegraph and telephone board (bttb) will introduce internet service soon, according to post and telecommunications minister mohammad nasim.  after the introduction of the internet service, a competitive atmosphere would be created in the field of internet services between public and private sectors and greater facilities would be ensured for the subscribers in the country, the independent daily newspaper quoted nasim quoted as saying here wednesday.  at present, a total of 18 private organizations are providing internet connections, linking bangladesh with the world of modern information technology, and all of them are doing so through "v-sat." but now, the canada-based tele-globe organization will provide services to the subscribers with its link to the world internet connection through direct satellite circuit, according to bttb sources.  as a result, bttb will be able to ensure a stronger system than the "v-sat" as rendered by the private organizations, they added.  the satellite circuit of the bttb internet service will be a able to include 32 telephone lines at a time in its server to get internet connection.  the bttb has fixed 2,000 taka (about 41.24 unitedstates dollars) for each internet connection and the internet user is to pay only one taka (about 0.02 dollars) per minute between 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. the bttb will start providing internet service through advertising within a few days.

title: interactive mba program launched in hk hong kong, january
body: hongkong telecom, hongkong's major full-service communications provider, and city university of hongkong thursday jointly announced the launch of an interactive master of business administration (imba) at postgraduate level.  scheduled to start enrollment in april 1999, the imba is the first full-degree program in hongkong to offer a truly interactive and schedule-free learning experience via an innovative combination of the latest interactive tv (itv) technology, broadband internet access and integrated on-campus activities.  enrolled imba students will be able to enhance their managerial and professional competence through high-quality videos of course lectures that can be viewed on-demand via hongkong telecom's itv service, as well as through web-based, interactive on-line discussion on course topics with instructors and tutors.  studies will also be facilitated by hyper-linked multimedia course materials available on the web, on-campus professional forums and residential trips to major overseas corporations where students will be able to apply knowledge learned from the program.  the imba program comprises various modules of studies --core, advanced and integrated. completion of all modules will lead to an mba degree award.  the modular structure of the program also allows participants, who have no immediate intention of obtaining an mba degree, to study on a course-by-course basis that matches their personal needs and interests.  credits earned in this way can be accumulated and counted towards an mba award, upon fulfilling the admission requirements and satisfactory completion of all courses. course lectures are also available for other viewers on a pay-per-day basis on itv lecture videos of the imba program can be viewed on-demand under itv's education service category, which also offers a comprehensive range of academic programs supporting the local primary, secondary and tertiary curricula, as well as general interest and family education program to widen viewers' scope of knowledge. linus cheung, chief executive of hongkong telecom, said that the interactive education can not only train people in a very efficient way, but also can enhance the overall competitive position of hongkong.  professor h. k. chang, president of the city university of hongkong, said that today's it age has opened up a new world of learning where educational activities have extended from the physical classroom to the cyber space.

title: on-line rail ticketing system hits the buffers
body: people who use the internet to book rail tickets on-line merely to test the system and never pick them up have been criticized for their behavior in a signed article in beijing daily, which says they are causing problems for railway staff.  since the beijing railway bureau started its on-line ticketing service on new year's day, approximately 350 tickets were booked up to january 5 but only 70 tickets were collected and used, bureau officials were quoted as saying.  a bureau official said that two staff have been deployed to handle the administration work but because many people didn't follow the system through, they are experiencing problems in keeping it efficient and the records accurate.  it is believed that there are two main reasons for this behavior: curious internet browsers who simply want to try out the system and potential passengers who are keen to check out if it really works but have no intention of traveling.  the railway bureau admitted that it knew the id card numbers of the offenders and maybe even their email addresses but didn't want to take official action at this stage in the hope that this warning will persuade them to stop abusing the service and behave responsibly.

title: three seconds, everything done
body: when olympic silver medallist xu nannan led changchun to win the women's freestyle skiing, the first gold medal in china's ninth winter games, her name appeared on the official web site just three seconds after the results were confirmed by chief referees. the official national winter games' site --http://sport.jl.cninfo.net, receives about 1,600-1,700 hits daily since it opened on the new year day. though it was not the first time for engineer han jian, director of the hub, to install a network for sports tournament, it's the only one he can boast of. "we grant instantness for every one who'd like to know the national winter games on web," said han, also chief of the computer technology electronic information center of the state sports commission. "quickness was always in my mind when i built the network. however, i didn't realize it in the eighth national games in shanghai in 1997." the atlanta olympic games in 1996 was the first sports games to be exploited by the internet, but it was until the nagano winter olympics last february that people started to enjoy watching the games on website worldwide. "competition results can be transferred to the host computer in the center instantly after the games, and to the web simultaneously. it takes just three seconds in the process," han said. "a data-transferring cable connects the results screen in the stadium and the mainframe in the center, and everything is done by the computer during a span of a blink. "in the shanghai national games, a group of 20 typists were hired to put the results into the internet, which wasted half an hour before it got hits." a team of 20 computer experts worked for four months to install the information network for the winter games, which cost just one million rmb (120,000 unitedstates dollars), comparing to 82.8 million rmb (10 million unitedstates dollars) expense and a team of 200 spanish experts at the bangkok asian games last december.

title: more than six million americans use internet for travel plan
body: a total of 6.7 million american adults have used the internet for an online service to make travel reservations in the past year, according to a new report released on saturday.  in other words, said the travel industry association of america in its national travel survey, nine percent of current internet users in the country have done that. travel reservations include the actual booking and paying for an airline ticket, hotel room, rental car or package tour.  the report, based on a telephone survey of 1,200 unitedstates adults, also said that use of the internet has grown dramatically in the past two years. the number of travelers who used the internet for travel-related and other purposes jumped from 29 million in 1996 to 70 million in 1998.  in addition, one-half of all online travelers consulted the internet to get information on destinations or to check prices and schedules.  "americans who enjoy travel seem to love the flexibility and convenience of the internet," the association said. "the internet is open 24 hours a day and it is right in our homes. it is fast, interactive and global." if the recent increase in traveler usage is any indication, the association added, the internet and online services are "the travel planning medium of the future." among the new travel technologies listed in the survey, travelers mentioned their awareness of satellite navigation systems in cars used to give directions and maps, electronic airline tickets, and computer kiosks at airports or hotels.  electronic passports ranked the lowest in awareness and use, according to the association.

title: largest u.s. bank offers fingerprint access to online banking service
body: bank of america, the largest bank in the unitedstates, has initiated a fingerprint-based smart card biometric program to give individuals access to their online banking services.  "biometric technology is becoming increasingly accessible, and we believe it will play a growing role in security and authentication for financial products, services and transactions in the new millenium," the bank said in a statement wednesday.  before using the system, the bank stores a customer's online banking login, passcode and fingerprint on the chip attached to a multi-application smart card. the customer then follows a customary login process to access banking information over the internet.  the biometric security authentication is completed when the customer places a finger on a small scanning device attached to a personal computer. the software matches it against the image already stored on the smart card's chip. finally the customer gets onto the the web page for the bank's pc load smart card program, from where he can transfer value from his checking account onto the visa cash stored value application on his smart card.  the bank first started testing smart cards more than four years ago and has a special group that explores new ways to utilize the technology. out of that group has come the first multi-application smart card program utilizing visa cash and non-finance features and the first pc program for visa cash stored-value chip cards.  the group has also deployed a variety of smart-card programs for companies and public facilities across the country.  "biometric technology --coupled with smart cards --has the potential to take security, convenience and versatility to another level for our customers," the bank said.  bank of america now provides financial products and services to 30 million households and two million businesses in the unitedstates. more than one million of the bank's customers bank online via the internet, america online or personal financial management software.

title: computer-related crimes surging in china
body: china's public security departments uncovered nearly one hundred hacker cases last year, a figure arousing public awareness of computer and network security.  according to sources, illegal activities involving computers an d the internet have soared by an astounding 30 percent annually in recent years. the hackers have hundreds of tricks," outnumbering the varieties of computer viruses in china," said one anti-hacker expert.  an official with the public security ministry said that the detected hacker cases account for only an estimated 15 percent of all such occurrences, and the majority of hacker cases go undetected, either because the hackers had done little harm or the victims cover them up for fear of damaging their own images.  the chinese media, in this case, do not follow the silent majority. they kept track of the latest hacker activities, and have called for measures to combat them.  a local computer journal reported that 95 percent of china's network management centers with internet access have been attacked by hackers from both home or abroad. as in other places, banking, financial and securities institutions are the main targets of those greedy intruders, the journal said.  zhao zhansheng, a computer security specialist with the chinese academy of social sciences (cass), said that china's information network is still at "a nascent stage," and the fragile "firewall" of information systems leaves loopholes through which hackers can enter. "it is most serious that a large portion of computer crimes are committed by insiders, because most companies lack a multi-level computer security system," he added.  jinhua'an information technology co. recently conducted tests of dozens of security agencies in shanghai and shenzhen, and found almost all of their network security systems were undefended. with a lap top computer hooked up to a telephone line, testers easily logged in their networks and reached restricted information in a minute.  "real hackers can now freely rewrite all vital data in the database," one tester said.  expert said that most hackers are youngsters with a good programming expertise. they decode a computer system only to show off their "special talent". but up to now, china has no laws or regulations to warn or punish these "fun-seekers".

title: microsoft creates web-commerce package
body: hoping to cash in on the emerging market for net retailing, microsoft has created complete commerce, a package of web hosting, development and technical support for electronic commerce sites.  the software giant said monday that the "all-in-one" package has been designed to meet huge demand from mid-sized to large businesses looking for help in hosting e-commerce sites. its partners include chipmaker intel, computer maker compaq and 10 commercial hosting services. the program is aimed at fortune 2000 companies.  while pricing will vary depending on the size of the sites to be hosted, a typical configuration offering business to consumers would cost roughly 50,000 unitedstates dollars to build and host for three months. contracts also include a maintenance fee.  there have been various estimations of the worldwide e-commerce potential. a moderate prediction made by the unitedstates research firm international data corporation (idc) last year put e-commerce revenue to 400 billion unitedstates dollars by 2002. idc also predicted that the global net audience will jump from 100 million by the end of 1998 to 320 million by 2002.  another unitedstates research firm, forrester research, estimated last november that worldwide "internet commerce" sales will be between 1.4 trillion and 3.2 trillion unitedstates dollars in 2003. the high potential estimate would represent nearly five percent of all global sales. forrester defines "internet commerce" as the trade of goods and services in which the final order is placed over the internet. it includes business-to-business and business-to-consumer sales and electronic data interchange (edi) orders placed on the internet, but exclude the value of financial transactions.  microsoft has been increasingly active on the e-commerce hosting and site-design front. last august the company, along with hewlett-packard and a troop of smaller vendors and consultancies introduced e-commerce quick-start, a bundle of hardware, software and services to get companies up and running on an electronic commerce system.

title: shoppers spend 1.2 billion on aol system during holidays.
body: about 1.25 million of 15 million subscribers shopped through american online (aol) during last year's holiday shopping season that ran from the day after thanksgiving to december 27, reports said monday.  subscribers spent about 1.2 billion unitedstates dollars shopping on line during the holidays as consumers increasingly shifted from mall shopping to internet surfing to find perfect gifts, said wendy goldberg, spokeswoman of aol, the world's largest internet service provider.  based on the number of hits on its shopping web pages, the aol spokeswoman said its "toys, kids and babies" category was the most popular, followed closely by apparel, the most popular online shopping destination last year.  "online shopping is really becoming a key part of the way people shop," goldberg said, "it's a new way for people to shop, and it's really only beginning." internet research group estimated that the average aol shopper bought two items a week online during the holiday season while online sales for clothing more than tripled.  with the holidays over, aol hopes its subscribers can still surf the mega-clearance sale. the company expects the strong holiday sales to translate into steady business for its retail partners through the coming year.

title: expert calls for promotion of arabic on internet
body: the use of arabic on the internet must be promoted to change the situation that other languages and cultures dominate international communications, according to a leading arabic software provider.  if effective solutions are not found to promote the use of arabic on the internet, the language will lose its international significance, hazem abdelazim, executive director of egypt's sakhr software, warned in emirates news on wednesday.  the number of arabic pages on the internet is 322,898 out of a total of 20 million web pages, said abdelazim.  "failing to create effective international quality solutions for any language would mean that this language will become less and less significant as information systems using other languages take center stage in everyday life," he said.  "the challenge of the internet reaches new heights with languages like arabic, due to its rich and high inflexional nature, that requires special technologies not provided by latin software," he said.  "the cultural, socio-economic and political implications of the internet is now motivating big companies, institutes and governments to respond with a competitive arabic solution," he added.  abdelazim will highlight solutions for arabic on the internet when he delivers the key-note address at the internet world middle east '99 (iwme '99) conference and exhibition scheduled here on february 22-24, 1999.  industry experts from six nations, namely, egypt, jordan, saudi arabia, the united arab emirates, britain and the unitedstates, will address the conference.

title: information superhighway in eastern china
body: using today's multimedia networks, china's shandong province has established an information expressway.  a wide-band multimedia network based on asynchronous transfer mode (atm) technology is the most advanced communications network, transmitting sound, pictures and data in digital form.  shandong's deputy governor han yuqun says that the agriculture and industrial sectors are still the basis of local economic development, but the information industry will play a key role in the next century.  local autorities in this economically developed coastal province began to develop the information industry last year, and the new communications network provides customers with various services like long-distance medical help, long-distance education, and long-distance conferences.  the speed of the internet will increase 200 times and internet users will be able to use the net while making phone calls on the same telephone line without interference.  zuo xunsheng, director of the provincial postal service bureau, says that key computer ports have opened in jinan, the provincial capital, and in qingdao, a port city and cities are now connected to the country's main atm network.

title: cybercop suggested to counter rumor-mongering on internet
body: an information technology (it) consultant has suggested that malaysia form a vigilant group known as "cybercop" as an alternative method to counter negative elements including rumor-mongering through the internet.  making the suggestion thursday, the association of computer industry malaysia chairman shaifubahrim saleh said cybercops should consist of people who are computer wizards who know how to patrol into the internet.  cybercops who could come directly under the home ministry or the police, would be technically-sound to detect any illegal usage of the internet, shaifubahrim said, adding "if people know that there are these intelligent undercover cybercops, they would be more cautious in what they do." "forming cybercops would be more effective than registering customers who wanted to use the internet in cybercafes," he told the malaysian national news agency bernama in an interview.  the suggestion came after an official announcement early this month compelling cybercafes to register their customers in order to keep tabs on cyber rumor-mongering, a move which was considered to be counter-productive to the government's own effort to develop an it-literate society.  shaifubahrim was of the view that registering customers would discourage honest users from using the internet as people from all age-group used the facility regularly at cybercafes.  he said rumors could still be spread by other ways such as writing a poison-pen letter as there are computer whiz kids who know how to use other people's computer id and hide their own identity.

title: strikes against iraq prompt surge of internet traffic
body: traffic on the internet has jumped as users worldwide turn to their computers for the latest news update covering the strikes against iraq.  many of the news sites in america and in the uk were able to beat national newspapers and television stations in getting information about the air strikes to the public first.  while millions of people were able to tune in to television for the coverage of the air strikes in iraq, millions more were at work with no tvs in sight.  for these people, the web, unhindered by many of the territorial boundaries inherent in traditional media, offered a way to get what otherwise would have been inaccessible news.  as many as 500 people streamed into the chat rooms of the web site of cnn, american's cable news network, just after the first strike was announced 22.00 gmt time wednesday. the traffic of cnn's website peaked at 475,000 hits per minute at one point.  apart from providing a vital link to breaking events, the internet has also been used as a vehicle for public opinion, with users registering their feelings live online as each new development occurs.  cnn's site, for example, features a message board where internet users from around the world have given a mixed response to the military action.  most sites were also giving users the chance to vote on whether air strikes should have been made on iraq. britian's sky news web site reflected much of the public opinion, with the voting split 60-40 in favour of the action.  the unitedstates online service aol conducted an online chat session between users and a journalist in baghdad, and said up to 12,000 people took part.

title: nz child-porn probe leads to 43 overseas arrests
body: an internet child-pornography investigation by new zealand authorities has led to the arrest of 43 people overseas involved in a huge network of internet child pornography, according to a local newspaper.  the dominion reported monday that a joint investigation involving new zealand ministry of internal affairs and police recently raided the home of an auckland man and found an extensive collection of child porn. an email address was traced back to britain and information forwarded to greater manchester police, who began operation venture.  since then 58 people from britain, northern ireland, the netherlands, france, germany, canada and the middle east have been identified as being involved, with 43 arrests so far. more arrests are likely.  the case against the auckland man has been completed and forwarded to the new zealand attorney-general for approval to prosecute for the possession and distribution of objectionable material.  according to the wellington-based newspaper, 45,000 child safety pamphlets are being printed in new zealand for the christmas season when children are more likely to be using the internet unsupervised.

title: liaoning library goes on line
body: china now has a booming internet industry and it is expected that by the end of this year some two million people will be on line, more than twice that of last year.  many find that they can use it for research and study without leaving their homes, like 23-year-old he li from liaoning, who is delighted that she can call up books from the provincial library on its own web site.  "it's much easier than physically visiting the library and it changes the whole concept of using the facilities," she said.  one of the main advantages for browsers and readers is that the library's web site has a comprehensive index which points to actual books.  the vice director of the library's technology department, li donglai, believes that this is one of the significant benefits of being on-line.  and the service also allows browsers and readers to access the library's valuable collection of 120,000 rare books, some dating back 200 years, which, because of their age and fragile condition, were previously only available on a restricted basis.  li and his colleagues began inputting the ibm technology for digitalizing their library earlier this year.  liaoning library, the largest in northeast china, boasts a collection of three million volumes including 560,000 volumes of rare and ancient books.  "this on-line service detailing most of our catalogue of books is just the beginning," said li. "our next job is to develop a wide ranging information resource." however, a shortage of funds has restrained li from digitalizing every book in the library. "we don't have the capacity or resources to digitalize one million books every year like the american library of congress," li added. "but we are speeding up and in less than a month we managed to input 5,000 volumes." meanwhile, a project to establish china's first nationwide on-line digital library was agreed two years ago by the giant ibm computer corporation and the national library of china in beijing, which is the fifth largest in the world.  the plan is to input all of the national library's collection of close to 20 million books and make them available via the internet with a super-charged web site.

title: chinese president meets with world media mogul rupert murdoch
body: chinese president jiang zemin today expressed appreciation for the efforts made by world media mogul rupert murdoch in presenting china objectively and cooperating with the chinese press over the past two years.  during a meeting here today with murdoch, chairman of the news corporation, and his party president jiang said that china has made remarkable achievements not only in economic construction, but in the media and culture as well.  exchanges between china and the rest of the international community has been constantly increasing, and china needs to reinforce its links with other countries to promote mutual understanding and cooperation, jiang said.  the news media play a very important role in boosting mutual understanding between china and the rest of the world, jiang noted.  murdoch expressed his admiration for china's tremendous achievements in every respect over the past two decades, and told jiang that he is willing to further enhance friendly cooperation to present the world with a better understanding of china.  ding guangen, member of the political bureau of the communist party of china (cpc) central committee, member of the secretariat of the cpc central committee and head of the publicity department of cpc central committee, was among those present at the meeting.  murdoch and his party are visiting china as guests of the information office of the state council.  the news corporation is a multinational media giant with holdings in entertainment studios, television, newspapers and publishing businesses.

title: u.s. computer, telephone firms propose fast internet service
body: major unitedstates computer and telephone companies on monday announced a proposal to speed availability of high-speed internet access services.  according to intel, one of the companies that launched the initiative, the proposal was presented to the federal communications commission (fcc) as a mean to encourage telephone companies to invest in high-speed services for consumers.  other companies involved include bell atlantic, compaq, gateway, gte and microsoft.  intel said that the proposal, once adopted by the fcc, would establish a set of ground rules that support rapid investment in high-speed infrastructure by the telephone companies while ensuring a competitive playing field.  the initiative came one week after the white house announced an effort with the fcc, the commerce department and unitedstates trade representative to push for increased private investment in high-speed networks so that consumers and businesses can be free from slow internet service.  according to the proposal, which calls for the promotion of competition in the local exchange data communications market, incumbent telephone companies will give competitors greater access to their central offices and all internet service providers will continue to have access to the broadband networks of the telephone companies.  meanwhile, unnecessary restrictive regulations will be lessened on the incumbent telephone companies. for instance, the regional bell companies, which now are allowed only to offer local services, will be able to provide long-distance data communications if such freedom would substantially reduce the cost of delivering high-speed internet connections to consumers.  the widely-touted asymmetrical digital subscriber line (adsl) is among the high-speed internet access services --the goal of the proposal.  this is a technology that uses existing phone lines for high-speed internet access up to 30 times faster than today's modems. a new modem would be required and telephone companies would need to install new equipment. once the service is installed, consumers would never need to dial their internet service provider again because adsl is always on.  also, people can talk on the phone and surf the web at the same time on the same line.

title: new tide of web advertising surging in china
body: qiu ke, 24, who has a degree in advertising, resigned from a well-known joint venture in beijing one year ago and joined the other pioneers who are exploring china's internet advertising market, still a novelty in the country.  to date, qiu's blue process company has 12 domestic clients for whom it has created internet ads. these clients include magazines and securities companies. "small as it's now, i'm bullish about this market," he said.  according to preliminary statistics, there are now more than 30 companies such as blue process in beijing.  the beijing-based stone rich sight company (srs), which has the most popular chinese website in china, has set out to establish the world's largest chinese website --sina.  deng hailin, marketing manager of srs, said that interactivity is one of the characteristics of the internet, facilitating convenient communication between advertisers and consumers. advertisers can also accurately calculate the number of people exposed to their online advertisements.  the number of internet users has rapidly increased over the past five years. statistics show that about 80 million computers were connected with the internet worldwide by last year, and this figure is expected to reach 200 million.  advertising on the internet has also become a booming commercial activity in western countries. experts predict that the world gross ad investment will reach five billion unitedstates dollars in 2000.  china's internet market is closely following the world pace. the country currently has 1.17 million users, and the figure will reach two million by the year 2000.  these people are mainly in their twenties and thirties, and are well-educated and well-paid, said deng.  most insiders and officials agree that china's internet ad market will make rapid progress in the next five years, though it is not mature now.  deng said that current internet ad income, which mainly comes from the information industry, is only less than one percent that of traditional mass media.

title: china accelerates opening of internet service sector
body: china's largest internet-based news service signed an agreement today with a major telecommunications company for long-term cooperation in internet-related services.  the pact between china internet information center (ciic), under the state council information office, and gte corp. of the unitedstates is the first china has entered into for internet development services.  "the agreement will allow ciic to more easily provide information about china to web users in north america and europe using gte's network," said bruce linton, vice-president of sales and marketing for gte internetworking services.  of the 2 million visitors to the ciic website, which started operation on jan. 1, 1997, one-quarter are internet users in the unitedstates.  experts say this is an important step toward the opening of china's web content service.  but this agreement is not such big news in the country's internet service sector, as a number of agreements and contracts between china's internet service providers and foreign firms have already attracted the spotlight in the internet community.  yahoo recently concluded its agreement with infoshare technology co., ltd. affiliated with china's ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation.  under the agreement, infoshare will help market yahoo's services in china, and the latter will promote chinese businesses and help them with online advertising.  yahoo expects to open its beijing office next year.  there is ample reason for the world's major networking and internet service companies to be optimistic about the china market.  the latest information shows that internet users nationwide has now reached 1.2 million, and is doubling every year.

title: china accelerates opening of internet service sector
body: Early this year, a delegation of top executives from major unitedstates internet service providers visited china; and unitedstates president bill clinton made a trip to the internet cafe in shanghai during his state visit to china this past summer.  now, hundreds of china's internet service firms are seeking cooperation from foreign counterparts for an injection of technologies and a wider variety of information.  the country's most profitable web content provider, china.com corp., has become the exclusive agent for america online, and has a firm cooperative relationship with 24/7 media of the unitedstates the chinese corporation is working with netscape right now to produce a chinese website.  the impact of all this transmission of internet information is obviously felt by chinese. currently, there are hundreds of thousands of yahoo users in china, and more and more chinese business people are approaching yahoo to discuss the possibility of online advertising.  the chinese government limits the involvement of overseas investment in electronic publications, and stipulates by regulation that the chinese side in a joint venture must be the majority shareholder. and overseas investment is not allowed to enter the mass media.  like everywhere else in the world, industry analysts say, government policies and regulations cannot keep up with china's internet market expansion, despite a few regulations related to internet operations and security which have come into effect.

title: australian tourism industry urged to go on-line
body: australia's tourism industry should embrace the marketing tool of the future and go on-line, federal tourism minister jackie kelly said friday.  while addressing an industry forum in sydney, kelly said the internet could provide huge opportunities for the sector, australian associated press reported.  nearly 14 million americans were already using it to plan their trips, she said.  "while i appreciate that tourism is an industry dominated by small business and the challenge of new technology is difficult for some, it is getting simpler and cheaper all the time and will soon be no different than subscribing to the yellow pages," kelly said.  "i intend to work closely with the industry to develop an integrated on-line tourism strategy --it is time to stop underestimating the potential of new ideas." she also reiterated the potential opportunities to create lasting wealth and employment from the sydney 2000 olympic games.  kelly highlighted the importance of going on-line, as this friday (november 27) is being marked nationally as "online australia day," a special day of events organized by the federal government's national office of the information economy, designed to showcase the benefits of the on-line economy in the general community and the business sector.

title: 1.2 million australian homes linked to internet
body: a total of 1.245 million of australian households were linked to the internet in august 1998, soaring above 1 million for the first time in the nation's history, the australian bureau of statistics (abs) said wednesday.  the number of households hooked up to the internet in august represents an increase of 18 percent from may 1998 and 46 percent higher than in february 1998.  more than half of these homes were using the internet to access or send email rather than to surf the worldwide web and hardly any was using it for home banking, a recent abs survey found.  but additional abs statistics found that 51 percent of those households, or 633,863, only used the email service on the internet.  nearly half of households on the internet consisted of a married couple with children while about a quarter were married with no children.  the abs said nearly 4.2 million adults, or one in three, had accessed the internet in the 12 months to august, up from 3.6 million in may.  of those adults, 1.9 million accessed the internet at home and 1.9 million at work.  others used the internet at other places, such as a friend's house or a library. most adults used the internet two to six times a week.  three-quarters of adults using the internet in the past year lived in capital cities and users were more likely to be male than female.  people aged over 55 were less likely to access the internet, with younger people the most frequent users.  the survey also measured the extent to which adults used the internet to buy or order goods and services for private use.  it found 13 percent of adults bought something over the internet in the past year, mainly an overseas item, from a home computer.

title: bt takes 50 percent share in excite uk
body: british telecom (bt) has dramatically entered the internet content market with a 50 percent investment in the uk subsidiary of american portal company excite.  the 6-million-pound (10-million-unitedstates dollar) deal, announced wednesday, brings bt into the realm of internet content, competing directly with the big names like yahoo, netscape, msn and aol.  this is the first time a major uk company has forged such a close relationship with a unitedstates-based internet portal. according to new figures from independent watchdog media matrix, excite.com web portal is the sixth most popular web site.  portals provide services ranging from free email to news, online shopping and search engines, which are aimed at retaining visitors to their web sites and attracting advertising by acting as one-stop shops.  bt sees the deal as developing its presence in internet advertising and as a major vehicle for pushing electronic commerce and its involvement in transactions.  excite will be able to take advantage of the better-known bt brand in the uk, the influx of cash and the new customers bt will drive to it as an internet service provider (isp).  coming after tuesday's news that american software and portal company netscape is to be bought by aol, it is further evidence of continuing convergence of services and utilities in the internet industry, analysts said.

title: news corp launches new broadcasting company for australia
body: the billionaire media baron rupert murdoch is launching a new company, news broadcasting australia pty ltd, by using new wave of broadcasting technology to expand its manor in australia.  the move is designed to position news corp in a nascent market delivering broadcast content over platforms such as the internet.  "it's a very wide brief. it covers all areas of broadcasting," jim blomfield, formerly head of news corp's digital satellite operation in tokyo and chief executive of the new company, was quoted by the australian associated press as saying thursday.  cross media ownership laws in australia prevent murdoch controlling a television station and newspaper in the same city.  as a result news corp cannot hold a broadcasting licence in australia because of its wide newspaper interests.  but new technology is moving in the company's favor to allow it to start transmitting through means other than radio waves.  murdoch has said recently that new technology would sweep away all efforts by the governments to control media ownership.  in launching the new company, lachlan murdoch, chief executive of news corp's australian arm, news ltd, said the new company aimed to "provide the australian public with greater freedom of choice in entertainment and information services".  "news' experience at the forefront of digital broadcasting and content development around the world puts it in a unique position to be a driving force in giving the public the competitive choice of programming to which they are entitled," he added.  news is also the 50 percent owner of pay tv company foxtel and has developed the film and television production house fox studios in sydney.  "news broadcasting aims to bring the full benefit of rapidly advancing broadcasting services to australian homes as soon as possible," murdoch said.

title: more chinese join internet
body: the family of hong xiujuan in south china's guangzhou city regularly surf the internet to find information used for a variety of purposes.  the internet has enabled the family to regularly contact friends and relatives living abroad, in addition to helping her remain abreast of the the latest developments in academia.  "i've been using downloaded computer programs to teach my daughter english, and she's learning quite fast." said hong.  many chinese families with good educational backgrounds are accessing the internet, with some 10 percent of the over 300,000 guangzhou families with computers currently surfing the net.  at present, some 45 newspapers and television stations have established homepages, including xinhua news agency, the people's daily and china central television (cctv).  chinese children who formerly opted for computer games are now using systems to search for information. computers have also emerged as useful tools for locating jobs, conducting business, purchasing or selling stocks, and accessing electronic newspapers.  statistics show that china currently has 1.5 million registered internet users, with the number expected to hit five million users by the end of the century. chinese computer users will thus emerge as an important consumer force in the near future.

title: u.s. small businesses urged to embrace internet
body: the overwhelming majority of small and medium businesses in the unitedstates have not strategically embraced the internet as a business tool, according to a new survey released on tuesday.  "nor do they grasp the unprecedented opportunity the internet offers to level the playing field," said the yankee group, an internet technology and communications market research firm.  as a result, the firm said, internet solution providers need to revise their product lines to reflect a staged approach to internet commerce focused on first building a foundation, before attempting to migrate small and medium businesses to higher-value services.  the research firm identified a three-phase process that small and medium businesses undergo as their internet commitment strengthens: connectivity, customer connections and commerce. more than two-thirds of the companies surveyed have yet to move into the customer connection phase.  "promoting the internet as a tool to transform the way small and medium businesses buy and sell will not connect with this market," the yankee group said.
