title: us "science" magazine has more readers in china
body: the american journal "science," one of the most authoritative academic periodicals in the world, is attracting more readers in china.  during the first six months of this year more than 24,000 chinese have visited the "science" website on the internet, said ellis rubinstein, editor in chief of the magazine, who is here attending a celebration of the 40th anniversary of the china association for science and technology.  "there were only 13 subscribers to "science" in china 10 years ago. but now there are about 800 subscribers of the printed edition in the mainland and hongkong," said rubinstein. "this is a good number compared with other countries." since "science" became available on the internet in beijing in january, chinese researchers and students have been accessing the lastest editions of the journal on both the china science and technology network and the china education and research network.  rubinstein said he hopes the chinese government will continue to support the development of the internet, through which chinese scientists may obtain instant information on the world wide web and thereby enjoy fair competition with their foreign counterparts.  "science" is published weekly and enjoys a high reputation in international scientific research circles, especially for its articles on biology and medical science.  although more and more chinese read "science," the number of chinese scientists who publish their papers in the magazine remains very small.  only two or three papers written by chinese scientists are published in the magazine every year, along with about ten papers written jointly by scientists of china and other countries, according to rubinstein.  "actually, it's difficult for scientists anywhere in the world to have their papers published in our magazine. lots of scientists submit their very best papers to us, but only one in eight or one in ten can be accepted," he said.  "but there's no nation we expect more papers from than china in the long run because of its devotion to science. so i expect very large changes."

title: internet awareness and use grow in kenya
body: the rise in internet awareness in kenya has triggered a spiral growth in on-line trading as at least 25,000 people in the country have internet access.  the vast potential of on-line trading was apparent at a recent internet auction of seats to various european destinations by lufthansa airlines. kenyans were among 600 potential buyers who bid through the internet.  the rise in internet awareness and use was first noted during the 1997 general election in the east african country and is largely credited to the nation media group website, which had an average of 50,000 hits a day.  during the december election month, internet services reported eight million visits to kenyan sites, barney lodge, chief of media street, an electronic advertising agency in nairobi, was quoted by monday's east african as saying.  in kenya, "at least 25,000 people have internet access and the number is bound to grow as the cost of connections and computers falls and back-up services improve," said lodge.  until two years ago, computers cost not less than 100,000 shillings (1,666 unitedstates dollars) but prices now average 60,000 shillings (1,000 dollars), largely due to a reduct o,hz7 import duty and competition among a large number of importers.  the growth in the number of internet users has, however, been hampered by poor telephone connections, with most business clients reluctant to invest in developing their own websites, fearing that these would not be easily accessible.  in response, the kenya posts and telecommunications corporation is planning to install a fiber optic telephone network by november, which will provide "clean" and fast internet connections.  however, victor mabachi, chairman of the advertising practitioners associations (apa), said the internet still lacks a solid client base to attract good advertising.  currently, the bulk of advertising on the internet is by small-scale traders, who constitute 75 percent of all advertisers, said geoffrey shimanyula, the marketing manager of africaonline, which is kenya's biggest internet service provider.

title: single currency data on internet
body: those who take interest in the single currency due out soon were offered from monday onward internet access to free information on the euro. eurostat, the statistical bureau of the european community, is responsible for this euro-related information program and the euro data will be updated on a daily basis. yves-thibault de silguy, european economy and finance commissioner, told the press that the publication of key euro indicators on the internet is an important initiative and the data provided will prove useful for the economic management in the euro zone as well as in the european union. the commissioner said, "the euro indicators will provide member states, the european central bank, national central banks, financial markets, enterprises, the media and the public with the latest economic and monetary union statistics essential for decision-making." he added that the statistics would be updated at noon every day, a significant improvement on eurostat's service. the indicators, accessible at http:europa.eu.int/eurostat.html, will include national accounts statistics, monetary and financial indicators, external trade, balance of payments, prices, industry, labor market, public finance and short-term qualitative surveys. the single currency and employment were among the top three topics for which more information is desired by the respondents to a recent eu questionnaire. the other top topic is the rights for being a european citizen.

title: middle east economic briefs
body: the following are economic briefs from middle east countries. jeddah --chief of islamic bank for development (ibd) ahmed mohammed ali said the training course on trade policies is part of the effort of the standing committee for economic cooperation and trade exchanges, an affiliate of the organization of the islamic conference (oic).  addressing the opening ceremony of the three-week course, ali said the aim of the course is to coordinate the efforts of the member countries in the face of the challenges posed by the trade globalization and the new world trade order. beirut --the visit of the armenian businessman delegation, headed by prime minister armen darbinyan, to lebanon helped the businessmen of the two countries define the available investment opportunities.  the visit also encouraged setting up of joint ventures and and enhancing exports as well as the exchange of commodities and services between the two countries, al-hayat daily reported. riyadh --the arab petroleum investment co. (apico) signed an agreement with the finnish nesti co., the italian icofuel and the saudi algin.  under the agreement the four firms will launch the national corporation for fuel improvement "tahsin" (improvement) with a capital of 500 million riyals (over 133 million unitedstates dollars).  apico said that the project aims to set up the world's largest plant for fuel improvement in yanbo'e city, saudi arabia. its capacity will hit 90,000 tonnes annually. it will start production in early 2001.  the algin will have a stake of 25 to 30 percent of the project, the icofuel 15 percent, apico 10 percent and the remaining will be taken by a number of saudi and gulf firms. amman --service related to the internet is booming in jordan, which has seven isp (internet service provider) companies and around 70 internet cafes for its 4.6 million people.  the isp companies have over 30,000 customers and each internet cafe has at least 10 regular visitors, it added.  jordan legalized the internet use in its territory in 1995.

title: xinhua world news summary

title: africa online to start roaming email service
body: africa online, a leading internet service provider in africa, will next month launch a new email service which will enable travelers to get their email messages and reply as they arrive.  this service is a response to the need among the firm's customers for easy access to their electronic mail messages, africa online's product manager david ochanda said thursday.  "we have grouped with a consortium of international service providers, known as the gric alliance, through which the company can provide a continuity of service for its customers wherever they are," said ochanda.  using the so-called roaming service, people traveling abroad will no longer live in fear of returning home to a stack of unattended electronic mail, the daily nation newspaper reported friday.  users will be able to access their accounts on their laptop computers while still abroad.  the roaming service allows customers to dial into numbers of internet providers who have signed into a consortium in the countries where they are visiting.  the service eliminates the need for international telephone calls and minimizes chances of bad connections, cut-offs or garbled messages, said the report.  the manager said the service is mainly designed for business travelers who are out of the country for at least three to six times a year, employees of international and multinational organizations, as well as students studying abroad.  previously, people traveling out of the reach of their service providers, especially in kenya, have had to suspend their accounts for the duration of their absence.

title: online grocery market in u.s. still immature
body: despite projected sales of 10.8 billion unitedstates dollars, the online grocery market in the unitedstates will represent less than 2 percent of consumer packaged goods revenues in 2003, according to a market forecast report.  the report released this week by the market analysis firm forrester research, said that online grocery sales will continue to be held back by limited geographic availability, delivery and membership fees, a small target audience and uncertainty about the market itself.  forrester researchers said that the market will remain tiny in the next five years. although packaged goods manufacturers are gearing up to sell directly, the report said, convenience-driven shoppers are still not used to online sales. "manufacturers should continue to sell through grocers both on-and off-line," forrester suggested.  the online grocery market can be divided into full-service and speciality sellers. the former sells a complete range of grocery products via a pc, phone or fax. the latter offers a limited selection of gifts, hard-to-find items or bulk replenishment products via the internet.  constrained by the costs and limitations of delivering fresh and frozen products to a limited audience of high-income online families, forrester said, full-service providers are currently struggling to develop a profitable operating model and gain critical mass in a few key markets.  despite a compounded annual growth rate of 92 percent over the next five years, full-service grocery sales will only reach 4.5 billion dollars in 2003 in the unitedstates, less than one percent of total industry sales, forrester predicted.  but forrester expects the speciality category, driven by online gift sales, to climb to 6.3 billion dollars by 2003.  although the market is small right now, forrester researchers said that the prospect of 15 million households making speciality purchases online will prove too important to ignore.  manufacturers will look for ways to exploit the web, like building loyalty, learning more about the buying habits of online consumers and driving off-line sales through online promotions, forrester said.  echoing forrester's study, companies attending the american marketing association's annual research conference this week agreed that the net has become a boon for marketers.  for companies in need of marketing information, researchers attending the meeting said, the internet offers a means of reaching consumers who can respond at their own leisure.

title: first u.s. web-only bank set to launch
body: the first nationally chartered bank in the unitedstates to operate exclusively over the world wide web is scheduled to go on line later this month or early october, computerworld reported on its online news wednesday.  compubank, a houston-based bank backed by 6 million unitedstates dollars in private funding, will offer several advantages over existing web-based banks or pc-based banking service. it will charge no monthly fee and require no minimum balance for its basic checking account, although a deposit of 200 unitedstates dollars will be required. customers will be able to pay an unlimited number of bills electronically for a flat fee of 5.5 dollars.  the web-only bank will also offer customers the ability to view their statements and images of processed checks online. customers can also view their accounts from any browser that supports 128-bit encryption. there is no need for the proprietary pc software many banks require online customers to use.  one downside is that, because of its small size, compubank owns no automatic teller machines (atm) of its own, forcing many customers to pay fees if they use atms owned by other banks. but the bank is looking for atm networks that don't charge a fee to outsiders and recommends its customers do withdrawals by using their compubank atm cards as debit cards at stores.  compubank also has to prove that its back-office systems can handle hundreds, thousands or tens of thousands of customers, computerworld said. currently, its web site boasts only a static billboard that says the service is "coming soon." according to computerworld, compubank has got approval to operate as a bank in the country's all 50 states and the unitedstates territories from the unitedstates comptroller of the currency in july. at the same time, it qualified for coverage by the federal deposit insurance corporation, which means the federal government insures each customer's savings up to 100,000 dollars.

title: hk well-placed to provide chinese support for internet
body: hongkong, as a bilingual city, is well-placed to provide chinese language support for the development of applications and content on the internet, a senior hongkong government official said here wednesday.  there is a growing demand for content in chinese on the internet in asia in particular as the use of the internet spreads around the globe, said k c kwong, secretary for information technology and broadcasting of the hongkong special administrative region (sar).  addressing the opening ceremony of the 9th asian information technology exhibition (it expo '98), kwong said that with the ever-increasing number of users all over the world, the internet has become an important channel for communication, information sharing, on-line government services and electronic business.  but communication on the internet is still based largely on the english language, he said.  this is only to be expected given the history of development of the internet, kwong said. however, the scene is changing rapidly as the use of the internet becomes popular around the world, he added.  kwong pointed out that the hksar government fully recognizes this and has taken measures to promote the use of chinese.  he said, "within the government, we have adopted a common chinese character set to facilitate data exchange between government departments and the public." "and, nearly all of our web sites now support both chinese and english languages. our current plan to deliver public services electronically, through the internet and other communication channels, will also be enabled for communication in chinese," he added.  "we are also working closely with other governments and institutions under the aegis of the international standards organization in the development of the iso 10646 standard, which is an international coding standard aimed at encompassing characters of asian languages into one single common character set," he continued.  kwong noted that harmonization of internal codes for chinese characters is not enough. there are equally important issues that demand immediate attention.  the first is the provision of more sophisticated and user-friendly conversion tools capable of supporting the use of traditional and simplified chinese characters, kwong said.  the second is the development of an efficient and effective mechanism for searching and retrieving information in either traditional or simplified chinese characters on the internet and the most important is the provision of content in chinese.  all this requires close collaboration between government, the information technology and services industry and academia, kwong said.

title: shanghai promotes tourism on internet
body: shanghai, china's largest economic center, recently opened a website on the internet to promote tourism.  shanghai international tourism, the third such site launched on the internet in china, after hongkong and beijing, was jointly initiated by the municipal organizing committee of the shanghai tourism festival, shanghai jiaotong university and the ast computer center in the unitedstates.  the site includes guides to scenic spots, tourist agents, hotels, restaurants, shopping centers and recreational facilities in the city.  the new web page highlights the shanghai tourism festival which will be held from october 17 to november 8.  recent statistics show that the number of overseas tourists coming to shanghai in the first half of the year was 729,200, down seven percent from the same period last year due apparently to the impact of the asian financial crisis.  since last october, the city has taken steps to attract outside tourists by sending out 100 tourism promotion teams to other countries, issuing 900,000 tourist guide brochures and video tapes to overseas agents.  local tourist agents have also created many new types of tours enabling tourists to "be a shanghainese for a day," "honeymoon in shanghai" and "cross the millennium."

title: uk cracks down on internet racism
body: british home secretary jack straw on tuesday announced that britain would crack down on racism on the internet.  speaking to the board of deputies of british jews, straw said the national criminal intelligence service (ncis) would play an important role against threatening, abusive and racist material published on the internet.  "the internet offers exciting opportunities for global communication, but it is vulnerable to abuse, because websites and newsgroups are accessible from across international borders," he said.  he also called for governments across the world to work together to remove illegal websites and prosecute those responsible.  an expert in the subject has warned that groups were not only using the internet for racism publicity but also for planning terrorist activity.  racism was identified in a report compiled by the ncis early this year as one of the principal areas in which the internet was abused.  the ncis has already been cooperating with other police agencies around the world to target child pornography rings, and intelligence reports suggest that similar co-operation will be required to combat racism.  net experts agree that the majority of right wing, neo-nazi and fascist websites that publish racist material are concentrated in north america, germany and scandinavia.

title: middle east economic briefs
body: the following are economic briefs from middle east countries. amman --investments in jordan's tourism are expected to reach 600 million jordanian dinars (about 847 million unitedstates dollars) by the end of 2000, the jordan times newspaper said sunday.  minister of tourism and antiquities akil beltaji said that the unique tourism characteristics in jordan, represented by the dead sea and some biblical sites, help boost the investment. amman --a number of jordanian companies have secured another 21 million dollars worth of contracts with iraq under the u.n. oil-for-food deal.  government sources said that under the 13 new contracts, jordan will supply iraq with soap, vegetable oil and medicine.  with the new contracts, jordan's relevant incomes have reached more than 350 million dollars since the deal was put into force in december 1996 to allow iraq to sell limited amount of oil to buy food and medicine. amman --jordanian exports to saudi arabia in the first half of this year reached 45.3 million dinars (about 63.9 million dollars), jordans arabic daily ad dustour said sunday.  the paper quoted government resources as saying that jordanian exports to saudi arabia were recorded at 70 million dollars in 1995 and 130 million dollars in 1996. kuwait city --the national bank of kuwait (nbk) announced sunday that its services are available on internet and clients will be furnished with the most up-to-date and fastest techniques of services.  general director of the banking group services adel abdel wahab al-majed said that the nbk clients, who have already enjoyed the telephone and computer convenience, can start conducting banking operations, such as account transfers, cancellation of payment orders and disclosure of all accounts via the internet.  a client can directly contact the employee responsible for his accounts via email, according to the kuwait news agency.  encouraging the clients to use the internet, the nbk has decided to cut service fees by 50 percent on the web operations, al-majed said. amman --the largest bromine factory in jordan will be set up by the jordan potash company and the albemarle company of the unitedstates.  the unitedstates company will offer 40 percent of the total 120 million dollars of investments and the rest will be raised through foreign loans, minister of information nasir judeh said.

title: experts divergent on e-commerce definition
body: experts who met in austin, texas this week to discuss issues concerning e-commerce could not reach consensus on the definition of e-commerce.  paul resnick, an associate professor at the university of michigan, said that e-commerce should be narrowly focused on transactions over computer networks, reported techweb friday.  but james mcandrews, a researcher with the federal reserve bank of new york, said that e-commerce also includes credit card transactions at local grocery stores.  "electronic commerce is a larger category than just web-based commerce," he said.  although the customer goes into the store to purchase, he said, the transaction is recorded electronically.  a software developer agreed with the wider scope of that definition, saying, "it's everything binary. we are taking our economy and digitizing it." kevin koym, president of the software company development system development, also supported the definition with wider scope, saying e-commerce is not just the internet.  instead, it includes everything from learning about products online and electronic transactions to online customer-service and support, said koym.  the national science foundation meeting, sponsored by the center for research in electronic commerce at the university of texas, was aimed to develop a strategy for studying e-commerce.  forty people, including computer scientists, attorneys, economists as well as government officials and industry researchers, attended the meeting.

title: 18.4 million u.s. households participating in e-commerce
body: some 18.4 million households in the unitedstates make use of the internet for their shopping, according to a survey released thursday.  more than 11 million households learn about products for non-internet purchases and 7.4 million shop for products to purchase via online service or the internet.  most online american shoppers spend 20 hours or more each week, learning about products that are then bought off-line or shopping for products to be purchased online, said zd market intelligence, a market data provider in la jolla, california.  the findings are based on a semi-annual survey of unitedstates pc use and users.  the study shows that internet users and electronic-commerce participants are similar in many ways. but the gap between these two groups and the unitedstates population as a whole widens when compared side by side.  online shoppers and internet users tend to be younger, more affluent and better-educated than the general unitedstates population.  the biggest challenge in closing the e-commerce gap --even bigger than security, payment and standard issues --is the fact that more than half of households do not have pcs or internet access, according to the study. this fact has contributed greatly to keeping e-commerce from reaching critical mass.  in addition to internet penetration, bandwidth --the transmission capacity of a communications network --presents another challenge to e-commerce growth. greater bandwidth is crucial to creating positive consumer experience and therefore enabling people to feel more confident participating in e-commerce activities.  "until there is a critical mass of pcs connected to the internet, e-commerce will continue to quickly outgrow the infrastructure in place to support it," the study said.

title: world internet server market to grow
body: the worldwide internet server market will grow considerably as more users look to purchase full-featured servers, rather than upgrade their current systems with internet software, according to a unitedstates market analysis firm.  dataquest, an information technology advisory service company based in california, released a new study tuesday, predicting that revenue of the worldwide internet server market will reach 13.27 billion unitedstates dollars in 1998, up 114 percent from last year.  the market grew 276 percent in 1997, with revenue reaching 6.21 billion dollars, dataquest said.  in 1997, the worldwide internet server market was led by the silicon valley company sun microsystems, whose revenue accounted for 22.3 percent of the market.  "it's important to remember that the internet server market is still in its infancy and has the kind of dynamic qualities that promise not just change, but very quick change," dataquest said in a report.  "as a result, significant opportunities exist for vendors that do not currently in the upper reaches of the revenue and shipment picture." although the market was dominated by a relatively small number of vendors, dataquest analysts said it is not too late for vendors to succeed in this thriving market.  midrange servers accounted for more than 63 percent of the worldwide market in 1997, with revenue reaching 3.97 billion dollars.  dataquest predicted that midrange internet servers will continue to dominate the market through 2002.  midgrange systems are often found in such applications as internet database, internet compute and high-end internet file serving.

title: first internet surfers emerge in china's poorest area
body: xin xiaodong, 34, has been spending some of his spare time on the internet daily just like other surfers around the world, and is now among the first group of 22 internet surfers in one of china's poorest areas.  xin became an internet user at the end of last year. the number of 'net surfers in xihaigu prefecture in northwest china's ningxia autonomous region now accounts for 3 percent of all internet users in ningxia, china's smallest autonomous region (province).  china registered about 1.1 million net surfers by the end of june this year.  xihaigu is an outlying mountainous area with poor roads and communications facilities, and 500,000 of its needy inhabitants still live below the poverty line.  but as part of the rapid economic growth now taking place in xihaigu, state-of-the-art telephone exchanges and optic fibre cables have been installed in the region.  a local government official said that only six years ago most of the local residents in xihaigu knew little about computers, but now many households have them.  xin xiaodong, mathematics teacher at guyuan teachers college, spent 7,600 yuan (910 unitedstates dollars) to buy a compaq computer. this represents nearly two years' salary.  xin said, "it is worth it to buy the computer and become a 'net surfer, as i gain more knowledge and my vision is widened," adding that his students are more interested in his lessons since he has been absorbing so much new information over the internet.  the websites xin usually visit are those of chinese and foreign university libraries. in the past, he had to go to yinchuan, capital of the autonomous region 400 km away from his home, to find such information.  he said, "all i need now is a few stroke on the keyboard of my computer when i want the latest information in a certain field." the internet also helps boost local economic growth. the haiyuan county government has already begun to issue information on agricultural cooperation via the internet.  hongxiang company, a privately-run venture, signed an agreement with a shanghai venture to sell 4,000 tons of potatos through the internet this past june. ningxia is famous for its rich-starch large potatos and chinese wolfberry fruit.  in guyuan county, the center of xihaigu prefecture, three computer shops have opened along the two-km-long main street, and advertisements for computer training are popular in newspapers and in shop-window displays.  the guyuan daily, the prefecture's only newspaper, will go on-line this october and is expected to be the first to do so among the region's media.

title: lebanon, world bank discuss internet program
body: lebanese prime minister rafik hariri monday discussed with a world bank delegation a program to get lebanon's secondary schools hooked to the internet.  hariri told the delegation that he attaches great importance to the plan, to be sponsored by the world bank, in view of the approach of the 21st century, which will feature advanced technologies, the lebanese orient radio reported.  the world bank launched a world links for development program last year to get 1,500 secondary schools in 40 developing nations connected with the internet to partner schools in australia, canada, european countries, japan and the unitedstates over a four-year period.  the program is aimed at enabling the students to cooperate in cultural, scientific and educational projects.  hariri described the program as an opportunity to lead lebanon into a regional center for education on internet.  he said the recent reduction in subscription fees to the internet is part of the lebanese government's effort to help the program succeed in the country.  head of the world bank delegation shimse diine said the program will be carried out in lebanon soon after a detailed plan is worked out.  the program is currently operated in six african and five south american countries.

title: bt launches new digital internet service
body: british telecom thursday launched its new bt highway mass market digital communication service, which is designed to allow people to surf the internet at high speed and use the telephone simultaneously.  the service, to begin from september 15, will transform a customer's existing telephone line into a new fast and multi-functional digital internet and multimedia connection, the company said.  bt highway offers customer choices of using combinations of analogue or digital connections over a single telephone line, which means families or small businesses could surf the internet or send emails and make calls at the same time.  currently, users with a single analogue telephone line have to disconnect from the internet when they are using the phone.  the new service will operate at a minimum speed of 64 kilobits per second, or a maximum of 128 kilobits per second, much faster than the fastest modems working on ordinary telephone lines.  "bt highway is a major step towards mass digitalisation of the uk." afshin mohebbi, managing director of bt's business division, said in a statement.  though internet growth has been phenomenal, only 1.8 million uk households are connected. bt hopes that its new service will help bridge the gap.  "our aim is to connect the majority of uk households with the latest high-quality, high-capacity digital communications by the year 2003." the company said.  at the moment ten percent of all telephone usage in the uk is for data, but bt expects data to become the most important aspect of the network some time before 2003.

title: expert suggests internet technology for science museums in china
body: an australian expert suggested today that china use internet technology to develop science and technology museums.  brenton honeyman, an expert with the national science and technology center of australia, offered the suggestion at the '98 beijing international conference on science and technology center/museums held today at the china science and technology museum in beijing. he pointed out that an increasing number of science centers around the world have introduced computers to enable people of all ages to enjoy the fascinating world of science and technology.  "science centers are discovering that the internet, the worldwide web in particular, provides an excellent opportunity to reach wide audiences and promote greater public contact," according to honeyman.  he added that significant developments in browser software have made it possible for web users to experience far greater levels of "interactivity" than the passive scrolling which has dominated the web in recent years.  honeyman noted that china's population of 1.2 billion people provides the nation's science centers and museums with the largest potential audience in the world. however, he pointed to the fact that most science museums have failed to give full play to computers and noted the vast potential and prospects for their use.  zhu youwen, a senior engineer with the china science and technology museum, said that low rate of computer usage for china's 285 science museums. he noted that most facilities simply use computers to daily affairs.  "apart from general problems such as the lack of funds, a major factor hindering the introduction of computer applications in science museums centers on the lack of suitable software," said zhu.  he called on related departments to increase funding to promote the development and use of advanced internet technology and computer application systems.  the three-day conference has attracted chinese experts and a large group of scholars from a dozen of countries and regions, including the untied states, france and the philippines. the participants will discuss the development of science centers, as well as related education, exhibits design and applications of modern technology.  the conference, carrying the theme "providing education and inculcation for the public," is a major academic exchange activity initiated by the world science center (wsc). the first international conference was held in finland in 1996.

title: hk open university to start web-based instruction
body: the open university of hongkong (ouhk) will implement full-scale web-based instruction in two years' time, the university's newly-appointed director of technology development, leung chun-ming, said thursday.  he said topping his agenda is to explore ways to enhance distant education using advanced technology.  in web-based instruction, teaching activities will be conducted on the worldwide web which integrates text, sound and images.  students will be able to plan their studies at their own pace and time.  to implement the plan, the ouhk will first convert materials of more than 100 existing courses into on-line version. by applying interactive multimedia technology, tutors and students will then be able to interact on the web.  web-based instruction is becoming popular in the unitedstates but has not yet been widely adopted in hongkong.  according to leung, the ouhk also plans to adopt speech recognition technology to upgrade language teaching at primary, secondary and university levels.  the ouhk projects will be carried out with the support of the 10-million-hk-dollar (1.3 million unitedstates) multimedia laboratory sponsored by the hongkong jockey club charities trust.

title: internet booming in northeast china's liaoning province
body: northeast china's liaoning province now has 16,595 internet subscribers, including 95 corporate users who rent special fiber-optic cables for greater and easier access to the internet.  information from the liaoning provincial digital telecommunications bureau said that 9,500 subscribers have been added in the first seven months of this year.  according to the bureau, several major libraries in liaoning, the provincial pricing bureau, and the provincial administration for industry and commerce, publish information on books, pricing, and consumer complaints on the internet.  the province's port city of dalian this summer organized a camp where students received free training on the world wide web during their holidays. many newspapers have also started special pages to popularize knowledge about the internet and related fields.  feng qiang, an official with the province's digital telecommunications bureau, said his province will use internet services for long-distance education, medical care, and inquiries into scores on national university and college entrance examinations in the future.  china was first connected to the internet in april 1994, and now has 1.06 million internet subscribers, said sources from china internet information center.

title: internet improves students' grades: study
body: a survey conducted by att last month said the internet "helps students get better grades." more than half of the 2,416 american respondents to the survey, whose results were released wednesday, agreed that "the internet has become a necessary tool for success in school." almost 70 percent of the parents, students and teachers who participated in the survey said they had seen students' grades improve through the use of the internet.  "the internet is to school research in the '90s what the calculator was to math in the '70s," said dan schulman, president of att world net service, which conducted the on-line survey, in a statement.  "it's a tool that lets students learn more in less time. in keeping with that belief, we're encouraging kids to use the internet in a variety of ways." att has created several web programs to introduce children to the internet and advise parents on helping children use the internet safely.  while the survey confirmed the internet can be an educational tool, other studies have revealed its "negative impact." researchers at carnegie mellon university, for example, found that people who spend even just a few hours a week on-line experience higher levels of depression and loneliness than they would have if they used the computer network less frequently. the results of their study, with att as one of the sponsors, were released last week.

title: worldwide internet child pornography ring uncovered
body: the unitedstates and 11 other countries have started a battle against child pornography through internet and on wednesday arrested almost four dozens of suspected members of a ring committing such crime worldwide.  the ring, wonderland club, was allegedly traded pictures of children as young as 18 months old over the internet. it has exchanged thousands of pornographic images of children via cyberspace.  a database of more than 100,000 pornographic photos of children were uncovered after five months of investigations by the british national crime squad, the associated press said.  "people try to smuggle in smut just like they try to smuggle dope across the border and we're ready to pounce on them," said dick weart, a special agent for the unitedstates customs service, which carried out 32 raids in 22 unitedstates states with the help of state and local police.  police confiscated boxes of pornography, various software materials and hardware that were part and parcel of the ring during the raids, weart said.  more than 40 arrests worldwide were made wednesday, and unitedstates customs predicted there would be more as officials evaluated the evidence collected. hundreds of people are suspected of being connected with the pornography ring.  "the people who exploit children in this way think they can hide in cyberspace. they are wrong. we will find them and bring them to justice," unitedstates customs commissioner raymond kelly said.  the raids occurred in australia, austria, belgium, britain, finland, france, germany, italy, norway, portugal, sweden and the unitedstates.  to join the child pornography ring, members had to have multiple images of child pornography, and some had as many as 10,000 pictures, unitedstates customs said. the ring allegedly began in the unitedstates.  the investigation, code-named "cathedral," linked members of the wonderland club through the types of images they allegedly sent to each other.

title: hke090104 --australian ministers ridiculed on internet by hackers
body: australian prime minister john howard and his key ministers suffered unexpected negative publicity as they were ridiculed on the internet by hackers monday, the first day of australia's federal election campaign.  the daily telegraph reported that the prime minister, instead of being referred to as "the honorable john howard mp", had become "the dishonorable john howard mp: prime minister for pain, suffering and inequity" on the liberal party's site.  a spokesman for the prime minister tuesday confirmed the report, saying the web site for the australian liberal party, whose leader is john howard, was vandalized monday evening.  the site closed soon after the attack was discovered and the offending material was then removed, the spokesman told xinhua.  treasurer peter costello, the would-be successor to john howard as leader of the party, australian foreign minister alexander downer and workplace relations minister peter reith also suffered ridicule on their web sites.  the treasurer, who was behind the sweeping taxation reform plan unveiled last month, became "minister for the rich, stomping the poor and wrecking the economy".  the foreign minister was called "minister for foreign humiliation" on his web site, which was also linked to disneyland.com.  workplace relations minister peter reith, who has launched a nationwide campaign to break the monopoly of the nation's trade union over seaports, became "minister for destruction of workplace fairness, the gestapo and propaganda" with his site linked to the maritime union of australia.  overnight repairs to the liberal party's internet site have restored dignity to prime minister john howard.  but early tuesday morning the sites of some key ministers were still unable to be accessed, including those of reith, environment minister robert hill, social security minister jocelyn newman, resources minister warwick parer, justice minister amanda vanstone and attorney-general daryl williams.  a spokeswoman for the australian federal police declined to say whether the police were going to investigate the case, adding they would consider taking action after receiving a complaint from the australian title: australian stocks end 1.44 percent lower
body: continued uncertainty in global markets and heavy falls in several blue-chip stocks sent the australian share market tumbling 1.44 percent monday.  the benchmark all ordinaries index was down 36.2 points to close at 2480.7, off an intra-day low of 2467.5.  "there is a lot of uncertainty in world markets and that is putting pressure on our market," said dicksons client adviser robert holle.  the local bourse traded in negative territory from the start, with the tone set by a 114.31-point drop on the dow jones industrial average in new york which closed at 8051.68 on friday.  ord minnett dealer chris shaw said sharp falls by news corp, diversified miner bhp and national australia bank stock were together responsible for a large slice of the australian market's fall.  news corp plunged 78.1 australian cents, or 6.81 percent, to 10.69 australian dollars while its preferred scrip dived 52.3 cents, or 5.20 percent, to close at 9.53 australian dollars.  on the resources board, bhp shares tumbled 34 cents to the five-year-low level of 12.06 australian dollars, with resources stocks generally succumbing to global market concerns and low commodity prices.  the all resources index finished the day 14.7 points lower at 916.1, while the all industrials index were down 62.8 points to 4409.0.  national australia bank ditched 32.7 cents to 21.62 australian dollars, contributing to a 99.4 point slide on the bank index to 5485.2.  shaw said bank stocks were generally weaker on speculation of a possible interest rate rise to prop up the weak australian dollar.  commonwealth bank of australia shed 24.8 cents to 18.66 australian dollars, anz bank slid 21.8 cents to 8.83 australian dollars and westpac bank dropped 20 cents to 9.30 australian dollars.  diversified miner rio tinto fell 20 to 16.96 australian dollars.  the gold index dropped 28.3 points to 843.6, and the spot price of gold bullion in sydney was 275.00 unitedstates dollars an ounce on monday afternoon, up from friday's close of 271.65 unitedstates dollars an ounce.  national turnover was 318.44 million shares traded for 789.53 million unitedstates dollars, with falling stocks outnumbering rising stocks 655 to 416.

title: u.s. net investment hits 124 billion dollars
body: unitedstates firms will invest 124 billion dollars in the "internet economy" this year, according to a study by the market research firm international data corp.(idc).  idc defines the internet economy as "spending on technology deployment, marketing and sales, content creation, professional services, and education and training to support internet technology-based applications." the study found that unitedstates net investment still exceeds return.  for every dollar and a half the firms invest, they will get back one dollar.  despite the fact that companies still invest more than they get back this year, idc said, the outlook is rosy. the study predicts that the tide could turn as soon as 2000, with unitedstates firms gaining more in benefits than they spend on net investment.  idc defines "benefits" as a combination of commerce conducted over the web and productivity savings from internet applications.  the current situation will change rapidly, idc said. "within five years, every dollar of internet investment in the unitedstates will be paying back 1.5 dollars, and the size of the total investment will be four to five times bigger. it looks like the unitedstates cross-over point --from investment to payback economy --could come as soon as the year 2000." idc is still finalizing the forecast of the worldwide internet economy. the western europe economy will be 44 billion dollars this year, about a third of the unitedstates internet economy. in 2000, the region's internet economy will reach 170 billion dollars.  "europe's lag in adopting internet technologies will mean a commensurate delay in turning into a payback economy," idc said.  idc will release more results from its study of the internet economy at a conference in september in san jose, california.  the research company said that it analyzed information technology (it) budgets and non-it budget technology spending across an array of industries for its research on the internet economy. it also surveyed 600 "architects of the internet economy," in conjunction with technology business magazine, the industry standard.

title: more shanghai people visit websites for leisure and shopping
body: shanghai hotline," one of the most popular websites in china, has been visited more than 10 million times since it was set up on november 22, 1996.  the website, according to zhang linde, general manager of shanghai information industry co., ltd., linked with six others in china, have more than 40,000 subscribers and about 180,000 regular visitors.  the number of daily average visitors has increased to 40,000 from several hundred only two years ago.  the rapid development of cyberspace has also led more people do their shopping on-line.  the xinhua bookstore on east nanjing road launched its site on the hotline last may, the first on-line bookstore in the city.  wang jinhua, manager of the on-line bookstore, said that sales volume has reached about 200,000 yuan from on-line sales, and the monthly average is approaching 20,000 yuan.  on-line flower shops, drugstores and booking offices are also very active on the hotline website.  experts say that department-store customers in shanghai are expected to decline by 20 to 30 percent by the end of this century due to the growth of on-line shopping and electronic businesses.  the "shanghai hotline" will soon enlarge its capacity for the third time, in an effort to boost the number of visitors to one million daily.

title: new study shows record numbers online
body: a new survey by nielsen media this week shows that more people in the unitedstates and canada are online and doing their shopping there.  the number of internet users older than 16 in the two countries reached 79 million as of june, according to the study. that's 36 percent increase over last year, when a survey showed 58 million users online.  of the 79 million net users, nielsen said, 20 million are buying products and services online. and the number of web shoppers --people checking out or comparing products and services on the web --is now 48 million.  "the internet continues its impressive growth as a communications, research, entertainment and commercial medium," said jerome samson, director of technology and business strategy at nielsen in a statement.  based on the statistics, he said, the number of internet users grew at a rate of 2.5 percent a month from january 1997 through june this year. when it came to e-commerce, the numbers grew at 3.5 percent a month from january 1997 through september 1997. and from september through june this year, the growth in online buyers accelerated 8 percent a month.  "the dramatic increase in online purchasing is primarily due to people realizing how quick and easy it is to shop on the web," samson said.

title: u.s. internet economy to nearly quadruple in four years
body: the internet economy of the unitedstates will grow to 518 billion unitedstates dollars in 2002, the research firm international data corporation (idc) forecast this week.  idc defines the internet economy, which will come to 124 billion dollars in 1998, as the combination of spending to build web businesses and applications and the revenue from products and services sold over the internet.  while technology deployment is the lion's share of the economy, idc said, significant spending is also occurring in marketing and branding activities, professional services, content creation and education and training.  manufacturers of hard goods are leading the spending in 1998, with an estimated 23 billion dollars being invested by the industry segment in web applications for extranet, intranets and commerce web sites.  next among the top five industries are communications/media and banking, each with 15 billion dollars to be spent this year.  idc said that it will announce its findings for the size and future growth of the worldwide internet economy at an internet executive forum to be held in september in san jose, california.  the conference will examine the business models driving the internet economy and the barriers that must be overcome to fulfill its potential.  idc's research on the internet economy is based on an analysis of information technology (it) budgets across major industries, as well as non-it budget technology spending. in addition, idc conducted a survey of 600 architects of the internet economy.

title: australian expert warns of terrorism on internet
body: terrorism on the internet was increasing at an alarming rate and threatening businesses and governments around the world, an australian computer expert warned tuesday.  organizations should review their security to protect themselves against cyber-terrorist attacks, deakin university computing expert matthew warren said in an interview in melbourne with the australian associated press.  he said many organizations were at present so preoccupied with the millennium bug that they had become lax on computer security.  "terrorist groups have difficulty in relaying their political messages to the general public without being censored and they can now use the internet for this purpose," he said.  he said some groups were even using the internet for fund-raising purposes, adding it was now possible to make a direct donation to a certain group by using your credit card.  terrorist groups could also use other methods such as email bombs where thousands of emails are sent to a particular computer system until that system crashed, he said.  most companies were preoccupied with the millennium bug and viruses and were too relaxed in their attitude toward computer security, leaving themselves open to internet terrorism, he said.

title: california forbids new taxes on internet activities
body: california governor pete wilson monday signed a state bill that bans any new taxes on internet activities for the next three years, calling on unitedstates congress and the president to enact a federal version.  the new state bill, the california internet tax freedom act, imposes a moratorium on taxes for any internet activity, including online purchases and server accounts. under the act, internet companies that are based in california but do manufacturing in other states or ship their products to other states will be exempt from california sales tax.  industry analysts believe that the new measure is intended to help companies dependent on the internet create new products, services and jobs.  representatives of high-tech industries welcomed the new law.  "for california's economy and its citizens, growth in electronic commerce means new jobs," the american electronics association said in a statement. "by prohibiting any new taxes on the internet, we encourage the growth of electronic commerce and enhance the opportunities available for californians to find work in cyberspace or related service industries." larry mccarthy, president of the california taxpayers' association, said the new measure will help california retain its leadership in high-tech industry.

title: ibm develops new encryption system to protect internet communications
body: mathematicians at ibm zurich research laboratory and the swiss federal institute of technology (eth) announced monday that they have co-developed a new public-key cryptosystem that provides the first practical and mathematically proven way to secure information from even the most aggressive internet hacking attempts.  the new cramer-shoup cryptosystem, which is being revealed on the same day at the crypto'98 conference at the university of california-santa barbara, effectively closes the backdoor on so-called "active" attacks.  all current commercially available cryptosystems are potentially vulnerable to active attacks, which are considered to be the most dangerous hacking attempts any cryptosystem might face, ibm said in a press release.  "it's important that we nip this type of powerful attack in the bud," said victor shoup of ibm's zurich research laboratory, who invented the new cryptosystem with ronald cramer for the swiss federal institute of technology (eth).  "earlier this year, an active attack decoded information secured by the most widely used encryption system for web browsers. our system will prevent this from happening," he said.  ibm plans to incorporate the new system into a future version of its vault registry software, the ibm secureway public-key infrastructure product that allows e-commerce transactions to travel across organizational boundaries in a private, secure manner.  "active" attacks bypass the difficulty of solving the underlying mathematical problem by sending a series of cleverly constructed messages to a publicly accessible server.  by analyzing the server's pattern of responses to the bogus text, an attacker can decode encrypted messages passing through that network. the cramer-shoup method thwarts these attacks by delivering the first non-malleable cryptosystem efficient enough for commercial use.

title: china's commodity website booms
body: china's first official entry into electronic commerce has been highly successful and the nation enjoys a promising future related activities. the government website for commodities has recorded over 10 million hits since its opening in july. the internet website --http://www.chinamarket.com.cn -established by the ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation (moftec), was officiated on july 8 and has since blossomed into a major link providing information on commodities carrying the label "made in china". moftec's china international electronic commerce center (ciecc) administrator the website, which has attracted millions of hits from people in more than 80 countries and regions, including a record 470,000 hits in a single day. experts point to the fact that the highly successful beginning reflects the promising future for using advanced information technology to expand foreign trade. some 82.7 percent of the total hits to the website originated from abroad, with domestic hits accounting 17.3 percent of the total. the vast majority of inquiries centered on textile, electronic and hardware commodities. virtually, unknown companies, including a dyestuff company, an electromagnetic products manufacturer and a company producing clothing for babies received the most attention. small to medium-sized enterprises accounted for a majority of the 2,000 ventures linked to the website. a recent ciecc survey of 100 businesses linked to the website found that 72 percent of the ventures received clear feedbacks. one hangzhou trade company listed 14 textile commodities in july and has since received 10-odd favorable inquiries from japan, the republic of korea (rok), australia, the unitedstates and canada. the company manager expressed great satisfication with the response and noted that additional products will offered via the web market.

title: number of non-u.s. web users to skyrocket by2002: study
body: there will be approximately 100 million web users in the world by the end of this year and 320 million by 2002, according to a new study of the unitedstates research firm international data corporation (idc).  in the new report on the global market forecast for internet usage and commerce, idc said that the number of non-unitedstates users of the world wide web will increase more quickly over the next four years than the number of their unitedstates counterparts.  while the growth of web users and internet access devices will remain steady in the unitedstates, the real explosion in numbers will occur in the asia-pacific region between 1997 and 2002. other areas outside the unitedstates will also experience high growth, idc said.  idc said that there were 78.1 million devices used to access the web in 1997 worldwide. this number will jump to 515 million by 2002.  in 1997, there were 18 million people using the internet for shopping worldwide, the idc report said, and the number will increase dramatically to reach 128 million by 2002.  due to the huge increase in the number of web shoppers, idc predicted that more than 400 billion unitedstates dollars worth of goods and services will change hands over the internet by 2002, a compound annual growth rate of 103 percent between 1997 and 2002.  overall, the percentage of worldwide users buying good on the internet will increase from 26 percent in december 1997 to 40 percent in december 2002, idc said.

title: chinese firms conduct business via internet
body: zhao lunjie, who joined the internet just six month ago, today enjoys a flood of business inquiries and orders from scores of foreign companies.  "a short six months ago we were an unknown entity and seldom received orders," according to zhao, general manager of the shanghai lansheng golf equipment co. ltd. "the internet has enabled us to access the international market." over half of china's 15,000 medium-to large-sized state-owned enterprises are conducting business via the internet and a growing number of small firms are following suit, according to the state economic and trade commission.  experts noted that internest use by enterprises represents the third trend in the arrival of the information age in china, followed by the popularization of personal computers and establishment of information industry programs funded by the government.  foreign trade firms, the most enthusiastic users of the internet during the first six months of this year established numerous websites, more than 1,000 export firms attempted to promote sales using the website offered by the asian resources, a philippine-based trade intermediary.  the ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation set up the china market, a special website providing information on products, on july 1 this year.  "accessing the internet has greatly improved the international competitiveness of chinese firms," according to sarah benecke, president of asian resources.  chinese experts have pointed out that china's fledgling electronic information industry offers vast potential for development. moreover, they suggest the adoption of relevant laws and regulations covering security and fees, forms of taxation and the reduction of risks to the maximum, as well as the prevention of price wars and global problems currently confronting the industry.

title: toronto stock exchange issues internet guidelines
body: canada's largest stock exchange, the toronto stock exchange (tse), has issued a set of proposed guidelines for releasing stock-related information through the internet.  the guidelines are primarily intended to provide standards for information disseminated on the internet and aimed at investors.  they also suggest ways for companies to respond to rumors in chat groups or news groups.  the tse "recommends against a company participating in a chat or news group in order to dispel or clarify a rumor," the guidelines say.  instead, the company should tell the stock exchange's market surveillance unit.  if the data is false and influencing the share price, it should consider issuing a news release.  the tse also asks companies to "prohibit employees from participating in internet chat circles or news groups in talks relating to the company or its securities." it says all postings on company web sites must conform to tse and securities regulators' disclosure rules.  the stock exchange also recommends all information given to analysts and institutional investors be made available to all investors via the web, but promotional material should be excluded.

title: malaysia's state woos visitors with cyberdining
body: a cyberdining system was introduced in sarawak, the largest state of malaysia, thursday to woo not only tourists but also industrialists to invest in the state. cyberdining, which enables hotel and restaurant reservation to be made through the internet, could put sarawak on the international map by encouraging not only tourists but also industrialists to visit the state, the state's industrial development minister abang johari tun abang openg said thursday. this latest electronic technology can be an enticement for industrialists to invest in sarawak, he said in the state's capital of kuching thursday while launching kuching hilton's cyberdining on-line fax reservation system, malaysia's national news agency bernama reported. "the website is not only an excellent source of information for potential visitors to our cities, visiting tourists and locals but also promotes our country's colorful and diverse food industry," he said. hilton kuching is the first hotel of more than 150 establishments in malaysia to utilize the internet facility. the e-system allows a person anywhere to make reservations through the hotel's six food and beverage (fb) outlets's web pages which can be accessed at malaysia's premier fb electronic directory and comes up with the estimated price of selections from the interactive menu. cyberdining located at http://www.cyberdining.net is a project of vensara sdn bhd, a sarawak-based internet development company, whose membership currently covers only restaurants, cafes, pubs, bars and lounges in kuching and the federal capital city of kuala lumpur.

title: nigeria to set up panel on millennium bug
body: the nigerian government will soon set up a national committee on the global computer problem known as the millennium bug, the head of state, general abdulsalam abubakar has said.  abubakar made the statement in a written speech read at a national workshop on the millennium bug wednesday in nigerian capital abuja, according to media reports thursday.  abubakar said the government has approved one billion naira (about 10 million unitedstates dollars) as initial take-off grant for the proposed committee.  the committee, he said, would facilitate the rectification of all government computers and also provide necessary assistance to the private sector.  abubakar expressed the government's determination to solve the problem by the end of june next year.  he also sought the cooperation of the private sector in funding the activities of the committee, saying the cost is too high for the government to bear alone.  abubakar reiterated his administration's resolve to attain self-reliance in the computer industry within the shortest possible time, saying provisions would be made in next year's budget for the establishment of a pilot scheme in collaboration with the private sector for local manufacture of computer components and units.  he lamented the difficulties encountered by nigerians in gaining access to the internet, disclosing that the government had directed the federal ministry of science and technology and that of communications to collaborate with the nigerian internet group to develop proper guidelines for internet connectivity in three months.

title: australian stocks close slightly weaker
body: the australian stock market ended marginally lower monday.  brokers described the day's trade as lackluster overall and said the two companies' (resources giant bhp and global media company news corp) better performance was the main reason for the steady outcome.  the all ordinaries index ended 1.6 points lower at 2597.4, the all resources gained 3.4 to 995.8, but the all industrials fell 6.9 to 4579.1.  overall, 395.17 million shares were traded worth 676.7 million unitedstates dollars, falling stocks beat rises by 563 to 410.  the market opened lower despite a 20.3 rise on the dow jones industrial average overnight to 8598.0, on fears that asian markets would fall monday.  resource stocks were boosted by a resilient bhp, which put on 28 cents to 13.48 australian dollars by the close, with rio tinto off 11 cents to 17.92 australian dollars.  the banking index tumbled 43.4 points to 5792.4, with all majors softer at the close.  national australia bank slid 20.7 cents to 22.04 australian dollars, anz bank slipped 16 cents to 9.90 australian dollars, westpac bank surrendered 3.9 cents to 10.111 australian dollars and the commonwealth bank of australia gave up 11 cents to 19.80 australian dollars.  the gold index eased 3.2 points to 990.8, with the spot price of the precious metal at the close in sydney at 285.60 unitedstates dollars an ounce, down 45 unitedstates cents from friday's close.

title: mysteries of science to be discussed at california universities
body: discussions and debates on some exciting and controversial new issues in science and medicine will be presented next weekend on three california university campuses.  according to the program posted on the internet at the wonderfest 98 web site, 33 researchers will speak at 15 separate events on the campuses of stanford university, the university of california at berkeley and san francisco.  among the 15 compelling scientific questions to be discussed at wonderfest 98 are: do genes largely determine human behavior? is the search for extraterrestrial intelligence dangerous? is alternative medicine worthy of further research? how is the quest for artificial intelligence progressing? and can human longevity be markedly increased?  ninety-minute presentations of each topic will be divided into three equal segments for introductory background remarks, debates and questions from the audience.  highlighting the values of debate at the festival of science, the program contends that intellectual competition inspires enthusiasm and promotes excellence.  "debate conveys the human/emotional side of science, and it entrusts listeners with the responsibility of making up their own minds," it said.  speakers at the festival will include physicists, astrophysicists, astronomers, computer scientists, molecular biologists, neurologists, psychologists and neurophysiologists.

title: nigeria's national phone firm to offer internet service
body: the nigerian telecommunications ltd. (nitel) is going into internet services in the next few weeks, according to a nitel official.  tayo ekundayo, deputy manager of the national telephone firm, said at the weekend that nitel has completed arrangements for the start of its internet services.  nitel, which has already completed its two megabits per second gateway handled by the german firm siemens, will revolutionize the speed and real-time delivery of internet services in nigeria, the guardian newspaper reported monday.  ekundayo denied that nitel wanted to edge out other internet services providers (isp) in nigeria.  nitel management has earlier demanded that all isps should pay 10,000 naira (about 120 unitedstates dollars) monthly for each receiving line they have subscribed to for their internet services, otherwise they will be disconnected.  nitel's demand is based on the fact that the over 800 telephones lines acquired individually by isps, under originating and receiving calls agreement, have been converted into "dedicated lines," contrary to the terms of agreement in their application letters.  nitel management, therefore, insisted that "by simply dedicating those lines as receiver only, there is already a violation of our agreement because our exchanges are configured to make and receive calls and not permanently on receiver only." internet operators, however, challenged that elsewhere in the world, internet service providers are even given some discounts by telephone companies as incentives for hooking on to their system.  "this formed the basis of petition to the head of state against nitel," one operator said.  nitel management, however, argued that it is not discouraging internet development in nigeria.  ekundayo said internet operators charge 80,000 naira (about 940 dollars) annually on its customers in addition to usage charges, while they only pay nitel 105 naira (about 1.2 unitedstates dollars) per month for each line.  what nitel asks from the internet operators "who hijacked so many digital telephone lines" is only 10,000 naira to help maintain the lines and exchanges, said the deputy manager.  on the allegation that nitel rakes in a substantial revenue from internet users, he said there are corporate bodies like hotels, banks and oil companies who pay as much as two million naira (about 24,000 unitedstates dollars) a month per telephone line.  he further said that some internet operators have already complied with nitel's directive, so there is no reason why others should decline.  however, toyin ogunseinde, the marketing manager of ross claytom, one of the signatories to the series of petitions against nitel, said that the nigeria internet group, an umbrella body for the operators, is only responsible to the nigerian communications commission (ncc).  if ncc is alive to its duties, it should call nitel to order, ogundeinde said, adding that "we did not obtain our licenses to operate internet services from nitel, so we know that there will soon be a compromise one way or the other."
