body: sixty-eight percent of american parents are concerned about their children being exposed to potentially harmful material on the internet, ranging from pornography to manipulative email from direct marketers, said a study released tuesday.  the study, based on a consumer survey and conducted by research firm nfo interactive, indicates that parents also are wary of their children interacting with strangers in chat rooms on the internet.  in addition, a high percentage of parents are taking active measures to limit what their children do online: sixty-six percent of them do not allow their children to give out personal information; about 62 percent prohibit online shopping; and 54 percent take steps to prevent children from accessing adult entertainment sites, according to the study, which was released at a conference in san francisco on children's online issues.  another study released at the conference ranked children's most common activities on the net: email topped the ranks, followed by chat, general web surfing, homework and games.  the top two most accessed services on the internet --email and chat --also were the two greatest concerns among parents.

title: american parents worry about net safety for children
body: more than half the american parents with web-surfing children are willing to pay for services that police internet content and chat rooms for material, a new study shows.  the study, based on a consumer survey, was conducted by the research firm, nfo interactive, and announced tuesday at a conference in san francisco on children's online issues.  the results reflect the heightened fear among parents over what their children are doing on the internet, and what material they are receiving by email.  sixty-eight percent of parents are concerned about their children being exposed to potentially harmful material on the internet, ranging from pornography to manipulative email from direct marketers.  parents also are wary of their children interacting with strangers in chat rooms, the report said.  also, a high percentage of parents are taking active measures to limit what their children do online.  the study shows 66 percent of them do not allow their children to give out personal information; about 62 percent prohibit online shopping; and 54 percent take steps to prevent children from accessing adult entertainment sites.  reported at the conference was another study which ranked children's most common activities on the net.  email topped the ranks, followed by general web surfing, homework, games and chat.  the top two most accessed services on the internet --email and chat --were also the two greatest concerns among parents.  speakers at the conference urged parents to demonstrate greater awareness.  "it's as much a parent's responsibility as to whether or not they should let their kids watch violent films," one speaker said.  they also urged both companies and parents to find common ground.  so far net companies have continually maintained a vocal stance for self-governance, and have been on the defensive about government intervention into their online privacy practices.

title: australian stocks weaken after lackluster ny session
body: a lackluster new york session overnight and local profit-taking, particularly in media giant news corp., conspired tuesday to push the australian bourse lower.  the benchmark all ordinaries index finished 14.2 points softer at 2,582.6.  the dow jones industrial average dipped just 1.74 points overnight to 8,711.13 in a quiet session of trade.  "new york offered no inspiration. i think news corp. continued to come off in profit-taking, similar to what happened in the unitedstates last night," one brisbane-based broker said.  "i also think we're seeing some tax-loss selling where investors are looking to offset some big gains made on the market over the financial year." the all industrials sector dropped 28 points to 4,501.4 while the all resources fell 2.7 to 1,039.2.  fellow market newcomer amp shed 34 cents to 19.68 australian dollars as its price retreated toward the company's share facility price of 18.7 revealed on sunday.  news corp. slid 40 cents to 10.93 australian dollars as its preferred scrip also forfeited 40 cents, woolworths slipped 10 cents, lend lease ended steady and coca-cola amatil lost 3.9 cents.  the gold index tumbled 27.6 points, or 2.5 percent, to 1,062, despite the precious metal selling 50 cents stronger at 295.2 unitedstates dollars an ounce.  only one of the big four banks defied the general market trend.  cba improved 8 cents, westpac eased 16, anz shed 10 and nab ended 11.2 lower.  national turnover was 361.28 million at a value of 1.03 billion australian dollars (628.3 million unitedstates dollars), as falls outnumbered rises 636 to 476.

title: china to export technology via internet
body: china's ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation (moftec) plans to link the nation's first virtual technology export market to the internet (moftec) via the "made-in-china" commodity market net launched last month.  moftec has granted approval to over 2,000 businesses and research institutes to display their technology on the online "china technology fair" which will be introduced august 12 on the ministry's official website, according to the china international electronic commerce center (ciecc), the server.  the organizer expects the site to offer some 3,000 technology items.  experts said that many chinese companies and businesses have the capability to export technology but are nonetheless often perplexed by the lack of information, high costs, the lack of sales channel and unclear market positioning.  moftec notes the vast potential to increase the export volume for key technological products such as computers and telecommunications, electronic and biological products which currently account for a mere 5.3 percent of china's total exports.  officials from the moftec science and technology department, host of the online fair, is placing great hope on the fact that the electronic-business system will enhance the efficiency for transmitting information and reduce the cost of data exchanges.  the goal of the "china technology fair", another e-business project sponsored by moftec, centers on reducing costs while greatly expanding the market recognition of domestic technology.  foreign experts point out that e-business, a method of "deals done via electronic mail", takes full advantage of a shorter trade process and the prompt response from the market and customers.  the united nations trade and development organization estimated that the transaction volume for global e-business will hit 200 billion unitedstates dollars by the year 2000.  moftec has announced that all import and export businesses will be required to apply to the ciecc for quota certificate by the year 2000. the ministry completed extensive testing of an application network in east china's shandong province last october, with assessment completed and the system accepted at the end of may.  the ciecc, established in 1996, is china's sole nationwide network for the e-business network for foreign trade linked to the internet.  various foreign companies have targeted the e-business market in china. for example, ibm has focused its development strategy on providing small-to medium-sized chinese enterprises with useful information technology.

title: geneva to host eighth annual internet society conference
body: the swiss city of geneva will host the eighth annual internet society conference scheduled on july 21-24, the organizers announced here friday.  one of the major issues at the so-called internet summit will be the future of the internet's domain naming system.  representatives from more than 120 countries are expected to discuss the next major steps needed to assist in the definition and development of a non-profit corporation, internet assigned names authority (iana).  the organizers expect that about 3,000 stakeholders, policy makers and internet leaders around the world will be attending the conference.  to help promote the internet in the developing countries, a special symposium will be held on the matter during the meeting.  "hands-on" training will be given to professionals who will play a vital role in establishing the internet's presence in their countries or facilitating the efforts of schools, government agencies, businesses, and residents to learn about and exploit internet services.  as the conference is not a purely technical one, 11 tutorials will be set up to help visitors understand the internet.  the internet society is a unitedstates-based non-profitable international organization. since 1992, it has served as the international organization for global coordination and cooperation on the internet, promoting and maintaining a broad spectrum of activities focused on the internet's development, availability and associated technologies.  the first internet society conference was held in 1991, when an estimated four million people had access to the internet.

title: china's image has improved since hk's return: poll
body: china's image has been improved by the way it has managed hongkong in the last year, according to the majority of respondents to the latest asian executives poll, carried out jointly by the far eastern economic review and cnbc asia.  a majority of asian executives (51 percent) say china is viewed in a better light since hongkong returned to china on july 1, 1997.  in hongkong, 76 percent of those polled say china's image has improved.  overall, 63 percent across the region say closer sino-american ties would be good for asia-wide security.  when asked the same question last year, 58 percent thought improved ties would boost security.  the asian executives poll is a weekly fax poll conducted by the far eastern economic review and cnbc asia. respondents are chairman, managing directors and other top corporate executives in 10 asian countries and regions.  singapore-based cnbc asia is a service of dow jones and company, publisher of the wall street journal, and national broadcasting corporation (nbc) is one of the leading television networks in the unitedstates. wholly owned by dow jones and company, the far eastern economic review is asia's first regional publication.

title: handheld devices to overtake pcs for net access, says idc
body: cheap devices for mass-market internet access will supplant desktop computers within the next six years, according to a unitedstates information technology market researcher.  in a report released tuesday, international data corp. (idc) predicted demand for handheld devices will nearly triple in annual volume from 1997 to 2002, and exceed pc unit sales by 2004 or 2005.  in a previous report, idc said that 1998 should be a banner growth year for the smart handheld device market as unit shipments are expected to hit 8.2 million worldwide. the projected growth represents a 61 percent increase over estimated 1997 unit shipments of 5.1 million units.  without hinting that the pc will fade away, the tuesday report, however, indicated that as prices of simple devices like handheld units, web-enabled phones or set-top boxes fall below 100 unitedstates dollars, they will become more popular than pcs.  some industry watchers say that the low-cost internet device will replace the pc simply because pc these days provide more computer power than most people need. but they predict that cheap access devices will proliferate until people find more compelling reasons to browse the internet.  an idc analyst said that even at a low price under 1,000 dollars, people won't have three, four or five pcs around their houses. people want to go online without having to go to the pc room --they want to use it wherever they are.  idc predicts pc makers will eventually get into the low-cost internet device market, or risk missing a passing wave.  indeed, a new wave of technologies and designs has resulted in more and more smart handheld devices. apart from letting users cruise the internet, they can keep phone number lists and calendars and send and receivers email. most handheld devices weigh less than a pound and fit into a jacket pocket. but the keyboards on most units are too small to comfortably write much more than a short message. in addition, improvements are also called to make the screens brighter.

title: thirty percent canadian households communicate by computer
body: nearly three out of 10 canadians households had at least one member who used a computer every month to communicate, statistics canada said wednesday.  according to the statistics agency's survey done last october, 35 percent of households in alberta had at least one member who had used some form of computer communication each month, the largest proportion of any canadian provinces.  communicating by computer, whether it was for email, electronic banking or surfing the internet, was more common in households with young people.  at least one person used a computer regularly to communicate in 38 percent of households in which there was someone under the age of 18, compared with only 25 percent of households in which there was no one under 18.  canadians were most likely to use a computer to communicate at their workplace, which was followed by the home, schools and public libraries.  of those households that typically used computer communications every month, 84 percent reported using this modern tool to search for information on the internet, the agency said.  meanwhile, some 83 percent said they used them for email.  about one third had someone using computers to communicate from home for employer-related business.  the survey also indicates that 15 percent of households used the internet from home in a typical month of communicating, compared with 14 percent in may, 1997.

title: big companies hesitant to commit to public internet
body: a new study shows that big companies are still hesitant to commit to public internet because of concerns about its reliability and security.  without a common set of specifications, technologies and products which guarantee a level of security and reliability businesses require, the internet may simply become an interesting public access network, international data corp.(idc) said in a report released on monday.  the information technology market researcher surveyed an unidentified number of multinational corporations, including those in retail, financial services, telecommunications, computer equipment and mail-order industries. each of them employed more than 19,000 workers, with average annual revenues of 1.5 billion unitedstates dollars.  according to the study, there has been a tremendous return on investment for companies that have developed intranets, in-house web sites that serve the employees of the enterprises, and extranet, web sites for existing customers rather than the general public, to reduce costs and increase productivity. meanwhile, new revenues have been realized by companies pioneering internet commerce.  but the findings also indicate that the phenomenal business growth in the internet may plateau because of the failure of technology standards to meet business requirements, idc said.  there is a danger that the internet will not complete its promise as a business infrastructure opening up new markets and encouraging new ways of doing business, idc said.

title: australian stocks close down on currency, interest rate concerns
body: the australian stock market wednesday closed weaker on concerns over the downward pressure on the australian dollar and fears that interest rates could rise.  the all ordinaries index closed down 31 points, or 1.18 percent, at 2,592.9, but off its low of 2,582.9.  the all resources index closed 7.1 points weaker at 1,061.2 and the all industrials index was 59.7 points lower at 4,501.0.  the australian dollar at the end of local trading was worth 58.32 unitedstates cents, down from 59.81 unitedstates cents at the previous session close, and off an intraday low of 58.09 unitedstates cents.  ausbil xiradis, a funds manager, said the australian dollar was "probably getting close to its bottom" and "it appears that there is not going to be any change to interest rates" by the reserve bank of australia, the central bank.  he said this had helped the market pick up off its low in the afternoon session with news corp. leading the way.  market heavyweight news corp. gained 14 cents, or 1.40 percent, to 10.14 australian dollars and its preferred scrip gained 9 cents, or 1.03 percent, to 8.82 australian dollars.  brokers said that because news corp. earned a significant amount in the unitedstates it was relatively insulated by the downward pressure on the australian dollar.  national australia bank shares dropped 45.1 cents, or 2.07 percent, to 21.303 australian dollars, commonwealth bank of australia fell 27 cents, or 1.50 percent, to 17.73 australian dollars, and anz banking corp. slipped 18 cents, or 1.66 percent, to 10.67 australian dollars.  but westpac banking corp. rose 5 cents, or 0.52 percent, to 9.60 australian dollars, with brokers saying the bank had bucked the trend because it had recently gone ex-dividend and been oversold.  "the stock has come back fairly savagely since it went ex-dividend," said xiradis, adding that westpac's share buyback scheme could have contributed.  major resource stocks finished mixed, with australia's leading company bhp closing down 10 cents at 13.44 australian dollars, and global miner rio tinto falling two cents to 19.65 australian dollars.  the gold index gained 1.9 points to 1,126.1.  gold bullion closed 4.75 unitedstates dollars lower at 290.75 unitedstates dollars in sydney trading. it was trading at 291.55 unitedstates dollars at midday.  national turnover was 338.78 million shares valued at 629.8 million unitedstates dollars, with falls easily outnumbering rises by 874 to 376, and 419 stocks were steady.

title: china plans to use internet to shop for hollywood movies
body: this past monday, china opened a website on the internet that it can use to place orders for hollywood movies.  the site is on chinacue, the internet designation for art topics, which will be used by the hollywood classics co. ltd. the first group of movies will be new ones from the 1990s and some 1940s classics.  the site also provides information about movies and shows not currently available. but some chinese surfers have been already watching western movies with the help of the site known as yahoo.  several european companies will also enter the chinese market through the new site, providing copyrights to chinese film and tv producers.  the new website was set up by the china federation of literary and art circles and the beijing telegraph bureau and is the best place for chinese and foreign artists to share their views and a place for chinese to learn about more things from abroad, according to the federation's shao mujun.  analysts say that the website is the effect of the combination of a market economy and technology, and china's opening up. the commercialization of culture is now common in china, and money-losing state film studios and artists and publishers are all urging that an easy information channel be created.  minister of culture sun jiazheng says that contacts with foreigners should be increased because culture has become a popular means of improving sino-foreign relations.  analysts say that the internet will have a complicated and profound impact on culture. but, chinese artists and writers are new to the electronic age, especially when compared with the fields of commerce, education, and science, and the number of internet users is small.  one commentator, yan peng, says, "there are no walls on the internet. we are therefore more directly, quickly and widely faced with various cultures in the world. that will bring happiness, and unexpected ideological shocks."

title: more americans reading news on internet
body: the percentage of americans getting news from the internet at least once a week more than tripled in the past two years --going from 11 million to 36 million news users.  most people use the internet to supplement, not replace, their traditional sources of news, according to a new study by pew research center, an independent opinion research group that studies attitudes toward press, politics and public policy issues.  for those who go online, science, health, finance and technology are big news draws, said the survey of 3,002 adults.  despite dramatic growth in online news consumption, cable television's impact remains far greater. fully 40 percent of americans now regularly watch one of the cable news networks, whose advantage lies in its immediacy. americans say that they would turn to cable channels first in the event of a big news story, whether it concerned politics, health or sports.  the survey found that 46 percent of americans only follow national news when something major is happening, and 63 percent of the people react the same to international news. only local news attracts a large regular audience that is not event driven --61 percent of americans follow it most of the time.  while accuracy and timeliness are the news values most important to consumers, the study found that a large segment of the news audience wants entertaining and enjoyable news presented by personalities who deliver it in a caring way.  illustrating how differently the generations are responding to the information explosion, the polling found that only 33 percent of americans ages 18-29 keep up with the news a lot, but 77 percent like having so many information sources. in contrast, 68 percent of seniors like following in the news, but only 52 percent like all the television news shows, magazines and computer information services at their disposal today.

title: roundup: thailand cracks down on world cup gambling
body: as the world cup matches are approaching, thai police have launched a clamp-down on soccer gambling operators who are set to earn an estimated 30 billion baht (about 730 million unitedstates dollars).  this is part of a nationwide campaign against gambling that has been on the rise in the recent years. police feared that the world cup would add fuel to the gambling fever.  police said gambling fever has spread everywhere --from private firms to government offices and from schools to local banks.  with such huge stakes being bet, the notorious underground lottery bookmakers have temporarily shifted their focus towards soccer.  police estimated that each gambler in bangkok alone would spend an average of 38,880 baht (about 948 dollars) to bet the upcoming world cup matches, 35 percent more than the sum during the 1994 world cup.  thailand's central investigation bureau deputy commissioner maj. gen. chat kuldilok acknowledged that lots of lottery bookmakers had taken up soccer gambling because more money is being spent on this sport.  chat told reporters that police chief gen. pracha promnok had instructed the police to set up special squads to crack down on the gambling-related businesses.  "we have asked police in each jurisdiction to come up with a list of people who are involved in the gambling business," chat said.  but he said clamping-down on such an illegal business was a daunting task.  the police department is seeking cooperation from banks, the education ministry, university affairs ministry and the mass media to help monitor the situation.  chat said he had requested the banks to check on "suspicious" transfers of large amounts of money among their customers.  "as for the media, we plead with them not to tacitly support gambling. i know some of them even suggest betting prices," he said, referring to newspaper columns which provide insights into soccer matches.  web sites available for gambling on the internet also pose a challenge to police. education ministry officials disclosed that soccer gambling is very popular among students who have easy access to web sites. police have difficulty chasing and locating such "internet gamblers".  the education ministry has instructed teachers and rectors of schools, colleges and universities to help prevent students from using the internet to bet on soccer games.  schools in bangkok have set up campus patrols in a bid to bar students from sneaking out of their classrooms to wander around shopping centers, computer game shops and theaters to bet on soccer matches during the world cup, a lecturer at chulalongkhon university in bangkok said.  "student patrols are not enough to deal with these students, so we would like to ask shops to cooperate with us as well," said the lecturer, who refused to be named.  a lottery bookmaker, who gave his name only as wad, said in an interview that since the number of his customers "is increasing rapidly", he had to expand his network by setting up a special pub. he said however that the pub is exclusively for "old" and "loyal" customers.  he said most of his customers are middle-aged and normally opt to bet 10,000 baht (244 unitedstates dollars) on each match.  "we have already screened our customers, so there shouldn't be any problem. we bet just for fun and most of our clients are financially sound. we are not destroying the country, or the cash flow in thailand,' wad said.  but a police officer, who preferred to be called paitoon, said gambling is eroding social morals and destabilizes the society.  "we must crack down on this illegal act for the sake of thailand," said paitoon, who is a member of an anti-gambling squad.

title: clinton calls for computer-literated students
body: unitedstates president bill clinton said friday that all the american students should be computer-literate before they reach high school and all children should share in high-tech opportunities.  "all students should feel as comfortable with a keyboard as a chalkboard, as comfortable with a laptop as a textbook," the president told 2,400 graduates at the massachusetts institute of technology.  "it is critical to insuring that they all have opportunity in the world of the 21st century," said clinton who was campaigning for his goal of wiring all classrooms to the internet by the year 2000.  "we shouldn't let a child graduate from middle school anymore without knowing how to use new technologies to learn," clinton said.  ten states already have such a requirement for high school graduation, but clinton said the same standard should be applied for younger children.  the president proposed to provide each middle school with 20,000 unitedstates dollar federal assistance over three years to promote high-tech literacy. that means the federal government will budget 180 million dollars for the program between fiscal 2000 and fiscal 2002.  clinton targeted that more than half of the nation's classrooms will be linked with the internet within a year. and as a promotion, he urged telecommunications companies to continue providing favorable services to poor schools, libraries and rural health centers.  clinton acknowledged that there is a gap between rich and poor children in technology opportunities in the unitedstates. but he said every child in america deserves a chance to participate in the information revolution.  he said affluent schools are nearly three times as likely as poorer schools to have internet access in the classroom and white students are more than twice as likely as blacks to have computers in their homes.  "unequal education hardens into unequal prospects," clinton said, urging private companies to invest in a school, embrace a community in need, and endow an eager young mind with opportunity.

title: miga launches privatization information service for investors
body: the multilateral investment guarantee agency (miga) monday announced the launch of privatizationlink, an internet-based information service for firms seeking to invest in the private sector of the emerging economies. the service will initially cover selected countries in central and eastern europe, central asia and sub-saharan africa, later expanding to include other regions. privatizationlink provides on-line access to business profiles of state-owned companies and assets currently for sale, along with details of the relevant laws, regulations and procedures governing these transactions. access to privatizationlink is free at http://www.privatizationlink,com. first-time users are required to register with the service. privatizationlink is a specialized facility within the investment promotion network (ipanet), the miga's on-line information clearinghouse for companies engaged in cross-border investment, which has been in operation since 1995. the miga, established in 1988, is a member of the world bank group. its mandate is to encourage foreign direct investment into developing countries by providing long-term guarantees against political risks, and by offering investment marketing services to host developing countries.

title: 1 million australians use internet at home: survey
body: one in every 18 australians, or 1 million australian residents, used the internet at home early this year, compared with 250,000 two years earlier, the australian bureau of statistics said here thursday.  according to figures released by the bureau, householders were still reluctant to buy over internet, with only about 207,000 people having made private purchases online in the 12 months to february, and only 170,000 paying online.  "only 44,000 persons are estimated to have used the internet to pay other bills or transfer funds in the last three months," the bureau said in its "use of the internet by householders." the total number of personal computers in australia is estimated at 6.9 million.  the bureau also found about 3 million australians aged 18 years or older had used the internet in the 12 months to february; 1.3 million from work, 1 million from home and 1.5 million from a friend or neighbor's house, a school or university or a public library.  having created an information economy ministry to oversee the internet and information industries last year, the australian government has been encouraging the use of internet and electronic commerce by government departments, business and individuals in a bid to improve efficiency and competitiveness.

title: australian sharemarkets ends higher after afternoon surge
body: australian shares enjoyed a rare afternoon surge to close one percent higher thursday after buying interest was revived by a recovery on the hongkong market.  the all ordinaries index closed 27.6 points firmer at 2714.6.  the all industrials index gained 56.9 to 4722.6 and the all resources put up 2.4 to 1101.0.  brokers attributed the rise to the revival in the hongkong market in the afternoon and the implications that held for wall street thursday night.  dicksons broker jon hancock said : " the expectation here is now that the unitedstates market will rise strongly tonight." the local main index started the day up 6.6 points and was up only 5.4 points by midday.  the strength in the local share market was reflected among most of the majors with particularly strong rises in the news corp shares, banks, retailers and some building materials companies.  news corp ordinary shares ended 28 cents higher and the preferred shares gained 17.5 cents.  banking shares also made strong gains with the sub-index up 86.8 points at 5899.0.  national australia bank rose 40.4 cents, anz climbed 32, commonwealth firmed 29 and westpac grew 13.8 cents.  retailer woolworths jumped 17 cents on expectations that retail sales figures due out on monday will be positive.  bhp closed four cents higher at 13.54 australian dollars. rio tinto firmed 15, wmc climbed 0.7.  the gold index lost 22 points to 1182.6. gold stocks defied the 1.30 unitedstates dollar rise in bullion to 293.50 an ounce to close.  overall 302.3 million shares changed hands worth 904.6 million australian dollars (560.85 million unitedstates dollars). falling stocks shaded rising stocks by 632 to 556.

title: fsa issues guidance on investment advertisements
body: the financial services authority (fsa) thursday issued guidance on investment advertisements on the internet.  the guidance concerns advertisements from overseas on internet sites which may be accessed by uk investors even though the advertisements are not targeted at them.  the fsa hopes that the guidance will enable financial services companies overseas to comply with uk regulation, and therefore minimize the likelihood of fsa enforcement action in this area.  the internet enables uk investors to access investment advertisements put onto the world wide web from anywhere in the world.  it is understood that while this increases the amount of information available to uk investors, it also carries the risk that the provisions in the financial services act (fs act), which are designed to protect investors from misleading or inaccurate information, might be evaded.  the protection is the requirement that an investment advertisement in the uk is issued by an authorized person or approved by such a person. breach of this provision is a criminal offense.  the fsa does not have the power to amend the fs act but does have discretion as to when and how it uses its enforcement powers.  the guidance expands on the fsa's enforecement approach towards possible breaches of this provision in the fs act.

title: mci sells internet unit to british firm
body: mci communications inc., the second largest telecommunication provider in the unitedstates, announced thursday that it is selling its internet business to britain's cable wireless plc for 625 million unitedstates dollars in a cash deal.  this move is made to clear the way for its pending merger to worldcom inc. of the unitedstates, analysts said.  the sale comes amid intense scrutiny of the proposed 37 billion unitedstates dollar merger between mci and worldcom. european and unitedstates officials fear that the merger would concentrate too much control of the internet in the combined company's hands. the two companies hope to complete their merger sometime this summer.  worldcom's uunet technologies division is the top provider of high-speed internet hook-ups through a global computer that makes up the "backbone" of internet communication. mci, an early entrant into the internet business, is number two. selling mci's internet backbone would eliminate an overlap with worldcom's internet business, thus making it easier to get the approval of the government.  according to press reports, cable wireless will take control of mci's contracts with internet service providers, but mci's residential and non-isp customers are not affected.

title: chinese web guides to increase internet usage by chinese speakers
body: with powerful new web guides and search engines providing chinese speakers around the world with an easier and more relevant web experience, the use of chinese on the internet is poised to grow fast, according to yahoo, a popular web guide.  jerry yang, co-founder of yahoo inc, said here wednesday that high-quality navigational guides such as the company's recently launched yahoo chinese site would greatly boost the use of chinese language services on the internet by making it much easier for users to find specific sites and research topics.  "without a solid guide to chinese web sites, it's often difficult for chinese users to find sites related to a specific interest," said yang, who co-created the yahoo internet navigational guide in april 1994 and co-founded yahoo inc. a year later.  "if an individual is searching for a topic in chinese or if a source is only available in chinese, standard english language web guides and search engines may not provide any or the most relevant results," said the young entrepreneur who was born in taiwan and brought up in the unitedstates.  launched on may 5, yahoo chinese catalogues more than 10,000 chinese-language web sites into 14 browsable categories allowing users to conduct comprehensive search in both simplified and traditional chinese characters.  yang said yahoo chinese would be a useful tool for chinese web surfers anywhere in the world.  according to relevant knowledge, an internet consultancy, yahoo was the most frequently accessed web site in the unitedstates last month with around 32 million users, ahead of netscape and microsoft.

title: more pcs in u.s. hooked to internet
body: nearly 45 million personal computers in the unitedstates regularly accessed the internet in the first quarter, a 43 percent jump from a year ago.  zd market intelligence, a california-based research company, reported that a total of 10 million pcs in the unitedstates were used for shopping on the internet, for electronic goods and services.  these included 5.7 million pcs for buying a pc or related products, 3.9 million for other consumer electronics products and nearly 7.7 million for other consumer products or services.  this compares with 3.7 million pcs being used to buy products and services over the internet a year ago, the company said.  in addition, netscape communications, the major internet browser maker, lost more share of the unitedstates internet browser market to microsoft as of january, the company said.  although microsoft is now involved in an antitrust lawsuit, its internet explorer's market share nearly doubled to 39 percent from 21 percent in january 1997, the company said.  the total share of unitedstates pcs using the netscape's navigator browser fell to 54 percent in january, from 63 percent a year ago.  including both navigator and communicator, a total of 24.2 million pcs in the unitedstates used a netscape browser as of january, a 33 percent increase from 18.2 million a year ago.  microsoft's ie was used in 17.3 million pcs as of january, an increase of 182 percent, it said.

title: survey reveals information on china's internet users
body: based on china's first national survey on the internet, the country had 820,000 internet subscribers by the end of march with 78.5 percent of them at the ages between 21 and 35.  the survey shows that computer technicians and educational and scientific research workers account for more than half of the internet users in china. "the connection of the number of users with their professions is a unique phenomena in the preliminary stage of internet development," said mao wei, director of the china internet information center, sponsor of the survey.  according to the survey, 65 percent of the users have a monthly salary below 1,000 yuan (120.48 unitedstates dollars), while those making 1,000-to-2,000 yuan make up 32 percent.  geographically speaking, beijing has the largest group of internet subscribers, accounting for 36 percent; guangdong province comes in second with 8.3 percent; and shanghai, third with 8 percent.  the survey also shows that 46.7 percent of the users are at public expense, while 25.3 percent pay for the net out of their own pocket.  as many as 80.4 percent of the respondents said they use the internet primarily to obtain information about science and technology; 42 percent seek social news; 39.6 percent want commercial information; and 24.8 percent look for entertainment and daily-life knowledge.  as for problems concerning the internet, 49.1 percent of those surveyed complained that it is too slow; 36.2 percent said the price is too high; and 7.3 percent said the information in chinese is insufficient.  the survey also shows that 6,459 chinese departments and enterprises have opened their own web sites on the internet, with 64 percent of those being commercial units.

title: u.s. phone company to offer high-speed internet service
body: pacific bell, a subsidiary local telephone company of sbc communications, announced wednesday that it plans to offer high-speed internet service this summer.  the service, to be available to more than a third of its customers across california, will use existing phone lines and move data at up to 30 times faster than today's computer modems.  behind the new service is a new technology known as asymmetric digital subscriber line, or adsl, which is designed primarily for internet and telecommuting, namely home office, applications.  packaged with internet service, adsl provides on-line consumers and small businesses with accelerated access to the world wide web.  in addition, as a stand-alone connection, adsl allows telecommuting employees and after-hours home workers to connect their employers' corporate networks via dedicated, secure links.  pacific bell had been moving cautiously to deploy the new technology in its service area covering over 13.4 million business and residential customers.  after a year-long test and a lengthy market trial, it plans to charge home users 89 unitedstates dollars per month and businesses up to 339 dollars per month for the service, including internet access.  the company already offers the high-speed service in parts of the san francisco bay area, with monthly prices ranging from about 160 dollars to 400 dollars.  to be eligible for the new service, users must be within about 5 kilometers of one of its offices in 63 cities. the deployment will start expanding in june, company officials said, and should be finished by late august or september.  to use adsl technology, a new modem would be required, and the phone company would need to install new equipment. once installed, adsl is always on and consumers would never need to dial their internet service provider again. also, people can talk on the phone and surf the web at the same time on the same line.

title: business on the internet set for big boom: report
body: the amount of business done over the internet is set to undergo a period of explosive growth, according to a report from the uk deloitte touche consulting group.  within two years, many businesses would be counducting more than half of their transactions over the internet as electronic commerce grows by 300 percent, the report said.  the survey polled more than 1,000 chief information officers in six major industries in 25 countries. asked about their expectations for e-commerce, most said they thought it would explode.  this explosion will bring many businesses and consumers into regular contact with the internet for the first time, marking the long-awaited arrival of e-commerce as an accepted way of doing business.  so far, the benefits of e-commerce are largely unrealised, but that is about to change. the most rapid growth is likely to be in the area of consumer transactions, where people and businesses actually use the web to order goods.  banking, retailing and energy are already aggressively embracing the new business medium, along with the public sector.  however, the report showed that the growth of the number of transactions over the internet in north america is likely to be twice that in europe, further extending the lead that u.s companies have in the field of e-commerce.

title: chinese ministry joins internet for new market outlet
body: chinese companies now have a new place to display their goods --made-in-china --a site on the internet that is linked to the ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation's web site at http://www.moftec.gov.cn, according to moftec's vice-minister liu shanzai a dozen enterprises were already handing out information on this web site in april while it was being tested. according to wang jianguo, deputy director of moftec's china international electronic commerce center, a trade group in shandong province earned 13 million unitedstates dollars from two quick deals done on the internet. the electronic commerce age has already arrived, wang says. it is especially valuable for medium-sized and small businesses, because it's just like having salesmen all over the world. a chemical factory in shandong saved eight million yuan when it contacted an italian raw materials source on the internet. in the past, it had to depend entirely on a japanese partner, a service it had to pay a lot more for. businesses on the internet not only display their products there, but also negotiate with other businesses in a negotiating room that has coded access for security's sake. moftec wants to turn the "made-in-china" web market into china's biggest marketing system on the net, so it established the coded system. it has a digital id card that can be used by many enterprises, liu explains, and adds that it has formulated imports and other trade procedures and ultimately will lead to eda --commercial transactions without paper.

title: backgrounder (6): hong kong -regional information, technology center
body: hongkong, the regional entrepot of finance and trade, is marked by the high degree of import and application of advanced technology, particularly that related to information industry.  taking advantage of its status of free port, hongkong maintains economic links with over 100 countries and regions, making it a pivot of information, and now it is trying to build itself into "the most informed city in the world" as described by the hongkong telecom.  wired by satellite, optical fibers, cables, microwaves and other media, hongkong has formed an information network, particularly economic information network, both locally and globally.  hongkong is the first major city in the world to have a fully digitized telephone network and the amount of its outgoing international phone calls is much higher than both the unitedstates and japan. hongkong now has a telecommunications network comprising over 300,000 kilometers of optical fiber.  about one-sixth of hongkong's population or 1.1 million people have subscribed to paging services --the highest per-capita rate in the world. and a total of over 1 million subscribers to cellular phone services also is among the highest levels of penetration in the world.  a recent market survey showed that the home penetration rate of pc is over 50 percent and there are more than 850,000 internet users in hongkong.  in march, the world's first-ever interactive tv (itv) was launched in hongkong, making it possible for people to see films, listen to music or deal with financial affairs at any time with clicks of a few buttons at home. and just two weeks ago, the internet service was added to the itv network, enabling users to get access to the worldwide web at a surprisingly high speed.  an international conference on the future of information and communications technology in asia had just concluded in hongkong.  organizers of the conference said the city provides a dynamic, technology-rich environment, whose government sees technology as a critical component of hongkong's successful future. also, the regional hub provides an open location in which to examine the various models of technology throughout asia.  since the 1960s, hongkong has brought in unitedstates and japanese investment in electronic industry, which has become the second largest industry in hongkong.  technology advancement is a key factor of economic growth in hongkong. a research on the manufacturing sector in hongkong shows that technology development accounted for an average of 42.9 percent in the sector's production during the period of 1969 to 1982.  hongkong's technology development is market-oriented and characterized by high efficiency. for instance, it usually takes a mere three months for general electronics and plastics from product design to production.  there are several prestigious academic institutions in hongkong, including hongkong university, the chinese university of hongkong, hongkong university of science and technology, and they are well equipped and have absorbed talents from all over the world.  political and social stability ensures hongkong favorable working and living conditions. in addition, hongkong's ability to develop technology-rich products has been well-complimented by the abundant outcome of the ever-increasing scientific research in china's inland areas.

title: internet shopping new fad in shanghai
body: virtual shopping via the internet is now a reality in this east china metropolis.  wang jihua, manager of an on-line book shop, said that his store has sold 150,000-yuan worth of books through the internet since may last year.  a professor at shanghai jiaotong university said that the quickest way to check out the books he needs is to do it on-line. in fact, same-day service is the norm, he emphasized, with satisfaction.  flowers and airline tickets can also be booked through internet flower shops and the web sites of airline companies.  an internet shopper said that it is more interesting and romantic to send flowers to his lover, and he can also get a delicate email from the flower shops.  experts say that more and more people will be able to do their shopping through the internet, resulting in 20 to 30 percent fewer people on the streets by the year 2000.  buying and selling stocks can also be done within minutes through the internet, according to local sources.  it is said that the shanghai information industry co. ltd is doing research on developing a security system for electronic business payments through the internet. the system is expected to be in place early next year, which will help stimulate further growth of electronic business transactions through the internet.

title: little gender difference among chinese net-using journalists
body: there is little gender difference in the frequency of using computers and visiting the internet among chinese journalists, according to a symposium, which closed here thursday.  the two-day symposium, women journalists and the 21st century'', witnessed the release of a survey on some 1,100 journalists here earlier this month, which shows that about 90 percent of them are computer users, and over one quarter of them visit the internet regularly.  according to the survey, the journalists use computers and the internet to write stories and get information. only a few of them conduct interviews, analyze news information and exchange ideas through the net. there is little gender difference either in this regard.  bu wei, an associate research fellow with the institute of journalism and mass communications under the chinese academy of social sciences (cass), who reported the survey, said that computers have changed the way of human communication greatly, and that grasping the computers and the internet means obtaining power over getting and releasing information.  "women should catch up with the trend so as not to be left out in the era of information," she said. "otherwise, the gender inequality will worsen.  "that is why many researchers care about the proportion of women internet users, and is why we conducted the survey," she said.  bu and her colleagues and journalists from the capital women journalists association surveyed some 1,100 journalists from the "people's daily", the xinhua news agency and the english-language newspaper "china daily", and found that "women and men journalists occupy the same position in terms of using computers and the internet.  "we may thus be optimistic about the improvement of the present situation that women account for one third of chinese journalists but occupy less than five percent of the leadership positions in the chinese mass media," said chen chongshan, a research fellow with cass's institute of journalism and mass communications.  women journalists have become the leading force among chinese women internet-users, according to the survey.  statistics show that in china women account for only 12 percent of net users, as compared with over 40 percent worldwide.  initiated in may 1995, china's internet servers serve some 620,000 users of nearly 300,000 computers.

title: new technology does away with cables
body: personal computers must be connected to a printer via cable, but a new technology is planning to change that.  ericsson, ibm, intel and other companies have unveiled their vision to revolutionize wireless connectivity for personal and business mobile devices.  the companies will work together to create bluetooth, the codename for a short-range radio link to exchange information, enabling effortless wireless connectivity between mobile phones, mobile pcs, handheld computers and other peripheral items of equipment. the radio will operate on the globally available 2.45-ghz "free-band," allowing international travelers to use bluetooth enabled equipment worldwide.  bluetooth will eliminate the need for business travelers to purchase or carry numerous, often proprietary cables, by allowing multiple devices to communicate with each other through a single port. enabled devices will not need to remain within line-of-sight, and can maintain an uninterrupted connection when in motion, or even when placed in a pocket or briefcase.  the companies said that bluetooth technology adoption is expected to be widespread throughout the computer and telecommunications industry.  with the technology, they said, users will be alerted to, and can respond to, incoming email via their mobile phone, even while their mobile pc remains in its carrying case. when the pc receives an email message, an alert will sound on the mobile phone. it is then possible to browse incoming emails immediately, reading the contents on the display of the mobile phone.  users will also be able to access the internet via a completely wireless connection. they could send an "instant postcard" by cordlessly connecting a camera to a mobile phone or any wire-bound connection. they also could add comments to their snapshots using a mobile phone or mobile pc, and send them instantly to recipients anywhere in the world.  the first products using the wireless port are expected by the second half of 1999.

title: china's e-business doing well
body: the bank of china has established the country's first standard electronic banking network. customers around the country and in the world can have access to their bank accounts and make deals through computers linked with the bank's branches or at atm machines in china.  an executive officer of the guoxin technology company said that china's on-line service companies enjoy a competitive edge over their foreign counterparts in e-business applications in the country.  he said that many international it giants have just put forward theoretical solutions to e-business in china while local on-line service providers have built networks that support the flow of information, funds and goods.  small-and medium-sized enterprises emerge as the largest group of beneficiaries of the rapidly expanding e-business in the country.  xu minghua, a farmer in east china's jiangsu province, has been marketing farm products of his village via internet since 1997. he found overseas buyers for 80 percent of the village's produces. earlier this year, he received an order from the unitedstates for 200,000 yuan worth of loofah.  vice-minister of the information industry lu xinkui said that e-business is one of the priorities that the chinese government will give in expanding the national it industry.  now china has established the framework of several nation-wide electronic data networks, including the telecommunications network, the computer-supported national economic information network, cable tv network and electronic networks for many specific industries.  local it experts pointed out that china has yet to establish a sound market order in the process of promoting e-business.  china should formulate laws and regulations on e-business and a universal credit evaluating system, they noted.

title: internet could reshape world economy, says expert
body: internet commerce is gathering tidal wave that could totally reshape the world economy, said a technology pundit at an ongoing conference in san diego, california.  speaking at the oracle applications user group convention, nicholas negroponte, director of the media lab at the massachusetts institute of technology, predicted that internet commerce would reach one trillion unitedstates dollars a year by 2000.  unitedstates government prediction is 327 billion dollars per year worldwide by the year 2002.  not only could smart cards replace cash, even for transactions as small as a pack of gum, computers could turn a handshake into a financial transaction, save books but kill bookstores, negroponte said.  but before internet commerce becomes that extensive, he said, consumers have to overcome two barriers, security and payment systems.  security is mostly a regulatory issue, he said, since very strong encryption technology already exists.  encryption could also help crack the other barrier --to make transactions as fast and cheap with credit as with cash --so that it could become cost-effective to bill a nickel or dime electronically, negroponte said.  microcash transactions "will change consumer behavior enormously," said the expert, whose laboratory focuses exclusively on the study and experimentation of future forms of human communication, from entertainment to education.  for one thing, readers might be more willing to pay for content if they only had to pay a few cents for each article that interested them. shopping for groceries and other necessities via the web might also become more common.  internet commerce is already flexing its muscles, negroponte said. on one hand, it is giving consumers more power by broadening their choices and letting them band together, for example, by pooling car purchases to get a fleet discount. on the other, it's killing off such traditional businesses as car dealerships, department stores and bookstores, turning them into mere showrooms to tempt online shoppers.  and it could wipe out jobs for all kinds of middlemen in the retail and credit industries, such as accountants, data processors and store clerks, he said.  negroponte said that the future of internet commerce will depend on enterprise information technology users.  internet could make cash obsolete. in a few years, he said, even "walking around money" could become purely virtual.  the media lab at mit is working on weaving computer circuits into clothing, using the body's own electrical currents to transmit information. instead of getting money from an automated teller machine by sticking a card in and getting printed pieces of paper out, a consumer could just press his thumprint to the screen to get the money downloaded to a computer in his shoe.

title: kodak creates online photo album
body: eastman kodak co., the world's leader in photography industry, will almost strike a deal with america online, the largest internet service provider, to store digital pictures for 12 million potential customers.  under a three-year alliance announced tuesday, america online's subscribers will be able to take conventional film to retailers on the street and have digitized copies delivered to their computer for an extra 5.00 unitedstates dollars to 7.00 unitedstates dollars a roll. more than 30,000 kodak photo-finishing stores around the country are expected to offer this new service.  the service, called "you've got pictures" will allow aol customers, having surpassed 12 million, to store photos in a private, online photo album. they will be able to personalize the albums by adding captions and backgrounds and cropping or enlarging the pictures. the photos could either be downloaded or transmitted online to friends or family.  while kodak and other photo-finishing companies have been offering electronic delivery, the deal with america online makes the technology readily accessible.  last month, kodak turned to computer-chip maker intel corp.  for help in developing and marketing a variety of digital-imaging products, notably a new line of leaner and cheaper cameras and cds used to store images.

title: roundup: africa bracing for information age
body: africa, a continent marginalized by the march of information technology in the early 1990s when the rest of the world witnessed an unprecedented growth in telecommunications, is striving to catch up with the galloping world information development.  the inexorable progress toward an information-driven society, particularly one which places heavy reliance on the electronic exchange of information, is making telecommunications development for all countries a matter of urgency.  "governments across africa are now recognizing the enormous importance of telecommunications… and are using their political will to implement change and upgrade their infrastructure," said pekka tarjanne, secretary-general of the international telecommunications union (itu), at the just concluded africa telecom 98' in johannesburg, south africa.  as perhaps the world's biggest potential market for improved telecommunications, africa represents one of the last great opportunities for external investors.  while most of the industrialized world takes access to telecommunications for granted, fewer than one in every 100 africans has access to one telephone line. the figure can be as low as two in 1,000 in sub-saharan areas.  the international telephone union believes that 70 percent of all africans are yet to make their first telephone call. average waiting time for a telephone to be installed in africa could be as long as five years.  it's encouraging to find that some african countries have made telecommunications a priority and are installing digital switches with fiber optic inter-city backbones and the newest cellular and mobile technology.  botswana and rwanda, for example, claim to have the world's most sophisticated national networks, with one hundred percent of the main lines are digital, compared with 49.5 percent in the unitedstates.  but at the other end of the scale, countries like madagascar and uganda have highly unreliable analogue telephone systems and poor national links between urban centers.  most african leaders realize that the information revolution offers africa a dramatic opportunity to leapfrog into the future, breaking out of decades of stagnation or decline.  one of the technology marvels is the internet, which has spread rapidly through africa over the last 18 months. two years ago only 16 countries had full internet access, now 47 of the 53 nations on the continent have developed some form of internet access.  currently, around 700,000 people use basic internet services, among them, about 600,000 are in the technology-thirsty south africa, leaving only 100,000 among the remaining 700 million on the continent.  this works out at about one internet user for every 5,000 people, far below the world average, which is about one user in every 40 people.  along with the emerging internet services, cellular phones and other wireless systems, funded partly by private capital, brought a more promising solution to africa's telecommunications needs.  research shows that while the number of telephone services in africa has reached a standstill, the mobile sector has developed over the past two years.  the number of global system for mobile (gsm) communications subscribers in africa represents three percent of the world's gsm users, a dramatic increase from zero three years ago.

title: blue chips, gold push australian stocks to stronger close
body: healthy gains among heavyweight stocks news corp, telecommunications giant telstra and a surging gold price offset negative sentiment surrounding indonesia-linked companies, pulling the australian share market to a positive close friday.  brokers said investors appeared to be switching into "safe" stocks and gold as asia economic and currency concerns resurfaced.  the all ordinaries index ended 6.4 points stronger at 2765.8, well off its mid-morning low of 2745.6.  the all industrials index gained 14.6 points to 4781.2 while the all resources index eased just 0.7 points to 1151.3.  telstra jumped 12 cents or 3.26 percent to 3.80 australian dollars on massive volume of 29.5 million worth 70 million unitedstates dollars, placing it at the top of the turnover table.  news corp rose 24 cents to 10.21 australian dollars, its preferred shares added 16.4 cents to 8.964 australian dollars.  global miner rio tinto fell 26.5 cents to 20.44 australian dollars.  resources giant bhp slipped 8 cents to 13.97 australian dollars. the shares slipped below the 14.00 australian dollar mark for the first time in five months friday, following a week long slide in the stock.  the gold sector grabbed the spotlight late in the session, rising 30.3 points or 2.35 percent to 1317.1 while the precious metal was selling 5.80 unitedstates dollars an ounce higher at 302.20 unitedstates dollars by 17:10 australian eastern standard time, friday.  the banking sector also proved resilient, adding 14.1 points to 5965.3.  the commonwealth bank of australia rose 17 cents to 19.10 australian dollars, westpac bank ended 14 cents higher at 10.83 australian dollars, national australia bank moved up 5.5 cents to 22.20 australian dollars, however anz bank dropped 22 cents to 10.88 australian dollars.  national turnover hit 321.78 million valued at 621.76 million unitedstates dollars, as falls outpaced rises 565 to 501 and 439 were steady.

title: australian stocks close down on u.s. rates
body: the australian sharemarket closed down marginally tuesday on concern over unitedstates interest rates and the collapse of merger talks between two big funds managers.  market heavyweight news corp continued to lose ground on negative sentiment towards its quarterly results after unitedstates investors sold their american depository receipts overnight.  but resources giant bhp gained ground in the afternoon session on takeover rumors and bargain hunters, despite lower world commodity prices overnight.  "there are rumors of a possible merger with rio tinto," said senior broker peter struk of reynolds co.  he also said the market was nervous on debate over a possible rise in unitedstates interest rates.  the all ordinaries closed down 10.7 points at 2786.9 after trading between 2797.6 and 2772.3.  the all resources lost 1.3 points to 1181.3, and the all industrials fell 21.8 to 4795.6.  shares in both lend lease corp and national mutual holdings fell after announcing that a plan to build a funds management powerhouse had broken down.  in october, both agreed to merge their funds assets into one house managing 51 billion australian dollars (33.15 billion unitedstates dollars), under a respective 51/49 split, to increase economies of scale.  national mutual dropped 27.7 cents, or 7.14 percent, while lend lease slumped 4.34 percent.  ordinary shares in rupert murdoch's news corp fell 36 cents to 9.96 australian dollars while its preferred scrip slipped 14 to 8.86.  national turnover was a thin 297.04 million valued at 854.60 million australian dollars (555.49 million unitedstates dollars). falls outnumbered rises 563 to 471, with 411 stocks steady.  national australia bank gained 8.5 cents, anz gained six, commonwealth dipped one and westpac slipped 2.9 cents.  topping volume was telstra corp with 16.78 million shares traded at a value of 61.04 million australian dollars (about 39 million unitedstates dollars).  bhp shares traded strongly after noon to close up five cents on a turnover of 2.93 million australian dollars (about 1.9 million unitedstates dollars).  the gold index closed down 3.3 points at 1321.3, with normandy mining losing three cents and lihir gold losing two. sydney trading in gold bullion closed at 299.80 unitedstates dollars an ounce, down 0.45.

title: yahoo premieres on-line movie site
body: yahoo inc, the world-famous provider of internet search engine, now is providing movies for its millions of users. yahoo inc. tuesday announced the release of yahoo movies (http://movies.yahoo.com ). this new site packages a comprehensive directory of compelling movie and entertainment information, including local showtimes, into one easy-to-use location. offering movie-goers the latest movie-related content and resources, yahoo movies also features upcoming movie releases, top box office movie information, news and reviews, net events, an actor index and movie matches. the site also provides a number of features to help users make informed viewing decisions. yahoo movies joins other members of the yahoo entertainment cast including yahoo games, yahoo tv coverage and yahoo comics. yahoo inc has been making big strides into the worldwide network, already having set up sites in 11 different languages: danish, english, french, german, italian, japanese, korean, norwegian, portuguese, spanish and swedish. yahoo's global network of properties served an average of 95 million page views per day during the month of march and continues to have the largest audience of any on-line service or site on the web with more than 30 million unique unitedstates adult users per month. yahoo inc. now offers a network of branded web programming serving millions of users daily.

title: australian share market end slightly low
body: a slide in news corp shares combined with a weaker resources sector pushed the australian share market slightly lower friday.  solid rises in the banking, insurance and building indexes helped offset the damage.  the benchmark all ordinaries index recovered to close just 0.3 point softer at 2780.5, off its intra-day low of 2757.9.  news corp's ordinary shares finished 31 cents or 2.9 percent worse at 10.32 australian dollars and its non-voting preferred stock was 22 cents or 2.4 percent off at 8.98 australian dollars.  news corp's fall pushed the media index 435 points, or two percent, down to 21,352.6.  the all industrials index still managed to add 8.9 points to close at 4793.6, however lower commodity prices overnight saw the resources index dip 9.4 points to 1169.8.  resources giant bhp fell to 14.00 australian dollars before midday, and recovered most of its losses at close just half a cent softer.  rio tinto tumbled 26.3 cents, wmc fell nine, woodwide was off 12, petsec shed 22 and comalco lost seven cents.  gold stocks also suffered as the precious metal dropped under 300 unitedstates dollars an ounce overnight. locally, bullion was trading 1.00 unitedstates dollar weaker at 298.80 per ounce.  the gold index finished 21.8 points lower at 1294.3.  anz and westpac led the banking index 59.5 points higher to 5960.8.  anz surged 33 cents or three percent while westpac added 14, nab gained 5.9 cents and cba rose seven.  telstra sat at the top of the turnover table, with a hefty 25.85 million changing hands worth 94.44 million australian dollars.  national turnover reached 306.38 million worth 998.27 million australian dollars (648.87 million unitedstates dollars), with falls outpacing rises 604 to 492 and 406 steady.

title: famous chinese comic series available on internet
body: shanghai people's radio station has made its famous comic program series, "the stories of wang xiaomao," available worldwide on the internet.  people in and out of china can use their personal computers to watch the program on "shanghai window" on the internet.  the comic program was created 10 years ago, and shanghai people have been exposed to more than 860 episodes. it features the lives of local people with a series of stories about wang xiaomao, a fictional youngster in this asian metropolis.  to help more people get to know shanghai and its people in an entertainment format, the program has been created as a cartoon series.  to date, more than 10,000 people in the world have watched the program and sent email to show their appreciation of the program.  "shanghai window" began putting press, film, radio and television programs on the internet in 1995. during the last three years, it has made available more than 30,000 pieces of chinese and english information, tv news, radio programs and chinese movies.  now, diversified programs in chinese, english and japanese are available through "shanghai window" on the internet, with an average of 150,000 daily "hits" by computer users in nearly 100 countries and regions.

title: canada not prepared to guarantee e-commerce tax free
body: the canadian government, fearing a huge loss of potential income, is balking at a unitedstates drive to guarantee that internet and global electronic commerce remain tax free.  so far, canada is one of the few countries that refuses to sign on to the unitedstates concept of not imposing duties or other taxes on electronic commerce.  at a trade negotiators' meeting in geneva last week, canada said it would only consider a four-year moratorium on taxing internet transactions.  the government insists it has not yet made up its mind whether it will tax internet transactions. at present, only goods and services tax is levied on internet sales at the federal level.  revenue minister herb dhaliwal had said that his government wanted to make sure tax laws are "appropriately applied" to electronic commerce.  "the department wants to ensure the integrity of canada's tax base continues to be maintained," he was quoted as saying in wednesday's financial post newspaper.  canada's federal and provincial governments are also worried that they will see their retail tax base quickly erode if internet sales remain tax free.  in the unitedstates, trade representative charlene barshefsky said tuesday that she had convinced most major countries not to impose import duties or other taxes on internet transactions.  "we already have a critical mass of countries that agree with the duty-free cyberspace concept," barshefsky said.

title: u.s. web users continue to grow
body: the population of unitedstates web users grew by 1.6 million to over 57 million from january to april of this year, according to a market research firm.  releavantknowledge inc., which based its research on interviews with 10,000 people, including users and non-users, and on demographic profiles of 1,440 web users, said that the growth can be attributed to an heightened awareness of the power and offerings of the internet.  while the growth was slower than in past studies, users are using the net more and more in their everyday lives for commerce, entertainment and information, the firm said.  the survey found that men composed 56 percent of the web audience. about 48 percent of the unitedstates population is male.  the 18-34 age group comprised the largest single age group online, making up 39 percent of the web universe, relevantknowledge said, although it accounts for only 30 percent of the unitedstates population.  industry watchers believe that the continued growth of the online population is essential if the internet is to become a truly mass medium. most sites now rely on advertising to bring in revenues. but experts say such ads can only become a significant source of funds once the audience reaches a critical mass.  different sources estimate worldwide web users differently. one estimation is 119 million by april 1998, or 2.4 percent of the total world population.

title: hka042260 --chinese language world cup soccer web site launched in hong kong
body: the world's most comprehensive chinese language world cup '98 web site was officially launched here on wednesday, offering chinese language internet viewers around the globe unparalleled coverage of this summer's festival of football. the chinese language world cup wed site has been developed by china internet corporation (cic), a hongkong-based company responsible for the creation of the nationwide business information network china wide web supported by such world leading news and information organizations as xinhua news agency, afp and reuters, in partnership with china telecom. the chinese language world cup site, at the web addresses http://www.worldcup98.china.com and http://www.worldcup98.hongkong.com, provides coverage of world cup france '98 to viewers across china's mainland via china telecom's public communications network, and to chinese language internet users in hongkong, asia, and the rest of the world. "i'm delighted to be associated with the launch of the chinese language world cup web site, which provides important opportunity to positively promote the work of local hongkong football, as well as that of international football, to a global chinese and english language internet audience," timothy fok, president of the hongkong football association, said at the launching ceremony. the site, available to internet viewers in both simplified and traditional chinese characters, as well as english language football fans, with fast-breaking news, photos and graphics provided by agence france presse (afp). the world cup site offers news coverage on the teams and events in the weeks leading up to the finals, together with a guide to the groups and fixtures, and match forecasts, venues, dates and times for all the matches from stage 1 through to the finals on july 1 this year. a comprehensive world cup archive details the news events, scorers, facts and figures throughout the entire history of the world's largest football competition. football fans can also get in on the action with interactive "chat rooms", world cup site email newsletters and exciting competitions for world cup prizes. "china is a country with perhaps the largest soccer following in the world -this is yet another example of china internet corporation leveraging on advanced multi-media technology to bring compelling and engaging content to chinese internet viewers," said china internet's director of product management vicky hung. "in 1997, china internet was responsible for delivering comprehensive coverage of hongkong's historic handover to a world internet audience. this year the world cup provides a focus for delivering world-class internet content to chinese language internet audiences, and will play a further significant role in internet development in china," she added. "the launch of the world cup wed site is a milestone for the co-operation between afp and cic and xinhua," said denis brulet, afp's regional director for asia pacific. "and we look forward for an even closer co-operation in the future," he added.
