title: internet users to miss out on sydney olympics
body: moving images of the 2000 sydney olympics will not be available on the internet to protect the rights of host broadcasters, the international olympic committee (ioc) said on wednesday.  according to reports from sydney, the internet received 600 million hits at the nagano winter games in february, up from less than 200 million at the atlanta olympics in 1996.  "the problem is you can no longer control the territorial issues so you are then breaching other broadcasters' rights," ioc marketing director michael payne told reporters in sydney.  "the moment you put it on it's worldwide so you can't then control it from the territorial side and i think the general view is that the technology will not be sufficiently advanced (by 2000) to even consider doing something on a territorial restricted basis." he admitted that the booming internet market was a threat to television revenue, which will account for almost one billion dollars (670 million) at the sydney games with the likes of us giant nbc and australia's channel seven invloved.  the ioc successfully trialled a system called video on demand (vod) in nagano, which allowed users to access broadcast footage of sport and press conferences at the games, plus archival material.  australia's senior ioc member kevan gosper, who also chairs the ioc's press commission, said an agreement was imminent between broadcasters and ioc technology partner ibm regarding internet rights.

title: salaries for web-related jobs surveyed in u.s.
body: salaries for internet and web-related jobs in the unitedstates range roughly from 40,000 to 120,000 unitedstates dollars a year, according to the findings of a survey released tuesday.  the survey, the first of its kind conducted by the american electronics association, was carried out on 19 large companies, including netscape communications, yahoo inc., cnet and cisco system.  it covers more than 30 of the "hottest" internet positions within engineering, design, administration, marketing/sales and web content groups.  as with many sectors of high technology, all of the jobs surveyed substantially outpaced the private sector wage average of 28,582 dollars, the association said.  start-ups can be 10 to 20 percent lower than the big companies when it comes to base salary. sometimes they are even 10,000 to 20,000 dollars lower, and offering stock or other kinds of alternative compensation are usual ways to make up for the loss.  the highest salaries, with an average of 121,200 dollars a year, are paid to "internet strategists," who develop strategy for use of the internet in support of division or company goals. this job requires a bachelor's degree in computer science, business or marketing and three to five years' experience in information systems design.  next come electronics commerce managers, who manage internet commerce for a business unit. the job requires a bachelor's degree in computer science or business, plus several years of experience in defining business systems. they earn 120,100 dollars a year.  those who earn 78,500 dollars and 76,700 dollars are web publishers and internet engineers. the former directs staff that produces content for web projects, and the latter acts as technical resource for company's internet unit.  forum managers, web editors and graphic artists earn between 50,000 and 45,000 dollars. forum manager handles an internet chat room and needs basic knowledge of online tools and company policies.  a web editor develops content for web sites and is required to have a bachelor's degree in english, journalism experience, knowledge of hypetext markup language (html) and web-page design. graphic artists use online tools to solve routine technical design problems.

title: australian stocks drift up in quiet trade
body: the australian stockmarket drifted higher on monday in quiet trade with media giant news corp posting better gains than most.  the all ordinaries index lifted five points, or 0.17 percent, to title: murdoch expands empire into russia by stake purchase
body: rupert murdoch's international media group news corp ltd made an unusual move into the telecommunications industry in russia on monday with the acquisition of a stake in pld telekom inc worth 81 million unitedstates dollars.  the global media concern announced it would purchase a 38 percent stake in pld telekom inc, a nasdaq listed telecommunications company with operations in russia, from london-based cable and wireless plc (cw), the australian associated press reported on monday.  cw later confirmed a sale price of 81 million unitedstates dollars.  analysts said news corp's move indicated its intention to launch pay television media into russia, despite no direct statement of such motives.  news corp chairman and chief executive rupert murdoch focused on the telecommunications benefits of the deal which will give news corp exposure to russia's market.  "this agreement offers an opportunity for news corp to be part of a company that is prepared to capitalize on the growth of telecommunications services in this market," murdoch said in a statement.  some experts believe the move provided a toe-hold in russia and eventually east europe, previously untapped markets for the media giant.

title: nanning using internet to invite investment
body: the capital of southwest china's guangxi zhuang autonomous region plans to release all its trade fair investment projects on the internet. the city will hold the '98 nanning optimizing capital structure trade fair may 5-7, and has prepared 768 projects, which can be found on the internet at http: //www.nnpr.com., according to li meisong, the city's deputy mayor. more than 500 businesses from china and overseas have been invited to the trade fair, including china's top 100 private firms, listed enterprises, and foreign consortia, to participate in the fair and choose projects in industry, agriculture, urban infrastructure, commercial distribution, culture and tourism, and property rights. one of the country's pilot cities to optimize the capital structure, nanning will offer consulting services on property rights' trading policies and laws, with a local property rights trading center to confirm procedures. during the fair, seminars will also be held to seek new ideas and methods for the private sector. the city now has 645 overseas-funded ventures from 23 countries and regions. last year, it introduced 271 million unitedstates dollars of overseas funds, up 13.58 percent on 1996.

title: hongkong telecom ims to offer better service to internet users
body: the hongkong telecom ims, the largest internet service provider (isp) in hongkong, announced on sunday a series of measures to upgrade and reinforce its technology, equipment and customer service.  one day after the second anniversary of the launching of the netvigator, internet on-line service of the hongkong telecom ims, managing director william lo said that the company will be the first in hongkong to invest in one of the most powerful and reliable email systems on the market, a commercial product adopted by some of the largest isps and on-line services in the world.  "though costly, the software migration underway will allow netvigator to offer world-class email service capable of supporting long-term customer growth, with outstanding performance and stability, as well as features such as anti-spamming," lo said.  since early this month, three 56.6k modem pools have been put into operation, which will help subscribers obtain easy connections, lo said.  lo continued to say that netvigator subscribers will enjoy free usage from 9:00 am to 5:00 pm everyday except sundays, plus 50 hours per month of free usage during other time slots, which is in effect a price reduction. the company will introduce more english content to its site, lo said.  the total access customers to the netvigator rose from 100,000 to 245,000 from april 18, 1997 to 1998, which represents an increase of 145 percent over the period from april 18, 1996 to 1997 and the hongkong telecom ims occupied 44 percent of the internet market share in hongkong.  hongkong telecom ims was elected 1997 best isp in hongkong and the netvigator.com was elected the 1997 best web site in hongkong by the pc world, a world known computer magazine.

title: u.s. government to hand over control of internet: senior adviser
body: the unitedstates government will hand over control of the internet to an independent global board, a senior adviser to unitedstates president bill clinton said here on friday.  ira magaziner, president clinton's information technology policy adviser, said one reason for unitedstates distancing itself from the internet was to reduce the government's legal liability for companies that operated from the internet, originally set up by the unitedstates defense department.  "what we are looking to do is to turn over all the authorities we have to a neutral, private, non-profit organization that would have a fully international board of directors which would be constructed in a way so that it could withstand legal challenges and not have to depend on the authority of the unitedstates government or any other government," the adviser said.  magaziner said the government wanted the new entity in place by mid-year and expected it would be based in the unitedstates at first.  the new entity's functions included allocating blocks of numbers (currently done by the unitedstates's internet assigned numbers authority), protocol directives, and allocating domain names, those suffixes on internet addresses such as .com, .org and .net.  said magaziner, who is in australia for the nation's first electronic commerce meeting which ended on friday.  ownership of the .com, .org and .net databases would be handed over to the new organization, which would set policy for these and new domain names, he said.  analysts said whether the new entity, envisaged by the unitedstates, will be accepted by other countries, particularly the european union, remains to be seen.  the unitedstates commerce department published a program last february aiming to transfer the management of the internet to a private business.  the program was later opposed by the european union and australia, arguing the program would strengthen unitedstates's control over the internet.

title: major news items in leading u.s. newspapers
body: the following are major news items in leading unitedstates newspapers thursday. the new york times: --president bill clinton toured birmingham, alabama, which was heavily hit by a tornado last week, and promised that the government would fully assist its recovery.  --the federal aviation agency agreed to delay the phase-in of an air traffic modernization project worth one billion unitedstates dollars until an agreement can be reached with controllers, who argue that the new equipment is less capable than the old one.  the washington post: --nearly one-third of american women undergoing annual breast cancer checkups for a decade can expect to get at least one false alarm, wrongly suggesting the presence of a tumor, said new research on the hidden financial and emotional costs of breast cancer screening. --fifteen years before the food and drug administration made its controversial move to regulate cigarettes, industry giant philip morris was already plotting to hide studies that might encourage what it feared was the government's intention, said a 1980 document introduced wednesday in minnesota's lawsuit against the industry.  the wall street journal: --internet commerce could pass 300 billion unitedstates dollars a year by 2002 and is boosting unitedstates economic growth and curbing inflation, said the commerce department's first report on the "emerging digital economy." it said internet traffic doubles every 100 days as on-line purchases by firms and individuals soar.  --the developed world's group of seven ministers continued their campaign to get japan to kick-start its flagging economy, but declined to help tokyo shore up its weak currency.  usa today: --millions of people scrambled wednesday in what most americans are pursuing: meeting the tax filing deadline.

title: u.s. expert explains tax system on internet commerce
body: the unitedstates opposed new taxes on the internet but would consider levying internet shoppers to ensure existing sales tax revenue was not lost in the shift to cyberspace shopping, an adviser to unitedstates president bill clinton said here on thursday.  speaking to the australia's first summit on electronic commerce attended by about 350 australian government ministers, business and research leaders, ira magaziner, senior policy adviser to president clinton, said that any new approach would have to be tax neutral, signaling it was looking to shift the onus for tax collection on to the shopper.  "we are opposed to any new or discriminatory taxation on internet or on electronic commerce," magaziner told the two-day meeting, which began on thursday, organized by australian national office for the information economy and australia's telecommunications giant telstra company.  "what we want is a uniform, simple automatic approach based upon principles of tax neutrality, and no discriminatory taxation.  so we are not proposing any new tax of any sort," he said.  industrialized nations were discussing ways to take existing value-added tax and sales tax and apply it to internet transactions in a neutral way, he said.  "we are favoring legislation in the unitedstates which would create a moratorium on the application of any new taxes on internet commerce," magaziner said.  "and then the creation of a commission among the states and cities and counties in order to develop a uniform approach to the collection of taxation." magaziner has completed a document recently outlining the unitedstates government's strategy for promoting the development of global electronic commerce on the internet.  the unitedstates was keen to develop the approach over the next few years, with a new way of collecting taxes but not a new tax, he said.  "we believe that as the internet takes off, electronic commerce takes off, more companies will do more business, they'll make more money and we automatically get our share," he said.  "the best thing for us to do is do nothing, just to let it go," he concluded.

title: australian governor-general on web problems
body: growth in the use of the world wide web has posed significant international questions relating to copyright, censorship and taxation that had so far gone unanswered, australian governor-general william deane said on wednesday. opening the seventh international world wide web conference in brisbane, the third largest city in australia, the governor-general, a regular internet user, said these issues would need to be addressed either by the industry or by governments. "it is undoubtedly the case that the borderless electronic and universal nature of the internet is not only beginning to change the nature of our transactions and delivery of services, it has many national and international legal implications," he was quoted by the australian associated press as saying. "questions, for example, of contract, of defamation, of harassment, of copyright protection and of where responsibility lies in cases such as where an employer provides staff with email and internet facilities, are assuming some importance." the governor-general, who was senior judge before he was appointed governor-general of australia, also cited examples of "cyber-terrorism," the ready availability of information on how to manufacture weapons, and widespread pornography as other issues that needed to be addressed. "while national and international legislation is needed to deal with criminal content on the internet, a degree of consensus is emerging in many parts of the world through industry self-regulation, using codes of conduct, hotlines and labeling schemes," he said. australia was ranked sixth in the world in terms of internet usage, and fifth for the number of internet hosts, he said, "within australia, the research company www.consult estimates that there are about 1.6 million who currently use internet, of whom around one million, including, i might add, myself, use it at least once a week." australia is a country with a population of about 18 million.

title: chinese academician says rights and interest important on internet
body: the protection of intellectual property rights on the internet needs to consider the balance of the interests of copyright holders and the interests of the public, according to xue hong of the chinese academy of social sciences' intellectual property rights center.  xue told a sino-french symposium on intellectual property rights here this week that the internet has become a hot topic in the chinese press and that this has also led to copyright infringements.  one example he cited was of a publishing house releasing a book with the title "financial turmoil" that had been downloaded from the internet. the protection of intellectual property rights on the web is uncharted territory in china, he said.  china has a number of international treaties on intellectual property rights, and if these treaties include information on the internet as part of their area of protection, china will have to modify its laws to meet its international obligations.  he said he believes that over-regulation must be avoided in intellectual property rights protection on the internet and that rights should not be concentrated in the hands of a few people while others who use the information to create new things are deprived of it.

title: u.s. information tech industry grows much faster than economy
body: the unitedstates information technology, including business on the internet, is growing twice as fast as the overall economy, the commerce department reported here wednesday.  in the latest report "the emerging digital economy," the department also found that the industry employs 7.4 million workers, some of whom earn among the nation's highest average salaries.  traffic on the internet has doubled every 100 days and internet commerce among business will likely surpass 300 billion unitedstates dollars by 2002, the report noted.  besides, the report also found: --the internet is growing faster than all other technologies that have preceded it. radio existed for 38 years before it had 50 million listeners, and television took 13 years to reach that level. the internet crossed the line in just four years.  --in 1994, about 3 million people were connected to the internet. by the end of last year, there were over 100 million people using it.  --without information technology, inflation in 1997 would have been 3.1 percent, more than a full percentage point higher than the 2 percent it was.  --workers in the information technology industry earn an average of almost 46,000 dollars annually as against an average of 28,000 dollars for the private sector overall. workers in the software and service industries are the highest wage earners, at almost 56,000 dollars annually.  the report recommends that governments stay out of the growing industry, saying electronic commerce shouldn't be "burdened with extensive regulation, taxation or censorship." government instead should help provide legal frameworks for business on the internet, and rules should result from "private collective action, not government regulation" whenever possible, the report said.  the department said consumers must be getting more comfortable making online credit-card purchases: 10 million people in the unitedstates and canada had purchased something on the world wide web by the end of 1997, an increase from 4.7 million people six months earlier.  the report also notes a shortage of highly skilled workers and recommends that students be better prepared.  "countries that have an insufficient supply of skilled workers will see high-skilled, high-paying jobs migrate to countries that can supply the needed talent," the report said.

title: web founder voices concerns about internet privacy
body: the inventor of the world wide web on wednesday said he was concerned about how personal privacy may be affected by the rapid growth of the internet and easier access to information.  tim berners-lee, who founded the web in 1989 as a medium for global information sharing, said privacy was now a top priority for the international world wide web consortium (w3c) which oversees use of the medium.  "i am very concerned about the privacy aspects of the use of the web at the moment," berners-lee told journalists at the seventh international world wide web conference in australia's coastal city of brisbane, the third largest city in the continent.  he said w3c was currently working on a platform for privacy preference, which would allow web users to dictate how much, if any, information was collected by internet providers about what sites they visited, what purchases they made and other web habits.  but despite privacy concerns, berners-lee said the web would become a much more creative and usable tool over the next few years.  he predicted the development of web browsers that would apply human-style reasoning to search for and provide more relevant information to users.  berners-lee was quoted by the australian associated press as saying he frowned on people or governments who sought to regulate or censor the internet, saying web technology did not force a particular policy or view on its users.  answering criticisms about allowing children access to inappropriate material such as pornography, berners-lee pointed to technology that allows parents to lock their children out of certain sites.

title: u.s. phone company to offer high-speed links to internet
body: gte corp., one of the major telecommunication providers in the unitedstates, will provide some of its telephone customers high-speed links to the internet.  it has become the latest phone company to join the race against cable tv companies to provide such access.  like other phone companies, gte of stamford, connecticut, plans to offer customers internet access over existing copper telephone lines using adsl --asymmetric digital subscriber line technology.  it is reported that it will offer speeds up to 50 times faster than conventional modems.  all five regional bell companies also plan to offer customer high-speed internet links via the adsl technology. cable companies, meanwhile, are using different technology to offer their customers fast internet access. those companies include tele-communications inc. and time warner inc.  gte said monday it will begin to offer the high-speed service in portions of 16 states this summer.  the states are: california, florida, hawaii, illinois, kentucky, michigan, missouri, north carolina, ohio, oregon, pennsylvania, texas, virginia, washington and wisconsin.  the company hopes to tap the fast-growing high-speed data market, which it said should account for 400 billion unitedstates dollars over next 10 years.  it will offer several packages of service. the low end, at 30 dollars per month, will be geared to people who work at home or like to surf the net and will let them connect at a speed of 256 kilobits per second. the high end package will cost 25

title: most uk businesses unaffected to internet: report
body: despite the attention being given in the media, internet is something that still doesn't seem to affect most uk businesses, a new report by the internet marketing and development agency (imda) showed.  from a telephone survey of 1000 businesses, the imda research found that although 98 percent of those called had "heard of the internet", only 12 percent believed that it had any bearing on their present business.  findings showed that most british businesses had been so lax in their understanding of the internet that they had ignored the opportunity offered to use their company names for domain registration.  only 14 percent of the companies surveyed had registered domain names and fewer than five percent realised that there was any issue of brand or marketing strategy when picking a domain name.  hundreds of thousands of trading names have been bought by rouge companies who are seeking to sell them back at inflated costs.  many domain names which could be registered as little as 60 pounds(100 unitedstates dollars) are now changing hands for thousands of pounds, the report said.  british businesses are falling behind their american counterparts and facing exclusion from global commerce on the internet, the imda report warned.

title: ncr system to facilitate bill clearing in beijing
body: the us-based ncr corp, the world's leading supplier of electronic banking solutions, signed a contract on wednesday to offer an intra-city automatic cheque clearing and sorting system to the people's bank of china (pboc) beijing branch.  the system, to be completed around july, will terminate manual bill sorting in the capital, according to today's china daily.  the system consists of two ncr worldmark 4300 mainframe computers, seven ncr 6760 cheque reader/sorters --each capable of handling 1,000 cheques per minute --and some other peripherals.  beijing is the fourth city in china to adopt ncr's cheque-clearing systems, following guangzhou, kunming and chengdu.  the system will cover more than 1,000 branches in beijing and the surrounding areas. when completed, beijing will become one of the country's largest cheque processing centers, capable of handling 300,000 bills every day, with settled volume exceeding 30 billion yuan (3.6 billion unitedstates dollars).  the pboc is launching a drive to spread computerized banking payment and settlement around the country. yu conglin, vice-president of the pboc beijing branch, said the ncr system was a key part of the pboc's computerization project.  china has become the company's fifth largest market. last year, ncr sold 1,300 automatic teller machines (atms) in china. in january this year, it set up a joint venture here in beijing with the beijing cable and wire co., which costs 20 million unitedstates dollars with the american side holding 70 percent of the stake. the joint venture will produce 10,000 atms every year.

title: yahoo's strong quarterly profit brightens internet firms
body: internet bellwether yahoo inc. reported strong net profits earlier this week, showing that there is a formula to make money in a largely unprofitable industry.  for the quarter ending on march 31, yahoo, the first major internet directory company, reported revenues of 30.2 million unitedstates dollars and net income of 4.28 million dollars, up from revenues of 10 million dollars and a net loss of about 700,000 dollars a year ago.  the silicon valley company said the average daily usage of its sites surged from 65 million page views in december last year to 95 million last month. a page view is defined as one electronic page of information displayed in response to a user request.  the report prompted a web-stock buying frenzy thursday. yahoo soared 17.25 dollars, to a record 114.50 dollars. propelled by the surge in yahoo's stock, shares of other web search companies also shot to record levels on the same day.  yahoo was the best-performing unitedstates stock last year, with a growth of 511 percent. last spring, yahoo traded at 32.69 dollars a share. its shares have nearly doubled since late january, and the company now has a market value of 5.3 billion dollars.  the growing popularity of yahoo and other internet companies has helped win over a skeptical wall street, analysts say.  financial investors, who a year ago openly questioned whether the young industry was more hype than substance, are now eager to plunk their money on internet stocks, realizing these internet media companies are real businesses.  it is estimated that advertisers are expected to spend 1.87 billion dollars on on-line spots this year, more than twice what they did a year ago. meanwhile, the number of households with accesses to the world wide web is expected to more than double to 56 million worldwide in 2002, from the current 25 million.

title: australian stocks ends at record high
body: australian shares closed at a record high monday on lower bond yields, a positive reweighting offshore of market heavyweight news corp and gold stocks gaining nearly seven percent as gold bullion prices rose.  the benchmark all ordinaries index reached a new intraday record high of 2802.6 in the morning session, eclipsing its previous record high of 2799.2 reached on march 24.  at the close of trade, the all ordinaries index had surpassed its previous record close of 2792.0 -also set on march 24 -rising a modest 24.8 points, or 0.90 percent, to 2795.6.  brokers and fund managers said the major influences on the market were lower bond yields, higher news corp shares and a higher gold bullion price, now up more than 9.00 us dollars since thursday in sydney trading.  while the all resources index was up 10 points at 1188.1, and the all industrials index was up 43.1 points at 4807.9.  but the stellar index performer was gold, rising 82.3 points, or 6.75 percent, to 1301.4, after gold bullion in new york rocketed 6.10 unitedstates dollars higher to 308.00 dollars an ounce.  ordinary shares in rupert murdoch's news corp gained 39 cents, or 3.69 percent, to 10.95 australian dollars, while its preferred shares gained 38 cents, or 4.18 percent.  reports that news corp unit twentieth century fox film corp would distribute the next george lucas-produced trio of star wars movies also boosted the stock, analysts said.  national turnover was 393.61 million shares exchanged, valued at 944.93 million australian dollars (623.65 million unitedstates dollars), rises outnumbered falls 646 to 515, with 382 stocks remaining steady.  in the bank sector, national australia bank gained 29.5, commonwealth bank climbed 34, westpac was up 10 cents and anz dropped 10 cents.  insurance and funds management giant national mutual holdings gained 19, or 5.74 percent, to 3.50 australian dollars.  telstra corp installment receipts closed down one at 3.84 australian dollars on a turnover of 7.13 million shares.  in the resources sector, bhp fell 4.9, rio tinto fell 1.4 and wmc gained 7.1.  copper prices, which influence the resource majors such as bhp, closed sharply lower in london on friday on the bad economic news from japan -a major market for australian resource companies.

title: 23 percent of us homes online by
body: by the end of this year, 23 percent of all unitedstates households will be accesssing the internet and other online services, according to a new study of international data corporation (idc), a leading american provider of information technology data, analysis and consulting.  dic analysts also expect home users to catch up business users when it comes to sophistication about use of the internet.  online and internet usage in the home has increased dramatically over the past 18 months, according to the idc study. by the end of 1996, only about 13 percent of all unitedstates households were online. the current level is more than 20 percent.  in addition to the increase in the number of users, both the frequency of use and the amount of time spent online have also grown significantly. nearly 60 percent of all online households access their online service at least once a day, increasing from only 35 percent for the prior year.  sub-pcs of 1,000 dollars and new devices like webtv and digital set-top boxes are partly contributed to the sharp increase.  the study also found that electronic commerce is even more widespread among home users than business users, indicating that more home users who are buying over the web seem to feel comfortable with web-based payment mechanisms.  business users tend to purchase more expensive goods such as airline tickets, hotel reservations, computer hardware and software.  aside from the availability of less expensive pcs and new internet devices, idc cites world wide web content as a driver for increase internet access from home.

title: thai provincial schools get free access to internet
body: blessed are those secondary school students across thailand who can enjoy free access to the internet through the so-called schoolnet from wednesday.  they must thank for the extensive "behind-the-scenes" work that has enabled free dial-up access from every province in the country, the bangkok post said wednesday.  this pioneering work, which puts the country ahead of others in the region, was spearheaded by the national electronics and computer technology center (nectec).  on monday, princess sirindhorn declared the network open during a private visit to nectec.  schoolnet offers internet access and uses the ppp protocol. it is now accessible free-of-charge by all school members who may dial a single special number from anywhere in the country. no long-distance phone charge is involved.  according to nectec director, professor pairash thajchayapong, schoolnet began as a pilot project in 1995, which is "a substantial component for the survival of thailand in the 21st century." the network was enabled without any specific national funding, thanks to other resources and projects and much behind the scenes work.  resources include the thai social/scientific, academic and research network, the country's largest league of higher education institution network, and nectec's own network testing laboratory, and later the "golden jubilee network project", which was set up to celebrate the king's 50th anniversary of accession to the throne in 1996.  international companies such as compaq, microsoft, intel also lent a hand.

title: hk government to provide "speedy news" on internet
body: the government of the hongkong special administrative region (sar) has begun providing a news service "speedy news" on the internet, thus allowing the public to get access to government press release almost at the same time when the media receive the same materials, an official spokesman said monday.  the "speedy news" would be a major improvement to the dissemination of information to the public by means of the internet, the spokesman for the information service department (isd) of the sar government said.  he said: "in the past, only major press releases were uploaded manually onto the internet after they have been issued to the media. all items were uploaded in the form of a daily information bulletin the following day." "with the installation of a specially-designed computer program, press releases issued by the isd can now be converted into internet file format and then be uploaded onto the government web site automatically and in a speedy manner throughout the day," the spokesman said.  according to the spokesman, press releases in both english and chinese would be uploaded within five minutes after they had been sent to the media via a dedicated network. internet users could choose from the daily index page the press releases, which were arranged in the chronological order, they were interested in, he added.  by clicking "daily information bulletin," internet users can read press releases, speeches and transcripts of remarks and statements made by senior officials of the sar, statistical reports and important announcements, the spokesman said.  in addition, he went on to say, major press releases will be further categorized to enable easy access to them from different sections of the web site.  the daily "hit" at the index page of the web site has increased 10-fold from 467 in december 1995, when the home page, or the "government information center," was launched, to 5,143 last month. over 22,398,000 visits to all pages of the web site were recorded during the period.

title: hewlett packard to bring internet monitoring program to malaysia
body: hewlett packard, the renowned unitedstates-based information technology firm, plans to bring an internet mentioning program called "e-monitoring" to malaysia, where the company's employees would mentor young people keen in information technology.  hewlett packard is confident that malaysia's multimedia super corridor (msc) project will not be affected much by the regional economic crisis, the company's president and chief executive officer lewis e. platt said here tuesday after discussions with malaysian prime minister mahathir mohamad.  "i think the good news is that the msc won't suffer because of the current economic issues," platt, who is a member of the international advisory panel for the msc, told reporters.  he said he was satisfied with the way the government was tackling the currency and economic problems.  he said he and mahathir talked about the msc in general, its development and also discussed bringing in hewlett packard's internet monitoring program called "e-monitoring" whereby the company's employees would mentor young people keen in information technology via the internet.  the program, started four years ago, has already attracted 1,500 hewlett packard employees worldwide on a voluntary basis.  hewlett packard already has investments in malaysia with two companies operating in the msc, a 750 square kilometer zone located south of kuala lumpur and designated as the hub for the development of multimedia products and services in the country.  hewlett packard's first company in the msc is involved in management and operations development while the second one is engaged in software activities.

title: australian stocks end slightly firmer
body: australian stocks closed marginally higher in a day of mixed trading friday in sydney following gains on wall street overnight.  the all ordinaries index closed up 2.6 points, or 0.09 percent, at 2775.2.  "it was a fairly steady day today," said james waggett, a stock exchange expert.  the all resources index closed down 2.8 points, or 0.24 percent, at 1160.2 while the all industrials gained 8.7 points, or 0.18 percent, to 4793.3.  waggett said national australia bank, news corp and coca cola amatil had been amongst the most active major stocks of the day.  market major news corp lifted 26 cents to 10.71 australian dollars amid what waggett described as a major change in the way people look at the stock. the preferred shares lifted ten cents to 8.95 australian dollars.  the banking index ended 15.3 points down to 5718.6.  national australia bank lifted 10.7 cents to 21.607 australian dollars, while commonwealth bank of australia dropped eight cents to 18.29 australian dollars and westpac fell one cent to 10.60 australian dollars.  anz bank dropped 23 cents to 10.15 australian dollars.  coca cola amatil lifted 42.6 cents to 11.676 australian dollars amid stronger asian stock markets.  among resource stocks, bhp lost three cents to 15.58 australian dollars.  global miner rio tinto gained 12 cents to 19.90 australian dollars.  the gold index gained 8.1 points, or 0.74 percent, to 1098.0.  gold bullion was trading at 291.15 us dollars late in sydney after closing thursday at 291.25 us dollars.  national turnover was 363.15 million shares, valued at 754.68 million us dollars with rises outnumbering falls 541 to 534.

title: eu criticizes u.s. internet reform plan
body: the european union (eu) has formally criticized a unitedstates green paper for reforming the internet's address system, saying it would give the unitedstates too much control over the global computer network.  the text, drawn up on behalf of the european commission and its 15 member states, will be submitted to washington in the few days to come, eu officials said thursday in brussels.  eu commissioner martin bangemann and british junior industry minister barbara roche accuse the unitedstates in the text of failing to "recognize the need to implement an international approach." the commission, the eu's executive body, last month drew up an identical draft which it later on forwarded to eu governments for approval, according to the eu officials.  the eu expresses concern in the text over the possibility that the internet reform plan would consolidate the jurisdiction of americans over the internet, including trademark disputes involving address names.  under the plan, the unitedstates is going to phase out the government's management of the address system for internet locations such as world wide web and electronic mail sites.  the plan also calls for an end to the monopoly of unitedstates-based network solutions inc, which registers all name addresses ending in ".com," ".org" and ".net." under the unitedstates proposal, up to five new "top-level domains," each with a registry to manage the address database, will be created to supplement the above three.  however, the unitedstates proposals "appear not to go far enough to ensure a level playing field and fair competition," the eu said in the text.  the eu accuses the green paper of failing to mention a competing plan for managing internet domain names drawn up by a global coalition of companies and organizations, which has already set up a council of registrars (core) in geneva.  the eu and its member states consider that "an additional effort is called for to reach a balance of interests and responsibilities, so that the international character of the internet is recognized," says the text.

title: australian stocks end higher
body: the australian share market closed slightly higher wednesday after a strong performance by bank and insurance stocks, fueled by a strong bond market.  but the bourse lost its earlier momentum in afternoon trade, retreating from its highs after falls on asian stock markets.  the all ordinaries closed just 2.5 points higher at 2769.6, despite an overnight record high on wall street and a strong start to the day that included an intra-day high of 2789.4.  the intra-day record for the index was 2797.3 set on september 25 last year.  henderson charlton jones broker philip toop said some re-rating in the insurance sector had most probably helped buoy its stocks, which pushed the index up a massive 194.6 points, or 2.62 percent to 7618.9.  insurance stocks were popular with investors seeking higher yield, analysts said.  they attributed the rise in insurance stocks to rallies in both the bond and equities markets.  insurance heavyweight national mutual holdings was behind the title: australian stocks end higher on industrials, banks
body: the australian stock market closed higher tuesday in sydney after strong performances across industrial stocks, boosted by a surge on wall street overnight and improving sentiment in asian markets.  reynolds co's grant williams said investors were flocking to the quality stocks, with australia's largest telecommunications company telstra an outstanding performer. title: hke031630--australia urged to become model for electronic commerce
body: australia was urged monday by microsoft chairman bill gates in sydney to capitalize on the growing popularity of the internet by becoming a model for electronic commerce and publishing.  gates, who founded microsoft two decades ago and whose operating system is now installed on over 90 percent of the world's personal computers, said politicians world-wide had already recognized the importance of the internet to the competitiveness of their countries in the global marketplace.  "in the infrastructure that exists here with the skills, the use of english, there are some incredible opportunities for australia in particular," he was quoted by the australian associated press as saying.  gates, who has a personal fortune estimated at 37 billion us dollars, is on a two-day whirlwind visit to australia.  "it's an incredible opportunity to share government information, to improve the educational system, to allow the businesses in the country to reach out in a way they never did before." gates spent an hour at a media conference in sydney about his vision for information technology which he said was still at the "paleolithic stage" of development.  "basically we're at the early age," gates said.  "maybe in 10 years from now we'll be through the early stages of the information age." with the evolution of the internet, governments faced major challenges including addressing privacy concerns and accessibility to technology for the entire population, he said.

title: china's internet users top
body: some 300,000 computers in china are now plugged into the internet and the country's real internet users now total 620,000.  according to a report compiled by the data communication department under china's ministry of posts and telecommunications, china had less than 20,000 internet subscribers in 1993, when it opened its international gateways to the internet.  the figure for 2000 is projected at two million subscribers.  on the composition of users, the report says more than 60 percent of subscribers are between 20 and 30, similar to the age range of computer users in china.  chinese net-surfers in general sort materials on the information industry, and those on business and finance, the report says.  it points out that, of the more than 100 internet service providers (isp), few offer local users china-related information that can reflect the country's political, economic, cultural and social changes, or other daily-use information.  personal computer sales in china this year are expected to top 700,000 units. the expanding network and increasing net-users provide massive business opportunities for content providers, especially those who can provide chinese-based information.

title: ge confident in further investments in asia market
body: the unitedstates-based general electric information service expressed confidence in the asia-pacific region's electronic commerce market, despite the continuing impact of the recent financial turmoil.  harvey seegers, company chairman, recently addressed a teleconference in hongkong, its asia headquarters, saying that ge's latest strategy in the region is to further localize electronic commerce services.  through the six asian branches, ge is capable of providing online services of electronic documents such as cargo orders, invoices and freight certificates with the technology of electronic data interchange (edi) in accordance with regional characteristics, seegers said.  he said ge has worked with the chinese ministry of post and telecommunications to set up china edi and electronic commerce centers in 13 provinces and cities. recently, it has teamed up with hongkong-based skylink to strengthen its presence in china's market.  electronic commerce is a major internet service item. edi services are catering to an increasing number of enterprises since they are time-saving and cost-effective. some insiders predicted that by 2000, more than 250 billion unitedstates dollars worth of business transactions will be done on the internet.  ge information service now has more than 40,000 business partners worldwide to provide edi, electronic telecommunications and internet services.

title: tibetan language fit for use on internet
body: successful coding has made the tibetan language fit for use on the internet, according to a deputy to the national people's congress, in session here since yesterday.  tibetan has thus become the first language of an ethnic minority in china to be usable in a computer age.  according to deputy jamyang losang jigme tubdain, who is a tibetan from gansu province, a tibetan-chinese bilingual information system has been successfully developed by more than 20 computer specialists and tibetan teachers of the northwest china institute of nationalities.  a major component of the system is computer-oriented coding of the tibetan language, he said.  other components of the system include designs of typefaces for tibetan characters, a data-bank relating to king gesser --a well-known tibetan epic, and tibetan medicine-related data and diagnosis.  the system has been assessed as up to standard by a group of specialists, according to jamyang.  a living buddha, jamyang is head of the lapuleng monastery in gansu.  the information system is expected to help promote the development of information technology in areas inhabited by the ethnic group as well as information exchanges in the tibetan language, he said.

title: cyprus to create information society
body: cyprus is ready to adopt a national strategy for the creation of an information society, minister of communications and works leontios ierodiaconou said wednesday.  ierodiaconou was addressing the euro-med net '98 conference on internet and the world wide web (www) which started here wednesday, with the participation of 300 representatives from european and mediterranean countries and european union (eu) officials.  ierodiaconou said this strategy is expected to strengthen the island's participation in the global information society.  the basic ingredient for this national strategy is the framework set by the eu itself for its member-states, a fact that confirms cyprus' full harmonization with the eu, in view of its accession to it, the minister noted.  the eu accession negotiations with cyprus will begin on march 31. the cypriot minister also stressed that cyprus can and wants to actively contribute to turning the mediterranean into an area of peace and prosperity for all.  the four-day conference will deal with the subject of the role of internet and the world wide web in the development of the euro-mediterranean society.  during the conference, there will be display of high speed internet connections via satellite and a host of european companies will present the latest achievements in the field of communication networks.

title: british government considers further crackdown on internet porn
body: the british government is considering further strengthening the measures currently in place for dealing with child pornography on the internet.  a voluntary body called the internet watch foundation (iwf) was set up by the government and industry over a year ago to tackle the growing problem of illegal material, chiefly child pornography, posted on the internet.  in its first annual report, the iwf said it had received 781 complaints referring to 4,300 items on the net in the 12 months since it established a complaints hotline.  department of trade and industry minister barbara roche tuesday welcomed what the iwf has done but announced that the government is to review the watchdog's role aimed at widening the work it does.  "the government is not complacent about illegal and harmful material on the internet and we intend to uphold the law on-line as we do off-line." the minister said.  almost 2,000 images of child pornography have been removed from the internet as a result of iwf's action, but as the iwf itself acknowledged, the amount it catches is just a "very small proportion" of the total available on the internet.  there are an estimated 70,000 pornography sites on the internet and more are added each day.  to remove more of those illegal materials more quickly, the iwf plans to patrol the net itself rather than wait for complaints from the public on its email hotline.  it is also proposing a ratings system for the internet, similar to that for classifying films and videos.  however, many child protection groups claimed that the iwf can only help to remove a small amount of child pornography, they said that a specialized police unit is still needed.  last week, london's metropolitan police force announced that it is considering prosecuting companies which provide internet services but fail to filter out illegal pornography.  the police are concerned about specific discussion forums, known as news groups, which they believed are used by paedophiles to exchange photographs and videos. the police said that they want these news groups banned.

title: eu suggests international charter on internet control
body: the european union has proposed an international charter on the regulation of the internet.  the draft charter came in response to the unitedstates green paper on internet governance, said martin bangemann, european commissioner in charge of telecommunications and information technologies.  he stressed that the principle of the charter should show no principle or discrimination, but reflect a wide range of international interests.  he appealed to eu member states to take a common position on the proposal of an international charter.  eu officials claimed that the unitedstates green paper, published last wednesday, appeared not to recognize the need to implement an international approach.  "the current unitedstates proposals could consolidate permanent unitedstates jurisdiction over the internet as a whole," they said.  the eu counter-proposal, expected to come out as a draft reply after the european council of telecommunications ministers meet on thursday, would include the private sector in the future organization of the internet.  the eu's specific objectives, according to commission officials, were to strive for balanced and equitable private sector participation in internet governance, including adequate procedures for the representation of consumer and user interests.  commissioner bangemann said that he did not want internet wars but hoped to encourage competition.  the eu wanted to apply competition rules in the internet to ensure that the transition to the new structures did not create or strengthen dominant companies and organizations charged with the regulation of the internet.

title: more u.s. computer makers sell products online
body: while american customers are becoming more comfortable buying clothing and books online, analysts said that they have not yet begun making major purchases.  websites offering advice about cars, computers and travel have expanded over the past two years in the unitedstates. customers do their research on the net and go to stores to pick up things they want to buy. but this is beginning to change. more and more businesses have started to realized that the internet can be a cheaper method of selling products.  major computer makers, such as apple computer inc., compaq computer corp. and hewlett-packard co., are selling their products over the web. dell computer corp. boasts of more than four million unitedstates dollars worth of products and services sold over the internet each day.  for a time, ibm seems not to envious, lavishing money on television ads touting its e-commerce software suite. now it also plans to start selling pcs over the web. one ibm senior executive said recently that the manufacturer intended to offer a way for customers to configure and order computers via its website in the "near future." in fact, the decision is part of a larger initiative to improve the performance of the pc company, which now ranks second in worldwide market share behind compaq and ahead of dell and nec.  ibm has resisted taking this step for fear it might alienate the company's resellers. however, under the proposed plan, resellers will ship the products to customers in a move designed to undercut any possible opposition from its distribution channel.  analysts say that the kinds of customers who buy computers over the web tend to be experienced users shopping for price and performance. it's still unclear whether the popularity of web-based pc sales will transfer into major incremental gains in the business for computer makers.  with ever-increasing online sales, banks, credit card companies and businesses will have to figure out better ways to communicate with each other. analysts say it may take some time for those issues to be settled. the adoption of the security electronic transaction (set) specification used to verify all the parties engaged in a credit card purchase, for instance, is at least a year away.

title: u.n. to promote internet in developing countries
body: the united nations development program (undp) is seeking to promote the use of internet by common families of the developing countries, said a official on friday.  chuck lankester, who is heading a sustainable development network program in the undp, made the remark at a press conference here.  the internet is the fastest growing information distribution facility in the world, with the number of its users doubling almost every year since 1988, lankester said.  but the internet is not evenly spread throughout the world, with the majority of users concentrated in the unitedstates, he said. the developing countries, however, are witnessing a very slow development of this modern information network.  lankester said that now, with the help of the undp, 35 countries have established an information network on sustainable development and that 40 more countries are considering joining the network.  what the undp seeking to do was to provide a kind of liaison service for the information network, with discussion of sustainable development as its major task, he said.  lankester said that the undp was working with member states on network designs with a precondition that governments were committed to let everyone enjoy the information provided by the network.  he said that until now the undp had discussed the matter with about 100 governments, among which only three countries refused to make such a commitment.  lankester said he understands the concern of some countries about allowing their citizens free access to the internet. he agreed there must be some restriction on violence and pornography contents.

title: zambia's tourism onto internet
body: a private company, africa insites, has been set up in lusaka to offer information on tourism in zambia on the internet, according to a local newspaper.  the company which has already won approval by the zambia national tourist board and the tourism council of zambia will focus on comprehensive and up-to date information relating to tourism, business and travel in the country.  the post today quoted the firm's chief executive robyn curtis as saying wednesday that his company has set up a web guide on zambia comprising 200 pages with information ranging from business to local culture.  "the information is supplemented by stunning color photos and adverts of local tourism products and packages," said curtis.  the company will operate on earnings derived from adverts placed by tour operators, lodges and hotels whose brochures can be advertised on the web guide.  the paper also quoted africa insites spokesman jifipa ngalande as saying wednesday in an interview that response from advertisers have been overwhelming with some adverts being from south africa and england.  he said the initiative has been taken following complaints about the difficulties of accessing information on zambia from around the world.  the advertising rates have been pegged at 250 u.s dollars for the whole year with incentives such as making amendments to the running adverts when necessary, curtis disclosed.  africa insites also offers companies and individuals with their own web sites to be part of the information package by listing them, at a cost of 100 dollars, in an appropriate section to enable users get linked to their sites.  the firm's spokesman added that more and more people are using the internet to decide where to go on holiday and zambia needs a good web site to compete with the rest of the world as a holiday destination.

title: microsoft peddles products among foreign governments
body: microsoft chairman bill gates said wednesday that the advent of the personal computer has made it possible for governments to set up services in a matter of weeks that previously took months or a year or more to build.  gates made the remarks at a company-sponsored conference in seattle which ended wednesday.  more than 300 foreign delegates attended the conference, called "empowerment 2001," where they shared ideas and learned how microsoft products can aid their administration.  the officials were shown microsoft and other software products designed to help governments contact and communicate with citizens via the internet.  software designed to smooth data exchange and communications among government agencies also was demonstrated.  a microsoft executive told the officials that the company wants to spread the word about its network servers to help governments install email, publishing, security and database software.  microsoft, largely known for its desktop software, is undertaking a pilot project involving six european cities that are constructing web sites to provide new services and communications.  in a reference to the unitedstates justice department's investigation of microsoft's business practices, gates assured the delegates that his company would continue to add features that make software more powerful and easier to use.  the development of windows 98 or windows nt 5.0, which are expected to be released later this year with built-in internet access capability and features, will not be affected, he said.
