title: australian share markets end slightly firmer
body: an afternoon surge in news corp. stocks following a strong profit result and a reported preferred share buyback helped winch the australian share market to a slightly firmer finish thursday.  the all ordinaries index spent most of the day in negative territory following a 30.6 point fall on wall street overnight and weaker resource and banking sectors. but by the close, the all ordinaries had crawled one point higher to 2657.9.  "news corp. definitely kicked the market along this afternoon," reynolds co.'s peter struk said.  "but the market generally didn't know which way to go. there was no lead from overseas so it just bobbed around," he said.  news corp.'s rally, along with positive earnings and sales news from coca-cola and coles myer respectively, pushed the industrials index up 7.9 points to 4520.9.  the gold index also proved strong on a rising bullion price, gaining 23.7 points or 2.07 percent to 1166.8.  the all resources however shed 5.3 points to 1176.8.  among other industrials, telstra installment receipts firmed two cents, lend lease lost 40 cents, qantas dropped seven cents, howard smith rose 30 cents while fairfax holdings slipped six cents.  bhp lost 17 cents, rio tinto ended 32 cents weaker, and wmc, which posted a 1.8 percent dip in interim profit to 98.9 million australian dollars, closed 12 cents softer.  the price of gold rose 1.75 to 298.10 unitedstates dollars an ounce.  the banking index tumbled 31.1 points to 5340, with anz faring worst among the big four, dropping 26 cents. nab eased 10.4 cents, cba was steady, westpac edged up 0.1 cents.  national turnover was modest at 367.67 million worth 1,001.58 million australian dollars (681 million unitedstates dollars). falls outpaced rises 553 to 517, with 366 steady.

title: deutsche telekom to offer online electronic business systems
body: germany's dominant telecom company, deutsche telekom, announced today that it would launch new complete systems to enable the handling of electronic business on the internet.  according to herbert may, a senior manager of deutsche telekom's global system unit, the so-called "shop and mall systems" to be launched by the company in a few months, would offer its business customers, shopowners for example, the opportunity to operate virtual shopping centers on the internet.  internet users will then be able to see and order certain products presented in the online "shops" and pay the bill by credit cards also through internet.  dr. may emphasized that the breakthrough for electronic commerce on the internet depended on the introduction of secure payment systems.  "for this reason, our objective… is to support… online payment systems that provide utmost security, anonymity and user-friendliness," he said.  dr. may also announced that deutsche telekom has entered into a strategic cooperation with ibm to develop viable online payment systems. as the first step, the two companies will conduct a pilot project based on the set (secure electronic transaction) standard, which currently meets highest security requirements.

title: ceos of computer companies on challenges of 21st century
body: chief executive officers (ceos) from unitedstates computer software and service companies monday discussed here challenges of the 21st century and how the internet will change our lives.  speaking at the 1998 annual meeting of the world economic forum, bill gates of microsoft said that two keys to his company's success were sharing wealth with employees to build a long-term relationship that makes best use of their talents and working with partners.  at the same time, gates said, his company continuously monitored what users needed and what competitors were producing in order to gauge the opportunities and threats facing the business.  he pointed out that microsoft had shared more wealth than probably any other company by giving employees stock.  on strategies for the 21st century, gates observed that interaction costs have now dropped to almost zero. "we are sure that information technology is changing the rules of the game. we don't know how that is going to restructure business," he added.  giving his vision of how the internet will influence people's lives, stephen case of america online suggested that just as the 1960 unitedstates election was said to have been decided by television, "the next election could be decided on the internet", because of the intense involvement of users of the world wide web.  he noted that america online had signed a final agreement to take over compuserve and become a business with 13 million customers.  larry j. ellison of oracle observed that to have its full impact, the internet would need to be as easy to use as the telephone or television and reach many more people.  oracle and microsoft now were involved in the production of more simple machines to hook-up through the television.  when the internet links become universal, ellison said, companies will be able to take advantage of instantaneous information technologies not just in financial transactions but also in labor, to commission work across the world, or in ordering supplies.

title: new spring festival activities in east china city
body: wang yi, a businessman in hangzhou city in east china, departed from the city with his family for a trip to singapore, malaysia and thailand on the first day of the spring festival holidays, immediately after his return from a business trip to guangzhou.  this year's spring festival has witnessed an unprecedented tour boom in hangzhou, capital of zhejiang province. an increasing number of local residents have opted to travel rather than staying at home for a traditional family reunion.  hainan, china's southernmost island province, is the first choice of hangzhou residents seeking warm weather. other choices include thailand and other countries in southeast asia as well as hongkong.  rising income has prompted the residents to expand their access to sources of information, with beepers and mobile phones remaining the hot consumer items. many hangzhou residents have exhibited great enthusiasm for the internet.  zhang lei, an employee in a trade company in zhejiang, used his annual bonus to apply for internet services. zhang said he would send new year's greetings to his friends across the country via email.  he also noted that the internet will provide him with greater access to wide-ranging sources of information.  an increasing number of department stores, shops and supermarkets is providing the hangzhou residents with greater options on where to purchase inexpensive, quality products.  consumers are benefitting from intense competition, which has forced some department stores to offer discounts.  the new vogue amongst the hangzhou residents centers on the aqusition of knowledge, with many people flocking to bookstores and libraries over the holidays.  the hangzhou xinhua bookstore has opened special counters to meet the demand for books the residents are presenting as new year's gifts. the store's business volume has doubled over the spring festival period.

title: australian stocks close lower
body: australian shares were wednesday weakened by fears of further financial instability in asia, particularly indonesia.  the all ordinaries index closed 16.6 points lower at 2622.8, having relinquished an earlier high of 2,622.8.  the indonesian rupiah hit a record low wednesday, dipping in early trade to 11,500 to 11,800 to the us dollar, on political and economic concerns and strong demand for the us currency.  the all industrials index fell 28.1 points to 4523.8.  swimming against the broader market, news corp soared on a buy recommendation put forward by leading us broking house morgan stanley.  news corp ordinary shares jumped 51 cents to 9.41 australian dollars on turnover of 7.8 million shares while the preferred shares vaulted 34 cents to 8.03 australian dollars.  banking stocks were generally weak, with the banking index falling 70.4 points to 5577.9.  national australia bank lead the way down with a fall of 50.8 cents to 21.13 australian dollars, while westpac bank dropped 14.8 cents to 10.292 australian dollars.  anz bank fell 15 cents to 9.97 australian dollars.  commonwealth bank shares rose against the trend, adding two cents to 18.50 australian dollars.  the all resources index fell 7.3 points to 1102.4 with mixed fortunes among the major stocks.  bhp fell 28 cents to 13.72 australian dollars.  on the other hand, rio tinto rose 39.8 cents to 18.598 australian dollars.  the gold index improved 11.2 points to 1029.5 as bullion increased 1.75 us dollars per ounce to 290.05 us dollars.  national turnover wednesday was 307.85 million shares worth 656.69 million us dollars with falls outnumbering rises 597 to 492.

title: eu defines position on internet telephony
body: those hooked to pc's chatting away via internet telephony will continue to enjoy their almost free long distance calls over mike and loudspeaker in european union countries.  the european commission, the executive body of the 15-nation union, defined thursday its position toward internet telephony in the context of the liberalization of the union's telecommunications market.  under the defined eu law, the provision of voice service on the internet is not voice telephony and may therefore not be subject by member states to individual licensing procedures.  voice communications can be made through the commercial services provided either from pc to pc, between pc and telephone handsets connected to the public switched telecommunications network (pstn), or between two telephone handsets connected to pstn.  only the third and last way is currently regarded as being close to voice telephony or voice communications.  internet telephony can be defined as voice telephony and therefore be subject to standard voice telephony regulation only if the communications are the subject of a commercial offer; the service is provided for the public; the service is provided to and from pstn, and the service involves direct transport and speech in real time.  the commission considered that internet telephony currently does not meet all these criteria and therefore will not be considered as voice telephony for the time being.  the commission's definition will keep markets open for innovation regarding the internet, which could lead to multimedia telephony offered over the computer network.  voice on the internet will therefore still enlarge the scope of services available to consumers and is likely to help foster consumer access to what is commonly known as the information society.

title: cic, afp sign on world cup soccer online coverage
body: china internet corporation (cic) and agence france-presse (afp) signed here on tuesday an agreement to provide landmark chinese language online coverage of this summer's world cup finals soccer tournament in france.  peter yip, cic's executive vice-chairman, said: "we are delighted to be participating with a world-class media organization of the caliber of afp, and using advanced multi-media internet technology, to bring the world cup to the chinese language audience." "we are delighted to be working with cic on what is without doubt the world's biggest sports event in a country with possibly the largest soccer following," denis brulet, afp regional director for asia-pacific, said.  under the agreement cic and afp will provide fast-breaking coverage of the world cup finals slated for june 10 to july 12.  the service will reach chinese football fans via cic's china wide web in both chinese and english.  world cup followers on china's mainland will not only have access to real-time reports on all 64 matches but will also see a wide selection of photos and graphics on the china wide web beginning february 1, 1998.  the china wide web service will include access to a huge soccer database compiled by afp including extensive information on the 32 teams in the finals, profiles of team managers, coaches and players and descriptions of stadiums and the french cities hosting the matches.  a database on the history of the world cup will provide information on previous tournaments going back to the inaugural tournament in 1930.  china internet corporation has been responsible for the creation of the china wide web, an online business information collaboration and communication system that spans china.  china wide web is supported through a series of alliances with global news and information corporations, and has developed its network infrastructure through partnerships with the world's leading computer hardware and software companies.  a strategic partnership with china's ministry of post and telecommunications has resulted in cic's china wide web service being available to internet viewers in more than 200 cities in china.

title: uk launches project to put schools on the internet
body: uk netyear, a project destined to connect the country's every school to the internet, begins today.  the launch ceremony, held simultaneously in london, belfast, cardiff and glasgow, includes the linking of a total of 23 schools across the uk through videoconferencing.  only 6,000 schools in the uk are currently connected to the internet. the aim of netyear is to increase this to 17,000 by the end of 1998, and 32,000 by 2002.  under the ambitious scheme, basic training in the use of the internet will be provided free of charge on a cd-rom to every school that registers with the new project.  free email for all pupils and teachers will be a key feature of the scheme, it was announced.  every school in the country will be urged to register, free of charge and they will be given help to raise money to provide computer equipment to get them on the internet.  founders of the project are cisco systems, icl, the daily telegraph and sun microsystems.  the four companies have underwritten a budget of about two million pounds (3.2 million unitedstates dollars) to help train teachers and students to use the internet for teaching and learning.  uk netyear is part of the british government's wider plan of national grid for learning, which ultimately aims to connect schools, libraries, museums and other organizations together via the internet by the year 2002.

title: more american travelers bypass travel agencies
body: americans nowadays do not have to rely on agents who make travel arrangement for them as they have found other ways to save money.  for instance, they could check web sites set up by airlines and see whether there are cheap last-minute internet specials on unsold seats.  last year, about four million air tickets, or one percent of the total, were transacted via the internet in the unitedstates, according to a report from the air transport association.  by the end of this year, some 13.4 million americans will buy tickets on-line, said the report.  industry analysts noted that when travel agents began to charge customers additional fees, more and more americans might choose to buy tickets directly from airlines' toll-free numbers or via the internet.  since the beginning of this year, an estimated half of the travel agents on the unitedstates west coast have begun charging "processing fees" tacked onto the regular cost of a ticket or reservation, which range between 5-40 dollars.  the analysts said that the number of such agents, who have been suffering from cuts of commissions by airlines, is to grow, which will lead to the fact that more and more travelers opt to bypass travel agents.

title: china to safeguard computer networks connected to internet
body: a special administrative regulation on the protection and management of computer information networks connected to the internet will be promulgated and become operational starting this tuesday.  zhu entao, assistant minister of public security, made his remarks here today at a press conference, adding that the regulation, approved by the state council on dec. 11, will govern institutions and individuals engaged in computer information networks hooked up to the internet.  statistics from the internet information center of china show that china had more than 49,000 host computers and 250,000 personal computers connected to the internet at the end of october, as well as some 620,000 subscribers to the internet.  zhu said that the regulation, formulated in accordance with several state laws and regulations, aims to enhance the protection and management of computer information networks connected to the internet to safeguard national security and social stability.  zhu pointed out that the implementation of the regulation is bound to help the national police force to crack down on computer-related crimes and safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of both institutions and individuals engaged in the field.

title: china to safeguard computer networks connected to internet
body: since china began its opening-up drive in 1978, computer information networks established by various regions, walks of life and government departments have become an indispensable means and tools in the management of state affairs, economic construction, national defence construction and frontiers of science and technology.  the assistant minister pointed out that the connection of china's computer networks to the internet in 1994 has tremendously promoted the country's cultural and scientific exchanges with the rest of the world.  "but the connection has also brought about some security problems, including manufacturing and publicizing harmful information, as well as leaking state secrets through the internet," zhu said.  he stressed that as china accelerates the growth of the information industry, wide applications of computer networks in various spheres have made it a pillar of social development.  "hence, the safe and effective management of computer information networks is a prerequisite for the smooth implementation of the country's modernization drive," zhu said.

title: most canadians want curbs on internet
body: canadians are growing suspicious of the internet and favor government regulation of cyberspace, according to a poll published today.  canadian women, especially mothers of young children, are leading the call for internet control, a year-end citizen-global poll showed.  sixty-six canadians said yes when asked whether they favored government passing laws to regulate the internet. among women in the 35-54 age group, 80 percent favor regulation.  "we have gone beyond the trailblazers, or first wave of users, who typically would not favor any regulation," said duncan mackie, senior vice-president of pollara, the polling firm that conducted the survey.  as the second wave is more likely to consist of families, they are sensitive to such things as violence and pornography on the internet, mackie said.  but david jones, president of the anti-censorship group electronic frontier canada, noted that people will change their minds about regulation the more they use the internet.  the poll also found that most canadians don't have access to the internet. sixteen percent have access at work, 13 percent have access at home and 10 percent have it in both places.

title: china opens insurance information network
body: the insurance information network, a special web site for chinese companies on the internet, makes it possible to sell policies on-line.  the network was jointly established by the china insurance institute and the weixin investment consulting company to promote chinese insurance companies and their services.  "this will help improve the information exchange among insurers in china, and chinese people's awareness about the importance of insurance in their lives," said chen yuan, deputy governor of the people's bank of china.  chen said that china's total sales of insurance policies reached 201 billion yuan between 1991 and 1995 at an annual growth rate of 26 percent.  china resumed operation of insurance companies in 1978, and the industry has been developing rapidly during the last few years.  about 20 chinese insurance companies, jointly-established ventures and overseas insurers now are selling 600 kinds of insurance services in china, he said.  however, china's fledgling insurance industry still has some defects and shortcomings, such as few channels for sharing information, chen said.  the xinhua insurance (life) co., ltd. reportedly sold the first insurance policy through the internet on china's mainland right after the network opened. the insured, zhang sumian, works for the beijing commerce college. she bought her son, a university student, a life insurance policy valued at 100,000 yuan.

title: egypt uses cyberspace to expose terrorists
body: keeping up with the high-tech, egypt has taken its war against islamic militants to the internet, local english weekly al-ahram reported today.  the state information service (sis) is using cyberspace technology to expose militant leaders living abroad, whom the egyptian government accuses of planning and financing terrorist acts back home.  it has recently added to its internet web site the names and pictures of 14 more fugitive terrorists together with some background information after the massacre in the southern city of luxor in november.  the attack, claimed by the gamaa islamiya and suspected of foreign masterminding, killed 62 people, including 58 foreign tourists.  echoing cairo's call for cooperation from european countries in combating terrorism, the sis web site has declared "terrorists do not recognize any boundaries. the international community is under an obligation to work collectively to deny such terrorists any safe haven." analysts say that the idea behind putting the names of the wanted terrorists on the web site is an attempt to expose them rather than catch them as the site virtually provides no guidance of action or hot lines.

title: lebanese first on-line mall opens
body: lebanese first on-line mall opened its doors wednesday with the launch of a website on the internet for shopping while surfing, lebanese newspaper the beirut times reported today.  the paper said that net surfers in lebanon and around the world can now make purchases on the shopping mall created by the data management, the country's largest internet service company.  the payment procedure is done through a klebox, a secure virtual wallet which contains credit cards for expensive purchases and change in the customer's own currency for small purchases.  the klebox service was developed by kleline, a financial service company based in france, which offers a set of secured payment services on the internet.  "for the customer, this service is completely free of charge as no fee transaction is debited. the merchant is the one paying the whole cost," said abdallah hitti, general director of kleline.  the data management spent 250,000 unitedstates dollars and eight months of constant work to set up the website.  in lebanon with a population of about 3.5 million, personal computers currently stand at about 80,000 and internet subscribers an estimated 14,000.

title: BC-China-Internet-Imperative Rules for Internet Must Suit Social Background, Chinese Official
body: Each country should establish laws, rules and ethics in accordance with its own social background to govern the use of the Internet, so that the information industry will make greater and healthier contributions to the mankind in the next century. Lin Quan, secretary-general of the State Science and Technology Commission, made the remarks today at a seminar titled "Inforamtion Imperative: Rules of the Road for the Internet", attended by both Chinese and unitedstates information officials and experts. Lin said, the Internet, as the craddle of the information age, has exerted prefound impact on the work mode and living style of the mankind. "In discussing the rules governing the use of the Internet, it is important to remind that the rules must be made in accordance with the United Nations acknowledged principles, in respect of the different political systems and economic development and cultural background of various countries. We should avoid enlarging the gap between developed and developing countries in the course of information globalization and we should arouse our concern over the dissemination of harmful information while expanding the Internet," he stressed. According to unofficial statistics, China now has 500,000 Internet subscribers, most of whom are businesses, government organs and scientific and cultural institutions in the more developed eastern part of the country. China also has a growing number of family-based subscribers, but the percentage is relatively small. Lin said Chinese parents have realized that the Internet contains information of low taste that is not suited to their children and have taken steps to educate them not to read those information. But, he said, the measures focus on ethical education instead of exerting fast rules. "The country has not yet set up any rules and regulations to control the access to the Internet," he said. He said that the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization convened last March on the ethics and rules over the Internet and did not result in a universal rule as the delegates varied in their opinions on a lot of issues. But he said the conference was useful for Chinese and foreign experts to further discuss the issues in order to exchange ideas and increase understanding. Lin Quan told the seminar that the Iinternet, that originated in the unitedstates, was first introduced to China in 1993 and has flourished over the past four years. And it will develop rapidly with the fast growth of the country's telecommunications and computer industries. According to Lin, China has established four major national information networks that have access to the Internet. They are ChinaNet run by the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, CERNET by the State Education Commission, NCFC by the Chinese Academy of Sciences and STINET by the State Science and Technology Commission. In addition, information service companies that are hooked up to the Internet platform have also mushroomed all over the country. The seminar was co-organized by the State Science and Technology Commission, the United Nations Development Program and the World Times Inc. of the unitedstates. It was sponsored by American AT&T, International Data Group Asia and Digital.

title: India Privatizes Internet Service
body: The Indian government has agreed on privatization of Internet service in the country in a bid to increase Internet users, official sources said here today. There will be no limit on the number of private Internet service providers (PISPs), for whom port and leased line charges will be fixed at "promotional rates." The railways, power grid corporation and state electricity boards have been permitted to lease out their excess capacity to PISPs, who have also been given the freedom to choose the gateway to be used, subject to the approval of the Inter-Ministerial Implementation Committee. "Market forces will be allowed to determine the access fee which PISPs will charge from their respective users," the sources said. The central government has adopted the Internet privatization policy to increase the number of Internet users in the country from 40,000 to between 1.5 million and 2 million by the turn of the century, the sources stressed.

title: Microsoft Nears Deal to Invest in Cable TV
body: The software giant Microsoft Corporation is close to an agreement to invest up to 1 billion unitedstates dollars in the cable television operations of U S West, a regional Bell telephone company, the New York Times reported today. Microsoft would buy as much as 6.3 percent of U S West's cable business at the current stock price. More important, it would further the software giant's strategy of turning the nation's cable systems into the primary providers of high-speed access to the Internet --with Microsoft hoping to control the cable TV customers to get on line. In June, it said, in a similar deal, Microsoft agreed to pay about the same amount for an 11.5 percent stake in another big cable company, the Comcast Corporation. It was also in close talks with the cable company Tele-Communications Inc. (TCI). All its efforts were to press the cable industry to make the large investments in the digital technology and set-top boxes necessary for updating their high-capacity networks for widespread Internet use. The software maker also tried to convince the cable TV providers that money spent on Internet technology will pay off in the future. Already, the news has improved the cable industry's status with Wall Street, having driven up the stock prices of many cable companies, according to the report. The company also spent 425 million unitedstates dollars earlier this year to acquire WebTV Networks Inc., an Internet service provider, and it is said to be working on ways to blend WebTV's set-top technology with the Windows CE operating systems.

title: yearender: more countries get wired to the net
body: the year 1997 has seen more countries getting wired and more people jumping online as computer networking gains greater momentum throughout the world.  such terms as internet, intranet and extranet are acquiring more and more currency among political leaders, business executives and the man in the street.  while the developed nations try to sharpen their competitive edge in the networking business, the developing ones, becoming more aware of the huge "net" potential, are trying desperately to catch up.  nowadays you can do virtually anything in the virtual world of cyberspace. networking has breathed new life into almost all facets of life, from industry, agriculture, telecommunications, transportation to education and entertainment.  in 1996, the value of electronic commerce conducted over the net totaled nearly 3 billion unitedstates dollars. the value is expected to increase annually by 100 percent in the coming years.  "the internet is going to change everything, and at a pace we have never seen before," said john chambers, ceo of the california-based cisco systems.  in canada and the unitedstates where the net was born, internet use doubled over the 18 months ending in march, according to a survey by commercenet/nielsen media research, almost one out of four --23 percent of people over the age of 16 --in the two countries now use the internet as opposed to only 10 percent in the fall of 1995, the survey said.  the european union, somewhat lagging behind in recent years, has proposed laws to promote the internet.  the european commission, the eu's executive arm, plans to increase investment in research and development, develop computer networks and encourage start-up ventures to help make the eu more competitive.  in asia, the region that witnessed the fastest economic growth, networking is also booming.  at the end of october, china had more than 100 internet service providers and 600,000 online users, said lu xinquan of the information task force under the country's state council.  china plans to inject an annual 100 billion yuan (about 12 billion dollars) in 1996-2000 to build fiber-optic cables and satellite communications facilities.  by the end of this century, all residents of singapore will be connected by a high-speed, broad-band network.  malaysia's construction of a multimedia super corridor in and around the capital of kuala lumpur is gaining steam. cyberjava city, a high-tech manufacturing area where homes and buildings will be equipped from the start to send, receive and process electronic information, held a ground-breaking ceremony recently.  cambodia, still struggling to rebuild itself from the rubble of war and unrest, established a full-time internet connection in may.  africa is also stepping up internet development. five west african nations passed a declaration in april calling for expedited establishment of the net in the region.  nevertheless a formidable disparity still remains between the developed and the developing countries in computer networking.  according to a report released by the international telecommunications union in september, two-thirds of the world's internet users are in the unitedstates and canada, 21.9 percent on the european continent, 6.3 percent in asia and 3.7 percent in oceania. internet users in latin america and africa account for only 1 percent and 0.6 percent of the total respectively.  although the yawning gap cannot be bridged easily or soon, the developing countries are not without opportunities.  developing countries can embark from a better established starting point and thereby avoid the pitfalls encountered by their developed counterparts.  networking needs many specialized talents. developing nations such as china and india, with a large number of specialists in computer softwares and related fields pooled over the years, are capable of competing with the developed countries.  networking technology has advanced the development of network computers, the production of which is relatively simpler. the developing countries are able to capitalize on this opportunity to develop and consolidate their fledgling computer industry and related sectors.  more importantly, the developing countries recognize the importance of information technology to economic growth and have put net development on the top of their agenda.  as malaysian prime minister mahathir mohamad put it: "eventually the entire world will have to come to use this new technology, which seems to have no respect for borders." and such a world online will surely be a smaller, and better, place to live.

title: eu-asia electronic forum to be launched
body: diplomats, civil servants, business executives, scholars, journalists, students and web users are expected to join an electronic forum on european union-asia relations in the next two months. the cyberforum will be launched on december 1 by the brussels-based european institute for asian studies (eias) with an aim at strengthening eu-asian ties, it was announced here today. european commission president jacques santer and european parliament president jose maria gil robles took part in today's pre-launch conference. the interactive forum, with a web-site at www.net7.net/eias/cyberforum, will offer not only debates on eu-asia relations but also eu-asia-related news and background information. the cyberforum was designed by the eias with the support of the european commission, the executive body of the 15-nation union, to take the advantage of the internet to meet the challenges facing eu member states in their relations with asia. cyberforum participants are expected to compare notes on such issues as the meeting between eu and asian leaders and two-way trade and investment. eias chairman willy de clercq said at the pre-launch conference that the cyberforum will add a tangible mobilization of public opinion to the positive symbols created by high-level meetings such as the asia-europe summit meeting. english will be used as the common language in the discussion which is also expected to be translated into several other languages to help disseminate information. the eias is a non-profit association founded in july 1989 and aims at highlighting the importance of asia in the future external relations of the european community and at developing a center of expertise on contemporary asian affairs and on relations between the european community and its partners in asia, through briefings, seminars, research publications and exchange of views on political, economic and social issues.

title: civil rights fighting internet hate speech
body: the largest civil rights coalition of the unitedstates and a regional bell telephone company have created a web site designed to fight internet hate speech. the leadership conference on civil rights said today the site --www.civilrights.org --will be maintained for two years with a contribution from bell atlantic. unitedstates president bill clinton made a call two weeks ago at a white house conference on hate crimes to find ways to fight the problem. "you are providing an antidote to cyberhate," clinton told the civil rights coalition in a letter read by transportation secretary rodney slater at a news conference today. wade henderson, lccr executive director, said the idea to create a web site was triggered by a proliferation of internet hate speech by groups such as the ku klux klan and white aryan resistance. bell atlantic chairman ray smith cited a study by the anti-defamation league showing the number of hate sites on the internet has doubled to 250 in the past year. calling the new site "an antidote for poison," he said the idea is to "counter the frightening espousal of hatred and violence against americans because of their race, gender, religious or sexual orientation," he said. henderson said hate groups have become more sophisticated in communicating their doctrines and recruiting. "instead of the street, they recruit on the net," he said. in addition to providing information on hate crimes around the country, the site will explain various strategies to address those crimes and offer materials for young people, parents and teachers to encourage diversity.

title: atlanta internet bank grows fast
body: atlanta internet bank (aib), the world's only full-service bank to operate exclusively through the internet, said that it has experienced a fast growing business since its establishment in october, 1996.  aib has nearly 4,000 customers by november 21, which increased by more than 30 percent from 3,000 in august, a report released by the bank on its web site said.  the number of new accounts has increased by 10 percent since the launching of a new web-based advertising at the beginning of this month, said the report. several thousand inquiries have been received during the same period, asking for more information about the bank.  "we are not altogether surprised at this exceptional response," said d. r. crimes, chairman of executive officer of aib.  "our high-yield interest checking, money market accounts and certificates of deposit have been very well received by consumers," he added.  the bank so far has absorbed more than 45 million unitedstates dollars from customers of 20 countries, including the unitedstates, the report said.  crimes attributed the fast growth of business to the convenience of the bank, low-cost banking via internet and the ability to earn great rates.  the bank also offers interest-bearing checking, electronic bill payment services, seven-day and 24-hour banking, and atm cards.  it expects to offer a full line of consumer products, including consumer loans, credit card, mortgages and brokerage services within a year, the report said.  "the kind of growth aib is experiencing proves that internet banking is the wave of the future," said stephen johnson, president of an atlanta-based bank consulting firm.

title: industry executives predict big day for e-commerce
body: the internet will have as much an impact as the industrial revolution, but it will take only 20 or 30 years instead of 200, the chief executive of a leading unitedstates software and hardware producer said here today.  "the internet is going to change everything, and at a pace we have never seen before," said john chambers, chief executive officer (ceo) of the northern california-based cisco systems, at the end of the two-day asia-pacific information technology summit.  before an audience of some hundreds of unitedstates and foreign government officials and industry executives at the gathering, the first of its kind, chambers made his prediction: "companies who don't know how to use high-tech will be left behind." however, he added, those that do know how to use will get rich at cyberspace speed.  founded seven years ago, cisco now boasts annual sales of over 7 billion unitedstates dollars, 40 percent of which are made over the net.  the 3.2 billion dollars of electronic sales cisco is expected to achieve this year will approach what experts predicted a few years ago to be today's total electronic commerce sales worldwide.  james barksdale, ceo of netscape communications corp., predicted that much of the business now done through the 300 billion product catalogs printed in the unitedstates each year will be transferred to the net soon.  and he said as much as 80 percent of all purchases made have the potential of being done over the net.  while the unitedstates is the leading innovator of net technologies and applications, asian countries are well aware of the potential benefits. barksdale said 35 percent of japan's current seven million internet users have used it for electronic purchases.  in australia, he said, 76 percent of enterprises will have deployed internet by the end of 1998, and that by the end of the century, 95 percent of all residents of singapore will be connected by a high-speed, broadband network.  participants at the conference also indicated that not all businesses will benefit. one such industry seems to be the newspaper business, said australian media tycoon rupert murdoch.  murdoch, whose empire includes newspapers, magazines, television networks and the twentieth century fox film corp., said the future of many newspapers is threatened by a loss of their lifeblood --classified advertising --which he said is "vulnerable to attack by the internet." only those papers that somehow can adapt, he said, will survive.  but he said information technology makes more winners than losers, citing that it has created more than 9 million jobs in the unitedstates over the past decade, while destroying only 2.5 million.

title: australian stocks end marginally higher
body: the australian sharemarket closed marginally higher in a day dominated by the listing of the country's newest and biggest company, telstra corp.  the all ordinaries index closed 8.6 points higher at 2487.7 on strong turnover resulting from trading in the telecommunications giant.  telstra corp's installment receipts closed at 2.67 australian dollars, representing a 72 australian cent premium for retail investors and a 67 cent premium on the issue price.  brokers said there was a mixed attitude in the market, with the shares of profit takers quickly snapped by buyers who saw more value in the stock.  telstra lists in the unitedstates tonight.  telstra trade represented more than half the value of today's sharemarket trade here, at 296.2 million shares traded at a value of 555.7 million unitedstates dollars.  however, it is yet to be included in calculating the all ordinaries index.  national turnover for the day was 532.38 million shares at a value of 1.03 billion unitedstates dollars, with falls outnumbering rises by 554 to 482.  aside from telstra, 480.4 million unitedstates dollars of shares were traded.  the all industrials index rose 38.4 points to 4215.0.  among the banks, anz and westpac were the main improvers, increasing 19 cents to 10.28 australian dollars and 29 cents to 9.00 australian dollars respectively.  macquarie bank increased ten cents to title: games dominate home computers in australia
body: only 300,000 people in australia accessed the internet from home and it was the most popular use for the home computers to play computer games, an official survey revealed here today.  a survey titled household use of information technology 1996, conducted by the bureau of statistics of australia, showed that 2.2 million homes, or one-third of australian homes, had a computer and there were four million home computer users in the country with a population of nearly 18 million.  that was high by world standards, but just 300,000 or 7.5 percent of home computer users were connected to the internet.  only a quarter of the home computer users had a modem, essential for accessing the internet.  and it's likely to be a long time before australians see the end of the post office, or "snail mail" as it is sneeringly referred to by internet users, with just 200,000 home computer users able to access electronic mails.  in a further indication of how computers are regarded in the australian homes, playing computer games was easily the most popular use for home computers.  about 58 percent of home computer users said they played computer games, compared with just 44.6 percent who said they used the computer for studies and 24.6 percent who used it for education.  the home computer also remains the domain of the young: the highest proportion of home computer users were 5-17 year olds (41 percent) followed by 18-24 year olds (29 percent).  only seven percent of over-55s used a home computer.  the pc computers which run microsoft's windows were dominant, with only nine percent using the rival apple macintosh.  the major reasons cited for not having a computer in the home were "no use" (40 percent) and "costs too high" (30 percent).

title: feature: internet opens up new realm in africa (part 1)
body: africa, a continent which is often seen as the last frontier for information technology, is now forging ahead by getting itself wired up on the internet.  for africa, a continent with the least developed telecom infrastructure, internet service has undoubtedly offered a "jump-start" opportunity to narrow its gap with the rest of the world.  currently 47 of the 54 countries in africa have developed some form of internet access --either a local dial-up store and forward email service with a gateway to the internet, or a full leased line service, according to michael jensen, "father of internet in africa" who has been engaged in this field in 29 african countries over the last 11 years.  of these, he added, 42 countries and territories have achieved live internet public access service in their capital cities.  therefore, it is no longer surprising to see name cards or newspaper advertisements being added with email addresses to the time-honored postal and physical addresses.  this telecommunications marvel has just started to infiltrate into various sectors of the african economy.  since tanzania has placed its tourism attractions on the internet, the sukuma museum in the country has become the first museum in east africa, and probably in the entire sub-saharan region to offer visitors virtual tours via the world wide web.  in kenya, manufacturers seeking to export to the common market for eastern and southern africa (comesa) member countries may soon benefit from a new computer service by making use of an email system that functions via the local area network.  in namibia, the ministry of environment and tourism has invested in an on-line booking system, which will enable customer queries and reservations to be processed in minutes.  south africa, the "technology-hungry country" with the most advanced telecommunications network on the continent, is even providing services like internet banking in the country, which is well ahead of the information-rich unitedstates, according to amolo ng'weno, an executive from africaonline, a multi-national internet provider headquartered in s. africa.

title: feature: internet opens up new realm in africa (part 2)
body: ng'weno, who is based in nairobi, kenya, said there are 150 to 200 internet service providers in africa, of which 70 are stationed in s. africa.  africaonline, the premier internet company in kenya founded in 1994, now has approximately 6,000 subscribers, 95 percent of which are small and medium-sized businesses in the country.  in ghana, cote d'ivoire, tanzania and zimbabwe, the company has another 6,000 users to its services. and the number is still increasing by 10 percent a month.  "the nice things about the service," said ng'weno, "are that businesses see an immediate return both in reduced communication cost and in finding things they need. it's very exciting to see people interacting internationally and easily." the picture in south africa is much brighter than in the rest of the continent. it is estimated that the number of south africans on line was about 500,000 in september, and could reach one million by the end of this year.  the country now ranks 14th in the world concerning domain names, leaving behind some developed countries such as new zealand, denmark and austria.  a recent study by international data corporation shows that 71 percent of south africa's top 200 organizations have set up a web server or are planning to do so.  what is more, on-line advertising is the largest component of internet electronic commerce. by the end of the century, the south african internet site development and advertising market could be worth one billion rand (222 million unitedstates dollars) with more than two million rand (about 444,000 us dollars) of on-line transactions a year, noted robin parker, a web publisher.  no wonder studies by the geneva-based international telecommunications union (itu) and the world bank indicate a direct link between efficient telecommunications and economic growth.

title: feature: internet opens up new realm in africa (part 3)
body: however, on-line advertising has only a minimal impact in africa, with a possible total of no more than 20,000 dollars a month on popular web sites, said arthur goldstuck, an expert on internet business, adding that 90 percent of this spending is probably taking place in south africa.  commercial transactions, which now focus mainly on travel, books magazines, records cds, cars and property real estates, still need a long time to take off.  internet, which takes a phone line and a computer unit for a user to cruise down the world information superhighway, has confronted some major obstacles in africa.  africa still has the slowest growth in the number of telephone lines per 100 people compared with the rest of the world.  sub-saharan africa has an average of 0.48 telephone lines per 100 people. yet the number of people waiting for a phone line is reported to be growing at 7 percent annually.  with 12 percent of the world's population, africa has only two percent of the world's telephones, while latin america has six percent of the lines and eight percent of the world's population and asia, 13 percent of the lines with 57 percent of the world's population.  the itu estimated that it would cost over 28 billion unitedstates dollars to increase sub-saharan teledensity levels to one line per 100 people by the year 2000. since individual nations can not meet the cost, it is suggested that the example of ivory coast and ghana be followed, which is to inject private capital combined with a relaxation of regulatory environments.  it is encouraging to note that some african countries have made telecommunications a priority and are installing digital switches with fiber optic inter-city backbones and newest cellular and mobile technology.  these would consequently give a great impetus to net service on the continent.  "internet business is nothing now (in africa), but it's growing quickly," said ng'weno, adding that "it's a business that can only grow."

title: Hong Kong to Apply Interactive Multimedia on Education
body: hongkong's scientists and educators are making joint efforts to promote the application of information technology on teaching and learning in secondary and primary schools. With the advancement of technologies and the increasing amount of information, the use of interactive multimedia would help maximize learning opportunities, experts in the telecommunications sector and local educators agreed at a seminar on the impact of interactive multimedia on teaching and learning held on Saturday. The seminar was organized by hongkong Telecom IMS, the largest Internet Service Provider in hongkong, and Chinese Books CyberStore, a book store which can be accessed through Internet. "Interactive multimedia, such as the Internet, CD-ROMs and Interactive TV (ITV), represent major pioneering technologies in information technology development, and they are capable of providing extensive resources for a diversity of educational purposes," said Gabriel Yu, chairman of Chinese Books CyberStore. Hongkong Telecom IMS Managing Director William Lo said the coming century represents a new world of information and technology and It is imperative to provide youngsters with the best possible information technology education to meet the challenges ahead. The Chinese Books CyberStore will open an interactive book store later this month, through which parents and children can browse books with ease and pleasure at home by categories of subjects and ages. The Rainbow Land Interactive Book Store is a typical example of the creative use of interactive multimedia technology in making teaching and learning a more interesting and fruitful experience for teachers, parents and children, in schools and at home.
