title: hk to combat indecent materials on internet
body: the hongkong government and the hongkong internet service providers association (hkispa) jointly announced today their measure to combat indecent and obscene materials transmitted on the internet.  at a press conference jointly held by the government's television and entertainment licensing authority (tela) and the hkispa, the hkispa made public a code of practice and practice statement to regulate the problem of obscene and indecent materials transmitted through the internet.  this is part of the government's initiatives to address the community's concern over the accessibility of indecent and obscene articles on the internet by children and young persons, tela commissioner eddy chan told the conference.  the code provides detailed guidelines and procedures in dealing with complaints relating to the transmission of obscene and indecent materials through the internet.  the code requires that the members of the hkispa should take reasonable steps to prevent users of their services from placing or transmitting through the internet materials likely to be classified as class iii (obscene) under the control of obscene and indecent articles ordinance of the government.  it also requires ispa members to advise content providers and distributors to provide warning notices to materials likely to be classified as class ii (indecent) under the control of obscene and indecent articles ordinance.  subscribers will be informed that such materials should not be made available to young persons under age 18.  upon receipt of a complaint, an information service provider (isp) will look into it and ascertain the problem. if obscene materials are published, the isp will block the web site concerned so that other subscribers would not be disturbed by the offending site.  "we will keep in view the implementation and effectiveness of the code with the hkispa and review it in a year's time," chan said.  he said that the code is the result of many months of hard work by the government and the hkispa. the adoption of this self-regulatory code of practice and practice statement achieves the balance of maintaining the free flow of information on the one hand and safeguarding the interests of the young people on the other.  daniel ng, chairman of the hkispa, said that all the members of the association agree that they have an important social responsibility to fulfill. the hkispa has 40 members whose services cover some 95 percent of the internet market in hongkong.  in addition to the promulgation of the code, the tela has launched a series of publicity and public education programs, leaflets and a list of filtering software to help parents exercise guidance.  these publicity leaflets have been distributed to the internet users through the internet service providers.  the education department has also issued guidelines to schools on the proper use of the internet. a list of filtering software is posted on the home pages of tela, the education department and the hkispa in a concerted effort.

title: mastercard pushes secured electronic commerce
body: the mastercard international announced today that it has made all the necessary preparation for the secured global electronic commercialization, which is expected to be conducted mainly on the internet.  at a meeting of mastercard's electronic commerce advisory group here today, representatives of more than 30 mastercard member financial institutions from around the world introduced their progress in the card-based electronic commerce.  mastercard, one of the leading credit card issuers in the world, completed the first secure electronic transaction (set) deal in denmark in late 1996. it has completed or is currently executing set pilot programs worldwide to meet the demand for a "reliable, safe and convenient way" to buy and sell on the internet.  set is a kind of software and protocol released in june by major industry players, including microsoft and ibm for internet commerce. it is believed to provide more secured means for online participants in electronic commerce.  "today, electronic commerce is poised to go mainstream," said steve mott, an executive of mastercard.  statistics show that european countries are taking the lead in electronic bill payments. consumers are using much fewer checks than americans.  but countries like mexico and south africa have also made big strides in pushing electronic commerce over internet, according to the meeting.  mastercard says it is now creating a global, commercially viable network of merchants, financial institutions and cardholders to promote the project. it also pays greater attention to the asian market.  china proved to be its second largest market except the unitedstates, according to margaret o'connor, an executive from the company's international communications department. she said mastercard entered the chinese market in 1986. there are now 15 million card holders in china, who made transactions equivalent to 35 billion unitedstates dollars during the first half this year, she said.  mastercard has 400 million credit and debit cards that are accepted at more than 14 million merchant, cash and atm locations worldwide. in 1996, its gross unitedstates dollar volume generated exceeded 550 billion unitedstates dollars.  the company is also introducing other means of payment using chip-embedded "smart cards", which is said to be able to store 80 times more information than a card with a magnetic stripe.

title: zambia upgrades high speed satellite link to internet
body: zambia's leading internet service provider, zamnet communications system, has successfully upgraded its high speed satellite line to the internet in the unitedstates in a move to boost the download speed for customers.  the satellite based service, which was lunched on january this year with a 64 kilobits per second dedicated circuit, has now been expanded to 128 kilobits to meet the growing demand for internet services across the country, according to a press release by zamnet managing director shuller habeenzu.  "we are seeing a growing and voracious demand for information from the internet. the expanded capacity will provide tremendous improvement in the quality of services to our customers," said the release.  zamnet, the first internet provider in zambia says it will be monitoring the traffic levels.  next month zamnet will launch the first wireless internet link for corporate customers which will enable them to by-pass the constraints posed by existing infrastructure.  these developments and other projects underway emphasize the company's commitment to provide quality services at affordable costs and maintain the entrepreneur approach in giving high quality affordable communication services, the release added.

title: lebanese parliament to open internet homepage
body: the lebanese people will have direct access to their representatives in the parliament through the internet and email by the end of this month, the daily star newspaper reported today.  by visiting the homepage of the parliament, the public will be able to read biographies of the 128 members of parliament, the lebanese constitution, the parliament's internal rules and by-laws, the activities of various committees, and the bills that are on debate by visit the home page of the parliament.  mahmoud batlouni, director of the project, said the people will also have the chance to comment on the issues that are being discussed in the parliament, and to make suggestions, the paper quoted him as saying.  however, they will be restricted to the topics of general interest, and kept away from "controversial issues," he added.  as the parliament installs more personal computers to meet the needs of the committees, members, and administration, email will result in easy and efficient communication both internally and externally, according to the report.  "email will provide the leaders and members of parliament with a tool to assist them in responding to constituent concerns," said batlouni.

title: internet development to be discussed in eastern africa
body: telecommunications ministers and information technology experts from eastern africa are to gather here from october 13-15 for a regional seminar on the development of internet infrastructure in the sub-region.  according to a press release jointly issued by the united nations economic commission for africa (eca) and the united nations development program (undp), the seminar will be organized by the the undp's regional bureau for africa (undp/rba) and the eca.  the seminar is aimed to facilitate sharing country experiences, taking stock of progress in internet connectivity, assessing internet services and their impact on development and mapping out future plans to support internet development in the sub-region.  the release said, it is one of a series of sub-regional seminars planned under the undp's internet initiative for africa, a multi-million dollar, three-year project aimed at establishing internet services and enhancing those currently available in 12 sub-saharan african countries.  it also falls under the umbrella of eca's african information society initiative, a comprehensive framework for the building of a development-serving african information infrastructure, and the harnessing information technology for development component of the un system-wide special initiative on africa.  telecommunications ministers from ethiopia, burundi, kenya, rwanda, tanzania and uganda will make presentations on the situation in their respective countries, the press release added.

title: joint internet bookstore launched in macao
body: an internet bookstore targeting overseas chinese has been jointly launched by a macao company and a mainland book export company. internet surfers can reach the "china modern bookshop" at the electronic address of "http://www.modernbooks.com" to get a glimpse of books and magazines published in china's mainland. they can also order books through the email service. johnny sitou, managing director of the sunnyland holding co. ltd., which co-runs the bookstore, said in a press conference today that the internet bookshop service has been warmly accepted by overseas chinese and those living in taiwan, hongkong and macao after it was launched in late august. currently, his company has got hundreds of orders from taiwan and the unitedstates. more than 500 publishing houses in china's mainland have joined in, he said. it now provides over 15,000 kinds of books and 6,000 kinds of magazines ranging from science, military, aerospace, medicine, and qigong and wushu (martial arts). sitou said that he plans to expand the service further to become a global internet chinese bookshop where readers can also find chinese-language books, magazines and newspapers published in taiwan, hongkong, macao and other parts of the world.

title: blair announces 1998 is uk netyear
body: november will see the launch of uk netyear, an on-going high-profile program designed to raise awareness of the potential of the internet as an education tool, according to a press release issued by the labor party conference.  uk netyear was given government support today as part of a package of education initiatives in prime minister tony blair's first speech to the conference.  schools across the uk need both the technology, and the teachers trained to use it, to equip children with the skills they need to excel in the next millennium.  at present only some 6,000 schools in the uk are connected to the internet. the aim of uk netyear is to increase this total to 17,000 by the end of 1998, and in conjunction with the national grid for learning to have all 32,000 schools on the "net" by 2002.  uk netyear will motivate local communities and businesses to become involved in the process, not only in sponsorship and fund raising but also guidance for schools, the press release said.  uk netyear will involve leading companies in the computing and communications sectors, experienced in the application of technology for the needs of society.  commenting on the program, the uk netyear board's executive chairman, david wimpress, said, "we are determined that our industry will make every effort to help school governors, teachers, pupils and parents fully utilized the significant potential of information and communication technology to enhance educational attainment."

title: internet gains increasing popularity in china
body: american pop music superstar mariah carey recently discussed her life and work in an interview with a prestigious beijing newspaper.  but unlike its conventional practice, the interview was conducted on the internet.  more and more chinese people are buying internet access, which has given a great number of chinese pc users more computer options and introduced them to the joy of traveling on the information superhighway.  thanks to listing on the internet, the little swan corporation, a namebrand washing machine producer in wuxi city, east china, had its output value increased by one fifth in the first half of this year and invited two foreigners to be its deputy general manager and assistant to the general manager.  internet was introduced to china in april 1994. a month later, a domestic system was opened, providing four categories of service, including science and technology, education and communications for 150,000 clients.  meanwhile, more than 100 various kinds of non-governmental computer service centers have sprung up across the country to help chinese pc owners onto the net.  the domestic system has been diversified to meet growing needs. a program to exchange information on the supply and demand for idle equipment and means of production was launched in june this year by the ministry of internal trade.  meanwhile, the ministry of agriculture has opened a network featuring information on flower trade. other networks in operation cover tourism, family teaching and food sales.  last june, china opened the first anti-cancer club on internet, by which, cancer patients can obtain advice from specialists, and exchange views on treatment.  thus far, only 150,000 pc users in china have been connected with the internet. the figure in other parts of asia was as high as three million, said zou xiangqun, deputy secretary-general of the state planning commission.  he believes that there is a great potential for computer network development in china in the coming years.

title: microsoft's chinese, english products developed at same pace
body: the end of september witnessed the simultaneous launching of the chinese and english versions of microsoft's latest internet browser, internet explorer 4.0 (ie 4.0), in beijing and san francisco in the us state of california.  this ended the trend of chinese-made versions of the world's leading software producer appearing later than the english-versions.  at a ceremony today, duh jia-bin, president of microsoft (china) co., ltd, said microsoft has all along been seeking to speed up the development of the chinese version of its software.  as a result, he said, from windows 3.1 to today's internet explorer 4.0, the time lag between the launch of chinese and english versions has rapidly decreased from two years. and the majority of the development work of the chinese version of ie 4.0 was done in china.  "ie 4.0 integrates the personal computer and the internet," making it easy for users to search for information either on their pc or the internet, duh said, adding that "this is an expansion of microsoft's concept imformation at your fingertips.'" seven major web sites, such as data communication bureau, people's daily and china economic information, have been pre-installed as active channels in chinese ie 4.0 and are just one click away for users.  up to now, microsoft has more than 300 authorized sales agents, and has a direct technological support relationship with 30-plus software developers, and 30-plus central government organs and banks.  duh said he believes the expansion of microsoft's china business demonstrates its confidence in the country's huge market potential and rapid economic growth.  bill gates, microsoft president and ceo, has paid four visits to china in the past two and a half years. beijing receives a visiting vice-president from the microsoft headquarters every month on average.

title: kenyan firms develop web site for trade via internet
body: two kenyan companies are collaborating to develop a web site that will enable the business circle in eastern africa to trade via the internet. media street ltd. is working with the international courier dhl in the computer venture, the east african weekly newspaper reported today. media street's managing director barney lodge said that www.eastafrica.com will provide an instant window, through which exporters can display their products, and an on-line mechanism for closing deals and collecting cash. a commission is charged for all the sales made through the network but no fee is levied for displaying products on the web site. although using the internet to export products does not cut down freight costs, it lowers the cost of information procurement, said lodge. dhl's role will be to provide efficient delivery services to consumers who place orders through the net. "we are already using the web site to export flowers by courier and we hope to expand into other products including coffee, tea and horticulture," said lodge. the idea behind the web site is not only to advertise goods and service wares but also to educate consumers by providing information about the production process, said the report.

title: canadian exchanges to beef up internet policing
body: canada's stock exchanges are beefing up their policing of stock promotion on the internet, following a similar move by the unitedstates stock market nasdaq.  canada's largest stock exchange, the toronto stock exchange (tse), has announced a two-phase plan to step up its surveillance of the internet.  the first phase is a software program that will take all the "usenet" discussion groups the exchange receives on its server and send them to its market surveillance department, using a filter that highlights tse-listed stocks.  that phase should be in place before the end of the year, according to rob cook, tse's director of market surveillance.  "in phase two, we'll get a web crawler to look for new information appearing on web sites, related to tse-listed stocks," he was quoted by a report today as saying.  the move by the tse came as nasdaq had said it would be increasing its policing of the internet through a search engine, which is designed to patrol the internet for illegal hyping of 4,000 nasdaq-listed companies.  the new tool will be programmed with a series of stock phrases such as "invest now you'll double your money in two months" -phrases people have been using.  nasdaq's new search engine is expected to be put into use before the end of the year.  gerry romanzin, an alberta stock exchange spokesman, said five market surveillance staff there spend up to two hours each a day surfing the net.  "it's a common area of concern amongst all exchanges," he noted.  the british columbia securities commission said it is also looking at specialized search engines to police the internet stock promotion.  yet, one canadian regulator conceded that the fight against stock promotion on the internet will be very difficult.  "we're regulators with a finite amount of resources and it's tough to keep up," he said.

title: cic to run netscape's internet site in china
body: china internet corporation (cic) today announced that it has signed a strategic agreement with netscape communications corporation, under which cic will become netscape's international internet site affiliate in china.  the announcement said that cic will be responsible for launching and running netscape's internet site in china, as well as for localizing information and developing local content.  cic will deliver worldwide financial news and services to individuals and business professionals, and it will also help bring netscape's netcenter --a new free online service announced today --to corporations in china.  ma yunsheng, chairman and ceo of cic, said: "this affiliate agreement represents a major step in the development of online information and services in china and will play a significant role in the growth of the internet and online services in china." cic has been responsible for the creation of china wide web (cww), the core of a nationwide online business information infrastructure project that spans the whole country.  the company has set up a key strategic partnership with china's ministry of posts and telecommunications, as a result of which the cww service is available to chinese internet subscribers in more than 200 cities across china.

title: internet telephony catches industry attention
body: more people are retrieving their voicemail and returning voice messages via laptops in remote locations such as hotel rooms around the world for the cost of a local phone call.  this is the result of the fast development of internet telephony, a hot product in telecommunications, according to jeff pulver, president of pulver.com, a major player in the industry.  pulver believes 1997 is the year of the telecommunications revolution.  dozens of companies with internet telephony offerings will participate in the world's largest public demonstration which will be held monday, september 22, 1997 at the world trade center in boston. these companies will be showcasing their products' compatibility and interoperability.  the internet protocol (ip) voice strategy can save people, especially companies, a large amount of money, experts said. "it is not a question of when, but rather how, your business is going to be affected by the voice on the net(tm) (von) industry," pulver said.  "quality internet telephony is real and readily available," pulver said.  internet telephony software, hardware and service companies including ibm, intel, lucent, microsoft and vocaltec have agreed upon internet telephony standards.

title: internet service providers compete for market
body: prodigy inc., the fourth largest internet service provider in the unitedstates, is making big progress by entering into the chinese market.  the investor's business daily reported today that the company grew faster in the second quarter than any of the other top players. it said that white plains, n.y.-based prodigy grew 18 percent to 1 million subscribers from 850,000. america online (aol), the largest in all, rose 9 percent to 8.6 million.  no. 2 compuserve corp. of columbus, ohio, fell 6 percent to 5.4 million members. and redmond, washington-based microsoft corp.'s microsoft network stayed at 2.3 million members. prodigy's gain moved it ahead of new york-based att corp's worldnet service, which rose 6 percent to 900,000.  analysts predicted that prodigy will have trouble making inroads in the unitedstates and europe, where aol and compuserve are entrenched, the paper said.  prodigy has become the first non-chinese internet service provider in china, according to the report. and it is going into mexico and south america.  analysts agree that international growth will continue to lead the way for unitedstates internet service providers to expand their market shares.  in addition to china, mexico and south america, prodigy has begun service in several african countries and is exploring ventures in central america, the paper said. the company expects international business eventually will account for 40 percent of revenue. it now accounts for just a fraction of sales, a company spokeswoman was quoted as saying.  unlike building a local infrastructure in the unitedstates, the company is partnering with foreign phone companies to develop a network of internet access points in their market.

title: china's development areas join internet
body: the economic and technological development areas, pioneers of china's reform and opening to the outside world, have their own page on the internet effective today. the "window for development areas in china" page will offer chinese and foreign investors information concerning china's investment environment, policies and other pertinent information. the state council's office for special economic zones and the china information association issued an april announcement on plans to create the page. "window for development areas in china" (internet address: http://www.sezo.gov.cn) will be offered through the china economic information net (ceinet) which is linked to internet. the page will offer information on a selected group of highly efficient and rapidly developing areas with favorable investment environments. the 48 areas appearing on the page will include 32 state-level and 12 provincial-level development areas. the page currently offers information in both chinese and english, with plans calling for the addition of japanese in the near future. all information will be updated on a regular basis. the state council approved the first group of economic and technological development areas in selected coastal cities at the end of 1984, and 11 years ago today chinese leader deng xiaoping wrote "development areas are full of promise." development areas have not only recorded the nation's most rapid development over the past 13 years, but have also attracted the largest volume of overseas investment. china's development areas attracted overseas investments totalling 13.2 billion us dollars between 1992-1996. the development areas are facing new challenges resulting from reduced state preferential policies, and are now expected to take advantage of favorable structures created since their establishment. the new internet page is expected to provide a favorable investment environment needed for the further development of these areas.

title: u.s. companies to put video network on internet
body: the mci communications corporation, the second largest player in the telecommunication industry in the unitedstates, is expected to offer a service that will permit computer users simultaneously to receive video broadcasts.  by using the technology of a small new company in seattle called progressive networks, mci wishes to let computer users to watch both live and on-demand broadcasts, according to a report by the new york times today.  although the alliance with progressive networks is another step in the convergence of television and the internet, experts said there are sill considerable barriers in producing television-quality programs by way of the internet. the images are small and motion is often jerky or sometimes nonexistent because of network congestion.  to solve the problem, mci and progressive networks planned to distribute copies of digital video programs to many points in mci's internet backbone. the so-called multicast capability of the realnetwork system will permit as many as 50,000 users to view it simultaneously and as many as 10 million to 15 million people daily to tune in to digital programs on their pc's, the paper said.  the two companies said that the project will be profitable even though they will reach far smaller audiences than are now reached by broadcast television.

title: cbi announces initiatives to meet information age's challenge
body: british business needs to work in new ways if it is to make the most of the opportunities offered by electronic commerce and the information age, adair turner, director-general of the confederation of british industry (cbi), said today.  launching both the cbi's own website and a new cbi initiative to spread best practice, turner said that the uk is well-placed to be a global leader in the information society.  with a total output of 57.6 billion us dollars, growing at around 7 percent a year, the uk's electronic and it equipment sector is the sixth largest in the world and is a major source of innovation.  eight of the top 20 investors in rd in the uk are electronics, it or telecommunications companies, said turner.  the markets open to electronic commerce are considerable and are set to grow at a remarkable pace. fifty million people in 150 countries are already connected to the internet.  it is believed that by the year 2000 there will be 250 million subscribers and the us marketplace alone will be worth 112 billion us dollars.  "companies need to develop completely new ways of thinking and acting to take advantage of these new markets," turner said. "the overall growth potential is huge, but the way in which these markets will develop is still very unclear -that means both big risks, but also big rewards." turner spelt out the issues business needs to consider as a result of the rapid growth in information and communication: --the very rapid development of new technologies; --the convergence of different technologies -telecommunications, electronics, multimedia and broadcasting; --the growing global business competition; --the urgent need for people with the right it skills and attitudes.  turner said, "it's not enough simply to put information about yourself on the internet and think you're participating in the information age. the potential is there to do your business electronically --and that's where the big benefits may well lie." he also announced the setting up of the cbi's information society forum. this is designed to spread best practice and help member companies address the implications of the information age.  it responds to fast-growing member interest, and will focus on such topics as technology in the retail supply chain, knowledge management and valuation, the creative use of technology, as well as a whole series on the specific challenges facing smaller firms.

title: lebanese internet market sees 60-percent annual growth
body: the internet market in lebanon is expanding at an annual rate of 60 percent, a leading analyst of the local information highway industry said today.  mahmoud soubra, commercial manager of datanet, a beirut-based communication company, said a combination of good marketing, better infrastructure and the internet's worldwide appeal has made this industry attractive in lebanon.  "from the demand we have been feeling in the past six months, 60 percent is the rate of internet growth. if another analyst said 75 percent, he might not be exaggerating," soubra said.  there are 50,000 computer users in lebanon, and one tenth of them have subscribed the internet, he said, adding that 55 percent of the subscribers are businessmen, while the remaining 45 percent are households and students.  soubra said that although the web allows companies to advertise their products and offer faster service, most local businessmen use the internet to communicate.  "lebanon has yet to tap the commercial potential of the internet. today most lebanese businessmen are using the internet to send and receive electronic mail, files, programs and images," he said.  he pointed out that the state of the local telephone network is a big factor in securing customers' satisfaction.  "although the modem might read 28.8 kilobytes per second (kbps), there are bottle necks in the telephone network that make data transfer unacceptably slow. this may make a subscriber unsatisfied and prompt him to cancel the subscription," he said.  richard doyle, director of marketing at cable and wireless, the state-run telecommunication company, said a new telephone system will take in more internet bugs.  "some of the old copper wires are in a very bad condition which means if you put your modem on them you will get distortions, noise, and the modem will operate very slowly," he said.  "the new network still has copper wires, but the combination of new modems plus the new fiber optic equipment we are putting in, will result in much better quality and much higher speeds," doyle added.  lebanon has set up two fiber optic cables, respectively linking beirut with cyprus and the egyptian resort of alexandria.

title: middle east business briefs
body: the following are business briefs from the middle east countries: nicosia --the cypriot stock market remained flat this week with volumes shrinking to the lowest levels for the current year.  according to a report issued by the cyprus investment and securities corporation limited (cisco) today, the cisco all-share index closed thursday at 376.7 points, virtually unaltered since last week's closing of 376.8 points and having fluctuated very mildly within the week.  on the very first day of trading of the current week, activity fell to the lowest daily level of the current year of 134,600 cyprus pounds (about 269,200 unitedstates dollars), while for the rest of the week volumes were slightly increased but still at extremely low levels. nicosia --the cyprus planning bureau has predicted that the country's economy will grow by around 3.5 percent this year as a result of increased domestic and external demand.  in its report on economic review for 1996, released here today, the planning bureau speaks of a slowdown of the cyprus economy in 1996 "due mainly to exogenous factors", such as the sluggish development in european union (eu) economies, the rise in oil prices and the further liberalization of world trade.  earlier this month, central bank governor afxentis afxentiou expected a modest recovery of the economy this year, with real gross domestic product (gdp) rising by 2.5-3 percent, compared with 1.9 percent in 1996.  but for 1997, the report says the external environment is expected to be more favorable, with britain's economy projected to grow by 3 percent this year, compared with 2.3 percent in 1996. britain is cyprus' leading trading partner. beirut --the internet market in lebanon is expanding at an annual rate of 60 percent, a leading analyst of the local information highway industry said today.  mahmoud soubra, commercial manager of datanet, a beirut-based communication company, said a combination of good marketing, better infrastructure and the internet's worldwide appeal has made this industry attractive in lebanon.  "from the demand we have been feeling in the past six months, 60 percent is the rate of internet growth. if another analyst said 75 percent, he might not be exaggerating," soubra said.  there are 50,000 computer users in lebanon, and one tenth of them have subscribed the internet, he said, adding that 55 percent of the subscribers are businessmen, while the remaining 45 percent are households and students. ankara --turkish and italian automobile giants tofas and fiat have recently signed a 262-million-unitedstates dollar contract to produce cars for turkish and european markets.  local english newspaper daily news today quoted fiat director general paoto cantarella as saying that a new plant will be set up in western turkey's coastal city of bursa to produce the fiat palio model cars.  but the report did not say when and where the contract was signed cantarella said the designed capability of the project is nearly 1 million cars per year.

title: u.s. company provides free email
body: excite, inc. of the unitedstates today introduced mailexcite, a free web-based email service which gives users a life-long permanent email address on the web. with this move, excite merges what consumers traditionally use on an online service with excite's broad range of navigational services and redefines what an online service on the web is. mailexcite is available immediately, without charge, at http://www.excite.com. accessible through any computer connected to the internet, mailexcite allows users to have one email address for life even if a user changes locations, isps or internet service providers. the user can have a private email account, whether accessed at home, work, or through a friend's computer. mailexcite makes it easier for business travelers who need convenient and constant access to email, college students who relocate quite often, professionals who change jobs but want to consistently stay in contact with friends and family and anyone looking for the convenience of an email address that they can keep for life, according to the company. users can simply go to http://www.mailexcite.com, enter their user name and password and immediately have access to free web-based email that operates similarly to other off-the-shelf email packages. no downloading of software or installation is necessary, the company said.

title: new software moves talkers out of chaotic chat rooms
body: now people are able to move out of the chaotic chat room on the internet and enter a more personal on-line chat, with the introduction of some new software.  until recently, if people want to enter a talk with someone over the net, he or she has to first get into a chat room where dozens of people talking things of their interest, a difficult environment for a discussion just between two or three.  the wall street journal reported that there is a new kind of chat designed for one-to-one communication with someone you know.  these new chat setups are more like a phone call with a friend or colleague.  consumers say they are finding myriad uses for small, private on-line discussions. some companies see opportunities to build the capability into business software.  before long, advocates say, electronic chats will seem as indispensable as electronic mail, the paper said.  about a half-dozen companies have put up such software on the internet for free downloading. they say that several million users are already chatting away, according to the report.  the instant reply of on-line chat provides more convenience than email, in which themail sender seldom knows whether his or her message has been received and read.

title: uk launches internet site to promote tourism
body: a 40,000 page internet site went live in britain today, providing the 50 million internet users all over the world with detailed information on traveling in the uk. the site, www.visitbritain.com, was built by the british tourist authority (bta) with the aim of promoting the country's booming tourist industry. britain's secretary of state for culture, media and sports chris smith welcomed the launching of the project, saying that "tourists from britain and overseas increasingly wish to travel independently. i welcome this use of new technology to give people all over the world easier access to the information they need." the site offers tourists a vast database of attractions, events and accommodation in england, scotland and wales by displaying picture-postcard style images of the uk's coasts, cities and countryside as well as detailed maps and information about its changeable climate. the bta intends to build links between the site and central hotel reservation systems to allow internet users to book hotel rooms easily. meanwhile, the site will also carry advertising, and british airways has already signed up as the first customer. it was reported that tourism is now one of the top five industries in britain, worth an annual 40 billion pounds (67.1 billion us dollars).

title: european ministers agree to limit state regulations on internet
body: european countries agreed in principle today not to impose new taxes or regulations on business conducted over the internet and instead they will largely allow the private sector to play a key role in determining how to run cyberspace.  in a non-binding declaration agreed after a two-day ministerial meeting in bonn, 29 european countries agreed that the potential of the internet could only be fully tapped if national governments reduced their intervention to the minimum level.  the declaration said private investment and standards should be given priority in building the internet; no new tax levies should be imposed on the commercial use of internet; the right to free expression should be protected; and data encryption technologies should be allowed.  but it also stressed that international agreements were needed to ensure that digital signatures on documents were legally acceptable.  the meeting was attended by ministers from the european union (eu) and the european free trade association nations as well as some eastern european countries. representatives from the unitedstates, canada, russia and japan attended the meeting as observers.  unitedstates commerce secretary william daley said the bonn declaration was close to suggestions made by unitedstates president bill clinton for an internet free trade zone, but there were also differences.  the unitedstates requires providers of encryption, or information scrambling, technologies to let the law enforcement authorities have a "key" in order to gather evidence against criminals. washington also keeps a tight control on the export of software with strong encryption.  because a majority of software powerhouses are in the unitedstates, the europeans fear that they will be put at a disadvantageous position in this area and that it will enable unitedstates intelligence services to read their sensitive data.  officials from the eu and the unitedstates are scheduled to meet in brussels wednesday to discuss the future of digital commerce. the talks will focus on issues such as intellectual property rights, the security of transactions, electronic payment systems, data protection and taxation on the internet.

title: israel to introduce high-tech mobile post office
body: the israeli postal authority (ipa) is to introduce 10 high-tech mobile post offices by the end of this year to provide convenient on-line banking and telecommunications services, according to local press today.  the new facilities, said to be the world's first computerized mobile post offices, are linked by a cellular phone line to the postal bank computer. the first such a mobile unit has been very successful in its trial run.  the ipa has shown the new facility to the members of the knesset (israeli parliament) economics committee during their recent visit to the authority in tel aviv. moshe tery, director-general of the authority, said that by the end of this year, another 10 computerized mobile offices would be shuttling around the country to provide services to local communities. there are urrently 50 mobile post routes.  the cellular-linked mobile post offices will provide on-line banking and telecommunication services to 1,000 small communities in the periphery, tery said.  by using the mobile services, customers will be able to transfer vehicle ownership, receive national insurance institute payments, exchange foreign currencies, remit money overseas and buy compulsory vehicle insurance from insurance companies.  postal bank director moshe tepper said the linkage to its central ibm computer would allow customers to carry out transactions in real time rather than order such services in advance.  the mobile post office was designed by a team from masad, or the country's computerized postal branches, with the help from ipa staff.

title: germany, us lobby for tax-free internet
body: both german and unitedstates officials said here today that governments should not levy new taxes on business conducted over the internet and, instead, they should turn it into a "free trade zone." addressing an international meeting on internet opened in bonn today, german economics minister guenter rexrodt said, "we must support digital commerce and should not put it under new burdens." noting that trade over the internet could reach several hundred billion unitedstates dollars by the year 2000, rexrodt said governments should allow the international computer network to develop as free as possible in order to make full use of its economic potential.  rexrodt's unitedstates counterpart, william daley, today also warned against too many national regulations on the internet. "the internet should not become a national market," he said.  unitedstates president bill clinton issued a report last week deciding not to impose new taxes or regulations on business conducted over the internet and instead will largely allow the private sector to determine on its own how it will operate in cyberspace.  daley said the unitedstates and the european union (eu) have more common ground on this issue than their differences.  despite the support for a market-oriented approach, eu commissioner martin bangemann said at the meeting in bonn that the eu still favors a set of minimum international regulations to safeguard the internet against criminal content and to enable data protection.  the organization for economic cooperation and development meanwhile announced in bonn that it would organize a conference in canada in autumn next year to discuss necessary internet regulations.  the internet meeting in bonn was sponsored by the eu and were attended by 40 government ministers and 80 international companies and organizations. on tuesday, the eu ministers are expected to adopt a unbinding declaration to make clear their positions on the use of the internet.

title: australia faces new round of price cuts on telephone calls
body: the new era in australia's telecommunications started today and so did the discount phone deals.  it's australian communications deregulation day, when the country's telephone duopoly, namely telstra corp and optus communications is blown away and the industry is open to all comers.  the reforms are designed to promote competition and benefit customers substantially through lower overseas call prices so as to improve overall economic efficiency by encouraging the efficient use of, and investment in, telecommunications, according to an official industry commission report.  aap telecommunications, australia's third largest telecommunications company but still relatively unknown outside the industry, blasted into the public domain with its offer of up to 55 percent and 60 percent off the costs of national and international calls, respectively.  telstra corp today offered a half-price std happy hour between 5 pm to 6 pm.  it's the kind of high profile phone call deals consumers can expect to see more of, said richard alston, minister for communications and the arts.  according to the commission, the country's major telecommunications companies telstra and optus charge five times what calls cost to provide.  the commission said deregulation should force international call charges down from an average of 1.11 australian dollars to as lower as 47 australian cents.  meanwhile, the australian communications authority had its first meeting today and granted carrier licenses to aapt, primus telecommunications, optus and telstra multimedia.  it said another two licence applications are being considered.  australian telephony is dominated by telstra with about 80 percent of the market. optus entered the telecommunications market only six years ago when partial reforms led to optus entering as the second legislated carrier.

title: hkhk --hk launches narcotics division homepage against drug abuse
body: hongkong's anti-drug messages will be brought into the schools and homes of young persons locally and internationally via a homepage on the internet on the international day against drug abuse and illicit trafficking tomorrow.  commissioner for narcotics clarie lo said here today that hongkong is and will continue to be a strong supporter of international actions to fight against drugs.  she said, "we choose june 26 to launch the homepage to commemorate the international day against drug abuse and illicit trafficking." the hongkong government narcotics division homepage on the worldwide web is one of hongkong's new strategies to steer young people away from drugs.  with the aid of color photographs and graphic illustrations, the homepage is divided into nine sections: anti-drug strategy, drug information, drug statistics, anti-drug laws and law enforcement, preventive education and publicity, treatment and rehabilitation, international cooperation, beat drugs fund and publications.  lo said the preventive education and publicity section of the homepage explains common factors leading to drug abuse, ways on how to "say no to drugs," and substances liable to abuse as well as their harmful effects.  she said that it also provides information on how to handle drug abuse by youngsters and supportive services provided by various government departments and voluntary agencies.

title: hkhk-high-speed direct internet backbone connecting hong kong and guangzhou
body: the first high-speed direct internet backbone connection between hongkong and guangzhou was inaugurated today, it was learned here.  also launched were two new data communications services that employ integrated services digital network (isdn) and frame relay technology.  the projects launched by hongkong telecom and the guangdong posts and telecommunications administration are believed to provide customers of the two places with more choices of cost-effective, fast and reliable data network solutions, sources of hk telecom said.  hongkong telecom's netplus is the first and only internet backbone provider in the asian region to have 512 kbps direct connection to china's internet backbone, chinanet. apart from the new high-speed backbone, there are already direct links to beijing and shanghai at present.  the new link further reinforces the position hongkong telecom as the internet hub in asia and a gateway to other parts of china, hongkong telecom experts claimed.  with the direct link, which will be upgraded to full t1 (1.5 mbps) by the end of this year, customers can conduct business with their mainland counterparts over the internet in a much faster, more reliable and secure environment and to generate more internet based business opportunities.  moreover, customers can also use the internet roaming services already available in beijing, shanghai, xiamen, guangzhou and tianjin.  the isdn services enable customers to transmit voice, fax, video images and computer data simultaneously to several destinations at high speed from 64kbps to 384kbps. besides guangzhou, the service is also available in beijing and shanghai.  the frame relay service also allows for simultaneous communications with multiple destinations via a single access line.

title: libraries superior to internet, research finds
body: libraries are still a more accurate source of information than the internet, thus students should not confine their research only to the net, according to a bar-ilan university researcher in israel.  david schwartz, a researcher of the university's school of business administration, compared materials on various subjects found in the world's three major libraries, the unitedstates library of congress, the new york public library, and the british royal library, to internet researches he carried out on the same topics.  in each case, schwartz said, the representation of the topics on the internet was inferior to that in the three libraries.  many internet sites are profit-oriented, so one can not always trust the information provided by vested interests, he added.  "the internet has opened up a treasure of information for researchers and seekers of knowledge throughout the world, and it has become common practice to turn to the internet as a convenient source of information," he said.  he questioned the effectiveness of internet int is presenting knowledge.  it is a foregone conclusion that the internet will become the infrastructure for a global digital library, he continued, "but this is still years away from happening."

title: german parliament approves multimedia law
body: the lower house of the german parliament, the bundestag, today approved a controversial multimedia law designed to govern commercial on-line services through the international computer network internet.  parliamentarians of the bonn's ruling parties said the law would provide a useful legal tool to strengthen data protection and block the distribution of pornography and material that glorifies violence over the internet.  what is unique internationally is that the law would provide protection for the so-called digital signature to ensure personal identities vital for on-line services like home-banking and home-shopping.  private certification units under state supervision would be charged with the tasks to prove the genuineness of the digital seals on demand.  the law also makes it more clear who is legally liable when forbidden material, like pornography or propaganda provoking ethnic hatred, becomes available over the internet.  under the law, internet services providers will shoulder full responsibility for the content of their own services. and if their services were used by customers to provides the forbidden material, the providers would only be held responsible when they know the content in advance and do nothing to block the material when it is technically possible.  parliament members of the main opposition in bonn, the social democratic party (spd), abstained from voting on the law, saying that it is not powerful enough to put private enterprises under control. another opposition party, the greens, voted against the law, saying that it would undermine the international competitiveness of german enterprises.  the law also faces strong opposition from german internet services providers who warn that the legislation could put their business in even greater legal danger and force them to move their operations to other countries.  the multimedia law is still scheduled to be voted on july 4 in the bundesrat, the upper house of the german parliament, where the spd controls a majority.

title: internet to offer s. africans cheaper phone calls
body: south africans will enjoy much cheaper international telephone calls when the global internetwork service is introduced in south africa next month, the local daily "business day" reported today.  the launch of internet service will see the price of international calls fall 80 percent in some cases to equal the cost of local calls, the report said.  the two-way system, which is capable of transmitting voice, fax, video and data via the internet, would not require the caller or recipient to have a computer, ivan fafandjel, the local presentative of call-back operator unitedstatesa. global link was quoted as saying.  the system transforms analogue voice tones to digital signal for transmission over the internet. the digital signal is reconverted to analogue for transmission over the local telephone service.  fafandjel said the discounted call rate is expected to attract strong support from local private and business users.  however, the plan has been slammed by south africa's state-owned telephone company, telkom, which stands to lose valuable long-distance call revenue.  rhynie greef, the managing executive of telkom's international business unit, said the use of the internet for voice communications was in direct conflict with telkom's exclusive rights to provide fixed-line voice communication services.  he referred to operators that used the system as "pirates", taking what was not theirs and investing nothing in the establishment or maintenance of the local telecommunications net work.

title: kenya raises payments for internet firms
body: higher payments recently introduced by the kenyan government for all internet services providers may reduce the number of users and force smaller operators out of the market, the "east african" reported today.  all internet services providers in the country will pay a five-year leasing fee of 8,200 unitedstates dollars from now to the kenya posts and telecommunication corporation (kptc) for connection to the high-speed 64-kilobyte international line, said the report.  moreover, all providers will be charged an annual interim payment of 4,716 dollars or one percent of their gross turnover.  firms will also be expected to provide a list of all users and their addresses to the communications commission of kenya, said the report.  the report quoted industry sources as saying that while most internet companies have already complied with the new licensing conditions, concern is mounting over the smaller companies' ability to meet the new payment requirement.  multinational services providers have claimed that the requirement that they hold only up to 70 percent in local subsidiaries would discourage foreign investment in the sector in the eastern african country.  during an internet workshop held here last week, participants complained about the high charges and called for an urgent meeting between kptc and all internet service providers to review them.  fred bukachi, a senior official at the east african internet association, warned that unless the licensing charges were revised, kenya's on-line business would be dominated by foreign companies.  small non-profitable bodies such as public institutions, community-based groups and civil organizations interested in setting up non-commercial internet services, particularly in the rural areas, would be discouraged by the charges, he said.  however, lucas kenani, a kptc assistant manager, said the internet providers can pass the costs to consumers by adjusting their prices which are already 10 to 20 percent higher than in europe or the unitedstates.  the flat monthly fee covering unlimited usage of internet services differs from company to company, with the upper limit being 188 dollars a month while unlimited email usage costs 47 dollars a month.  the average cost of internet connection and installation is about 19 dollars in kenya where the internet computing industry is estimated to have an annual growth rate of between 50-60 percent with about 5,000 subscribers.  the sector is dominated by africa online and form-net africa.  basic services they provide include email, world wide web access, email-to-fax or faxaway and paging and designer products targeting specific clients.

title: information technology exhibition sees fast-growing computer market in kenya
body: thousands of enthusiastic kenyans swarmed into the sixth africa information technology exhibitions and conferences (aitec) which is to end here later today, a symbol of the fast-expanding computer market in kenya and the continent.  the three-day aitec, the largest since it started in harare in 1987, attracted 67 exhibitors this year with the most advanced software, hardware, telecommunication systems and office equipment displayed and more than 2,000 visitors coming in a day.  the aitec was attended by 30 exhibitors with more than 7,000 visitors.  "it has been a resounding success… the outstanding feature of the show, besides tremendous exposure of the internet, is the atmosphere of friendship and cooperation between exhibitors and visitors," said sean moroney, head organizer of aitec.  "all exhibitors have been very pleased with quality of visitors and many have reported positive sales results already," he said.  according to kenya-based africa online, a premier internet service provider in africa with offices in ghana, cote d'ivoire, tanzania, uganda and zimbabwe, their visitors are curious about the new technological advancement and most of them are keen on doing serious business.  "we have sold over 10 subscriptions already," said a representative of the firm.  "there is a big potential of the computer market in both kenya and africa," a manager from the comtech system limited company, one of all the seven local dealers here for world-famous compaq, told xinhua.  "we are very optimism. the market here is very strong and expands very fast," he said. his company sold 500 computer sets in kenya last year.  computech, another local dealer of compaq, sold some 1,000 computer sets in 1996. compaq now holds more than 20 percent share of the kenyan computer market.  now there are more than 300 information technology companies in kenya which holds 60 percent of the computer market in the eastern african region partly as a result of the economic liberalization in recent years.  duties on imported computer-related products stand at five percent, the lowest in east africa, said an ibm officer at the show.  currently there are estimatedly 240,000 computer sets operating in kenya. the internet users reached 5, 000 in nairobi with a total of 11 internet service providers.  the kenyan government has introduced a number of specialized courses such as computer science, information technology and management information services in national polytechincs and other technical training institutions in the country.  the computer companies participating at the show also include carl bro, gath management, abacus, modern business communications, microsoft, copycat, dec and other giants in the field.
