title: macao to establish information network center
body: a joint information network center will be established in macao before the end of this year to facilitate the exchange of information between china's interior areas and macao, and other parts of the world.  an agreement was signed here wednesday by three parties involved --the macao foundation, china's state science and technology commission (sstc) and the macao-based international institute of software technology of the united nations university.  according to the agreement, the sstc will provide computers, the un institute will supply technical services, and the macao foundation will be in charge of management of the macao information-net center.  wu guoxiang, an expert who signed the agreement on behalf of the sstc, said that the center will enable users of the internet to have a quicker access to information on china's interior areas and macao.  "it is now difficult to get access to information about china via the internet in china because communications facilities are not so good," wu told xinhua. "macao's communications facilities, however, are much better." world internet users can, via the center, get a quicker contact with relevant departments in china's interior areas while the latter can spread information on science and technology, economic affairs and business information via the center, he said.  the center will also benefit macao, he added. it will help spread information about macao, expand its information service so that macao will gradually become a hub of international business service.  wu said that the center is set to start operation before 1998 as further negotiations are still under way.

title: pm calls on every adult singaporean to master information technology
body: singapore prime minister goh chok tong said today that singaporeans must keep pace with technology and urged the country's adults to learn how to use information technology (it).  speaking at the opening of the public service exhibition, the prime minister said that the message of the exhibition is that singaporeans must keep pace with technology and adapt to the changes in order to stay ahead.  noting that the younger generation is being equipped to handle the new technology, goh said however that it is not enough that only children learn how to use the information technology. "adults have to use it as well", he stressed.  the number one reason for this, as he said, is that the children need guidance. "a responsible parent must seek to learn about the world of the internet," he said.  "the largely unregulated internet is overflowing with information for all kinds of purposes and audiences. our children need guidance in navigating the internet. we must teach them to choose and use information wisely," he explained.  in addition, he said, adults must set a good example of willing to learn at whatever age. "we too must be learners if we want our children to love learning", the prime minister urged.

title: vietnam regulates internet connection market
body: all foreign and domestic establishments in vietnam wishing to disseminate information on the international information highway (internet) will need to obtain permission from the ministry of culture and information, local press reported today.  according to a latest decision by the ministry which took effect on may 21, all law-making, law executive and justice agencies as well as state-run research and training institutes, administrative offices and national data banks are not allowed to connect to the internet.  diplomatic missions or consulates as well as representatives of international, inter-and non-governmental organizations, and foreign news agencies and newspapers are required to get confirmation from vietnam's foreign ministry when applying for internet connection permits.  other foreign economic and cultural establishments, including joint ventures, must submit their operation or investment licenses and foreign employee registration certificates for the site where information will be launched on the net.  a formal request from the organ in charge is needed for domestic applicants.  all applications must be submitted to the ministry's press department which must give a response 15 days after receiving the application.

title: memo signed to regulate internet domain name registration
body: some 150 delegates from all over the world signed a memorandum of understanding here today to regulate registration of generic internet top level domain names (gtlds) after a three-day meeting.  the self-regulatory framework under the memorandum consists of the depository of the gtld memorandum, a gtld policy advisory body, a gtld policy oversight committee, a council of registrars and administrative domain name challenge panels.  for the time being, the memorandum will cover only seven newly-created gtlds: .firm, .store, .web, .arts, .rec, .info and .nom, and their registrars.  before the expiration of an agreement giving the unitedstates-based network solutions inc monopoly on registration of .com, .org, and .net, the three existing domains and its registrars will not be subject to the memorandum.  under pressure, the national science foundation, a unitedstates government entity, has announced that it will not renew the agreement when it expires in march 1998.  the memo will not cover the two-character tld name space within the domain name system, which is reserved for iso 3166 country codes from .af for afghanistan to .zw for zimbabwe, and some other special tlds.  delegates to the geneva meeting have arrived at no agreement on the issue of selecting 28 registrars among seven regions in the world by lottery as recommended by the internation ad hoc committee to the session.

title: us computer company shows great interest in china
body: the chairman and ceo of sun microsystems, inc., one of the world's leading network computer enterprises, says here today that his company will invest billions of us dollars on the exploitation of computer network technology in china in the "foreseeable future." scott mcnealy said at a press conference that china is in the enviable position of being poised to gain from the internet like no other country before it.  "china's leaders have the vision to create an infrastructure built on the very latest technology that not only optimizes performance and accelerates the population's access to it but also enables the internet to be a vehicle for viable electronic commerce," mcnealy said.  he also expressed his eagerness to share sun's knowledge and experience in this area with china.  as an internet pioneer, sun technology helped form the backbone of the explosive growth of the global information network. sun's java, a platform-independent programming environment that was designed for the internet and corporate network computing, allows developers to create applications that can be adapted to any computer system.  with offices in beijing, shanghai, guangzhou, chengdu and hongkong, sun's global strategic area is china's inland areas and hongkong.

title: sub-saharan countries get undp fund for internet
body: eight sub-saharan african countries will benefit from a 10.2-million-unitedstates-dollar fund from united nations development program (undp) for internet services.  these countries include nigeria, sierra leone, gambia, burkina faso, gabon, congo, sao tome and principe and cape verde, according to the guardian today.  to benefit from the fund, countries will have to provide a counterpart fund that is 50 percent of the undp amount, said richard kerby, the information manager of the undp africa regional bureau.  thirty-one african countries are currently said to be linked with internet, but most of them including nigeria can only access the gateway through foriegn internet service providers, the newspaper said.  only south africa, ghana, cote d'ivoire, kenya, mauritius, senegal, zambia and zimbabwe have full internet connectivity, it added.  ray akwule, a professor from the goerge mason university of the unitedstates was quoted as saying that the lack of knowledge rather than funds and technology accounted for the underdevelopment of internet in africa.  on the other hand, richard kerby said, the lack of adequate telecommunications infrastructure and enabling policy environment is preventing african countries from getting more international support in development internet services.

title: hka042246 --hk telecom to offer high-speed digital data service
body: hongkong telecom today signed a memorandum of understanding with att to provide a high-speed digital international private line service which will benefit internet service providers, financial institutions and other multinational companies.  according to hongkong telecom, transmission speed of the new service will reach 44.737 mbps and marks the first such agreement for high speed, high-bandwidth transmission between hongkong and the unitedstates.  under the agreement, hongkong telecom international and att are responsible for the development of the network architecture so that proper maintenance, testing provisioning, service performance and other related issues will be addressed.  in addition, both parties will provide the necessary technical modifications and share management of the international portion of their respective services.  work on the service is expected for completion by the third quarter of this year.  alistair grieve, deputy chief executive, said that the agreement clearly signifies hongkong telecom's commitment to enhancing the territory's international connectivity which reinforces hongkong's position as the hub of asia.  he said that the new service will help meet the needs of customers for high speed transmission and it enables multinational business to send and receive large amounts of digital data at speeds of up to 45 million bits per second, the equivalent of transmitting the contents of a set of encyclopedia once every 15 seconds.  typical service applications include internet, multimedia, video imaging and lan-to-lan interconnection, and cad/cam.

title: hong kong 1997 web site launched in hk
body: the hongkong 1997 web site, developed by china internet, was launched here today to provide comprehensive information on all the activities and celebrations associated with hongkong's handover.  the web site includes information in chinese and english about the history of hongkong, a pictorial history, hongkong archives, the first chief executive of the hongkong special administrative region (hksar), major events in hongkong and a hongkong encyclopedia.  editorial content has been contributed by the xinhua news agency, which has provided the web site with a comprehensive review of hongkong --its past, present and future.  a unique section, a pictorial history of hongkong, is also featured, with some historical archive photographs available for public viewing for the first time.  the web site is also a partnership with some of the world's most prestigious multinational corporations including oracle, sun microsystems, china telecom, ibm, bay networks, netscape, intel, mitsubishi electric, hongkong telecom, microsoft, kodak, unitedstates robotics and poppe tyson interactive.  a comprehensive and up-to-the minute handover news and photo service will be featured on the site. it has been planned that from late june onward, live on-line coverage of key events will be provided on a daily basis.  speaking at the ceremony on behalf of the advisors to the hongkong 1997 web site, raymond ch'ien, member of the hk sar executive council, said the web site is the result of an international corporate initiative and is designed to be a gift for hongkong and a recognition of the contributions of all its people.  he said it gives the world a comprehensive view of hongkong, a forward-looking, cosmopolitan city that will be world-leading in the 21st century.  zhang junsheng, deputy director of the xinhua news agency hongkong branch, and rita fan, president of the hk sar provisional legislative council, attended the launching ceremony of the web site.

title: more people to surf internet for purchasing
body: more than 10 million people will regularly make purchasing on internet by the year 2000, according to a survey by a unitedstates research group recently.  "we are about to experience a fundamental change in marketing and in how we approach the internet," said j. neil weintraut, founder of the 21st century internet partners.  the on-line marketplace recorded 300 million unitedstates dollars in commerce in 1996.  the survey involving 100 of the nation's foremost marketing, advertising and media experts, who met recently to debate the future of on-line commerce.  while 22 percent of survey respondents felt internet commerce would become a profitable industry by 2000, 43 percent felt internet commerce would not be a profitable business for most companies until after the turn of the century. marketers and advertisers are trying to decide how and when their investment in new media will pay off.  the experts polled all agreed that there are still serious barriers to the web becoming a mature retail medium.  twenty-four percent of respondents who thought the most serious barrier was that many products cannot be fully experienced on the web. other barriers noted included the difficulty of using the web for purchasing transactions, and the perception by consumers of a lack of "iron clad" credit card security.

title: chinese, us libraries to sign cooperation pact
body: for the first time, a cooperation pact will be signed on april 21 in shanghai, china, between public libraries in china and the unitedstates.  the announcement was made by gary e. strong, director of the queens borough public library in new york, while meeting xinhua correspondents here today.  strong said that he would go to shanghai on april 18 to sign with ma yuanliang, director of the shanghai library, this first-time international agreement enabling the exchange of library materials. in addition to books and exhibits, he added, the library materials would include information that will be accessible via the internet.  the queens library, the highest-circulation public library(15 million items), is on the cutting edge of information technology.  for internet users in the unitedstates, the information disclosed by the shanghai library will be accessible through "worldlinq", a new electronic information system developed by queens borough public library.  the queens library is the only public library in this country which offers "net users" easy access to chinese home pages in both chinese and english. the library also has the largest chinese collection in the unitedstates for general readers--102,000 items.

title: internet shopping service opens in hk
body: aeon world, an internet shopping service jointly run by aeon credit service (asia) co.  ltd, ibm china-hongkong corporation and mitsubishi corporation (hongkong) ltd., opened in hongkong this week.  as the first internet shopping mall in asia and pacific region, aeon world is built and managed by ibm with aeon credit service handling the marketing and clearing function for the transactions process.  mitsubishi corporation will cooperate in the recruitment of merchants to the mall.  aeon world has attracted a number of shopping companies including jusco department store, yaohan best (electronics), city super, challenger (car beauty and maintenance service), fujitsu (software and personal computers) and a andrews (catalog sales).  yoshiaki ishii, chairman and managing director of mitsubishi corporation (hk) ltd., said that aeon world is introducing a new era of shopping in hongkong as it combines the excitement of shopping in hongkong with the convenience of the desktop computer.  he said that it provides hongkong's shoppers with access to a range of shops with all the convenience over the internet 24 hours a day.  once a customer makes his purchase, the payment transaction will be automatically handled by the merchant and the clearing bank and no additional action is required by the customer, he said.  financial transactions of the aeon world will be handled through secure electronic transaction (set), a complex encryption procedure allowing the credit card payment to pass through the clearing bank in a secure environment.

title: Quicker, Greener Access to HK Government Information
body: The Daily Information Bulletin (DIB), issued by the hongkong Government Information Services (GIS), has been uploaded onto the Government Home Page on the Internet since April 1. Internet users can now read the DIB, which covers all the press releases and regular statistics and figures issued through GIS by various government departments, under the News Update of the Page. A GIS spokesman said today that the new arrangement was environment-friendly, as more than 3.1 million sheets of A4-size paper could be saved each year, not to mention the postage, labor and other costs incurred in printing and mailing. At present, 853 copies of the Chinese and English versions of the DIB are sent daily to subscribers, including local and overseas public organization, consulates and the business community. It will no longer be sent to subscribers in the form of hard copies from May 1. "Internet users can now view the DIB the day immediately after the press releases have been issued, compared with two or three days through the normal mailing method," the spokesman said. "Major press releases issued by policy branches and government departments have already been included in the Internet since the end of 1995, yet the launch of the DIB on the Internet provides a more comprehensive set of government press releases which Internet users might find useful." The News Update in the Government Home Page attracted more than 5,400 visitors in March.

title: Roundup: Nepal's Bitter-Sweet Access to Information Highway
body: Tourists from western countries often found to their surprise that there are almost as many computer service companies as travel agencies in downtown streets of this capital city of Nepal. Despite one of the poorest countries in the World, the Himalayan kingdom of Nepal has caught up the latest development of information technology and has access to the worldwide computer-based communication network --the Internet. With the country's other sectors growing by less than five percent in recently years, the turnout of the computer-related industry is surging at an annual growth rate of over 50 percent. Many businesses of the tourism sector as well as Nepal-based international organizations and aid agencies quickly opened their cyber addresses on the Internet when a local private company initiated the Internet service here three years ago. Travel agencies in Nepal have realized the importance to lure foreign visitors through advertising the country's picturesque Himalayan peaks, exotic cultural heritage and hospitable people in a multimedia way on the Net. It is estimated that there are already over 22,000 sites on the Internet established for disseminating messages about Nepal or matters related to the country, according to local daily the Kathmandu Post. Although many of these Net sites have been created by Nepali students studying abroad or foreign tourists sharing their adventures in Nepal, computer service companies here saw a favorite prospect of the tourism-driven Internet business for local clients and are scrambling to begin their networking service. Earlier the Tourism Ministry of Nepal has set up its own home page on the Internet in order to promote the government's "Visit Nepal 1998" program, which is aimed at attracting some 500,000 foreign tourists in the year. Kathmandu's media circles also showed their enthusiasm for the Internet as almost all English-language daily and weekly papers, including the official daily the Rising Nepal, have launched their cyber editions. The state-owned Radio Nepal linked up with the Internet last week to bring its English news broadcasts to listeners around the World. However, compared with their counterparts in developed countries, Internet users in Nepal have to pay relatively high rates --at least several hundreds US dollars for one year's service. At present, Nepal's Internet service companies depend on the satellite channels of the state-run Nepal Telecommunication Corporation (NTC) to transmit and receive Internet signals, mainly contributing to their hefty operation costs, industry sources said. According to an official of the Mercantile Office System Company, the first Internet service provider in the country, the price of using the Internet has gone down about 80 percent in the last one and half years. If the communication costs could be cut down further, more customers would apply for the Internet access, he said, adding that the number of Internet users in the country is expected to grow 40 percent every year. He added that his company had a plan to establish a national network to provide Internet service to users outside the capital city and had already set up a service station in a tourist destination in West Nepal. But local users have no reason to expect a considerable price decrease for the Internet service in the near future as the government seems unwilling to break the state-run NTC's monopoly over communication links and allow private companies to install their own satellite receivers, service providers said.  Enditem

title: Ports of Entry of Guangdong and Hongkong to Cooperate more Closely
body: Shared information through the Internet and unified standards of commodity inspection are among the achievements hoped-for between Guangdong Province's and Hongkong's ports of entry. A study on strengthening cooperation between the ports of entry of the two places after Hongkong is turned over to the motherland in July 1 is now under way. "The objective is to create a more efficient port of entry mechanism for the increasing trade and passenger flows of the two localities", said a participant of a national ports of entry work conference which opened here today. Under the principle of "one country, two systems", safeguarding the national interests, and facilitating the flow of goods and people, the plan calls for complying the work of the ports of entry with international practices. It suggests simplified procedures for cargo and more freedom of passage for vehicles. It proposes to use the Internet to share information on the passenger and cargo flow, and the condition of vehicles. Guangdong is one of the most developed regions of China and the ports of entry linking it with neighboring Hongkong are of great importance. The Luohu Port of Entry in the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone, for example, is China's largest passenger port of entry, while the Huanggang Port of Entry, also in Shenzhen, is the largest cargo outlet. Experts say if the cooperation plan can be approved by the Central Government and by the authorities of the two regions, it can be realized in three stages, possibly between 1998 and 2005.

title: unauthorized internet users face penalties in vietnam
body: unauthorized internet users in vietnam could be taken to the court under two new government decrees regarding the use of the worldwide computer network.  vietnam investment review, a weekly newspaper, reported in the latest issue available today that one of the decrees calls for the establishment of a watchdog body to monitor the internet.  the other decree, according to the newspaper report, requires all users to apply for permission to open a network account.  "it is obvious that not everyone will be allowed to have access to the internet and everyone will have to apply for permission," an official from the directorate general of posts and telecommunications was quoted as saying.  violators of the decrees could be "logged off" from the on-line service and banned from using the internet. in more serious cases, they could be fined or face criminal prosecution, officials said.  so far, while the internet offers a wide range of services worldwide, only electronic mail, or email, and limited domestic on-line services have been available in vietnam.  however, the government announced last year that vietnam will eventually have a direct internet link.  the new decrees are expected to give the government better oversight over the flow of electronic information into the country.

title: microsoft to turn out new internet browser
body: microsoft, the world leading software publisher, announced that it will soon release its internet explorer 4.0 which is believed to make it easier to integrate the internet and the personal computer's desktop.  preview versions of the highly anticipated browser will go to developers this month. it will be ready for the public this summer, according to a report of the usa today.  explorer 4.0 is significant because it puts most windows 95 functions, including the "start" button --which launches programs --right on the internet browser.  the browser becomes the first screen a personal computer user sees.  microsoft said it is also trying to create an open standard for so-called push technology and has signed partnerships to integrate the technology into the explorer 4.0 browser. the push services automatically deliver information from a corporate network or the internet to an individual's pc. by using the technology, explorer can make that information as easy to get as a document sitting inside the pc's hard drive.  the paper said that netscape communications, the leader in browsers, is heading in the same direction. its next-generation browsers also are designed to be the main screen on a pc.  that boosts the already intense competition between netscape and microsoft in the battle over how people will use pcs to access information.

title: internet-linked suicides raise concern in canada
body: the internet-linked suicide by a young couple has raised concern in canada about the growing problem of how to control what is published on web sites and how it can affect people.  those who are not inclined to suicide will never be affected by the suicide information on the internet, said dr. antoon leenaars, a psychiatrist and former president of the canadian association for suicide prevention (casp).  "but those who get the message that life is not worth living, etc., then the internet will reinforce that tendency," he said.  on sunday, canadian police found the bodies of a 21-year-old canadian man and a 24-year-old american woman at a downtown hotel in toronto. a suicide note said the two met several months ago on the internet.  police believe the couple died of an overdose, using a recipe of drugs and pills they found on the internet.  "information about how to kill oneself is a growing problem because it is so easily available in a matter of seconds," said dr. leenaars.  the governments may ban books on how to commit suicide, "but how can they control the internet," he said.  a spokeswoman for the police admitted that police lack the manpower to control the internet for information on suicide, which is not illegal in canada.  she noted that what bothers her the most about all the detailed information on the internet is that the information is available to anyone, especially young children who may be depressed because they broke up with their friends.  to counter the information on suicides, the casp has set up a web site on the internet in which it tries to offer some help to those contemplating suicide.  it contains information on crisis lines, literature and counselling agencies.

title: vietnam to set up national internet control board
body: the vietnamese government has decided to set up a board to control and coordinate the operation and development of the internet in the country, the local press reported today.  the board is tasked to coordinate operations by ministries, branches and localities in the formation, management and expansion of internet operations and services and to control, develop and appraise policies and projects on information exchange on the net.  the minister of science, technology and environment will be the board chairman and the general director of the directorate general of posts and telecommunications will be the vice chairman.  members of the board will include leading officials of the ministries of culture and information, interior, and education and training, the national steering board on information technology and the national center for natural science and technology.  the government has also issued a decree to promulgate a 24-article provisional regulation on the establishment, management and use of the internet.  under the regulations, the government will control the operations, services and entry gates to the internet in vietnam as well as the content of information circulated on the net.  all agencies, organizations and businesses must base their servers in vietnam when connecting computer networks to the internet, and bear full responsibility for the content of the information they disseminate.

title: expert proposes building information security system
body: a chinese expert today suggested that china build its own information security system.  professor qian jingren from the chinese university of science and technology made the suggestion when attending the current session of the eighth national committee of the chinese people's political consultative conference, china's top advisory body.  china plans to promote the development of electronic and information technologies, said its minister in charge of the state planning commission at the current session.  the establishment of an information security system is an important part of this process, professor qian said.  qian, an expert on electromagnetic field theories and microwave technologies, said the explosive information flow brought by the internet indicates that the human race has entered the information age, and network security begins to stand out as an issue meriting serious attention.  problems concerning security include computer virus, steal of secret information, on-line fraud, transmission of unhealthy information, and attempts to subvert other countries through information transmission, explained the professor.  china is making fast progress in the information field. there were only 2,100 computers linked up with the internet at the end of 1995, which sprang five-fold to 11,000 in september 1996.  to better develop information resources, qian proposed that china follow the example of other countries in enacting laws and regulations on information security, strengthening management, and make legislative and judicial explanations.  he suggested china increase research on key technologies and equipment for a high-speed information network when introducing foreign-made hardware and software, and formulate policies aimed at protecting the national information industry.  it is reported that the vast majority of china's high-speed information networks have been built with imported technologies, with most information flowing on them originating from overseas, too.  "a more important thing is to learn to publicize china's own national culture, achievements in economic development, and industrial and agricultural products, and to develop its own information resources in a well-organized way," qian noted.

title: un launches "womenwatch" internet site on women's day
body: three women entities in the united nations system have pooled efforts and resources to create "womenwatch," a joint space on the internet on the advancement and empowerment of women, which will be launched on international women's day, 8 march.  the three women entities are the division for the advancement of women in the department for policy coordination and sustainable development, the u.n. development fund for women and the international research and training institute for the advancement of women.  a press release by the three entities said womenwatch is a gateway to u.n. information and data on women worldwide and an evolving electronic forum on global women's issues in the follow-up to the 1995 fourth world conference on women held in beijing.  the joint initiative responds to a growing demand for information, which can be obtained today at unprecedented speed through the use of computer communication technology. women stand to benefit from these new technologies and to be on the cutting edge of their development.  one of the objectives of womenwatch is to enable more women to not only be mere users of computer networking, but also be producers and full beneficiaries as recommended by the beijing platform for action, the press release said.

title: internet narrows gaps, speeds competition: intel president
body: the internet will narrow gaps between developing and developed nations and accelerate competitiveness globally, intel corporation chief executive officer and president, dr. andrew grove, told xinhua in a recent interview.  "the internet has the power to level the playing field between societies." grove said, "access to information allows the time between decisions to decrease, which accelerates competitiveness globally." giving his vision of the emerging "network society", the central theme of the 1997 annual meeting of the geneva-based world economic forum, grove said the network society was overwhelmingly positive.  "for business and government it is a case of economic competition and development," he said.  data transference was still slow in the present internet due to slow or busy communications links. in the wake of that, intel was designing a personal computer able to compensate for some of these problems.  intel, the world's largest semiconductor producer, introduced its latest pentium processors with multi-media chip technology in early january. the new processors are said to be far better at compressing and decompressing data, squeezing it down so that it can fit into a smaller bandwidth connection.  referring to china's computer technology, grove said: "china is leapfrogging ahead of many western countries." he was extremely impressed with the speed with which china was moving into the "information age".  speaking about intel's cooperation with china, the president mentioned intel's computer architecture laboratory in shanghai.  intel was helping numerous chinese software and hardware developers to develop technology to make internet access more rewarding and enjoyable to chinese speakers around the world, he said.

title: us firm strikes deal with japanese company
body: telecom-japan, one of japan's largest telecommunications companies and a leading provider of internet access services, has chosen unitedstates robotics' total control network as the standard for its nationwide internet project, bi-weekly israel business reported today.  tsion ezra, head of unitedstates robotics' israeli marketing company team computers' communications division, explained that unitedstates robotics equipment will be initially installed in tokyo -the largest installation in the world outside the unitedstates.  ezra added that telecom-japan also placed an order for unitedstates robotics new x2 technology which offers the internet and on-line services at a speed of 56 kbsp --almost twice the commonly-available speed on today's market --via standard telephone lines.  telecom-japan will also be able to upgrade the total control equipment which it operates to support the new technology by means of the addition of a simple software application.  ezra said that unitedstates robotics management expects telecom-japan to be the first company to provide internet and on-line service operation via standard telephone lines --at a transmission speed of 56 kbps --to customers throughout the world.  he added that over 40 telecommunications service suppliers, representing more than 15 million users, have already pledged their support for the new technology.  the israeli golden internet company, which employs the unitedstates robotics network package, has also announced its willingness to join the list of x2 technology users in the near future.  domestic users of unitedstates robotics modems will also be able to upgrade their modems to make use of the new technology.

title: indonesia to market textile through internet
body: indonesia has signed a cooperation agreement with global textile network (gtn) to market its textile products through the internet, local press reported today.  "the textile trade through the internet is one of our efforts to boost indonesia's exports of textile and its related products," lendo novo, an official of the indonesian textile association (api), said after signing the agreement here sunday.  the new york based gtn is an organization of thousands of textile companies around the world. the network also provides support services such as storaging, transportation and technical assistance.  novo said that the internet would provide more opportunities to gain orders and inform buyers about indonesian products as competition in international markets "is very tough".  api's studies, he said, revealed that the growth of world demand for textiles "is decreasing, but its time delivery is shorter. this tendency can be anticipated by entering the internet network." information was formerly distributed by telephone, facsimile and exhibitions but these methods were costly, novo said.  the cooperation with gtn, he said, "is just like moving the exhibition arena into the computer screen where the traders can offer their products and the buyers are able to get their needs in a shorter time." he predicted that if 20 percent of api's 2,000 members had access to the internet, "their contribution to the export volume will be significant because the possibility of getting buyers instantly is greater." indonesia's textile and textile products export increased 10.5 percent in 1996 to 6.85 billion unitedstates dollars.  at present, textile is one of the four largest foreign exchange earners of indonesia's non-oil and gas exports.

title: internet to create new industries, says intel president
body: intel corporation president andrew grove said here today that the internet would radically change and create new industries from current telecommunications, media and services industries.  "such radical changes create opportunities for businesses and economies which can operate in these new industries," grove said in his speech to the plenary session of the annual meeting of the world economic forum (wef) being held in davos from january 30 to february 4.  "these changes are already taking place throughout the world," he said. the internet provides a direct link between consumers and advertisers of goods and services without having to go through an intermediary like television or print media, he said.  also in his speech, grove urged the european government and business leaders to take advantage of their existing infrastructure and substantial investments in information technology (it) as a competitive tool in the race toward globalization.  he warned that without significant national programs and incentives toward increased utilization of existing technology, it investments alone would not be enough to maintain competitiveness with emerging markets in eastern europe.  during the session, grove used digital graphics projected to a big screen to make his statement more direct and demonstrable.  demonstrating a typical day in his office, grove read an electronic message from his computer and then accessed an intel intranet site using the intel worldwide data network to gather more recent information regarding the issues mentioned in the electronic message.  he finally had live video conferences with his colleagues in different departments of the intel to discuss issues of diversity.

title: world economic forum launches global visual network in davos
body: the world economic forum (wef) launched here today its new global visual network, welcom (world electronic community).  "welcom was designed to vastly extend the wef's mission to facilitate high-level, personalized, high-value-added interaction among global leaders," wef president klaus schwab said at a ceremony to unveil the first commercial visual network in the world.  "the central theme this year at davos is building the network society', and welcom is a direct reflection of the forum's commitment to help enable its members to positively shape the direction and influence the impact of this rapidly emerging society on a global basis," schwab said.  the wef set up its own development center, advanced video communications, in late august, 1995 in burlington, massachusetts of the unitedstates. with a fund of five million unitedstates dollars and help from several wef partner companies like dell computer (desktop computers), intel (videoconferencing) and shiva (terminals and routers), wef succeeded in developing the brand-new global visual network.  the wef will provide for the first time its community of global leaders from business, government and academia with a "secure, private, high-level and reliable" global visual communications network, according to a wef press release.  the electronic community will be formed basically by the wef's 1000 companies worldwide and the wef hopes to expand it.  "welcom transcends the barriers of space and time and allows members to hold visual and interactive sessions at any time during the year from wherever they are in the world," said schwab.  the new system is said to enable wef members to open up new business opportunities, facilitate expanded commerce, joint ventures and strategic alliances, and enhance global business and government understanding.  the system uses the same protocol that internet uses, but the audio and video files are fragmented over fast digital isdn telephone lines. only registered users within its intranet can have access to the files. common internet users cannot have access to the intranet while welcom users are still able to login internet servers.  some of the services welcom offers are multi-point video-conferencing both with welcom and non-welcom members, a 24-hour multilingual concierge service, crisis management support, direct face-to-face counseling with world experts and organizations such as the world trade organization (wto).

title: indonesia to join asian multimedia forum
body: indonesia's pt. indosat and pt.  telkom, in conjunction with 11 leading asian providers of telecommunications and internet services, will establish a joint forum to promote multimedia applications in the region, local press reported today.  the asian multimedia forum (amf) aims to promote the development, acceptance and implementation of multimedia applications in the asia-pacific region, particularly through collaboration in cross-border applications, safwan natanegara, corporate development director of indosat was quoted as saying.  "the forum's framework and organizational structure will be worked out in the second quarter of 1997, when more organizations could join," he said.  he noted that participants could be telecommunications or internet service providers, information providers, end-users and other entities that share the same goal.  the other organizers of the forum are firms from singapore, hongkong, japan, south korea, thailand, malaysia and the philippines.  natanegara said the forum, whose temporary secretariat is at the nippon telegraph and telephone corp., will coordinate multimedia activities, including joint development of applications, supporting 'connectivity' to the internet and organizing symposiums and field trials.

title: china has 100,000 internet subscribers
body: some 100,000 chinese people have become subscribers of the internet, a senior official with the ministry of electronics industry said today.  according to a national meeting on the electronics industry, which ends today, about 20,000 chinese departments are involved in information services and more than 1,000 databases have been established across the country.  the chinese capital of beijing alone has 30 internet service outlets, the ministry said.  china began offering the internet service to the general public in june of 1995.  two public networks --"chinanet," launched by the ministry of posts and telecommunications, and the "golden bridge network" set up by the ministry of electronics industry --are operating smoothly.  in addition, china has built four special networks including one controlled by the elite chinese academy of social sciences.  internet is the largest computer network in the world and also the largest information databank.  some 150 countries and regions, including 40,000-50,000 local networks and 60 million people, had gone on-line with the internet as of early 1996.  industrial giant ibm has predicted that 100 million computers, 100 computer networks and 500 million people will subscribe to internet in the next century.  chinese experts said that the hook-up with internet is one of the most important steps to push forward the information-oriented construction of the national economy.  internet provides information only in english, so an increasing number of chinese departments and network companies have developed and will start information networks in chinese, and incorporate them with internet through china's six international internet outlets.

title: virtual bank launched in canada
body: canada's newest bank -the branchless citizens bank of canada -has opened its telephone lines for business, reports said today.  the bank, granted the federal charter monday, enables clients to do their banking by telephone, personal computer and automatic teller machine 24 hours a day seven days a week.  services will also be offered through the internet once the bank can solve some security concern, the reports said.  as a wholly owned subsidiary of vancouver city savings credit union, citizens bank will start by focusing on the toronto, calgary and vancouver markets, providing clients with loans, deposit accounts and mortgages.  in canada, a number of banks have already launched their own electronic banking versions, it is reported.  "we're not opening up an electronic banking arm for a big bank.  we're something completely different," linda crompton, president of the vancouver-based electronic bank was quoted as saying.  as the name citizens bank suggests, it is a bank of the people, "branchless, but not faceless," she said, adding that the bank will offer financial services with a social conscience.  crompton predicted that the new bank hopes to have 30,000 to 40,000 members by the end of the year.  citizens bank has assets of exceeding 450 million unitedstates dollars.  its parent company is the largest credit union in canada with 226,000 members and 3.5 billion dollars in assets.

title: liffe launches improved, redesigned web site -liffenet
body: the london international financial futures and options exchange (liffe) monday launched its redesigned web site, liffenet, which offers visitors ease of use with the latest and most accurate information on the exchange and its contracts.  the liffe said that after extensive modification, the redesigned site is now structured by product sector and uses a simplified navigational system, providing the internet user with easier information access.  meanwhile, the site comes with key generic subject areas, such as contract statistics, operations of the exchange, as well as new and updated features including the most recent ten days of statistical data on liffe's contracts (previously five) and general information on the exchange.  commenting on liffenet, liffe's chief executive daniel hodson said: "the redesigned site reflects liffe's commitment to internet users world-wide who have an interest in the exchange and its products." "as the leading exchange in europe, the site provides the user with more information, as well as easier access to that information. additionally the information is now updated on a more frequent basis," he added.  the web site remains free of charge and is still located at its original address, the liffe said.

title: uk to establish virtual business park
body: britain will launch a project in march to create the world's first virtual business park, where companies can conduct full electronic commerce on the internet, ian taylor, minister for science and technology, said today.  the park, named uktrade, "will put the british exporters directly in touch with customers all over the world," said taylor at a press conference.  he said that the park is expected to boost the country's competitiveness in world trade.  the park, which will have more than 250,000 members in the next few years, will initially contain about 12,500 companies and any british company or organization can register and be listed.  a directory of companies in the park will provide links to the companies' web sites and allow potential customers to make email sales inquiries.  taylor said that the use of new technology in business has improved britain's trade and exports.  some 23 percent of british companies are using the internet and 52 percent more are potential users, a recent survey has said.  the uktrade program is jointly launched by the british trade associations and the private icl, a leading european information technology company.  "we expect the directory to be the first international reference source of the uk business," said icl director dereck sayers.  the icl will provide companies with free entry to the internet and a cd-rom listing as well as a paper directory listing, considering some developing countries.  reports said that free information service and multi-language support will also be available soon.

title: internet's growth slow in business
body: the internet network service has not become a fashion among most chinese industrial and commercial companies, according to an official with the beijing telegram bureau (btb).  there have been only about 10,000 users in the country since the bureau opened the connection service of the internet to the public in 1994, said shao ming, a director who is in charge of the btb's chinanet --the backbone of the country's internet network.  most chinese firms have not become conscious of the benefits of the internet service, shao said.  the domain names of more than 100 well-known chinese companies have been poached by overseas firms, according to today's "china daily".  the beijing-based english language newspaper quoted gong haifeng, general manager of beijing eastnet communication co (becc) under the btb, as saying "such rush registrations by overseas businesses also include names of big hotels and big cities including beijing and shanghai." in general, it costs a company 5,000 yuan (602 us dollars) to register its name with the internet through the becc, gong said.  gong urged chinese firms to protect their intangible assets and legitimate interests as soon as possible.  "improper internet registration of domain associated with chinese companies by overseas businesses is a huge potential threat to the country's international exchange and commodity exports as well as chinese firms' image," gong said.  the indifference is only a transient phenomenon, he said, adding that more companies will gradually enter the internet with the popularization of network knowledge and improvement of the network service.

title: bay networks to provide core for china wide web
body: bay networks, a worldwide leader in the internet working market, announced today that it will provide the infrastructure for the china wide web (cww), one of the most ambitious and far-reaching information technology projects in china's history.  in a multi-million-us-dollar deal, bay networks is partnering with the hongkong-based china internet corporation (cic) to design and implement the cww, a subscriber-based on-line network providing comprehensive business information service to chinese and international corporate users.  based on a network of powerful servers to be located in more than 50 major cities across china, the first phase of the network, covering the first five cities --beijing, hongkong, shanghai, shenyang and guangzhou, is now being installed and is expected to be operational within a month.  cic plans to add an additional five cities to the network each quarter, reaching a minimum of 20 cities by the end of 1997.  launched by cic, cww is china's first nationwide intranet designed to help businesses embark on the information superhighway, providing them an opportunity to keep up with the times and facilitating the development of economic and trade ties between china and the rest of the world.  as a technology partner, bay networks will provide network design, internetworking hardware, remote access solutions and network management software products as well as a customized training program for cic engineers.

title: shanghai turns to internet for technology exports
body: china's largest city of shanghai plans to load its technology export information onto the internet later this year in an effort to boost exports, according to a city official.  other immediate measures for technology exports are setting up a special fund for the development of new and high technology and launching a technology exhibition fair in kuala lumpur, malaysia.  "shanghai's technology export recovered from its doldrums last year and is expected to bring in 500 million us dollars in hard currency this year," the official said.  he revealed that shanghai made a record 400 million us dollars from technology exports in 1996, up 64 percent from a year ago.  normally, over 300 shanghai units export each year a total of 200 items of new and high technology, which the official said has emerged as a driving force for shanghai's technology export.  some of the items were valued at more than 10 million us dollars each, the official said, adding that the export market has expanded to some developed countries in europe and america from mainly developing countries in southeast asia and africa.  as china's largest economic and industrial center, shanghai is poor in natural resources but rich in scientific and technological talent.  the city, with a population of well over 10 million, has more than 1,300 research institutes and produces over 2,000 scientific and technological results each year.  the official said that shanghai will make a greater effort to boost technology export during the ongoing ninth five-year plan period (1996-2000).  the annual growth for technology export earnings has been set at around 40 percent for the five years, to a target of one billion us dollars for the year 2000, with 20 percent of the amount expected to come from the exports of new and high technology.

title: sanyo unveils internet tv
body: sanyo electronic co., ltd.  unveils its internet tv at the on-going 1997 consumer electronics show in las vegas, in western unitedstates.  it will demonstrate on-tv, the personal internet tv channel prepared by its unitedstates partner called viewcall america, the company announced today.  with a single integrated unit and a standard telephone line, internet communication capability and television reception are combined on the tv set.  the user of the internet tv can switch quickly between tv and internet screens at the touch of a button. and special remote control unit operates like a video game controller.  on-screen icons make it easy to surf the net and quickly access the information needed.  viewcall's on-tv is the personal internet tv channel that keeps viewers in touch through email, information tailored to viewer needs and general web access.  on-tv enhances television by giving viewers personalized information at the click of their tv remote, a widely-appreciated approach.  viewcall america also announced today that it has begun to offer local tv viewers with the on-tv channel at the rate of 3.50 unitedstates dollars a month.  sanyo and viewcall america have also agreed to cooperate in the creation of open tv-html standards, hoping to be joined by tv manufacturers.

title: vietnam to link with internet
body: the vietnamese general posts department has installed internet vietnam, which will be directly linked up with international internet, local media reported today.  the internet project has been carried out in two phases. the first phase was the establishment of two gateways in hanoi and ho chi minh city, and the upgrading of the hanoi gateway which will become the country's gateway.  the second phase, to be completed within 1997, will see the expansion of internet activities across the whole country, and an increase in equipment capacity as well as transmission speeds inside and outside the country.  at present, two gateways in hanoi and ho chi minh city and a link with the international internet through australia in ho chi minh city are in operation.  since 1994, the national center for natural science and technology, the science information and the center for science and technology in ho chi minh city have used the internet for information exchange. however, these nets are not online when connect with the international internet.  gradually these nets will be unified into internet vietnam which will supply internet services throughout the country. it is expected that internet vietnam will be officially registered within the international internet in 1997.

title: zhu jiazhi named new coach of chinese women basketball
body: zhu jiazhi was named as the head coach of the new chinese national women's basketball team on thursday to replace chen daohong, according to the chinese basketball association (cba).  chen, who had led the chinese women's squad to win the silver medal in the 1994 world championship in sydney, suffered a disappointed ninth place at the atlanta olympic games last summer.  "there were many reasons for chinese girl's upset in atlanta, but head coach should take the responsibilities for lack of training and tactics mistakes." cba vice-president zhong tianfa said.  zhu jiazhi, who was head coach of the national women's champion august first army team, will be assisted by liu jiz and a standard telephone line, internet communication capability and television reception are combined on the tv set.  the user of the internet tv can switch quickly between tv and internet screens at the touch of a button. and special remote control unit operates like a video game controller.  on-screen icons make it easy to surf the net and quickly access the information needed.  viewcall's on-tv is the personal internet tv channel that keeps viewers in touch through email, information tailored to viewer needs and general web access.  on-tv enhances television by giving viewers personalized information at the click of their tv remote, a widely-appreciated approach.  viewcall america also announced today that it has begun to offer local tv viewers with the on-tv channel at the rate of 3.50 unitedstates dollars a month.  sanyo and viewcall america have also agreed to cooperate in the creation of open tv-html standards, hoping to be joined by tv manufacturers.

title: on line buyers increase
body: a growing number of web surfers visited shopping sites and ordered articles on line last year.  statistics quoted by the journal of commerce show that in 1996, the percentage of people of the unitedstates doing on-line shopping doubled from 12.5 percent to 25 percent in september.  meanwhile, the numbers of home web surfers grew from 6.4 million households in january to 11 million in october.  free-to-download software and sales of computer-related equipment used to drive much of the cyber-shopping activity. but in recent months, things have diversified.  the top 10 shopping destinations on the web include three sites that sell music cds and one bookseller, the paper reported. also, the retail giant wal-mart has emerged as a top-25 web-shopping site.  the continued growth of the medium was bolstered by a surge of holiday shoppers towards the end of last year.  cyber-retailers can use less expensive warehousing facilities.  they are not burdened by the real-estate costs of traditional stores.  men represent the greatest percentage of cyber-shoppers, since most of web surfers are men. and among the top 10 shopping sites, those most heavily dominated by males were computer related.  female shoppers are best represented at sites offering consumer goods.

title: on-line shopping on rise
body: the number of retailers of the unitedstates going on-line has more than tripled in the past year, although on-line shopping makes up less than 2 percent of retail sales, according to a report of the usa today on tuesday.  entering the christmas shopping season, shopping is hot suddenly on internet, the paper said. now 14 percent of retailers are on line --up from 4 percent a year ago, it quoted a survey results as saying.  there are now about 10,000 on-line shopping sites which expected to hit 1.2 billion unitedstates dollars in sales this year.  that's more than double the amount last year, the paper said.  while shoppers have been reluctant in the past to make computer transactions with unknown businesses, a new generation of well-established retailers is luring customers.  "with some big name retailers coming on line, it's making people more comfortable to shop over their computers," says analyst nicole vanderbilt of jupiter communications, a texas-based research firm that estimates on-line sales will reach 7 billion unitedstates dollars by 2000.  items sold on line vary to a great extent, ranging from cars, steel products to books and pizza pies. book stores found their customers on line are among the most enthusiastic on-line buyers.  as protective software has become a standard of internet browsers, concerns about credit card security have declined, retailers say.

title: new internet pricing leads to communication jam
body: a new internet pricing system adopted recently by major net service providers in the unitedstates led to increasingly frequent jam on the internet and telephone system.  almost all internet users in the unitedstates can now enjoy a monthly flat rate of only 19.95 unitedstates dollars for staying on line for unlimited time. it is offered by big companies like the america online, the microsoft network (msn) and prodigy.  the new york time reported today that this new "all you can eat" price is rapidly causing indigestion among network-access providers, phone companies and many customers.  since america online adopted the new pricing, its subscribers had increased from 7 million to 9 million --totaling 3.1 million hours of connection time, the paper said.  because many people are having so much trouble getting on line, once they do get a connection, many deliberately keep the line tied up, even when they go for lunch or during their sleep.  "it is as if a diner at a fixed-price buffet had someone hang onto his seat after lunch, so he could still have a place for dinner," the paper said.  for the internet enthusiasts, the all-you-can-eat price plans are prompting residential phone customers to add second and even third phone lines.  america online is also working around the clock to add phone lines, computers, modems and network connections to deal with the surge.  the phone companies are likely to spend millions of dollars to increase the network capacity, according to the report.  the nynex corporation, the regional bell company for new york and new england, estimated that the number of additional lines was up 14 percent over the past year.

title: u.s. advocates "fair use" of copyrighted digital materials
body: the unitedstates calls for a "fair use" of copyrighted materials on the internet and elsewhere within the digital environment in a public statement to a wipo conference.  according to the statement made available today, the unitedstates wants it to be clear that two new copyright treaties under negotiation in geneva "will permit application of fair use in the digital environment".  wipo, the world intellectual property organization, is having the diplomatic conference on certain copyright and neighboring rights questions from december 2 to 20. the three draft treaties on certain questions concerning the protection of literary and artistic works, on the protection of the rights of performers and producers of phonograms, and on intellectual property in respect of databases are under talks by over 850 participants.  bruce lehman, unitedstates assistant secretary of commerce and commissioner of patents and trademarks, said he made the call in response to the concerns of librarians, educators, and on-line service providers in the unitedstates "we want to make it clear that the treaties we are negotiating are not going to restrict their appropriate use of copyrighted works," he stressed.  at a press conference on december 11, kenyan ambassador mrs esther mshai tolle, the president of the conference elected on december 5, said that the participants spent the first week mainly on structural work such as the election of the conference leadership. on december 9, they began work in substance on the reading of the treaties. consensus through consultations should be reached before the treaties are adopted.

title: canadian defense officer charged with internet porn
body: a high-level civilian scientist in canada's department of national defense has been charged with making and distributing child pornography using his office computer hooked to the internet.  blair evans, 46, a father of two and a civilian employee in the department for almost 20 years, is to appear in court on january 2, local media reported today.  evans, who has phd in physics and worked in a unit enhancing radar images for surveillance purposes, has been suspended without pay.  the physicist was arrested on november 29 when police raided his office at the national defense research establishment.  a computer and about 300 diskes containing more than 20,000 pictures and short video clips of children --some still in diapers --engaged in sex acts were seized as a result.  "i find it absolutely disgusting and abhorrent that anyone can get any kind of sexual gratification out of children who are that young," a police officer involved in the investigation was quoted as saying.  the child porn came from a variety of sources from all over the world, and the investigation is continuing and more people could be charged, he added.  defense minister douglas young has ordered his department "to take every possible measure to find out as much as possible about this problem" and to determine how to control access to the internet.  however, he acknowledged that it is difficult to prevent anyone from gaining access to pornography on the internet.  possession of child pornography carries a maximum five year penalty in canada. a conviction for distributing, selling or making child pornography carries a maximum 10-year sentence.

title: chinese economic information network opened
body: a network that provides chinese economic information hooked up to the internet went into operation today.  the china economic information network (ceinet) was jointly set up by the state information center, provincial information centers and the information centers of various ministries.  it will help add china-developed economic information to the internet, which is badly short of such information, to promote the country's information development as part of the national economic growth.  ceinet will provide not only economic information to the country's governmental organizations, enterprises and private users, but also internet services, such as email, information retrieval and other transmission services.  ceinet will first provide roaming services in china's ten major cities. it has joined hands with a company under the ministry of electronics industry to set up 24 satellite telecom stations nationwide to increase its reach.  the network will provide a variety of economic information in fields such as macro-economic development, industrial and commercial surveys and investment opportunities.  chinese vice premier zou jiahua attended the opening ceremony for the network today in the great hall of the people.

title: china to set up network of women
body: chinese women may soon be making contact with their sisters from the rest of the world through the internet.  a network that will connect chinese women with the world, via the worldwide web, is under preparation.  the information center of the chinese women's college (cwc) is now busy collecting as much information as possible to feed into the network.  the network is designed to promote china's study on women's issues, and strengthen exchanges and communication between chinese women, and women from other countries and regions.  by linking relevant research institutes with grassroot women's federations, the network will also enable women across the country to be better and more effectively informed.  "for example," said sun, "when the world bank announced a plan to help poor women with small loans, we could have sent the information through the network immediately, so that women in poor areas could learn how to apply for the funds." sun xiaomei, director of the cwc information center, said that it is very important to set up the network for the study of women's issues, and methods of information communications must keep up with the pace of time.  some 300,000 yuan (about 36,000 unitedstates dollars) is required to cover the cost of the network construction. the cwc is negotiating for cooperation with some network companies and international foundations.  sun and her colleagues are now trying to establish an information data bank specializing in women's issues. the data bank will include books, newspapers, periodicals published in chinese, languages of ethnical minorities, and foreign languages, papers and audio-video material.  cwc has collected periodicals about women published in china. sun and her colleagues are also checking major newspapers, such as people's daily, guangming daily, for more information about women.  information exchanges are expected to be carried out in printed form before the network is set up in grassroots units. sun plans to mail the first information letter in december to local women research institutes and women's federations.

title: macao promotes tourism via internet
body: macao has placed information about its tourist attractions and related data on the internet as of monday in a bid to woo more tourists. joao manuel antunes, director of the macao tourism office, said the introduction of tourism data into the internet will help promote the tourism industry in macao. "in an era when computer is increasingly widely used, the introduction of tourism data will help people around the world better know macao," he said. "it will also help cultivate the macao tourism industry." data included in the internet page cover macao's geography, history, art, climate, hotels, well-known restaurants, shopping, entertainment and annual events like the selection of miss macao, grand prix, international music festival and fireworks exhibition. in addition, the page has information about the hygienic conditions, currency exchange, tariffs and customs procedure as well as the macao international airport. the tourism office said people may find the information via the homepage address of "http://turismo.macau.gov.mo" or the email address: dstlhmacau.ctm.net. the tourism industry is one of the leading income earners in macao, which attracts about 8 million visitors each year.

title: internet replaces airwaves at broadcasting symposium in china
body: an international symposium on broadcasting and music held in south china today found a new way of reaching its audience.  instead of relying on their usual medium -airwaves, the broadcasters have switched to the internet. papers presented by experts attending the event in guangzhou can be seen simultaneously through the world wide web.  it means that more broadcasting and music industry workers can read the papers and take part in discussions from outside the meeting room.  it is the first time chinese broadcasting people have used the internet for academic exchanges.  over 300 specialists and experts from china, germany, britain, france, japan, russia and viet nam are attending the symposium held in guangzhou, capital city of south china's guangdong province.  topics for discussion include social values of broadcasting in the 21st century, advantages over other competing media, application of new technology, opportunities and challenges faced by broadcasting in the next century.  the symposium is a major part of the '96 guangdong international radio music fair a number of world famous radio anchormen and anchorwomen are giving performances and music exchange presentations during the fair.  guangdong, china's first province to start the reform and opening up drive, has exchanged radio programs with countries such as the unitedstates, hungary, japan, canada and australia. some 90 excellent radio music programs, recommended by broadcasting organizations from 34 countries and regions, have been broadcasted by four major radio stations in the province.

title: beijing opera enters internet
body: chinese artists and technicians have sent the 200-year-old beijing opera onto the information highway.  the culture ministry revealed today that it has successfully put written materials and photos about beijing opera on the internet this week, with the help of the beijing calmar network engineering co. ltd.  this will enable computer users worldwide to enjoy and study the traditional art through networks, said huang yudong, a researcher from the calmar company.  beijing opera is considered a national treasure in china --as famous as the great wall and the capital city's summer palace -for its unique lyrics, recitation techniques, songs, dances, martial arts and acrobatics. as with much of chinese folk art, it is experiencing a setback in today's society.  in recent years, china has been using various modern means, including television and karaoke, to spread the popularity of beijing opera.  the introduction of the internet is a new experiment and will enable more people to understand the art, according to lin ruikang, director of the office for reviving beijing opera of the culture ministry.  ironically, the unpopularity of beijing opera in recent years is partly a result of the introduction of high technology and new entertainment means, which are luring away the young audience.  however, more artists who turned a blind eye to high technology are now catching up with the trend.  huang said that their participation in reviving beijing opera is a by-product of the recent national campaign to promote the art.  however, due to technical and copyrights reasons, it is still difficult to show a movie about beijing opera on the internet, he said. there are some 40,000 internet users in china by september of this year.

title: more chinese roam on internet
body: more and more chinese will roam the internet, the world's largest computer network, to gain information, communicate with friends or play games, according to a report in "china woman's news." the paper said there will be an estimated 100,000 internet users in china by the end of this year. among them are more than 20,000 people who have discovered the link with internet via chinanet, which is operated by the ministry of posts and telecommunications, according to the paper.  a survey in september showed that china had approximately 40,000 internet users scattered throughout more than 10 cities and provinces in the country, including beijing and shanghai.  they were linked mostly via six international lines, according to the survey.  the number of internet users in china has grown rapidly in the last two years --ten times more than the figure in 1995.  so far, internet users at home and abroad could read information and background about many chinese enterprises or cities on the international information highway.  a new chinanet, funded by 80 million yuan from the ministry of posts and telecommunications, is expected to open at the end of this year.  sources said that internet now has a total of 60 million users in 150 countries and regions.

title: on-line fashion news service launched in china
body: a new "silk road" was unveiled today in china -using the worldwide internet. it means that fans of the internet in every corner of the world can access chinese silk and other fabric fashions by clicking a mouse, instead of shopping in department stores.  from today china's leading fashion newspaper, china garment news, launched an on-line service.  the computer newspaper, "china fashion net," is the first internet-based information service in the world for the chinese garment industry. its coverage will extend to the latest works of chinese designers, new products from local enterprises, daily changes in market demand, latest trends in china's big cities, and knowledge of dressing and making up.  based on java language, the china fashion net will use latest moving picture technology and high fidelity background music.  wang zhuo, deputy editor-in-chief of the paper, said that the on-line fashion service will offer a faster and higher-capacity information medium for china's garment enterprises, who are eager to promote their corporate image and products abroad. compared with traditional news media, such an on-the-spot information service boasts two predominant advantages -low cost and high speed.  in addition to a new channel for the chinese and foreign fashion world to exchange ideas, the on-line service will provide a new advertising method for domestic entrepreneurs, he said.

title: over 40,000 chinese subscribers hooked up to internet
body: china has hooked up 6,000 computers and 40,000 subscribers to the internet through six international channels. it gives 20,000 subscribers access to the international computer network by chinanet.  deng zhenyin, secretary general of china institute of communications, said today that subscribers in more than a dozen chinese provinces and municipalities are able to download information from the internet.  addressing a press conference on the china international electronics telecommunications exhibition (ciete), which will be held in china international exhibition center in beijing next september, professor deng predicted that the number of computers and subscribers with access to internet is expected to hit 10,000 and 100,000 respectively by the end of this year.  he said internet services are developing fairly fast since china gained access to such services. the number of subscribers, he said, increased ten times last year alone, he added.  many chinese enterprises and localities now send their information via the internet, and many others have started to publicize themselves through the internet. a powerful information network with interfaces in chinese will go into operation in eight cities by the end of this year.  as an international network for the information superhighway, the internet has attracted around 40,000 to 50,000 local networks and 60 million people in more than 150 countries and regions. it is estimated that about 100 million computers, one million local networks and 500 million subscribers will be connected to internet by the beginning of the next century.

title: government to control internet services in kuwait
