body: service providers of the world immensely popular internet operating in kuwait will soon have to market their services under certain conditions under a proposed managing plan by kuwaiti ministry of communications, according to official sources.  underscretary of the ministry salman al-roumi told local daily arab times sunday that kuwaiti communications ministry is intended to have full control of the main internet up-link out of which it will lease lines to anyone or any company that wishes to be a provider.  he said it would be compulsory for the providers in the country to operate under the dome of the ministry which will be the sole main up-link to the internet service.  "this operation will give us full control of the internet in kuwait, as well as full control of the necessary equipment," he said adding that "anyone who wants to be a provider wil have to do so under certain conditions which we are currently drafting." two internet service providers are currently operating in kuwait and the unmber is expected to be increased.  the fact that no one owns the immensely popular internet makes it difficult for a single organisation or government to mount control on it and it is becoming increasingly controversial in kuwait. this makes it neccesary for the official authorities to set up certain conditions for the providers to follow and start governmental supervision over the services, according to the official.  according to al-roumi the ministry also contemplating drafting a law enabling it to contol certain aspects and services readily available on the intenet.  however, regarding to this, he said unless it could be technically controlled, a law is no use. "if it is made possible to cotrol the flow of certain information, the ministry will formulate this idea," he said.  there are two providers of internet services currently in kuwait and the number is expected to be increased to a mimimum of 10 or 20 in the near future.  under the new operation, government will lease lines to internet providers and the providers will have the freedom to take on as many subscribers as they wish.  this new operation was supposed to have been introduced about six months ago, but accoding to al-roumi, it came up against some technical and financial problems.  recently, however, the ministry has "progressed very well with this project," al-roumi said.  the effort in mounting control on internet services in kuwait is amidst frequnt appeals in the country for checking influence of western satellite channels on the young generation.  fears over growing addiction to western channels via satellite attracted much attention of the media in the country. heads of schools and parents interviewed by a local newspaper recently said satellite channels influence the young generation to the extent of forcing them to imitate the west in every aspect of life even if they are contrary to their own culture and tradition.  the effort is also being made against a recent gulf council cooperation agreement on joint efforts in fighting against western media which they described as broadcasting false reports about their countries.

title: saarc secretariat launches homepage on internet
body: the south asian association for regional cooperation (saarc) secretariat has launched here a homepage on internet, the global information network, with a view to disseminating information about its activities and programs. the internet homepage of the south asian regional organization's headquarters currently includes information contained in various publications and periodicals published by the secretariat and declarations adopted by saarc summits, the secretariat said in a press release today. the page, designed and maintained by a kathmandu on-line service company, also contains selected photographs of important events sponsored by the saarc during the last decade. the saarc, established in 1985 with the objective of strengthening regional cooperation in south asia, groups bangladesh, bhutan, india, the maldives, nepal, pakistan and sri lanka. the saarc internet homepage can be accessed through the address http://www,south asia,com/saarc by any on-line computer in the world. the saarc secretariat will make efforts to develop its internet page and include more information about the organization and its member states, the press release added.

title: china's own "internet" to start operation at year-end
body: infohighway space," a powerful information network with all interfaces in chinese, will go into operation in eight chinese cities by the end of this year.  experts here said the move indicates that this information highway with chinese characteristics will be accepted by an increasing number of ordinary chinese people.  china infohighway communications co. ltd., jointly launched by a number of chinese departments with a total investment of 80 million yuan, will provide beijing, shanghai, guangzhou, shenzhen, fuzhou, xi'an, shenyang and harbin residents such services as network-based education, email, an line stock market, games, shopping opportunities, medical information and other information services covering almost all aspects of daily life.  president zhang shuxin said that the company will develop high-speed connection technology in order to link up more chinese families, schools, hospitals, offices and public facilities in the future.  "infohighway space" is one of the country's few chinese interactive networks. some 2.3 million connections were made over the past year of trial operation.  zhang said that the much-publicized internet is based on the social values, culture, language and customs of the unitedstates, which sometimes run counter to chinese culture and actual conditions. therefore, it is imperative to build an interactive network with chinese characteristics.  by the end of august, china had hooked up 6,000 computers and 40,000 subscribers with internet through its six international channels.  and both figures are expected to hit 10,000 and 100,000 by the end of this year.  some 40,000 to 50,000 local networks and 60 million people in 150 countries and regions have hooked up with internet as of the beginning of this year.  latest ibm figures show that about 100 million computers, one million local networks and 500 million subscribers will be connected to internet in the 21st century.

title: feature: internet craze in south korea
body: just five years ago, few south koreans knew anything about the internet. now they are finding themselves surfing the global network, which provides a sea of information.  the number of computers connected to the internet has reached 36,000, a ninefold increase over last year, with the country's major companies and universities capitalizing on the net to promote their image or products.  the internet went into operation here when a network was set up between seoul national university and the korean institution for electric technology in 1982.  ten years elapsed before individuals with personal computers were permitted to surf the network in 1993.  the number of internet domains now stands at 1,754 in south korea, according to the national computerization agency. it has been grewing at an annual rate of 300 percent from 1990, one of the highest in the world.  companies subscribing to the internet grew four times to 355 over last year. they are taking advantage of the net to enhance their corporate image, promote their products and recruit employees.  almost all south korean universities have opened pages on the world wide web. internet cafes have become popular places among the young netizens.  government policy and news media campaigns to foster an information society have created an internet boom.  in particular, leading news media in south korea have spearheaded the internet craze. the media campaigns have made people who do not know anything about the internet feel left behind.  according to a survey conducted by an internet news provider last july, 38 percent of the web users are college students, followed by science researchers with 17.8 percent, engineers with 16 percent and office workers with 15 percent.  one out of every four respondents said that they click on to the net for news, 19.3 percent are searching the web for academic purpose and 19.3 percent for various purposes.  the performance of south korean network companies is brisk as interest in the internet grows fast.  currently, nine computer networks, including hitel, chollian and now nuri, are offering indirect internet service through their local pc communication networks, while 12 other networks are making direct on-line connections for surfers to the internet.  the major local communication networks --dacom, korea telecom and nowcom --are scrambling to take initiatives in internet services.  meanwhile, local subsidiaries of such foreign companies as ibm, hewlett packard and elex corporation are expanding their internet business in south korea.  the internet dates back to 1969 when the defense department of the unitedstates linked four research laboratories to exchange information. through the 1970s and the 1980s, the network linked unitedstates university computers and personal computers as well.  one estimate puts the number of netizens in the world at 40 million. some experts predict it will reach 60 million in 1997.

title: china to joint hands with overseas it companies to develop internet
body: china's state information center has joined with three computer giants to give a boost to chinese people wanting to surf the world on the internet.  us-based hayes (asia pacific) company, microsoft (china) company, and hongkong-funded stone rich sight company, announced today that they are joining with the state information center in a unique cooperation arrangement.  the parties will provide full-scale solutions to problems for china's internet users in order to promote the development of the country's information technology industry.  low speeds in information transmission, lack of high-quality information services offered in chinese, as well as relatively higher costs for hooking up to the internet, have had a negative influence on china's internet development.  in addition to providing chinese clients with the most advanced modem to help speed up information transmission, hayes will cooperate with the other three parties to develop a special vcd, which contains hayes' digital telecommunication software, microsoft's chinese-version netscape software, and stone rich sight's chinese tool software, as well as access to china economic information internet service.  the cooperation is expected to lift the number of subscribers linking up in china to the internet, and provide users with large amounts of china's economic information.  the four parties plan to hold a large-scale symposium in beijing in november, and promote the vcd to the chinese market. hayes already has a 30 percent to 40 percent share of china's modem market.

title: few canadians use internet: report
body: despite all the fanfare about internet, few canadians seem to have been lured into actually surfing the information highway.  currently, some 32 percent of canadian households have a personal computer, but only 7.4 percent of them actually use the internet from their home computers.  the figures are far lower than most internet experts had predicted, the globe and mail newspaper reported today.  in other words, 92.6 percent of canadian households don't use the internet, the paper added.  fewer than half of canadian who had computers with modems were hooked up, the paper quoted the latest statistics canada survey as saying.  quebec had the lowest usage of the internet of any canadian province, with 4.1 percent of households hooked up, compared with 8.7 percent in neighboring ontario, and about 10 percent in albert and british columbia.  while lots of canadians are buying computers, the machines are often for their school-aged children, said jim carrol, holder of the 1996 title canadian internet person of the year.  "to be honest, half of the people who have a modem don't know what to do with it," he said, adding that canadians remain largely confused by computers in general, much less the intricacies of the internet.  "the technology has outstripped the ability of people to deal with it," he noted.  in canada, hooking up to the internet cost 15 to 23 unitedstates dollars a month, which may also help explain the fact fewer canadian are enthusiastic about the internet.

title: internet access point operational in northwest china
body: the world-wide internet has arrived in china's northwest region, marking a milestone in china's march along the information super highway.  an internet access point has been built and brought into operation in lanzhou, capital of northwest china's gansu province.  the facility, the first of its kind in the northwest region, has been jointly sponsored by the scientific and technological information department of the state science and technology commission and gansu provincial committee of science and technology.  experts said that the event signifies that china's information super highway is being brought into the international inter-connected information network.  it will also produce a profound effect on the economic activities of northwest china and local people's lives, they say.  according to the experts, the access point has also been linked with seven other similar points in china, forming a huge computer web information network.  the experts added that currently they provide customers with three services through the access point: information from internet, from the china scientific and technological information network and from the gansu provincial scientific and technological information network.

title: more companies worry about computer security
body: more than 70 percent of the executives who oversee data systems for major companies in the unitedstates say they lack confidence in the security of their networks, the usa today reported today.  a poll of 1,320 executives conducted by a professional survey company found significant increases in problems from computer viruses and hackers --especially from fired employees, no-longer-used temporary employees, and corporate spies.  respondents reporting losses due to computer viruses jumped from 8 percent in 1995 to 24 percent, when the survey was conducted in august and september, according to the report.  about 32 percent of the respondents said they discovered serious losses due to malicious acts by company insiders --nearly twice the number reported last year. that increase could be tied to the growth of corporate layoffs, the paper said.  another 18 percent of the respondents reported problems from outside hackers. computer security systems appear to be increasingly vulnerable to attack as more companies open sites on the internet.  about 34 percent say they use the internet for business purposes, up from 26 percent last year. but 40 percent of the users said they depended on an outside service provider --such as america on-line or compuserve --for the service, and for security.  one in four of the respondents said that someone had tried to break into their networks via the internet over the last year.  only about 31 percent said they could determine when a hacker tries to access the company system from the net. and 74 percent said they haven't designated a special group to respond to such incidents.  meanwhile, 6 percent reported problems from industrial espionage. the figure may be low, because the good spies don't get caught, according to the report.

title: rules urged for protection of stock investors in cyberspace
body: japanese analysts are urging the government to formulate rules to protect investors buying stocks on the internet, kyodo news service reported today.  as many businesses eyeing the internet for the release of their stocks, the analysts called on the government to come up with new rules for stock trading, which now only cover transactions taking place inside brokerage houses.  "we need to sort out the problems of stock transactions on the internet and make clear what is lawful and what is not," kyodo quoted one analyst with the nomura research institute as saying.  "in the process, we must also make sure that regulation does not wipe out opportunities for growing venture businesses." analysts note that in the unitedstates, on-line transactions are approved by the securities and exchange commission and investors are given due protection.  currently, virtually any japanese can raise funds on the internet, kyodo said.  "we don't have any particular rules against it," the news service quoted an official at the securities bureau of the finance ministry as saying.  the only requirements are that companies that plan to issue stock for 50 or more people, submit papers to the ministry and draw up financial statements, the official said.

title: hk, shanghai universities launch information network
body: the university of hongkong and the fudan university of shanghai launched the first world wide web (www) mutual mirroring system here on monday.  the hongkong-shanghai information network is a collaboration between the computer center of the hongkong university (hkucc) and the network and information engineering center of fudan university, shanghai (funiec).  the idea of the project was first initiated by hkucc and funiec a year ago when the two universities agreed to establish a closer collaboration between them.  the aim of the network is to make available selected information of hongkong and shanghai which are of common interests in both cities, such as those on arts and culture, commerce and industry, economy and trade, etc., to their internet communities.  and as internet communications are becoming increasingly important to modern societies, the development of the information network is considered in the long term to be able to establish a closer relationship, better understanding and strengthen cooperation between the two cities and their residents.  this network project is an extension of an existing project of mutual mirroring of the information kept on the www servers at the two universities.  future development of the network will realize innovative ideas with state-of-the-art technologies for continuous enhancement and refinement of the performance and functions of the network.

title: science magazine to be available on internet
body: one of the world's most prestigious scientific weeklies, science, will be available on the internet for anyone to read and search, the magazine said today. as of next friday, october 18, virtually all of each week's science magazine --text, figures and graphics, everything that appears in the print edition --can be found at science on-line (http://www.sciencemag.org). according to science editor-in-chief, mr. floyd bloom, the on-line science will have the advantages of immediacy, searchability, greater interactivity and much more information. readers in other countries will be able to see the lastest issue at exactly the same time as in the unitedstates; the previous issues will be fully archived, which can be searched by keyword, author or date; readers will have expanded opportunities to provide feedback and communicate easily with author, science editors and other readers. at present, users of science on-line will be required to subscribe jointly to the journal and the electronic service. access to science on-line is free until january 1997, and individuals must subscribe at that time for 12 above the standard subscription price of the journal. the readers who don't want to subscribe will be able to view an abbreviated version of the contents, which include summaries of science news reports, the journal's weekly editorial and so on. science, which was founded by inventor thomas edision in 1880, is published by the american association for the advancement of science in washington, d.c., an estimated half million people around the world read it each week.

title: 34 us universities agree to set up another internet
body: a group of 34 universities agreed last week to create a new national network dubbed internet ii for higher education, the chronicle for higher education, a newspaper about education, reported.  the new network is expected to cost more than 300 million unitedstates dollars and transmit data more than 10 times faster than the current version of internet, which will be a great help for simultaneous transmission of voice, video and data.  representatives of the universities chartering the internet ii project met in chicago last tuesday, the paper said. each of them agreed to contribute 500,000 dollars a year for three years and kick in 25,000 dollars upfront to get the project going.  the developer will include 34 most prestigious unitedstates universities, such as the university of california-berkeley, cornell, harvard, yale, princeton, the massachusetts institute of technology, stanford and the university of virginia.  the project will take three to five years to complete and is likely to expand to include other universities, major technology companies and federal agencies.  the explosive surge in internet usage, as people send photographs, music, ads and entire books across it, has made the network increasingly congested. scientists complained that the data they send across the country or around the world can get delayed, lost or scrambled in cyberspace, hampering experiments in fields such as physics and astronomy.

title: singapore promoting use of internet
body: singapore is stepping up its efforts to further promote the use of the internet, while at the same time curb the spread of unwanted materials and information via the global computer network, according to the national internet advisory committee (niac) today.  speaking at a press conference, associate professor bernard tan, chairman of the niac, said that the niac is forming three sub-committees to advise the singapore broadcasting authority (sba), which is the government agency in charge of the regulation of the internet, on regulating and promoting the network, which now has about 50 million users world-wide.  the sub-committees will deal separately with legal, industry and public education issues concerning the use of the internet in singapore, he said.  mr tan said the niac will not only advise the sba on its regulatory framework but will also stress on internet promotion.  the committees will seek a diverse range of public views before making any recommendations to the sba, he said.  key issues expected to be addressed include internet privacy, wider use of electronic mail, and concerns of parents over the use of the net by their children.

title: bbc to make cantonese programs available on internet
body: bbc world service is to make programs in cantonese available on the internet while cutting back on its short wave broadcasts, it was announced here today.  the new internet service, will comprise program material from the bbc's cantonese short wave transmission. in addition to world news this includes financial news and analysis and regular feature programs.  lorna ball, head of the bbc chinese service, said "while we shall continue to serve short wave listeners effectively, we are concentrating our resources on developing audiences of the future using this new and growing medium." "i am sure that internet access to this information from the bbc will appeal to a great many people," she added.  it was also announced that from next april, bbc cantonese transmissions on short wave will be halved to 30 minutes a day and switched to the evening, when there is a bigger audience for international radio stations.  the existing morning transmission at 0700 hongkong time will be replaced by the new mid-evening slot, expected to be at 2100.  the changes in the bbc's cantonese service are part of a plan announced today by bbc world service to introduce key developments for high priority audiences while making savings in overall cost.  availability of bbc programs in english and mandarin is unaffected by the changes.

title: survey finds more users taking direct route to internet
body: a survey of home computer users has found for the first time, more people are gaining access to the internet through direct internet services than through commercial on-line services, the new york times said today.  the findings of the semiannual homefront survey by odyssey inc.  of san francisco said that 48 percent of all households connected to the internet used an internet service provider like netcom and att worldnet, compared with 35 percent who used a commercial on-line service like america online and compuserve.  however, the paper said, just six months ago 54 percent of households with internet access used a commercial on-line service, as against 30 percent for the internet providers.  unlike the service providers, who typically offer home computer users access to the internet but little else, the commercial on-line services create a self-contained world of services and features available only to paying members.  the survey data also indicated that 14 percent of all households in the unitedstates now have access to the internet or to an on-line service. over all, 36 percent of all households have a personal computer of some sort, which means that on-line households are still a minority even among pc households.  among households that have an on-line connection, electronic mail emerged in the survey as the most popular application, followed by research, news and information gathering. the least popular applications were home banking, on-line shopping and making hotel and airline reservations.

title: singapore's changi airport, world first with internet services
body: singapore's changi airport becomes the first airport in the world to offer 24-hour internet services to airport passengers, with the opening of an internet center at the airport's terminal 2, the civil aviation authority of singapore (caas) announced today.  the internet center is designed to meet the information and entertainment needs of airport users, the caas said, adding that with the internet, business travelers can literally bring their offices to the changi airport.  they can send, retrieve, download and print electronic mail as well as scan documents or digital photos for attachments to out-going email. airport users can also charge up their laptops or notebooks at the internet center.  "the setting up of the internet center at the changi airport is part of our ongoing efforts to improve the facilities and services offered to our passengers," ms elizabeth chua, a public relations official of the caas, said.  "in this information age, 24-hour internet services will serve to meet the increasingly sophisticated needs of travelers at the changi airport," she said.  the user-friendly internet center provides software packages for email in different languages, namely english, chinese, japanese and korean. qualified instructors, known as cyber-guides, are on hand to provide personalized services to internet novices, the caas said.

title: i.b.m. and big banks in home service deal
body: international business machines(i.b.m.) and a group of big banks announced on monday that they had set up a venture that would improve their ability to offer services through home computers.  the venture, known as integrion, is an attempt by both the banks and i.b.m. to develop standards for transactions and contract most of the actual processing to i.b.m and other vendors.  it will also help solve the security concerns raised in doing business over the internet.  "with this new venture, electronic commerce will take its biggest step forward to date," louis v. gerstner, chairman of i.b.m., said. " this is a secure network marketplace that is essential to the growth of electronic business." the service will be first used by nationsbank and the banc one corporation as part of internet banking products to be introduced early next year. other major banks involved include bank of america, first chicago nbd, fleet financial group, keycorp and pnc bank.  integrion will mainly provide what is known as "middleware" software that helps banks handle electronic transactions from a variety of sources. customers will perform transactions using a variety of methods--from the bank's home page on the internet to software like "managing your money".  hugh l. mccoll jr., chairman of the nationsbank, described the venture as an essential step in maintaining the banks's control of the financial system.

title: apec wants telecommunications further liberalized
body: apec telecommunications ministers today agreed on further trade liberalization and support for joint activities of research and development across the asia-pacific region.  the agreement was reached at the second ministerial meeting for telecommunications and information industry of the members of the asia pacific economic cooperation (apec) forum, which concluded today in gold coast, australia.  the two-day meeting was attended by all, except malaysia, of the apec members.  australia's minister for communication richard alston told a news conference in gold coast that there was broad agreement among the ministers on the principles of trade liberalization and telecommunication cooperation.  there was also a commitment to providing services to all consumers, not just the top end of the market.  "we understand the importance of ensuring that people in rural and remote areas, low income groups, those that don't have a high level of access to even pay telephones, are not left behind," alston said.  a declaration issued after the meeting includes agreement on the conformity of technologies and technical assessment, progressive reductions of restrictions on market access, and support for joint activities of research and development.  the meeting also directed apec's telecommunications working group to promote electronic commerce, the use of the internet in electronic commerce and business sector investment in telecommunications.  an electronic data interchange pilot project will be set up to focus on technical and system application aspects using the internet, while a distance learning pilot project will be launched to develop and deliver courses on distance education via the world wide web as well as other training and education projects.  the third apec ministerial meeting for the telecommunications is scheduled to be held in singapore in 1998.

title: asean to continue cooperation on internet regulation
body: member countries of the association of southeast asian nations (asean) agreed here today to continue their cooperation and sharing of information in formulating and fine-tuning regulations on internet.  at the end of a three-day asean forum on internet here today, the asean members said in a statement that they acknowledged the value of internet as a communications and information resource.  they said they agreed that asean should harness the potential of internet to project its rich heritage and identity to the region and the rest of the world.  they also agreed that regulations and laws were necessary to set up a framework for internet to develop and flourish, given the great potential for business, information and cultural exchange, the statement said.  however, the forum agreed that the appropriate regulatory framework should depend on the culture and legal system of each country.  the forum "affirmed the importance of having safeguards against easy access to sites which ran counter to our cherished values, traditions and culture," the statement said.  in this regard, the forum statement said that asean would encourage other nations, especially the west, to understand its concerns.  the meeting also affirmed that government regulations played an important role in safeguarding national values, while industry self-regulation was equally important.  the member countries agreed at the forum that given the rapidly evolving nature of internet, there should be continued regional cooperation and sharing of information to help each country formulate and fine-tune its regulatory approaches.

title: internet improvements in library
body: thanks to the spread of internet services to libraries, people can now enjoy reader services from various libraries worldwide in the quiet of their homes.  the international federation of library associations and institutes (ifla) is engaged in a global project to promote reading and the use of library reference services through the internet, which will connect the general office of ifla with its regional offices and member libraries.  there are now 4,500 customers in 89 countries and regions who receive some 10,000 documents every week through the library internet system, and libraries worldwide are establishing more data bases in order to change the printed word into electronic information.  scholars from beijing university and university of hongkong are conducting research on the basic law for the hongkong special administration region through the internet, according to sources at the 62nd general conference of ifla which opened here today.  t.d. webb, a ph.d. from the university of hawaii, said that the development of electronic information services has made the library change its function to provide more convenience for readers.  the internet will help libraries become a public media system for a greater number of people in the world instead of a reference warehouse for researchers and scholars.  robert wedgeworth, president of ifla, said that competitive libraries in the future will be those that use the internet to provide readers with more services.

title: canada's bank going on internet
body: canada's bank of nova scotia will soon offer its retail customers internet banking service, local media reported today.  bank of nova scotia, the fourth biggest bank in canada, announced monday that it will test internet banking with its own staff and customers in ontario province this fall before the service goes national at the beginning of next year.  the system, developed by ibm canada, will initially allow balance checks, fund transfers and bill payment on the internet.  eventually, customers will be able to apply for loans, mortgages and insurance, or buying mutual funds.  all customers need is a computer, a modem and access to an internet service provider.  there is no special software required to tap in, the bank said.  the bank is billing its move as an industry first for canada, saying that no other financial institution currently offers as wide a range of "fully transactional banking services on the internet." internet banking could be "the biggest milestone in banking since the invention of the automatic banking machine," the bank said in a statement.  currently, most canadian banks have been concentrating on personal computer banking that connects with customers over secure private telephone lines.  security concerns over customers' funds and personal information have been a roadblock to getting more banking services on to the internet.  but nova scotia bank said its system, which masks customer account numbers and doesn't identify customers by name, is "entirely secure." it also promised to bear the cost if there ever is a security breach.

title: britain may act against internet pornography
body: the british government may be forced to legislate to control pornographic and violent material on the internet if the industry doesn't regulate itself, a government minister said today.  "government will face calls for legislation to regulate all aspects of the internet, unless and until service providers are seen wholeheartedly to embrace responsible self-regulation," british science and technology minister ian taylor was quoted by the daily telegraph newspaper as saying.  internet companies in france and germany were temporarily closed down or had their services curtailed by regulators last year because they allowed access to offensive material on the net.  taylor challenged britain's internet industry to help parents and schools control children's access to undesirable material by using software compatible with the platform for internet content selection (pics) screening system.  developed by a consortium of academics and computer companies, pics is a universal and free system for labeling internet text and images with ratings according to their sexual, violence, nudity and language content.  parents or teachers can set acceptable levels for each of the four types of content on a sliding scale of one to five.  taylor has previously asked the internet industry to exercise responsible self-regulation. this stronger call to use the screening system came as the first software that incorporates the pics filtering system became available.  the three largest british internet companies -demon internet, uunet pipex and compuserve -said that they will now offer the free software, made by microsoft, to new customers.

title: internet users in s'pore to have only filtered access from sept.
body: internet users in singapore will have only filtered access to the global computer network starting from september 15, a measure the government takes to curb objectionable contents on the net, the straits times reported today.  it said the date of september 15 is the deadline for the net users to link their computers to special computers, called proxy servers, at their internet service provider's (isp) end.  these servers will block access to sites which the singapore broadcasting authority (sba) deemed objectionable, the report said.  proxy servers are computers used mainly to speed up access to the internet users. they store or cache a database of often-accessed material locally, it said.  a user's request for foreign-based material does not mean sending an electronic request abroad to fetch it. it can be served locally and this can cut access time by almost half.  in the meantime, the report said, proxy servers can also be used as filters to block unwanted sites. they do this by checking a user's request against a list of unwanted sites before granting him access.  many internet users were concerned that the filtering would lead to slow access, the straits times said, adding that 10 of 12 users it contacted shared this concern.  one expert agreed with some surfers, who noted that access time might rise if the list against which proxy servers must check became very big. but "at the moment, i don't see the filtering process having an impact on the rate of access as the number of blocked sites is still low," the expert was quoted as saying.  on the concern that proxy servers would retard access speed, a singapore broadcasting authority spokesman said, "our objective is not to slow down or impede the performance of the proxy servers.  we will hold regular discussions with the isps and will work with them to monitor the performance of the servers."

title: internet banking threatens traditional banks' market
body: the market for internet banking is poised to grow sharply in the next three years, affecting the competitive advantage enjoyed by traditional banks as demand for internet banking services increases.  a survey of internet banking by booz-allen and hamilton, international management consultants, has found that 154 european banks already have sites on the world wide web, with sites increasing at a rate of nearly 90 percent a year.  but use of the sites is growing faster, and almost all the banks that have an internet presence plan to upgrade both the size and capacity of their sites and the level of services they offer.  the survey found the cost of an average payment transaction on the internet was 13 cents or less. this compares with 26 cents for a personal computer banking service using the bank's own software, 54 cents for a telephone banking service and l.08 unitedstates dollars for a bank branch.  that means costs for internet banking run at only 15-20 percent of income, compared with an average cost:income ratio for the banking industry of about 60 percent.  "the cost advantages are just so huge that there would be no reason not to try it out," said michael berger, of booze-allen's financial services team.  booz-allen said the internet poses considerable threats to traditional banks, both because it costs them more to set up web services and because it neutralizes many of their competitive advantages.  moreover, it will be easier for customers to pick and choose, and harder for banks to differentiate their web sites from their competitors', including non-banks which can bundle financial services together on the internet.

title: software error knocks 6 mln america online users off-line
body: a technical error of america online (aol), the largest internet access provider in the unitedstates, left 6 million online users off-line today, cutting them off from email, chat rooms and the world wide web.  the system went down at 4 a.m. of eastern time during a scheduled maintenance update, routine work that is generally done at that hour to affect the fewest possible members. it was still down 12 hours later, making it one of the worst outages in online history in terms of length and number of people affected.  aol hoped to have the system back up later today, according to local press reports.  when america online users tried to log in, they were greeted by a message saying "good-bye from america online the system is temporarily unavailable. please try again in 1 hour. thank you for calling." aol chairman steve case said every possible resource was being brought to restore the service.  "we regret any inconvenience this may have caused our customers. we will work to ensure that the problem does not recur," he said.  previously, a software glitch brought down america online's email system for an hour on june 19, but it is said that was a different problem from the one today.

title: microsoft plans big push in application
body: microsoft corp., the world's software giant, is preparing an aggressive new push in application programs this fall, the wall street journal reported today.  the project includes an overhaul of its popular office package that will offer animated on-screen assistants to give personalized tips to puzzled users, it said.  office 97, a suite of eight products that includes the company's popular spreadsheet and word-processing programs, is being revamped to add multiple internet features as well as a program called outlook that combines scheduling, electronic-mail and address-book functions.  the new suite is expected to ship in november, the paper said.  the office effort, more than two years in the making, is likely to have a big impact on the company's revenue in the next 12 months, according to the report. an official from microsoft said that the company has invested twice as much on the new suite as on its predecessor.  in combination with a forthcoming version of microsoft's browser software for the world wide web, users can use tools from the company's word processor to create and find web pages without leaving the browser to launch those programs.  but the paper said the applications business faces a series of new challenges, the biggest of which is that many companies already own office and aren't eager to spend more on new versions.

title: intel to unveil internet-phone software
body: intel corp. will unveil a free software program today that enables users to make long-distance telephone calls over the internet.  such phone calls only cost as much as the local connection to the global computer network, so that if computer telephony catches on it could greatly affect the profits of telephone companies, according to a report by the wall street journal today.  a few people already use the internet to make phone calls, it said, but caller and receiver must have identical software and sound quality is poor.  however, intel's software is based on a standard embraced by at least 120 companies, including microsoft corp., which will plug a compatible product, netmeeting, into its operating systems. the new standard will allow users of different computers and different phone software to talk to each other.  once the technology is widespread, a user would be able to access the directory service, click on a particular name, and immediately initiate a call to that person. microsoft will distribute its similar product, netmeeting, from its web site in september, the paper said.  but experts also said internet telephony also faces barriers now. it is still plagued by delays in voice transmission, and widespread adoption will put a big strain on the global network, which wasn't designed for real-time applications.  moreover, no one knows the real number of internet users. in the unitedstates, the number is estimated at anywhere from 10 million to 20 million, but only about 10 percent to 15 percent of that number use the internet with great frequency.

title: internet usage growing rapidly for job market
body: usage of the internet for seeking jobs in the unitedstates is rapidly changing the way job hunters and companies seek out one another, according to a national research study released by hwt specialized communications.  it also said that the number of job seekers found on the net will be doubled in the coming year.  the study found that corporate recruiters have only begun to scratch the surface of the net's applications for their industry.  the study is based on more than 400 telephone interviews with human resources professionals and a survey of nearly 800 job-seeking internet users.  although newspapers and trade publications remain the number one medium of choice, the study found that the advantages of internet recruitment are substantial.  the internet reaches an extremely large group, giving human resources personnel a broader selection of candidates.  additionally, contact is immediate and the internet is inexpensive and relatively easy-to-use.  companies that use the internet for recruiting report positive, results.  they fill significantly more positions per year than non-users with.  in addition, companies using the internet tend to fill more higher level jobs.  recruiters looking for technical people are especially successful when using the internet since most of those who surf the net are highly knowledgeable users.  ninety four percent of companies currently using the internet for recruitment intend to continue their use for that purpose in the future, and of that number, 75 percent will increase usage in the coming year.  tomorrow's future use of the internet is expected to increase substantially.  thirty-nine percent of internet literate, non-users will try it in the year ahead and 84 percent of "current users" will increase their use of the net, according to the survey.  job seekers using the internet are predominantly highly educated, young males (18-34 years old) with household incomes well above the unitedstates average.  both job seekers and human resource professionals consider job posting sits to be the most effective means of locating career connections on the net, according to researchers.

title: singapore unveils internet regulation scheme
body: the singapore government unveiled today a scheme to regulate the internet, the master network of the global computer networks, which now has over 40 million subscribers worldwide.  in announcing the class license scheme for regulating the internet at a press conference today, the singapore broadcasting authority (sba) reiterated its commitment to "safeguard the interest of the internet community while promoting the healthy development of the industry." the scheme, which takes effect next monday, aims to encourage responsible use of the internet while facilitating its healthy development in singapore, the sba said.  "it encourages minimum standards in cyberspace and seeks to protect net users, particularly the young, against the broadcast of unlawful or objectionable materials," it explained.  the automatic licensing scheme will cover internet service providers and internet content providers. under the conditions of the license, these providers are obligated to assist the sba with any relevant information on persons who violated the rules. it will focus on groups which provide content pages on an organized basis.  "sba will focus on content which may undermine public morals, political stability and religious harmony of singapore. however, sba recognizes that it is impossible to regulate the internet fully," the sba said.  it stressed that the success of internet regulation will depend very much on industry self-regulation and community action.  "singaporeans can help sba in the identification of objectionable sites in order to keep cyberspace clean," it said.

title: tv set can be linked to internet
body: families who now do not own personal computers may soon use their tv to surf the internet.  a new company in california has created a low-cost device to enable tv sets to browse the internet's world wide web, an idea computer industry veterans have talked for months but not realized.  webtv networks inc., a silicon valley startup firm, planned to demonstrate its device publicly for the first time today and announce two powerful partners.  the potential market is huge: 100 million unitedstates households have tvs. two-thirds of those don't have pcs and many of those can't afford them, said a press report here today.  sony electronics inc. and philips consumer electronics co. will produce and sell machines based on webtv's technology in september, according to the report.  nearly a dozen companies, including large ones like oracle corp. and ibm, have talked about lower-cost internet access devices in recent months.  webtv networks kept quiet, working with sony and philips for months and building their trust by adhering to design deadlines.  webtv's machine uses a phone line and universal remote control to navigate the worldwide computer network. logging on is as simple as pushing a green button marked "web" on the remote. a wireless keyboard is optional.  through clever programming, the company has overcome a major hurdle by making web pages look good on a tv screen, which portrays images with less resolution than most computer monitors.

title: unep launches on-line international register on biosafety
body: the geneva-based un environment programme launched on monday on the internet the first-ever international register on biosafety with a view to help countries to better monitor and manage biotechnology risks.  the register will contain authoritative and comprehensive information on existing biosafety regulations, related conventions and other legal instruments, risk assessment and management procedures and programmes, as well as advisory services.  it will be linked to relevant national, regional and global information networks accessible on the internet. the information subscribed will be provided by governments, un entities, universities, scientific institutions and biotechnology industry.  by establishing a knowledge base and promoting information exchange, the register is expected to help governments to control or prevent imports of living modified organisms that the country may lack the ability to safely manage, the unep said.  according to the unep, the register is inspired by growing concerns about the potential risks posed by living modified organisms produced by modern biotechnology.  the risks include unintended changes in the competitiveness, virulence, or other characteristics of the target species, and the possibility of adverse impacts on non-target species and ecosystems.  while many countries with modern biotechnology industries do have domestic legislation, many others lack a national regulatory regime governing the safe development, use and transfer of biotechnology. the unep said.  another concern is that many developing countries do not have the technical, financial and institutional capacity to address biosafety.  there are also no binding international agreements addressing the situations where living modified organisms cross national borders, according to the unep.

title: hk monetary authority launches homepage
body: the hongkong monetary authority (hkma) launches its homepage on the internet today, providing a wealth of timely monetary and banking information of hongkong around the clock.  an hkma spokesman said today that the hkma homepage includes descriptions of what the hkma is and what it does, together with an introduction of its organization and operations.  he said that it also features information on the linked exchange rate system, hongkong's monetary system after 1997, the development of hongkong's debt market, banking services, notes and coins, exchange fund and foreign exchange reserves.  the homepage shows the information about the 1997 world bank and imf annual meetings which are to be held in hongkong in september next year.  monthly updated monetary and banking statistics, press releases and hkma's recruitment ads are available at finger tips.  joseph yam, chief executive of hkma, said that the hkma homepage truly expands our ability to keep the general public abreast with the development of hk local monetary system, allowing the world to keep track on what is happening in the financial system of hongkong.  he said, "the launch of the hkma internet homepage further represents our commitment to promote public understanding and transparency of our objectives and policies."

title: internet becomes part of chinese people's daily life
body: every morning, professor he zhimin of tianjin university boots up his computer and checks for email.  about 200 teachers at both tianjin and nankai universities have linked up with the internet, an increasingly popular information network among chinese intellectuals.  he zhimin has used his access to internet to prepare for an international conference, and he receives several email messages on holidays.  china sold nearly one million computers in 1995, 40 percent more than the previous year, according to statistics.  about 20 percent of the computers sold last year were bought by chinese families for use in the home.  chinese people have gradually recognized computers as a more powerful instrument than typewriters, especially after the popularization of networks such as internet.  "ever since i got access to internet, i found that the distance with the rest of the world has been shortened and the traditional work method has changed," he zhimin said.  recently, a three-month-old baby who suffered from a rare disease soon recovered after a local research institute sent medical information to the infant's doctors via the internet.  experts predict that china's computer market will show an annual growth rate of 40-50 percent, and that one-tenth of the 100 million urban families in the country will have computers by the year 2000.

title: china internet to start in april
body: the china internet is to officially open to the public in april this year, according to the data telecommunications bureau of the ministry of posts and telecommunications.  the china internet, believed to be the embryo of the future "information superhighway", will enable users in china to exchange electronic information with users on the world's largest computer information network --the internet --and enjoy all of the information resources on that network.  according to the bureau, the china internet has been founded on the two major data telecommunications networks china has built in the past few years --the china public packet switching data network (chinapac) and the china public data and digital network (ddn), both of which are fairly large in scale and are internationally technically advanced.  in recent years china's public data telecommunications network has been developing fairly rapidly. to date, chinapac directly covers 688 cities, with nearly 60,000 terminals; while ddn covers 292 cities.  in addition, china has so far set up nine email systems, with a terminal capacity of 30,000, and five cities have opened videotex businesses.  the bureau indicated that the china internet will be further expanded within the year, so as to make it a backbone information network for the development of the national economy.

title: software enables voice communications on internet
body: an israeli company has developed a software that enables voice communications on the worldwide computer network internet.  vocaltec inc. said its software allows two-way voice communications on the internet at a fraction of telephone-company long-distance rates, the wall street journal reported today.  the software takes the digitized voice from the sound card in the computer, compresses and then sends it; the software in the receiving computer decompresses the message and completes it by an "error-correcting" process when some information is missing.  the internet, now linking some 20 million to 30 million users, is designed for sending data in one direction at a time, unlike duplex phone lines that permit both parties to speak at once.  vocaltec said its technology is "half-duplex" that enables two users at both ends to speak and listen in turn.  a user in new york city tested the software and said the voice is "crystal-clear" in the unitedstates and canada but conversations sometimes get jumbled when speaking to a man in hongkong.  vocaltec said that on international calls, on average there is a delay of one second between both ends.  with the same software, a user is able to call anyone anywhere in the world, for the price of local internet access, typically 2 unitedstates dollars an hour. in comparison, the lowest rates for overseas calls from the unitedstates over major phone carriers start around 30 dollars an hour. the quality of the internet phone is "reasonably good", but not up to regular phone quality.  vocaltec plans to start selling the software over the internet monday, at an initial price of 49 dollars a copy, which is scheduled to rise to 99 dollars at the end of march.

title: macao launches internet services
body: customers in macao can make a trial of exchanging information with over twenty million people in the world with the internet service launched by the macao telecommunications company (ctm) from today onwards.  also, through the computer screen, customers can get access to the most updated information and data worldwide.  the ctm internet, a service of global prevalence, is to offer customers an all-weather computer communication, according to george russell, ctm chief executive officer.  he explained that with internet, customers are allowed to communicate with each other through computers, thus enhancing the cost-effectiveness. he added that both individuals and companies can be customers of the internet and they can communicate with their clients or suppliers more efficiently and effectively to eliminate paper work and go-betweens.  the ctm internet offers three alternatives of access mode, including telephone network, data network and special lines, for customers to meet with their individual needs.  presently, the major features available from internet include electronic mail, access to remote files and file transfer. other features also include group discussions and network news.  contents of information, which keeps renewing, include written materials, cartoons and audio-visual materials.

title: d e 1906 bc-us-investment-computer service eaed122106hke --"on-line" investment for u.s. internet users
body: beginning today, unitedstates users of the internet computer network will be able to use their computers for the first time to buy and sell securities, a unitedstates investment firm announced.  the net investor on-line investment service was sponsored by howe barnes investments, inc., a chicago-based full-service regional investment firm. it also enables users to obtain up-to-the-minute information on their investment portfolio and access advanced information services rivalling those of an investment professional.  the net investor is designed to appeal to both first-time and experienced individual investors who want to readily perform their own computerized investment research and make their own investment decisions. a full array of services is being provided at low cost, with users paying only for the services they need.  according to richard griffin, senior vice president of the net investor, an investor can open an account directly through the world wide web at an electronic address. when the account is approved, the individual may enter buy and sell orders directly through the internet for stocks traded on major unitedstates exchanges.  the services offered also include: real-time access to stock market quotes; investment portfolio accounting and allocation; research, sophisticated market analysis and planning tools; and news and financial information.  additional capabilities to be added in coming months will include load and no-load mutual fund transactions, bond transactions and margin accounts, making the net investor part of the most comprehensive on-line financial service available, the company said.

title: india plans to build information highway
body: the indian government is planning to set up an ambitious inter-connected and inter-operable countrywide information network, according to official sources here today.  the national communication infrastructure termed "information super highway" will comprise a seamless web of communication networks of optical fiber, co-axials, twinwire, microwave links, radio, television and satellites.  it is said the proposal on the information super highway plans has been okayed by indian minister for information and broadcasting k.p. singh deo and is being sent for final consensus to various departments before forwarding it to the cabinet committee on economic affairs.  under the plan, broadcasting will be most powerful constituent of the information super highway and the government was suggested to create "broadcast hub centers" which will be linked with different information sources using existing networks put up by the telecommunication department.  on the other hand, the sources said the plan is also to focus on socio-economic objectives and to provide free exchange of information among various government agencies.  the indian government is expecting to give a boost to research and development through better communications between various institutes.

title: new york times to invest more in electronic media
body: the new york times company has announced a strategic shift that would increase its involvement in the businesses of the cable television, cd-rom computer disk and on-line services.  the new york times reported today that the company's executives expected the company to invest one billion to 1.5 billion unitedstates dollars in the next five or six years for the acquisition of television stations and for investments in other electronic media businesses.  the times quoted its president lance primis as saying,"as television stations, programming and cable networks occupy our near-term focus, the world of new electronic media will be the target of our investing for the long term." the times company, with annual revenues of more than 2 billion dollars, gets about 90 percent of its profits from newspapers and other electronic media.  company executives said they planned to increase the company's reliance on electronic media so that ultimately 75 percent of the profits came from print and 25 percent from electronic media.  primis said last night that the company's new approach to investments in electronic media represented "a shift in emphasis." some media industry analysts said that they were concerned that the company might now pay too high a price for electronic properties. but others said that accelerating the times company's investments in electronic media amounted to needed insurance at a time when newspapers faced increasing competition from other media.

title: china to build education info-highway
body: china will soon complete its first education "information highway", it was announced here today.  the network will link computer terminals in most of its 1,000 universities and colleges by the year 2000, and provide email, electronic news, electronic library and document services for teachers and students, according to the state education commission.  wei yu, deputy minister of education, said that the project, named the "china education and research network (cernet)", has been approved by the state planning commission, and it will be heavily subsidized by the government.  by 1996, cernet will have set up its mainstays, which will extend to major chinese cities and be connected with international computer networks such as internet. by the year 2000 it will have a complete set of regional branches.  the network will make full use of the current public communications facilities and channels, according to wei, and it will introduce up-to-date technologies for the protection of intellectual property rights and the prevention of computer crimes.  the project will allow chinese universities to share information freely, and enable the country to fully join in the worldwide sharing of information and high technology, wei added.  deputy premier zhou jiahua told a press conference here today that the information network will be very significant for the improvement of the chinese people's living standards and china's international status, as well as the safeguarding of world peace.  "china has set up a state information joint committee and it is working hard for the construction of the info-highway," he said. "in the process, we will learn from experiences abroad and find a suitable road with chinese characteristics." deng nan, deputy minister of the science and technology commission, said that her commission will make great efforts to support the project.  sources said that the state education commission will be responsible for cernet, and a management committee comprised of ten university presidents together with a top-class experts committee have been set up.

title: s'pore bank to use smart phone for new service
body: the overseas chinese banking corporation (ocbc) of singapore will be the first bank in asia outside japan to use tandem smart phone technology in electronic banking service, bank officials confirmed today.  they said the bank will launch the new service, easi-tellafone, which combines the features of a telephone and personal computer, on sunday.  this high-technology phone, with a touch screen that displays text and graphics, works like an automatic teller machine but does not dispense cash.  in addition to its large crystal display screen, the phone system has a microprocessor chip, built-in modem and slot for an integrated-circuit memory card.  customers can also use a printer for receipts to confirm their transactions, since the customers can use the phone for trading shares from home.  officials said this system will enable customers to carry out transactions quickly, accurately and quietly.  in addition to share transactions, customers of the ocbc can also use the smart phones to tap information on interest rates for deposit and savings accounts, foreign exchange rates and housing loan and unit trust rates.  besides, they can check account balances, transfer funds between accounts and pay bills to selected organizations.

title: rok-europe "information highway" operates
body: an "information highway" linking south korea and europe has become operational, according to the ministry of science and technology here today.  the so-called ekorn (eu-korea link of research networks) is a computer communication network that connects europan with kreon, one of south korea's five largest computer networks, the ministry said.  supported by the european commission, europan is an initiative which interconnects existing national research networks in 23 countries in the european union and provides a harmonized set of services such as electronic mail, file transfer and super computing services.  it is linked with library databases (db) in 200 european areas, about 1,000 multimedia servers, free db in 51 areas, and pay db in 56 areas.  the ekorn link will enable researchers in south korea and europe to quickly exchange information and thereby promote scientific dialogue between the two regions' research and development communities, the ministry said.  researchers in south korea will be able to freely make use of the massive data stored in the european network.  the project is one of the actions in the framework of administrative arrangement for cooperation in science and technology signed between the south korean government and the european commission in november 1992.  the ekorn can transmit data at a speed of 64 kbps, which means about 8,000 alphabetic letters can be sent in a second.  south korea has already been connected with a research computer network in the unitedstates and plans to link the kreon with japan's inter-ministry net.

title: roundup: china to build information superhighway
body: china has mapped out an ambitious plan to build its own information superhighway with a focus on an information application system, a nationwide public data service network and an advanced telecommunications network.  in a recent symposium on the wide use of information in the national economy and china's information superhighway, wu jichuan, minister of posts and telecommunications, said china will watch closely the world's latest development of the information superhighway construction and carry out its own in a planned and step-by-step manner.  he said china will expand the application of computers in digital exchanges and accelerate the construction of optical fibers and build an internet by developing a network telecommunications platform based on the country's public telecommunications network.  the symposium, attended by china's senior officials and information experts, exchanged information on the world's current trend of information superhighway construction, its definition and its social economic significance. china's demands for such a highway and its potentials were widely discussed in the symposium, the first of its kind in china.  as part of the effort to cope with the world's new information revolution, china is busy building 22 national-level optical fiber trunk lines to connect all the provincial capitals, 20 digital microwave trunk lines, and large and medium-sized satellite telecommunications ground stations.  according to government sources, the large capacity digital transmission network connecting the country's major provincial capital cities will be completed early next year. first phase construction of a nationwide digital exchange network was completed last september.  at present, the network extends to 267 of china's major cities and has started to exchange information with 37 centers in 20 countries and regions.  meanwhile, the first phase project of the high speed digital trunk line connecting 21 provinces and municipalities will be put into operation this july. a cellular phone network has covered the coastal provinces in the southeast and some central provinces.  viewing the current level of information modernization, experts said that the 700,000 mobile telephones will be linked by a nationwide network soon. china's seven million radio pagers have made the country one of the world's largest paging markets. computers have been widely used in banking, customs clearance, railway transportation and civil aviation and weather forecasting. these, in all, will contribute to china's information modernization, experts commented.  as another major step in the construction of the information superhighway, china plans to accelerate hi-tech research concerned with information modernization, especially advanced remote sensing, surveying, computers, automation facilities and modern telecommunications technologies.  the construction of the information superhighway is a systematic project which will involve different fields of work, said wu jichuan, minister of posts and telecommunications. he called on the joint efforts of participating departments to work toward erecting the modern information network.

title: joint venture to help upgrade telecommunications
body: a joint venture for affordable, high-quality telecommunications equipment has been launched with the aim of helping upgrade china's telecommunications industry.  the joint venture, at and t consumer telecommunications equipment beijing, ltd, was formed by at and t china inc., s. megga telecommunications ltd and the central technology center of the china national posts and telecommunications industry corporation (ptic).  a contract signing ceremony was held here wednesday.  the joint venture will develop, produce and deliver telecommunications products meeting china's standards.  its main products will include videophones, cordless telephones, digital telephone answering machines and facsimile machines.  the chinese side takes a 30 percent interest, and at and t and s. megga take 53 percent and 17 percent interests, respectively, in the joint-venture, which has a registered capital of four million unitedstates dollars.  the business volume of the corporation in the first four years is expected to reach 150 million dollars.  sources said that there exist ample and excellent opportunities in china's telecommunications market.  the joint venture will use advanced technologies from at and t and the experience of s. megga in telecommunications equipment production as well as the sales and service networks of ptic to promote china's telecommunications industry.

title: Chinese Websites to Increase Cooperation with Mass Media
body: About 36 major Chinese websites and websites of mass media organizations issued a joint statement here today calling for intensive cooperation to promote the healthy development of the web-based information service industry. The statement was announced at a meeting held in Beijing today which focused on the development of China's Internet industry. DOMESTIC NEWS; ECONOMICRepresentatives from the websites of Xinhua News Agency, the China News Agency, China Central TV, the China International Radio Station, China Daily and websites such as Sina.com, Sohu.com and Netease.com attended the meeting. Both the websites and the news agencies and newspapers noted the important role played by the web-based information service industry in modern society, and reiterated the principle of "self- discipline" among the websites operators needed to create a positive social environment. These website operators and the mass media websites will meet two times a year to discuss problems related to the development of China's web-based information service industry.

title: CAAC Opens E-commerce Website
body: A new E-commerce website(www. travelsky.com), launched by the computing center under the Civil Aviation Administration of China(CAAC), has been  put into operation recently. DOMESTIC NEWS; ECONOMIC According to general manager Yang Jun, the website will enable passengers browse the latest information on flights of Chinese and foreign airlines. Clients may select suitable time, ideal airlines and acceptable airplanes at home or in their offices through the Internet, Yang said. The website also offers information on tourist destinations, hotel reservation and car renting. Assisted by the Bank of China, clients may pay their bills through the Internet. The website will soon have an English version to better serve foreign passengers, Yang said.

HE SAID THAT WEB SITE TRAFFIC TOTALS ARE NOT ACCURATE NOW BECAUSE DIFFERENT WEB SITES USE DIFFERENT MEASUREMENT CRITERION.  SOME USE FIGURES BASED ON AMOUNTS OF HITS ON THE SITES, WHILE OTHERS DETERMINE VOLUME TOTALS THROUGH NUMBERS OF USER SESSIONS. CINIC HAS FORMULATED A SET OF NEW STATISTICS TERMS AND EVALUATION STANDARDS, AND IS COOPERATING WITH ASIAINFO TECHNOLOGIES (CHINA),INC, TO SET UP A THIRD-PARTY AUDITING SYSTEM. SINCE 1994, WHEN CHINA LINKED WITH THE INTERNET, THE COUNTRY HAS SEEN BREAKNECK DEVELOPMENT IN ITS WEB ECONOMY. BY THE END OF THIS JUNE, CHINA HAD FOUR MILLION PEOPLE WITH INTERNET ACCESS AND HAD SET UP NEARLY 10,000 WEB SITES.

title: MEE122701HKE -- INTERNET USE IN UAE GROWING QUICKLY
body: INTERNET IS BECOMING MORE AND MORE POPULAR IN THE UNITED ARAB EMIRATES (UAE), AND THE POPULATION WITH ACCESS TO THIS SERVICE IS EXPECTED TO RISE DRAMATICALLY IN THE NEXT FEW YEARS. THE THREE-DAY EXHIBITION WILL COVER COMPUTERS AND PERIPHERALS, INFRASTRUCTURE, INTERNET ACCESS, SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT TOOLS AND APPLICATIONS AND SERVICES.

title: HKE122454 -- MYANMAR TO PROVIDE INTERNET SERVICES
body: THE MYANMAR TELECOMMUNICATION AUTHORITIES WILL SOON PROVIDE INTERNET SERVICES TO THE PUBLIC AS PREPARATIONS FOR SUCH SERVICES AS INTERNET AND email ARE AT THE FINAL STAGE, SAID A GOVERNMENT STATEMENT HERE FRIDAY AFTERNOON. THE SERVICES ARE TO BE EXTENDED BY THE STATE-RUN MYANMA POSTS AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS (MPT), THE ONLY ENTITY ALLOWED TO PROVIDE PUBLIC POSTAL AND TELECOMMUNICATION SERVICES IN THE COUNTRY, THE OFFICIAL INFORMATION SHEET ADDED. MYANMAR HAS BEEN STRIVING TO PROMOTE ITS TELECOMMUNICATION SERVICES TO MEET THE INCREASING NEED OF LOCAL AND FOREIGN INVESTORS TO FACILITATE THEIR BUSINESS LINKS SINCE THE COUNTRY OPENED TO THE OUTSIDE WORLD IN LATE 1988 BY ADOPTING A MARKET- ORIENTED ECONOMIC SYSTEM. title: HKE122363 -- AUSTRALIAN FARMERS HOOK UP TO INTERNET
body: HALF OF AUSTRALIA'S FARMERS USED COMPUTERS AS OF THE END OF MARCH 1999 AND THEY ARE HOOKING UP TO THE INTERNET IN DROVES, THE AUSTRALIAN BUREAU OF STATISTICS ( ABS) SAID ON THURSDAY. THE ABS ESTIMATED 49 PERCENT OF THE NATION'S 147,160 FARMS WERE USING COMPUTERS, 26 PERCENT MORE THAN THE SAME PERIOD OF THE PREVIOUS YEAR. THE PROPORTION OF FARMS USING THE INTERNET INCREASED FROM 11 PERCENT IN MARCH 1998 TO 20 PERCENT IN MARCH 1999, REPRESENTING A MASSIVE 84 PERCENT BOOST. "THE GROWTH IN THE USE OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT) BY FARMS IS IMPORTANT GIVEN THE GROWING INTEREST IN THE SPREAD OF IT THROUGHOUT AUSTRALIA," THE ABS SAID IN A STATEMENT. THE NORTHERN TERRITORY HAD THE HIGHEST PROPORTION OF FARMS USING COMPUTERS, FOLLOWED BY THE AUSTRALIAN CAPITAL TERRITORY (ACT) AND THE WESTERN AUSTRALIA STATE, THE ABS SAID. THE NORTHERN TERRITORY AND THE ACT HAD THE HIGHEST PERCENTAGE OF FARMS SURFING THE NET, AT 36 PERCENT AND 29 PERCENT RESPECTIVELY, IT ADDED.

title: AFG122232HKE -- S.AFRICAN REVENUE SERVICE TO SHUT DOWN INTERNET
body: THE SOUTH AFRICAN REVENUE SERVICE (SARS) SAID ON WEDNESDAY THAT IT WILL SHUT DOWN ITS INTERNET AND E- MAIL OPERATIONS TO AVOID A RUSH OF COMPUTER VIRUSES EXPECTED TO STRIKE AROUND THE YEAR 2000 CROSS-OVER PERIOD. THE SARS SAID IN A STATEMENT THAT IT HAD TAKEN A BUSINESS DECISION TO SHUT DOWN THE SYSTEMS FROM DECEMBER 24. "MEMBERS OF THE PUBLIC ARE ADVISED TO USE ALTERNATE MEANS OF COMMUNICATION WITH SARS DURING THIS PERIOD." "THE INTERNET AND email CONNECTIONS WILL BE RE-CONNECTED ON JANUARY 5 AFTER THE SARS INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY DIVISION HAS CHECKED AND VERIFIED THE SAFETY OF THE INTERNET AND email OPERATIONS," THE STATEMENT SAID.

title: HKE121470 -- AUSTRALIAN STOCKS CLOSE SLIGHTLY LOWER
body: THE AUSTRALIAN SHARE MARKET CLAWED BACK EARLY LOSSES IN LATE TRADE TUESDAY TO CLOSE JUST INSIDE NEGATIVE TERRITORY, DESPITE MEDIA HEAVYWEIGHT NEWS CORP FALLING MORE THAN TWO PERCENT.
