title: new web sites about macao start operation
body: as china is going to resume its sovereignty over macao at the end of the year, two new web sites now enable internet surfers to learn more about the region which has been under portuguese rule. internet surfers just have to type in the web addresses of www. macao1999.org or www.macau1999.org to get access to the information about various aspects of macao. the data are provided in simplified chinese, traditional chinese and english. columns include "basic law," "past and present," "chinese and portuguese official documents about macao," "overview of macao," "political structure" and "media services." during the handover period, the web sites will also give reports on celebration activities and important local news, according to the managers of the web sites. the web information is jointly run by the macao-based international institute for software technology of the united nations university and the beijing-based china internet information center and stone rich sight info tech co. ltd.

title: farmers in east china province doing business via internet
body: with the click of a mouse or the press of a key, farmer zhang luozhi can sell tons of vegetables from his homepage on the internet. zhang's case is not unusual in his hometown of shouguang, in east china's shandong province, which is the largest wholesale market of vegetables in china. more than 600 farmers there are profiting from on-line business.  these internet-savvy farmers can now follow and analyze the market, and pinpoint where sales opportunities exist both domestically and overseas.  on-line business has brought more than six million yuan (about 720,000 unitedstates dollars) in returns for local farmers.  shandong's jinxiang county, also known as china's "hometown of garlic," is the first county in the province to be linked with the internet. farmers there sell nearly 200,000 tons of garlic and finished garlic products through on-line sales annually.  many farmers in less-developed zhanhua county are also eager to sell their produce via computer.

title: france telecom to launch new internet phone technology
body: france telecom, france's state monopoly of telecommunications, will launch in 2000 a new technology for putting together portable phones and internet.  the executive officer of france telecom, michel bon, said that the technology, called general package radio service (gprs), will help push forward the marketing of portable phones for connecting with internet.  gprs has been undergoing experiments with two phone producers, the french company alcatel and unitedstates motorola, with great success, he said.  "the connection of portable phones with private computers is developing with great steps and is making the industrial perspective of webphone more uncertain," he said.  gprs will help stimulate the use of portable private computers connected with portable phones as a space of webphone, he added.

title: un environment book shop landing on internet
body: a new web book shop for the united nations environment program (unep) was launched monday in arendal, norway, the agency's headquarters in nairobi said monday. unep executive director klaus toepfer and state secretary of norwegian environment ministry jesper simonsen attended the launching ceremony. the book shop will allow customers to order copies of all unep publications and cover topics such as environmental laws, climate, industry, and environment and biodiversity. customers using the web site at http://www.earthprint.com will have various payment and delivery options including the use of credit cards and quick delivery service. the book shop will be jointly operated by unep, grid-arendal and smi distribution services (britain).

title: survey shows most u.s. web users do not trust sites they visit
body: a majority of world wide web users in the unitedstates do not trust the sites they visit, according to a report released wednesday by an internet market research firm --jupiter communications.  the report said that 64 percent of on-line consumers surveyed do not think web sites are trustworthy enough in following privacy practices, including not passing user information on to third parties.  consumers' fears are fueled by government and media warnings about the abuse of personal information passing over the internet, according to the report.  the consumers' fears are not easily assuaged despite the majority of web sites post some form of privacy policy.  unless sites take action and educate and communicate with online consumers, the research firm said, the fears will affect both on-line advertising and digital commerce revenue.

title: on-line auctions for rare chinese stamps
body: during the upcoming china 1999 world philatelic exhibition, philatelists worldwide will be able to bid for rare chinese stamps, including the treasured dragon stamps which were issued in 1878 and marked the establishment of a modern postal service in china, via the internet. the on-line auctions for the stamps will be the first of its kind in china, officials with the all-china philatelic federation said here today. all of the 148 lots that will be up for auction are highly valuable, they said. gmai-asia.com, a subsidiary of world-famous auctioneer greg manning auction inc., will organize the stamp auctions on the internet. the company plans to extend its on-line sales in china to include antiques and works of art. the exhibition will be held from august 21 to 30. gmai-asia.com has rented eight exhibition booths for their auctions, and their website address is: http://ccec-auction.com.cn.

title: macao telecom promotes school internet access
body: the macao telecommunications company (ctm) plans to provide equipment, free internet access and technical support to local middle schools to help them make better use of the latest information technology.  sources with the company said that the project will promote the sharing of knowledge and experience among schools, teachers and students.  ctm will provide schools with required hardware, software and installation service to ensure that they have high speed access to the internet. an expert webmaster will assist schools to convert existing teaching materials and other data to web pages.  the company plans to link all education home pages in macao so as to organize better online education. in addition, there will be online discussion areas to facilitate communication between schools.  ctm also considers running online workshops and competitions to allow students to learn and produce innovative web pages. and relevant training will enable teachers to design and produce educational web pages and give them a better understanding of internet security and ethics.

title: australian stocks slide
body: the australian sharemarket suffered its fourth consecutive fall wednesday, forced down by the weakness in key blue chip stocks bhp, news corp and telstra.  the local market's journey into negative territory came after another fall on wall street overnight and continued rate increase fears in the unitedstates.  the all ordinaries index slipped 23.8 points to close at 2,934.9, off a high of 2,958.7.  falls were recorded in most sectors, with the all industrials index down 37.6 points to 5,042.7 and the all resources index falling 14.4 points to 1,299.4.  the big four banks had a mixed day, with the commonwealth bank of australia down 54.9 cents to 23.846 australian dollars and anz falling 17 cents to 10.18 australian dollars.  investors jumped back into the national australia bank, lifting its shares 9.9 cents to 22.529 australian dollars. westpac also finished higher, up one cent to 9.71 australian dollars.  national turnover on the australian stock exchange was 391.52 million shares traded worth 1.231 billion australian dollars (812.5 million unitedstates dollars).

title: indian, dutch firms join in internet venture
body: indian software giant wipro ltd. and the 8-billion-unitedstates-dollar kpn (royal dutch telecom) signed a memorandum of understanding thursday to form a 55 to 45 joint venture to provide internet service in india.  according to a statement released by wipro in bangalore, the internet service will be offered through wipro net, a subsidiary of wipro corporation.  the current management structure of wipro net will be augmented with functional experts from kpn and all services offered by the company will be branded under wipro. wipro net also plans to issue an initial public offer in three years.  wipro net will be an exclusive vehicle for kpn and wipro for internet protocol (ip)-based communication services in india and for multinational customers of kpn in india.  it will also have connectivity with kpn's international ip network, which will enable the joint venture to offer superior quality services.

title: shanghai to enjoy business service via internet
body: shanghai will open its first internet business service center on october 1 this year.  local residents in this oriental metropolis then will be able to enjoy a variety of convenient services such as on-line shopping, food delivery, hotel reservations, and home delivery of consumer goods via the internet.  the center will be linked with more than 100 local department stores promoting their brand-name products on the 'net.  internet users will find easy shopping and quick home delivery simply by typing in their credit card number and password on their home computer keyboard.

title: china construction bank begins internet banking services
body: china construction bank (ccb) announced today that it has begun providing internet banking services the bank's general manager of the online banking department, li kejun, says that this includes a national integrated business network, state-of-the-art information service, and network technology that support real time online settlement of accounts, online shopping, and other electronic commerce services.  customers can manage their current account business, fixed deposits, and credit card accounts online and the advanced coding technology ensures the security of the online business.  the bank's internet banking services begin in beijing and guangzhou and are expected to be available in shenzhen and shanghai soon.

title: australian stock market remains flat
body: the australian stock market closed virtually flat thursday, with falls in banking stocks overriding a strong performance by news corp.  the all ordinaries index closed 0.2 points up to 3,060.0, while the all industrials ended 4.6 points higher at 5,327.0.  in the banking sector, all the four major banks were down, with sector leader national australia bank losing 9.3 cents to end the day at 23.99 australian dollars.  commonwealth slipped 40 cents to 24.40 australian dollars, westpac lost six cents to 10.02 australian dollars, and anz dipped 15.5 cents to 10.98 australian dollars.  national turnover was 469.28 million shares traded worth 1.273 billion australian dollars (840 million unitedstates dollars). falling stocks outnumbered rising stocks 692 to 597 while 514 stocks were steady.

title: china's cybermarketing project
body: china began a cybermarketing project recently to help companies with marketing on websites, the china information industry association (ciia) reports.  the project is sponsored by ciia, china telecom's data communication bureau, and the china financial net information technology co. ltd, according to gao xinmin, vice-director of ciia.  it helps companies with market research and analysis and product development via the internet.  the project has 2 parts: training and internet service. in the first, managers will receive training on cybermarketing and basic internet use; in the second, internet service providers and internet platform providers will provide services.  gao says that it is still difficult to do e-commerce in china, but that cybermarketing, which does not have website costs, will help develop e-commerce.  a survey by the china entrepreneur system this year showed that although 20 percent of chinese companies have a homepage, the addition of information on the homepage is very slow, and 85 percent didn't even add to the homepage in half a year.

title: isps provide consultation for small businesses
body: more than 10 software firms and internet service providers (isp) today set up a consultation group to voluntarily provide information technology consultation for small businesses in china.  named "it volunteer action", it's the second-phase of the "21st century small and medium-sized enterprises informationization training project" , which started may this year.  the project, launched by the state economic and trade commission and funded by the china hewlett packard co. ltd, was to provide training on information technology for small businesses.  so far, it has offered training courses to managers of 25 small businesses around china.  small and medium-sized businesses account for 99.7 percent of all industrial businesses in china, and employ 73 percent of the industrial work-force.  along with improving training services for small businesses, chinese government is working on favorable policies on financing them.  china hp co. ltd the first sino-us joint venture in hi-tech industry, has previously sponsored management training programs for large state-owned businesses in china.

title: intel introduces internet service provider support program
body: the computer chip giant intel corp. has introduced a massive internet service provider (isp) support program, an intel spokesman announced here recently.  according to the spokesman, intel will provide product, technology, information and training services to some 14,000 internet service providers in more than 40 countries.  the corporation has already established a special network for this purpose.  the spokesman said this program will enable internet users to obtain more timely and cheaper services.  more than 20 chinese internet service providers already have joined the program.

title: netscape launches enhanced china netcenter
body: netscape communications, now a subsidiary of america online inc, said thursday that its china netcenter has been enhanced with new localized content and services.  two chinese portals, in simplified and traditional chinese characters, were launched, offering localized content and services integrated with netscape's first chinese language browser.  netscape said that it is working with china internet corporation to provide new localized content for the china netcenter portals in topical areas such as business, computing, entertainment, finance, news, shopping, sports and travel.  the mountain view, california-based company has just released its first chinese language internet browser --netscape communicator 4.51 in simplified and traditional chinese characters.  highlighting its commitment to the development of china's internet industry, netscape said that now, the approximately four million chinese consumers with internet access have a choice of internet browser and can use it in their native language to access the internet.  in addition, netscape said that the new browser source code has been made available to the developer community in china.

title: online shopping pushing up worldwide electronic software sales
body: the worldwide market for electronic software commerce is expanding as more businesses and consumers get accustomed to shopping on the internet.  according to a report released thursday by unitedstates market research firm international data corporation (idc), the market will be worth 3.5 billion unitedstates dollars in 1999 and is expected to reach 32.9 billion dollars by 2003.  online retailers are taking a major share of this market and will continue to command the end-user experience as they improve their customer tracking and product management, idc said.  electronic software commerce consists of the sales of software online, irrespective of the method of delivery. idc said that the market is being driven by a surge in the number of online "e-tailers" with more sophisticated customer tracking and product management techniques and will be driven by the continued migration of computer users to the internet.  in addition, idc said, software vendors are increasingly recognizing the need to provide end users with more options for acquiring software, including direct internet sales and the electronic delivery of both software and licenses.

title: internet access to world remote island nation niue
body: the web has come to the remote south pacific atoll of niue, with the setting up an internet access company on the island, the new zealand infotech weekly reported monday.  internet equipment was hooked up to niue's frame-relay telephone switch, which pipes data at 128 kilobit per second by satellite between the island and new zealand.  other communications between niue's 1,750 inhabitants and the outside world are largely confined to the one aeroplane flight each week to the "rock of polynesia," 2,400 kilometers north-east of new zealand.  an engineer from netlink, an internet company in wellington, spent a week installing the equipment on the island earlier this month, to give the island's 250 users free dial-in web browsing and email.

title: australian stocks close lower despite strong news corp
body: the australian sharemarket finished in negative territory on wednesday, with a strong showing from media giant news corp failing to offset mixed performances among other bluechips.  the benchmark all ordinaries index finished 9.5 points lower at 3054.4, off a high of 3067.9 during the day.  the all industrials index dropped 24.3 points to 5286.7 and the all resources index finished 5.3 points higher at 1305.3 after mixed performances among resource stocks.  "news corp held our market up a bit today," hartley poynton's justin klintberg said.  news corp shares closed 15.8 cents higher at 13.708 australian dollars, with its preferred scrip up 20.4 cents at 12.65 australian dollars.  the commonwealth bank lost 14.3 cents to 24.207 australian dollars, the national australia bank shed 33.7 to 24.04 australian dollars and the anz dropped 0.6 of a cent to 11.10 australian dollars.  westpac was the only major bank to finish higher, up 9.7 cents at 9.847 australian dollars.  national turnover reached 439.69 million shares traded with a valued at 1.25 billion australian dollars (825 million unitedstates dollars), with 643 falls, 564 rises and 420 stocks steady.

title: chinese internet users hit four million
body: the number of chinese internet users hit 4 million last month, according to a report from the china internet network information center (cinic) which was made available today.  the number of on-line computers totaled 1.46 million, with 29, 045 registered domain names, while internet users are now surfing through 9,906 international websites, the report says.  the report was compiled using the answers received on 52,549 questionnaires, and was accomplished in accordance with international practice.  a considerable proportion of internet surfers are young people with good education living in china's economically developed cities, according to the cinic. the report says that 85 percent of all users are male, and 40 percent are in the 21-25 age group. some 86 percent have college degrees, and computer specialists account for 25 percent of all professional users.  china's internet technology has developed remarkably in the past five years and experts predict that the number of internet users in china will reach 5-8 million by the end of this year.

title: australian news makes chinese book donation
body: the australian news corporation donated a number of copies of the macquarie english-chinese dictionary to the national library of china today.  the dictionary is a translation of the macquarie dictionary that was done by the australian studies center at suzhou university, which was published in may by the suzhou university press.  australian news's representative in beijing, laurie smith, said at a donation ceremony that the dictionary will provide a useful reference for students, teachers and researchers and help to increase understanding and cooperation between the people of australia and china.  the macquarie dictionary provides a unique australian outlook on words and usage in the english language. autralian news is one of the world's largest media companies, with total assets worth 36 billion unitedstates dollars.

title: african countries urged to get access to internet
body: african leaders participating in the on-going 35th summit of the organization of african unity (oau) have been urged to get access to internet, the so-called information highway.  the appeal was made by mark malloch brown, administrator with the united nations development program (undp), when addressing a press briefing here monday afternoon.  he said africa's poverty is at least in part attributed to its general absence of access to advanced technology.  "africa, which accounts for some 10 percent of the world's population, has only 0.1 percent internet access rate, the lowest in the whole world," he said.  the hi-technology on the internet can provide many opportunities of business for african countries in dire need of technical guidance, brown added.  african leaders gathered here for the three-day summit of the continental organization, which started monday. as many as 46 heads of state and government and 2,400 delegates attended the opening ceremony of the summit. the summit, the last of this century, is widely regarded as one of paramount importance to the future of the 53-member bloc and the whole continent as a whole.

title: shanghai-taiwan website opens
body: a new website focusing on shanghai and taiwan, www. shanghai-taiwan.org, was launched here yesterday. the website technology is supported by the "window of shanghai", a famous internet website opened by the city government earlier this year. all internet users will be able to refer to the website for details and pictures about exchange information in the fields of tourism, visiting relatives, business cooperation, studying across the taiwan straits, medical treatment and care of people in shanghai and taiwan.

title: china launches first commericial all-sports online
body: shawei announced its launch of china's first commercial all-sports online network (http://www. shawei.com) here today. "shawei will provide china's sports fans with the most exciting sports coverage from china and around the world -all in chinese." from basketball and football to badminton and cricket, shawei plans to offer the latest breaking news, scores, and features covering all sports, and developing a range of interactive services never before available to china's sports fans. "what makes us different from other sources of news and information is that we're an entire online community expecially for china's sports fans."

title: lhasa establishes links to information highway
body: lhasa, the capital of the tibet autonomous region, is now linked to the national information highway thanks to assistance provided by scientists from east china's jiangsu province.  scientists from jiangsu helped the municipal science and technology bureau establish the lhasa science and technology information center which features advanced hardware and software.  local companies, institutions and individuals can access the internet and a number of science and technology information centers throughout the country.  the lhasa city government is also developing scientific achievements and market information databases.  the central government has named 1999 as the year governments at all levels will gain access to the internet.

title: china telecom to get more customers onto cyberspace beijing, june
body: china telecom plans to get more enterprises and families to enter cyberspace this year and to provide government offices access to the internet.  the company has over 2 million customers on line, nearly 100 of them, corporate bodies. it established an e-commerce certificate system last august and has provided platform for on-line securities trading, on-line shopping, and on-line medicare since november.  china telecom hopes to expand its cooperation with various enterprises and plans to provide services like website design, information updating, and technology training for its customers.

title: half of australian homes have computers: abs
body: nearly half of australian households have a home computer and the number of australian households hooked up to the internet has soared to 1.3 million, a five-fold increase in just two years.  that means almost one in five homes has internet access, the australian bureau of statistics (abs) said in its social trends report issued thursday.  the number of households with computers rose from 1.9 million in february 1994 to 3.2 million last november.  and the abs tips 3.5 million households will have computers by the end of this year.  but the growth in internet access has been even more rapid.  in february 1996, just 262,000 households, or 4 percent of the total, had an internet connection, but the number rose to 1.3 million by last november.  but daily computer usage at home rose by only six minutes to 103 minutes between 1992 and 1997.  canberra residents led australia in computer ownership, with 66 percent having computers and 28.2 percent linked to the internet.

title: australian dollar closes higher
body: strong offshore buying pushed the australian dollar nearly half a unitedstates cent higher wednesday, with the upcoming sale of a further stake in australia's leading telecommunications company telstra also supporting the currency's strength.  the news that the australian senate has supported the further partial sale of the australian federal government's stake in telstra corp. sparked a rush to cover short positions.  at the close the australian dollar was at 65.65 unitedstates cents from 65.16 unitedstates cents tuesday.  economist michael workman said the previous sale of telstra had boosted the currency in november 1997 and a similar impact could be expected this time around.  the government got the green light late monday from the senate to proceed with a sale of 16.6 percent of telstra, of which it sold one third in 1997.  the government is expected to retain a 50.1-percent share of telstra.  at the close of the local session, the australian currency was also trading at 63.45 euro cents from 63.03 euro cents tuesday, and 80.05 japanese yen from 79.48 yen.

title: china telecom to put more enterprises into cyberspace
body: china telecom is aiming to put more enterprises into cyberspace. so far, the company has over two million on-line customers, nearly 200 of which are enterprises.  a china telecom official revealed this at a symposium on the government on-line program here today.  besides having established nationwide telephone and mobile phone networks, china has also set up multi-media networks.  china telecom will also find a way to put more families into cyberspace, the official said.  the company established an on-line business certificate system in august 1998, and has developed on-line securities, on-line shopping and on-line medicare since last november.  he also noted that china telecom aims to expand various kinds of cooperation with enterprises, and will also provide services like website design, information updating and technology training for its customers.

title: qinghua university establishes journal website
body: prestigious qinghua university today introduced a new website for chinese journals. the website --www.chinajournal.net.cn --carries excerpts of more than 3,100 journals, as well full texts of over 3,500 journals included on the disc version of china academic journals which the university has published every month over the past four years. the site offers some three million full texts published in chinese journals between 1994-1999, four million extracts and 10 million quotations. the spread of valuable information on the internet will greatly facilitate the creation and application of knowledge, according to experts.

title: beijing to host int'l computer safety exhibition
body: an international exhibition on computer information system safety will be held in beijing between october 25-28.  the exhibition will be jointly sponsored by the ministry of public security and the state information center. exhibits will include software, technology and systems related to computer system safety.  computer-based information networks have established throughout china and are playing an important role in the country's economic and social development.  china had 2.1 million internet subscribers and some 17,000 registered domain names by the end of last year. the nation also had over 744,000 on-line computers.

title: pagers seek salvation online
body: china's paging business is turning to the internet to survive the squeeze from the expansion of mobile phone communication.  there are more than 60 million pager users in china, but the popularity of mobile phones has outstripped pagers and begun to crunch into pager profit margins, according to an official from the ministry of information industry.  the number of mobile phone users grew by 11.3 percent last year to 24.98 million. "the impact of mobile phones is compelling and we must find alternative ways to reshape our paging business," said yang jun, general manager of the china motion telecom development co, one of the country's leading paging operators.  with the help of the paging center, pager users can access their email information and special web news without dialing up the internet.  telecom experts say paging operators should take advantage of their large pool of clients and make use of the internet to provide convenient services to ease people's daily lives.  however, limited room for internet applications in china has slowed their pace of investment in such developments.

title: china's relics protectors looking to computerized information
body: china's state administration of cultural heritage has decided to standardize information on cultural relics in the nation's museums.  it will establish an information database for cultural relics in museums, according to dong baohua, vice-director of the administration.  china has a wealth of cultural relics and fossils but its museums are using backward management methods. although 60 or so are linked to the worldwide web, only a few like the henan museum and qufu confucius museum have their own web-sites.  most have wasted time developing repetitive software for linking up with the internet, dong says, and the databases they established are not uniform.  in april, the administration decided to overhaul the information on cultural relics, world heritage sites, and important archaeological digs.

title: u.s. internet marketing firm gains access to china
body: a unitedstates company announced friday that it has received a license from the chinese government to market goods and services directly to the chinese populace through its web site.  chinamallusa.com inc., an e-commerce company established in 1997 for the purpose of marketing chinese and unitedstates products through the internet, said that it is the only foreign firm to receive such a comprehensive license allowing it to sell retail throughout the entire country.  to date, according to the company, only wal-mart, the unitedstates department store giant, has been granted a license to establish a retail store in china but that license is limited to operating in shenzhen, one of china's special economic zones.  china's retail market is huge, the company said, although there are only four million households currently on the internet.  the e-commerce company has so far established partnerships with two major beijing-based retail businesses, as well as ties with other three chinese companies.

title: access from foreign domains nearly half internet traffic in u.s.
body: internet access via foreign domains has reached nearly half of all web traffic in the unitedstates, according to a report released thursday.  on june 6, for instance, about 44 percent of unitedstates web traffic was from foreign domains, nearly matching the traffic from commercial (.com network organizations (.net), educational (.edu), organization (.org military organizations (.mil) and government (.  gov) domains combined.  the information published on statmark, a provider of global data on domain usage, reflected real-time data gathered from some 28 million unitedstates daily visitors to more than 86,000 web sites.  "it is important to note that america online and other noncountry-code-specific internet service providers moving into global markets affect the representation of foreign domains," statmark said.  the countries whose domains most frequently serfed by americans include japan, canada, australia and some european countries.  as far as unitedstates domains are concerned, commercial and network organizations web sites attracted most visitors, while military organizations and government domains were the least visited.

title: on-line shopping available in wenzhou
body: a new online shopping service, the first of its kind in east china's zhejiang province, provides local residents with convenient stay-at-home shopping.  wenzhou telecom bureau introduced internet system as part of an effort to spur local business development, shorten the commodity circulation process and ultimately reduce the cost of commodities by a wide margin.  the rapidly increasing use of computers in china, along with modern lifestyle orientation and advanced attitudes portends great potential for the new approach to shopping.

title: chinese children contacting each other over internet
body: children in the chinese cities of guangzhou, shanghai and beijing greeted each other and showed their art works over the internet today.  the activity, co-sponsored by an intel china office and china's computer giant greatwall group, was aimed to help increase chinese's children's awareness of the internet.  children participating in today's internet activity were also invited to visit some high-tech research and development centers, in an attempt to further provoke their curiosity about science.

title: chinese english-language internet forum
body: china's first internet forum for english speakers has gone into operation in beijing, using a system developed by beijing's zhaodaola internet co., ltd.  the english forum is expected to help increase communications and an exchange of views on the nato bombing of kosovo and other issues.  the company opened a chinese forum for chinese internet users to express their anger on the global network after unitedstates-led nato's brutal attack of the chinese embassy in belgrade, yugoslavia on may 7, 1999.

title: shenyang internet exchange established
body: the shenyang internet exchange computer center was set up today in this capital of northeast china's liaoning province, linking the city's computer networks.  the new system will increase the transfer speed of information for users of the local networks.  the city has many networks based on internet technology providing information services for education, science and technology, the economy, and telecommunication.  but up till now, there had been no link between the networks, causing low transmission speed and poor connections. to better share information sources and data, the city decided to operate a high-speed data exchange service through the center.  with the help of the new center, computer users in the city now will find it easier to exchange information among the local networks.

title: 1 million australian households with internet access
body: the number of australian households with internet access nearly quadrupled in the past two years to top one million, a survey revealed thursday.  almost 1.1 million households, nearly 16 percent of the total, in australia, had internet access in 1998 -up from 286,000 in 1996, the australian bureau of statistics (abs) said.  households with children were the most likely to have access to the internet, along with families earning more than 66,000 australian dollars (43,560 unitedstates dollars).  in 1998, 45 percent of australian homes had a computer and nearly 16 percent had access to the internet.  just over 60 percent of australia's adult population (8.1 million) used a computer and 32 percent (4.2 million) accessed the internet in 1998 -mostly from work or home.  by international standards, the monthly internet access cost in australia is relative low, totaling 26 unitedstates dollars on average per household user, or about one percent of the per-capita monthly income.

title: new zealand's pay tv network plans interactive service
body: sky network tv, major pay tv network in new zealand, is set to become more interactive by introducing email, banking and shopping to its digital satellite television service, new zealand press association (nzpa) reported friday.  sky tv recently announced a conditional agreement to buy 30 percent of the internet group, an internet service provider trading as ihug.  according to nzpa, chairman craig heatley of sky tv outlined an array of services subscribers would be able to access through their digital remote, "from shopping, banking, games, email and information options," when speaking at company's annual general meeting thursday.  "we have done a great deal of work on how much of the capacity we will allocate for pay-perview and how much we leave for data transmission, like the internet," he said.  sky has already trialled television internet access in hotels, with "very promising" results, he added.

title: icrc opens website to help family members separated in balkan crisis
body: the international committee of the red cross (icrc) wednesday opened a special website to help restore contact between members of families split up by the crisis in the balkans.  people anxious to locate relatives can have access to the special website. this is the first time the geneva-based icrc has used the internet for this purpose.

title: fierce telecoms competition emerging in tianjin
body: the china jitong tele-communication co. ltd. today opened an ip telephone experimental network in tianjin, the biggest port city in north china, as well as providing such services to local consumers. the city now has three large-scale telecommunication companies --china telecom, china unicom and jitong, offering telephone services, and become the market with the most fierce competition in telecommunications anywhere in the country. as the cost of ip telephone calls is much cheaper than fixed lines, most insiders are bullish about its prospects. since the newly-established ip telephone network is still at an experimental stage, only 12 chinese cities, including beijing, tianjin, shanghai, guangzhou, can provide such services at present. insiders also pointed out that china telecom and china unicom, the country's two biggest telecommunication companies, have greatly improved tianjin's telecommunication industry over the past few years. and jitong's arrival in the city will further activate the local telecommunication market and hopefully help lower telephone fees.

title: microsoft upgrades windows
body: microsoft corporation has upgraded windows 98. the company will make the upgrade edition available this week at a price of 89.95 unitedstates dollars.  it will also sell the upgrade over the world wide web to existing windows 98 owners for 19.95 dollars.  the new edition will include the company's recent browser technology, internet explorer 5.0, and all virus prevention measures. it also includes new hardware and electronic commerce support, as well as a new home networking feature that will enable several computers to connect to the internet simultaneously through a single account with an internet service provider.  meanwhile, apple computer also plans to introduce an operating system upgrade called mac os 8.6, at no charge to current users.

title: macao, shanghai students hold internet exchanges
body: middle school students in macao and shanghai saturday started their two-month exchanges through the internet. the activity is aimed at boosting contacts and understanding between young people in macao, which will return to the motherland on december 20 this year, and shanghai, china's largest metropolis. the students in macao and shanghai can form different teams to participate in the internet exchanges by way of locating the web sites at "www.shma.edu.mo" and "www.shma.online.sh.cn", respectively. those in shanghai are required to design web pages in english featuring macao's technological, educational, economic and cultural conditions, while students in macao can learn more about the achievements the inland areas have made in reform and openingup, organizers said. sponsors of the activity include the macao association for scientific and technological promotion, macao university, macao computer society and shanghai scientific and technological association.

title: china culture web-site launched
body: comprehensive information about china's cultural legacy is now available on the internet from today. culture vultures can satisfy their curiosity and thirst for knowledge by searching the web address: http://www.ccnt.com.cn, which is the new china culture information net (ccin). ten sub-items are on offer providing information from the ministry of culture which includes a digital library, details of relics and museums, literature and art, book reviews, and so on. indeed, 1999 is the year the chinese government intends to accelerate the pace of being wired on the net and the launch of this website marks the timely reaction of the ministry of culture to this national and global trend. as a registered website sponsored by the ministry of culture, ccin aims to offer the general public a wide-range of cultural information and serves as a window into chinese culture to the world. it will regularly update its information databank to meet the needs of the public and gradually develop into the largest cultural website in chinese, a ministry official said.

title: intel to promote internet use in shanghai
body: the unitedstates intel corporation plans to join hands with a shanghai company to promote the use of the internet in this largest industrial and commercial city of china.  intel's vice-president dr. john davies signed a memorandum here recently with zhang linde, general manager of shanghai information industry co. ltd., agreeing to cooperate in the application of internet technology in both the local government and enterprises.  according to the vice-president, intel will introduce advanced computer equipment and technology into government departments, local manufacturers, internet providers, and other shanghai enterprises.  shanghai, and china as a whole, has great potential demand for computer technology, as doing business electronically becomes increasingly popular, davies said.  intel now has representative offices in 12 major chinese cities, including beijing, shanghai and guangzhou, and its first production center in china, specializing in assembling and testing flash memory, began operations here last year.

title: shaanxi has over 50,000 internet users
body: the number of internet users has reached 50,400 in northwest china's shaanxi province, representing a five fold increase from the end of 1997's figure.  the increase is higher than the national average. the number of shaanxi's internet users accounts for 2.4 percent of the country's total, compared with 1.2 percent at the end of 1997. the province has input more than 200 information websites and data bases into the internet, according to a local source.  shaanxi has become a regional information center in the western part of china, authorities say. at present, more than 200 enterprises, institutions, social groups and government organs are making use of the internet.

title: microsoft solutions fair in hk displays web technology
body: microsoft solutions fair'99 opened here thursday, showcasing how businesses and end users can connect to success by taking advantage of the internet technologies.  the fair, previewing the latest and most essential solutions offered by microsoft and both local and international microsoft certified solution providers, presented the latest web-related technologies used to support on-line business initiatives.  a microsoft office 2000 workshop at the fair will provide a preview of the latest tools for office automation in the collaborative workplace, while over 40 seminars and workshops will provide a closer look at what innovative technologies and internet connectivity can do to increase a company's productivity and profits.

title: e-china forum to promote e-business
body: the china council for the promotion of international trade (ccpit) will host a july forum to encourage chinese government administrations and enterprises to use the internet.  the e-china forum will be held in beijing on july 5 and later in shanghai, wuhan, chengdu and guangzhou.  the two-day forums in the respective cities will feature one panel, three keynote speakers and 18 general sessions.  topics covering e-service, e-business, e-community and emarketing will inform participants of related practices in singapore, taiwan and hongkong.

title: china's online bookstores to thrive
body: china's largest bookstore estimates that its book sales via the internet will be thriving in the near future, the people's daily reported today. beijing book mansion, a new, large-scale book store, initiated its own electronic sales network in march. within the first ten days, its website, www.jbbb.com.cn, was visited by 40,238 customers and received 704 orders worth 54,584 yuan (6,576 unitedstates dollars), an encouraging sign compared with other businesses in this field, the newspaper said. meanwhile, store staff say their turnovers at the store on recent weekends have doubled to 600,000 yuan. after the first on-line bookstore opened in 1997 in hangzhou in east china's zhejiang province, many other bookstores followed suit. unfortunately, most of them were not as successful as amazon, a unitedstates on-line bookstore giant. a great number bookstores only use their websites as a window to introduce latest publications, but do not have the necessary mechanism to handle on-line sales.

title: china to form orderly local market for internet industry
body: china's internet industry is trying to regulate the market at an early stage.  on thursday, eight leading chinese internet content providers ( icps) clinched an agreement in beijing to form the china icp united development high-profile conference, china daily reported today.  in this way, some irrational business operations are not so likely to harm the sector over the long run, the companies decided.  the eight icps are: sohu, sina, chinabyte, netease, china wide web, goyoyo, shanghai online and information highway tech.  although competing toughly in the market with 2.1 million internet users nationwide, the eight icps said they hope the organization will help to pave the way for a healthy competitive arena and set up business rules accepted by all.  the conference agreed that local companies need a regulated domestic market which ensures chinese companies are able to expand quickly and have enough strength to compete with their foreign counterparts that have shown a lot interest in entering the market.  the organization is committed to take united action to promote internet-related training and education, the newspaper said.

title: shanghai lawyers association introduces homepage
body: the shanghai lawyers association has established a new homepage --www.lawyers.com.cn --to serve internet surfers from both at home and abroad. the association's goal is to enhance the general public's awareness of the law and promote professional exchanges between local lawyers and their counterparts in other parts of china and abroad. the association is the largest group of its kind in china. the homepage is expected to provide shanghai residents with access to valuable legal assistance. "the homepage will help people understand the legal profession, " according to one local resident.

title: internet use becoming a daily essential in u.s.
body: approximately 37 million unitedstates adults use the internet at home on at least a daily basis, compared to only 19 million in mid-1997, according to a new study released wednesday.  the study, based on a nationally representative survey of more than 1,000 unitedstates adults by the end of 1998, also found that the number of daily unitedstates internet users at work has mushroomed from 19 million to 32 million since mid-1997.  "the internet has gone from being a curiosity to being a daily source for email, shopping, research and news," said the study conductor strategis group, an e-data resources and market analysis company. the group estimates that 84 million americans or 42 percent of unitedstates adults, now use the internet at home or at work.  according to the study, 44 percent of internet users in the unitedstates spend less time watching television due to internet use. therefore, there will be a market share war between television and internet web sites for viewship and advertising money.  adults in 34 million unitedstates households now use the internet a total of 65 million hours per day, compared to 525 million television viewing hours for all unitedstates adults.

title: more chinese to get connected to internet
body: more chinese are expected to connect up to the internet for information and for other activities like shopping, booking tickets, and taking part in parties.  the internet service is becoming less expensive and a lot more convenient. by the end of last year, about 747,000 computers were hooked up to the internet in china, with more than two million users, sources said.  the number of people joining the internet grew 78.7 percent in the latter half of last year.  previously, slow speed, high charges, and limited information in chinese kept the business from going faster, now these obstacles are beginning to disappear.  on march 1, telecommunications authorities cut internet charges and technical improvement are accelerating the internet speed.  chinese and foreign developers have been making an effort to increase chinese information on the internet and more government organizations will be hooked up to the net to increase the information in chinese.  the china internet network information center expects by the end of the year to see 6.7 million internet users in china.

title: china merchant bank opens on-line service beijing, march
body: shopping can now be done at the click of a mouse by the residents of beijing.  china merchant bank has opened a website on the internet that provides on-line banking services and also provides internet users with information and account settlement services all in the quiet of their homes.  people with bank credit cards can apply for these services and a 2,000-yuan shopping limit for each purchase and 5,000 yuan a day.  the bank is negotiating with major department stores and electric appliance manufacturers in beijing to expand these services.

title: china set to introduce philatelic web site
body: china national philatelic corporation and all-china philatelic federation (acpf) will introduce the nation's first philatelic web site on april 1. china philatelic information (cpi) will provide information related to policies and specific regulations governing stamp issues and collecting, according to the acpf. the web site will also offer reports on global stamp collecting activities and provide a data base for collectors. china will host the 22nd conference of the universal postal union and the china 1999 world philatelic exhibition in august. internet surfers can visit the site at http://www.cpi.com.cn to obtain information on stamp collecting, auctions and related business activities.

title: china puts trade information on internet beijing, march
body: china has recently opened a trade information website on the internet, the first of its kind, offering a 24 hour information service about chinese trade and business for the russian and east european markets. the website is jointly set up by a shenzhen and a harbin electronic technological corporation and the address is www. russiamarket.com. all the information on the website is offered in russian, which is hugely convenient for businessmen and enterprises in russia and east european countries, said chang chun, chairman of the shenzhen corporation. colored pictures of products are also available, he added. usually interested foreign countries can only get information about chinese trade and business at commercial fairs.

title: internet access expected to rise in u.s.
body: internet penetration is projected to rise to one third of unitedstates households by the end of 1999 and close to two thirds by the end of 2003, from the current 25 percent level, a unitedstates research firm reported on tuesday.  consumers are expected to spend 56 billion unitedstates dollars on internet access services over the next five years and the market is forecast to grow at an annual rate of 21 percent, said the massachusetts-based yankee group following its latest study.  falling personal computer prices are enabling more households to buy the devices to get on-line, said the company, which has found that 46 percent of unitedstates households with pcs cite the internet as the main use for their computers.

title: real estate information found on internet shanghai, march
body: east china's shanghai municipality has opened a new website page on the internet today, offering information about shanghai's real estate. the website address is http://www.real estate.sh.cn.. people can get information about latest policies, regulations, and real estate quotations. people can also find details about houses for rent and for sale, including the sizes, prices and locations by just entering into the website. the information system, which combines information, management, services and transactions, has been listed among the 20 key information system projects for the 50th anniversary of the founding of new china. the website has utilized the latest technology of internet/ intranet to accomplish the information collection, check and confirmation, and maintenance.

title: sino-u.s. cooperation in internet application project
body: shanghai information industry co.  , ltd. signed an agreement here today with the intel semiconductor ltd. to cooperate in promoting internet application and development in china.  they will conduct a series of cooperation in opening websites for the shanghai municipal government, the local electronic sector and medium/small-sized enterprises.  at the same time, the companies will join hands in the fields of internet education programs and internet promotion and application technology.  statistics show that the "shanghai hotline", the city's largest information network, has so far received nearly 20 million visitors to its 200 websites, and the number of its registered users will rise to 100,000.

title: internet advertising to become new favorite in china
body: the internet advertising sector will be much favored in china amidst a booming computer market and the internet surfing craze, according to china commercial news.  with no time and space limitations, internet advertising has better opportunities for development compared with other advertising methods. internet surfers only need to click the mouse to get information, and through email, customers and the staff of enterprises can keep in direct contact with each other.  "but internet advertising is only at a nascent development stage in china, and it has not produced its due economic returns," an internet advertisement designer has said.  according to him, several factors stand in the way of development. the most obvious ones are the low-level of design ability and inappropriate distribution.  major players in the sector are now stepping up their efforts to upgrade technology in this regard and substantial achievements have already been made.  china's internet surfers are expected to hit 4.5 million by 2000, and experts believe internet advertising will become a favorite sector in the near future.

title: grave details of australian war dead available on internet
body: australians are now able to obtain details about the graves of more than 100,000 countrymen killed in the two world wars by looking up the internet. australian federal veterans affairs minister bruce scott said wednesday that a new debt of honor register had been established by the british-based commonwealth war graves commission detailing the graves of 1.7 million members of british commonwealth forces killed in action. "a very important part of australia's history was written on the battlefields of many conflicts this century --101,285 australians were killed in the two world wars alone," scott said. the register database makes it possible to pinpoint the grave site of any name commemorated. details of 60,000 civilian casualties of world war two are also recorded. the debt of honor register is located at http://www.cwgc.org.

title: asia's largest book store opens on-line service beijing, march
body: the beijing book mansion, the largest retail bookstore in asia, opened an on-line buying facility today, which will cater for millions of chinese website browsers, the beijing youth daily reports.  the on-line bookstore has a catalogue of 160,000 books and operates an all day service.  readers can purchase books by credit card and will receive their books within 24 hours, a result of co-operation between the book mansion and financial institutions.  the manager of the book mansion says that if the on-line bookstore runs smoothly he will consider expanding the on-line business to video products and electronic publications.  the beijing book mansion opened for business last may.

title: brazil's internet users increase sharply
body: the number of internet users in brazil grew by more than 130 percent in 1998, reaching 2.  7 million, a study by the international data corporation (idc) said on tuesday.  the unitedstates-based firm predicted that the brazilian internet market would register a growth of 40 percent this year, to reach 3.  8 million users.  before the year 2003, the expectation is that the market will grow 133 percent yearly, surpassing nine million users.  the investigation revealed that 27 percent of brazilian internet users had bought products or services through the net. in the unitedstates and asia, the figures are 53 and 45 percent respectively.

title: machinery, electronics producers to bid over internet
body: china's trade ministry has released information about the bidding for the import of machinery and electronic products on the internet for the first time. the ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation (moftec) recently posted information on 56 kinds of machinery and electronic products that it wishes to import on its official website at: www.moftec.gov.cn. the on-line information includes product descriptions, technical specifications and bidding deadlines for traders in these products. it also covers administration regulations. moftec official said that on-line information can raise efficiency, standardize the bidding process and increase transparency in administration. the ministry held on-line bidding successfully for textiles last year, and adopted this electronic methods this year for paraffin wax and other 12 types of commodities. the ministry said it will speed up the development of on-line identification and license releasing for commodities, and create a comprehensive electronic bidding system as soon as possible.

title: consumer can lodge complaints on website
body: chinese consumers now can file their complaints through the internet.  sohu, a famous web search engine, and china consumer news, jointly launched a one-month special internet service from march 1, for the consumers to forward their discontent and criticism over products and services. the effort is made to greet the consumer rights day on march 15 which has been designated by the government to safeguard the interest of consumers.  it is learned that it is the first time that chinese consumers resort to high-tech telecommunication means in the protection of their rights and interest.  besides offering advice on protection of interest, the website also provides application forms for filing complaints and a complaint mail box.  after receiving the application form, sohu and china consumer news will cooperate in contacting relevant departments to look into the case according to law, and will inform the consumer of the results through email.

title: korean air launches on-line reservation service
body: korean air on wednesday launched an on-line reservation service, from which customers can book, pay for tickets and request delivery via its internet home page (http:/ /www.koreanair.co.kr), the company said. the airline has opened its on-line service for its direct routes to japan and china and will expand to southeast asian and european routes in the second half of the year. full service to all routes is scheduled in the first half of next year. those who buy tickets from the internet may receive a fivepercent discount off the list price before may 31 this year. customers can have tickets delivered to them within five days or pick up them at the airport at no extra charge.

title: italy uncovers world child pornography ring
body: an italian association announced sunday that it had discovered an international ring made up of at least 92 multinational pedophiles who produce and swap child pornography via the internet.  italy's rainbow telephone association, formed to counter child abuse, said that one of its operators stumbled on october 4, 1998 in a spanish internet site which promised the free exchange of child porn.  "the operator pretended to be a pedophile and then it took four months to win the confidence of the organization to get them to send us a list of 92 members", the association said.  in recent weeks, rainbow telephone brought to light and reported to italian authorities about 20 other pedophile sites, "a real worldwide chain for the exchange of pedophile materials involving thousands of children aged between two and 12 years," described the association.  the president of rainbow telephone fortunato di noto said, " this is the biggest such organization we've come up against in three years."

title: eds-college student-internet more chinese college students using internet
body: more chinese college grads are adding internet abilities to their resumes and consider it a good recommendation.  today's "china youth daily" reported that over 80 percent of china's major colleges have their own local area network (lan) to prove more opportunities for their students.  one english major at beijing's languages and culture university said that he spends twenty hours a week on the internet and considers it the best way to get the information he needs.  a survey of qinghua university students found that 88.1 percent of those surveyed have been using the internet for a year and a half and nearly 70 percent have got information via the internet.  some college seniors, the paper said, consider the internet a lifestyle as well as a special way to look for jobs.  the guangdong provincial government has begun rejecting applications from people who cannot use the internet and it plans to establish its own lan and will allow only those who can use the network to do ordinary government work, according to the report.

title: beijing tops in china internet surfers
body: china's capital beijing leads the country in internet surfers, according to the china internet network information center.  guangdong, jiangsu, and zhejiang provinces and the city of shanghai rank the second, third, fourth and fifth respectively.  a recent survey by the center shows that about 77 percent of china's internet users are in the eastern part of the country, with western regions accounting for only 23 percent.  the number of internet users has increased to 2.1 million from 670,000 just two years ago. south china's guangdong province has had the greatest growth in the number of users since 1997, followed by east china's jiangsu and zhejiang provinces.  tibet, qinghai and ningxia have the smallest surfer populations.

title: cable fault cuts off key part of uk's internet
body: a key part of uk's internet suffered a severe and surprising blow when a transatlantic cable breakage took over 24 hours to fix.  the joint academic network (janet), the largest computer network in britain, was unable to route emails and other information to and from american over the weekends after a cable deep below the atlantic failed.  "for a large part of britain's internet users it meant that what they had been assured could never happen, had happened," the daily telegraph said tuesday in a report.  it had been widely believed that the internet, designed to withstand nuclear attack, would be impervious to failure. however, the new incident shows that the internet is not robust enough.  teleglobe international, the telecoms company operating the cable which janet uses, said that service had been restored by late afternoon on monday.  normally, internet traffic would be re-directed via another cable but teleglobe said this did not happen because the volume of traffic was too high.

title: commercial homepage directory established in macao
body: the macao telecommunications company (ctm) has established a commercial homepage directory via the internet. entering ctm's web site of www.macau.ctm.net, internet surfers around the world can easily locate the commercial homepages established at ctm to obtain information and related services and products. the directory includes over 100 business homepages which are divided into 12 categories according to their business nature.

title: illegal ip telephony operation strictly banned
body: illegal operation of ip telephony is an act of information smuggling and should be strictly banned, a senior official said here today.  zhang chunjiang, director of the telecommunications administrative bureau under the ministry of information industry, told a press conference that the ministry has decided in principle to apply the ip telephony, a kind of internet-related telephone service, to the domestic market.  the ministry has already entrusted several telecommunication companies to run the business on a trial basis, zhang said, adding that licenses will be formally issued later this year.  "the ip telephony should be subject to the strict government regulation," he stressed.  according to him, the country has suffered an annual loss of billions of yuan to the illegal operation by some domestic operators in collusion with foreign companies.  "we'll reinforce the crackdown on such unlawful practices," he told the press conference.

title: iraq to be connected with internet
body: iraq will be hooked up to the internet in the coming few days, an iraqi weekly reported on thursday.  al-zawra weekly quoted helal al-bayaty, director of the national computer center, as saying that preparations are being made for the project.  iraqi ministries and state offices will have access to the internet soon, he said.  special programs had been designed to guarantee users to get information without any other immoral cultural infiltrations.  iraq will transmit the genuine iraqi culture through the internet, he added.

title: yahoo finds ad agency in china
body: the internet content provider yahoo has authorized the beijing-based infoshare technology co.  ltd. to be its exclusive advertising agency in china.  according to an agreement inked today between yahoo and infoshare, the latter will promote yahoo services in china and help chinese customers create on-line advertisements on yahoo's worldwide network.  infoshare is an internet service company funded by the china international electronic commerce center. the company designed and built the "made-in-china" web market and china's ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation web site.  a chinese textile exporter and a local town government have signed agreements with infoshare to display their ads and economic and investment information on yahoo's global network, according to reports.

title: agricultural bank of china shanghai branch encouraging consumption
body: the agricultural bank of china shanghai branch will spend part of a ten billion yuan fund to provide consumer loans to farmers this year. these loans will help farmers to purchase agricultural machinery, housing, cars, and to further their education.  yan qifen, the shanghai branch governor, today said that in addition, the branch will offer loans to the pudong new area, nine municipality level industrial development zones, high-tech industries, key infrastructure facilities, and rural-electricity grid renovation.  this year, the branch will open an on-line bank, an on-line consultation system, and provide investment-consultation services to individuals in urban and suburban shanghai.

title: chinese web search engine profitable
body: sohoo, a web search engine, has become the first profitable chinese website making one million unitedstates dollars of profits last year, the shanghai based wen wei po reported today.  this figure accounted for approximately 70 percent of the total profits in china's internet market.  sohoo is based on a chinese language platform. its categorization of websites and other information mainly caters to the chinese people.  most of sohoo's profits were from commercial business websites such as microsoft, intel, hewlett-packard and beijing beer, said sohoo president zhang chaoyang.  currently, the engine serves 2 million visitors every month.  however, the newspaper reported that another major chinese website, information highway is actually in the red.  it is now moving from providing internet services to investment consultation, the paper said.

title: eu opens "one stop internet shop for business"
body: the european commission, the european union's executive body, said here monday that it has created a one stop internet shop (osis) for business on the internet with a new website of http://europa.eu.int/business. eu single market commissioner mario monti said in a statement that the osis aims to give business better and easier access to information and advice on single market rules and opportunities. "we also expect the internet shop to provide us with valuable feedback from business on the problems companies encounter in the single market, which will help us to improve the single market framework further." the commission also said the most important added value of the new website is to offer direct access to those parts of existing sources of information and advice which are most relevant to companies operating in the single market. while showing how to surf in the shop, a commission's expert said that by simply "bookmarking" the osis, companies and individuals can obtain a fast track to the information and sources of advice most relevant to them without having to sort through the wealth of data available on the world wide web. this access is likely to be of particular value to small and medium-sized companies which may lack the resources to track down such information on their own. the one stop shop also offers direct access to over 230 euro info centers (eics), the commission's largest business advice network, while giving free, direct access to public procurement tender notices published on the eu's tenders electronic daily data base and to contract points for citizens and business in member states' administrations for resolving single market problems, the commission said. the eu executive also said the one stop internet shop, available in the 11 languages of the 15 eu nations, is part of its dialogue with citizens and business set up under a eu's single market action plan.

title: china's "government on internet" project launched
body: china launched its "government on the internet" project today, aiming at encouraging government departments to put their information on the net to share with the public.  more than 60 percent of them are expected to be on-line by the end of this year and this is expected to reach 80 percent by the year 2000, an official in charge said.  the information project is jointly hosted by the data communications bureau under the china telecommunications corporation and the economic information center the under the state economic and trade commission of china.  the xinhua news agency network has been authorized to offer information and consulting services for the construction of government websites.  statistics show that the number of china's internet users has reached 2.21 million even though it was only became available three years ago.

title: china's internet users exceed 2 million
body: china had more than 2.1 million internet users by the end of the 1998, four times the figure of a year ago.  by the end of last year, china had 744,000 computers connected to the internet, more than doubling the figure in 1997.  the number of registered names of internet users in china grew to 18,000 in 1998, three times the figure in 1997. some 5,300 web sites have been opened on chinanet, the official server for the internet in china.  the ministry of information industry forecasts that the number of internet users will increase by 1.5 million this year and they will top 4.5 million in 2000.  china has put priority on developing a data communication network connected with the rest of the world. it will invest 140 billion yuan in construction of wide-band telecommunication networks every year in the next three years.

title: china's peking opera goes on line
body: peking opera, one of china's main traditional performing arts which has been popular for more than two centuries, has made its debut on the internet, according to chinese cultural news. by visiting the web site: www.beijingopera.org., viewers can enjoy performances by familiar stars, receive information about this long-acclaimed theatrical art, as well as exchanging opinions with fans worldwide using today's electronic forum. these days peking opera usually attracts much older chinese fans but it is hoped that by making it available on the latest medium of our time, it will win favor among youngsters.

title: web surfers can attend wef annual meeting through internet
body: web surfers, no matter where they are and when they wish to, can take part in the 1999 annual meeting of the world economic forum (wef) through the internet. one plenary session per day from the main program will be bro adcast live, along with several press conferences each day, the wef announced at a press conference here tuesday. this will be the first time that a wef annual meeting can be accessed through the web. its special site http://live99.weforum.org is the product in cooperation with the cable news networks financial news service, novell inc, and realnetworks inc. "responsible globality: managing the impact of globalization" has been chosen as the theme of the wef 29th annual meeting scheduled from january 28 to february 2 in the eastern swiss city of davos.

title: china puts seismological data on internet
body: china has put its seismological data on the internet. the china seismological information net was created by the information center of the china seismological bureau, and covers seismological data, documentation, disaster prevention and the related technology. this new website connects the computer network of china's seismological system with china's technological network and the internet. experts say that the opening of the website is conducive to the development of the country's seismological research and will help promote information and technology exchanges with other countries. the website address is: http://www.eq-csi.ac.cn.

title: family planning commission goes on line
body: the state family planning commission (sfpc) has opened a website on the internet to introduce china's family planning policies and achievements. the website was established in mid-december and includes pages concerning the "basic views and policies on population and development," "efforts to control population growth and improve the quality of the population," and "achievements and progress in china's family planning." the site has already received hundreds of visitors. the sfpc has also added information on the organizations and structure of the commission, international exchanges and cooperation in family planning, and the problems and challenges faced by these efforts. the website address is: www.sfpc.gov.cn.

title: greek internet users strike against ote rise in phone calls
body: greece's internet users thursday staged a 24-hour boycott of the web in protest against the plans by the state-run hellenic telecommunication organization (ote) to increase local phone call charges.  this is the first such mass protest in greece.  the internet users sent protest letters via email and fax to the greek prime minister's office, ote and the greek parliament.  it was reported that ote's new tariff systems would raise the cost of local phone calls by up to 72 percent, making the use of the internet a financial burden for most of its users.  currently, greece has about 40,000 to 50,000 internet users.

title: number of chinese internet users up dramatically
body: the number of internet users in china grew by 900,000 in 1998 from the previous year to more than 1.5 million.  beijing has 400,000 internet users, the largest number in any province and municipality in china, followed by guangdong province, and shanghai.  the chinese have 540,000 computers linked to the internet and more than 14,000 internet service businesses, 3,550 of which are in beijing.  internet users below the age of 35 account for 84.1 percent of the total number of users. of these, 43.3 percent spend one to five hours each week on the internet; 26.3 percent,five to ten hours; and 20.1 percent, more than ten hours.

title: ethiopian telecoms corporation to improve internet services
body: the ethiopian telecommunications corporation announced wednesday that it is prepared to instal additional gateway satellite stations and modems to avoid web site traffic congestion and strengthen its server capacity.  berhe seyoum, liaison department manager of the corporation, told the press here that 128 modems have been newly purchased to add up to the 96 already existing ones.  berhe said upon going operational, the additional modems will ease traffic congestion for the 2,400 internet subscribers and increase the present server capacity three-fold.  the corporation is also preparing to construct gateway satellite stations to cater for the ever increasing demand of subscribers, he said.  according to berhe, the construction of the gateway satellite stations to be carried out with 1.3 million unitedstates dollars will be completed at the end of this year, the ethiopian telecommunications corporation started its internet service in 1997 and has now 2,400 subscribers. the additional stations will raise the number of subscribers to 14,000.

title: banking services over internet in eastern china
