body: uganda investment authority has licensed another internet service provider acr, bringing to three the number of full internet providers in the country.  acr was granted the license to provide among other services, email and internet, the new vision newspaper wednesday quoted uia investment officer dr. james mutende as saying.  cliff obi, one of the acr directors, said that his company is not only setting its eyes on providing internet services, but also aims at being a third network operator.  "our aim is to be the premium internet service provider in uganda, providing real-time internet web-browsing capabilities and email," he said, adding "our primary goal is to take the information superhighway to the rural areas, the villages and the schools." he also said that his company would introduce wireless communication and use solar energy to power their systems.  acr is a consortium formed by californian businessmen who visited the east african country recently.  they also plan to establish video-conferencing and video-phone services.

title: hk launches first broadband internet service on itv
body: hongkong telecom ims announced on tuesday that a new internet application will be added to its multimedia interactive tv (itv) services.  the supernetvigator, a broadband internet service for users in hongkong, will offer remarkably enhanced internet access speed and connecting ability via the broadband network.  the service speed is up to 1.5 mbps, 30 times higher than that of a dial-up connection.  hongkong launched in march the world's first itv services with which over 90 percent of local households will be able to see films, listen to music, shop for fun or deal with individual financial affairs with clicks on a few remote control buttons at the comfort of their own homes.  using the pc as the medium, supernetvigator is supported by two existing ims services -itv and a web service, netvigator.  william lo, managing director of hongkong telecom ims, said the company is "committed to developing a dynamic and comprehensive range of multimedia services to enhance the way people live and work." hongkong telecom ims, a cable and wireless company, is the largest internet service provider in hongkong.

title: s. africa rights group urges laws against internet porn
body: the south africa human rights commission (sahrc) has expressed concern about pornography on the internet, saying it will ask parliament to make stricter laws to curb the phenomenon.  sahrc spokesperson anne routier said at the weekend that pornography on the internet had arisen because it appeared that neither current nor coming legislation dealt expressly with distribution of pornographic material through the internet.  the commission was extremely concerned about the abuse and violation of children for pornographic purposes and condemned the use of the internet for such purposes.  given the increased use of the internet as both communications and entertainment channel, and also the relatively easy access to the net for both children and adults, this aspect of the law requires urgent attention," routier said.  earlier, the opposition national party in the country also made complaints about child pornography circulated on the internet.

title: city invites internest bids
body: southwest china's chongqing municipality is offering international companies the opportunity to bid for a number of major projects via the internet.  the projects include construction of a municipal administrative center, a science and technology center, an arts and cultural center, a central square, a conference and exhibition center, an international trade zone and a dock for yachts.  the web site has received hits from some 5,000 companies, with 20 international companies tendering bids.  wang genfang, director of the municipal construction commission, pointed to the encouraging success of the initial offering and noted that the city will use the system to invite international bids in the future.  chongqing became china's fourth municipality in march 1997, following beijing, shanghai and tianjin. the local government is currently extending great effort to transform the city into a regional center in southwest china.

title: enterprises in qidong city linked to internet
body: some 200 enterprises in qidong city, east china's jiangsu province, have been linked to the internet.  new internest users include local state-owned and township-run enterprises, as well as foreign-funded and private ones.  the qidong posts and telecommunications bureau invested three million yuan in september 1997 to provide the internet access to local enterprises. the users now can timely exchange information vis the global network and send email rather than fax messages.  enterprises can also use the internet to publicise recent progress and follow changes on the international market. the internet is more efficient and less costly, according to the manager of a local foreign-funded enterprise.

title: results at at and t challenge tennis tournament
body: following are the results at the at and t challenge tennis tournament at the atlanta athletic club on monday (prefix number denotes seeding): singles first round: dennis van scheppingen, netherlands, bt 4-vincent spadea, unitedstates, 6-3, 4-6, 7-5 john van lottum, netherlands, bt marcello craca, germany, 4-6, 6-3, 6-2 johan van herck, belgium, bt 7-gianluca pozzi, italy, 6-2, 6-4 2-jason stoltenberg, australia, bt luis horna, peru, 6-3, 6-4 davide sanguinetti, italy, bt mark knowles, bahamas, 6-3, 6-2 8-wayne black, zimbabwe, bt jared palmer, unitedstates, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 doubles first round: mark merklein and jack waite, unitedstates, bt chris decker and travis parrott, unitedstates, 6-4, 7-5 qualifying: vincent spadea and greg van emburgh, unitedstates, bt mark keil, puipo beach, unitedstates, and sargis sargisian, armenia, 6-1, 6-3

title: stoltenberg wins in first round of at and t challenge
body: second seeded jason stoltenberg scored a 6-3, 6-4 victory in the first round of the at and t challenge tennis tournament at duluth, georgia, on monday.  stoltenberg broke the serve of peruvian luis horna in the first game of each set, then ralied on his dominating serve on clay.  "i felt like i was in control the whole match, " said stoltenberg, ranked 42nd in the world.  stoltenberg lost only five of 45 service points and finished off the match in 52 minutes.  top seed pete sampras and third-seeded jim courier will play their first matches tuesday night.  sampras will take on alex o'brien on the stadium court, followed by courier against marcio carlsson.

title: china sets up market information system on internet
body: china is set to establish an export information system on internet, introducing the country's famous and fine export products, said an official with the ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation (moftec).  according to zhang daming, deputy-director of office of information leading group of moftec, software designing for the internet information system titled "products made in china" is under construction.  it will be developed as the world's largest export products transaction center by taking advantage of internet, which has so far aroused strong reaction from industrial and commercial enterprises nationwide, said the official.  the move is designed to blaze new trails in an effort to boost the country's import and export trade by fully utilizing the modern information network technology, he added.  the internet information system "products made in china" will involve all the country's prestigious enterprises and their products, which will be available for consultation to all the government institutions, commercial groups and enterprises across the world.

title: yahoo offers new computer service on net
body: yahoo, the leading search engine provider on the internet, has introduced yahoo computers, a new web site providing computer news, forums and shopping. the company said the new site --http://computers.yahoo.com -is designed to combine much of the computer-related content that already appears on different yahoo sites, with additional new services into a single area. the site includes news that is updated daily and many frequently asked questions by computer users. questions and answers include such as "relocating the taskbar (on windows-95)," "placing a drive icon on the desktop," and "how can i set up windows to start up without asking for a password." separately, yahoo also reached an agreement tuesday for onsale to become its main auction content provider. onsale sells a variety of merchandise, from computer electronics to specialty foods, through auctions conducted over the internet.

title: shanghai people finding jobs through internet
body: finding a job on the internet is becoming increasingly popular in shanghai, china's largest trade and financial city, with 200,000 people having visited the city's first job-finding web site: www.shrc.online.sh.cn. about 5,000 internet surfers reportedly have listed their resumes on the web site, which contains detailed information about 4,500 jobs. nearly 70 percent of the job-seekers can get feedback from possible employers. and the network, which has nearly 100 computers at separate locations around the city, has taken a 20-percent share of the local human resources market.

title: macao posts transition, return to motherland data on internet
body: the macao government has posted a new homepage on the internet to provide viewers data concerning macao's transition and return to the motherland. internet surfers can find the portuguese homepage at http://1999.macau.gov.mo, which is also part of the official page of macao government at the world wide web. the homepage includes the full text of the sino-portuguese joint declaration on the question of macao, the basic law of the macao special administrative region and 99 questions and answers concerning macao's transition. the chinese and english versions of the macao basic law were put into the internet in 1996.

title: chinese brand-name products connecting via internet
body: the jiangsu brand-name product network in east china's jiangsu province got connected to the internet on wednesday.  this will give more than 74 million internet users around the globe access to a brand-name product inquiry line of 425 companies in the province.  the network will provide a range of information about the products and photos of products and of production facilities.  a provincial economic information center also plans to set up a website on the internet to help foreign users learn more about the brands names. it also has an email address that allows companies to hook up to the network free of charge to get in touch with customers.

title: internet stocks rising to dizzying high
body: investors continued to pile onto the internet bandwagon today, powering stocks to new highs as yahoo showed the sector can be profitable.  yahoo inc, the famous search engine maker on the internet, has been chased by buyers over the past few weeks and its stock price has been pushed as high as 119 unitedstates dollars at the opening today.  it retreated a bit as the broad market dipped at profit taking after the dow jones industrial average set new highs over the past two sessions on end.  on wednesday, the american stock exchange of internet stocks was up 2.5 percent as the sector sprinted ahead of the broader market.  some analysts believed that as compaq and other computer hardware companies missed earnings estimates, a lot of institutional money were turned into internet stocks.  yahoo's stock price was just a bit more than 20 unitedstates dollars last june and it jumped to 60 dollars by the end of the year.  talk of a stock split at yahoo also is fueling the share price, said analysts, who cautioned that the dizzying rise makes internet stocks vulnerable to a sharp pullback.

title: shanghai gets internet stock trading service
body: a chinese stock trader now can do trading in a-shares on the shanghai stock exchange in just seconds if he or she has access to the internet, no matter where he or she is.  starting on wednesday, an electronic trading system developed by the shanghai branch of the communications bank, minfa securities co., and shanghai information port provided automatic transfer services from bank accounts to the exchange through the internet shanghai hotline.  any internet user who wants to buy or sell a-shares (reserved for domestic traders only) can do so by getting a pacific credit card at communications bank and a minfa securities account there or at minfa offices.  minfa officials say they can guarantee the confidentiality and security of the trading because of a code-word system.  the system also provides instant access to stock quotes and information every eight seconds.

title: beijing establishes public information platform
body: beijing plans to significantly upgrade its information technology industry, according to the government office in charge related work.  the chinese capital has already established a public information platform which links various networks from domestic institutions and provides internet access, according to hu zhaoguang, president of the capital information technology development corporation.  the expanded platform will link the capital's telecommunications, personal computer and cable television networks.  the corporation will create virtual reality platform for electronic business and cyberspace entertainment.  in addition, the information platform offers a window to beijing and will allow net surfers to learn more about the city, according to local officials.  in a related development, a us-based information technology company signed a cooperative agreement today to support the program.

title: fujian plans 10 billion yuan investment in information industry
body: east china's fujian province plans to allocate ten billion yuan during 1998 to expand development of its information industry.  funds will primarily be used to launch a digital data network and expand internet services.  other projects will include the development of a wide-band multimedia digital telecommunications net and wide-band business platforms.  fujian has extended great effort in recent years to promote development of the information industry.  the province took the lead in optical fiber networking in 1986 and has since established a 16,000-km network.  fujian also established a public multimedia information network and established links with the state net in 1997.

title: china opens women's page on internet
body: the institute of women's studies of the all-china women's federation has launched a women's page on the internet, according to today's overseas edition of people's daily. the web site features data for and about chinese women and offers information on laws and regulations on women, key documents concerning women's movements both at home and abroad, organizations and experts on women, and an electronic magazine on women. the paper said that 20 more databases will be opened at the web site (http://www.cwomen.ac.cn) by the end of this year.

title: bank of china providing on-line services
body: china's foreign exchange bank, the bank of china (boc), will gradually provide on-line electronic banking services and is expected to have them for its branches in major cities this year.  li yongjia, the deputy-general manager of boc's information technology office, told a press conference here today that it has successfully completed a pilot operation in its beijing, shanghai, tianjin, guangzhou, and qingdao branches and this has laid a solid foundation for electronic banking.  people in these cities can do business at any boc branch bank or in an atm machine. foreigners can also have access to international networks.  the new electronic services come courtesy of canada's slm software inc., which announced today that it will soon open a beijing office to provide full support for the system.  boc is the 15th largest bank in the world. two weeks ago, china's first on-line transaction was done through the boc network.

title: information program for africa starts in nigeria
body: the information networking program for africa, midwived by the united nations industrial development organization (unido), has kicked off with the successful installation of an internet system in nigeria.  nigeria, the daily times reported thursday, is one of the five countries chosen in africa by unido as national focal points for the acquisition, processing, packaging and delivery of industrial and technology information to users in and outside the continent.  unido is carrying out the program in the country in collaboration with the manufacturers association of nigeria (man) and the federal ministry of industry.  in a statement, man director-general uzor okeke disclosed the program, known as "information networking for technology investment and business", would be used as a means of reaching out to the outside world markets by subscribers to the internet system.

title: tianjin sees increasing number of internet users
body: the number of internet users has been growing rapidly in the northern chinese port city of tianjin.  according to the municipal scientific and technology commission, the number of internet users was up to 10,000 last year, and has kept growing by more than 1,000 a month since the beginning of this year.  the municipal data telecommunications bureau spent 30 million yuan last year in expanding its capacity for internet users.  most institutional internet users are in foreign trade enterprises, joint ventures, and some large state-owned enterprises, and most individual internet users are adults involved in scientific research, education, or the computer industry, or middle school and college students.

title: uk pm denies helping murdoch win mediaset bid
body: british prime minister tony blair on tuesday denied reports he had approached italian prime minister romano prodi in an attempt to help the news corp boss rupert murdoch break into italian television.  the reports said blair secretly contacted prodi last week to support murdoch's bid to gain control of mediaset,the media company controlled by silvio berlusconi, italy's former prime minister.  blair's official spokesman told a regular briefing the claims blair had helped murdoch in the business were "a complete joke".  the spokesman said prodi's conversation through phone calls with blair was part of their regular contact during britain's presidency of the european union.  "this was not a conversation about rupert murdoch," he added.  talks on the television deal collapsed last friday after berlusconi rejected a 5.8 trillion lire (3.2 billion unitedstates dollars) offer to buy his stake.

title: more canadians use internet
body: more canadian families went onto the information highway last year, especially for those with higher incomes, said reports friday.  the proportion using the internet from home "almost doubled" to 13 percent of canadian households between 1996 and 1997, according to the latest figures from statistics canada.  use of the internet among families whose incomes were in the top fifth of all households soared to 26 percent, up from 16.5 percent.  though families with incomes in the bottom fifth were slow to be plugged into the internet, their use of the technology from their homes actually increased faster, more than doubling to 5.3 percent.  the statistics agency also noted that families with children are more likely to possess a computer.  last year, one half of canadian families with children under 18 had a computer.  a 1994 survey found that 81 percent of young people aged 15 to 24 were able to use a computer, the highest rate for any age group.  in contrast, only one in 10 "elderly" canadians knew how to operate a computer.

title: microsoft teams up with bt for trial of webtv
body: microsoft, the american computer giant, and british telecom linked up for the first time by announcing the start of a trial of webtv product in the unitedkingdom.  the trial, due to start at the end of this month, will involve several hundred bt customers, who will be furnished with a set-top box and a connection to bt internet, allowing them access to the internet from their televisions.  webtv networks, the microsoft subsidiary which specializes in providing internet over the television, will provide core technology and platform management.  the set-top box will be provided by pace micro technology and philips electronics.  because the set-top boxes only cost a few hundred unitedstates dollars, the webtv system, which allows users to watch tv while surfing the internet at the same time, has proved popular in the unitedstates and japan.

title: nortel buys into internet market
body: canda's telecommunications giant northern telecom ltd. (nortel) has agreed to buy a startup unitedstates internet equipment maker for 290 million unitedstates dollars, said reports thursday.  the massachusetts-based aptis communications inc. has no revenue but could push nortel ahead in the race down the information highway, analysts said.  "this deal is a home run," said glenn falcao, nortel's general manager of public data networks.  "if we had waited until the company had revenue, i couldn't have afforded it," he was quoted as saying.  the move pushes nortel ahead of such competitors as lucent technologies inc., which have alliances with access equipment makers that focused on seeling to companies.  the purchase is the second major acquisition in the past four and half months for nortel's data networks division. in november, it bought broadband networks inc. for 586 million dollars.  nortel has been looking for ways to improve its portfolio of products that move data on to the internet.

title: tianjin opens public internet service
body: tianjin, north china's biggest port city, has opened its first public internet service, which is expected to expand the use of the high-tech communication by ordinary residents.  the internet service, provided by a post office in tianjin university, involves sending and receiving electronic mail, file transactions and remote access service. the internet was introduced to china in april of 1994. a month later, a domestic system was opened, providing four categories of service, including science and technology, education and communication.

title: s'pore internet providers required to offer porno filter
body: singapore's internet service providers will be required by law to offer parents a way of weeding out on-line pornography by the end of this year, information and the arts minister george yeo said on monday.  speaking in parliament, the minister said that the internet service providers would, according to the law, install a filter in their servers to block access to undesirable sites.  "all internet service providers will be required by regulation to provide parents with the option," he said.  the "cleaner, more sanitized" internet service will be built in at the server level, he stressed, citing cyber patrol and nanny net as examples of such filtering programs. the minister noted that children were now knowledgeable about gaining access even to blocked sites.  the singapore broadcasting authority (sba) has banned some 100 websites that promote pornography, violence, and racial or religious hatred.

title: china telecom to develop internet browser
body: china's largest public telecommunications provider, china telecom, has signed an agreement with microsoft corp. to jointly develop a special internet browser. china telecom expects the browser to consolidate its leading position in the country's internet market.  the launching of the "internet explorer china" project marks the beginning of a long-term cooperative program between microsoft and china's ministry of post and telecommunications (mpt), which runs china telecom, said leng rongquan, deputy director in charge of the department of telecommunications of the mpt.  subscribers to the internet through china telecom will receive "ie china" free to encourage use of the company's public multimedia telecom service.  neither china telecom nor microsoft revealed financial terms.  according to the long-term agreement, china telecom will also use microsoft platforms and other technology in information system applications. microsoft will be involved in the training for online skills.  statistics from the mpt show china had 620,000 subscribers to the internet at the end of 1997.

title: u.s. firm sees it market growth in china
body: a leading unitedstates information technology media company predicted that china's it market may reach 21.5 billion unitedstates dollars by 2002 from 7.3 billion dollars in 1997.  in its recent forecast the boston-based international data group (idg) set the 1997-2001 compound annual growth rate of internet users in china at 73 percent, idg said in a press release on monday.  idg sees an increase of its presence in the asia pacific region with the recent launch of the monthly magazine internetworld in china.  the publication informs an audience of 50,000 readers about new trends and technologies in the networking market, industry events, and the effects of the internet on chinese economics and society.

title: u.s. firm sees it market growth in china
body: a leading unitedstates information technology media company predicted that china's it market may reach 21.5 billion unitedstates dollars by 2002 from 7.3 billion dollars in 1997.  in its recent forecast the boston-based international data group (idg) set the 1997-2001 compound annual growth rate of internet users in china at 73 percent, idg said in a press release on monday.  idg sees an increase of its presence in the asia pacific region with the recent launch of the monthly magazine internetworld in china.  the publication informs an audience of 50,000 readers about new trends and technologies in the networking market, industry events, and the effects of the internet on chinese economics and society.

title: chinese oceanic information network operational
body: the chinese oceanic information network has become operational recently with a chinese and english web site on the internet, according to the state oceanic administration.  browsers can access the network by visiting the web site at nmdis.go.cn on the internet. the network provides an information search, browsing through data, and other services. it also can offer on-line date transmission for oceanic information systems.  chinese oceanic departments and industries can take advantage of the network to make them known to the rest of the world, using multi-media technology. they can also exchange information and discuss marine scientific problems with their foreign counterparts through the net.

title: clinton endorses shield for internet taxes
body: unitedstates president bill clinton thursday said thursday in san francisco that the internet should be shielded from any tax, at least for five years.  he called for the passage of the internet tax act, which would put up to a five-year moratorium on new local, state or federal taxes on electronic commerce and the internet.  "there should be no special rates for the internet, but we can't allow unfair taxation to weigh it down and stunt the development of the most promising new economic opportunity in decades," clinton told a high-tech conference.  some unitedstates governors expressed their concern that untaxed sales over the internet will drain money from their budgets as consumers shift purchases away from stores.  clinton said that during the moratorium, a bipartisan commission would work with states to help devise a tax strategy for dealing in the future with online transactions, which will not drain money from states while allowing "the internet to flourish."

title: internet costs to be reduced in argentina
body: argentina's ministry of communications has announced a 75 percent reduction in telephone charges related to the use of the internet in libraries, schools and public universities.  the discount will be accessible by dialing the 0610 prefix beginning in mid march, said alejandro garro, director of the internet commission of the ministry.  he said that with the implementation of prefix dialing, the number of internet users is expected to increase from 50,000 to 200,000 in the coming months.  the prefix will allow telephone companies to provide internet communication calls with the appropriate discounts and isolate and identify them from normal calls.

title: internet hurts family life: survey
body: half of canadians know someone who spends so much time surfing the internet or playing computer games that it hurts their family life, according to a survey published monday.  "there is a resonance among many canadians that the internet is helping to create new, virtual communities, and has the potential to improve family life," the survey said.  "but there are also others who see it as impersonal, dehumanizing and a distraction," it noted.  forty-nine percent of those surveyed said they know people who spend so much time at home using the internet and other computer activities that it is having a negative impact on their family life.  in the meantime, some 30 percent of those surveyed said they strongly disagree with the notion that internet has had a negative impact on the quality of people's family life.  the survey, done by ekos research associates inc., interviewed 3,522 canadians, according to the globe and mail newspaper.

title: chinese tea museum gets its own website
body: internet users can visit the china tea museum thousands of kilometers away without leaving home, museum staff say.  the museum in this capital of east china's zhejiang province, got its own website in an experiment in three-dimensional virtual reality, that provides a general introduction to the museum and exhibits, the history of tea, tea sets, teahouse displays, and anecdotes about tea.  many people have visited the museum via the website, according to the staff.  museum authorities also plan to make some of their most valuable tea sets, which have not been seen by visitors before, available to internet enthusiasts.

title: german government opens internet homepage for young people
body: the german government announced thursday that it has opened a special internet homepage, called the "youngnet", to offer convenient information services to young people between 16 and 26 years old.  according to german government spokesman peter hausmann, the youngnet will serve as a user-friendly platform to gather and provide useful information available on the internet for the young people.  programs offered by the youngnet include job introduction, education, science, political information and entertainment. it would also allow young people to participate in on-line discussion forums, to chat with prominent figures or to make use of the email-service to send post worldwide free of charge.  "under the framework of the youngnet, we are offering the positive side of the internet in all aspects," said hausmann.  the youngnet also has a young editorial group which knows the special interests of young people and would ensure a better communication with them.  according to hausmann, the german government has invested 500,000 marks (about 275,000 unitedstates dollars) on the project.

title: german government opens internet homepage for young people
body: the german government said thursday it has opened a special internet homepage, called the "youngnet," for attract young people aged between 16 and 26 years.  german government spokesman peter hausmann said the youngnet will serve as a user-friendly platform to gather and provide useful information available on the internet for the young people.  programs offered by the youngnet include job introduction, education, science, political information and entertainment.  it would also allow young people to participate in on-line discussion forums, to chat with prominent figures or to make use of the its electronic mail service free of charge.  "under the framework of the youngnet, we are offering the positive side of the internet in all aspects," said hausmann.  behind the youngnet is a young editorial group which knows the special interests of people in their age group and would ensure a better communication with them.  according to hausmann, the german government has invested 500,000 marks (about 275,000 unitedstates dollars) on the project.

title: hackers attack israeli parliament's website
body: the internet site of israeli knesset (parliament) has been invaded by unknown hackers, local english daily the jerusalem post reported wednesday. this occurred on tuesday when the hackers, claiming to be a group called israel internet underground (iiu), invaded the website and left a note in poor and badly spelled english, the report said. the note said the group hacked the site without "evil goals" and made some changes to prevent future security problems. "iiu hacked this page to prevent future security problems, we did it for no evil goals and some of this pages might be changed just cause few reasons one of them is the credits of course," the note reads. it added that the group made backup to the original homepage in order to avoid real damage to it. they also claimed having found and blocked 19 holes in the system, which led to their invasion. among the changes made to the site (http://www.knesset.gov.il) was the additional comment under the picture of president ezer weizman: "the best president we ever had." the report added that the knesset is launching an investigation into the incident.

title: internet bringing chinese mainland books to taiwan
body: china's first bookstore on the internet now allows many taiwanese to get a look at some mainland titles for the first time.  authorities on taiwan have banned the sale of mainland books in bookstores on the island, but the china modern bookstore, which was established on the internet last august, provides services around the world, and taiwanese can order mainland books over the email.  so far, some 25 percent of orders are coming from taiwan, according to the china publishing industry trading corporation, the sponsor of the bookstore.  "this is a new means for people across the straits to increase exchanges and contacts," says sun ou, a company staff member.  the bookstore's web site has been visited by people from 95 countries and regions, sources say.

title: 6.3 million households online in europe: survey
body: there are now 6.3 million households in europe subscribing to online services, said a new survey from the uk company datamonitor.  germany, the uk and netherlands are the largest internet markets in europe, with more than four million online households between them, according to the survey.  the netherlands saw the fastest increase in residential users between 1996 and 1997, where the number of users increaseed from 144,000 to 510,000.  surprisingly, the report showed that smaller isps (internet service providers) have more market shares in western europe than the big name online services, such as aol or msn.  small isps, which are usually cheaper, now provide 56 percent of the online connections in western europe, the report said.

title: child porn grows on internet: professor
body: the number of internet sites devoted to pornography and child porn is growing despite laws intended to limit them, said a report today.  in addition, the success of the online porn industry, virtually the only web sites that make money, is driving the development of technology as consumers demand better monitors and faster internet access speeds.  "it's quite clear that the number of adult-oriented web sites is growing," dr. michael mehta, professor of canada's queen's university, was quoted as saying.  there are perhaps 250,000 adult-oriented web sites, which constitute less than 2 percent of the total number of web sites, said the professor, who is researching the issue.  the current laws appear adequate and new laws won't help, he said in an interview with the globe and mail newspaper.  the internet industry needs to develop voluntary initiatives and extend the use of filtering software, the professor said.

title: french scientist offers tips for efficient internet use
body: director of cite des sciences of france joel de rosnay offered here today his suggestions to help those who are stuck, lost, or spend too much time in their search for information on the internet. at a session on the internet of the annual meeting of the world economic forum, de rosnay gave the following suggestions: 1. europeans should use the internet in the morning so far as possible, before the 49 million us "internauts" have connected; 2. use fast modems, 28.8kbs or above. the investment is well worth the time saved; 3. de-activate graphics for faster downloads. this can usually be done through the "options" on the menu bar of web browsers; 4. the most important tip and the clever way to use the internet is to open several web pages at a time, rather than waiting for each successive page to download. while one page is loading, go to another. if the modem is a 28.8kbs, up to 14 pages can be downloaded at once at full speed. finally he advised: stick to an "information diet." "limit your time, as you limit your lunch, so you are not swamped with information." de rosnay's homepage is www.cite-sciences.fr/derosnay.

title: south china region opens information network
body: the guangxi hot line, a new multimedia telecommunication network which entered operations today in south china's guangxi zhuang autonomous region, signals further progress in efforts to establish the guangxi information highway.  the network, which is based on internet technology, will offer reliable written, audio and graphic information on wide-ranging subjects, including stock exchanges, travel and education, according to an official from the guangxi posts and telecommunications bureau.  the computer network links all areas in guangxi and provides local residents with convenient worldwide access, according to the official.  the overall project, completed at a cost of three billion yuan, included expansion of the long-distance transmission capacity and a complete upgrade of technical standards for the entire network.  guangxi's transmission lines stretch 18,000 km, and the region has installed a fiber optic transmission network linking all provincial cities and 95 percent of local counties.

title: siemens, 3com cooperate to integrate telephone with internet
body: germany's siemens ag announced wednesday that it is working together with the unitedstates 3com corporation to launch in spring this year a new technology to integrate telephone with the internet.  siemens said that the new technology, which incorporates 3com's remote data access technology with the ewsd digital switching system of siemens, would allow telephone network operators to offer their customers efficient internet access via existing telephone switching systems without needing to set up additional new internet infrastructures.  meanwhile, combined with the new technology, siemens is also developing new internet services which would make it possible for customers who are surfing the internet to identify incoming telephone calls or to display their telephone account on their pc screens.  siemens said that it expected about 300 million german marks (about 160 million unitedstates dollars) in extra sales from this product innovation by the year 2000.

title: bbc world service goes on internet
body: bbc world service in english is now available in audio on the internet following a deal with the unitedstates internet company audionet, the bbc announced today in a statement. internet users all over the world can now tune in to bbc world service round the clock every day via the website www.bbc.co.uk/worldservice or www.audionet.com/bbc, the statement said. caroline thomson, deputy managing director of bbc world service, said that bbc world service sees online as an increasingly important way of reaching listeners alongside shortwave, fm and am. the deal with audionet is part of the self-help strategy to offset delivery costs, thomson said. bbc world service now broadcasts in english and 43 other languages to over 140 million listeners around the world. the audience in english is estimated at 35 million.

title: internet use is booming
body: internet users were estimated to number 99.96 million at the end of 1997 and the number is growing, according to a unitedstates industry publication.  the california-based computer industry almanac inc., which publishes the internet industry almanac, said in a press release monday that the unitedstates leads the world in internet use, having 54.68 million users and a 54.70 percent share of the world internet market at the end of 1997.  but as more and more people enjoyed the benefits brought to them by the new technology, smaller industrialized countries with the largest number of internet users were expected to be replaced by the most populous countries such as china and russia.  the almanac, to be released in february, predicts that the unitedstates share of world internet market will dip to 40 percent by the end of 2000 as more and more countries adopt internet technology.  the unitedstates share was about 80 percent in 1981 and 65 percent in 1994.  other countries with more than one million internet users are japan, britain, canada, germany, australia, the netherlands, sweden, finland and france.

title: wide-scale internet services soon in kuwait
body: internet services would be available in kuwait on a wide scale in three months, kuwaiti minister of electricity, water and communications jassem al-oun said today.  al-oun was quoted by kuwait news agency as saying that 54 companies had been tentatively chosen to provide the services in a bid to promote scientific and cultural awareness among the people. there are only two internet companies operating in the gulf state now.  kuwait was the first country in the gulf to provide internet services to its people. thousands of computers in governmental institutions, companies, education and scientific bodies are enjoying the modern information services.  internet has been developing quickly in kuwait and more and more people are getting familiar with its services and expect to use it for deferent purposes.  al-oun noted that the authorities would censor the internet services for security purpose and to preserve national customs and ethics.  the companies would be compelled to install certain systems to prevent the clients from having access to unwanted web sites, he said.

title: leading chinese bank on internet
body: the industrial and commercial bank of china (icbc), one of the largest state-owned commercial banks in the nation, has announced it will join the internet on saturday.  internet subscribers around the world will be able to surf the world wide web and check icbc's web page featuring a detailed introduction to the bank which includes information related to its institutional organization, range of services, and important financial news information.  the web page will also provide detailed information concerning the bank's integrated circuit (ic) card and international business operations.  icbc, which has total assets of some three trillion yuan and is one of china's major banking institutions, has electronic links with some 35,000 operational outlets throughout china. the capability enables the bank to electronically transfer funds nationwide on a 24 hour basis.

title: u.s. computer companies to restrict release of personal data
body: unitedstates 14 largest computer data companies have reached an agreement over blocking public access to certain types of personal data.  signing the agreement are lexis-nexis and the nation's three main credit reporting bureaus, which represent 90 percent of the database market.  according to the agreement, the 14 companies will not release to the general public certain types of non-public information, including social security numbers, birth dates, credit history and a mother's maiden name. the companies also agree not to release unlisted telephone numbers obtained from non-public records and unlisted addresses from telephone companies.  however the restrictions would not apply to sensitive information that is derived from public records, such as birth certificates or state motor vehicle information. qualified subscribers, such as law enforcement agencies and private investigators, would still have access to all data.  "this is an important first step toward ensuring the privacy of users, while keeping government intrusion at a minimum,"said rep. billy tauzin, chairman of the house telecommunications,trade and consumer protection subcommittee.

title: china puts teen-agers' drawings on internet
body: china is placing an exhibition of teen-agers' paintings named "lovely motherland" on the internet for the first time.  about 600 teen-agers' paintings, processed by computers and transmitted by modern technology, have been contributed from all over the world.  the exhibition --jointly sponsored by the jiangsu provincial education commission, and the science and technology commission -is the biggest of its kind in recent years. the original paintings will be put on display next month in the nanjing museum.  the 600 paintings were selected from works submitted by more than 20,000 youngsters studying in 500 elementary and secondary schools in 13 cities in east china's jiangsu province.  the paintings include watercolors, crayon drawings, sketches, wood engravings and papercuts.  zhen qi, a well-known chinese painter, said: "the standard of this show is very high. some paintings are imaginative and have good artistic taste."

title: beijing residents gain internet access
body: the number of internet users in beijing, the chinese capital, has grown dramatically to more than 100,000 over the past three years.  "beijing residents are equally enthusiastic about gaining access to the internet as they were installing residential telephones years ago," according to an article in today's beijing daily.  the actual number of internet users is most likely somewhat larger since several people often share one internet account.  this year alone, chinanet, which is managed by the beijing telegraph bureau, has enrolled 2,300 new users. chinanet offers preferential services such as reduced rate to renowned scientists, including over 400 academicians with the chinese academy of sciences and the chinese academy of engineering.  universities, research institutes, banking and financial institutions and trade corporations account a large majority of the users, with a constant increase in the number of individuals joining the network.  individuals account for over half of the chinanet users and an ever increasing number of business people are learning to use the internet to promote their business, according to the article.

title: s. african companies become victims of web racket
body: some "pirate" operators have been deliberately registering the names of south african companies on the internet and then demanding money from them if they want to use their own names on a web site, local press reported today.  since this is reaching alarming proportions, companies are urged to register their domain names even if they are not considering a web address in the foreseeable future, according to the sunday tribune newspaper.  "the disturbing fact is that because the amounts the pirates charge companies to hand over their domain names are not that high, usually no more than 5,000 or 6,000 rand (1,040 or 1,250 unitedstates dollars), so most companies simply pay up rather than take the more costly litigation route," said douglas reed, a computer company executive.  but the ransom money could be very high, reed warned.  a domain name registration costs only 200 rand (a little more than 40 dollars). therefore, even companies not planning a web site could find registration good insurance for their brands.

title: sri lanka sets up web site to promote national image
body: the sri lankan foreign ministry, in collaboration with the university of colombo, has set up a new site on the world wide web (www) in a bid to promote the national image of the country.  viewer, while browsing the site --sri lanka web window, can get general information about government, history, the peace process, the economy, education, travel, culture and sports, local press reports said today.  several government departments, including the defense ministry, also use the site to release news bulletins and up-to-date situation reports on the battlefield in the north of the country.  in addition to the english version, the site also provides parallel translations in sinhala, tamil, french and german, the reports said.

title: hewlett-packard leads global consortium on internet
body: hewlett-packard co., one of the unitedstates biggest computer makers, is launching a global consortium with major financial companies to establish electronic banking and commerce on internet, the company reported today.  the move, which was called the first global commerce initiative, will open electronic commerce's doors for more traditional merchants and counter an aggressive drive into the electronic commerce arena by international business machines corp., which has launched an advertising campaign aimed at attracting businesses into its camp, analysts said.  the consortium includes electronic data systems corp. of dallas, hewlett-packard and its verifone commerce unit, the royal bank of canada, sumitomo credit of japan and the banking of major card vendors such as visa international and mondex, the report said.  according to a survey company, business over the internet will soar to more than 220 billion unitedstates dollars by the year 2001, over 20 times more than its forecast for 1997.

title: laws of hk launched on the internet
body: the statutory laws of the hongkong special administrative region (sar) of china and a selection of constitutional documents are now available to anyone who has access to the internet, a government official said today.  this facility launched by the department of justice would greatly help to promote public knowledge of these laws, secretary for justice elsie leung said.  with the launch of the new system, the laws of hongkong for the first time will be readily accessible to the public, to the legal profession in hongkong and to interested persons and organizations around the world.  government staff who administer the various laws in their daily work will also benefit from having access to up-to-date laws.  with wider public understanding of the laws that apply to them in their everyday life, there should be greater awareness of and support for the rule of law, leung said.  the laws of hongkong on the internet are being made available in both english and chinese, without charge. an english/chinese glossary of terms used in the laws will also be available soon.

title: u.s. summit to discuss ways to keep children away from internet sex and violence
body: unitedstates government officials and heads of interested groups and companies will hold a summit meeting next week to discuss ways to shield children from sex and violence on the internet.  vice president al gore, attorney general janet reno and two cabinet secretaries will participate in the three-day meetings beginning monday to explore technological and legal avenues for keeping kids away from pornographic and violent content on internet sites.  in july, unitedstates president bill clinton organized a meeting at the white house to find new solutions and warned the private sector to act fast or face new legislation.

title: eu adopts proposal for safe use of internet
body: the european commission, the european union (eu)'s executive body, today adopted a proposal for an action plan on promoting the safe use of the internet.  the plan, covering the years from 1998 to 2001, identifies the main areas where the commission believes concrete measures are needed and could be supported by the eu, says a press release issued here wednesday.  under the plan, a european network of centers, known as hot lines, will be created to allow users to report content which they come across during their use of the internet and which they consider to be illegal.  the plan points out that self regulation and content-monitoring schemes should be developed by access providers, content providers and network operators.  the plan urges for internationally compatible rating and filtering schemes to be used to protect users, especially children against "undesirable" content.  it envisages measures to increase awareness of the possibilities available among parents, teachers, children and other consumers and help them choose the "appropriate" content while surfing the internet.

title: first internet service provider in inner mongolia
body: the first internet service provider in northern china's inner mongolia autonomous region opened today in hohhot, the regional capital.  the inner mongolia haixun information and network technology development co. ltd. will provide various services to local internet subscribers, including linking computers to the system, gathering information on the global network, establishing data platforms, developing network software and training users.  "the internet will enable people throughout the world to learn more about inner mongolia, and vice versa," according to general manager nian yi.  he noted that few people or enterprises in the region currently have access to the internet.

title: indian schoolkids to work with foreign students on internet
body: students from five indian schools will work with their counterparts in canada, belgium, japan, the unitedstates, britain and other countries to build their own web sites through virtual classroom programs on the internet.  according to local press reports today, the students will collaborate over the next five months in planning, designing and building web sites on projects like the generation gap, children's lifestyles in varying cultures, world peace and harmony, and wildlife.  the programs also include online training and tutorials, and in some cases, computer-based video conferences.

title: un agency to hold seminar on role of internet, racism
body: a united nations agency will hold a seminar on the role of the internet and racism here in geneva next week, according to a press release of the united nations office at geneva (unog) today.  the seminar on november 10-14, organized as part of the implementation of the program of action for the third decade to combat racism and racial discrimination, will look at the extent of racism on the internet, technical aspects of screening racist propaganda and the possibilities for a code of conduct and good practice for displaying material on the internet.  ralph zacklin, acting deputy to the united nations high commissioner for human rights (unhchr), the organizer of the seminar, will deliver the welcome address at the opening session.  a statement, entitled conclusions and recommendations, will be made at the end of the seminar.

title: about half million s. africans use internet
body: nearly half a million south africans are using the internet and most internet service providers are growing their customer base by 10 percent a month, according to a survey.  there is a minimum estimate of about 450,000 internet users in south africa, the 1997 south african internet services industry survey compiled with the cooperation of all the major south african service providers said.  the survey divided the internet market into three categories: dial-up users accessing the internet via modems, corporate users gaining access through company networks, and academic users gaining access at schools and tertiary educational institutions.  a total of 154,276 south africans are using dial-up modems via service providers. there is an estimated 200,000 corporate users and potentially 500,000, but not less than 100,000, users in educational sector, the survey showed.

title: eu to further develop mobile communications
body: the european union (eu) adopted a proposal today aimed at creating a favorable environment for further development of mobile communications in europe.  the proposal, put forward by eu commissioner martin bangemann, who is responsible for technology and telecommunications, will allow mobile users wireless access to the internet and other multi-media services.

title: web sites don't boost sales: survey
body: few north american retailers are making money from their internet investments, according to a new study published today.  north american retailers are pouring an average of roughly 20,000 unitedstates dollars into setting up their web sites, but they expect little payoff in the way of increased sales.  "until the typical middle-aged consumer feels comfortable with this burgeoning technology, adoption rates in most retail categories will remain low and various retail applications will be restricted," the study said.  "like many technological innovations, it may take a generation for internet shopping to attain mainstream status," it added.  however, retailers who ignore the internet do so at their own peril, warned the study, which was done by the toronto-based polytechnic university's center for the study of commercial activity.  by 2005, large chunks of some retail sectors will have to set up shop on the internet, according to prof. ken jones, who co-authored the study.  but a big stumbling block is money, he said. the cost of experiments and the uncertainties of adoption have created many barriers to entry.

title: software to translate internet documents
body: chinese scientists have developed a computer software system to automatically translate internet files into the chinese language.  the software has the capacity to translate 150,000 characters per hour, with some 80 percent of the total content easily understandable after the translation process.  the major problem hindering the development of the internet in china centers on the language barrier. many chinese users point to the fact that their english is inadequate for operating the internet which is predominantly in english.  development of a translation software is part of a high-tech program introduced by the state science and technology commission in the mid-1980s.  the software, which was jointly developed by a research institute and a university in southwest china's sichuan province, runs in the windows environment. users can use a mouse to achieve instant translations, while maintaining the original format of documents or pictures.

title: xiamen trade fair connected to internet
body: the chinese people now have internet access to information about the china investment and trade fair, which opened today in the chinese coastal city of xiamen.  the fair, which is held on september 8 every year, went on-line sunday, and the data is available on terminals and private computers connected to internet.  the information includes a general description of the fair, invitations for investment, and a brief introduction of xiamen and fujian province where xiamen is. people can book hotel rooms and find out where meetings are being held via the internet.  similar services were offered at last year's fair, but this year's offerings cover a larger geographic area and the network's capacity has been expanded.  this year, the fair was promoted to national status from its former position as a regional business event.

title: number of brazilian internet users soars
body: brazil has surpassed russia and some asian countries and regions to rank 19th in internet users in just two years, a high-ranking official said here today.  speaking at a meeting on software, ivan moura campos from the science and technology ministry, said brazil now has 1.1 million people linked to the world wide web in 110 hosts.  from december of 1995 to july of 1997, the number of hosts in brazil grew by 536 percent, while that of commercial computers connected to the internet increased by 1,792 percent.  during the same period, more than 1,000 suppliers of access to internet and up to 5,000 web information suppliers were installed.

title: live internet coverage for chinese bridge event
body: the china cup international bridge event will be broadcasted live through the internet, the first time in the world for the sport, organizers said here on monday. anybody who has the access to the world wide web in any part of the world can closely follow the actions in the team competitions through the web site www.cpisn.cn.net. the team competition will take place in the first three days of the the september 1-9 event. the rest is individual tourney. organizers said the event has attracted some international bridge stars, which include world number one player lynn deas. live internet coverage for sports events is not rare. the chess match between russian gary kasparov and the ibm supercomputer "deep blue" had been broadcasted live on an ibm web site last may, drawing millions of fans worldwide.

title: germany lags behind in internet race: german hp chief
body: germans have tend to be too suspicious of the commercial development of the internet computer network, thus falling far behind in its commercial use, the german subsidiary of the unitedstates computer giant hewlett-packard (hp) said today.  while german companies were generally interested in the potential of the internet as a business tool, they've been relatively slow to adopt it, said joerg menno harms, head of the hp's german subsidiary, in an interview with the german news agency dpa.  currently in europe, britain and the scandinavian countries have the highest rate of internet use per capita, said harms, adding that this will probably not change within the next few years.  but european countries in general are still lagging far behind in the use of internet in comparison with the unitedstates, he noted.  according to his estimates, european commerical transactions over the internet will reach about 7 billion unitedstates dollars annually by the year of 2000. while two thirds of that volume would come from britain and scandinavia, germany will have a relatively modest share of about 10 percent, he predicted.

title: chaozhou information network
body: chaozhou, in south china's guangdong province, has opened its first information network linked to internet.  the network, which is also linked to the china economic information network, is expected to speed up modernization of the local information industry and will provide chaozhou with access to the worldwide information superhighway.  the network offers users access to a wide variety of timely domestic and international information, as well as convenient exchange mechanisms such as email.  the city is promoting the new network by offering free registration.

title: asia-pacific strives to expand internet capacity
body: malaysia, mongolia, nepal and papua new guinea would be the first countries to benefit from the united nations development program (undp)'s new asia-pacific development information program, which aims to expand information technology and internet access and presence in the region, said a report released by undp today.  the report said the program, introduced in the annual conference of the internet society in kuala lampur, focused on linking undp partners to the internet, including governments, non-government organizations, the private sector and academic institutes.  the goal was to help all major development partners get on-line, and to promote the use of the internet in designing innovative programs in areas such as poverty alleviation, environmental protection, disaster management, education and telemedicine, said the report.

title: hong kong sets up homepage for natural scenery
body: internet surfers now can gain access to hongkong's country parks and marine parks through homepage newly opened by the government.  a spokesman of the hongkong agriculture and fisheries department said today that details of individual country parks, marine parks, nature trails, hiking trails and other recreational facilities such as barbecue sites are provided on the internet.  densely populated with 6.3 million people on an area of around 1,000 sq. km, hongkong has earmarked 40 percent of its land as country parks for outdoor recreational and nature conservation purposes.  through the homepage, users can obtain hints on hiking safety, statistics related to country parks and marine parks, and useful telephone numbers, according to the official. in addition to more than 1,000 color pictures and maps, there are 20 real-time videos with sound tracks in english, cantonese and putonghua on the homepage.

title: accord to provide world-class information signed in hk
body: the china internet corporation and china's ministry of post and telecommunications have signed a partnership agreement designed to provide world-class business information to internet users across china, according to a press release circulated here tonight.  the accord will bring the china internet's world-leading business information to over 100 major cities in china via chinanet, the ministry's nationwide internet network and the backbone of china's internet infrastructure.  under the agreement, the china internet's china wide web, an internet information provider, will deliver comprehensive business information from a number of world's big news agencies and corporations to chinese subscribers via chinanet.  additional joint services for the two sides will include corporate solution packages, with utilization of the software and hardware technology of the china internet's technology partner, the press release said, adding that the china internet will be the only national internet subscription re-seller for the ministry in all major cities across china.

title: macao chinese language newspaper steps on internet
body: macao daily news, the largest chinese language newspaper in macao, launched an internet edition today to become macao's first chinese language newspaper available in the world wide web service. internet surfers can reach the newspaper at the address of http://www.macaodaily.com, and read news, commentaries and view pictures. the news column includes what's new in macao, macao's economy, sports, news from the pearl river delta, and feature stories. the daily also offers three commentaries and main pictures it publishes each day. the formal launch of the internet edition of the daily was based on trial operation over the past several months. the daily said that during the trial period, it received a great deal of encouraging information from readers. it vowed to provide the best service with the help of the macao telecommunications company (ctm). several portuguese language newspapers have already launched their internet editions.

title: tianjin opens public information service
body: tianjin municipality today opened the tianjin hotline, the first computer public information service, to provide local users with the most up-to-date news about a variety of fields in this north china city.  the hotline has 13 volumes and 15 databanks, which can be accessed by dialing "169" via the internet.  tianjin's net is on line with public information computer sites in shanghai and six other chinese provinces.

title: chongqing goes on line
body: the municipal government of chongqing, which became china fourth municipality under the central government early this year, has opened a public service site on the internet.  the network, which has been in trial use since mid-june, provides information to all internet users about chongqing's overall conditions, local policies and law on foreign investment, and also offers an email post office.  current listings on the site are "chongqing municipality," "drawing foreign business and investment" and "tourism in chongqing," available in both chinese and english.

title: canada's electronic banking to increase rapidly
body: banking by internet, phone and debit card is expected to soar in canada over the next three years, said a report today.  computer banking --primarily on the internet --is expected to skyrocket by 450 percent in canada over the three years, according to ernst young canada, a company that did a 17-country study of banking and financial institutions recently.  banking in cyberspace is just getting going now, but the internet "is going to be one of the fastest growing distribution channels within the next three years," said ali hamza, a principal of the company.  the survey also suggests comparable growth in the use of banking by phone and an 82 percent rise in such things as debit card transactions by 1999.  "from the bank's point of view, technology banking is lower cost," hamza was quoted by the financial post newspaper as saying.  "from the customer's point of view, it's more convenient." however, bank branching will still remain the no.1 way canadians bank, hamza added.

title: us computer software giant to introduce new version
body: the microsoft corporation, the largest computer software maker in the unitedstates, announced today the introduction of a test version of its internet software that will bring millions of new users to the internet.  the product's new features include what micro officials are calling "true web integration," which is more closely linked to the company's windows 95 operating system, according to a report of the new york times.  the tested version will permit internet content to be embedded directly onto the basic control surface of the computer screen.  it is believed that more than 250 companies will use the product's new features to deliver entertainment and information to personal computer users.  microsoft, which is based in redmond, washington, is locked in a bitter struggle for control of internet industry standards with the netscape communication corporation, the silicon valley software company that is the leading developer of internet browsers.  "we think we will bring millions of new people to the internet," usuf mehdi, microsoft's director of internet marketing was quoted as saying.

title: nigeria to link all universities with internet
body: nigeria is planning to link all its universities to the internet worldwide web site, the official news agency of nigeria reported today.  dennis onyekwelu, director of the data management department of the nigerian universities commission said in abuja today that the plan has reached an advanced stage.  he said the plan is in line with the commission's objective of developing and standardizing the information management base of nigerian universities.  the university internet program is being undertaken by the abuja internet group, a non-governmental organization devoted to connecting nigeria with internet.  some nigerian universities are already using email services but they have problems with the local telecommunications services, which remain to be improved, onyekwelu said.

title: malaysia's oldest chinese newspaper on internet
body: malaysia's oldest chinese newspaper, kwong wah yit poh, today launched its own homepage on the internet. kwong wah yit poh, with its headquarters in malaysia's northwest state of pulau pinang, was founded in 1910 by dr. sun yat-sen, who led the revolution in 1911 overthrowing the feudal qing dynasty in china. the kwong wah homepage is available to internet users at http://www.kwongwah.com.my. and news on the kwong wah homepage is updated every day at 7:30 p.m. the daily provides foreign and local news as well as information relating to the company and its subsidiaries, color lab private ltd. and kwong wah realty.

title: internet school to train stock traders
body: the first school to train stock traders through the internet has been set up here.  the web site of the china finance and securities investment information network consists of six parts: enrollment, classroom, visitors' book, office, library and examination room.  "it only takes one or two days to graduate from the school," said wang yajun, general manager of the hexun corporation, which established the school.  the school provides students with basic stock knowledge and operation skills.  more and more beijing residents are trading in the stock market these days, with an estimated increase rate of more than 1,500 traders per day in recent months.

title: one million internet users in s. africa predicted
body: south africa could have one million internet users by the end of this year, local daily sunday independent quoted a web publisher as reporting today.  "there are already about 500,000 users in south africa and at the current private and corporate connectivity levels, it is not unrealistic to expect it to reach the million mark by the end of the year," robin parker, the marketing director of africa, said.  by the turn of the century, the south african internet site development and advertizing market could be worth one billion rand (222 million unitedstates dollars), with more than two million rand of on line transactions a year, parker said.  "individual connectivity is growing by about 12 percent a month and the usage of specific value sites is growing at between 20 percent and and 40 percent," he noted.

title: internet surfers chats about hong kong's return
body: hongkong's return" is a popular topic of a "virtual saloon" created on the internet by users in south china's hainan province as july 1, the red-letter-day, is approaching. many local internet users have communicated with their "network friends" through the on-line services to hail the momentous event with words like "proud", "happy" and "enthusiastic." wang houhong, deputy governor of hainan, has also shared his feelings with other internet users in the unitedstates, hongkong and the interior of china through the "virtual saloon." it is learnt that many internet users in shanghai, china's largest trade and financial city, have also held similar exchanges through the network.

title: fujian surfs on internet for overseas investment
body: east china's fujian province has set up an information network on local overseas investment to provide overseas investors with business opportunities via the internet.  the information network with internet access is sponsored by the fujian provincial foreign trade and economic cooperation commission.  the commission has signed contracts with the industrial development organization of the united nations and the hongkong trade development bureau, for priority in information exchange.  internet users can download the information available on the network, including the overall investment environment, laws and regulations on overseas investment, business opportunities for overseas investors, and recent information on local overseas-funded enterprises.  all cities in fujian will publicize timely information for overseas investment.

title: bank of china available on internet
body: the bank of china (boc), the nation's leading foreign exchange bank, has become the first state-owned commercial bank to publicize itself on the internet.  internet subscribers around the world will now be able to surf the world wide web and check out the bocs web page which features a detailed introduction to the bank, including information on its range of services, branches at home and abroad, foreign exchange rates, and other financial news.  regarding this only as a first step for the bank to publicize itself on internet, an official said that boc also planned to improve its electronic banking provisions by introducing services such as bills of exchange and electronic settlement for internet users.  about 400 financial institutions worldwide release information on the internet, but only a few chinese banks do so.

title: new york company offers wireless internet service
body: cellularvision usa announced today that it has begun marketing a new wireless high-speed internet access product, which it hopes to stay ahead of the industry for long.  called cellularvision digital network(sm) or cvdn 500, the product uses wireless lmds technology. the service enables consumers to bypass over-burdened telephone lines to access the internet at 500 kbps --four times the speed of an isdn line (128 kbps) and about 20 times the speed of a typical consumer's 28.8 kbps modem.  the cost of installation and monthly access are affordable for commercial and home users, according to the new york-based company.  the technology's highly flexible nature will allow cvus to stay ahead of the market, and the company will offer such internet access at even higher speeds in early 1998, the company said.  in addition, the company also announced recently that it has signed an agreement with nynex, the local telephone company, which will allow it to bundle local telephone service to consumers along with its high-speed internet access and subscription television service.

title: internet brings chinese closer to world
body: the internet system is playing an increasingly important role in chinese people's daily lives.  dong qiang, a resident of shenyang, the capital of liaoning province in the northeastern part of china, happened to get in touch with a nephew of his whom he had not seen for a long time, not long after he got the access to internet. "i have also made a friend on the net recently," he notes, "he's a factory director, and we jointly developed a new product for his enterprise." more than 200,000 chinese are using a national internet system to get in touch with one another and look up information of all kinds.  residents of cities such as shanghai and wuxi get international information at home, making internet very popular in many residences.  the chinese have also become fond of sending email to friends or relatives living or studying in foreign countries.

title: china opens first environmental protection web site
body: china has opened its first environmental protection web site this month on the internet, "china environment news" reported.  the paper said that the shanghai environment online is being jointly run by the state and the shanghai environmental protection bureaus, and the operation of the huge data base will help enhance public awareness of environmental protection.  it provides all information about environmental protection, and citizens are encouraged to join in discussions of hot topics in this respect.  some 4,000 people have visited the site since it was opened on june 5, the paper added.

title: thai police to use internet to fight crimes
