body: thai police authorities are launching a program to use the internet to fight crimes in a bid to improve their crime suppression efficiency.  under the program which will be in full operation in 1999, people could report complaints and crimes by email, while the latest crime suppression details, such as suspects' identities, missing vehicles and warrants for wanted criminals, are also provided on the internet.  the first phase of the program is expected to come on-line later this year, which would provide general information, including telephone numbers, about the (bangkok) metropolitan police bureau (mpb) as well as basic guidelines on how to avoid becoming a victim.  local newspapers said that information supplied to the police via e-main will remain confidential and only police offers know the password.  the police authorities believed that the internet-based system would be effective in fighting crimes, as the use of the internet is becoming popular around thailand.  the system will also be linked with the international criminal police organization (interpol) to facilitate cooperation on international anti-crime cooperation.

title: hong kong web site 1997 launches new edition
body: the hongkong 1997 web site was recently packed with a new edition with informative pages on hongkong's handover to the world's internet audience, according to china internet corporation (cic).  the new edition concentrates on hongkong's future, with sections reflecting all that is best about a city facing the 21st century. the official 1997 handover web site has partnered with key hongkong bodies including the hongkong airport authority, hongkong trade development council, kowloon-canton railway, mtr and hongkong tourist association.  it also features a daily "today's news" section which keeps viewers up-to-date on what is happening in hongkong throughout the handover period.  a "picture news" section brings exclusive shots of events in hongkong with regular updates every few hours during the handover itself.  michael mcleod, cic's director of sales and marketing, said, "we have attracted overwhelming interest to the site since its launch in april and we expect the interest to increase substantially as hongkong's handover approaches."

title: shanghai bookstore on-line
body: the xinhua bookstore on east nanjing road in shanghai, the largest in the metropolis, has been connected to a local computer network, becoming the first on-line bookstore in the city.  customers now have access to the bookstore's information and service through the "shanghai hotline", a public access computer network in shanghai.  the on-line bookstore provides 40,000 kinds of books, and the book information can be searched through the network in five ways.  other information on books can also be gained through the network, and readers' advice and requirements can be received by the bookstore instantly through email.  more than 4,000 people have visited the bookstore through the network since it went into operation two weeks ago.

title: british ncis asks for powers to fight crime on internet
body: the national criminal intelligence service (ncis) of britain has called for extra powers to face the growing threat of fraud, theft and terrorism to be conducted over the internet in the 21st century.  the ncis also has called for legislation on the theft of electronic information, saying that internet crime is "the policing challenge of the next millennium." albert pacey, director general of ncis, told a conference on wednesday that the internet was creating criminal opportunities that might ultimately affect every citizen.  a new police beat was on the way of emerging on the information highways, he added.  to establish an internet crime group within the national crime squad will be possibly one of ncis's suggestions to the police and government in the summer, pacey said.  however, observers here believe ncis's push for increased regulation is likely to meet some opposition from the software industry and advocates of free speech.

title: online bookstore opens in beijing
body: china opened an online bookstore yesterday to showcase its publications on the world market, today's "china daily" reported.  more than 200 chinese publishing houses, 6,000 periodicals and nearly 20,000 titles of books are available through the internet, the paper said.  the electronic bookstore is operated by the china national publishing industry trading corporation and asia pacific net, inc in the unitedstates.  about 500 million copies of books published in china are purchased overseas annually, according to the paper, adding that the new bookstore will help meet the growing overseas demand for chinese publications.

title: beijing to promote on-line service on campus
body: college teachers in beijing will enjoy 30 percent discount from on-line service fees, as a result of the beijing municipal telecommunications administration's efforts to promote digital communication on campus.  according to a plan made by the administration, special communication lines will be provided to link colleges and research institutes in beijing to china-net, the framework of the information highway in china, which is hooked up to nearly 20,000 users.

title: east china city attracts investment via internet
body: fuzhou, the capital of east china's fujian province, started an international investment promotion months yesterday on the local network hooked up with the internet.  the information about key local investment projects, in both chinese and english, is sent through "window of fujian" , the local address, to worldwide web readers.  according to local sources, the project is aimed at making the city better known to the rest of the world.  it is expected that the city's various development zones, investment centers, bonded areas, and export-oriented enterprises will soon make full use of the channel either by presenting itself or tapping the information on the net.

title: indonesia's internet users reach 60 million
body: the number of internet subscribers in indonesia has grown significantly in the last couple of years.  up to now, by one account, the number has already reached 60 million, an internet company's executive said.  cbn-net's director sugiharto darmakusuma said here tuesday that there is clearly an attractive market for internet service providers (isp) in indonesia, a local newspaper the observer reported today.  at present, sugiharto said, 42 isps have already secured licenses, at least 21 of which are already in operation in the country.  cbn-net, which was established in 1995, said it currently has 4,000 subscribers, 120 of which are japanese expatriates.

title: us local phone giant to acquire internet giant
body: the gte corporation, the largest local telephone company in the unitedstates said tuesday that it had agreed to pay 616 million unitedstates dollars in cash to acquire the bbn corporation, one of the nation's biggest internet service companies.  the move is aimed at becoming a major operator of corporate data networks which will then be able to open a new round of fierce competition against the big long-distance companies including the att corporation, the new york times commented in a report wednesday.  "we are undergoing very dramatic, fundamental change in our industry. we are becoming a nation-wide provider of telecommunications services--voice, data and video," charles r.  lee, gte's chairman, was quoted as saying wednesday.  att is the leader in running national corporate networks, with about 60 percent of a 12 billion unitedstates dollar market, followed by the mci communications corporation, the sprint corporation and worldcom inc.  "together we are an almost perfect strategic fit--our technology and their resources," george h. conrads, bbn's chairman, said of the proposed merger with gte.

title: brazilian beats chang at at and t challenge
body: brazilian fernando meligeni ended top-seeded and defending champion michael chang to retain his at and t challenge title in duluth, georgia, on tuesday.  the brazilian beat chang in a two hour thriller frist round match, 2-6, 6-3, 6-4.  chang, winner on clay last week in orlando, florida, and ranked second in the world, played adequately but was unable to make a lasting impact on meligeni, ranked 72nd.  fourth-seeded andre agassi posted a 6-3, 6-2 win over jamie oncins of brazil.  in an afternoon upset, qualifier steve campbell ousted foting impact on meligeni, ranked 72nd.  agassi was delighted yet cautious with his win, a definite improvement after losing four opening round matches in his last four events.  campbell, a 26-year-old ranked 236th in the world, was completely outplayed at the start, losing the first five games.

title: nepali official calls for promotion of internet use
body: a senior government official has said nepal should promote the use of the worldwide internet to make the rest of the world know about the country.  speaking at a talk program on "internet in information technology" here sunday, state minister for information and communications rakam chemjong said the country needs to be familiar with the use of the latest technology of communication, otherwise it would be left far behind in the communications sector.  the role of the computer-based communication network is increasing in nepal though many people here still don't know about the internet, he said.  he called on those working in the field to strive to promote the identity of nepal through the web of the internet.  n

title: german police track down airport blackmailer on internet
body: german police authorities have tracked down on the internet a blackmailer who threatened to sabotage passenger airliners unless he was paid 50 million german marks (30 million unitedstates dollars), a german newspaper reported today.  according to the bild am sonntag newspaper, the blackmailer sent in march letters to 15 german airports threatening to steer a remote-controlled model plane into jet turbines of an airliner with several hundreds passengers on board as it took off.  because the blackmailer conducted all the later negotiations through the internet computer network with his own email address, investigators managed to track him down in the area of hamburg.  further probe into the case found out that the suspected offender was a 25-year-old computer freak who was in heavy debt and had already been detained by police earlier for tax evasion, the report said.

title: singapore moves ahead in attempt to secure cyber-shopping
body: singapore has taken another step towards reality in its attempt to secure cyber-shopping, as it launched here today a pilot project called commerce payment.  this project is a joint effort by the country's network for electronic transfer (nets), hewlett-packard, verifone, major banks and credit card companies.  under the project, cyber-shoppers will be issued digital certificates by credit card companies that can be used at approved websites. and retailers will be able to recognize genuine shoppers through the certificates.  a senior executive officer of the nets said that shoppers do not have to pay a service charge for the service, which is only open to credit card holders.  however, he said, plans are now in the pipeline to make it available to other cash cards holders.  some 4,000 shoppers and 75 retailers will take part in the project till the end of this year, he said.

title: nigeria to host sub-sahara internet workshop
body: nigeria is to host a worshop on internet services in sub-saharan africa from april 20 to 23, the news agency of nigeria reported today.  nigeria's no.2 figure, the chief of general staff, lieutenant-general oladipo diya is to deliver a keynote speech at the workshop in abuja, the report said.  participants of the workshop will share their experiences in internet uses, assess the development of internet in the sub-region and decides on actions to be taken to ensure its sustainable development, it said.  the workshop is co-organized by the nigerian ministry of communications and the united nations development program.

title: remote city hooked up with national telecom network
body: lanzhou, capital of northwest china's gansu province, has shortened its distance with the outside world thanks to the opening of a public information network.  the lanzhou public information service network, hooked up with chinanet, the country's national telenet linked with internet, now provides access for local users to surf on the information highway.  based on recognized networking technologies, the subscribers now can dial in the net and sort out information as they require.  local sources said that the current database is divided into 17 information categories with contents covering such beats as news, finance, securities, material supply, tourism, transport and telecommunications.

title: fbi seeks more money to combat internet child pornography
body: fbi director louis freeh tuesday said that his agency is trying hard to protect children from the "dark side" of the internet, where pedophiles search for victims.  but freeh and ernest allen, president of the national center for missing exploited children, said law enforcement needs more money to deal with the problem, which has increased along with the popularity of the internet.  "it's more of a resource issue for us and other agencies," freeh told the senate appropriations subcommittee that oversees funding of the justice department, the parent agency of the fbi.  "i think we have the tools there. i just think we need more resources." "the dark side of that technology is that criminals or pedophiles can reach into your home… without many, many safeguards," freeh said.  freeh said the fbi was attacking the problem through its "crimes against children" initiative, which covers sexual exploitation of children, abductions and violent crimes.

title: China's First Computer Contest for University Students
body: China will hold its first computer contest this month for university students using the Internet. Today's "China Youth Daily" quotes an official with the All-China Students Federation as saying that students from at least 32 universities will take part in the contest. Students will be asked to send software designed by themselves to the Organizing Committee by mid-June. Debates on hot topics regarding information revolution will be conducted on the Internet, the paper said. Only 100 students will be selected for the final round in Beijing later this year, and winners will be given a computer as a prize. Statistics show that there are more than 100,000 Chinese using the Internet, but that only a few families in major cities have bought computers. A computer with the Pentium CPU costs almost half the annual income of an ordinary family in the 1990s. Some primary and high schools have opened computer courses.

title: NZ Ranks Fifth in Internet Use
body: New Zealand boasts the fifth highest number of Internet-linked computers, known as hosts, per head of population among the world countries. The local magazine NZ Infotech Weekly today quoted a global survey conducted by the California-based consultancy Network Wizards in January that New Zealand's placing is below Finland, Norway, the unitedstates and Australia, but ahead of Britain, France and Japan. The survey found that hosts in New Zealand totaled over 84,000 in January, up 58 percent from the numbers a year earlier. But many hosts are used by more than one person, so the actual number of New Zealanders using the Internet is likely to be very much greater than the figure suggests, according to the survey.

title: nz ranks fifth in internet use
body: new zealand boasts the fifth highest number of internet-linked computers, known as hosts, per head of population among the world countries.  the local magazine nz infotech weekly today quoted a global survey conducted by the california-based consultancy network wizards in january that new zealand's placing is below finland, norway, the unitedstates and australia, but ahead of britain, france and japan.  the survey found that hosts in new zealand totaled over 84,000 in january, up 58 percent from the numbers a year earlier.  but many hosts are used by more than one person, so the actual number of new zealanders using the internet is likely to be very much greater than the figure suggests, according to the survey.

title: north china tourism fair starts in tianjin
body: the three-day second north china tourism trade fair is going on in tianjin, a port city 100 km east of the chinese capital beijing.  the fair. which opened friday at the joint sponsorship of tourism administrations of beijing, tianjin and inner mongolia autonomous region, and hebei, shanxi, shandong, henan and seven other provinces, has also drawn some 400 travel agencies, hotels, resorts and official tourism promotion organizations from 27 provinces, municipalities and autonomous regions across china and counterparts from the us, canada, germany and singapore.  the organization committee has put the fair participants on the internet, giving each of them a permanent web site.  seminars, introductory conferences and investment project negotiations will also be staged during the fair, in addition to acrobatics, dances and other artistic performances.

title: macao has 3,350 internet users
body: the number of internet service users in macao has reached 3,350, and is expected to grow to some 5,000 by the end of this year.  fifty-seven percent of them are chinese-language users, 27 percent of them portuguese users and the remaining are english users, according to a report in today's macao daily news.  in addition, most of the users are individuals instead of companies or institutions, because "macao business people are quite conservative in expanding their business via the internet," said ma chi kong, manager of the macao telecommunications company (ctm), who is in charge of the internet service.  "they are not fully aware of the role that internet plays in international business and trade," he added.  macao introduced the internet service in 1995, and the number of users rose from 800 in the end of 1995 to 2,600 in 1996.  most users choose to enter the internet on saturdays and sundays. on other weekdays, they usually enter after eleven o'clock in the evening.  the macao government has established several homepages on the internet, in a bid to let users know more about macao's tourism, weather, hotels and transportation.

title: chinese industrial zone benefitting from internet
body: the songjiang industrial zone, one of nine industrial development zones in shanghai, has gotten 50 million us dollars in overseas investment in the first two months of this year by creating a homepage on the internet. the amount of investment is two times that for the same period of last year. the industrial zone put its homepage on the internet last june, and at least 110,000 people have visited the site located at http://www.sh.com/zone/sjiz/sjiz.html. songjiang's homepage visitors can learn about the local investment environment via the main menu, and can get in touch with it through email. other industrial zones in shanghai are said to be applying for their own homepages on the internet.

title: german neo-nazis profit from internet
body: the internet is being widely used by right-wing extremists in germany to gather information on neo-nazi organizations worldwide, the german media reported today.  computer samplings on the internet have found thousands of contact addresses and telephone numbers of right-wing extremist organizations, nazi symbols and slogans, such as "skinhead front," "storm front," and "aryan crusaders," according to a report by the german news agency dpa.  german police said a unitedstates-based extremist group known as white aryan resistance, which preaches white supremacy, is one of numerous far-right organizations using the internet to publicize its activities.  a computer specialist was quoted by the german daily bild as saying that the internet was currently being "swamped by right-wing propaganda, above all from the unitedstates and canada." german officials said far-right organizations in the country were profiting from such information. they also feared that international links among extremists might be created as a result.

title: british queen puts royal matters online
body: the queen of britain is launching a web site which will provide computer access to materials on royal topics, a local newspaper said today.  queen elizabeth ii will start the new service on the world wide web next thursday, offering information ranging from royal finance to the palaces and private estates illustrated by 150 color pictures, the daily telegraph said.  buckingham palace said setting up a web site was an effective way of reaching people. the world's internet users has reached 35 million and is expected to rise to between 100 million and 160 million by the millennium.

title: vietnam launches first electric newspaper
body: the national committee for overseas vietnamese (ncov) has put its monthly journal que huong online as the first electric newspaper in the country.  local media reported today that the electric newspaper was launched on the internet on february 6, the eve of the lunar new year.  the vietnamese-language newspaper provides overseas vietnamese with latest information on government policies and the daily life of the vietnamese at home and abroad.  the printed journal came out three years ago with low circulations. ncov deputy chairman pham khac lam was quoted as saying that he hoped that the journal will be able to reach about 50,000 vietnamese readers abroad via the internet.  the first issue of the electric newspaper includes new year greetings from vietnamese president le duc anh and foreign minister nguyen manh cam's speech at a new year's meeting with overseas vietnamese returning for lunar new year's holiday. it also includes vietnam's socio-economic achievements in 1996 and the main tasks set for 1997, as well as newly promulgated policies relating to vietnamese living abroad.

title: irish government to crack down on internet abuse
body: the irish government announced in dublin today that it would set up a working group to fight against the illegal use of the internet.  irish prime minister john bruton said in a statement that the main task of the working group was to focus on "such issues with particular reference to the need to address the issue of child pornography (on the internet) in the short term." the government group was also charged with drawing up various recommendations to crack down on internet abuse across the country, according to press reports from dublin.

title: clinton announces computer grants to public schools
body: unitedstates president clinton announced saturday the first "technology literacy" grants to provide needy public schools with computers and internet access.  "that's how we must prepare our children for the 21st century --with the full promise of the information age at their fingertips," clinton said in his weekly radio address.  the new grants are expected to fund programs in each of the 50 states by the end of 1997, help disadvantaged schools to buy classroom computers, provide internet access and train teachers to use it. illinois, mississippi and new mexico will share the first installment of a total of 14.3 million federal funds.  according to a survey by the education department, only one in five teachers in american public schools used advanced telecommunications, and only 13 percent of public schools required teacher training in the technology.  schools with the highest concentration of poverty and those in the most rural areas are also lagging far behind in computer access, the survey found.

title: internet will create new industries, intel president says
body: intel corporation president andrew grove said here today that the internet would radically change and create new industries from current telecommunications, media and services industries.  "such radical changes create opportunities for businesses and economies which can operate in these new industries," grove said in his speech to the plenary session of the annual meeting of the world economic forum (wef) being held in davos from january 30 to february 4.  also in his speech, grove urged european government and business leaders to take advantage of their existing infrastructure and substantial investments in information technology (it) as a competitive tool in the race towards globalization.

title: china and microsoft to develop foolproof internet software
body: china info-highway corp., the country's largest on-line service provider, has signed a contract with microsoft which permits the chinese firm to use the powerful microsoft commercial internet system (mcis) in its network.  this is the first time that microsoft awarded an on-line service provider the license to an asian-pacific business firm to use the mcis software.  "the use of mcis in the chinese-language based computer network will speed up the development of a 'foolproof' internet interface and enable most chinese families who do not speak english to access internet," a microsoft representative said here today.  china info-highway corp., a company jointly started by the ministry of posts and telecommunications and the construction bank of china, has emerged as the largest on-line service provider in the country, with tens of thousands of surfers everyday.  "people now in the eight large chinese cities, including beijing, shanghai and guangzhou, are now easily able to surf it," said zhang shuxin, the firm's president.  "our eventual goal is to let the average chinese work, study, play and shop by travelling leisurely in cyberspace," she noted.

title: direct access to internet for china's overseas scholars
body: chinese scholars studying overseas wanting to find out about an investment policy for a domestic high-tech development zone can now get the information directly through the internet.  the network includes information about overseas scholars and their work, policies about returning home and working for the country, lists of major colleges and universities, scientific research institutes, and enterprises, and information about key subjects and labs in china.  official from the chinese service center for scholarly exchange (cscse), which is in charge of the network, say they will make it a professional information resource center for overseas scholars and a "technology information board".  sites will also be set up in chinese embassies and consulates, cscse branches, and groups of overseas scholars in foreign countries to speed information access.  founded in early 1994 by cscse, the information network has provided information about overseas scholars and domestic companies.

title: microsoft offers internet software to macao
body: the microsoft company's hongkong branch has signed a memorandum with the local dealer of internet service to provide a new internet software to local customers.  the macao telecommunications company (ctm) said in a press release that under the agreement, the ctm will provide licensed copy of microsoft internet software, namely, microsoft internet explorer, free of charge to local customers who apply for ctm's internet service as of january 16.  the new software will help users get a quicker access to the internet, said the release.  two versions of the software will be available together with the installation kit. windows 95 version can be obtained first while windows 3.1 version will be available later, according to the release.  fernanda madeira, director of ctm's internet service, said that the cooperation will benefit customers, especially, computer beginners, in the installation of internet software to connect to the internet service.  internet service was introduced to macao by the ctm in 1995, and the number of customers has reached 2,700 in macao.

title: ibm offering patent information on line
body: ibm is making the contents of more than 2 million patent filings available to the public on the world wide web, the company announced today.  the database contains information on all patents granted by the unitedstates patent and trademark office since 1979, and a majority of those granted from 1971 to 1979, an ibm spokesman said.  the patent information available fills 2,800 cd-roms. web users will be able to search for patents by various categories, including the subject, inventor and key words.

title: ibm offering patent information on line
body: ibm is making the contents of more than 2 million patent filings available to the public on the world wide web, the company announced today.  the database contains information on all patents granted by the unitedstates patent and trademark office since 1979, and a majority of those granted from 1971 to 1979, an ibm spokesman said.  the patent information available fills 2,800 cd-roms. web users will be able to search for patents by various categories, including the subject, inventor and key words.

title: china news link with internet
body: the china news information platform, set up by the china internet information center, has been hooked up to the internet via the chinanet. the new platform, whose address is http://www.china.or.cn, will begin operating on january 1, and will provide news about china, special topics, statistical data, local information, chinese publications, and outlines about china. major chinese newspapers, periodicals and other publications of interest to overseas users will provide a round-the-clock retrieval service through the new platform.

title: data telecom network be operational in hebei
body: north china's hebei province has spent 300 million yuan launching a data telecommunications network in order to speed up the modernization of its telecommunications infrastructure.  so far, the network has extended its coverage to all cities, counties and some economically developed townships across hebei, providing such data telecom services as data interchange and frame relay, according to the "guangdong-hongkong information daily." the network, which includes a internet node in shijiazhuang, capital of hebei, has signed up more than 3,000 regular users.  based on the network, hebei will build a province-wide super information highway which will add the digital, broad-band and intelligent functions to hebei's telecom system.

title: liaoning province on information superhighway
body: an information superhighway has opened in northeast china, connecting 14 cities and prefectures with the information systems with other parts of the country.  the network was built by a beiguo data telecom ltd., a company jointly launched by the province's posts and telecommunications administration and a local hi-tech group.  beiguo infonet now provides network communications and information services for local governmental organs, enterprises and families.  the network, which is linked with internet and chinanet, a chinese branch of internet, issues 1.4 million words of information every day, covering the fields of electronics, chemical industry, materials supply and the automotive industry.

title: another internet sub-node opens to customers
body: another sub-node affiliated to chinanet, has recently opened to public service in beijing since the general public can hook up to internet service in june, 1996.  the sub-node, jointly built by beijing cyber netology co. ltd and beijing telegraph administration bureau, can provide internet service with 28.8 kpbs in speed and 15 yuan in service charge for each hour. it can also provide wireless internet service for major events, such as international exhibitions and conferences, said hong chengjing, a spokesman for cybernet.  to help provide rudiments for internet funs in china, beijing cyber netology co. ltd has launched 28 training classes with more 300 trainees. an internet training class solely in english for foreign diplomats and businessmen in beijing will begin in the middle of next month, he said.  since china hooked up to internet service, the country has established two major public nodes, namely chinanet and chinagbnet as well as four specialized networks such as casnet, cernet, stinet and cminet. the number of individual customers has come up to 100,000 in beijing.

title: aid-poor-children program gets access to internet
body: children in china's impoverished families will be able to receive worldwide charitable assistance now that the hope project has established a web site on the internet, the "china youth daily" reported today. the hope project was launched by the china youth development foundation (cydf) in 1989 to help school dropouts in poverty-stricken areas return to school. the hope project entered the internet on december 6, giving clients of the global computer network access to news about the charity program, and also donation information, according to sources with the cydf. the internet address for the hope project is http: 11www.wtdb.coml, cydf sources said. as of november, the cydf had received more than 800 million yuan (96 million us dollars) from domestic and overseas donors, and 1.3 million dropouts in poor areas resumed their schooling.

title: "malaysia's gift to the world" on sale on internet
body: royal selangor pewter, often regarded as "malaysia's gift to the world", is now on sale on the internet. royal selangor, the world's largest pewter manufacturer, today officially launched its homepage and interactive pewter gallery, the first of its kind in asia. those with access to the world wide web can visit royal selangor's very own website at "http://royalselangor.com," and cyber customers can conveniently shop for gifts without leaving their homes or offices. pages, introduced today at a news conference at royal selangor pewter factory complex in setapak near here, include the background of the company, pewter news, global presence, on-line shopping, special orders and gift assistance. royal selangor's website also features a selection of more than 100 types of pewter gifts and tableware in its on-line shopping section. the company has expanded operations in recent years and has its own retail outlets in seven countries in addition to malaysia. royal selangor, which has a history of 111 years, produces more than one million pieces of pewter gifts and tableware annually with half of them exported, they said.

title: fbi searches 20 cities in computer sex
body: agents of the unitedstates federal bureau of investigation (fbi) searched 20 cities today in a nationwide investigation into the use of computer online services and the internet to expose children to sex and pornography.  the searches were conducted in virginia, maryland, florida and washington, d.c. decisions on arrests will be made later after prosecutors review the materials seized in the searches.  in the three-year investigation, 80 people have been arrested in 207 searches. fbi director louis j. freeh said today's searches "are a continuation of a highly successful investigation." "these cases have already revealed the ease and frequency with which criminals have used modern technology to cause grave harm to children," freeh said. "these crimes, preying on innocent children, represent every parent's worst nightmare." investigators uncovered adults across the nation using computers to lure minors into illicit sex with pedophiles and to transmit pictures of minors that show full frontal nudity and sexually explicit activities, fbi said.

title: netscape, bells forge tie for internet service
body: the netscape communications corporation and five regional bell internet companies of the unitedstates today announced a marketing agreement which targets at a market of 26 states.  according to the agreement, netscape navigator software will be used as the default browser for their services, allowing clients to easily select these telephone companies' internet services through the new netscape isp select.  ameritech interactive media services, bell atlantic internet solutions, bellsouth.net, pacific bell internet services and southwestern bell internet services will use netscape navigator as the default browser for their internet access services.  together, the companies represent a potential market of 72 million consumers and businesses in 26 states, including washington, d.c., and in 15 of the nation's 20 largest markets.

title: nigeria's stock exchange internet system begins operation
body: the nigerian stock exchange (nse) internet system (lapnet) has begun operation, said a nse statement today.  the statement said the exchange has begun "sending and receiving information through email," which is one of the facilities available on the internet.  it said that participants in the market, including stockbrokers, issuing houses and quoted companies have started subscribing to the internet services.  the report said that subscribers now can have access to key market information through the internet from anywhere in the world and at any time.  the internet project is one of the infrastructural support being provided by the management of the exchange to adequately postion the market for the challenges of internationalization, with a view to meeting current and future needs of the economy, the statement said.

title: sadc conference to join information highway
body: the southern african development community (sadc) consultative conference to be held in windhoek in february next year will be linked to internet, sadc executive secretary kaire mbuende said today.  speaking at a press conference in windhoek, capital of namibia, mbuende said the entire proceedings, including conference documents, will be available on the sadc site to internet users, reported the south african press association.  the theme of sadc's scheduled 1997 consultative conference will focus on productivity, a key to sustainable growth and development in the region.  "enhanced productivity is a key factor to be mastered by our people if the region's economies are to become competitive in the global market place," said mbuende.  the 12-member sadc bloc comprises angola, botswana, lesotho, malawi, mauritius, mozambique, namibia, south africa, swaziland, tanzania, zambia and zimbabwe.

title: athens boosts bidding for 2004 games on the internet
body: athens used the internet's world wide web to boost its effort to bid for the right to stage the 2004 olympic games. "we wanted to provide people with direct information on our bid as well as information on how other cities are doing," manolis mavromatis, press director for the organizing committee, said tuesday. the graphics-rich site, which can be found at http://www.athens2004.net, provides news briefs and file summary for athens' bid as well as hotels, information of facilities and infrastructure works in progress. users of the web could also find briefs on the history of the olympic games -from their roots in ancient greece to their revival here 100 years ago. mavromatis said the site is one of five already put on the web by contending cities. others include buenos aires, argentina; istanbul, turkey; lille, france; seville, spain and stockholm, sweden. eleven cities are bidding for the 2004 games. the others are cape town, south africa; rio de janeiro, brazil; san juan, puerto rico and st. petersburg, russia. they will be pared down to four or five in march, and the final decision will be announced in los angeles on september 5.

title: china publishes negroponte's new book
body: a chinese translation of "being digital" by nicholas negroponte, the us futurist, has hit chinese bookstores.  the book, translated by two scholars at the chinese academy of social sciences, tells chinese readers the latest concepts about the information revolution, according to the hainan publishing house, the publisher.  negroponte, a professor at massachusetts institute of technology, and the founder of the media lab, is regarded as one of the most influential masters in the field of computer and communications.  he was listed as one of the most important futurists by time magazine this year.  the best seller describes how digital technology and the internet are affecting people's lives, and changing the course of work, education and entertainment. the book has already been published in 30 languages.  the publisher said that the book will attract a large number of computer fans in china, especially the younger generation who want to communicate with the world on the internet. though at a relatively slow pace, the number of chinese internet users continues to increase at a steady pace.

title: chinese economic information network
body: a network that provides chinese economic information, which is hooked up to internet, is scheduled to open on 3 december, according to china's state information center.  the china economic information network (ceinet) is being jointly built by the state information cente, provincial information centers, and information centers in various ministries.  ceinet will provide not only economic information to the country's governmental organizations, enterprises and private users, but also internet services, such as email, information retrieval and other transmission services.  ceinet will first provide services in china's ten major cities, and has joined a company of the ministry of electronics to set up 24 satellite telecom stations nationwide, to increase its reach.  ceinet will provide a variety of economic information, such as macro-economic developments, industrial and commercial surveys, and investment opportunities.

title: macao lowers charges on internet services
body: charges for internet services in macao were cut by 30-60 percent as of wednesday, the macao telecommunications company (ctm) announced.  the price cut, which includes deletion of peak hour charges and reduction of usage fees, will benefit both the ctm's internet customers and internet service providers in macao, the ctm said.  "after the operation and development of internet for about one year and a half, more people in macao are now aware of the service, … and internet has become more popular," said fernanda madeira, director of ctm internet services.  "ctm took the initiative (price cut) … to further promote the popularity of internet," he said.  macao started internet services in june 1995.

title: internet symposium on broadcasting in south china
body: the city of guangzhou, the capital of south china's guangdong province, has hosted an international symposium on radio broadcasts for the 21st century over internet.  researchers, engineers, musicians, and educators from china, britain, germany and japan had a get-together with the help of the internet to discuss the challenges, opportunities, and future of radio and music in the next century.  the event was sponsored by guangdong people's radio station and the information network engineering research center of the south china engineering university.

title: microsoft buys equity of israeli firm
body: microsoft corp., the software giant in the world, has purchased equities in the israeli company vdonet, which specializes in software enabling high-quality video transmissions over the internet.  according to today's jerusalem report, the companies had signed a licensing agreement on internet communication technologies.  the report did not specify the extent of microsoft's investment, but the purchase is believed to be microsoft's first major investment in israel.  "microsoft has been actively evolving technology and products to make communication over the internet a valuable experience," said john ludwig, vice president in the internet platform and tools division at microsoft.  "we concluded that vdonet and its technology will complement our efforts and play a vital role in the future of network communication," ludwig was quoted by the newspaper as saying.  the report said that the vdonet's breakthrough technology offers high-quality video optimized for communication over low-bandwidth connections.

title: hke102345 --malaysia's 1997 budget announcement to be transmitted live on internet
body: malaysia's 1997 national budget announcement, which is scheduled for friday, will be transmitted live on the internet, an official statement said here today. this will be the first time in asia's history that a national budget is made available on the internet. malaysian deputy prime minister anwar ibrahim, also finance minister of the country, is scheduled to unveil the national budget in parliament on friday. radio television malaysia (rtm). net chairman ismail mustapa said in a statement that the broadcast could be accessed from anywhere in the world via the internet by visiting the rtm home page on the web site: http://live.rtm.net.my/budget97. the live announcement will be captured and updated on the internet at five-second intervals, making it almost "live", it said. the national budget on the internet is said to be timely, as it is expected to be very much an "information technology (it) budget" focused on preparing the country for the multimedia super corridor.

title: symposium on internet for commercial use opens
body: a symposium on the commercial use of the internet opened today in beijing.  specialists from the china institute of scientific and technological information, and us asian net, gave a detailed introduction to the internet.  china has now more than 4,000 computer service devices working with the internet, while in beijing the number of internet users who joined through china net, has risen ten fold since last year.  information from many chinese enterprises in urban areas can be read through the internet, and many chinese companies have tried to find foreign partners, and promote their products, via the net.  the internet is now the biggest computer network in the world. it has 2.5 million commercial users, and the total volume of commodity transactions and services has reached up to 20 billion us dollars.

title: cic launches china wide web
body: china internet corporation (cic) today announced the inauguration of the china wide web (cww), erecting a "golden bridge" for chinese enterprises to go abroad, and for overseas enterprises to learn more about china.  cww is an on-line network providing value-added business, financial and economic information in chinese language to subscribers in china and world-wide.  it is china's first nation-wide internet for corporate users to search, exchange and promote business information and services, both in chinese and english languages.  the announcement was made in beijing this afternoon at a seminar on cww information network, and the first annual conference of the cic corporation, which is a hongkong-based company established by a group of hongkong investors and the xinhua news agency.  more than 300 chinese and foreign guests, including over 80 entrepreneurs from the unitedstates, japan and hongkong, attended the seminar and conference.

title: eu makes efforts to fight misuse of internet
body: european union(eu) governments, industry groups and parents should unite to fight child pornography and other illegal or harmful content on the internet, the european commission(ec) said here today.  with the adoption of two reports, the commission is trying to find ways to protect children and to prevent criminals from misusing the global computer network.  instead of proposing strict legislation, the ec offered solutions such as industry codes of conduct, cooperation between the 15 eu governments to enforce existing laws and software that can screen out unwanted material.  the ec said that industry codes of conduct should guarantee that all material on the internet is traceable and that it would encourage the use of filtering software and the introduction of one or more european rating systems.  the ec also proposed a working meeting organized by the g/7-countries to examine the feasibility of immediate measures using existing legal framework and to discuss the possibility of an international convention on harmful and illegal content.

title: shanghai public information network on trial
body: shanghai on-line, a public information network, today went into operation on a trial basis in china's largest city.  from now on, local residents who own computers will be able to join the information highway through the new system, which reflects the progress in shanghai information industry.  the network, which is funded by the shanghai post and telecom administration, is one of the city's major information projects and links up with domestic and international webs.  shanghai on-line now has over a dozen databanks involving economics, trade, news, tourism and education. it offers more than 10,000 items of information and data as well as services such as email and document transmission.

title: imf launches electronic bulletin board on internet
body: the international monetary fund (imf) today opened to public access, through the internet, the electronic bulletin board for its special data dissemination standard (special standard).  the move is designed to provide information about the data dissemination practices of its subscribing member countries.  as a major step to monitor the financial markets, launching of the special standard and its associated bulletin board could respond to the need for comprehensive and timely economic and financial data, with equal and ready access for all users.  as of today, the metadata for 18 countries on the dissemination standards bulletin board and 34 countries have subscribed to the special standard.  the standard and system is set up at the request of the imf's ministerial-level interim committee in april 1995 to guide imf member nations in providing economic and financial statistics to the public. the special standard on statistics includes four categories of real sector, fiscal sector, financial sector, external sector as well as population.

title: un launches new home page on internet
body: the u.n. department of public information (dpi) launched the new united nations home page on the internet world wide web today.  the enhanced u.n. web site contained a host of new information materials set up under five categories: peace and security; economic and social development; international law; human rights and humanitarian affairs, according to dpi.  users may get detailed information on various bodies of u.n., news items, documents and audio-visual services. in addition, a hot-linked map of u.n. web sites around the world will provide connections to u.n. offices and agencies in geneva, paris, vienna, tokyo and other locations.  u.n. entered the information superhighway on june 24, 1995, with the pilot project on the world wide web.

title: indian government to connect schools to internet
body: the union government has chalked out a blueprint to connect schools across the country to the internet, a senior official said here today.  the program will, however, be open only for government-run and recognized institutions with a major focus on those in rural areas.  the scheme involves linking a cluster of eight to ten schools in a region to a very small aperture terminal (vsat), which would in turn be connected to a hub in the nearest town through the indian satellite, insat-2c.  "financial aid will be provided for the first three years, after which the school would have to take care of operational expenses," said minister of state for planning and program implementation and science technology y.k. alagh.  "we would like to have a vsat in each school, when it becomes feasible," he said.

title: india launches first on-line science magazine
body: india today launched its first on-line science magazine comcom.  the first ever electronic magazine will feature the latest in the world of science, besides a number of popular science features and fiction articles written by renowned science writers.  india also introduced its own home page on the internet for providing up-to-date information on indian science and technology to science journalists, non-governmental organizations and others.  anyone who has an internet connection can have access to this home page.

title: apple delivers new internet-ready apple color onescanner
body: apple computer, inc. of the unitedstates today unveiled its first flatbed scanner for the macintosh market to offer optical character recognition (ocr) to hypertext markup language (html) conversion, a necessity for scanning documents for placement on the internet.  with apple color onescanner 1200/30 ocr to html conversion, users simply scan a document, apply ocr, and seamlessly drag-anddrop html to their web authoring application within apple's new onescanner dispatcher software.  the new scanner users will enjoy a 600 x 1200 optical resolution and a 4800 x 4800 interpolated resolution for improved ocr accuracy and scanning small areas at high resolutions.  for superior image quality, the apple color onescanner provides 30-bit depth color, which recognizes over 1 billion colors, a significant advancement over 24-bit scanners.

title: hk computer magazine launches web site competition
body: the computer magazine pcworld hongkong today announced a competition for world-wide web internet sites.  the contest is open to all web sites hosted on a hongkong server or maintained solely from hongkong.  "the aim of the web site competition is to provide recognition for the numerous quality hongkong sites that are using cutting-edge web technologies to create a powerful presence on the world wide web for hongkong," said alison treasure, editor of the magazine.  the hongkong internet market has grown rapidly and local web sites are now some of the best in the world.  winners of the best business site and the best personal site, as well as runners-up in each category will be awarded with prizes including a complimentary lease line with worldlink, a p-100 desktop computer from ipc and software.  the pcworld hongkong invites individuals and corporations to enter their web sites in the competition, which will be a showcase of hongkong's mastery of web site design.

title: '96 internet, computer technology expo ends in hk
body: internet and computer technology expo ended here today with participation of 32 noted hongkong-based and overseas companies at internet services.  organized by american expositions and conferences (hk) ltd., the expo focused on the presentation of new equipment and technology of internet.  global one, a major internet service company formed by us sprint, france telecom and deutsche telecom, provided the exposition with a special cable to connect with the web in the unitedstates.  visitors can freely operate at computers at over 50 exhibition booths to learn more about the services of internet and world wide web.  derek wong, project manager of american expositions and conference (hk) ltd., said that internet services grows rapidly in the world as well as in hongkong.  now there are over 50 million users of internet in the world, while in hongkong the users reached 300,000.  during the three-day exposition, a series of seminars were held, covering internet phone, video conferencing, email, internet shopping and computer security system.

title: hk launches new internet gateway
body: with the launch of a regional internet gateway today, internet traffic between hongkong and taiwan will be carried through a direct link instead of passing through the unitedstates.  the gateway service was jointly launched by hongkong telecom and data communication business group, a subsidiary of chunghwa telecommunications company ltd. of taiwan.  a spokesman said that the introduction of the service will significantly improve the transmission efficiency and ease network congestion on the internet, and it would be particularly beneficial to tourists and frequent business travelers between the two places.

title: thailand's grand palace, crocodile farm on internet
body: internet users can now admire the beauty of bangkok's number one tourist attraction, the grand palace, electronically.  internet users can access world wide web site, which is set up as an electronic image gallery, to see several beautiful shots of the 200-year-old palace of traditional thai architecture.  each shot shows them a wonderful aspect of thai architecture and art, with a description below the picture.  samut prakarn crocodile farm and zoo, the world's largest crocodile farm with over 50,000 reptiles, has also put itself on the global network to attract foreign tourists to its crocodile and elephant shows.  pizza hut in thailand now allows local customers to order various menu items through the network for home delivery.  by filling the electronic ordering form and sending it electronically, customers will be able to receive their favorite pizza within 30 minutes at their door step.

title: southern province increases data communications
body: guangdong province has raised its annual investment in data telecommunications to 400 million yuan and built a province-wide data web involving the country's biggest financial network.  the province expanded its network for ddn (digital and data network) and internet services in 1995, adding 9,000 and 13,000 accesses to its packet exchange and ddn networks, respectively, bringing combined switching capacity to 34,000 terminals, according to china electronics news.  with 10,000 subscribers, the internet service now is available in all the cities and counties in the province , the paper said.  the expansion of the packet exchange network used pass port machines from northern telecom, a leading canadian telecom business, and att's dacs ii for the ddn project.  guangdong's financial network, which was completed in 1995, now has more than 1,000 automatic teller machines linked, the largest in the country.  guangdong plans to develop wireless data telecom systems in the pearl river delta, the richest region of the province, and other booming coastal areas over the next five years.

title: more canadians use internet
body: more and more canadians are using the internet, both at work and at leisure, a new survey shows.  some 29 percent of the 1,081 canadian adults polled have used the internet at least once in the past year, up from 12 percent a year ago, the survey commissioned by anderson consulting and conducted by gallup canada and goldfarb consultants showed.  anderson consulting's tom healey attributes the increase to greater opportunities for logging on to internet --both at work and in public places such as community centers and libraries.  the numbers are another sign that the internet has become a viable place to do business, said healey, whose firm helps companies use the information highway.

title: chengdu provides internet service
body: chengdu, the capital of sichuan province in southwest china, began to provide internet service on july 1.  chinanet, the chinese branch of internet, will provide the internet service to 2,000 users through telephone lines and the ddn (digital and data network) system.  the chengdu node is one of the largest in china's 31 chinanet affiliates, according to people's post and telecommunications daily.  the fee for the network is 100 yuan, and subscribers get three months' service free of charge, the paper said.

title: ji'nan enters into chinanet
body: the capital of east china's shandong province today signed on with chinanet, which serves the entire country and is one of the world's largest commercial internet distributors.  chinanet has two high-speed outlets in shanghai and beijing that link it with the internet, and five of the largest databanks, that include information on business, travel, news events, tourism, and international information services.  other chinese major cities and provinces that have internet access are beijing, shanghai and guangdong, as well as jiangsu, zhejiang, liaoning, and hainan.

title:
today's economic news in brief.
beijing connects with internet
body: beijing, home to many elite universities such as beijing university and qinghua university as well as the chinese academy of sciences, has connected with internet, the largest information network, usually referred to as the information superhighway in the unitedstates. scientists here can conduct direct exchanges with the rest of the world via the network and watch closely the latest developments of science and technology around the globe.

title: COPYRIGHT 1999 XINHUA NEWS AGENCY
body: AS MORE CONSUMERS IN CHINA BEGAN TO SURF ON THE INTERNET, ON-LINE SHOPPING IS EXPECTED TO FLOURISH, WITH SEVERAL COMPUTER COMPANIES ALREADY REPORTING GROWING PROFITS. ZHANG CHENGGUO, AN ECONOMIST WITH THE CHINESE ACADEMY OF SOCIAL SCIENCES, PREDICTED THAT AN INCREASING NUMBER OF CHINESE CUSTOMERS WILL GO ON-LINE DURING THIS HOLIDAY SEASON, ALTHOUGH ELECTRONIC-COMMERCE IS NOT FULLY DEVELOPED IN THE COUNTRY. AN E-COMMERCE OPERATOR, 8848.NET, WHICH OPENED AN ON-LINE SUPERMARKET IN MAY THIS YEAR, HAS SCORED SURPRISING SALES GROWTH, ACCORDING TO A REPORT BY CHINA DAILY BUSINESS WEEKLY TODAY. THE COMPANY'S REVENUES GREW FROM THE FIRST MONTH'S 500,000 YUAN (ABOUT 60,200 unitedstatesDOLLARS) TO 3.8 MILLION YUAN IN SEPTEMBER SAID. HOWEVER, CHINA'S ON-LINE SHOPPING IS STILL HINDERED BY SEVERAL FACTORS. INTERNET APPLICATIONS, TO MOST CHINESE SURFERS, ARE STILL LIMITED TO NEWS AND email. THE E-COMMERCE MARKET IS STILL IMMATURE BECAUSE THE COUNTRY LACKS A COMPLETE CREDIT SYSTEM AND EFFECTIVE EXPRESS NETWORK. JUSTIN TANG, CHAIRMAN OF ELONG.COM CORP., SAID THAT HIS COMPANY HAS SPONSORED A NATIONAL CAMPAIGN TO TEACH WEBSITE SKILLS AND AROUSE PEOPLE'S AWARENESS OF E-COMMERCE. THE NUMBER OF INTERNET USERS IS GROWING RAPIDLY IN CHINA, FROM FOUR MILLION IN THE FIRST HALF OF THIS YEAR TO AN ESTIMATED 10 MILLION BY YEAR'S END.

title: COPYRIGHT 1999 XINHUA NEWS AGENCY
body: ONE-FOURTH OF ALL unitedstates  BUSINESS-TO-BUSINESS PURCHASING WILL BE DONE ON-LINE BY 2003, ACCORDING TO A NEW STUDY RELEASED TUESDAY. BETWEEN 1998 AND 2003, unitedstates BUSINESS-TO-BUSINESS E-COMMERCE WILL GROW BY 33 PERCENT PER YEAR AND REACH 2.8 TRILLION unitedstates  DOLLARS IN TRANSACTION VALUE, ACCORDING TO THE STUDY CONDUCTED BY THE BOSTON CONSULTING GROUP (BCG), A MANAGEMENT CONSULTING FIRM WIDELY REGARDED AS A GLOBAL LEADER IN BUSINESS STRATEGY AND E- COMMERCE. IN 1998, BCG SAID, unitedstates BUSINESS-TO-BUSINESS E-COMMERCE WAS 671 BILLION DOLLARS, COMPRISING 92 BILLION DOLLARS IN INTERNET-BASED TRANSACTIONS AND 579 BILLION DOLLARS IN TRANSACTIONS USING ELECTRONIC DATA INTERCHANGE (EDI) OVER PRIVATE NETWORKS. BY 2003, THE TRANSACTION VALUE OF BUSINESS-TO-BUSINESS E-COMMERCE OVER THE INTERNET WILL BE TWO TRILLION DOLLARS, AND AN ADDITIONAL 780 BILLION DOLLARS IN PURCHASES WILL BE MADE OVER PRIVATE NETWORKS USING EDI. BCG'S DEFINITION OF BUSINESS-TO-BUSINESS E-COMMERCE INCLUDE EDI OVER PROPRIETARY NETWORKS, EDI OVER THE INTERNET, AND PURE INTERNET TRANSACTIONS TO ARRIVE AT TOTAL MARKET SIZE ESTIMATES. INTERNET ACTIVITIES, SUCH AS INFORMATION GATHERING THAT INFLUENCES OFF-LINE PURCHASES, WERE NOT INCLUDED. NON-SALES RELATED TRANSACTIONS, SUCH AS email EXCHANGES OF PROPOSED PRODUCT SPECIFICATIONS AND DRAWINGS, ARE IMPORTANT BUSINESS FACILITATORS, BUT DO NOT RESULT DIRECTLY IN A COMMERCIAL TRANSACTION. BCG'S ESTIMATES ALSO EXCLUDE PURCHASES OF FINANCIAL CAPITAL, LABOR AND BENEFITS SUCH AS HEALTH INSURANCE, ALL OF WHICH ARE MIGRATING ON-LINE. WHILE BUSINESS-TO-BUSINESS E-COMMERCE IS A GLOBAL PHENOMENON, BCG SAID, THE NORTH AMERICAN MARKET CURRENTLY DOMINATES. THE 700- BILLION-DOLLAR NORTH AMERICAN MARKET IS TWICE THE SIZE OF BUSINESS- TO-BUSINESS E-COMMERCE IN THE REST OF THE WORLD COMBINED, WHICH IS 330 BILLION DOLLARS. IN WESTERN EUROPE, WHICH LAGS 18 MONTHS BEHIND NORTH AMERICA IN BUSINESS-TO-BUSINESS E-COMMERCE ADOPTION, SEVERAL COUNTRIES HAVE ACCELERATED THEIR E-COMMERCE INVESTMENT AND WILL SIGNIFICANTLY CLOSE THIS GAP. ASIA AND LATIN AMERICA REMAIN FURTHER BEHIND. BUT BCG SAID THIS COULD CHANGE RAPIDLY AS GLOBAL SUPPLY CHAINS GO ON-LINE. IN THE unitedstates, OVER 65 PERCENT OF ALL BUSINESS-TO- BUSINESS E-COMMERCE WILL BE MADE BY SIX SECTORS BY 2003: RETAIL, MOTOR VEHICLES, SHIPPING, INDUSTRIAL EQUIPMENT, HIGH TECHNOLOGIES AND GOVERNMENT.

body: PAN PENGHUI, AN OVER 40 YEAR OLD MAN LIVING IN AN OUTLYING COASTAL VILLAGE IN EAST CHINA'S ZHEJIANG PROVINCE DID NOT EXPECT THAT THE INTERNET WOULD PROVIDE HIM WITH SO MANY BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES. AN OWNER OF A VALVE PRODUCING FIRM IN SHUILONG VILLAGE OF YUHUAN COUNTY, A SIX-HOUR BUS DRIVE FROM HANGZHOU, THE PROVINCIAL CAPITAL, PAN'S BUSINESS HAS BEEN BOOMING SINCE HE BOUGHT A COMPUTER AND BEGAN SURFING ON NET TWO YEARS AGO. PAN DESCRIBES THE IMPACT OF THE NET ON HIS BUSINESS AS AKIN TO AN "EARTHQUAKE MEASURING 6 ON THE RICHTER SCALE." HIS COMPANY'S MONTHLY BUSINESS HAS RISEN FROM 300,000 YUAN (ABOUT 3,500 unitedstates  DOLLARS) TO ONE MILLION YUAN (120,000 US DOLLARS). HAMPERED BY POOR, RUGGED ROAD CONDITIONS AND LITTLE ACCESS TO INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY, VILLAGERS IN SHUILONG (LIT: "WATER DRAGON") HAVE RELIED SOLY ON CROPS AS A MEANS OF EKING OUT AN EXISTENCE.  HOWEVER, WITH THE INTRODUCTION OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (IT), IN PARTICULAR, THE NET, LOCAL FARMERS IN THE VILLAGE HAVE BEEN ADOPTED A NUMBER OF OTHER WAYS TO COMPETE AND SURVIVE. CHEN XIUPING, OWNER OF THE YUHUAN CARBURETOR FACTORY, HAS INVITED A COLLEGE STUDENT TO HELP HIM GET ACCESS INFORMATION FROM THE NET. HIS FACTORY PRODUCES ACCESSORIES FOR CHINA'S LARGEST AUTOMOBILE MANUFACTURER -- CHINA NO.1 AUTOMOBILE WORKS. AUTOMOBILE ACCESSORIES FROM CHEN'S FACTORY HAVE ENTERED THE WORLD MARKET AND ARE SOLD TO ITALY, INDONESIA, TURKEY AND OTHER COUNTRIES. MORE AND MORE PEOPLE IN THE VILLAGE HAVE TELEPHONES AND COMPUTERS IN THEIR HOMES, ATTEND TECHNICAL TRAINING COURSES AND SURF THE NET. THE TELEPHONE HAS NOW BECOME AN INTEGRAL PART OF THE LIFE IN SOME 300-HOUSEHOLD SHUILONG VILLAGE. MORE THAN 30 PERCENT OF THE VILLAGERS ARE ON-LINE. "WE HAVE COME TO REALIZE THAT THE NET IS WINDOW TO THE OUTSIDE WORLD," PAN NOTED. TODAY, PAN NO LONGER TRAVELS TO SHANGHAI, THE COUNTRY'S LARGEST COMMERCIAL CENTER, TO ACCESS BUSINESS INFORMATION. HE  SITS AT HOME INSTEAD AND COMMUNICATES TO BUSINESSMEN AS FAR AS AUSTRALIA. CURRENTLY, 21 ENTERPRISES WITH AN OUTPUT VALUE OF MORE THAN ONE MILLION YUAN (120,000 US DOLLARS) HAVE SET UP THEIR OWN HOMEPAGES ON THE NET. FROM JANUARY TO OCTOBER, TOTAL EXPORTS IN SHUILONG VILLAGE EXCEEDED 41 MILLION YUAN (5 MILLION US DOLLARS), MORE THAN FIVE TIMES THAT FIGURE FIVE YEARS AGO. LOCAL VILLAGERS NOT ONLY USE THE NET FOR BUSINESS, BUT ALSO USE IT FOR ACCESSING ALL KINDS OF INFORMATION. YAN JIANQIAN, A YOUNG WOMAN VILLAGER IN HER 20S, READS NEWS ON THE NET EVERYDAY AND emailS HER FRIENDS, AND HER FAMILY HAVE ALSO LOGGED ONTO THE NET.

title: HK FORMS BILLION-DOLLAR TELECOM JOINT VENTURE
body: hongkong-BASED HUTCHISON WHAMPOA AND unitedstates FIBER OPTIC NETWORK PROVIDER GLOBAL CROSSING MONDAY ANNOUNCED THE AGREEMENT TO FORM A JOINT VENTURE TO PURSUE FIXED-LINE TELECOMMUNICATIONS AND INTERNET OPPORTUNITIES IN hongkong. THE 50:50 JOINT VENTURE WILL COMBINE HUTCHISON WHAMPOA'S EXISTING TERRITORY-WIDE, BUILDING-TO-BUILDING FIXED-LINE TELECOMMUNICATIONS AND CERTAIN INTERNET-RELATED ASSETS IN hongkong WITH GLOBAL CROSSING'S INTERNATIONAL CABLE CAPACITY AND GROWING INVENTORY OF WEB HOSTING, INTERNET APPLICATIONS AND DATA SERVICES. THE JOINT VENTURE, WHICH WILL BE NAMED HUTCHISON GLOBAL CROSSING (HGC), IS VALUED AT 1.2 BILLION unitedstates DOLLARS (9.3 BILLION HK DOLLARS). HUTCHISON WHAMPOA CHAIRMAN LI KA-SHING SAID THAT HE WAS VERY PLEASED THAT HUTCHISON WILL HAVE A SUCCESSFUL COMPANY LIKE GLOBAL CROSSING AS ITS PARTNER FOR THE TELECOMMUNICATION BUSINESS IN hongkong. UNDER THE JOINT SPONSORSHIP OF GLOBAL CROSSING AND HUTCHISON, HGC WILL BUILD ON HUTCHISON'S POSITION AS THE LARGEST FULL-SERVICE ALTERNATIVE TELECOM OPERATOR IN hongkong, ONE OF THE FASTEST GROWING TELECOMMUNICATIONS MARKETS IN ASIA. HGC WILL PURSUE FIXED-LINE TELECOMMUNICATIONS NETWORK BUSINESS IN hongkong. USING THIS NETWORK INFRASTRUCTURE AS A PLATFORM, HGC WILL OFFER HIGH QUALITY BROADBAND TELECOM SERVICES TO HIGH VOLUME CUSTOMERS IN hongkong, INCLUDING MULTINATIONAL CORPORATIONS, GOVERNMENT BODIES, INTERNET SERVICE PROVIDERS AND OTHER TELECOM OPERATORS.

title: china to form orderly local market for internet industry
body: china's internet industry is trying to regulate the market at an early stage.  on thursday, eight leading chinese internet content providers ( icps) clinched an agreement in beijing to form the china icp united development high-profile conference, china daily reported today.  in this way, some irrational business operations are not so likely to harm the sector over the long run, the companies decided.  the eight icps are: sohu, sina, chinabyte, netease, china wide web, goyoyo, shanghai online and information highway tech.  although competing toughly in the market with 2.1 million internet users nationwide, the eight icps said they hope the organization will help to pave the way for a healthy competitive arena and set up business rules accepted by all.  the conference agreed that local companies need a regulated domestic market which ensures chinese companies are able to expand quickly and have enough strength to compete with their foreign counterparts that have shown a lot interest in entering the market.  the organization is committed to take united action to promote internet-related training and education, the newspaper said.

title: Nasdaq Closes Above 4000 Milestone
body: The technology heavy Nasdaq composite index on Wall Street closed above the 4000 milestone for the first time Wednesday. The index finished up 69.35 at 4,041.46, just 38 trading days after its first close above 3,000. WORLD NEWS; ECONOMICThe Nasdaq has set 14 new closing records so far in December, becoming a dominance force on the stock market. Broader stock indicators were also higher. The Dow Jones industrial average rose 7.95 at the record high of 11,484.66 and the Standard & Poor's 500 index rose 5.80 at a record 1,463.46. The market was driven up by technology stocks. Qualcomm, which developed code division multiple access technology on cellular phones and wireless communications, rose more than 100 points . Other technology stocks also performed well. Most online brokerages rose after Charles Schwab Corp. said it expects to beat analysts' profit forecasts for the fourth quarter. The strength of technology stocks also boosted the blue chip stocks. American Express was the best Dow performer and DuPont also gained. The NYSE index rose 1.73 at 646.03 and the American Stock Exchange index rose 9.33 at 851.86. The Russell 2000 index of smaller companies rose 8.53 at 497.01. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 5-to-3 margin on the New York Stock Exchange, with 1,919 up, 1,176 down and 471 unchanged. NYSE volume declined to 566.20 million shares from 654.17 million in the previous session. Financial markets will close at 1 p.m. on Friday.

body: ONLINE SECURITIES TRADING BY PRIVATE INVESTORS IN ASIA-PACIFIC MARKETS WILL ACCOUNT FOR AT LEAST 20 PERCENT OF ALL RETAIL EQUITY MARKET TRANSACTIONS IN THE REGION BY 2003, A unitedstates MARKET RESEARCH FIRM PREDICTED MONDAY. IN FACT, ACCORDING TO THE STUDY OF DATAQUEST, A SUBORDINATE OF THE WORLD'S PREMIER TECHNOLOGY ADVISOR GARTNERGROUP, 70 PERCENT OF RETAIL BROKERAGES HEADQUARTERED IN ASIA-PACIFIC WILL OFFER REAL- TIME ASIAN STOCK MARKET TRADING FACILITIES VIA SECURE WEB SITES BY 2002. THROUGH 2002, HOWEVER, LESS THAN 50 PERCENT OF BANKS BASED IN THE REGION WILL BE ABLE TO LEVERAGE THEIR INTERNET BANKING SYSTEMS TO SUCCEED IN CONSUMER ELECTRONIC COMMERCE SERVICES. FINANCIAL SERVICES ORGANIZATIONS IN THE REGION'S LEADING MARKETS WILL BE REQUIRED TO HANDLE UNPRECEDENTED RETAIL TRANSACTION VOLUMES OVER THE INTERNET IN THE NEXT FIVE YEARS, THE RESEARCH FIRM SAID. ACCORDING TO DATAQUEST, THE MARKETS OF JAPAN, SOUTH KOREA AND TAIWAN WILL BE HOME TO THE BULK OF WEB-BASED SECURITIES TRADERS AND ONLINE RETAIL BANKING CUSTOMERS FOR AT LEAST THE NEXT THREE YEARS. HOWEVER, THE EMERGING MARKETS IN THE REGION, INCLUDING INDIA AND MALAYSIA WILL CONTINUE TO FACE ONLINE SECURITIES TRADING AND PERSONAL E-BANKING OBSTACLES CAUSED BY REGULATORY HURDLES AND THE LACK OF AN INTERNET-CONCERNED INFRASTRUCTURE. BECAUSE OF THE SHEER DEMAND FOR SECURITIES TRADING OVER THE WEB, DATAQUEST SAID, MOST ASIAN BROKERS WILL SHIFT THEIR RETAIL BUSINESS TO THE INTERNET OVER THE NEXT FIVE YEARS. AS IN NORTH AMERICA, MANY BROKERAGE CUSTOMERS IN THE REGION MAY ABANDON TRADITIONAL BROKER INTERMEDIARIES WHEN THEY REALIZE THE POWER AND COMPETITIVE PRICING OF DIRECT GLOBAL MARKET ACCESS THROUGH INTERNET TRADING.

title: ONLINE TRAVEL SITES ATTRACT MILLIONS OF AMERICANS
body: ONLINE TRAVEL SITES HAVE ATTRACTED MILLIONS OF AMERICANS SINCE THE BEGINNING OF THIS YEAR'S HOLIDAY SEASON. ACCORDING TO A STUDY RELEASED FRIDAY BY PC DATA, A SERVICE TRACKING WEB USAGE INFORMATION AND BUYING PATTERNS, PRICELINE. COM EMERGED AS THE TOP SITE FOR unitedstates INTERNET USERS SHOPPING FOR INFORMATION ON THANKSGIVING HOLIDAY AIR TRAVEL, WITH 3.2 MILLION UNIQUE HOME VISITORS IN NOVEMBER. THIS TRANSLATED INTO A 71 PERCENT INCREASE OVER THE PREVIOUS MONTH'S FIGURES OF THE ONLINE SERVICE WHICH ALLOWS TRAVELERS TO BID ON AIRLINE AND HOTEL FARES. FOLLOWING PRICELINE WERE ONLINE TRAVEL SITES OF TRAVELOCITY AND EXPEDIA, WITH 2.8 MILLION AND 2.1 MILLION VISITORS RESPECTIVELY. OF THE AIRLINE-SPONSORED SITES, SOUTHWEST AIRLINES CAME FIRST WITH 1.5 MILLION USERS, FOLLOWED BY AMERICAN AIRLINES AND DELTA AIRLINES. THE STUDY ALSO REVEALED THAT MOST unitedstates HOME INTERNET USERS RESERVED THEIR HOLIDAY FLIGHTS THROUGH DIRECT CHANNELS AS OPPOSED TO TRAVEL AGENTS. THIRTY-TWO PERCENT BOOKED FLIGHTS ONLINE, WHILE 31 PERCENT BOOKED FLIGHTS BY TELEPHONE DIRECTLY THROUGH AN AIRLINE.  TWENTY PERCENT BOOKED THROUGH A TRAVEL AGENT. AIR TRAVELERS GO ONLINE, PC DATA SAID, BECAUSE THEY WANT INFORMATION, ESPECIALLY WANT TO KNOW THE SHORTEST, EASIEST AND LEAST EXPENSIVE PATH TO BOOK THEIR FLIGHTS. THE SUCCESS OF THE SOUTHWEST SITE HAS TO DO WITH A DESIGN THAT TRANSFERS THE COMPANY'S REPUTATION TO THE INTERNET, ACCORDING TO PC DATA. THE TRADITIONALLY LOW-COST AIRLINE FARED WELL IN THE STUDY BECAUSE ITS DIRECT CHANNEL PHILOSOPHY TRANSFERS EASILY TO THE INTERNET, ENABLING IT TO EXPAND ITS CONSUMER BASE AND CONTINUE TO KEEP ITS COSTS DOWN. PC DATA SURVEYED 4,100 HOME-BASED INTERNET USERS IN NOVEMBER.  SIXTY-EIGHT PERCENT OF THE USERS BETWEEN THE AGES OF 18 AND 34 BOOKED THEIR FLIGHTS ONLINE OR BY TELEPHONE DIRECTLY TO AN AIRLINE COMPARED WITH 56 PERCENT BETWEEN THE AGES OF 35 AND 65.

ONLINE ADVERTISING SPENDING WILL GROW FROM 3.1 BILLION unitedstates  DOLLARS IN 1999 TO 4.82 BILLION IN 2000 AND 13.3 BILLION BY 2003, SAID THE REPORT FROM EMARKETER, A unitedstates FIRM SPECIALIZING IN ONLINE BUSINESS. "AS THE BASE GETS BIGGER, THE RATE OF GROWTH IN ONLINE ADVERTISING WILL SLOW DURING THE NEXT FIVE YEARS." ONLINE ADVERTISING SPENDING IN 2003 WILL REPRESENT 4.7 PERCENT OF TOTAL ADVERTISING EXPENDITURES IN THE unitedstates, WHICH ARE EXPECTED TO TOP 285 BILLION DOLLARS. NEW MEDIA CONTENT PROPERTIES AND COMPUTER-RELATED PRODUCTS AND SERVICES ARE BUYING THE LARGEST PORTION OF WEB ADS IN THE unitedstates, ACCOUNTING FOR 48 PERCENT OF THE TOTAL ONLINE AD SPENDING, THE REPORT SAID. COMPUTER HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE ADVERTISERS ARE ALSO SPENDING HEAVILY ON THE INTERNET AS THEY ARE A NATURAL FIT FOR THE WEB AUDIENCE. CONSUMER PACKAGE GOODS MARKETERS ARE NOW BEGINNING TO DIVERT MORE OF THEIR MASSIVE AD BUDGETS TOWARD ONLINE ADVERTISING. THE REPORT ALSO STRESSED THAT WHILE THE INTERNET IS EXPERIENCING RAPID GROWTH, IT WILL NEVER TOTALLY SUPPLANT ADVERTISING IN TRADITIONAL FORMS OF MEDIA. "ONLINE MARKETERS WILL STILL RELY ON OTHER, OFF-LINE MEDIA TO CREATE AWARENESS, BUILD AND PROMOTE THEIR BRANDS, AND DRIVE TRAFFIC TO THEIR WEB SITES," THE REPORT SAID. "THE NET IS MERELY ONE TOOL, WITH SPECIFIC STRENGTHS AND WEAKNESSES, IN THE OVERALL ADVERTISING MIX."
