title: HKE120352 -- ROUNDUP: BANGLADESH VULNERABLE TO Y2K PROBLEM
body: WITH LESS THAN ONE MONTH LEFT BEFORE THE YEAR 2000 ARRIVES, BANGLADESH IS STILL UNSURE WHETHER ALL ITS COMPUTERS HAVE BEEN MADE "MILLENNIUM BUG-FREE." BANGLADESH IS AMONG THE 12 "WORST-PREPARED" COUNTRIES IN THE WORLD TO HANDLE THE MILLENNIUM BUG, OR THE Y2K PROBLEM, ALTHOUGH IT FORMED A NATIONAL COMMITTEE IN AS EARLY AS MAY 1998 TO TACKLE THE MILLENNIUM PROBLEM, ACCORDING TO THE BRITAIN-BASED INTERNATIONAL MONITORING, A TECHNOLOGY CONSULTING GROUP. AT A SEMINAR ORGANIZED BY THE BANGLADESH COMPUTER SAMITY AND OTHERS RECENTLY, STATE MINISTER FOR PLANNING MOHIUDDIN KHAN ALAMGIR SAID THE Y2K PROBLEM WAS UNLIKELY TO UNLEASH ANY CATASTROPHIC DAMAGE IN BANGLADESH SINCE THE COUNTRY HAD VERY LIMITED USE OF COMPUTERS. SIRAJUL ISLAM, THE Y2K COORDINATOR OF THE BANGLADESH COMPUTER SAMITY, SAID THE COUNTRY'S ENERGY SECTOR HAD ACHIEVED 97 PERCENT OF COMPLIANCE, BANKING SECTOR 95 PERCENT, AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS 90 PERCENT. BUT COMPUTER EXPERTS SAID THAT WITHOUT 100 PERCENT COMPLIANCE, ANY MAJOR BREAKDOWN COULD AFFECT LARGE-SCALE INDUSTRIES. THEY SAID IT WAS DIFFICULT TO PREDICT WHAT WOULD HAPPEN TO BANGLADESH WHEN THE COUNTRY GREETS THE YEAR 2000. THE AMERICAN CHAMBER OF COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY IN BANGLADESH HAS WARNED ITS MEMBERS TO LEAVE DHAKA WITH A VIEW TO AVOID THE MILLENNIUM GLITCH. A RECENT EDITORIAL IN THE FINANCIAL EXPRESS DAILY NEWSPAPER SAID THERE WAS A STRONG PROBABILITY THAT THE BANGLADESH POWER DEVELOPMENT BOARD COULD BE HARD HIT BY Y2K BECAUSE IT MADE EXTENSIVE USE OF COMPUTERS AND ITS COMPUTER SYSTEMS IN GREATER PART HAD BEEN HARDLY SCREENED FOR Y2K ADAPTATION AND COMPLIANCE, AND CONSEQUENTLY, WATER SUPPLY IN URBAN AREAS COULD BE SIMILARLY AFFECTED BY DISRUPTED ELECTRICITY. AS A PREVENTIVE MEASURE, BANGLADESH'S NATIONAL AIRLINES, BIMAN, HAS DECIDED TO RECALL ALL ITS AIRCRAFT FROM MIDNIGHT DECEMBER 31 TO 7 A.M. THE NEXT DAY AND THE FLIGHTS WOULD REMAIN SUSPENDED DURING THE PERIOD TO AVOID ANY EVENTUALITIES DUE TO THE Y2K BUG. BIMAN OFFICIALS SAID A ROLLOVER TEST WAS QUITE EXPENSIVE BECAUSE IT HAD A LIMITED NUMBER OF AIRCRAFT, AND A SINGLE ROLLOVER TEST INVOLVED A HUGE AMOUNT OF DOLLARS. A ROLLOVER TEST MEANS CHANGING DATES OF ALL CHIPS IN ADVANCE AND CARRYING OUT A TEST RUN TO SEE HOW THEY FUNCTION. THE DHAKA STOCK EXCHANGE, ONE OF THE COUNTRY'S TWO BOURSES, WOULD CARRY OUT MOCK AUTOMATED TRADING IN MID-DECEMBER BY CHANGING INTERNAL DATES OF COMPUTERS TO DECEMBER 31 AND ROLLING OVER TO YEAR 2000 TO ENSURE A SMOOTH TRANSITION TO THE NEW MILLENNIUM, WHILE THE CHITTAGONG STOCK EXCHANGE WOULD TRY TO BYPASS THE MILLENNIUM BUG BY GOING BACK THE MANUAL TRADING SYSTEM IN CASE ITS AUTOMATED PROCEDURE WAS BOGGED DOWN. BUT THE STOCK EXCHANGES, WITH THEIR MEMBERS DIALING IN TO THE SYSTEM AND TRADING ON-LINE, COULD NOT CONSIDER THEMSELVES TO BE FREE FROM SUCH GLITCHES UNLESS THE BANGLADESH TELEGRAPH AND TELEPHONE BOARD DECLARED ITSELF FULLY Y2K-READY. THE FINANCIAL EXPRESS EDITORIAL CALLED ON THE AUTHORITIES IN VARIOUS UTILITY BODIES TO BRACE THEMSELVES ON AN EMERGENCY BASIS TO TRY TO PREPARE AS MUCH AS POSSIBLE WITHIN THE SHORT TIME AVAILABLE TO ACHIEVE AS MUCH Y2K COMPLIANCE AS POSSIBLE. THE Y2K PROBLEM IS CAUSED BY THE COMMON PROGRAMMING PRACTICE OF USING THE LAST TWO DIGITS IN A DATE TO REPRESENT A PARTICULAR YEAR, SUCH AS 98 FOR 1998, AND WITH THE ONSET OF THE NEW CENTURY, THE YEAR DIGITS WILL SHOW 00, WHICH MAY BE INTERPRETED BY THE COMPUTER AS 1900, GIVING ERRONEOUS RESULTS WHICH MAY HALT NORMAL OPERATIONS OF THE COMPUTER SYSTEMS.

title: HKE112913 -- BANGLADESHI STOCK EXCHANGE TO TEST Y2K COMPLIANCE
body: THE DHAKA STOCK EXCHANGE (DSE) WILL CARRY OUT MOCK AUTOMATED TRADING IN MID-DECEMBER BY CHANGING INTERNAL DATES OF COMPUTERS TO DECEMBER 31 AND ROLLING OVER TO YEAR 2000 TO ENSURE A SMOOTH TRANSITION TO THE NEW MILLENNIUM. THE DAILY STAR BUSINESS MONDAY QUOTED OFFICIALS OF THE DSE, ONE OF THE COUNTRY'S TWO BOURSES, AS SAYING THE HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE PROVIDERS HAD ASSURED THEM OF THE SYSTEMS' COMPLIANCE TO FACE THE YEAR 2000 GLITCHES. "WE HAVE OBTAINED NECESSARY PAPERS CERTIFYING THE COMPLIANCE OF OUR MACHINES, BUT WE PLAN TO CONDUCT THE ROLLOVER TEST TO ENSURE THAT NOTHING WILL GO WRONG," DSE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER G.Q.  CHOWDHURY SAID. BUT THE STOCK EXCHANGES, WITH THEIR MEMBERS DIALING IN TO THE SYSTEM AND TRADING ON-LINE, CANNOT CONSIDER THEMSELVES TO BE FREE FROM SUCH GLITCHES UNLESS THE BANGLADESH TELEGRAPH AND TELEPHONE BOARD (BTTB) DECLARES ITSELF FULLY Y2K-READY, THE REPORT SAID. THE TWO BOURSES LAUNCHED AUTOMATED TRADING LAST YEAR, MAKING THE BTTB AN INTEGRAL PART OF THE STOCK BUSINESS. THE PROBLEMS THAT ARE EXPECTED TO ARISE FROM NON-COMPLIANCE ARE MODIFICATION OF INTERNAL DATE OF COMPUTERS FROM DECEMBER 31, 1999 TO JANUARY 1, 2000 AT MID-NIGHT ON DECEMBER 31, 1999, MALFUNCTION OF HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE USING TWO-DIGIT YEAR CONVENTION, HARDWARE SHUTDOWN AND DATA CORRUPTION. MEANWHILE, THE CHITTAGONG STOCK EXCHANGE, THE OTHER BOURSE OF THE COUNTRY, IS SET TO BEGIN MOCK MANUAL TRADING FROM NEXT MONTH TO GET RID OF THE Y2K PROBLEM, THE FINANCIAL EXPRESS DAILY REPORTED.

title: china to develop e-commerce in its own way
body: china is planning to multiply the number of people in the country using the internet in the near future by implementing the latest technology.  the integrated e-business service platform, developed by the shenzhen liming networks systems, one of the largest computer network integration firms in china, enables users to access service providers and other users of e-commerce via television, telephones and facsimiles, as well as personal computers. the core of the technology is an information switch, or i-switch, that can bridge the flow of data between such electronic networks as tv, telecommunications, and the internet.  the shenzhen liming network systems signed an agreement today with ibm of the unitedstates on strategic cooperation in developing applications of e-commerce that are suitable for conditions in china today.  director of the national office of information technology song ling said at the signing ceremony that the chinese government is considering listing this new technology as one of the national experimental e-commerce projects.  the shenzhen liming network systems has already installed this technology for the shenzhen stock exchange for the on-line trading of securities.  henry chow, chairman of ibm operations in the greater china region, said today that the company will help china explore various ways to expand e-commerce.

title: feature: a breeze from china --chinese-american painter opens exhibition in new york
body: wearing three flowers in hair and a jade ring around wrist, a chinese lady is playing pipa, a traditional chinese plucked string instrument, beside a quiet pond teeming with lotus flowers.  a fisherwoman mother is helping his son walk in shallow waters from the fish boat to the shore in south china. a pavilion in suzhou garden is greeting its reflection in the tranquil pond.  these are the scenes from the painting exhibition, which opened at the well-known hammer galliers here on monday night. with the theme "a breeze from china," the painter, chen yiming, offers new yorkers a pleasant and quiet world in the city with so many skyscrapers and so heavy traffic.  here and there, some 40 paintings are all mirroring chinese culture, which, to a large extent, remains mysterious to american viewers.  "as modern technology --email, fax, the global internet -draws the world closer together, it creates a more dehumanized environment, replacing, in many instances, actual human interaction," said ronald pisano, a famous american scholar.  "communication may be improved (certainly with regard to speed and efficiency), but emotional content --the inflection of one's voice, the expression on one's face --are sacrificed in the process," pisano said.  although not intended as a social commentary, the delicate figure paintings of chen yiming express this alienation. his art, which he clearly maintains is not intended to be narrative or symbolic, does invite interpretation and, most definitely, elicits an emotional response from the viewer.  his masterful technique is used to entice the viewer to take part in an emotional experience, rather than entertain or create a specific story of some sort.  "i want to give the viewer space to communicate with the painting --to promote a personal exchange," chen told xinhua.  "each person will bring something different to the experience." "painting figures is the most difficult job," he said. "just like you are setting your foot into a mine field, one careless step will lead you to nowhere." "i have been working very hard to portray the inner world of the people in my paintings, trying to bring an unfinished story to my viewers," he said.  although his paintings are generally large in scale and conception, the mood chen creates is very personal. and, though the emotions he deals with are universal, they are at the same time limited in range --serenity, introspection, nostalgia, reverie, or even sadness --and the time frame, a mere interlude, is restricted as well.  li zhaoxing, the chinese ambassador to the unitedstates, told xinhua, "i love these paintings, because they are telling chinese stories." "i am proud of chen because he was nurtured by new china," li said. "this exhibition is very helpful in promoting the sino-unitedstates cultural and art exchange." the former unitedstates secretary of state, henry kissinger, was also present at the opening ceremony. he voiced his appreciation of the paintings and said that he would find some more time to view the paintings a couple of days later.  born in 1951 in shanghai, east china, chen has been working as both a peasant and a worker when he was young. after his training program at the shanghai school of fine art, he enrolled himself into the department of oil painting, shanghai drama college in 1979.  chen was a teacher of fine art at shanghai light industry college from 1979 to 1981, when he came to the unitedstates.  in 1982, he made a successful debut with his paintings exhibition at the new york-based international gallery. since then, he gave a series of art displays in shanghai, paris, singapore, canada and some other asian countries and regions.

title: hsbc launches internet credit card payment services
body: the hongkong and shanghai banking corporation limited began offering over the weekend its internet payment gateway, a senior hsbc official announced monday.  the internet payment service, the first of its kind in hongkong, enables merchant customers in hongkong to accept credit card payments for goods and services over the internet, the official said.  "we believe that the launch of this service will provide a significant boost to the growth of e-commerce in hongkong," said eric tai, hsbc's head of personal banking development in asia.  "the response from our merchant customers has been very encouraging so far and we are confident that both merchants and cardholders will benefit from having a secure means to deal with payments over the internet using the hsbc payment gateway service, " tai said.  a number of major organizations in hongkong have already signed letters of intent and are expected to connect their websites to hsbc's payment gateway in the coming months, tai said.  the system, which has developed in conjunction with compaq computer limited, supports both the secure sockets layer (ssl) and secure electronic transaction (set) security standards and allows hsbc's merchant customers to accept visa, mastercard and jcb payments over the internet in a wide range of currencies, tai said.

title: electronic transactions progress in malaysia
body: malaysian electronic payment system (meps) has been effective since its nationwide implementation on march 22, 1999, according to a bank negara official.  payments totaled 8.25 million ringgit (2.171 million unitedstates dollars) through the meps secured electronic transactions (set) payment gateway, bank negara (state bank) assistant governor zamani abdul ghani said here tuesday at the launch of premium-link, the online payment and renewal services for motor insurance.  there are already 170 merchants acquired by four participating banks --maybank, public bank, rhb bank and hong leong bank --in the payment gateway and 3,500 e-wallets (digital certificates) have been issued free to cardholders, he added.  meps has been entrusted to develop a payment gateway based on set, given that the credit card is commonly used for internet purchases, he said, adding that set protocol provides a more promising solution in terms of security as the information pertaining to credit cards will not be transmitted over the network and the identity of the cardholder is based on the digital certificate.  he said that as the set technology is new, the central bank has allowed the use of security socket layer (ssl) protocol to coexist with set to support the development of e-commerce.  he urged the insurance industry to prepare itself for the transition to a new business era as it enters the 21st century, saying, "in malaysia, only about half of the licensed insurers had set up information with non-interactive websites on the internet.  as it is, we still have a long way to go." according to the central bank official, studies in the unitedstates estimated that more than 200 billion dollars' worth of business will be transacted over the internet by the end of next year and there are currently more than 8,000 insurance-related websites.  he said the internet enables insurers to expand their marketing potential in ways previously not possible or economically feasible.  the central bank official said that in promoting e-commerce in malaysia, the government established in 1998 the national electronic commerce committee (necc) to provide strategic governance of e-commerce and set the direction for the development of e-commerce.  one of the objectives of the necc is the formulation of an electronic commerce masterplan for malaysia and this is currently being finalized.

title: hk to pick up speed to boost e-frastructure
body: hongkong plans to speed up the development of the internet-based infrastructure in a move to enhance its competitiveness as an international financial center, a report released tuesday showed.  the report, released by the securities and futures commission ( sfc), recommends that to keep the leading position of hongkong as an international financial center in terms of risk mitigation, increased efficiency and cost reduction, hongkong should put together an "e-frastructure." the e-frastructure will facilitate the development of e-trading in securities and derivatives in hongkong and the asia region, sfc chairman andrew sheng told a press briefing.  sheng said that the e-frastructure is a web-friendly technology infrastructure for the securities and derivatives industry that allows local and global market participants to access the full spectrum of financial products and services on an open, robust, secure, scalable, and high performance network.  "with implementation of the e-frastructure, hongkong can aspire to become one of the leading centers for liquidity, clearing, settlement and risk management in asia and the portal for strategic links with global markets in the region," sheng said.  the e-frastructure includes the components of a single clearing arrangement for better risk management, end-to-end straight through processing for improved cost-effectiveness, a scripless securities market for enhanced efficiency and legal certainty, and an open, robust, current and scalable technology structure for local and remote connectivity and high performance.  "hongkong already has the best telecommunications infrastructure to enable the development of e-commerce and etrading," added sheng, who also chairs the steering committee on the enhancement of the financial infrastructure (scefi) in hongkong.  the scefi report has been submitted to financial secretary donald tsang yam-kuen, proposing an array of measures to facilitate and accelerate the implementation of the e-frastructure.

title: umyk launches new on-line stock trading service
body: united mok ying kie ltd. ( umyk), one of hongkong's oldest and most respected brokers, tuesday announced the launch of its new on-line stock trading service, swiftradehk.  umyk is a member firm of the stock exchange of hongkong (sehk) and a registered dealer under the securities ordinance with the securities and futures commission (sfc). umyk is also a corporate member of the hongkong securities institute.  the new service provides clients with on-line technology for easy, efficient and inexpensive access to the sehk. it ensures swift execution and rapid confirmation of trades, along with accurate and updated balances and position.  users have access to real-time sehk stock prices, to enable them to check prices instantly and have their portfolios updated automatically and in real-time.  in a recent joint report entitled "internet investment services --conclusions and recommendations for hongkong", hongkong's most respected financial institutions, including the sehk, sfc, hongkong futures and the better hongkong foundation, concluded that there will be a significant shift among local retail investors towards on-line services.  an estimated 20-30 percent of investors will be trading on-line by 2010, accounting for 30-40 percent of total retail trading volume.

title: hk university wins world's internet awards
body: researchers from the university of hongkong have won the world's special internet achievement awards for their successful development of a virtual university campus on internet.  the geographical information system (gis) research center of the university of hongkong also received the gold medal of the best arcview ims application competition from the environmental system research institute (esri) in the unitedstates, the largest gis software company in the world.  the university of hongkong is the first institute in the region to receive this award, which is being given to user sites around the world in recognition of their outstanding work in gis field.  it was selected from over 100,000 sites worldwide.  the virtual campus was developed and used on the homepage of the university of hongkong in august 1998 to provide the twodimensional, three-dimensional and multimedia campus information in the worldwide web for visitors using the rsri technology.  apart from serving as a campus information system, it is also a showcase on how advanced applications of the internet gis technology can be used in the service and marketing industries, such as property agencies and advertising firms, to provide similar information service to their clients.

title: stareastnet.com brings asian entertainment on-line
body: the star east information technology corp. (star east it) announced here tuesday the launch of its interactive entertainment web site --stareastnet.com, with its strategic partner, ibm china/hongkong limited.  based on ibm's e-business solution, the web site leads the world in e-entertainment transformation and provides an interactive channel for the global chinese community to the world of asian entertainment and lifestyle, said star east it in a statement announcing the launch of the site.  the site provides open and interactive windows of communication from people to people, especially from artists to the public.  running on an ibm rs/600 server, the web site will feature updated entertainment news, official artists profile, art and entertainment, on-line games, on-line and off-line interactive events, city guides, live broadcasts from star east entertainment complexes, real time on-line chat between artists and fans, new star recruitment and freebies.  content of the web site is first presented in cantonese and will subsequently be in putonghua (mandarin) and english to reach chinese communities everywhere in the world.  among the executive directors of the company are famous hongkong artists alan tam wing lun, eric tsang chi wai, natalis chan pak cheung and jing wong yat cheng.  so far, in addition to its artist shareholders, agreements have been signed with more than 70 artists to develop their own web pages, in an effort to make stareastnet.com the leading destination site for the asian entertainment industry.  the company will focus its efforts on e-business and has plans to include international stars to expand the market internationally.

title: citibank introduces new internet services in hk
body: citibank hongkong today announced the launch of the second generation of its internet financial services, which will make on-line investing easier and more convenient.  the internet securities services, introduced by citibank for the first time in the asia-pacific region, will offer users online stock trading access with very low brokerage charges.  the key feature of the services, namely "power trader," allows customers to easily visualize their transactions by viewing the securities and settlement account status on one screen while simultaneously checking stock prices and placing up to five stock trading orders.  another important feature is the "stock watch" service which permits customers to preset stock watching service delivered by email. when a specific stock reaches the preset price, an email notification will be sent to the customer.  in addition, citibank also offers on-line financial services including credit card access, utility bill payment and mutual fund inquiry.  william lo, ceo of citibank global consumer banking for hongkong, said internet financial services have gained increasing popularity and acceptance as a remote banking channel since it was first launched last november.  "currently, eight percent of our banking transactions are conducted on the internet while only 21 percent of them are carried out at branches," lo said. "this clearly shows the growing importance of remote channels compared with conventional banking methods."

title: hk hosts asia advertisement fair
body: the marcomasia '99, the only trade fair featuring the latest concept, techniques and tools of the asian marketing and communication industries, opened here wednesday.  organized by the hongkong trade development council, the fair drew the participation of 80 exhibitors from hongkong, the chinese mainland and taiwan, and singapore and india.  addressing the opening ceremony, robin chan, chairman of the chinese general chamber of commerce, said hongkong is the ideal platform to host marcomasia as it ranks first in the world in terms of per capita advertisement spending.  it is also regarded as the most prominent exporter of marketing, advertising and communication services in the asia-pacific region, he added.  "apart from being a big advertising market itself, hongkong is also a leading exporter of advertising services including ad design, media buying, direct marketing, graphic design, marketing consultancy and customized market research," chan said.  "the export of these advertising and market research services totaled 2.7 billion hk dollars (346 million unitedstates dollars) in 1997, representing an average annual growth of over 21 percent since 1990," he noted.  chan also highlighted the emergence of the internet as a new medium for advertising.  "more companies with strong it background are providing internet advertising and marketing services and it is widely believed that internet advertising will continue to grow at a fast pace," he said.

title: hong kong sets up first cyberschool
body: hongkong has set up its first cyberschool, so as to bring a new era to the metropolis' online education through a series of home-grown and universityindustry cooperative programs.  an inauguration ceremony for the newly-built center for enhanced learning and teaching and the cyberschool of information technology was held at the hongkong university of science and technology (hkust) on monday.  "the key objective of the center is to facilitate effective learning and teaching by fostering a culture in which both students and teachers can learn to continuously upgrade their knowledge and skill to face today's global challenges," the center 's director grace au said at the ceremony.  the cyberschool, a joint venture between the hkust, cable wireless hkt and ibm china/hongkong ltd., is an on-line learning infrastructure. the school utilizes web-based course delivery and multimedia technology that enables students to access from campus or at home a wide range of tertiary-level information technology courses over a broadband internet.  "there is no doubt that information technology has become part of our lives and it is going to revolutionize the education environment as well," said linda young, manager of the department of e-business and multi-industry solutions of the ibm china/hongkong limited.  "as the world enters the new millennium, so does the global education environment," young said, adding "the launch of cyberschool is just the beginning of our initiative to make information technology education pervasive in hongkong."

title: sun hung kai co. limited to launch online broking
body: sun hung kai co. limited (" sun hung kai" or "the group") has a clear policy to develop the " online" or electronic broking capacity to complement the current electronic delivery of its research and financial information services.  the launch of the group's online broking, to be operated on the stock exchange's future ams/3 which allows straight through processing (stp) providing terminal and open gateway approaches, will be announced later this year.  with the gateway approach, sun hung kai will be able to directly connect with the stock exchange using an open gateway device and the group is expecting benefits from this initiative.  "apart from our enhancement of broking services for clients, sun hung kai is proceeding with the marketing and business development activities announced at our annual general meeting in june," said sun hung kai's executive chairman, arthur george dew.  sun hung kai thursday announced its interim results for the six months period ending june 30, 1999. the group recorded an operating profit of 28.8 million hk dollars (3.68 million unitedstates dollars) and a profit from ordinary activities of 57.2 million hk dollars (7.33 million unitedstates dollars).

title: uk logs on to e-commerce: surveys
body: britain is experiencing an e-commerce boom, with growing numbers going online to do their shopping or manage their finances, according to local median reports.  a recent survey by management consultants datamonitor said that online shopping and banking are becoming increasingly popular, as more than one in five consumers with access to the internet have ordered products online, while 8 percent of those surveyed used the net to monitor their finances.  internet share trading is showing rapid growth too, up by 21,555 users in the second quarter of 1999, according to a separate survey by the association of private client investment managers and stockbrokers (apcims).  the level of e-commerce penetration was particularly high in london, where almost one in two people have access to a computer at home. in the capital, 27 percent of net users had shopped online, the report said.  "one in four londoners online at home or work order products via the internet," datamonitor analyst alexander rainer said.  "this figure is surprisingly high, considering a minority of uk websites currently have transactional capabilities. " however, for internet banking, rural areas proved the most fertile territory, with the highest rate of use in east anglia, at 14 percent.  "rural regions such as east anglia and scotland appear to have the biggest appetite for online banking as many consumers live far from their branch," a bbc report quoted rainer as saying. "where people live in a more pressured working environment, like in london, online banking is driven by the convenience of 24-hour availabililty." the separate apcims survey showed that internet share trading rose by nearly 60 percent in the last quarter. however, it still only accounts for 1.6 percent of all trades, the association said.  online trades averaged a value of 4,730 pounds, compared to 6,444 pounds for trades through other stockbrokers.  the growth in internet trading is expected to increase in the coming months, as more brokers develop the capacity to trade online, according to analysts.

title: u.s. online ad spending expected to grow
body: unitedstates online advertising is expected to grow to 11.5 billion unitedstates dollars in 2003, surpassing dollars spent in some traditional media, according to new research released wednesday by an internet commerce research firm.  jupiter communications said that ad spending will increase 40 percent over the next four years, with financial services, automotive, and media ventures leading the spending.  according to an earlier jupiter report, in 1998, online advertising increased 34 percent over 1997 to reach 1.92 billion dollars.  driven by growing online population, the rise in time spent online, and increasing digital commerce adoption, online advertising revenues have already surpassed those for outdoor advertising and will exceed spending for cable advertising and equal roughly three-quarters of today's radio spending by 2003, according to jupiter.  car companies, media firms and financial services companies will account for nearly half of online ad spending in 2003. but packaged goods companies, whose ad spending will account for 18 percent of offline dollars, will only contribute seven percent of online dollars by that time.  "online advertising will serve as a catalyst for change in the traditional ad business," jupiter said. "media integration and the inevitable erosion of traditional markets will be more important than the effects of online ad dollar growth." another unitedstates research firm, forrester research, estimated last week that global spending for online advertising will reach 33 billion dollars by 2004, one-third of which will be spent outside of the unitedstates.  forrester projected that unitedstates online ad spending will hit 22 billion dollars by 2004. this figure represents 8.1 percent of projected expenditures for traditional advertising --exceeding magazine, yellow pages and radio spending.  over the next five years, the internet will siphon 27 billion dollars or 10 percent of all unitedstates ad spending --away from traditional media, according to forrester.  outside the unitedstates, online ad spending will increase from 502 million dollars in 1999 to 10.8 billion dollars in 2004, capturing 33 percent of global spending, forrester estimated. in europe, online ad will total 5.5 billion dollars in 2004, representing 5.1 percent of europe's ad spending. the asia-pacific nations will spend an additional 3.3 billion dollars, or six percent of traditional ad spending in the region. latin america will grow to 1.6 billion dollars in 2004, or 4.8 percent of regional spending.

title: worldwide internet security software market expands
body: the worldwide market for internet security software jumped 43 percent over 1997 and reached 3.2 billion unitedstates dollars in 1998, a unitedstates market research firm said tuesday.  this year, according to international data corporation (idc), the market will jump another 39 percent to 4.4 billion dollars.  in 1998, the unitedstates was the largest regional market for internet security software, representing 54 percent of the market.  western europe presents the next-largest opportunity, with 28 percent of the market share.  idc expects the market to continue to expand. by 2001, the market will have more than double its 1998 value. by 2003, revenues will approach 8.3 billion dollars, representing a solid 21 percent compound annual growth rate from 1998.  idc splits the internet security software market into four segments: firewall, encryption, antiviral, and authentication, authorization and administration software.  authentication, authorization and administration products represented the largest segment in the 1998 market with 1.6 billion dollars, idc said. this segment will maintain its top spot through 2003, when its worth will exceed 3.7 billion dollars.  firewalls are a fast-growing segment. from 1997 to 1998, the value of this segment increased 80 percent to 442 million dollars. by 2003, its revenues will approach 1.5 billion dollars. the increasing popularity of e-commerce is contributing to the growth of firewalls, idc said.

title: on-line ads destined for rosy future
body: fueled by an increasing number of the internet users, on-line advertising is expected to have a glorious future in china, reported today's china daily's weekend edition, business weekly.  "although on-line advertising appeared in china only four years ago, it has great market potential," said li fangwu, director of the information center of the china advertising association (caa).  caa reports indicate china's internet advertising was valued at 20 million yuan (about 2.4 million unitedstates dollars) last year.  li said this can be mainly attributed to the increasing popularity of the internet on the chinese market.  sources from china national network information center (cnnic) indicate that by the end of 1998, there were 2.1 million internet surfers in china, twice the figure in 1997.  by the end of june this year, the figure has increased to four million.  "the advent of on-line advertising has enriched the variety of advertising forms along with television, radio, newspapers, magazines," he said.  at the beginning of the 1980s, most customers preferred to advertise in major central governmental newspapers because of their large circulation and identifiable reader groups.  "however, as the market gradually matured, many businessmen choose to advertise in places where they felt they would have a greater market potential for their products," said li.  he said that compared with other forms of advertising such as tv ads and newspaper ads, internet advertising has many advantages and huge possibilities.  on-line advertising is more effective, he said, with welldesigned three-dimensional pictures and bountiful relevant information.  meanwhile, internet advertising can provide precise feedback for advertising enterprises, because computers may be used to easily record a web surfer's search patterns.  "however, compared with developed countries, on-line advertising in china is still in its infancy," li said.  in 1998, sales of global on-line advertising were two billion u.  s. dollars, 100 percent more than in 1997.  in many developed countries, such as the unitedstates, internet advertising is earning more than three billion unitedstates dollars a year.  it is difficult to clearly define internet advertising in china because many enterprises are using the internet to introduce themselves and their products. controversy remains whether this should be regarded as advertising.  at present, internet ads in china are mainly banners and icons.  problems affecting the industry include a lack of unified standards for billing for internet advertising, he added.  industry analysts believe it would be a good idea to form authoritative advertising companies specializing in offering customers internet advertising services.  "given the rapid development of china's internet and the sustainable economy, market potential is huge and overwhelming," li said.  experts from within the circle predict that by the end of 1999, china will have more than five million internet surfers, and the figure is expected to surpass ten million by 2000.

title: world leading online broker to open business in hk
body: td waterhouse, a world leading online broker, announced here on thursday that it will launch local stock trading during the fourth quarter of 1999 and electronic trading in the first quarter of 2000.  approved by the council of the stock exchange of hongkong ( sehk) and the securities and futures commission, td waterhouse is the first foreign discount broker to open share trading service in hongkong.  td waterhouse has also acquired a seat of the sehk from a leading hongkong brokerage, harvester (securities) co. ltd.  "local trading will allow us to offer the hongkong market to our two million clients around the world." said andrew nevin, managing director of td waterhouse hongkong, at the press conference.  "given the importance of the hongkong market, we know that many of these customers will take advantage of this capability." he added.  as the second largest discount broker in the world, td waterhouse has operations in canada, the unitedstates, hongkong, australia and britain.  the company provides internet-based investing services and related financial products, and has over 2.8 million customers accounts and 113 billion unitedstates dollars in assets under administration.  stephen d. mcdonald, chief executive officer of td waterhouse, said, "adding stock trading in hongkong is an important step in our global strategy of being a significant player in every market we enter." "the internet is revolutionizing the brokerage industry and td waterhouse is at the forefront of these changes," he said.

title: ca unveils line of internet-security software
body: computer associates international, the world's leader in mission-critical business software, said tuesday that the company is starting an internet-security line of software as another way to tap into the surge in companies doing business on line.  the e-trust line will include encryption, which creates codes to protect data; fire walls, for keeping out unauthorized users and information; and virtual private networks, which provide privacy while using public networks, charles b. wang, ca's chairman and chief executive officer, said here at the companies 5th annual meeting since 1995.  ca said it is working on a new version of its jasmine program, used in creating software, to sell to companies that want to do business on the internet, the worldwide link-up network.  the new jasmine program is to include neutral-network technology, patterned on the human brain's decision-making ability, that can be used in making forecasts.  "users can build and employ web application in wed speed," he said.  wang, an overseas chinese who was born in 1944 in shanghai, east china, and came to the unitedstates in 1952. he set up ca in 1976 and developed it into the the no. 4 unitedstates software company.  with the revenue of 5.3 billion unitedstates dollars in the fiscal year 1999, ca employs 14,000 professionals in more than 100 countries and regions.

title: leading software producer introduces end-to-end security solution for e-business
body: computer associates international (ca), leading software producer in the world, monday announced a broad-based solution that supports customers' e-business initiative with the industry's most comprehensive portfolio seamlessly bundles security functions that are essential to delivering trusted e-business solutions.  the solution allows customers to get to market more rapidly and reduce development costs without compromising transition integrity.  the announcement came as ca's week-long annual meeting entered its second day, which attracts more than 25,000 computer science professionals all over the world.  e-trust addresses the challenges of buyers and sellers in an e-business relationship. buyers with assurances that their transition will be honored and private. sellers want assurances that they have resource.  both parties want to work within an auditable, policy-based business model that is effectively protected from viruses, malicious code, cyber-criminals and other threats.  "security is the essential ingredient for every virtual business relationship," said ca chairman and chief executive officer charles b. wang. "as e-business exponentially, ca's e-trust is designed to facilitate security and trust by delivering some of today's most powerful integrated security, trust and privacy services and solutions." the e-trust portfolio of tools and solutions includes trust certificates, encryption controls, antivirus mechanisms, malicious code prevention, denial-of-service counter-measures, intrusion detection, firewar facilities, policy compliance and comprehensive auditing capabilities.  e-trust includes a trust certificate solution that confirms the identity of the trading parties in any e-business transaction.  through a powerful implementation of the on-line certificate status protocol (ocsp), e-trust enables any company to conduct trusted business-to-business e-commerce with any other member that is also a member of the trust network, the global banking industry's foremost trust infrastructure.  "everyone wants the internet to be a secure, 'well-lit' place in which to do business," wang said. "an essential pre-requisite is to have in place a highly reliable and trusted security solution that deals with issues such as identification, authentication, privacy, fraud control --as well as the more traditional aspects of authorisation, administration and auditing." wang, one of the overseas chinese in the unitedstates, is ca's chairman and chief executive officer, the world leader in mission-critical business software.  with revenue of 5.3 billion unitedstates dollars in fiscal year 1999, ca employs more than 14,000 people in 100 countries around the world.  wang founded ca in 1976, launching the company with three associates, a single product and a simple idea: that technology must serve business. today, ca software provides the computing foundation for hundreds of thousands of businesses all over the world.

title: singapore airlines introduces internet booking
body: singapore airlines (sia) will launch tuesday an internet-based system called sq-etravel, which will allow sia customers to use the internet to book their seats and pay for sia tickets, the sia announced monday. sia said from july 13, 1999, sia customers flying between singapore and five destinations --hongkong, kuala lumpur, london, manchester and penang --will be able to book their travel via the internet through sq-etravel at www.singaporeair.com. the service, 24 hours a day and seven days a week, will initially be available for economy class travel and will be extended to all classes by september 1999 and more routes will be added by the end of the year, sia said. customers booking their travel through sq-etravel can collect their boarding pass by producing the credit card used to make the booking as verification, sia explained further. recounting the merits of the system, sia said sq-etravel will offer customers greater convenience, choice and control in planning their travel and provide them a just-mouse-clicking means to check flight availability, select the flight of their choice, order a special meal, pay on-line by entering their credit card details and print a receipt. sia also said planning is underway to enhance the system to allow first and business class customers to view real-time seat map and select their preferred seat.

title: boc launches internet banking services
body: the bank of china (boc) announced today that it has launched a range of internet banking services providing its customers with online shopping facilities.  the vice-president of the boc, hua qingshan said that this will enable boc customers to conduct online inquiries, account transfers, payments, settlements and other business.  he said that the boc had introduced the state of the art secure electronic transaction model in designing its internet services, in a bid to ensure the security of online payments and shopping.  according to hua, these services include corporate online financing, internet payments and bank-securities express.  the corporate online financing provides corporate customers with online account inquiries, corporate internal transfer of accounts, statements on international income and expenditure and other services.  the internet payment service enables individual customers to do online shopping using the great wall charge card issued by the boc, while bank-securities express is specially designed for securities firms to conduct capital clearing businesses.  "boasting the most advanced internet security measures, these new services can ensure the safety of card holders' trading information," hua said.

title: china opens first nationwide on-line university
body: china opened its first nationwide on-line university today, marking the beginning of a new era for its education system.  the distant learning school of beijing university of post and telecommunications (bupt) is jointly sponsored by the university and china telecom.  the first year's intake of 1,000 students are from beijing and tianjin cities and guangdong, liaoning and fujian provinces. they will attend real-time classroom lectures of the university through the internet and the atm telecommunication network at 31 different locations around the country. after earning adequate academic credits through four years of study on line, they will gain an official certificate or even a degree.  apart from bupt, qinghua university, hunan university and zhejiang university have also been given government approval to run on-line education courses on a trial basis. however, hunan and zhejiang universities are only open to on-line students in their own provinces.  vice-minister of information industry qu weizhi said at the today's ceremony that on-line distant learning will lead to a revolution in the means of education in china. she said that it is a major step forward in the drive to rejuvenate the nation through scientific and technological advances and a vital way to improve national competitiveness.  zuo feng, director of the data communications bureau of china telecom, noted that limited resources have restricted further expansion of the higher education market in china. he said that online education will make full use of the existing educational facilities by breaking down the barriers of time and distance. it will help stimulate demand in a huge potential market.  china now has some 696 million employed persons. if only a quarter of them receive further education every year, the potential market will be 174 million persons. as a result, qu said that on-line education has tremendous prospects.  a student from liaoning province in northeast china said at the launch ceremony that the on-line university will allow greater flexibility for him to balance study, work and family. he said that on-line education is the best choice for him to complete higher education.  noting that on-line distant learning is still in a trial stage at present, zuo said that the new method of education has yet to resolve such problems as inadequate utilization of network resources and returns of investment.  china telecom has invested near 50 million yuan in the first phase of setting up the distant learning school at bupt. a bupt official said that the university is still waiting for government approval on the level of tuition fees of on-line education.  the official said that the first year of on-line students are employees from post and telecommunications bureaus in various localities. the university is yet to get government approval to widen the base of students to people from all trades, he added.

title: merrill lynch launches internet service
body: merrill lynch co., the largest u.  s. stock brokerage, announced here tuesday that it will allow customers to trade stocks over the internet for 29.95 unitedstates dollars per transaction.  "whether clients want advice and guidance from a skilled financial consultant, convenient, self-directed internet investing, or some combination, they'll get it at merrill lynch," david komansky, chairman and chief executive officer of the company, said at a press conference.  the company made the decision in face of challenge for its business from on-line traders such as charles schwab corp. the internet now accounts for 30 percent to 35 percent of all stock trades by individuals.  the company will also permit investors to do unlimited free trading in return for an annual account fee equaling about 0.2 percent of the account's asset. its minimum fee will be 1,500 dollars a year.  the decision marks a dramatic change for merrill lynch after spending decades to forge a nationwide network of 14,800 brokers, who provide customers with investment advices and earn commissions for placing stock trades. analysts estimate that about two billion dollars of merrill's 1998 revenue of 17.5 billion dollars came from commissions paid by individual investors for stock and bond trades.  the merrill's internet service will be available starting december this year. clients who want to continue to deal with merrill as before --advised by a broker and paying full commissions, will still be able to do so.

title: singapore's tradenet passes y2k tests, official says
body: singapore's trade development board (tdb) declared monday that its on-line trade documentation system, tradenet, has passed a six-day y2k test and will be ready to handle the year 2000 and the leap year processing of trade documentation.  tdb's director for computer information services division martin tsang said in a press release that the tradenet y2k integrated simulation test was declared a success after six days of stress testing from may 10 to 15.  during the test, more than 500 trade documentation cases were tested with the participation of the tdb, the customs and excise department (ced), singapore network services (sns), cargo community network (ccn), nine controlling agencies, four tradenet software vendors and 10 of their shipping agents and traders.  tsang said, "we are pleased at the success of the simulation exercises and it will still be business as usual for our traders as we enter the year 2000." tsang also said two minor problems were encountered and quickly resolved during the test.  they were the communication problem which obstructed the connectivity between customs and excise department and singapore network services and the permit date problem which made tradenet system unable to format some permits correctly when the system was set to february 28, 2000, and february 29, 2000.  tsang was confident that tdb's services will continue to run smoothly without any disruptions as it crosses over into the year 2000. the y2k problem arises when software records the year in two digits instead of four, which will cause confusion when the year 2000 approaches.

title: u.s. company to develop music download system
body: universal, the world's largest music company, wednesday entered into a partnership with a california-based software company to develop a system that would allow customers to download music to their computers in a secure format that prevents mass copying.  "we have to try and find out what the consumers want and what they are willing to pay for," larry kenswil, head of electronic commerce at universal, said wednesday. "one thing for sure is people want to download music," he added.  industry sources say universal's move underscores the music industry's difficult search for a way to take advantage of the internet and, at the same time, curb piracy that cost companies about 5 billion unitedstates dollars a year.  they say universal's announcement is significant because it marks the first attempt by a major music company to go digital.  the legitimate music market is worth about 40 billion dollars a year and a report by forrester research said digital distribution of music will be worth 1.1 billion dollars by 2003.  other technology companies, including sony, microsoft and ibm are competing to develop secure systems for digital transmission of songs.

title: web ad revenue in u.s. doubles in
body: online advertising revenues in the unitedstates more than doubled in 1998, reaching 1.92 billion unitedstates dollars, according to a report released monday.  it grew by 112 percent over the 906 million dollars for 1997, said the leading online ad association internet advertising bureau (iab).  in the fourth quarter alone, web ads increased by 34 percent to 655.6 million dollars. two years ago, internet annual revenue was only 267 million dollars.  noting that the internet as a viable advertising medium is barely four years old, iab said that its growth, measured in billions of dollars, is astounding. the association expects a sustained growth period in coming years due to increasing online ad budgets and greater commitment by large traditional advertisers.  the categories which lead the online spending were consumerrelated advertisements at 31 percent, computer-related ads at 26 percent, and financial services at 19 percent. top sectors represented in the consumer category include retail, auto, toys, travel and music.  top 10 web sites drew 71 percent of all ad spending for the fourth quarter of 1998. meanwhile, banner advertising represented 56 percent of all online ads, while sponsorships declined to 30 percent from 36 percent at the end of 1997.

title: computer-related crimes surging in china
body: china's public security departments uncovered nearly one hundred hacker cases last year, a figure arousing public awareness of computer and network security.  according to sources, illegal activities involving computers an d the internet have soared by an astounding 30 percent annually in recent years. the hackers have hundreds of tricks," outnumbering the varieties of computer viruses in china," said one anti-hacker expert.  an official with the public security ministry said that the detected hacker cases account for only an estimated 15 percent of all such occurrences, and the majority of hacker cases go undetected, either because the hackers had done little harm or the victims cover them up for fear of damaging their own images.  the chinese media, in this case, do not follow the silent majority. they kept track of the latest hacker activities, and have called for measures to combat them.  a local computer journal reported that 95 percent of china's network management centers with internet access have been attacked by hackers from both home or abroad. as in other places, banking, financial and securities institutions are the main targets of those greedy intruders, the journal said.  zhao zhansheng, a computer security specialist with the chinese academy of social sciences (cass), said that china's information network is still at "a nascent stage," and the fragile "firewall" of information systems leaves loopholes through which hackers can enter. "it is most serious that a large portion of computer crimes are committed by insiders, because most companies lack a multi-level computer security system," he added.  jinhua'an information technology co. recently conducted tests of dozens of security agencies in shanghai and shenzhen, and found almost all of their network security systems were undefended. with a lap top computer hooked up to a telephone line, testers easily logged in their networks and reached restricted information in a minute.  "real hackers can now freely rewrite all vital data in the database," one tester said.  expert said that most hackers are youngsters with a good programming expertise. they decode a computer system only to show off their "special talent". but up to now, china has no laws or regulations to warn or punish these "fun-seekers".

title: virtual university launched on net in zhejiang province
body: more than 600 students from three cities in zhejiang province will begin their campus life at a university that exists only on the local computer network and was launched today by zhejiang university, the largest university in china.  at this virtual university, lectures, seminars and all multi-media academic material will be transmitted via the internet. professors and students will be able to have electronic, visual discussions through the computer screen, and students can freely arrange their schedule to do research in the electronic library or access previous lectures simply by clicking on whatever they want.  long-distance education is only dawning in china, and so far the chinese ministry of education has permitted only four universities to install this method on a trial basis, including prestigious qinghua university in beijing.  a total of 11 long-distance electronic education center are expected to be established by next spring, covering all of zhejiang province.  zhejiang university's long-term goal is to have the provincial electronic educational network available on every personal computer in the region, making higher education easily accessible to everyone.

title: new tide of web advertising surging in china
body: qiu ke, 24, who has a degree in advertising, resigned from a well-known joint venture in beijing one year ago and joined the other pioneers who are exploring china's internet advertising market, still a novelty in the country.  to date, qiu's blue process company has 12 domestic clients for whom it has created internet ads. these clients include magazines and securities companies. "small as it's now, i'm bullish about this market," he said.  according to preliminary statistics, there are now more than 30 companies such as blue process in beijing.  the beijing-based stone rich sight company (srs), which has the most popular chinese website in china, has set out to establish the world's largest chinese website --sina.  deng hailin, marketing manager of srs, said that interactivity is one of the characteristics of the internet, facilitating convenient communication between advertisers and consumers. advertisers can also accurately calculate the number of people exposed to their online advertisements.  the number of internet users has rapidly increased over the past five years. statistics show that about 80 million computers were connected with the internet worldwide by last year, and this figure is expected to reach 200 million.  advertising on the internet has also become a booming commercial activity in western countries. experts predict that the world gross ad investment will reach five billion unitedstates dollars in 2000.  china's internet market is closely following the world pace. the country currently has 1.17 million users, and the figure will reach two million by the year 2000.  these people are mainly in their twenties and thirties, and are well-educated and well-paid, said deng.  most insiders and officials agree that china's internet ad market will make rapid progress in the next five years, though it is not mature now.  deng said that current internet ad income, which mainly comes from the information industry, is only less than one percent that of traditional mass media.

title: yahoo gets foothold in china
body: global internet content provider yahoo has signed a landmark agreement with china to sell its services here, yahoo international vice president heather killen announced here today.  she said in a speech delivered at the third cic-china.com conference here that beijing-based infoshare technology co. ltd. will be the exclusive sales agency for yahoo in china.  infoshare is a state-owned company under the china international electronic commerce center (ciecc) of the ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation (moftec).  ma yun, general manager of infoshare, said that this cooperation will begin in december. infoshare will promote yahoo services in china and help chinese enterprises create on-line advertisements on yahoo's worldwide network.  "this is just the first step in cooperation, and we have a complete plan," he said.  but he did not elaborate, saying that the plan will be unveiled at a joint press conference in the unitedstates in the next 48 hours.  killen said that it is a good idea to cooperate with moftec, which has direct links with import-and export-oriented companies in china.  she said that yahoo will offer a global platform for chinese companies entering the international market.  it is necessary to have a local sales agency in the country because the number of chinese companies contacting yahoo for on-line advertisement is increasing, she said.  according to ma the newly established ministry of information industry (mii) is drafting new regulations on the rapidly growing internet market and there is no requirement that the mii approve this cooperative project.  "we will go through all necessary procedures if any are introduced in the future," he said.  china now has six million internet users and the figure is doubling every year.

title: content provider holds annual conference in beijing
body: china's most promising internet content provider china internet corporation (cic) held the third cic-china.com conference here today.  several hundred representatives from the chinese government and international information technology and financial circles attended the meeting.  under the joint sponsorship of cic, the news and information center of xinhua news agency and the data communications bureau of china telecom, the conference invited representatives from successful internet content providers in the world to give lectures, including jack davis, president of america online.  the conference focused on four topics under the theme of "creating network society, embracing network civilization," including growth of international network technologies, internet market in china, network applications and on-line advertisement.  cic was jointly developed by xinhua news agency and the former ministry of posts and telecommunications. the china.com company (ccc), or china wide web (cww), is a solely owned company of cic. the first and second china.com conferences were held in october, 1996 and december, 1997 respectively.  since early this year, china.com has achieved success in creating a number of specialized web sites during such major events as the world cup football games, unitedstates president bill clinton's visit to china and serious floodings in china. as a result, it has become a pace setter in terms of on-line information and advertisement in the country's fledging internet industry.  at present, china.com provides information about china and its hongkong and taiwan regions in both chinese and english. it has four major web sites and access to users in over 200 cities and regions in china, as well as to those around the world.  it has formed cooperative relations with america online and nescape and strategic partnership with 24/7 media. its sources of informations include afp, dow jones business video, xinhua, thomson financial service and financial times.

title: china to hold internet export fair
body: china is planning to introduce internet into china export commodity fair, which is one of the most influential foreign trade event in the country.  face-to-face talks and internet trading will become a new trend for the fair to be held biannually in guangzhou, officials attending the current 84th event told reporters.  preparations for such a fair are being made by china international electronic commerce center under the ministry of foreign trade and economic cooperation, the officials disclosed. the internet will play the role of introducing participating enterprises and products, statistics and background information of previous fairs.  according to zhang daming, deputy director of the center, the projected internet event is expected to expand the scale and influence of the fair, and facilitate the exchange between exporters and importers.  the novelty will also become an extension of the biannual event, providing chances for further contacts after the on-the-spot event is closed, zhang said.  internet was used for the first time two years ago during the 80th fair when a web-site of the fair was opened. statistics show about 4,000 people visit the site everyday.  the 83rd fair employed internet to send invitations to over 2,000 chain stores and department stores.  during the current fair, legend group, a leading chinese computer maker, struck a deal worth 18 million us dollars with a hongkong company.  "all these have paved the way for the coming of the internet fair in the future," zhang said.

title: internet awareness and use grow in kenya
body: the rise in internet awareness in kenya has triggered a spiral growth in on-line trading as at least 25,000 people in the country have internet access.  the vast potential of on-line trading was apparent at a recent internet auction of seats to various european destinations by lufthansa airlines. kenyans were among 600 potential buyers who bid through the internet.  the rise in internet awareness and use was first noted during the 1997 general election in the east african country and is largely credited to the nation media group website, which had an average of 50,000 hits a day.  during the december election month, internet services reported eight million visits to kenyan sites, barney lodge, chief of media street, an electronic advertising agency in nairobi, was quoted by monday's east african as saying.  in kenya, "at least 25,000 people have internet access and the number is bound to grow as the cost of connections and computers falls and back-up services improve," said lodge.  until two years ago, computers cost not less than 100,000 shillings (1,666 unitedstates dollars) but prices now average 60,000 shillings (1,000 dollars), largely due to a reduct o,hz7 import duty and competition among a large number of importers.  the growth in the number of internet users has, however, been hampered by poor telephone connections, with most business clients reluctant to invest in developing their own websites, fearing that these would not be easily accessible.  in response, the kenya posts and telecommunications corporation is planning to install a fiber optic telephone network by november, which will provide "clean" and fast internet connections.  however, victor mabachi, chairman of the advertising practitioners associations (apa), said the internet still lacks a solid client base to attract good advertising.  currently, the bulk of advertising on the internet is by small-scale traders, who constitute 75 percent of all advertisers, said geoffrey shimanyula, the marketing manager of africaonline, which is kenya's biggest internet service provider.

title: worldwide online advertising to grow
body: global spending for online advertising will hit 15 billion unitedstates dollars in 2003, an american technology research firm said wednesday.  forrester research, inc. based its estimation on the steady growth in the world's online population and the arrival of mainstream advertisers.  the company said that spending for online advertising will continue to be dominated by the unitedstates, with internet advertisements growing from 1.3 billion dollars in 1998 to 10.5 billion dollars in 2003.  but the unitedstates share of the worldwide market will decline from 87 percent in 1998 to 70 percent in 2003, forrester said, adding that the global online advertisement spending was estimated at one billion dollars in 1997.  outside the unitedstates, advertisement spending will be led by europe, where the online market is expected to grow from 105 million dollars in 1998 to 2.8 billion dollars in 2003.  this spending, forrester said, will be pushed by an increasingly cohesive european market, a growing internet population, competition from unitedstates-based companies and maturing technologies.  slowed by ongoing economic difficulties, asian advertisement spending will grow to 1.25 billion dollars in 2003. dramatic growth in latin america will be masked by a small internet population and a low starting point for advertisement spending, it said.  "the internet has arrived as an accepted advertising medium," forrester's report said. "this is evidenced by the amounts that will be spent for online advertisements during the next five years, as well as by the arrival of large mainstream advertisers." in addition to the growth in overall spending, forrester expected per capita spending for online advertisements in the unitedstates to bypass radio and magazine advertisements by 2003.  internet advertisers will spend 25 dollars per person in 1998 --double the amount spent in 1997. by 2003, this number will grow to 104 dollars per person, roughly one-third of per capita spending for television advertisements but slightly ahead of magazine and radio spending.

title: more americans do stock trading at home
body: a growing number of americans are doing their stock trading at home, all they use is a computer and a modem, according to a report of the new york post today.  a study by investment banking firm piper jaffrey found that online trading accounted for 17 percent of all volume from retail investors in 1997. in the first half of 1998, it grew to 20 percent. the piper jaffrey study estimates that online could account for 30 percent of retail volume by the end of the year, and 50 percent by the new millennium.  the low cost of online trading is what first attracted investors.  "when people move from traditional brokerage or phone execution of trades to online execution of trades, they do increase their trading," said alex goor, president of datek online, which allows customers to trade up to 5,000 shares of stock for just 9.99 unitedstates dollars.  "the costs are just so much lower that the investors feel they can move in and out of stocks quickly," goor said.  according to brokerage firms and the stock exchanges, the average individual investor conducts two transactions each month -typically one sell order and one buy order.  the average online brokerage customers conducts 4.5 transactions each month, the paper said.  some customers would do more trades a day.  more than 75 firms currently offering online trading, up from fewer than 20 just one year ago.  many of these firms are taking advantage of newly released technology to process trades of 1,000 stocks or more for less than 10 unitedstates dollars.  and many more providers of online trading are popping up every day.  people also uses the internet to search for information on which they base their trading decisions. there are hundreds of websites providing investment information.  they can also customize the site to track their favorite stocks.  meanwhile, it said, the securities and exchange commission is stepping up its oversight of the internet, in hopes of stopping stock promoters from pushing bad offerings on innocent investors.

title: australian bank to introduce internet banking
body: australia's leading bank national australia bank ltd. (nab) announced thursday that it would introduce an online banking service with unprecedented levels of security.  the service, known as national internet banking, would be based on java software and feature the use of digital certificates, the first in the australian banking market, the bank said.  the use of digital certificates is equivalent to an electronic signature and is assigned to each customer's personal computer.  it is encrypted and held on the customer's personal computer, preventing unauthorized access from any other location.  the service would feature online registration, so nab clients would not need to visit a branch before using it.  it would offer users account balances, 100 days of statement information with search and sort functions, transfer of funds between nab accounts and other banks, secure email to and from the bank, set up and change periodic payments and bill payments.  glenn barnes, nab executive general manager of business and personal financial services, said national internet banking would be made available progressively to nab staff and selected customers from this week, with a general release later in the year.

title: miga launches privatization information service for investors
body: the multilateral investment guarantee agency (miga) monday announced the launch of privatizationlink, an internet-based information service for firms seeking to invest in the private sector of the emerging economies. the service will initially cover selected countries in central and eastern europe, central asia and sub-saharan africa, later expanding to include other regions. privatizationlink provides on-line access to business profiles of state-owned companies and assets currently for sale, along with details of the relevant laws, regulations and procedures governing these transactions. access to privatizationlink is free at http://www.privatizationlink,com. first-time users are required to register with the service. privatizationlink is a specialized facility within the investment promotion network (ipanet), the miga's on-line information clearinghouse for companies engaged in cross-border investment, which has been in operation since 1995. the miga, established in 1988, is a member of the world bank group. its mandate is to encourage foreign direct investment into developing countries by providing long-term guarantees against political risks, and by offering investment marketing services to host developing countries.

title: fsa issues guidance on investment advertisements
body: the financial services authority (fsa) thursday issued guidance on investment advertisements on the internet.  the guidance concerns advertisements from overseas on internet sites which may be accessed by uk investors even though the advertisements are not targeted at them.  the fsa hopes that the guidance will enable financial services companies overseas to comply with uk regulation, and therefore minimize the likelihood of fsa enforcement action in this area.  the internet enables uk investors to access investment advertisements put onto the world wide web from anywhere in the world.  it is understood that while this increases the amount of information available to uk investors, it also carries the risk that the provisions in the financial services act (fs act), which are designed to protect investors from misleading or inaccurate information, might be evaded.  the protection is the requirement that an investment advertisement in the uk is issued by an authorized person or approved by such a person. breach of this provision is a criminal offense.  the fsa does not have the power to amend the fs act but does have discretion as to when and how it uses its enforcement powers.  the guidance expands on the fsa's enforecement approach towards possible breaches of this provision in the fs act.

title: satellite education network to cover sub-saharan africa
body: helped by the world bank, a satellite distance education network, known as the african virtual university (avu), will launch four undergraduate degree programs for the sub-saharan african countries next year.  local media thursday quoted professor beda mutagahywa, the director of the computing centre of the university of dar es salaam (udsm), as saying that the avu will run computer science, computer engineering, electric engineering and nursing degree courses.  the avu will enroll its own students for the programs under private basis at 12 receiving sites in six anglophone countries, tanzania, kenya, ethiopia, uganda, ghana and zimbabwe, mutaagahywa said.  he said that avu is designed to offer undergraduate degree programs of televised instructions from the unitedstates and ireland to train a large number of african scientists, technicians, engineers, business managers and employees.  "it also aims at providing an academic environment in which african educational institutions and students can participate effectively in the worldwide community of learning, research and dissemination of knowledge,"he added.  in tanzania, the sites are at the udsm and the tanzania open university. in kenya, at kenyatta university and in uganda at makerere university, kyambogo polytechnic and martyrs university.  mutagahywa said the avu project is implemented in three phases. as a pilot, the first phase started on february 26 this year in udsm to comprise seminars and short courses to the would-be students.  he said that several basic equipment, provided by the world bank, have been stationed in the udsm including one satellite dish and a lot of personal computers, video recorders, fax machines and others.

title: most uk businesses unaffected to internet: report
body: despite the attention being given in the media, internet is something that still doesn't seem to affect most uk businesses, a new report by the internet marketing and development agency (imda) showed.  from a telephone survey of 1000 businesses, the imda research found that although 98 percent of those called had "heard of the internet", only 12 percent believed that it had any bearing on their present business.  findings showed that most british businesses had been so lax in their understanding of the internet that they had ignored the opportunity offered to use their company names for domain registration.  only 14 percent of the companies surveyed had registered domain names and fewer than five percent realised that there was any issue of brand or marketing strategy when picking a domain name.  hundreds of thousands of trading names have been bought by rouge companies who are seeking to sell them back at inflated costs.  many domain names which could be registered as little as 60 pounds(100 unitedstates dollars) are now changing hands for thousands of pounds, the report said.  british businesses are falling behind their american counterparts and facing exclusion from global commerce on the internet, the imda report warned.

title: deutsche telekom to offer online electronic business systems
body: germany's dominant telecom company, deutsche telekom, announced today that it would launch new complete systems to enable the handling of electronic business on the internet.  according to herbert may, a senior manager of deutsche telekom's global system unit, the so-called "shop and mall systems" to be launched by the company in a few months, would offer its business customers, shopowners for example, the opportunity to operate virtual shopping centers on the internet.  internet users will then be able to see and order certain products presented in the online "shops" and pay the bill by credit cards also through internet.  dr. may emphasized that the breakthrough for electronic commerce on the internet depended on the introduction of secure payment systems.  "for this reason, our objective… is to support… online payment systems that provide utmost security, anonymity and user-friendliness," he said.  dr. may also announced that deutsche telekom has entered into a strategic cooperation with ibm to develop viable online payment systems. as the first step, the two companies will conduct a pilot project based on the set (secure electronic transaction) standard, which currently meets highest security requirements.

title: firms to fund on-line education program in u.s.
